title: Career and experience

title: Health and wellbeing
content_markdown:
[Vector illustration of UBC students doing different activities\. From left to right: lounging in a cozy living space, making a meal together, stretching before a workout, and riding a bike](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/hero_health_wellbeing.jpg)

Take care of your whole self with support at UBC and off campus\.

## Crisis support 24/7[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/\#crisis\-support\-24\-7](https://students.ubc.ca/health/#crisis-support-24-7)

Get help if you or someone else is in immediate danger, or at risk of harming yourself or others\. Call [911](tel:911) or visit your [nearest emergency room](https://www.vch.ca/en/health-topics/emergency-care)\.

If you or someone you know is feeling hopeless or at risk of harm, call or text [988](tel:988) toll\-free at any time to reach the [Suicide Crisis Helpline](https://988.ca/)\.

## Physical health[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/\#physical\-health](https://students.ubc.ca/health/#physical-health)

[A student speaks with a health professional at their Student Health and Wellbeing medical appointment](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/health_landing_medical_care.jpg)

### Medical care on campus

If you have a health concern, book an appointment with Student Health and Wellbeing\.

Congratulations on joining a diverse community of scholars\. We can’t wait for you to arrive on the beautiful UBC Vancouver campus, situated on the [traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory](https://indigenous.ubc.ca/indigenous-engagement/musqueam-and-ubc/) of the Musqueam people\.

title: Health insurance
content_markdown:
UBC requires all students, both domestic and international, to have basic and extended health insurance for the duration of their studies\.

Find out what kind of health insurance you need during your time at UBC:

-   [Domestic students](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-domestic/)
-   [International students](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/)
-   [Indigenous students](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-indigenous/)

## Basic health insurance[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/\#basic\-health\-insurance](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/#basic-health-insurance)

The [BC Medical Services Plan](http://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp) \(MSP\) is a provincial government program which provides basic medical benefits\. Study permit holders are charged a $75 healthcare coverage fee per month, while other eligible residents of British Columbia will have access to the provincial government health insurance free of charge\.

Everyone living in British Columbia \(BC\) for **more than 6 months** is required to enrol in MSP, except for students with existing coverage from another Canadian province or territory\.

If you arrive in British Columbia without coverage under MSP or another provincial or territorial health plan and will be here for 6 months or longer, you must apply for MSP online immediately upon your arrival\. Follow the [MSP application tutorial](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/apply-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/) if you are an international student\.

Since there is a 3\-month waiting period before MSP coverage begins, you must ensure you have basic health insurance for those first 3 months in British Columbia\. Canadian citizens or permanent residents are advised to purchase private temporary health insurance for coverage during that 3\-month MSP waiting period, such as the [Global Campus Health Plan](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/global-campus-health-plan/)\. Most new\-to\-UBC international students registered for one or more on\-campus courses are automatically covered by [iMED health insurance](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international/) for their first 3 months in Canada\.

Most new\-to\-UBC international students registered for one or more on\-campus courses and who are charged AMS/GSS student fees are automatically covered by [iMED health insurance](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international/) for your first 3 months in Canada or the full duration of your program of studies if you will be studying for less than 6 months\.

## Extended health insurance[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/\#extended\-health\-insurance](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/#extended-health-insurance)

If you are a UBC student registered in classes, you are automatically enrolled in the [AMS/GSS Health and Dental Plan](https://www.ams.ubc.ca/support-services/health-dental/)\. At the start of the academic year, you are automatically charged a [fee for the plan](https://www.studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_Cost_HowMuchDoesItCost)\.

This extended health insurance covers some fees and services which are not covered by basic health insurance, such as up to 80% of the cost of eligible prescription medicine, dental care, vision care, psychologist visits, and travel insurance\. Find out [what’s covered](https://studentcare.ca/plan/en-CA/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS/understanding-my-coverage) under the plan and how to [make a claim](https://studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_Claims_HowtoClaim)\.

The plan also includes student health benefits for counselling\. Learn how to find a [private mental health professional](https://students.ubc.ca/health/counselling-services/finding-private-counsellor/) for your concerns\.

### Exchange students

If you are an exchange student and you pay tuition at your home university, you are not automatically enrolled in the AMS/GSS Health and Dental Plan\. You may, however, be [eligible to apply](https://studentcare.ca/rte/en/SelfEnrolment%2811%29) once you arrive at UBC\. You will need to fill the AMS Fee Opt\-in form and submit your request during the [change of coverage period](https://www.studentcare.ca/View.aspx?locale=en&uid=UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_ChangeofCoverage_ChangeofCoveragePeriod&)\. If you wish to opt into the AMS/GSS Health and Dental Plan, you must opt into all other [AMS fees](https://www.ams.ubc.ca/about-us/finances/ams-fees/)\. It is important that you have extended health and dental coverage while you are in Canada\.

### If you’re covered by another plan

You can request to [opt out](https://www.studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_ChangeofCoverage_OptOuts_HowtoOptOut) of the AMS/GSS Health and Dental Plan if you have a separate extended health insurance plan which is equivalent to the coverage provided by the AMS/GSS Health and Dental Plan\. BC MSP coverage alone is **not** an equivalent to the AMS/GSS Health and Dental Plan\.

If you want to opt out, you must do so within the [change of coverage period](http://www.studentcare.ca/View.aspx?locale=en&uid=UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_ChangeofCoverage_ChangeofCoveragePeriod&) or within 3 weeks of your registration date, whichever is later\.

title: Equity, diversity, and inclusion resources
content_markdown:
UBC is committed to providing a safe, supportive, and inclusive living and learning environment with resources and services to support all students\.

The University does not tolerate racism or bias and strives to create an inclusive campus community through resources, services, conversations with critical groups, and funding for program initiatives\.

-   [Review UBC’s Respectful Environment Statement](https://hr.ubc.ca/working-ubc/workplace-experience/respectful-environment)
-   [Learn about UBC’s Equity and Inclusion Office](https://equity.ubc.ca/)

[Musqueam Post in the foreground, University Boulevard on UBC Vancouver campus](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/edi_musqueam_post.jpg)

## About the UBC Vancouver campus[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/equity\-diversity\-inclusion\-resources/\#about\-the\-ubc\-vancouver\-campus](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/#about-the-ubc-vancouver-campus)

The University of British Columbia is located on the traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the xʷməθkʷəy̓əm Musqueam people\. We are grateful to live, work, and study on a land full of rich history and community\. 

Learn about what it means to be on this land in the [introduction to Musqueam and UBC](https://indigenous.ubc.ca/indigenous-engagement/musqueam-and-ubc/)\.

## Responding to discrimination[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/equity\-diversity\-inclusion\-resources/\#responding\-to\-discrimination](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/#responding-to-discrimination)

Support is available if you’ve experienced or witnessed an act of discrimination on the UBC Vancouver campus\.

[Learn what to do](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/responding-discrimination/)

## Browse UBC resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/equity\-diversity\-inclusion\-resources/\#browse\-ubc\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/#browse-ubc-resources)

[Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/)

Connect with an advisor if your disability or ongoing medical condition is impacting your learning and participation in UBC activities\.

[Gender Diversity Hub](https://equity.ubc.ca/resources/gender-diversity/)

Get information on inclusive washrooms on campus, changing your gender marker, gender\-affirming healthcare, and more\.

[https://antiracism\.ubc\.ca/resources/](https://antiracism.ubc.ca/resources/)[Anti\-racism resources and support](https://antiracism.ubc.ca/resources/)

Find toolkits, funding, courses, and support to learn about and help advance anti\-racism efforts\.

[https://indigenous\.ubc\.ca/students/](https://indigenous.ubc.ca/students/)[UBC Indigenous Student Portal](https://fnhl.ubc.ca/students/student-resources/)

Access resources specific to Indigenous students, including mentorship, jobs, and tutoring\.

[UBC Women’s Centre](https://womenscentre.ams.ubc.ca/about/)

The Centre offers a safe space and access to snacks, feminist literature, safer sex products, pregnancy tests, and free menstrual products\.

[Students who are parents](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/resources-who-are-parents/)

Caring for a child during your studies can be challenging\. Find childcare options, food assistance programs, and more\.

[Scholarships and bursaries](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/)

Browse awards available to specific student groups, offered by UBC to meet financial needs and recognize academic or extracurricular achievements\.

[Strategic Equity & Anti\-Racism Enhancement Fund](https://equity.ubc.ca/resources/funding-opportunities/strategic-equity-anti-racism-enhancement-fund-student-stream/)

Review funding for projects and initiatives that advance racial, disability, gender, and 2SLGBTQIA\+ equity\.

[2SLGBTQIA\+ resources](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/2slgbtqia-resources/)

UBC offers inclusive resources, support, and community for students exploring or affirming their 2SLGBTQIA\+ identities\.

[Black Student Space](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/black-student-space/)

The Black Student Space is a dedicated place for Black students to study, connect, recharge, and build community\.

## Get involved[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/equity\-diversity\-inclusion\-resources/\#get\-involved](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/#get-involved)

Participate in discussions, programs, or councils to support other students\. Join a task force or student club\.

[Learn more](https://equity.ubc.ca/get-involved/)

title: 2SLGBTQIA+ resources
content_markdown:
UBC aims to create a safe and inclusive campus environment where all genders and sexual identities are welcome\.

Whether you’re learning about your identity or supporting a friend, there are campus resources, involvement opportunities, and career guidance for Two Spirit, lesbian, gay, bisexual, trans, queer, intersex, and asexual \(2SLGBTQIA\+\) students\.

[Pride flag of rainbow colours waving in the breeze](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/resources_lgbtq_flag.jpg)

## Find resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/equity\-diversity\-inclusion\-resources/2slgbtqia\-resources/\#find\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/2slgbtqia-resources/#find-resources)

[Changing your personal information](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/)

Make sure your student information is up\-to\-date, including your legal and/or preferred name\.

Find out how to change your UBC pronouns and gender identity on your official student documents\.

## Get support[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/equity\-diversity\-inclusion\-resources/2slgbtqia\-resources/\#get\-support](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/2slgbtqia-resources/#get-support)

[If you experience or witness discrimination](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/responding-discrimination/)

UBC doesn’t tolerate discrimination in any form\. Learn what to do if you’ve been treated unfairly due to your identity\.

[Sexual Assault Support Centre \(SASC\)](https://www.amssasc.ca/)

SASC supports people of all identities who have been affected by sexualized violence\.

[Sexual Violence Prevention and Response Office \(SVPRO\)](https://svpro.ubc.ca/)

## Learn more and get involved[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/equity\-diversity\-inclusion\-resources/2slgbtqia\-resources/\#learn\-more\-and\-get\-involved](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/2slgbtqia-resources/#learn-more-and-get-involved)

Attend Pride events, join a discussion group, and shop at the Gender Empowerment Store\.

[Positive Space: Foundations online course](https://wpl.ubc.ca/browse/equity-and-inclusion/courses/wpl-eio-psfnd)

Take a self\-paced Canvas course covering topics such as 2SLGBTQIA\+ terms, inclusive practices, and the concepts of gender, sex, and sexuality\.

[Strategic Equity & Anti\-Racism Enhancement Fund](https://equity.ubc.ca/resources/inclusive-initiatives-fund/)

Funding is available for student\-led projects that can positively impact the student experience and create change on campus\.

[Trans, Two\-Spirit, and Gender Diversity Task Force](https://equity.ubc.ca/trans-two-spirit-and-gender-diversity-task-force/)

Propose recommendations to UBC’s senior leadership for a more inclusive campus\.

title: Career resources
content_markdown:
## UBC Career Centre[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/career\-resources/\#ubc\-career\-centre](https://students.ubc.ca/career/career-resources/#ubc-career-centre)

Book an appointment to explore future career possibilities, review your job application or resume, or craft a strategy with a Career Educator\.

[Find out how](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/ubc-career-centre/)

## Getting a job

Find tips and suggestions for job\-searching or preparing a job application\.

[Job search](https://students.ubc.ca/career/career-resources/job-search/)

Whether you’re looking for a part\-time or full\-time role, learn how to use targeted strategies to improve your chance of success\.

[Resumes and cover letters](https://students.ubc.ca/career/career-resources/resumes-cover-letters/)

Learn how to identify and articulate employable skills in ways that make your application stand out\.

[Curricula Vitae](https://students.ubc.ca/career/career-resources/curricula-vitae/)

Know how to highlight your education and accomplishments on the academically\-focused curricula vitae\.

[Interviews](https://students.ubc.ca/career/career-resources/interviews/)

Identify what employers are looking for in interviews and strengthen your approach to speaking about your experience, skills, and interests\.

[Job offer negotiations](https://students.ubc.ca/career/career-resources/job-offer-negotiations/)

When you start a full\-time position, there may be room to negotiate your salary, benefits, vacation time, and more\. Get tips to build your case and anticipate their response\.

## Networking and meeting professionals

Gain expert insight from people working in your field of interest\.

[Making the most of LinkedIn](https://students.ubc.ca/career/career-resources/make-most-linkedin/)

Build your personal brand and strengthen your employability on the most popular networking platform in North America\.

[Networking](https://students.ubc.ca/career/career-resources/networking/)

Develop relationships to get advice, referrals, and inside information from experts in the field\.

[Informational interviews](https://students.ubc.ca/career/career-resources/informational-interviews/)

Talk to an industry professional to get a better understanding of the job or field\.

[What to do before attending career events](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/what-do-before-attending-career-events/)

Prepare to meet alumni and employers and ask questions that matter to you\. 

[What to do after attending career events](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/what-do-after-attending-career-events/)

Take next steps with the people you met and the opportunities you learned about\. 

## Exploring future career possibilities

Many tools and resources exist to help you reflect on your career goals and interests\.

[Self\-assessment tools and resources](https://students.ubc.ca/career/career-resources/self-assessment-tools-resources/)

Trying out an analytical tool may give you insights about who you are, what matters to you, and what you’re good at\. This can help you make informed decisions about your career goals\.

[Design your career](https://students.ubc.ca/career/career-resources/design-career/)

If you want to be very intentional in your decision\-making, the design process and mindset will help you clarify your goals, prototype options and make data\-informed career decisions\.

[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/career\-resources/career\-resources\-historically\-marginalized\-students/](https://students.ubc.ca/career/career-resources/career-resources-historically-marginalized-students/)[Career resources for students from specific communities](https://students.ubc.ca/career/career-resources/career-resources-for-students-from-specific-communities/)

Find resources tailored for students from diverse and intersecting communities, including 2SLGBTQIA\+ students, students with disabilities, and graduate students\.

## Additional support

[Video series: Activate Your Career](https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLtqusylF2447AEf45mVGcPNA8yJKQRNYE&si=zeHGbeKSs3tT_X1B)

Review tips and tricks to support you in your job search and career planning processes, including how to reframe your beliefs, tapping into the hidden job market, and more\.

## Career events and workshops[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/career\-resources/\#career\-events\-and\-workshops](https://students.ubc.ca/career/career-resources/#career-events-and-workshops)

Browse virtual and in\-person workshops and events to help you navigate your career questions and strengthen your employability\.

[Go to calendar](https://events.ubc.ca/organizer/centre-for-student-involvement-and-careers/)

title: Exams
content_markdown:
Most exams are automatically scheduled on the Vancouver campus\. Review the table below for standard final exam periods and when the exam schedule is normally available for each term\. 

Some exams require an application and may follow a different exam schedule, including [Standing Deferred and Supplemental exams](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/exams/standing-deferred-supplemental-exams/)\.

All exams follow [UBC policies and regulations](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/exams/exam-clashes-hardships-cancellations/)\. Make sure you understand your responsibilities before you write your exam\.

title: Imagine UBC
content_markdown:
## Information for first year students[https://students\.ubc\.ca/new\-to\-ubc/orientations/imagine\-ubc/\#information\-for\-first\-year\-students](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/orientations/imagine-ubc/#information-for-first-year-students)

Imagine Day is on **Tues, Sep 8, 2026**\.

For most students, Imagine UBC replaces the first day of classes\. If you’re a first year undergraduate student, you will have the chance to meet great people on campus, including your Dean, some of your future professors, and other students\. It will be an opportunity to learn about your new academic environment and the specific expectations of your faculty\. You’ll also tour campus in a small group led by student leaders\.

You will receive your personalized Imagine UBC schedule by email in late August\. Make the most of this day and find out what awaits you at UBC\. Be sure to check if your email address is up to date in [Workday](https://myworkday.ubc.ca/), and [update your contact information](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/personal-information/updating-your-contact-information/) if needed\.

[imagine day ubc](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/imagine_day_ubc.jpg)

## Transfer students[https://students\.ubc\.ca/new\-to\-ubc/orientations/imagine\-ubc/\#transfer\-students](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/orientations/imagine-ubc/#transfer-students)

If you are coming to UBC from another university or college, Imagine UBC is also for you\!

By participating in Imagine, you’ll be able to make little connections all day long that will help kick start your UBC experience\.  
  
You will receive your personalized Imagine UBC schedule by email in late August\. Make the most of this day and find out what awaits you at UBC\. Be sure to check if your email address is up to date in [Workday](https://myworkday.ubc.ca/), and [update your contact information](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/personal-information/updating-your-contact-information/) if needed\.

## Returning students[https://students\.ubc\.ca/new\-to\-ubc/orientations/imagine\-ubc/\#returning\-students](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/orientations/imagine-ubc/#returning-students)

Imagine UBC is an event that most UBC students don’t forget\. All students are invited to participate in the day’s activities\. 

By attending exciting events, you’ll be able to reconnect with the community, show your school spirit, and find opportunities to get involved\.

Details about how you can participate in Imagine UBC will be emailed to you by late August\. Check if your email address is up to date in [Workday](https://myworkday.ubc.ca/), and [update your contact information](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/personal-information/updating-your-contact-information/) if needed\.

## If you’re a graduate student[https://students\.ubc\.ca/new\-to\-ubc/orientations/imagine\-ubc/\#if\-youre\-a\-graduate\-student](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/orientations/imagine-ubc/#if-youre-a-graduate-student)

You’re invited to the Campus Life Expo on Main Mall during Imagine Day\! It’s a great opportunity to discover campus resources, connect with services, and learn about the support available to you as a graduate student\.

Check out upcoming [Graduate Student Orientation events](https://orientation.grad.ubc.ca/events/)\.

## Notice about accessibility[https://students\.ubc\.ca/new\-to\-ubc/orientations/imagine\-ubc/\#notice\-about\-accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/orientations/imagine-ubc/#notice-about-accessibility)

If you have a disability or medical condition that may affect your participation in Imagine Day, please check out the [Imagine Day Accessibility FAQ](https://orientations.students.ubc.ca/accessibility-faq)\. If you have any questions after looking through the FAQ, please reach out to us at [orientations\.info@ubc\.ca](mailto:orientations.info@ubc.ca) as soon as possible so that arrangements can be made to ensure full participation\.

## Continue your orientation after Imagine UBC[https://students\.ubc\.ca/new\-to\-ubc/orientations/imagine\-ubc/\#continue\-your\-orientation\-after\-imagine\-ubc](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/orientations/imagine-ubc/#continue-your-orientation-after-imagine-ubc)

Your orientation doesn’t end at Imagine UBC\. You are invited to participate in a number of other exciting events\.

### Faculty\-based orientation events

Your faculty or undergraduate society may be hosting events in the first weeks of September\. Check out their offerings:

-   [Arts](https://www.arts.ubc.ca/student-support/compass/)
-   [Engineering](https://students.engineering.ubc.ca/get-set-for-ubc-engineering/)
-   [Forestry](https://www.ubcfus.com/)
-   [Kinesiology](https://kin.educ.ubc.ca/undergraduate/new-to-kin/)
-   [Land and Food Systems](https://www.lfsus.landfood.ubc.ca/lfs-firsts)
-   [Science](https://www.susubc.ca/)
-   [UBC Sauder School of Business](http://ubcsauderspark.ca/)
-   [Vantage College](https://vantagecollege.ubc.ca/frequently-asked-questions)

### Indigenous students

The [First Nations House of Learning](https://fnhl.ubc.ca/longhouse) and [šxʷta:təχʷəm](https://fnhl.ubc.ca/students/sx%ca%b7tat%c9%99%cf%87%ca%b7%c9%99m/) offer additional orientation opportunities and events for Indigenous students\.

### Homecoming

UBC Homecoming is the University’s premier celebration of school spirit for students, alumni, and the neighbouring community\.

Find more information on [UBC Homecoming](https://alumni.ubc.ca/ubc-homecoming/)\.

### Continued connections

If you’re a first year commuter student looking for continued connections with upper\-year peers and other new students, register for [UBC Collegia](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/ubc-collegia)\.

### Visit the New to UBC guide

Find resources and tips to help you get started, stay connected, and navigate online academics during your first year at UBC\.

[Go to the guide](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc)

## About UBC Collegia[https://students\.ubc\.ca/new\-to\-ubc/ubc\-collegia/\#about\-ubc\-collegia](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/ubc-collegia/#about-ubc-collegia)

Are you an incoming first\-year commuter student or Indigenous student?

Collegia offers welcoming, lounge\-like spaces located across the UBC Vancouver campus, perfect for studying, relaxing, or connecting with your peers between classes\. It’s also a community where you can ask questions, get guidance from upper\-year students, and build friendships that can support you throughout your time at UBC\.

[View map of locations](https://www.google.com/maps/d/viewer?mid=1nduxHQ3D_Y83GJf8h6eUPdchoYUiTZ-a&femb=1&ll=49.26642999663815%2C-123.25320005&z=16)

### Collegia programs

There are 2 Collegia programs available at the UBC Vancouver campus:

-   **First Year UBC Collegia**  
    Available to first\-year undergraduate students who don’t live in a UBC residence and have graduated high school within the last 2 years\.
-   **Šxʷta:təχʷəm**  
    For self\-identifying Indigenous graduate and undergraduate students\. By registering, you’ll gain access to both the first\-year Collegia community, as well as the [šxʷta:təχʷəm](https://fnhl.ubc.ca/students/sx%ca%b7tat%c9%99%cf%87%ca%b7%c9%99m/) community\.

## Reasons to join Collegia[https://students\.ubc\.ca/new\-to\-ubc/ubc\-collegia/\#reasons\-to\-join\-collegia](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/ubc-collegia/#reasons-to-join-collegia)

-   **Find community**  
    Join regular small group gatherings to build friendships, ask questions to your peers and upper\-year students, and have fun together at social events\.
-   **Get support from peers**  
    Learn from the experiences of upper\-level student leaders and hear how they’ve navigated their university journey so far\.
-   **Discover resources and opportunities**  
    Explore your interests through involvement opportunities and student resources, all while building your community at university\.

[Embedded content: UBC Collegia: A space for first\-year commuter students](https://www.youtube.com/embed/OQqUx3I3oC8?feature=oembed)

## About the space[https://students\.ubc\.ca/new\-to\-ubc/ubc\-collegia/\#about\-the\-space](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/ubc-collegia/#about-the-space)

Your UBC Collegium is a place where you can take a break between classes to socialize, use a kitchen, or relax in a comfortable, friendly, and welcoming environment\.

Amenities in each space include:

-   Bright, open space with floor\-to\-ceiling windows 
-   Kitchen facilities with an oven, microwaves, refrigerators, small appliances, dishes, and cutlery
-   Study spaces with desks, lamps, and shelves
-   Comfortable lounge chairs, sofas, and fireplace
-   Bathroom and shower facilities with lockers
-   Secure Wifi and plenty of outlets to charge your devices
-   A social area with board games, cards, and activities

## How to join First Year UBC Collegia[https://students\.ubc\.ca/new\-to\-ubc/ubc\-collegia/\#how\-to\-join\-first\-year\-ubc\-collegia](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/ubc-collegia/#how-to-join-first-year-ubc-collegia)

To be eligible for the UBC Collegia program, you must meet the requirements below:

-   You’re in first\-year standing of a direct\-entry undergraduate program at UBC\.
-   You don’t live in UBC residence\.
-   You’ve graduated from high school within the past 2 years\.

If you’re registered for Jump Start 2026, you’ll be automatically enrolled in the year\-long UBC Collegia program\.

While Indigenous students of all years are welcome at [šxʷta:təχʷəm](https://fnhl.ubc.ca/students/sx%ca%b7tat%c9%99%cf%87%ca%b7%c9%99m/) without requiring registration, first\-year Indigenous students who commute to campus are especially encouraged to register for the First Year UBC Collegia program\.

[Register now](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_aa7k0lzQZYtpr1Q)

## UBC Collegia hours[https://students\.ubc\.ca/new\-to\-ubc/ubc\-collegia/\#ubc\-collegia\-hours](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/ubc-collegia/#ubc-collegia-hours)

### First Year Collegia

First Year Collegia is open **Monday to Friday** from 9:00 am to 7:00 pm during the Winter Session \(September to April\)\. These hours may change during exam periods\. First Year Collegia is closed on all [statutory holidays](https://hr.ubc.ca/working-ubc/statutory-holidays) observed by UBC\.

### šxʷta:təχʷəm

šxʷta:təχʷəm is open on weekdays during the Winter Session \(September to April\) except on all [statutory holidays](https://hr.ubc.ca/working-ubc/statutory-holidays) observed by UBC\. The hours below may change during exam periods: 

-   **Mon to Thurs**: 9:30 am to 7:00 pm
-   **Fri**: 9:30 am to 6:00 pm

## Collegia Code of Membership[https://students\.ubc\.ca/new\-to\-ubc/ubc\-collegia/\#collegia\-code\-of\-membership](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/ubc-collegia/#collegia-code-of-membership)

All new Collegia Members must familiarize themselves with the [Collegia Code of Membership](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/ubc_collegia_code_of_membership.pdf) \(pdf\)\. You’re also recommended to review the [UBC First Nations Longhouse Teachings](https://fnhl.ubc.ca/longhouse/)\.

Following both of these documents will help create a welcoming and inclusive shared environment in Collegia\.

## New to UBC guide[https://students\.ubc\.ca/new\-to\-ubc/ubc\-collegia/\#new\-to\-ubc\-guide](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/ubc-collegia/#new-to-ubc-guide)

Learn everything you need to start at UBC\. Check off what you need to do before classes start, get connected to student resources, and more\.

[Go to the guide](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/)

## If you are a graduate student[https://students\.ubc\.ca/new\-to\-ubc/ubc\-collegia/\#if\-you\-are\-a\-graduate\-student](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/ubc-collegia/#if-you-are-a-graduate-student)

You may visit the [Graduate Life Centre or GSS Loft](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/campus-community/graduate-student-spaces) for amenities including self\-serve kitchens with microwaves and kettles, and study spaces\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/new\-to\-ubc/ubc\-collegia/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/ubc-collegia/#if-you-have-questions)

For more information about UBC Collegia, email [collegia\.program@ubc\.ca](mailto:collegia.program@ubc.ca)\.

title: Indigenous Mental Health and Wellbeing program
content_markdown:
## Land acknowledgement[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/indigenous\-mental\-health\-wellbeing\-program/\#land\-acknowledgement](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/indigenous-mental-health-wellbeing-program/#land-acknowledgement)

UBC Student Health and Wellbeing acknowledges with deep respect that the [xʷməθkʷəy̓əm land](https://musqueam.bc.ca/) we work on at UBC is the traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Musqueam people\. We also recognize with gratitude the knowledge systems, ceremonies, and healing traditions of the Musqueam Nation, and other Indigenous people, the First Nations, Métis, and Inuit communities\.

[The Musqueam Post, installed on University Boulevard\. The post tells the story of the two\-headed serpent who shaped the landscape of Musqueam territory, and who is the origin of the name Musqueam\.](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/imhw_land_acknowledgement.jpg)

## About the program[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/indigenous\-mental\-health\-wellbeing\-program/\#about\-the\-program](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/indigenous-mental-health-wellbeing-program/#about-the-program)

Student Health and Wellbeing is committed to a process of Indigenizing and decolonizing mental health services at UBC\. Our work in the Indigenous Mental Health and Wellbeing \(IMHW\) program strives to be respectful of wisdom traditions practiced across our nations and within the individual experiences of Indigenous UBC students\.

We offer many support options to Indigenous UBC students with a focus on helping to identify wellbeing goals encouraging their academic success\.

### What the program offers

-   Free and confidential drop\-in and brief counselling services
-   Planning sessions to help you meet difficult challenges while attending UBC, including how to locate a doctor or find community resources like a daycare
-   Mentoring from professional staff
-   Connections with community resources that encourage wellbeing
-   Facilitation and support of cultural work

## How to access the service[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/indigenous\-mental\-health\-wellbeing\-program/\#how\-to\-access\-the\-service](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/indigenous-mental-health-wellbeing-program/#how-to-access-the-service)

Students who self\-declare as Indigenous, including First Nations \(Status/Non\-Status\), Métis, Inuit, and other Indigenous relations from around the world, are welcome to participate in program services\.

Indigenous self\-identification is voluntary, confidential, and used only to provide you with the relevant services that meet your needs\.

-   **Visit in person  
    **Speak to Welcome Desk staff at the [Gateway Building](https://maps.ubc.ca/?code=GWHB) \(Level 3\) or the [First Nations Longhouse](https://fnhl.ubc.ca/students/advising-counselling/#counsellors)\. Please let the Welcome Desk staff know you are an Indigenous student and would like IMHW support\. IMHW staff members are also available to answer questions or book appointments at FNHL’s [Indigenous Student Lunch Series](https://fnhl.ubc.ca/students/indigenous-student-lunch-series/)\. 
-   **Contact Us**  
    To book an appointment, call [604 822 3811](tel:6048223811) and speak to our Welcome Desk staff for more information\. Please let the staff know you are an Indigenous student and would like IMHW support\. 
-   **Book an appointment online**  
    Select “Counselling – Indigenous” on our [appointment booking system](https://ubcshw.inputhealth.com/ebooking#new) to schedule an appointment with an IMHW team member\. If you are unable to find an appointment, please contact Counselling Services at [604 822 3811](tel:6048223811)\.

If you are a UBC staff member requiring a referral form, please email [indigenouscounselling\.support@ubc\.ca](mailto:indigenouscounselling.support@ubc.ca), or call UBC Counselling Services at [604 822 3811](tel:6048223811) and ask to speak with an Indigenous Mental Health and Wellbeing program staff member\.

[A wooden walkway curving through a dense temperate rainforest\.](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/imhw_how_to_access.jpg)

## Program approach[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/indigenous\-mental\-health\-wellbeing\-program/\#program\-approach](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/indigenous-mental-health-wellbeing-program/#program-approach)

We ground our work within the Mi’kmaq principles of Etuaptmumk or “[Two\-Eyed Seeing](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/pdf/10.1177/1609406918812346)” as shared by Elder Albert Marshall\. This means that we respectfully support both the use of traditional holistic practices, or Indigenous science and knowledge, as well as conventional therapeutic Western counselling techniques\.

The IMHW [Peer Support Program \(PSP\) toolkit](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/imhw_peer_support_program_toolkit.pdf) \(pdf\) was created for use with Indigenous student groups with a particular interest in life promotion and wellbeing\.

### Indigenous Cultural Safety

We are committed to offering culturally safe mental health and support services basing our work on foundational healing values which include cultural humility, a person\-centered approach, trauma\-informed healing work, and continued dedication to improving our services with a lens of self\-reflection\.

Our work is also informed by the following:

-   [United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples \(UNDRIP\)](https://www.un.org/esa/socdev/unpfii/documents/DRIPS_en.pdf) \(pdf\)
-   [Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada Calls to Action](https://nctr.ca/about/history-of-the-trc/truth-and-reconciliation-commission-of-canada/)
-   [In Plain Sight](https://engage.gov.bc.ca/app/uploads/sites/613/2020/11/In-Plain-Sight-Summary-Report.pdf) \(pdf\)
-   [The Final Report of the National Inquiry into Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women and Girls](https://www.mmiwg-ffada.ca/final-report/)
-   [Psychology’s Response to the Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada’s Report](https://cpa.ca/docs/File/Task_Forces/TRC%20Task%20Force%20Report_FINAL.pdf)
-   [UBC Indigenous Strategic Plan](https://isp.ubc.ca/)

## Meet the program staff[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/indigenous\-mental\-health\-wellbeing\-program/\#meet\-the\-program\-staff](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/indigenous-mental-health-wellbeing-program/#meet-the-program-staff)

[Headshot of Hali McLennan](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/indigenous_mental_health_wellbeing_hali_mclennan.jpg)

### Social Work Wellbeing Navigator

**Hali McLennan, MSW, RSW \(she/her/hers\)**

I am a member of the Métis Nation of British Columbia\. I was born in the Yukon but as a child moved to the unceded territories of the Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil\-Waututh\. I completed both of my Social Work degrees at UBC’s School of Social Work and I am grateful to have the chance to support current UBC students through the challenges they may face while at the university\.

[A tree branch dappled with sunlight\. The generic image used for Counselling Services team members who don't have headshots\.](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_services_generic_avatar.jpg)

### Counsellor

**Anne Sinclair, MCP, RCC \(she/her\)**

I am of Peguis First Nation ancestry and have lived experience working in the remote Heiltsuk First Nation community of Bella Bella\. I hold a Master of Counselling Psychology from Adler University and a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology from UBC\. My practice is grounded in a holistic approach that honours mind, body, and spirit, while providing a culturally safe and supportive space for each client\. I draw on Rational Emotive Behaviour Therapy \(REBT\), Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing \(EMDR\), Narrative Therapy, Solutions\-Focused Therapy, and other creative, client\-centred approaches to support personal growth and healing\.

## Additional Indigenous support and crisis resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/indigenous\-mental\-health\-wellbeing\-program/\#additional\-indigenous\-support\-and\-crisis\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/indigenous-mental-health-wellbeing-program/#additional-indigenous-support-and-crisis-resources)

-   [Hope for Wellness Help Line](https://www.hopeforwellness.ca/)  
    Get immediate mental health counselling and crisis intervention by phone \(toll\-free [1\.855\.242\.3310](tel:18552423310)\) or online chat\.
-   [Indian Residential School Crisis Line](https://www.fnha.ca/what-we-do/mental-wellness-and-substance-use/residential-schools#:~:text=National%20Indian%20Residential%20School%20Crisis%20Line)  
    Call toll\-free [1\.866\.925\.4419](tel:18669254419) for 24/7 emotional support available to former Indian residential school students and their families\.
-   [Kuu\-us Crisis Line Society](https://www.kuu-uscrisisline.com/)  
    Get crisis support in British Columbia by calling toll\-free [1\.800\.588\.8717](tel:18005888717)\.
-   [Métis Crisis Line](https://www.wellbeing.gov.bc.ca/resource/metis-crisis-line)  
    Call [1\.833\.638\.4722](tel:18336384722) for immediate help if you are experiencing a crisis, or get help with relationship troubles, depression, anxiety, financial issues, bullying, and more\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/indigenous\-mental\-health\-wellbeing\-program/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/indigenous-mental-health-wellbeing-program/#if-you-have-questions)

Please call [604\.822\.3811](tel:6048223811) and request to speak to an IMHW program staff member\.

title: Awards: scholarships and bursaries
content_markdown:
## Award types[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/\#award\-types](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/#award-types)

UBC and the University’s donors provide a range of financial support to reward your academic and extracurricular achievements and meet your financial needs\.

-   **Scholarships** are merit\-based awards primarily based on academic achievement\. Other merits such as community involvement or athletic achievements may also be considered\.
-   **Hybrid awards** are given based on a combination of academic and/or other achievement and financial need\.
-   **Bursaries** are assessed based on unmet financial need\. Bursaries and student awards based solely on financial need are not shown on a student’s transcript\.
-   **Fellowships** are given at the start of the academic year to a graduate student primarily based on academic achievement, research ability or research potential\.
-   **Medals** are non\-monetary awards given at the end of an academic year to a graduating student, based primarily on academic achievement\.
-   **Prizes** are given to a student at the end of the academic session to recognize performance in a particular course, research performance, or publication record\.

Read the [Academic Calendar](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/university-awards) for how UBC defines different types of awards\.

If you’re a UBC Okanagan student, please refer to the [information](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/finances/financial-support/awards-scholarships-and-prizes/) specific to your campus\.

## Automatic consideration awards[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/\#automatic\-consideration\-awards](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/#automatic-consideration-awards)

Certain awards do not require an application\. As a UBC student, you are automatically considered for the following awards:\.

-   [Student Housing Supplement Grant](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/student-housing-supplement-grant/)  
    Eligible students can receive additional financial support for their first\-year residence experience\.
-   [Trek Excellence Scholarship](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/trek-excellence-scholarship/)  
    Granted to the top continuing domestic students ranked in the top 5% of their year\.

## Apply for an award[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/\#apply\-for\-an\-award](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/#apply-for-an-award)

The following awards are by application only\. Make sure you meet the award requirements and submit your application by the deadline\.

### General awards

Any UBC student who meets the eligibility requirements is invited to apply to these awards\.

| Award | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [UBC Bursary Program](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/) | Designed to support students with unmet financial need |
| [Affiliation Bursaries](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/affiliation-bursaries/) | Based on financial need and for students connected to a specific club or group |
| [Affiliation scholarships](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/affiliation-scholarships/) | Based on merit such as academic achievement, community involvement, or leadership, for students in a specific club or group |
| [Faculty recommended awards](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/faculty-recommended-awards/) | Merit\-based awards are presented for strong academic performance and community leadership, usually requiring an application to assess award eligibility |
| [John R\. Scarfo Wellness Bursary](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/john-r-scarfo-wellness-bursary/) | Available for students who demonstrate a financial need and a commitment to a healthy lifestyle |
| [Premier Undergraduate and Wesbrook Scholarship](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/premier-undergraduate-wesbrook-scholarships/) | Awarded to senior students with outstanding academics, leadership, and community involvement |
| [Rhodes Scholarship](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/rhodes-scholarship/) | 11 Canadians are selected each year to join a class of 84 Scholars at the University of Oxford |
| [McCall MacBain Scholarship](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/mccall-macbain-scholarship/) | Leadership\-drive scholarship open to graduate students in a master’s program at McGill University |
| [3M National Student Fellowship](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/3m-national-student-fellowship/) | Honours 10 full\-time diploma and undergraduate students at Canadian post\-secondary institutions demonstrating outstanding leadership |

### Awards for specific student groups

These awards are available for specific groups of students who meet additional requirements\.

| Award | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [Awards for Indigenous students](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-indigenous/) | Non\-repayable scholarships and bursaries for First Nations, Métis, or Inuit students |
| [Musqueam First Nation Scholarship](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/musqueam-first-nation-scholarship/) | Renewable scholarship valued up to $5,500 annually for Musqueam students |
| [Women in part\-time studies](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-women-part-time-studies/) | Available to women studying on a part\-time basis |
| [Students participating in Go Global](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/new-programs-ubc-students/new-student-resources/awards-students-participating-go-global) | Available to UBC students in Go Global International Learning Programs |
| [Students with disabilities](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-disabilities/) | Need\- and merit\-based awards for students with disabilities |
| [International student awards](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-international/) | For outstanding international undergraduate students at the UBC Vancouver campus |
| [Graduate student awards](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/scholarships-awards-funding) | Merit\-based awards for students in graduate programs |
| [Funding for former youth in care](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/funding-former-youth-care/) | Tuition waivers or funds for former youth in care |
| [Funding for Canadian Veterans](https://www.veterans.gc.ca/eng/education-and-jobs/back-to-school/education-training-benefit) | Financial help for individuals planning to return to school after a career in the military |

## External awards[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/\#external\-awards](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/#external-awards)

Organizations and groups outside of UBC also offer [external awards](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/external-awards/) for post\-secondary students\.

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/#additional-resources)

-   [Special circumstances for students receiving awards](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/special-circumstances-receiving-awards/)
-   [Maintaining awards and loan eligibility](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/maintaining-awards-loan-eligibility/)
-   [Financial planning](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/)
-   [Direct deposit](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/setting-up-your-direct-deposit/)
-   [Taxes](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/#if-you-have-questions)

**Vancouver Students**: Please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

**Okanagan Students**: Please contact [Enrolment Services Advising](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/advising/)\.

title: 3M National Student Fellowship
content_markdown:
## About the award[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/3m\-national\-student\-fellowship/\#about\-the\-award](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/3m-national-student-fellowship/#about-the-award)

The [3M National Student Fellowship](https://www.stlhe.ca/awards/3m-national-student-fellowship/) honours up to 10 full\-time diploma and undergraduate students at Canadian post\-secondary institutions who have demonstrated outstanding leadership and innovation in their lives and at their college or university\. These students embrace a vision of quality education that enhances their academic experience and beyond\.  Awards are coordinated through the Society for Teaching and Learning in Higher Education \(STLHE\)\.

The award consists of:

-   An award of $2,000
-   Certificate and recognition at the annual Society for Teaching and Learning in Higher Education \(STLHE\) conference in June, to participate in a 3M National Student Fellows Conference Summit
-   Coverage of all costs for conference registration, travel, and accommodation to attend the annual STLHE conference
-   2\-year membership to the Society for Teaching and Learning in Higher Education
-   Letter from STLHE President and 3M Canada to their identified institutional leader and to the individual awarded
-   Recognition in STLHE and 3M Canada social media, and partnering media, such as Maclean’s and University Affairs

## Eligibility requirements[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/3m\-national\-student\-fellowship/\#eligibility\-requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/3m-national-student-fellowship/#eligibility-requirements)

You must meet all of the following requirements before applying:

-   You’re enrolled full\-time in an undergraduate degree or college program at a post\-secondary Canadian institution, as defined by UBC\.
-   You’ve completed at least 1 full term of study at the time of nomination\.
-   You have not previously received a 3M student fellowship\.

In recognition of the systemic conditions of disadvantage in higher education and society, the Society for Teaching and Learning in Higher Education \(STLHE\) encourages nominations of members of groups that have been historically disadvantaged and marginalized, including First Nations, Métis, and Inuit peoples, Indigenous peoples of North America, racialized persons, persons with disabilities, and those who identify as women and/or 2SLGBTQI\.

## Application timeline[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/3m\-national\-student\-fellowship/\#application\-timeline](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/3m-national-student-fellowship/#application-timeline)

- **Row 1**

  - **Header cell 1:**
  
    Time period
  
  - **Header cell 2:**
  
    Description

- **Row 2**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Early November 2025 to January 2026
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Applications usually open in mid\-fall and close in January 2026\. Check the [STLHE website](https://www.stlhe.ca/3mnsf-deadlines-submission-requirements-and-timelines/) for yearly deadlines\.

- **Row 3**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Early January 2026
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    3 weeks before the award deadline, applicants must submit their completed application package, transcript, and letters of nomination and support to the VP Students Office for review\.  
      
    Applications will be reviewed within 10 to 14 days\. A statement from the VP Students Office will be provided to all students who meet the eligibility criteria set out by STHLE\. You may also receive feedback on ways you can strengthen your application\.  
      
    Students can then add the VP Students statement to their application package and submit the full application directly to STLHE\.

- **Row 4**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    April 2026
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Winners are contacted by the 3M and STLHE Presidents\. Unsuccessful nominees will also be informed by email\.

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/3m\-national\-student\-fellowship/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/3m-national-student-fellowship/#how-to-apply)

To apply, you will need the following: 

-   Your completed application
-   A nomination letter and additional letters of support
-   A copy of your transcript
-   A statement from the UBC VP Students \(Vancouver students\) or
-   A statement from the Associate VP, Students, UBC Okanagan \(Okanagan students\)

Visit the [STLHE website](https://www.stlhe.ca/awards/3m-national-student-fellowship/) for more information and detailed instructions on applying for this award\.

Submit your completed application by email for review and to request your statement letter:

-   Okanagan students: [avps\.ok@ubc\.ca](mailto:avps.ok@ubc.ca)
-   Vancouver students: [vpsassist@mail\.ubc\.ca](mailto:vpsassist@mail.ubc.ca)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/3m\-national\-student\-fellowship/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/3m-national-student-fellowship/#if-you-have-questions)

If you have questions about the award criteria, procedures, or eligibility, please review the [frequently asked questions](https://www.stlhe.ca/frequently-asked-questions/) about the fellowship or contact the 3M National Student Fellowship Program Coordinator at [3mnsf@stlhe\.ca](mailto:3mnsf@stlhe.ca)\.

title: Affiliation bursaries
content_markdown:
## About the bursaries[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/affiliation\-bursaries/\#about\-the\-bursaries](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/affiliation-bursaries/#about-the-bursaries)

Affiliation bursaries are based on financial need and require that students be connected to a specific group, such as:

-   Clubs
-   Trade unions
-   Companies
-   Geographic regions
-   Demographic groups

Some bursaries are open to students at other British Columbia universities and colleges\. Students enrolled in Certificate Programs, Diploma Programs, and other Non\-Degree Studies categories \(including Unclassified, Visiting, and Access Studies\) are **not** eligible\.

**If you are applying as a non\-UBC student,** please read the award descriptions carefully to determine your eligibility and follow the application process below\.

[Read award descriptions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/affiliation-bursaries/descriptions-affiliation-bursaries/)

## Eligibility requirements[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/affiliation\-bursaries/\#eligibility\-requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/affiliation-bursaries/#eligibility-requirements)

To be considered for an affiliation bursary, you must meet **all** the following requirements:

-   You are a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or have refugee status\.
-   You are not enrolled in a Certificate Program, Diploma Program, or other Non\-Degree Studies categories, including Unclassified, Visiting, and Access Studies\.
-   You meet the requirements and apply for the [UBC Bursary](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/) by the deadline\.
-   You can demonstrate financial need\.
-   You are enrolled in a full\-time [course load](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/course-load-guide/)\.
-   You meet the eligibility requirements as outlined in [UBC’s Regulations Governing University Award](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/university-awards)\.
-   You are receiving full\-time Canadian government student loans for a study period that is a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks in length and matches the period for which you’re applying for bursary support\.
-   You have received confirmation of enrolment for your Canadian government student loan by the bursary deadline\.
-   You have an assessed unmet financial need using UBC’s Common Assessment Mechanism, which is based on [StudentAid BC](https://studentaidbc.ca/) policies\.

### Additional requirements

Some awards have additional eligibility requirements or are only open to students attending a specific campus or post\-secondary institution\.

Please review each [award description](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/affiliation-bursaries/descriptions-affiliation-bursaries/) carefully to make sure you meet the eligibility criteria and can get the supporting documentation\.

## Before you apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/affiliation\-bursaries/\#before\-you\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/affiliation-bursaries/#before-you-apply)

You can find detailed instructions on the application form but before you start, make sure you:

1.  Meet all general and specific eligibility requirements for applicable awards\.
2.  Read each [award description](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/affiliation-bursaries/descriptions-affiliation-bursaries/) carefully, as they all require different supporting documents\. You will be required to upload your supporting documentation before you can submit your completed application\.
3.  Apply for the [UBC Bursary](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/) by the deadline\.

### Non\-UBC post\-secondary students

You do **not** need to apply for the UBC Bursary\. Instead you will need to prepare the following financial items for your online application:

-   Taxes
-   Income
-   Assets
-   Resources
-   Student loan assessment
-   Official transcript
-   Estimated costs for the upcoming school year

title: Affiliation scholarships
content_markdown:
## About the scholarships[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/affiliation\-scholarships/\#about\-the\-scholarships](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/affiliation-scholarships/#about-the-scholarships)

Affiliation scholarships are based on merit such as academic achievement, community involvement, or leadership, and require that students be connected to a specific group, such as:

-   Clubs
-   Trade unions
-   Companies
-   Geographic regions
-   Demographic groups

Some awards are open to students at other British Columbia universities and colleges\.

If you are applying as a **non\-UBC student,** please read the award descriptions carefully to determine your eligibility and follow the application process below\.

Apply only for awards you are eligible for\. Applying for scholarships you do not qualify for may delay the review of your application\.

[Read award descriptions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/affiliation-scholarships/descriptions-affiliation-scholarships/)

## Eligibility requirements[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/affiliation\-scholarships/\#eligibility\-requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/affiliation-scholarships/#eligibility-requirements)

You must meet all the following requirements to apply:

### UBC Vancouver Campus students

-   You must have been registered in **at least** 24 percentage\-graded credits in the prior Winter Session\.
-   You must be registered in **at least** 24 percentage\-graded credits in the upcoming Winter Session\.
-   You must have an average of **at least** 75% with no failed or incomplete courses\.
-   You must meet the terms for awards eligibility set out in [UBC’s Regulations Governing University Awards](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/university-awards)\.
-   Incoming first\-year Post\-secondary students will be reviewed based on their high school transcript submitted to UBC Undergraduate Admissions\.

Courses in Pass/Fail or Credit/D/Fail format are not taken into account, except Doctor of Dental Medicine \(DMD\) or Doctor of Medicine \(MD\) courses\.

### UBC Okanagan Campus students

-   You must have been registered in **at least** 24 percentage\-graded credits in the prior Winter Session\.
-   You must be registered in **at least** 24 percentage\-graded credits in the upcoming Winter Session\.
-   You must have an average of **at least** 75% with no failed or incomplete courses\.
-   You must meet the terms for awards eligibility set out in UBC Okanagan Campus Minimum Scholarship [Course Load Requirements](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/finances/financial-support/awards-scholarships-and-prizes/minimum-course-load-requirements/)\.
-   Incoming first\-year Post\-secondary students will be reviewed based on their high school transcript submitted to UBC Undergraduate Admissions\.

Courses in Pass/Fail or Credit/D/Fail format are not considered, except Doctor of Dental Medicine \(DMD\) or Doctor of Medicine \(MD\) courses\.

### Non\-UBC Post\-secondary students

-   You must have been registered in **at least** 24 percentage\-graded credits for your program during the previous academic year between September and April\.
-   You must be registered in **at least** 24 percentage\-graded credits at your institution during the upcoming academic year between September and April\.
-   You must have an average of **at least** 75% with no failed or incomplete courses\.
-   You must provide an official transcript showing your academic records for the 2025/26 academic year as well as proof of registration for the upcoming 2026/27 academic year\.
-   First\-year post\-secondary students must also upload their official high school record showing proof of high school graduation and final grades for Grade 11 and 12\.

Courses in Pass/Fail or Credit/D/Fail format are not considered\.

### Additional requirements

Some awards have additional eligibility requirements or are only open to students attending a specific campus or post\-secondary institution\.

Please review each [award description](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/affiliation-scholarships/descriptions-affiliation-scholarships/) carefully to ensure you meet the eligibility criteria and can obtain supporting documentation\.

## Before you apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/affiliation\-scholarships/\#before\-you\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/affiliation-scholarships/#before-you-apply)

Detailed instructions are provided on the application form, but before you start your application, make sure you complete the following:

1.  Meet all general and specific eligibility requirements for the scholarship you are applying to\.
2.  Read each [award description](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/affiliation-scholarships/descriptions-affiliation-scholarships/) carefully because they all require different supporting documentation before you are able to submit your completed application\.

title: Awards for students with disabilities
content_markdown:
## About the awards[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/awards\-disabilities/\#about\-the\-awards](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-disabilities/#about-the-awards)

Awards of different values and eligibility criteria are available for students with disabilities\.

-   **Scholarships** are based on academic achievement, community involvement, or leadership\. 
-   **Bursaries** are based on demonstrated financial need\. 

[Read award descriptions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-disabilities/descriptions-awards-disabilities/)

### Disability programs

British Columbia \(BC\) residents who are student loan approved and have a disability are encouraged to submit a [Disability Programs Application to Student Aid BC](https://studentaidbc.ca/explore/grants-scholarships/bc-access-grant-students-disabilities)\. Once approved, you may be eligible for grants, additional financial support for services and equipment, and a reduced course load\.

The application process for disability programs is different in each province\. Contact your home province loan provider to ensure that you are submitting the correct information and forms\. 

## Eligibility requirements[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/awards\-disabilities/\#eligibility\-requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-disabilities/#eligibility-requirements)

You must meet all the following requirements to apply:

-   You are a Canadian citizen or permanent resident\.
-   You are a UBC Vancouver student with a disability\.
-   You’re considered a full\-time student \(or approved by the Centre for Accessibility to study at a reduced course load\)\.
-   You meet the terms for awards eligibility set out in [UBC’s Regulations Governing University Awards](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/university-awards)\.
-   If you are not registered with the Centre for Accessibility, you must also provide supporting documentation\.

Each scholarship or bursary has additional eligibility requirements such as financial need, nature of disability, or demonstrated merit\. Read the [award descriptions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-disabilities/descriptions-awards-disabilities/) to determine your eligibility for specific awards\.

If you are a part\-time student and you have a disability that causes you to take a reduced [course load](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/course-load-guide/), you may be considered for awards even if you registered for fewer than 24 credits per academic year\.

For more information, contact an advisor from the [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/)\.

## Before you apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/awards\-disabilities/\#before\-you\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-disabilities/#before-you-apply)

Detailed instructions are provided on the application form, but before you start your application, make sure you complete the following:

1.  Read through the [award descriptions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-disabilities/descriptions-awards-disabilities/) to view specific eligibility criteria\.
2.  To be considered for a bursary, you must apply for the [UBC Bursary program](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/) by Sep 15, 2026\.
3.  If you aren’t registered with the Centre for Accessibility, you’ll need to provide medical documentation to confirm your eligibility for award consideration\. Email your documentation before Sep 29, 2026 to [info\.accessibility@ubc\.ca](mailto:info.accessibility@ubc.ca)\. All medical information received by the Centre will be treated as confidential\.

## Application timeline[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/awards\-disabilities/\#application\-timeline](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-disabilities/#application-timeline)

| Description | Date |
| --- | --- |
| Applications open | Wed, Jul 15, 2026 |
| Applications close | Tues, Sep 15, 2026 |

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/awards\-disabilities/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-disabilities/#how-to-apply)

Submit your application online during the application period\.

[Apply online](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_56iaPu39O1rCRAG)

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/awards\-disabilities/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-disabilities/#additional-resources)

-   [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/)
-   [National Educational Association of Disabled Students \(NEADS\)](http://www.neads.ca/)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/awards\-disabilities/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-disabilities/#if-you-have-questions)

For help with finances, registration, records, and more, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

You can also connect with the [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/) for disability\-related accommodations and programming initiatives\.

title: Awards for Indigenous students
content_markdown:
## UBC Awards for Indigenous Students[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/awards\-indigenous/\#ubc\-awards\-for\-indigenous\-students](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-indigenous/#ubc-awards-for-indigenous-students)

The UBC Awards for Indigenous Students include scholarships and bursaries\. When a student applies for these awards, they are considered for both merit and need\-based awards\.

-   Scholarships are awards that recognize academic, community, or athletic achievement\.
-   Bursaries are based on financial need\. Student awards based solely on financial need are not included on your official transcript\.

You can find a full list of how UBC defines different types of awards in the [Academic Calendar](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/university-awards)\. There are also external scholarships and bursaries available for Indigenous students outlined on the page below\.

[Read UBC Indigenous award descriptions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-indigenous/descriptions-awards-indigenous/)

## Eligibility requirements[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/awards\-indigenous/\#eligibility\-requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-indigenous/#eligibility-requirements)

To be considered for UBC Indigenous awards, you must meet all the following requirements:

-   You are a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or have refugee status\.
-   You are an Indigenous student and have [self\-identified in Workday](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/personal-information/updating-your-indigenous-self-identification/)\. 
-   You will submit the application for intended Indigenous awards by the award program deadline\.
-   You are enrolled in a full\-time [course load](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/course-load-guide/) studying on the Vancouver campus\.
-   You meet the eligibility requirements as outlined in [UBC’s Regulations Governing University Awards](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/university-awards)\.
-   You demonstrate financial need to be considered for bursaries\. 

Unclassified or qualifying students are not eligible for these awards\. Read through the [Academic Calendar information](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/admissions/classification-students) on the classification of students\.

UBC uses the term “Indigenous” in place of “Aboriginal” as held in the spirit of its use in section 35\(2\) of the Canadian Constitution, to refer inclusively to members of First Nations, status and non\-status, treaty and non\-treaty Indians, Métis, and Inuit peoples in Canada, recognizing that many people prefer the terms that are specific and traditional to their communities\.

### Additional requirements

Some awards have additional requirements, which are listed in the application\. Please read the [award descriptions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-indigenous/descriptions-awards-indigenous/) before you start your application, to better target the awards you qualify for\.

If you are eligible for bursaries, submit an application to the [UBC Bursary Program](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/) by the deadline to be considered for UBC General Bursary at the same time\. Application to the general bursary program at UBC is helpful in determining your financial need\. An application to the UBC Bursary Program **is not required** for your application to UBC Awards for Indigenous Students\.

## Before you apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/awards\-indigenous/\#before\-you\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-indigenous/#before-you-apply)

There are detailed instructions on the application form\. Follow these steps before you apply:

1.  Make sure you meet all [general and specific eligibility requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-indigenous/descriptions-awards-indigenous/) for applicable awards\.
2.  Prepare written statements describing your personal situation, financial need, and connection to any Indigenous UBC campus communities\. Include any additional information for specific awards as requested\.
3.  If you are applying for bursaries, consider applying for the [UBC Bursary Program](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/) before the deadline\. Application to this program helps establish your financial need\. but is **not required** to apply for UBC Indigenous Awards\.

## Application timeline[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/awards\-indigenous/\#application\-timeline](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-indigenous/#application-timeline)

| Description | Date |
| --- | --- |
| Applications open | Sat, Aug 15, 2026 |
| Applications close | Fri, Oct 16, 2026 |

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/awards\-indigenous/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-indigenous/#how-to-apply)

Submit your application online during the application period\.

[Apply online](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_9XlM2YQS4q5Be8m)

## External awards for Indigenous students[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/awards\-indigenous/\#external\-awards\-for\-indigenous\-students](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-indigenous/#external-awards-for-indigenous-students)

In addition to UBC Awards for Indigenous Students, there are scholarships and bursaries available from non\-profit organizations, private companies, and other award search portals\. Visit the specific award pages linked below for details, deadlines, and how to apply\.

Some awards may require a personal statement or a short essay describing why you are a suitable candidate\. Many may be based on your financial need, academic merit, or both\. View the list of awards below in order of application deadline\.
