title: Awards for international students
content_markdown:
## Entrance awards[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/awards\-international/\#entrance\-awards](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-international/#entrance-awards)

If you’re an international student applying to UBC, there are scholarships, awards, and other financial support available to you\.

[Find awards](http://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/scholarships-awards-international-students/)

## International Community Achievement Awards[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/awards\-international/\#international\-community\-achievement\-awards](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-international/#international-community-achievement-awards)

The International Community Achievement Award recognizes international students who contribute to our campus and communities while maintaining strong academic standing\.

Awards up to $10,000 each are available to continuing international undergraduate students who have demonstrated leadership in one or more of the following areas:

-   Community service
-   International engagement
-   Intercultural understanding
-   Promotion of diversity
-   Intellectual, artistic, or athletic pursuits
-   Other campus activities

## Eligibility requirements[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/awards\-international/\#eligibility\-requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-international/#eligibility-requirements)

You must meet all the following requirements to apply:

-   You must be a continuing international student in a four\-year undergraduate degree program at UBC’s Vancouver campus\.
-   You must be studying on a Canadian study permit and paying international undergraduate tuition and fees\.
-   You must have been registered at the Vancouver campus for the previous Winter Session\.
-   You must be registered for the current Winter Session\. Students registered in a Go Global Program or Co\-operative Education are eligible to apply\.

To retain eligibility for international student awards, students should be continuing as an international student\. Change in citizenship status or tuition fee rate will affect award eligibility and may result in recovery of award funding\.

## Application timeline[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/awards\-international/\#application\-timeline](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-international/#application-timeline)

| Description | Date |
| --- | --- |
| Applications open | Mon, June 15, 2026 |
| Applications close at **11:59 pm PT** | Thur, Oct 1, 2026 |

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/awards\-international/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-international/#how-to-apply)

Submit your application for the scholarship online during the application period\.

[Apply online](https://undergraduatescholarships.ubc.ca/prog/2026_international_community_achievement_award_icaa_/)

## Recommended awards[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/awards\-international/\#recommended\-awards](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-international/#recommended-awards)

Thanks to the generosity of external donors and UBC faculties, UBC offers many awards to undergraduate students after their first year of study\. These awards may be in the form of scholarships, prizes, fellowships, and more\.

Individual faculties are responsible for recommending their students for these awards\. Their recommendations are based on a range of factors, such as academic achievement, leadership, UBC involvement, and participation on varsity athletic teams\.

International students must pay the international rate for tuition in order to be considered for any award, scholarship, or funding opportunities for international students\.

[Get details](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/faculty-recommended-awards/)

## Tax information[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/awards\-international/\#tax\-information](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-international/#tax-information)

If you receive an award, you’re required to submit a T4A form at tax time\.

Make sure your [Social Insurance Number](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/) \(SIN\) or your [Individual Tax Number](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/individual-tax-number-itn/) \(ITN\) is updated on Workday as soon as possible so UBC can process your T4A form\. 

If you haven’t applied for your SIN or ITN, do so as early as possible\. It can take 2 months to process your ITN\.

## International Student Guide[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/awards\-international/\#international\-student\-guide](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-international/#international-student-guide)

Find everything you need to know about life as an international student at UBC’s Vancouver campus\.

[View the guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/awards\-international/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-international/#if-you-have-questions)

For help with finances, registration, records, and more, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

You can connect with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for questions related to immigration, health insurance, and life as an international student in Canada\.

title: Awards for women in part-time studies

## About the awards[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/awards\-women\-part\-time\-studies/\#about\-the\-awards](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-women-part-time-studies/#about-the-awards)

Scholarships are available for female\-identifying students on the Vancouver campus enrolled in part\-time studies for both the previous and upcoming Winter Sessions\. The Winter Session is from September to April\.

[Read award descriptions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-women-part-time-studies/description-awards-women-part-time-studies/)

You must meet all of the following requirements to apply:

### Undergraduate students

-   You must be registered in 23 credits or less in the upcoming Winter Session\.
-   You must have been studying part\-time during the past academic year\.

### Graduate students

-   You must be paying [part\-time fees](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/prospective-students/tuition-fees-cost-living/graduate-tuition-fees) in the upcoming Winter Session\.

title: John R. Scarfo Wellness Bursary
content_markdown:
## About the bursary[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/john\-r\-scarfo\-wellness\-bursary/\#about\-the\-bursary](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/john-r-scarfo-wellness-bursary/#about-the-bursary)

The John R\. Scarfo Wellness bursary has been made available through an endowment established by Dr\. John R\. Scarfo for students who have demonstrated financial need and are committed to a healthy lifestyle\. Successful applicants will demonstrate a commitment to health as described in the eligibility requirements below\.

Dr\. Scarfo came from a family with 12 children and would not have been able to receive his MD at UBC without the generosity of Dean Walter Gage\. Having been the recipient of the generosity of others, Dr\. Scarfo wishes to support UBC students and honour those who had supported him\. These bursaries are adjudicated by Enrolment Services\.

## Eligibility requirements[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/john\-r\-scarfo\-wellness\-bursary/\#eligibility\-requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/john-r-scarfo-wellness-bursary/#eligibility-requirements)

You must meet all the following requirements to apply:

-   You must be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident\.
-   You must be considered a [full\-time student](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/course-load-guide/)\.
-   You must meet the terms for awards eligibility set out in [UBC’s Regulations Governing University Awards](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/university-awards)\.
-   You must demonstrate unmet financial need based on [UBC’s Common Assessment Mechanism](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/)\.
-   You must meet the eligibility requirements and submit an application to the [UBC Bursary Program](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/) by Sept 15, 2026\.
-   You must prepare a statement \(max 150 words\) demonstrating your commitment to health and wellness in your daily life\. Examples may include, but are not limited to:
    -   Leading a balanced and healthy lifestyle and communicating a clear vision for what this means\.
    -   Demonstrating one or more of the multiple aspects of healthy living, including social, environmental, mental, emotional, physical, and spiritual\.
    -   Identifying the damaging effects of the use of tobacco or illicit drugs on an individual’s or the general public’s health and wellbeing\.
    -   Providing leadership in wellbeing promotion\.

## Before you apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/john\-r\-scarfo\-wellness\-bursary/\#before\-you\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/john-r-scarfo-wellness-bursary/#before-you-apply)

Before you start your application, make sure you complete the following:

1.  Review the eligibility requirements for the John R\. Scarfo Wellness Bursary outlined above\.
2.  Prepare a 150\-word \(max\) Personal Statement explaining your commitment to health and wellness to the selection committee\.
    -   Your Personal Statement should define what health and wellness means to you and how you strive to lead a personally healthy lifestyle or promote healthy living in your community\. Health can be related to your social, environmental, emotional, physical, or spiritual wellbeing\. 
    -   **Your Statement should identify your single most meaningful commitment or contribution to health and wellness** which could can include personal commitments, leadership roles, promotion activities, club participations, academic projects and/or research, sports and recreation/active engagement, volunteer and/or work experiences\., as well as your goals for the future\.
    -   Your statement should articulate how you work towards integrating your belief system in your own life and the lives of others\.

## Application timeline[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/john\-r\-scarfo\-wellness\-bursary/\#application\-timeline](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/john-r-scarfo-wellness-bursary/#application-timeline)

| Description | Date |
| --- | --- |
| Applications open | Fri, Aug 14, 2026 |
| Applications close | Tues, Sep 15, 2026 |

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/john\-r\-scarfo\-wellness\-bursary/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/john-r-scarfo-wellness-bursary/#how-to-apply)

The John R\. Scarfo Wellness Bursary application is part of the General Bursary program\. Apply and check your eligibility for the [UBC General Bursary](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/) during the application period between **Aug 14, 2026** and **Sep 15, 2026**\.

In the section, “Personal Interests and Community Participation” in the General Bursary application, clearly write “SCARFO” followed by your Personal Statement \(maximum 150 words\)\.

If you have already submitted your General Bursary application, you can log back in and edit your application to add your statement and re\-submit it during the application period by **Tues, Sep 15, 2026**\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/john\-r\-scarfo\-wellness\-bursary/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/john-r-scarfo-wellness-bursary/#if-you-have-questions)

**Vancouver Students**: Please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

**Okanagan Students**: Please contact [Enrolment Services Advising](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/advising/)\.

title: McCall MacBain Scholarship
content_markdown:
## About the scholarship[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/mccall\-macbain\-scholarship/\#about\-the\-scholarship](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/mccall-macbain-scholarship/#about-the-scholarship)

The McCall MacBain Scholarship is Canada’s first comprehensive, leadership\-driven scholarship to support graduate students enrolled in a master’s program at McGill University\. Current undergraduate students are invited to apply\.

The scholarship will cover your tuition and fees for a [full\-time master’s program](https://www.mcgill.ca/gradapplicants/programs) or a second\-entry professional undergraduate program such as dentistry, law, or medicine at McGill University\. You will also receive a living stipend of $2,300 per month during academic terms\.

Watch the video below where McCall MacBain Scholars discuss what it’s like to study at McGill University in Montréal, Québec\. The video features Julian Lam, a UBC scholar and recipient of the scholarship\.

[Embedded content: Hear from Scholars: Why McGill and Montréal?](https://www.youtube.com/embed/FcjLmp7hsKI?feature=oembed&enablejsapi=1&origin=https://students.ubc.ca)

## Eligibility requirements[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/mccall\-macbain\-scholarship/\#eligibility\-requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/mccall-macbain-scholarship/#eligibility-requirements)

You must meet all the following requirements to apply:

-   You are in good academic standing and have good overall conduct\.
-   You are enrolled in an undergraduate degree or are on track to complete your undergraduate degree by August 2027\.
-   After applying for the scholarship, you must apply for full\-time enrolment in an eligible master’s or professional program at McGill for Summer or Fall 2027\.

## Before you apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/mccall\-macbain\-scholarship/\#before\-you\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/mccall-macbain-scholarship/#before-you-apply)

You can find detailed instructions on the application form\. Before you start, make sure you complete the following:

1.  Attend an online information session to learn more about the scholarship\.
2.  Prepare the following items for your online application:
    -   Two reference letters
    -   Official transcript
    -   Personal statement
    -   Short essays reflecting on your community and goals, a significant leadership experience, a significant volunteer contribution, and a “course correction”
    -   A list of your community and work experiences, as well as your extracurricular activities

After the application period, successful candidates will be invited to a regional interview, followed by a final interview in Montréal\. Your travel for the final interviews is funded\.

### Current students and alumni

If you are a current student at UBC or you graduated in 2021 or later, you must earn the endorsement of your institution\.

At minimum, a university representative will review your application once it is submitted through the [McCall MacBain Scholarship website](https://mccallmacbainscholars.org/) and verify your academic standing and overall conduct\.

## Application timeline[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/mccall\-macbain\-scholarship/\#application\-timeline](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/mccall-macbain-scholarship/#application-timeline)

Students are responsible for applying to the program\(s\) of their choice by the first possible deadline and gaining admission\.  
  
The graduate program application is separate from this scholarship application\.

| Date | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Mon, Jun 1, 2026 | Applications open |
| Wed, Sep 23, 2026 | Applications close |
| November 2026 | Regional interviews for successful applicants |
| March 2027 | Final interviews for shortlisted students |

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/mccall\-macbain\-scholarship/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/mccall-macbain-scholarship/#how-to-apply)

Applications are now closed for 2026\. Check back in June 2026 for updates on the 2027 application process\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/mccall\-macbain\-scholarship/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/mccall-macbain-scholarship/#if-you-have-questions)

Please email [info@mccallmacbainscholars\.org](mailto:info@mccallmacbainscholars.org) and include your full name and student number\.

title: Musqueam First Nation Scholarship
content_markdown:
## About the scholarship[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/musqueam\-first\-nation\-scholarship/\#about\-the\-scholarship](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/musqueam-first-nation-scholarship/#about-the-scholarship)

To acknowledge the strong relationship UBC has with the Musqueam First Nation, the President’s Office has created a community\-based scholarship for Indigenous students\.

Valued up to $5,500 annually and renewable for up to four years, the scholarship supports students from the Musqueam First Nation studying at UBC in their undergraduate, post baccalaureate \(including Medicine, Dentistry, Law, Education, Pharmacy, Nursing, Midwifery, and Social Work\), and graduate studies\. 

Recipients will have demonstrated academic and leadership achievements including, but not limited to, engagement in the arts, athletics, school, and/or their community\. Recipients will be selected on their ability to demonstrate their openness to continuing to learn who they are, where they come from, and their responsibility in enriching and carrying knowledge forward in their community and the world\.

View other [awards for Indigenous students](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-indigenous/) you may be eligible for\.

## Eligibility requirements[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/musqueam\-first\-nation\-scholarship/\#eligibility\-requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/musqueam-first-nation-scholarship/#eligibility-requirements)

You must meet all of the following requirements to be eligible to apply:

-   You are a Canadian citizen or permanent resident\.
-   You are an Indigenous student who is an enrolled member of the Musqueam First Nation\.
-   You are a newly admitted or continuing student in an undergraduate, graduate or post\-baccalaureate program at UBC\.
-   You meet the eligibility requirements as outlined in [UBC’s Regulations Governing University Awards](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/university-awards)\.

UBC uses the term “Indigenous” in lieu of “Aboriginal” in the spirit of its use in section 35\(2\) of the Canadian Constitution, to refer inclusively to members of First Nations, status and non\-status, treaty and non\-treaty Indians, Métis, and Inuit peoples in Canada, recognizing in doing so that many people prefer the terms that are specific and traditional to their communities\.

## Before you apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/musqueam\-first\-nation\-scholarship/\#before\-you\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/musqueam-first-nation-scholarship/#before-you-apply)

In the application, you’ll need to prepare the following information for the application:

1.  A 500 to 750 word personal statement outlining how you demonstrate your openness to continuing to learn who you are, where you come from, and your responsibility in enriching and carrying knowledge forward in your community and the world\.
2.  Two community references who can speak to the award description\. You’ll be asked to provide their name and contact information including email and phone number\.
3.  Permission in writing for UBC to provide the Musqueam First Nation with your application for the final selection\.

## Application timeline[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/musqueam\-first\-nation\-scholarship/\#application\-timeline](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/musqueam-first-nation-scholarship/#application-timeline)

| Description | Date |
| --- | --- |
| Applications open | Wed, Jul 1, 2026 |
| Applications close | Tues, Sep 15, 2026 |

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/musqueam\-first\-nation\-scholarship/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/musqueam-first-nation-scholarship/#how-to-apply)

Submit your application online during the application period\.

[Apply online](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_ezntr2gV6iEjm3X)

## Band sponsorship[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/musqueam\-first\-nation\-scholarship/\#band\-sponsorship](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/musqueam-first-nation-scholarship/#band-sponsorship)

### Third\-party billing

If you are an Indigenous student and are thinking about how to finance your education, you might consider [band sponsorship](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-support-indigenous/)\. Depending on your band, sponsorship can cover some costs and not others\.

One common type of sponsorship is band funding for tuition, also known as third\-party billing, where your band office provides your tuition and fee payments directly to UBC through Enrolment Services\.

If you are considering band sponsorship, always **be aware of deadlines** for your band office and UBC Enrolment Services\. For more information, read about third\-party billing\.

If you are already receiving band sponsorship, it’s important to make sure you understand the type of sponsorship you are receiving and any restrictions on it\.

[View sponsorship details](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/sponsorship-billing/)

### Things to consider

-   **Housing**  
    If you are receiving band funding for 4 years of on\-campus housing, one question to ask your band is whether you could still be funded if you chose to live off\-campus\.
-   **If you are in a co\-op program**  
    If you are participating in a co\-op program and need an additional year to finish your degree, check with your band about continued funding for your fifth and last year, or if this makes you ineligible for continued sponsorship\.
-   **Other costs**  
    If band funding is not enough to cover all your costs, look at other [financial options](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-support-indigenous/) available to you\.

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/musqueam\-first\-nation\-scholarship/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/musqueam-first-nation-scholarship/#additional-resources)

-   [Student loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/)
-   [UBC Bursary Program](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/)
-   [Awards for Indigenous Students](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-indigenous/)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/musqueam\-first\-nation\-scholarship/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/musqueam-first-nation-scholarship/#if-you-have-questions)

Please contact your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) directly\. All undergraduate students have an assigned advisor for personalized advising\. 

If you do not have an assigned advisor, you can email the Indigenous Advising Team at [es\.indigenous@ubc\.ca](mailto:es.indigenous@ubc.ca)\.

title: Work Learn program
content_markdown:
> > Work Learn jobs
> 
> > From **Mon, Jul 27** to **Wed, Aug 12**, browse and apply to Work Learn jobs for the Winter Session on [CareersOnline](https://ubc-csm.symplicity.com/)\.

## About the Work Learn program[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/work\-learn\-program/\#about\-the\-work\-learn\-program](https://students.ubc.ca/career/work-learn-program/#about-the-work-learn-program)

The Work Learn Program supports and subsidizes meaningful work experiences on and off campus, offering current UBC Vancouver students the opportunity to develop their professional skills in a work environment\.

Learn from a mentor, expand your professional network, and gain work experience and skills through a part\-time UBC job while taking classes\.

### Examples of past Work Learn jobs

Employers in the Work Learn Program are faculty, staff, and affiliates with UBC Vancouver\. Work Learn positions span a wide range of industries, including research, project coordination, marketing, and more\.

Past positions include:

-   Indigenous Engagement Climate Emergency Research
-   Health Promotion Undergraduate Research Assistant
-   Oral Microbiology Project Assistant
-   Arena Operations Staff
-   Environment Data Analyst
-   UBC Library Shelving and Circulation Assistant
-   UBC Farm Marketing and Education Assistant

### Student experiences

Read the stories below to learn more about student experiences in Work Learn:

-   [Ife Onwumelu’s story](https://facultystaff.students.ubc.ca/sites/facultystaff.students.ubc.ca/files/Ife_Onwumelu%20WL%20W24%20Student%20Story.pdf) \(pdf\), Neuroscience, Development Project Assistant
-   [Hengyin Liao’s story](https://facultystaff.students.ubc.ca/sites/facultystaff.students.ubc.ca/files/Hengyin_Liao%20WL%20W24%20Student%20Story.pdf) \(pdf\), Natural Resources Conservation, MGEM Program Assistant

## Time commitment[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/work\-learn\-program/\#time\-commitment](https://students.ubc.ca/career/work-learn-program/#time-commitment)

There are 2 sessions of the Work Learn program:

-   **Winter Session \(September 1 to April 30\)**  
    You can work up to a maximum of 10 hours per week, which is a total of 300 hours over Winter Term 1 and 2\. Some Project Worker and Project Assistant positions can only work a maximum of 4 hours per day, up to a maximum of 10 hours per week\.
-   **Summer Session \(May 1 to August 31\)**  
    You can work a maximum of 20 hours per week, which is a total of 300 hours over Summer Term 1 and 2\. Office or Library Worker positions are limited to 10 hours per week, which is a total of 180 hours for the summer session\.

Not all positions will offer the maximum number of hours listed above\. Employers request how many hours they expect for each position when submitting a proposal to the program\. This number varies between units\. Check the job listing and confirm with your employer when you are interviewing for a position\.

## Pay and compensation[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/work\-learn\-program/\#pay\-and\-compensation](https://students.ubc.ca/career/work-learn-program/#pay-and-compensation)

Work Learn positions are part\-time\. Compensation varies depending on the role’s responsibilities and the session it takes place in\.

Review the different job categories and rates for each session:

-   [Winter Session \(September to April\) Position Classification Guide](https://facultystaff.students.ubc.ca/sites/facultystaff.students.ubc.ca/files/WL%20Winter%20Position%20Classification.pdf) \(pdf\)
-   [Summer Session \(May to August\) Position Classification Guide](https://facultystaff.students.ubc.ca/sites/facultystaff.students.ubc.ca/files/WL%20Summer%20Position%20Classification.pdf) \(pdf\)

When employers submit their proposal for the program, the level and type of work must match the rates and duties as outlined in the Position Classification Guide\.

## Eligibility requirements[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/work\-learn\-program/\#eligibility\-requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/career/work-learn-program/#eligibility-requirements)

Before you apply, you must meet **all** of the following requirements:

-   You are a current student at UBC Vancouver with a UBC student number\.
-   You have or are planning to apply for a valid [Social Insurance Number](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/) \(SIN\)\.
-   You are not holding a [Co\-op position](https://coop.ubc.ca/) for the term you plan on holding a Work Learn position\.
-   You can only hold one Work Learn position at a time\.
-   Your research for the Work Learn position is not based on your own thesis work\.
-   You are not holding a [NSERC Undergraduate Student Research Award](https://students.ubc.ca/career/undergraduate-student-research-awards-nserc-cihr-sshrc/) \(USRA\) or [Work Learn International Undergraduate Research Award](https://students.ubc.ca/career/work-learn-international-undergraduate-research-awards/)\.

If you hold another research award or funding, such as faculty\-based awards like [SURE](https://science.ubc.ca/students/undergrad-research/sure) or [EnSURE](https://science.ubc.ca/students/undergrad-research/ensure), you must confirm that a Work Learn position does not conflict with the terms and conditions of those awards\. If you’re uncertain, ask the awarding faculty or program before you accept a Work Learn position\.

## Specific requirements for students[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/work\-learn\-program/\#specific\-requirements\-for\-students](https://students.ubc.ca/career/work-learn-program/#specific-requirements-for-students)

Depending on what type of student you are, you must meet specific requirements to be eligible for a Work Learn position\. 

### Domestic students

**

Undergraduate students

**

**Summer Session \(May to August\) positions**

You must be registered in courses for one of the following:

-   The previous term \(Winter Term 2\)
-   The Summer Session \(either in Summer Term 1 or 2\)

**Winter Session \(September to April\) positions**

You must be registered in courses in **both** Winter Terms 1 and 2 to hold a Work Learn position for the full duration of the Winter Session\.

**

Graduate students in a Masters or PhD program

**

For both Winter Session \(September to April\) and Summer Session \(May to August\) positions, you must either be registered in courses **or** have continuing registration and be paying tuition fees\.

**

Students in a professional or diploma program

**

**Summer Session \(May to August\) positions**

You must be registered in summer courses \(either in Summer Term 1 or 2\)\.

**Winter Session \(September to April\) positions**

You must be registered in courses in the term you plan to hold a Work Learn position\.

**

Unclassified students

**

**Summer Session \(May to August\) positions**

You must be registered in summer courses \(either in Summer Term 1 or 2\)\.

**Winter Session \(September to April\) positions**

You must be registered in courses in each term you plan to hold a Work Learn position\.

**

Visiting students from outside of UBC

**

**Summer Session \(May to August\) positions**

You must be registered in summer courses \(either in Summer Term 1 or 2\)\.

**Winter Session \(September to April\) positions**

You must be registered in courses in each term you plan to hold a Work Learn position\.

 **If you’re in your last term of courses and graduating**

You are eligible for a Work Learn position only for the academic term directly following the completion of your courses, regardless of your graduation date\. This applies to both undergraduate and graduate students\.

-   If you finish your courses in the Summer Session \(August\) and graduate in November, you are eligible to hold a Work Learn position in Winter Term 1 only\.
-   If you finish your courses in Winter Term 1 \(December\) and graduate in May, you are eligible to hold a Work Learn position in Winter Term 1 and Winter Term 2 only\.
-   If you finish your courses in Winter Term 2 \(April\) and graduate in May, you are eligible to hold a Work Learn position in the Summer Session after\.

### International students

Make sure you have a valid [Social Insurance Number](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/) \(SIN\) before you start your Work Learn position\. The application process for a SIN can take several weeks\.

**

Undergraduate students

**

**Summer Session \(May to August\) positions**

-   You must be registered in courses for the previous term \(Winter Term 2\) **or** the Summer Session \(either Summer Term 1 or 2\)\.
-   You must have a valid study permit\.
-   You must be on a [scheduled break](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#scheduled-break), or be considered [full time for immigration purposes](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#full-time)\.

**Winter Session \(September to April\) positions**

-   You must be registered in courses in **both** Winter Terms 1 and 2 to hold a Work Learn position for the full duration of the Winter Session\.
-   You must have a valid study permit\.
-   You must be considered [full time for immigration purposes](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#full-time)\.

**

Graduate students in a Master or PhD program

**

For both Winter Session \(September to April\) and Summer Session \(May to August\) positions:

-   You must be registered in courses **or** have continuing registration and paying tuition fees\.
-   You must have a valid study permit\.
-   You must be considered [full time for immigration purposes](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#full-time) in the term\(s\) you plan on holding a Work Learn position\.

**

Students in a professional or diploma program

**

For both Winter Session \(September to April\) and Summer Session \(May to August\) positions:

-   You must have a [valid study permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/#maintaining-your-student-status) or have applied to extend your study permit and have [maintained status](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/maintained-status/)\.
-   You must be enrolled [full\-time for immigration purposes](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#full-time) during academic terms or are eligible to work during a [scheduled break](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#scheduled-break)\.
-   Your study permit [includes conditions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/#before-you-apply-for-a-sin) allowing you to work on campus such as, “May accept employment on or off campus if meeting eligibility criteria, per paragraph R186\(f\), \(v\), or \(w\) and must cease working if no longer meeting these criteria”\.

**

Unclassified students

**

For both Winter Session \(September to April\) and Summer Session \(May to August\) positions:

-   You must have a [valid study permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/#maintaining-your-student-status) or have applied to extend your study permit and have [maintained status](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/maintained-status/)\.
-   You must be enrolled [full\-time for immigration purposes](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#full-time) during academic terms and during Summer Session\.
-   Your study permit [includes conditions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/#before-you-apply-for-a-sin) allowing you to work on campus such as, “May accept employment on or off campus if meeting eligibility criteria, per paragraph R186\(f\), \(v\), or \(w\) and must cease working if no longer meeting these criteria”\.
-   You **cannot work** during scheduled breaks\.

**

Exchange or visiting students from outside of UBC

**

**Summer Session \(May to August\) positions**

-   You must be registered in summer courses \(either Summer Term 1 or 2\)\.
-   You must have a valid study permit\.
-   You must be considered [full time for immigration purposes](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#full-time) in the term\(s\) you plan on holding a Work Learn position\.

**Winter Session \(September to April\) positions**

-   You must be registered in courses in each term you plan to hold a Work Learn position\.
-   You must have a valid study permit\.
-   You must be considered [full time for immigration purposes](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#full-time) in the term\(s\) you plan on holding a Work Learn position\.

**

If you’re in your last term of courses and graduating

**

You are eligible for a Work Learn position only for the academic term directly following the completion of your courses, regardless of your graduation date\. This applies to both undergraduate and graduate students\.

-   If you finish your courses in the Summer Session \(August\) and graduate in November, you are eligible to hold a Work Learn position in Winter Term 1 only\.
-   If you finish your courses in Winter Term 1 \(December\) and graduate in May, you are eligible to hold a Work Learn position in Winter Term 1 and Winter Term 2 only\.
-   If you finish your courses in Winter Term 2 \(April\) and graduate in May, you are eligible to hold a Work Learn position in the Summer Session after\.

**Additional requirements**

-   If you completed program requirements and your program completion letter is not yet available, you are considered by UBC to be [full time for immigration purposes](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#full-time) and are still eligible to work unlimited hours on campus\.
-   If your letter of completion is available, you must meet **one** of the following scenarios:
    -   You have a valid study permit **and** you have applied for a [work permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/post-graduation-work-permit/), such as a Post\-Graduation Work Permit, within 90 days after completing your program at UBC\.
    -   You have an official letter of acceptance into a new academic program, **and** you have a valid study permit or you have applied to extend your study permit when the old study permit was still valid\. 
    -   You have some other form of authorization to work in Canada\.

If you have questions about your eligibility, please speak with an [International Student Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/)\.

## Applying for a Work Learn position[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/work\-learn\-program/\#applying\-for\-a\-work\-learn\-position](https://students.ubc.ca/career/work-learn-program/#applying-for-a-work-learn-position)

There are over 500 Work Learn positions available each term\. Work Learn jobs are posted on [CareersOnline](https://ubc-csm.symplicity.com/) throughout the year, usually March for summer roles and August for winter positions\.

1.  Log into [CareersOnline](https://ubc-csm.symplicity.com/index.php/pid388249?)\.
2.  On the left sidebar under *Opportunities*, select “Work Learn Program”\.
3.  Browse jobs and read the job descriptions carefully\.
4.  Follow the application instructions listed on the posting\.

If you are interested in creating your own Work Learn position, learn about the program details from a [Work Learn supervisor’s perspective](https://facultystaff.students.ubc.ca/student-development-services/centre-student-involvement-careers/work-learn) and email [work\.learn@ubc\.ca](mailto:work.learn@ubc.ca) if you have questions about this option\.

### Tips for applying

-   Before applying, learn what to include in your [resume and cover letter](https://students.ubc.ca/career/career-resources/resumes-cover-letters/) and how to articulate your employable skills\.
-   You can apply for as many Work Learn positions that interest you, but be sure to mention skills and experiences relevant to each job posting to increase your chances of being invited for an interview\.
-   Some job postings interview on a rolling basis, so consider submitting your applications sooner rather than later\.
-   Review how to [prepare for an interview](https://students.ubc.ca/career/career-resources/interviews/) including what to expect during and after your interview\.
-   For further guidance, visit the [UBC Career Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/ubc-career-centre/) to meet with a Career Advisor and to access Career Resources\.

## Work Learn student resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/work\-learn\-program/\#work\-learn\-student\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/career/work-learn-program/#work-learn-student-resources)

If you want to apply for a Work Learn job or are currently a Work Learn student, take the [Work Learn Fundamentals Canvas course](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/TXPREG)\.

Course topics include:

-   Finding a Work Learn job
-   Navigating the workplace
-   How to schedule your hours
-   Receiving your payment
-   Reflecting on your work experience

The following resources can also help you make the most of your Work Learn experience:

-   [UBC HR Employee Handbook for Students](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/HR_student_handbook.pdf) \(pdf\)
-   [UBC Respectful Environment Statement](https://www.hr.ubc.ca/respectful-environment/)
-   [Work Learn Student Resource Guide](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/work_learn_student_guide.pdf) \(pdf\)
-   [Work Learn Student FAQ](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/work_learn_student_FAQ.pdf) \(pdf\)
-   [BC Employment Standards Act \(ESA\)](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/employment-business/employment-standards-advice/employment-standards)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/work\-learn\-program/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/career/work-learn-program/#if-you-have-questions)

Email [work\.learn@ubc\.ca](mailto:work.learn@ubc.ca) or call [604 822 8278](tel:6048228278)\.

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/work\-learn\-program/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/career/work-learn-program/#additional-resources)

[Career resources](https://students.ubc.ca/career/career-resources/)

Find tips on getting a job, improve your application, or book an appointment with a career advisor\.

[Working in Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/)

If you’re an international student, learn what conditions you need to meet to work in Canada\.

[Social Insurance Number \(SIN\)](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/)

If you’re planning to work in Canada, you’ll need an SIN to be paid\.

title: Launch Your Career in Canada
content_markdown:
## About the event[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/events\-workshops/launch\-career\-canada/\#about\-the\-event](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/launch-career-canada/#about-the-event)

Launch Your Career in Canada is UBC’s annual career development intensive for international undergraduate and graduate students\. The event provides a space to explore career possibilities with your UBC degree, test your assumptions about the job market with industry professionals, and learn from UBC alumni who have been where you are now\. This is your opportunity to practice job search skills in a low\-stakes environment with people who are interested in your success and growth\. Registration opens on **Mon, Jan 26, 2026** on [CareersOnline](https://ubc-csm.symplicity.com/students/app/events)\.

### Event details

-   **Date**: Mon, Feb 23 to Thurs, Feb 26, 2026
-   **Location**: Virtual and in\-person

## 2026 Event schedule[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/events\-workshops/launch\-career\-canada/\#2026\-event\-schedule](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/launch-career-canada/#2026-event-schedule)

### Path to Professional Success: Your First Canadian Work Experience 

-   **Date:** Mon, Feb 23, 2026
-   **Time:** 1:00 to 2:00 pm
-   **Session format:** Virtual

Gain valuable job search strategies that can help you pave the way to securing your first Canadian job\. Learn about common career challenges as international students, the norms of the Canadian labour market, and how to explore on\-campus experiences to enhance your professional skills before you enter the job market\. This workshop will address issues that are important to both undergraduate and graduate students\.

### Chart Your Path: Making Career Decisions in Uncertain Times

-   **Date:** Tue, Feb 24, 2026
-   **Time:** 12:00 to 1:00 pm
-   **Session format:** Virtual

This workshop provides a clear roadmap, practical strategies, and tailored resources to help expand or clarify your possibilities and guide your decision\-making process\. Learn how to navigate uncertainty with confidence and make choices that set you up for success in launching your career in Canada\.

### Pathways to Post\-Graduation Work Permit \(PGWP\)

-   **Date:** Wed, Feb 25, 2026
-   **Time:** 1:00 to 2:30 pm
-   **Session format:** Virtual

Get up\-to\-date information about the recently announced changes to the Post\-Graduation Work Permit \(PGWP\) Program, eligibility criteria, application process, work eligibility during the transition to a PGWP, and important considerations when travelling after completing your studies\. The presentation will be followed by a Q&A session with Regulated International Student Immigration Advisors \(RISIAs\) from [International Student Advising\.](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/)

### Ask Hiring Managers and Alumni How to Get Recruited

-   **Date:** Thurs, Feb 26, 2026
-   **Time:** 6:00 to 8:00 pm
-   **Session format:** In\-person

Attend an in\-person event featuring insightful discussions and networking opportunities with hiring managers and UBC alumni\. You’ll have the chance to hear from hiring managers about what they look for in candidates, what unique strengths international students bring to organizations, and connect with alumni who were international students and have successfully established their careers in Canada\.

## How to register[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/events\-workshops/launch\-career\-canada/\#how\-to\-register](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/launch-career-canada/#how-to-register)

Register for the events on [CareersOnline](https://ubc-csm.symplicity.com/students/app/events) starting **Mon,** **Jan 26, 2026\.** You will need to register for each event separately\.

Contact the [UBC Career Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/ubc-career-centre/) for any questions regarding the Launch Your Career in Canada or career\-related information\.

title: Multidisciplinary Undergraduate Research Conference (MURC)
content_markdown:
## About the conference[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/events\-workshops/multidisciplinary\-undergraduate\-research\-conference/\#about\-the\-conference](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/multidisciplinary-undergraduate-research-conference/#about-the-conference)

The Multidisciplinary Undergraduate Research Conference \(MURC\) is a conference for UBC undergraduate students to present their research with fellow UBC students, family, and friends\.

Since 2003, the conference has been led by undergraduate students and is centred on showcasing and celebrating undergraduate student research through presentations, workshops, and keynote speakers\.

MURC is free to attend and open to the UBC community\. Other students, including graduate students, can support the conference as volunteers or adjudicators\.

Browse the 2026 conference schedule and list of presentations in the [program guide](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/murc_program_guide-2026.pdf) \(pdf\)\.

### Event details

-   MURC 2027 will take place on Sat, Mar 20, 2027\.

## Register to attend MURC[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/events\-workshops/multidisciplinary\-undergraduate\-research\-conference/\#register\-to\-attend\-murc](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/multidisciplinary-undergraduate-research-conference/#register-to-attend-murc)

Registration for MURC 2027 will open in March 2027\.

Stay connected through our [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/ubcmurc/?hl=en) for the latest updates and don’t miss the opportunity to explore undergraduate research from students across the UBC community\.

## Get involved[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/events\-workshops/multidisciplinary\-undergraduate\-research\-conference/\#get\-involved](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/multidisciplinary-undergraduate-research-conference/#get-involved)

[MURC Planning Committee](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/multidisciplinary-undergraduate-research-conference/join-murc-planning-committee/)

If you’re passionate about research, leadership, and event planning, apply to organize the conference\.

[Presenting at the conference](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/multidisciplinary-undergraduate-research-conference/present-murc/)

UBC undergrad students currently participating in or have completed their own UBC faculty\-supervised research project are welcome to apply\.

[Volunteer at MURC](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/multidisciplinary-undergraduate-research-conference/volunteer-murc/)

Help out with the conference or be an adjudicator for the conference presentations\.

## Past conference information[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/events\-workshops/multidisciplinary\-undergraduate\-research\-conference/\#past\-conference\-information](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/multidisciplinary-undergraduate-research-conference/#past-conference-information)

### MURC 2026

In 2026, MURC had:

-   380 presenters
-   255 unique presentations
-   Over 390 attendees
-   Over 65 volunteers and 105 adjudicators

#### 2026 MURC Journal publication

MURC is excited to partner with the Canadian Journal of Undergraduate Research \(CJUR\) for a special edition publication including MURC conference abstracts\. This journal is a student\-led, peer\-reviewed publication for Canadian undergraduate research\. CJUR will publish a special edition in collaboration with MURC 2026 to promote accessible undergraduate research initiatives\.

Check out the [CJUR Website](https://cjur.ca/) for the MURC 2026 special edition publication\.

content_markdown:
## About this event[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/events\-workshops/west\-coast\-virtual\-fairs/\#about\-this\-event](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/west-coast-virtual-fairs/#about-this-event)

The annual West Coast Virtual Fairs event is a collaboration between the University of British Columbia \(UBC\), Simon Fraser University \(SFU\), and the University of Victoria \(UVic\)\. These three institutions are pleased to offer students and alumni the exciting opportunity to connect with hundreds of employers and graduate schools at the Career, Volunteer, and Graduate Schools event this spring\.

The event will take place on a virtual fair platform called Eventus\. Check out exhibitor booths to learn more about various organizations and their opportunities\. Over 60 employers, graduate schools, and charities are invited to this one\-of\-a\-kind virtual event\. Attendees do not need to be present for the entire fair, and are encouraged to schedule breaks in between sessions\.

### Event details

-   **Date:** Wed, Feb 11, 2026
-   **Time:** 10:00 am to 4:00 pm
-   **Location:** Virtual \(on Eventus\)

### Fair format

Pre\-book 1\-on\-1 and group sessions with exhibitors\. Early access to the virtual fair platform will only be sent to those who register for the event on CareersOnline\.

-   **1\-on\-1 sessions**: Enjoy 15\-minute private conversations with exhibitors using the video conferencing tool embedded in the platform\.
-   **Group sessions**: Join company and graduate school representatives for group information sessions with other UBC, SFU, and UVic students\.

### Reasons to attend

-   Create meaningful connections with recruiters and graduate school representatives across multiple industries
-   Learn about full\-time, part\-time, co\-op, and internship opportunities without leaving the comforts of your home
-   Develop your networking and job search strategy skills by participating in virtual career\-related workshops and interacting with hundreds of exhibitors

## Preparation webinars[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/events\-workshops/west\-coast\-virtual\-fairs/\#preparation\-webinars](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/west-coast-virtual-fairs/#preparation-webinars)

Additional workshops will be available to support you on your career journey\.

### Building Career Connections: Your Guide to Easy, Authentic Networking 

-   **Date:** Tues, Feb 10, 2026
-   **Time:** 12:30 to 1:20 pm
-   **Session format:** Virtual

Get tips on how to approach employers at a career fair and foster connection beyond the event\. Learn how to turn casual conversations into meaningful professional connections and expand your professional circle\.

title: Join the MURC Planning Committee
content_markdown:
## About the committee[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/events\-workshops/multidisciplinary\-undergraduate\-research\-conference/join\-murc\-planning\-committee/\#about\-the\-committee](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/multidisciplinary-undergraduate-research-conference/join-murc-planning-committee/#about-the-committee)

The MURC Planning Committee is responsible for the ideation, development, implementation, and exhibition of the Multidisciplinary Undergraduate Research Conference\. This student\-led conference is supported by staff advisors from the Centre for Community Engaged Learning, but the emphasis is on student leadership for conference design and planning\. Students interested in developing their leadership, project management, event planning, and communication skills may be interested in one of the director or chair positions available through the MURC Planning Committee\.

## Time commitment[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/events\-workshops/multidisciplinary\-undergraduate\-research\-conference/join\-murc\-planning\-committee/\#time\-commitment](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/multidisciplinary-undergraduate-research-conference/join-murc-planning-committee/#time-commitment)

The MURC Planning Committee holds biweekly collaboration sessions during Winter Session Term 1 \(September to December\) and weekly collaboration sessions during Winter Session Term 2 \(January to April\)\. All collaboration sessions are 2 hours long and mandatory for all members\.

On average, Planning Committee members can expect to commit approximately 10 hours per week in Winter Session Term 1 and 20 hours per week in Winter Session Term 2, depending on portfolio\-specific timelines and responsibilities\.

## 2027 MURC Planning Committee[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/events\-workshops/multidisciplinary\-undergraduate\-research\-conference/join\-murc\-planning\-committee/\#2027\-murc\-planning\-committee](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/multidisciplinary-undergraduate-research-conference/join-murc-planning-committee/#2027-murc-planning-committee)

The planning committee holds 10 positions within 5 portfolios:

-   Co\-Chairs
-   Communications and Promotions Portfolio Co\-Directors
-   Logistics and Programming Portfolio Co\-Directors
-   Volunteer Engagement Portfolio Co\-Directors
-   Adjudicators and Presentations Portfolio Co\-Directors

## 2027 MURC Planning Committee positions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/events\-workshops/multidisciplinary\-undergraduate\-research\-conference/join\-murc\-planning\-committee/\#2027\-murc\-planning\-committee\-positions](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/multidisciplinary-undergraduate-research-conference/join-murc-planning-committee/#2027-murc-planning-committee-positions)

### Co\-Chair

The MURC Co\-Chairs are the detail\-oriented, strategic leads of the MURC Planning Committee, which is composed of peer executive members from across the university\.  MURC Co\-Chairs work closely with staff advisors to create a strategic plan for the conference and provide leadership, mentorship, and guidance to all executive portfolios, including Logistics and Programming, Adjudicators and Presentations, Volunteer Engagement, and Communications and Promotions\. 

Co\-chairs are expected to lead their peers by coordinating key conference deliverables, implementing marketing and logistic plans, managing the conference budget and especially by ensuring conference deadlines and milestones are met in a timely manner\. Co\-chairs are clear communicators with strong organizational skills and a keen ability to work both independently and in collaboration with a hybrid staff and student team\. View the [position description](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/murc_cochairs_description_2027.pdf) \(pdf\)\.

### Communications and Promotions Co\-Director

title: Present at MURC
content_markdown:
Any UBC undergraduate student who is participating in or has completed their own UBC faculty\-supervised research project can apply to present at the [Multidisciplinary Undergraduate Research Conference](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/multidisciplinary-undergraduate-research-conference/) \(MURC\)\. Students from all faculties and programs are welcome, and presentations can be made individually or in groups of up to 5\. Students who present at MURC 2026 cannot adjudicate\.

Student presenters can participate in 1 of 2 ways: 

-   In\-person oral presentations
-   In\-person poster presentations

On the day of the conference, presentations will be adjudicated by a mix of senior undergraduate students with research communication experience, graduate students, and faculty members\. After the conference, MURC presenters will receive individualized feedback on their research and presentation skills\.

The MURC conference will take place on **Sat, Mar 21, 2026** on the UBC Vancouver campus, in the Ponderosa ballroom \(Ponderosa Commons North\) and Centre for Interactive Research on Sustainability \(CIRS\) building\.

MURC 2026 applications are now closed\.

Stay connected with us on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/ubcmurc/?hl=en) and check out our [MURC webpage](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/multidisciplinary-undergraduate-research-conference/) for the latest updates and announcements\.

## Before applying[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/events\-workshops/multidisciplinary\-undergraduate\-research\-conference/present\-murc/\#before\-applying](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/multidisciplinary-undergraduate-research-conference/present-murc/#before-applying)

### 1\. Talk to your research supervisor

Talk to your research supervisor and get permission to apply for the conference\. As the nature of some research may be sensitive, this step is crucial and applications will not be accepted without supervisor approval\. Your research supervisor will be contacted via email to confirm their approval of your presentation at MURC\.

### 2\. Prepare your abstract

When writing your abstract, please ensure it is under 250 words and accessible to a generalist audience\. Use brief definitions, clear explanations, and concrete real\-world examples to help readers understand the study’s focus and importance\.

Since MURC is not a specialized conference, the MURC review committee will be assessing whether a generalist audience will be able to follow the abstract\. To support your learning, the MURC Review Committee will provide feedback on each submitted abstract based on the following criteria:

-   **Clarity:** Abstract is understandable to a non\-expert audience
-   **Quality of writing**: Spelling, grammar, formatting, and general flow of the abstract
-   **Methodology**: Methods are clearly explained and justified
-   **Findings**: Results, or expected outcomes, are explicitly linked back to the research question
-   **Significance**: The importance of research to the field and the value of addressing the knowledge gap is articulated

To prepare your abstract that speaks to a generalist audience, you are encouraged to review the [tip sheet](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/murc_how_to_write_abstract.pdf) \(pdf\) and watch the [abstract writing workshop recording](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CG2ej_xYGFo), which shares key components of an abstract and how to develop it for an interdisciplinary audience\. Review the [abstract rubric](https://ubcca-my.sharepoint.com/personal/cora_li_ubc_ca/_layouts/15/onedrive.aspx?id=%2Fpersonal%2Fcora%5Fli%5Fubc%5Fca%2FDocuments%2FMURC%20Abstract%20Rubric%2Epdf&parent=%2Fpersonal%2Fcora%5Fli%5Fubc%5Fca%2FDocuments&ct=1769537618705&or=Teams%2DHL&ga=1&LOF=1) for details on the assessment criteria\. You should also ask your research supervisor for feedback on your abstract before submission\.

### 3\. Select a presentation format

#### Oral presentations 

During an oral presentation, you will discuss your research and findings, and you may support your presentation with slides\. There will be a brief 5 to 7 minute Q&A session after your presentation\. 

#### Poster presentations 

During a poster presentation, you’ll talk about your research for a brief period of time, then answer a few questions from an adjudicator\. You are not required to do a formal poster presentation\.

The general poster dimensions are 36 inches by 48 inches, and the conference will print your poster for you for free given you meet the free poster printing deadline\. Check back for the final poster printing submission date in January 2026\.

See [poster examples](https://f1000research.com/browse/posters?&selectedDomain=posters) from previous years\.

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/events\-workshops/multidisciplinary\-undergraduate\-research\-conference/present\-murc/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/multidisciplinary-undergraduate-research-conference/present-murc/#how-to-apply)

Applications to present at MURC 2026 are now closed\.

## After your application is approved[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/events\-workshops/multidisciplinary\-undergraduate\-research\-conference/present\-murc/\#after\-your\-application\-is\-approved](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/multidisciplinary-undergraduate-research-conference/present-murc/#after-your-application-is-approved)

For Multidisciplinary Undergraduate Research Conference \(MURC\) presenters, preparing your abstract and presentation can be challenging\. Attend oral and poster presentation workshops sessions to learn more about presenting your research in a multidisciplinary format and get feedback on your preliminary work\.

Whether you are presenting a poster or doing an oral presentation, you are practising an important research skill by effectively communicating your findings or conclusions to an audience\.

Workshop details will be shared via email once your application is approved\.

## Frequently asked questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/events\-workshops/multidisciplinary\-undergraduate\-research\-conference/present\-murc/\#frequently\-asked\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/multidisciplinary-undergraduate-research-conference/present-murc/#frequently-asked-questions)

**

Can I present on a research project that is incomplete?

**

Yes, you can submit your research project even if it is not completed\.

**

Can I present on multiple research topics?

**

Presenters are welcome to present up to two research topics\. You are free to choose whether to present them both in one format, or split them between two formats\. After completing the registration form, submit both your presentations through the “Submission” page\.

If you wish to present on more than two topics, please email us at undergraduate\.research@ubc\.ca

**

Can I present on a project where I’m part of the research team?

**

Yes, you can present at MURC provided permission has been granted by the research supervisor\. Your research supervisor will be contacted to confirm their consent, in order for you to present at the conference\.

**

Are there restrictions on the type of research that can be presented?

**

There’s no restrictions provided you have a research supervisor for the project who is aware that you want to present at MURC\. Also, you \(and the co\-presenters if any\) must be undergraduate students\. Your research supervisor will be contacted to confirm their consent, in order for you to present at the conference\.

**

Can I edit my abstract after submitting it?

**

After you submit your application, the MURC review committee will review and provide feedback on your abstract\. You will be granted 2 to 3 weeks to submit your final abstract which will be featured in the MURC 2026 program guide\.  

**

What do I do with the feedback from the MURC review committee?

**

You are encouraged to implement it\. Please consult with your research supervisor when making edits and resubmitting your abstract\.

**

What citation style do I use?

**

MURC doesn’t prescribe a specific citation style\. We advise you to follow the citation style used in your discipline\. 

**

Are citations included in the word count?

**

Yes, citations are included in the 250\-word count limit\. We only require in\-text citations, if applicable\.

title: Volunteer at MURC
content_markdown:
## Volunteer for the conference[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/events\-workshops/multidisciplinary\-undergraduate\-research\-conference/volunteer\-murc/\#volunteer\-for\-the\-conference](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/multidisciplinary-undergraduate-research-conference/volunteer-murc/#volunteer-for-the-conference)

Multidisciplinary Undergraduate Research Conference \(MURC\) volunteers are important to the success of the conference\. Volunteers are given the opportunity to network with other student leaders and researchers on campus and learn about the research being conducted by their peers\.

Volunteers will be supported by the MURC Planning Committee and the staff at UBC Centre for Community Engaged Learning\.

### Qualifications

-   The ability to work independently and as part of a team
-   Effective time management and organizational skills
-   Adaptability and openness to new experiences
-   Strong communication and interpersonal skills
-   Interest in learning more about student development and research
-   Willingness to learn technological platforms that MURC will be hosted on
-   Previous experience navigating Zoom, Collaborate Ultra, and Canvas is an asset
-   Previous public speaking experience is an asset, but is not required
-   Able to commit to a mandatory training session

Experience in research is **not** required to apply\.

 **Volunteer tasks**

Event volunteers will be tasked with several roles, including:

-   Assisting with pre\-conference preparations as required
-   Assisting with the facilitation, timing, and evaluation of presentations
-   Moderating presentation sessions and introducing presenters
-   Answering general inquiries from conference attendees and adjudicators
-   Providing any additional logistical assistance as needed

 **Anticipated learning outcomes**

-   Teamwork and collaboration skills
-   Problem\-solving and decision\-making skills
-   Experience in running and logistically managing a large conference
-   Professional communication with peers, presenters and staff

 **Benefits and recognition**

-   Opportunity to network with other student leaders on campus and work in a collaborative team with other volunteers
-   Opportunity to learn about undergraduate research from a variety of disciplines at UBC
-   Letter of Service upon request
-   Panel and networking session with graduate student adjudicators to learn about different fields of research and get career advice or tips for getting involved with research 

### Apply to volunteer

Volunteer applications are now closed\. Please check back in Fall 2026\.

## Become an adjudicator[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/events\-workshops/multidisciplinary\-undergraduate\-research\-conference/volunteer\-murc/\#become\-an\-adjudicator](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/multidisciplinary-undergraduate-research-conference/volunteer-murc/#become-an-adjudicator)

Adjudicators play a vital role at MURC by evaluating presentations on the day of the conference and offering presenters valuable feedback\. We invite graduate students as well as upper\-year undergraduates \(third year and above\) with research presentation experience and who are enthusiastic about supporting student research, to apply for this role\. Adjudicators **cannot** present at MURC 2027\.

### Expectations of the position

MURC stands apart from typical research conferences in 2 key ways\. First, it serves as an entry point for UBC undergraduate students to gain initial experience with research presentations\. Second, MURC evaluations focus on how effectively students explain their research, rather than on disciplinary expertise\.

As an adjudicator, it’s essential to understand the unique goals and format of MURC\.

### Qualifications

To provide our students with reliable, consistent and constructive feedback, adjudicators must meet the following qualifications:

-   Strong communication and interpersonal skills
-   Passion for supporting undergraduates in their research journey
-   Positive and professional attitude to help students feel comfortable presenting
-   Undergraduate applicants must have experience presenting research projects, such as through course presentations, directed studies, symposiums, research fairs, and conferences

### Benefits

Adjudicators benefit in several ways through participation:

-   Network with students, faculty, and staff
-   Develop critical skills in assessment and constructive feedback that are applicable in academic, research, and professional settings
-   Support and inspire undergraduate researchers by providing meaningful growth\-oriented feedback

### Apply to be an adjudicator

Adjudicator applications are now closed\. Please check back in Fall 2026\.

To learn more about the adjudication process or for any other questions about the conference, please contact [undergraduate\.research@ubc\.ca](mailto:undergraduate.research@ubc.ca)\.

title: LFS Academic and Career Engagement (ACE) Team
content_markdown:
## About the role[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/peer\-programs/lfs\-academic\-career\-engagement\-ace\-team/\#about\-the\-role](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/peer-programs/lfs-academic-career-engagement-ace-team/#about-the-role)

The LFS Academic and Career Engagement Team \(ACE Team\) focuses on planning and implementing programming related to academic success, wellness and career development\.

Team members develop project management and communication skills, increase their knowledge of student resources, and expand their network and professional relationships\.

The team is divided into the following committees:

-   **Communications Committee**  
    Preparing and developing communications content for LFS ACE events and workshops, LFS Student Services on platforms including the [LFS Student Services Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/lfsnewslettuce/)\.
-   **Events Committee**  
    Planning and implementing LFS ACE events, such as Let’s Talk About Research and LFS: Career Stories with LFS Alumni\.
-   **Workshops Committee**  
    Preparing, coordinating, and facilitating academic, wellness, and career\-related workshops for LFS undergraduate students including, but not limited to, Bounce Back in Term 2 and Mapping Your Major\.

## Who can apply?[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/peer\-programs/lfs\-academic\-career\-engagement\-ace\-team/\#who\-can\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/peer-programs/lfs-academic-career-engagement-ace-team/#who-can-apply)

LFS undergraduate students in second year and above in good academic standing can apply for the role\.

Each year, there are typically **18 to 30 roles available**, with 6 being Team Lead positions\. Team Lead positions are hired before LFS ACE student leader committee members\. Learn about the [Team Lead applications](http://www.landfood.ubc.ca/undergraduate/lfs-academic-and-career-engagement-team/)\.

### If you require accommodations

The Peer Programs Program Advisors would like to recognize that being able to participate in student leadership opportunities is a privilege\. The weekly commitment for each Peer Program varies in length but may not be possible for some students who need accommodations based on chronic health conditions, disabilities, mental health, and/or other lived experiences\.

If you have specific accommodations for your ability to participate and contribute to the program, please connect with Thilini Leitan, LFS Student Engagement Officer to discuss what accommodations can be made for your particular situation for participation in the LFS ACE Team\.

## Time commitment[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/peer\-programs/lfs\-academic\-career\-engagement\-ace\-team/\#time\-commitment](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/peer-programs/lfs-academic-career-engagement-ace-team/#time-commitment)

The time commitment for the role is **5 to 8 hours per week**\. 

Please review the LFS ACE Student Leader position description for detailed time requirements\.

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/peer\-programs/lfs\-academic\-career\-engagement\-ace\-team/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/peer-programs/lfs-academic-career-engagement-ace-team/#how-to-apply)

Applications are now closed\. Check back in 2027\.

Review the [2026/27 LFS ACE Team position description](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/peer_programs_lfs.pdf) \(pdf\) for complete details about the role\.

### Additional application questions

You will be required to list your committee preference and respond to 3 additional short answer questions

1.  Why do you want to be involved as a student leader in the LFS ACE Team? 
2.  What knowledge and skills do you hope to learn through the role? 
3.  Please identify 2 to 3 strengths and/or qualities that you will bring to the LFS ACE Team\. Be sure to refer to your past experiences that have helped you develop them\.

## Skills developed[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/peer\-programs/lfs\-academic\-career\-engagement\-ace\-team/\#skills\-developed](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/peer-programs/lfs-academic-career-engagement-ace-team/#skills-developed)

-   Written and oral communication skills
-   Adaptability
-   Motivation
-   Organization
-   Teamwork
-   Project management
-   Analysis and problem solving
-   Networking

## Contact[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/peer\-programs/lfs\-academic\-career\-engagement\-ace\-team/\#contact](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/peer-programs/lfs-academic-career-engagement-ace-team/#contact)

If you have questions, please email the Program Advisor, Thilini, at [thilini\.leitan@ubc\.ca](mailto:thilini.leitan@ubc.ca) or visit the [LFS ACE webpage](https://www.landfood.ubc.ca/undergraduate/lfs-academic-and-career-engagement-team/)\.
