title: Peer Health Educators
content_markdown:
## About the role[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/peer\-programs/peer\-health\-educators/\#about\-the\-role](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/peer-programs/peer-health-educators/#about-the-role)

Peer Health Educators will join a diverse community of volunteers who share their interests in health and wellbeing, and work together to provide outreach and education to the UBC student community\. Students will learn from the Health Promotion and Education staff through ongoing support, training, and feedback\. In this role, you will contribute to campus health education and give back to the UBC student community\.

## Who can apply?[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/peer\-programs/peer\-health\-educators/\#who\-can\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/peer-programs/peer-health-educators/#who-can-apply)

Undergraduate and graduate students are welcome to apply to the position\.

### Qualifications

The Peer Health Educator volunteer position is a good fit for those who demonstrate the following:

-   Passionate about student health and wellbeing, sexual health, substance use health, and mental health and wellbeing
-   Interest in learning about the intersections of systemic oppression
-   Interest in learning about equity, diversity, and inclusion with health and wellbeing
-   A desire to learn and develop new skills through experiential learning
-   Interest in developing presentation and facilitation skills
-   Is flexible, open to change, and receptive to constructive feedback
-   Strong organizational and time management skills
-   Enjoys meeting new people and leading groups
-   Enjoys working collaboratively with others on projects
-   Takes initiative and is self\-motivated

### If you require accommodations

The Peer Programs Program Advisors would like to recognize that being able to participate in student leadership opportunities is a privilege\. The weekly commitment for each Peer Program varies in length but may not be possible for some students who need accommodations based on chronic health conditions, disabilities, mental health, and/or other lived experiences\.

If you have specific accommodations for your ability to participate and contribute to the program, please connect with team to discuss what accommodations can be made for your particular situation\.

## Time commitment[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/peer\-programs/peer\-health\-educators/\#time\-commitment](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/peer-programs/peer-health-educators/#time-commitment)

The time commitment is **5 to 6 hours per week**\. For detailed time requirements, please review the position description\.

Review the [2026/27 Peer Health Educators Position Description](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/peer_programs_health_educators.pdf) \(pdf\) for complete details about the role\.

title: UBtheChange Community Activators
content_markdown:
## About the role[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/peer\-programs/ubthechange\-community\-activators/\#about\-the\-role](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/peer-programs/ubthechange-community-activators/#about-the-role)

UBtheChange Community Activators work alongside staff, community partners, and schools to plan and implement community action projects throughout the year\. They support and mentor fellow UBC students to apply their strengths and classroom learning, while engaging directly with community knowledge and priorities\. Through this work, UBtheChange Community Activators support community\-identified goals and create meaningful, hands\-on learning experiences for UBC students\.

## Who can apply?[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/peer\-programs/ubthechange\-community\-activators/\#who\-can\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/peer-programs/ubthechange-community-activators/#who-can-apply)

Students from all disciplines and years are invited to apply for the role\.

Preference is given to alumni of the Community Action Days projects, former UBtheChange Activators, CCEL Grant recipients, and others with student leadership experience\.

### Qualifications

-   Passionate about community engagement, social change, and justice
-   Interest in understanding systemic injustice, power, personal positionality, and community strength in the Metro Vancouver context
-   Enjoys collaborating with peers and community partners
-   Excited to build skills in facilitation, reciprocal collaboration, and strengths\-based leadership
-   Respectful of diverse perspectives and lived experiences
-   Reflective, open to feedback, and committed to growth
-   Desire to learn through hands\-on experience
-   Organized, self\-motivated, and able to manage tasks and deadlines
-   Able to be adaptive, prioritize, and take initiative when needed

## Time commitment[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/peer\-programs/ubthechange\-community\-activators/\#time\-commitment](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/peer-programs/ubthechange-community-activators/#time-commitment)

The time commitment for the position is **15 to 25 hours** of independent project planning, including mandatory bi\-weekly meetings on **Wednesdays, 5:00 to 6:30 pm**\. 

For detailed time requirements, please review the position description\.

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/peer\-programs/ubthechange\-community\-activators/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/peer-programs/ubthechange-community-activators/#how-to-apply)

Applications are now closed\. Check back in 2027\.

Review the [2026/27 UBtheChange Community Activator position description](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/peer_programs_ubthechange.pdf) \(pdf\) for complete details about the role\.

## Skills developed[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/peer\-programs/ubthechange\-community\-activators/\#skills\-developed](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/peer-programs/ubthechange-community-activators/#skills-developed)

-   Ethical community engagement
-   Reciprocal relationship building, collaboration, and team building
-   Critical reflection and systems thinking approaches

title: Ordering a parchment (diploma)
content_markdown:
## About your parchment[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/ordering\-parchment\-diploma/\#about\-your\-parchment](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-parchment-diploma/#about-your-parchment)

Your parchment refers to your diploma\.

If you’re a UBC Okanagan student, please [read information](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/graduation/ordering-diplomas/) specific to your campus\.

You will receive your parchment at your in\-person graduation ceremony\. If you do not attend your ceremony, you can request to pick up your parchment afterwards at the [Enrolment Services Advising Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) on the first floor of [Brock Hall](http://www.maps.ubc.ca/PROD/index_detail.php?locat1=112-1) during opening hours, or have it sent by courier\. If you’d like it couriered, contact [graduation@ubc\.ca](mailto:graduation@ubc.ca) and they can further assist you\. Please include your full name and student number in the email\.

The information on this page is for students who have already graduated and need a replacement or certified copy of their parchment\.

If you have already graduated, and have not yet collected your parchment, please contact [graduation@ubc\.ca](mailto:graduation@ubc.ca) to arrange for courier delivery, or collect it in person at the [Enrolment Services Advising Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

If you need a Program Completion Letter, [download the letter](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/student-documents/downloading-your-program-completion-letter/) in Workday\.

Alumni who aren’t able to log into Workday can log into the [UBC Official Documents tool \(ODMT\)](https://ubc.appiancloud.com/suite/sites/ubc-official-documents) to access a Program Completion Letter\.  

## Replacement parchments[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/ordering\-parchment\-diploma/\#replacement\-parchments](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-parchment-diploma/#replacement-parchments)

A replacement parchment is an official reprint of your original UBC parchment\. It will look almost exactly like an original parchment, with a notation that says “Replacement Parchment month/year” in small print along the front and bottom\.

Rush orders are not available during May and November due to graduation, and in December over the holiday break\. Rush orders can be placed online and in person\.

| Order type | Estimated processing time | Cost in Canadian dollars |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standard | 2 to 4 weeks, plus [additional delivery time](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-parchment-diploma/#pick-up-and-delivery-options) | $75\.54 including tax per parchment \(courier cost is additional\) |
| Rush | 3 to 5 business days, plus [additional delivery time](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-parchment-diploma/#pick-up-and-delivery-options) | $151\.62 including tax per parchment \(courier cost is additional\) |

## Certified copies of your parchment[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/ordering\-parchment\-diploma/\#certified\-copies\-of\-your\-parchment](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-parchment-diploma/#certified-copies-of-your-parchment)

A certified copy is a photocopy of the original or replacement parchment with a stamp to certify that it is a true copy of the original document\.

Your original parchment is required to produce a certified copy\. If you do not have your original parchment, you must order a replacement parchment to request a certified copy\. A replacement parchment takes 2 to 4 weeks to process\.

For same\-day orders, you must place the order in person at the [Enrolment Services Advising Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) in Brock Hall\. You’ll receive your certified copy and original parchment immediately\.

| Order type | Estimated processing time | Cost in Canadian dollars |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Regular | 3 to 5 business days | $7\.81 including tax |
| Same\-day | 1 to 2 hours | $15\.84 including tax |

## How to order[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/ordering\-parchment\-diploma/\#how\-to\-order](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-parchment-diploma/#how-to-order)

### Ordering online

Learn how to [order a replacement parchment](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/student-documents/ordering-a-parchment/) and certified copies in Workday\.

Alumni who aren’t able to log into Workday can log into the [UBC Official Documents tool](https://ubc.appiancloud.com/suite/sites/ubc-official-documents) to order a parchment and certified copy instead\.

If you choose to order a certified copy online, you’ll need to order and pay for a replacement parchment as well\. This will increase the processing time by 2 to 4 weeks\.

### Ordering in person

You can order your replacement parchment and certified copies at the [Enrolment Services Advising Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) in Brock Hall during opening hours\. If you wish to order only your certified copy, make sure to bring your original parchment to the [Enrolment Services Advising Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\. You must present a photo ID when picking up your order and pay by debit card, VISA, or MasterCard\.

## Pick up and delivery options[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/ordering\-parchment\-diploma/\#pick\-up\-and\-delivery\-options](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-parchment-diploma/#pick-up-and-delivery-options)

### Courier delivery

If you choose courier delivery, replacement parchments or certified copies will be sent via FedEx as soon as they are processed\. Couriers cannot deliver to PO boxes\. You will be notified when your order has been completed\.

| Destination | Cost in Canadian dollars | Estimated delivery time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Within Canada | $23\.20, plus replacement or certified copy cost | 1 to 2 business days, depending on destination |
| United States | $45\.20, plus replacement or certified copy cost | 1 to 3 business days, depending on destination |
| International locations | $45\.20, plus replacement or certified copy cost | 3 to 5 business days, depending on destination |

### Picking up in person

You’ll receive an email when your document is ready for pick up at the [Enrolment Services Advising Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) in Brock Hall\. Check the [Enrolment Services Advising Centre webpage](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) for opening hours and seasonal hour changes\.

You must bring the following:

-   Proof of your name change if you’ve requested a name change on your parchment
-   A piece of photo ID with a name matching the name on the parchment for pick\-up

### If someone is picking up your documents for you

You must order your replacement parchment or certified copy yourself, even if you authorize a third party to pick it up\. The person picking up your document should be authorized on your Workday account\. They must have your student number and authorization code in addition to their identification\. Learn about [third\-party authorization](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/third-party-authorization/)\.

Alternatively, if you are unable to provide authorization through Workday, the person picking up your document must provide the following:

-   A completed [Third\-Party Pick\-up Form](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/third_party_document_authorization_form.pdf) \(pdf\)\.
-   The required identification noted in the pick\-up form instructions, for both the third party and the document owner\.

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/ordering\-parchment\-diploma/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-parchment-diploma/#additional-resources)

-   [Ordering your parchment in Workday](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/student-documents/ordering-a-parchment/)
-   [Applying to graduate](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/graduation/applying-graduate/)
-   [Changing the name on your parchment](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/changing-name-parchment-diploma/)
-   [Graduation FAQ](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/graduation/graduation-faq/)

title: Ordering a transcript
content_markdown:
## About transcript orders[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/ordering\-transcript/\#about\-transcript\-orders](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-transcript/#about-transcript-orders)

If you’re a UBC Okanagan student, please [read information](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/transcripts/) specific to your campus\.

If you are a current UBC student or alumnus, you can order an official transcript or download an unofficial transcript of your complete academic record at UBC\. Transcripts are confidential and can only be released by request from a student or alumnus\.

To order an official transcript or download an unofficial transcript, access the [UBC Official Documents tool](https://ubc.appiancloud.com/suite/sites/ubc-official-documents) \(ODMT\) from within Workday\. Alumni and former students who aren’t able to log into Workday can log into the UBC Official Documents tool directly\. If you are logging into the UBC Official Documents tool for the first time, you may have to wait 3 hours for your information to sync before you can proceed with the order\.

Review and follow the instructions to order your transcript in one of the available formats:

-   [Unofficial transcript](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-transcript/#unofficial-transcript), downloaded directly from the UBC Official Documents tool
-   [Official PDF transcript](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-transcript/#pdf-transcripts), sent through email
-   [Paper copy](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-transcript/#paper-transcripts) of your official transcript is available through:
    -   Mail
    -   In\-person pick\-up on campus
    -   Courier delivery

## Before you order[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/ordering\-transcript/\#before\-you\-order](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-transcript/#before-you-order)

1.  You will need a [Campus\-wide Login](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/logging-into-workday/) \(CWL\) account to access Workday or the [UBC Official Documents tool](https://ubc.appiancloud.com/suite/sites/ubc-official-documents)\. If you cannot remember your login details, [follow instructions online](https://it.ubc.ca/services/accounts-passwords/campus-wide-login-cwl/problems-your-cwl) to troubleshoot your access\.
2.  Check that your grades are up\-to\-date by downloading an [unofficial transcript](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-transcript/#unofficial-transcript) on the UBC Official Documents tool\. Updates to your academic record can take up to **48 hours** to appear on your transcript\. The grades that appear on the unofficial transcript will appear on an official transcript\.
3.  In addition to ensuring that your grades are up\-to\-date, please confirm your contact details and address under *Personal Info* in Workday\.
4.  Current students can download a [Confirmation of Enrolment Letter](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/student-documents/downloading-your-confirmation-of-enrolment-letter/) in Workday if needed\.  
    

## Important information about transcript orders[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/ordering\-transcript/\#important\-information\-about\-transcript\-orders](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-transcript/#important-information-about-transcript-orders)

-   All transcript orders are non\-refundable\. Cancellations and changes are not permitted\.
-   The student or alumnus must order the transcript themselves\.
-   Order your official transcript **48 hours** after your grades appear in your Workday account, since it takes time for the system to update changes on your official transcript\. To verify your grades will appear on your official transcript, check your [unofficial transcript](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/student-documents/ordering-a-transcript/) first\.
-   Your degree will be conferred after the Senate meets, and it will appear on the official transcript on **Thurs,** **May 21, 2026**\.
-   Your transcript will not show your courses for the current academic session until the first day of classes\. If you need your transcript to include your current academic session, you must order it **on or after** the first day of classes\.
-   UBC is not responsible for delayed or lost mail\.
-   Credit card payment cannot be accepted over email or the phone due to credit card security policies\.
-   Students on financial hold are not permitted to order transcripts\. Please contact [Enrolment Services](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) about paying overdue fees\.

### Submitting additional forms

Forms that need to be enclosed with the transcript must be submitted with the transcript order\. Right after you place your order, email the additional form\(s\), along with your name, order number, and student number to [transcripts\.students@ubc\.ca](mailto:transcripts.students@ubc.ca)\.

### Reference and application numbers

If you are ordering transcripts for an application, provide your reference or application number in the address field on your [transcript order](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/student-documents/ordering-a-transcript/) in the [UBC Official Documents tool](https://ubc.appiancloud.com/suite/sites/ubc-official-documents)\. Please note that the address field has a character limit of 57\. For example, write “Institution Name, Reference/Application \#1234”\.

Students are responsible for reviewing the application details and transcript requirements of the respective institution’s or organization’s website\. Students are also responsible for reordering and paying for another transcript if the original transcript method is not accepted\.

### World Education Services \(WES\)

UBC is a World Education Services \(WES\) institution partner and uses a closed, secure channel to directly transmit documents to WES\.

If you are ordering transcripts for WES, write “World Education Services Ref\#” and your WES reference number for the Institution/Name field\. The official email for WES is [submit@wes\.org](mailto:submit@wes.org)\.

Once you’ve placed the order, please email [transcripts\.students@ubc\.ca](mailto:transcripts.students@ubc.ca) with your order ID and reference number, and your transcript will be uploaded to the WES student portal\. Read the [WES document requirements](https://apps.wes.org/required-documents) for more information\.

### Transcript processing and grade availability

-   It takes at least 48 hours for official transcripts to be updated when changes are made to your Workday account\. This includes the posting of grades, changes to grades, or course adjustments during or after the [add/drop deadline](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/course-change-dates/)\.
-   Undergraduate students can view their grades after the last day of exams\.
    -   Term 2 grades will be visible starting **Apr 28, 2026** after grades have been submitted by instructors\.
    -   Summer grades will be visible on your official transcript 24\-48 hours after they have been posted on your Workday profile\.

## PDF transcripts[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/ordering\-transcript/\#pdf\-transcripts](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-transcript/#pdf-transcripts)

Official PDF transcripts cost $11\.60 CAD, including tax, and are sent through email\. They can take 24 hours to process\. Official PDF transcripts will be sent from [no\-reply@bpms\.svc\.ubc\.ca](mailto:no-reply@bpms.svc.ubc.ca) or [transcripts\.students@ubc\.ca](mailto:transcripts.students@ubc.ca)\.

Learn how to [order your official PDF transcript](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/student-documents/ordering-a-transcript/) in Workday\.

Alumni and former students who aren’t able to log into Workday can log into the [UBC Official Documents tool](https://ubc.appiancloud.com/suite/sites/ubc-official-documents) to order official transcripts\.

### Same\-day PDF transcripts

You must place the order in person one hour before the [Enrolment Services Advising Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) in [Brock Hall](http://www.maps.ubc.ca/PROD/index_detail.php?locat1=112-1) closes, which is typically before 3:00 pm\. You can expect to receive the PDF transcript through email by the end of the day\.

Same\-day PDF transcripts cost $17\.12 CAD, including tax\.

See the [Enrolment Services Advising Centre website](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) for any seasonal hour changes\.

### Unofficial transcripts

Unofficial transcripts are reports of a student’s academic record at UBC, and are intended for personal use only\. UBC does not issue unofficial transcripts to third parties\. Unofficial transcripts do not contain the UBC seal or the Registrar’s signature\.

Unofficial transcripts are free and can be downloaded from the [UBC Official Documents tool](https://ubc.appiancloud.com/suite/sites/ubc-official-documents) by current students, alumni, and former students who don’t have access to view past grades on Workday\.

Learn how to [download your unofficial transcript](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/student-documents/ordering-a-transcript/) in the UBC Official Documents tool\.

## Paper transcripts[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/ordering\-transcript/\#paper\-transcripts](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-transcript/#paper-transcripts)

All paper transcripts cost $12\.41 CAD, including tax\. There are 3 ways you can receive your paper transcript:

-   Mail
-   In\-person pick\-up at the [Enrolment Services Advising Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) in [Brock Hall](http://www.maps.ubc.ca/PROD/index_detail.php?locat1=112-1)
-   Courier delivery

Learn how to [order a paper transcript](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/student-documents/ordering-a-transcript/) in Workday\. Alumni and former students who aren’t able to log into Workday can log into the [UBC Official Documents tool](https://ubc.appiancloud.com/suite/sites/ubc-official-documents) to order official transcripts\.

### Delivery to a third party

If you are requesting your official transcripts to be sent to a third party, you must enter your own email address as the “Requestor Email” on the [UBC Official Documents tool](https://ubc.appiancloud.com/suite/sites/ubc-official-documents)\. Do not enter the third party’s email address in the Requestor Email section\.

**

Delivery by mail

**

You can request your paper transcript to be delivered by Canada Post regular mail by placing an order in [Workday](https://myworkday.ubc.ca/)\. Learn how to [order a paper transcript](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/student-documents/ordering-a-transcript/) in Workday\.

Orders take 3 to 5 business days to process, then additional time for delivery\. Regular mail is delivered through Canada Post and there is no tracking number available\. Please note that PO Box addresses are not accepted for courier orders\.

**

Pick up in person

**

You can pick up your paper transcript at the [Enrolment Services Advising Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) in [Brock Hall](http://www.maps.ubc.ca/PROD/index_detail.php?locat1=112-1)\. Please check the [Enrolment Services Advising Centre website](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) for their opening hours or any seasonal hour changes\.

Place your order online in [Workday](https://myworkday.ubc.ca/), or in person at the [https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/enrolment\-services\-advisors](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors)[Enrolment Services Advising Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) in Brock Hall\. You must pay by debit card, VISA, or Mastercard\.

Learn how to [order a transcript](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/student-documents/ordering-a-transcript/) in Workday\.

If you place your order before 6:00 pm, you can pick up your transcript on the next business day after 2:00 pm\.

You must provide the following to pick up your transcript in person:

-   Photo ID matching the name on the transcript
-   Proof of name change, where applicable

**If someone is picking up your transcripts on your behalf**

You must order your own transcript yourself, even if you authorize someone else to pick it up for you\. The person picking up your document must provide the following:

-   A completed [Third\-Party Pick\-up Form](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/third_party_document_authorization_form.pdf) \(pdf\)
-   The required identification noted in the pick\-up form instructions for both you and the person you authorized to pick up your transcript

Alternatively, if the person picking up your document is authorized on your Workday account, they must have your student number and authorization code in addition to their ID\.

Learn about [third\-party authorization](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/third-party-authorization/)\.

**

Delivery by courier

**

You can request a paper transcript to be delivered by courier via FedEx\. Couriers cannot deliver to PO boxes\. Delivery times depend on your location\. Learn how to [place an order](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/student-documents/ordering-a-transcript/) in Workday\.

You will be able to see your tracking number on your order summary one business day after your request has been placed\. Please allow for additional processing time by courier\.

#### Courier delivery times

| Destination | Cost in Canadian dollars | Estimated delivery time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Within Canada | $23\.20 plus transcript costs | 1 to 2 business days, depending on destination |
| United States | $45\.20 plus transcript costs | 1 to 3 business days, depending on destination |
| International locations | $45\.20 plus transcript costs | 3 to 5 business days, depending on destination |

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/ordering\-transcript/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-transcript/#if-you-have-questions)

For help with finances, registration, records, and more, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

title: About UBC Student Services
content_markdown:
UBC staff are here to help you throughout your university experience\.

## Academics[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/\#academics](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/#academics)

[Academic Advisors](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/)

Contact your faculty’s academic advising office for program planning and degree requirements\.

[Academic and learning resources](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/)

Browse services and tools to help you navigate your academic journey at UBC\.

[Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/)

Learn about accommodations if you have a disability or ongoing medical condition\.

[Enrolment Services Advisors](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)

Get help navigating UBC, from troubleshooting course registration to understanding financial support options\.

[International Student Advisors](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/)

Connect with an advisor on topics like study permits, working in Canada, and health insurance\.

[UBC Libraries](https://www.library.ubc.ca/)

Find research material or get help on research and citations\.

## Health and wellbeing[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/\#health\-and\-wellbeing](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/#health-and-wellbeing)

[Health and wellbeing](https://students.ubc.ca/health/)

Learn about the services available, including medical and mental health care, online programs, wellness advising, and more\.

[Nurse on Campus](https://students.ubc.ca/health/student-health-service/nurse-campus/)

Visit a registered nurse at their weekly drop\-in booths on campus throughout the school year\.

[Here2Talk](https://here2talk.ca/main)

Get started with free, 24/7 single\-session counselling by phone or online chat for all UBC students\.

[UBC REC](https://recreation.ubc.ca/)

Check out recreation programs and experiences, including intramural, group fitness classes, and sports facilities\.

[Wellness Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/health/wellness-centre/)

Speak to Wellness Centre Assistants for health, mental health, and wellbeing resources and support options\.

[Wellness Centre Sexual Health Shop](https://students.ubc.ca/health/wellness-centre/wellness-centre-sexual-health-shop/)

Browse and purchase safer sex, sexual health, and sex toy products\.

[UBC Accessibility Shuttle](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/ubc-accessibility-shuttle/)

Travel on campus with the free, shared ride service if you have a condition that impacts your mobility\.

[Student Recovery Community](https://students.ubc.ca/health/ubc-student-recovery-community/)

Get one\-on\-one peer support in a safe and confidential setting or join a peer\-based support group for addiction recovery\.

[Food Hub Market](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/food-hub-market/)

Shop for affordable groceries and build food literacy through workshops on meal planning, practical cooking skills, and more\.

[Group counselling](https://students.ubc.ca/health/counselling-services/group-counselling-programs/)

Join a staff\-facilitated peer group to discuss your experiences and concerns in a supportive environment\.

## Sexual assault support[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/\#sexual\-assault\-support](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/#sexual-assault-support)

Help is available if you have experienced sexual assault or sexual violence\. We believe you\.

[Sexual Violence Prevention Response Office](https://svpro.ubc.ca/)

Get support if you’ve experienced sexual assault or violence

[AMS Sexual Assault Support Centre](https://www.ams.ubc.ca/support-services/sasc/)

Access support and educational resources if you’re a survivor of sexualized violence\.

## Student government[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/\#student\-government](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/#student-government)

Your student government plays an active role at UBC by offering student\-run services, businesses, and events\.

[Alma Mater Society \(AMS\)](https://www.ams.ubc.ca/)

Find out how the AMS supports undergraduate students through services, advocacy, and campus\-wide resources\.

[Graduate Student Society \(GSS\)](https://gss.ubc.ca/)

Learn more about how the GSS assists graduate students through advocacy, services, and resources tailored to grad studies\.

## UBC community services[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/\#ubc\-community\-services](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/#ubc-community-services)

Browse on\-campus spaces and services for everyday and long\-term support\.

[UBC Bookstore](https://bookstore.ubc.ca/)

Shop online for textbooks, lab equipment, UBC merchandise, and get your digital UBC Card\.

[UBC Housing on campus](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/)

Get information on living in residence and meal plans\.

[Housing for graduate students](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/campus-community/housing)

Learn about housing considerations and options both on and off campus

[UBC Food Services](https://food.ubc.ca/)

Check out what restaurants and eateries are open on campus, and get tips on cooking and eating healthy\.

[Chaplains](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/)

Join other students in a faith tradition or get pastoral or spiritual counselling\.

[Learning Spaces](https://learningspaces.ubc.ca/)

Find a classroom or informal learning space on campus for conversation or quiet study\.

[UBC Parking](https://parking.ubc.ca/)

Plan ahead for parking and know where to park when driving to campus\.

[Community Safety](http://communitysafety.ubc.ca/)

Access 24/7 support for first aid, security services, and Safewalk\.  

[Equity & Inclusion](https://equity.ubc.ca/)

Get confidential advising for discrimination or harassment concerns\.

[UBC Ombuds Office](https://ombudsoffice.ubc.ca/)

Receive confidential and impartial support if you need help navigating UBC policies and processes\.

[First Nations House of Learning](https://fnhl.ubc.ca/)

Learn about the dedicated space for Indigenous peoples to share their knowledge and cultures, and host a range of activities\.

[Black Student Space](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/black-student-space/)

Drop by to study, connect, and attend events in a welcoming space for Black students\.

[UBC Life Building](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/ubc-life-building/)

Drop by the student space to grab food, eat lunch, work out, study, or hang out with friends\.

## Connect with UBC Student Life online[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/\#connect\-with\-ubc\-student\-life\-online](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/#connect-with-ubc-student-life-online)

The UBC Life Instagram and TikTok are your go\-to sources for the latest events, opportunities, and insights\. From study hacks and wellness tips, to student stories and campus happenings, get the inside scoop on university life\.

[UBC Student Life on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/ubc_studentlife)

Discover campus highlights, key events, and need\-to\-know updates to make the most of your time at UBC\.

[UBC Student Life on TikTok](https://www.tiktok.com/@ubcstudentlife)

Get a real look at students life at UBC—created by students, for students\.

## Crisis support 24/7[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/\#crisis\-support\-24\-7](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/#crisis-support-24-7)

Get help if you or someone else is in immediate danger, or at risk of harming yourself or others\. Call [911](tel:911) or visit your [nearest emergency room](https://www.vch.ca/en/health-topics/emergency-care)\.

If you or someone you know is feeling hopeless or at risk of harm, call or text [988](tel:988) toll\-free at any time to reach the [Suicide Crisis Helpline](https://988.ca/)\.

title: Black Student Space
content_markdown:
> > Black Student Orientation
> 
> > If you’re new to UBC, [register online](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0TbhaCCZOqBcMC2?utm_source=sfmc&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=RMPSE+07+26+Black+student+orientation&utm_term=https%3a%2f%2fubc.ca1.qualtrics.com%2fjfe%2fform%2fSV_0TbhaCCZOqBcMC2) for the orientation event on **Thurs, Sep 10**\. Meet other Black students, faculty, staff, and clubs, enjoy a complimentary dinner, and enter to win prizes\.

## About the space[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/black\-student\-space/\#about\-the\-space](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/black-student-space/#about-the-space)

The Black Student Space is an identity\-affirming space available only for Black undergraduate and graduate students currently enrolled at the UBC Vancouver campus\. Students can use the space to  connect with peers , recharge, host events , and build community\. They can also access networks, programming, and resources that are specific, relevant, and representative of Black experiences, intersectional identities, and cultures\. 

The Black Student Space recognizes that anti\-Black racism exists in all systems, including higher education, and provides a safe space and dedicated support that contributes to Black students’ academic success, personal growth, and wellbeing\. All staff and faculty are welcome to organize programming and resources in the space that support the needs and interests of Black UBC Students\.

### History of the Black Student Space

The Black Student Space was opened in fall 2023 by the [Office of the Vice\-President Students](https://vpstudents.ubc.ca/) and the [Centre for Student Development and Leadership](https://students.ubc.ca/centre-for-student-development-and-leadership/), in consultation and co\-creation with the UBC Black student community on the Vancouver campus\. It is an intentional step in response to the [Student Strategic Plan](https://studentplan.ubc.ca/) \(strategies 4 and 9\), as well as the [Anti\-Racism and Inclusive Excellence Recommendations Taskforce Report](https://antiracism.ubc.ca/) \(recommendations 3 and 41\)\. 

## Location and layout[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/black\-student\-space/\#location\-and\-layout](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/black-student-space/#location-and-layout)

The space is located in the Exchange Building \([5960 Student Union Boulevard](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Exchange+Student+Residence/@49.2685506,-123.2476201,15z/data=!4m6!3m5!1s0x548673f2f3ddf7db:0x400bae9c95148b3!8m2!3d49.2685506!4d-123.2476201!16s%2Fg%2F11hzhg7zh1?entry=ttu)\) and consists of an Upper and Lower area that cater to different activities: 

-   The Upper Space, located on the second level, is a dedicated quiet area for studying, individual contemplation, meditation, and other quiet activities\. See how it looks with the [interactive tool](https://my.matterport.com/show/?m=WxrQp1BgNWN)\.
-   The Lower Space includes a lounge space for napping and resting, as well as a large open area for events and group activities\. Students, staff, and faculty can book the Lower Space\. Find out how it looks with the [interactive tool](https://my.matterport.com/show/?m=GZX91RC2KRd)\.

## Space amenities and features[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/black\-student\-space/\#space\-amenities\-and\-features](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/black-student-space/#space-amenities-and-features)

To ensure a welcoming space, the Black Student Space offers multi\-purpose activities from baking, hosting movie nights, reflecting and writing, to hosting events\.

Review the lists below to learn more about the amenities available in each space\.

**

Upper space for quiet study and reflection

**

-   Quiet study and contemplation area
-   Beanbag chairs
-   Ample charging outlets
-   Library
-   Meeting room with capacity for 6 to 8 people
-   Whiteboards and bulletin boards

**

Lower space for lounging and events

**

-   Moveable furniture for study, group activities, and events
-   Lounge and napping area with couches and fireplace
-   Television and projector
-   Board games

**

Shared facilities in both spaces

**

-   Kitchens with oven, microwaves, refrigerators, small appliances, dishes, and cutlery
-   Showers and lockers
-   Printer and scanner
-   Refreshments 

**

Accessibility supports

**

-   Ramp access at the main building entrance
-   Wheelchair accessible gender\-neutral bathrooms and shower facilities
-   Wheelchair accessible automated doors
-   Soft lighting and warm paint colours
-   Elevator access between Upper and Lower Spaces

### Opening hours

The Black Student Space is closed on all [statutory holidays](https://hr.ubc.ca/working-ubc/statutory-holidays) observed by UBC\.

-   **Monday**: 10:00 am to 8:00 pm
-   **Tuesday**: 10:00 am to 8:00 pm
-   **Wednesday**: 10:00 am to 8:00 pm
-   **Thursday**: 10:00 am to 8:00 pm
-   **Friday**: 10:00 am to 8:00 pm

[black student space puzzle](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/black_student_space_puzzle.jpg)

## How to access the Black Student Space[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/black\-student\-space/\#how\-to\-access\-the\-black\-student\-space](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/black-student-space/#how-to-access-the-black-student-space)

The space is open to all currently enrolled UBC Vancouver students who identify as Black, including, but not limited to, those of Black African descent, African\-American, African\-Canadian, Afro\-Caribbean, Afro\-Latinx, and Afro\-Indigenous heritage\.

To access the Black Student Space, please complete the sign up form below\. Requests are processed bi\-weekly\. You will receive a confirmation email once your access is approved\.

For urgent access, email [bss\.info@ubc\.ca](mailto:bss.info@ubc.ca)\.

title: Centre for Community Engaged Learning
content_markdown:
The Centre’s programs provide you with community\-based opportunities to learn, participate, and collaborate on projects on and off campus\. You can engage with passionate students and community partners through a [UBtheChange](https://students.ubc.ca/career/community-experiences/ubthechange/) event or Community Action Day project, present your research skills at the [Multidisciplinary Undergraduate Research Conference](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/multidisciplinary-undergraduate-research-conference/), lead a project by writing a [community grant](https://students.ubc.ca/career/community-experiences/grants-community-projects/), and learn how strategize for action on complex social issues through the [Social Impact Lab](https://students.ubc.ca/career/community-experiences/social-impact-lab/)\.

The Centre also provides resources and support to instructors, departments, and faculties to enhance teaching and learning processes and connect university resources to the community in ways that support lasting relationships\.

### Reasons to connect with the Centre

-   Connect with community organizations to lead or collaborate on projects\.
-   Learn how to affect positive social change in your community\.
-   Grow your network by connecting with like\-minded students and community\.
-   Channel your values into personal growth\.
-   Explore something you are passionate about\.

### Programs offered

In person and virtual programming are being offered\. Please check out the programs below\.

-   [CCEL workshops](https://students.ubc.ca/career/community-experiences/ccel-workshops/)  
    Learn how to get started in community\-based projects and learning experiences\.
-   [Social Impact Lab](https://students.ubc.ca/career/community-experiences/social-impact-lab/)  
    Develop ideas and solutions through actionable projects that tackle social and environmental issues\.
-   [UBtheChange](https://students.ubc.ca/career/community-experiences/ubthechange/)  
    Work towards becoming a changemaker through on\-campus engagements and short\-term community projects\.
-   [Community grants](https://students.ubc.ca/career/community-experiences/grants-community-projects/)  
    Apply to fund your in\-person or virtual projects\.
-   [Multidisciplinary Undergraduate Research Conference](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/multidisciplinary-undergraduate-research-conference/)  
    Present your research with fellow UBC students, family, and friends\.
-   [Student Directed Seminars](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/student-directed-seminars/)  
    Coordinate your own 3\-credit seminar class with a small group of peers\.

## Faculty and partner resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/centre\-community\-engaged\-learning/\#faculty\-and\-partner\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-community-engaged-learning/#faculty-and-partner-resources)

### Faculty resources

Working under the principles of Community\-Based Experiential Learning \(CBEL\), we provide support to faculty and staff members who are seeking to enhance student learning and further their teaching practices by working with nonprofits and community organizations\. 

See [more information](https://ccel.ubc.ca/faculty) on faculty resources\. 

### Community partners

The Centre for Community Engaged provides its community partners with resources to help them build relationships with students and facilitate successful projects\. 

Find [more details](https://ccel.ubc.ca/community) on community partner resources\.

title: Centre for Accessibility
content_markdown:
> > Awards for students with disabilities
> 
> > Browse and apply for [bursaries and scholarships](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-disabilities/descriptions-awards-disabilities/) from **Jul 15** to **Sep 15, 2026**\.

## What the Centre can help with[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/centre\-for\-accessibility/\#what\-the\-centre\-can\-help\-with](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/#what-the-centre-can-help-with)

The Centre for Accessibility facilitates disability\-related accommodations designed to remove barriers for students with disabilities and ongoing medical conditions in all aspects of university life\. The Centre works with students to explore their accommodation needs, and to connect them with appropriate support and resources\. 

## How UBC accommodates students with disabilities[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/centre\-for\-accessibility/\#how\-ubc\-accommodates\-students\-with\-disabilities](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/#how-ubc-accommodates-students-with-disabilities)

[Disability Accommodation Policy LR7](https://universitycounsel.ubc.ca/policies/disability-accommodation-policy/) provides guidance for students, faculty, and staff to understand the process through which accommodations for students with disabilities are made at the University\. It defines responsibilities and key terms regarding accommodation\. Read through [frequently asked questions](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/frequently-asked-questions-about-policy-lr7-accommodation-disabilities/) about the policy\.

## Requesting an accommodation[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/centre\-for\-accessibility/\#requesting\-an\-accommodation](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/#requesting-an-accommodation)

At UBC, [academic accommodations](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/) are intended to provide students with a disability or ongoing medical condition access to the academic environment\. They do not apply to temporary injuries or acute medical conditions that are not expected to persist for longer than one term\.

Before requesting an accommodation, you must [register with the Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/registering-centre-accessibility/)\. Registration with the Centre is a multi\-step process and can take some time\. We encourage you to start the process as early in the term as possible\. Please reach out to the Centre directly if you have any questions about the process\.

## If you’re already registered with the Centre[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/centre\-for\-accessibility/\#if\-youre\-already\-registered\-with\-the\-centre](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/#if-youre-already-registered-with-the-centre)

Please log into your [Clockwork account](https://clockwork.as.it.ubc.ca/ClockWork/custom/misc/home.aspx) and submit an accommodation letter and/or exam reservation request\. The Centre for Accessibility online services portal, Clockwork, is for UBC Vancouver students only\.

If eligible, submit your peer notetaking request as well\. Review important [notetaking request guidelines](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/types-academic-accommodations/)\.

[Student login](https://clockwork.as.it.ubc.ca/ClockWork/custom/misc/home.aspx)

## Information for faculty[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/centre\-for\-accessibility/\#information\-for\-faculty](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/#information-for-faculty)

If you are a faculty member, please log in to view student accommodation letters and upcoming exams requested by your students registered with the Centre\. The list of Accommodation Letters does not represent the students who have booked an exam\.

Exam information, including duration, format, and exam allowances must be received at least 2 business days prior to the exam date, otherwise the Centre is unable to host the exams\. UBC’s obligation to provide the exam accommodations will fall to the instructor\. You will be responsible for implementing the exam accommodations, as listed on the Letter of Accommodation\.

Review the [online guide](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/centre_for_accessibility_canvas_guide.pdf) \(pdf\) for how to adjust for student exam accommodations\.

View [Faculty and Staff resources](https://facultystaff.students.ubc.ca/student-affairs/centre-accessibility) for more information and answers to frequently asked questions about Genio Notes\.

[Faculty login](https://clockwork.as.it.ubc.ca/ClockWork/user/instructor/default.aspx)

## Contact us[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/centre\-for\-accessibility/\#contact\-us](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/#contact-us)

-   **Phone**: [604 822 5844](tel:6048225844)
-   **Fax**: [604 822 6655](tel:6048226655)
-   **Email**: [info\.accessibility@ubc\.ca](mailto:info.accessibility@ubc.ca)

### Locations

-   **Main office**: Room 3110, Brock Commons South \([6180 Walter Gage Road](https://maps.app.goo.gl/LRv3y4Pe7aZsZSGe6)\)
-   **Accommodated Exam Writing Centre:** Room 3080, Brock Commons South \([6180 Walter Gage Road](https://maps.app.goo.gl/LRv3y4Pe7aZsZSGe6)\)

### Opening hours

The Centre for Accessibility is closed on all [statutory holidays](https://hr.ubc.ca/working-ubc/statutory-holidays) observed by UBC\.

-   **Monday**: 8:30 am to 4:30 pm
-   **Tuesday**: 8:30 am to 5:00 pm
-   **Wednesday**: 8:30 am to 4:30 pm
-   **Thursday**: 8:30 am to 4:00 pm
-   **Friday**: 8:30 am to 4:30 pm

### Drop\-in advising hours

Drop\-in advising is **only** available for students who are already registered with the Centre and have quick or urgent questions that cannot wait for a full advising appointment with their advisor\.

-   **Monday**: 10:00 am to 4:00 pm
-   **Tuesday**: 10:00 am to 4:00 pm

content_markdown:
## What ES Advisors can help with[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/enrolment\-services\-advisors/\#what\-es\-advisors\-can\-help\-with](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/#what-es-advisors-can-help-with)

If you are an undergraduate student in a degree program, you’re assigned a dedicated Enrolment Services Advisor \(ES Advisor\) to help you navigate registration, finances, and more at UBC\. The majority of newly admitted students are assigned an ES Advisor by the end of June\. If you don’t have an assigned advisor, you can still connect with other ES Advisors for help\.

For questions about course planning or program requirements, please connect directly with your [academic advising office](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/)\.

Reach out early for support, especially during registration periods and the beginning of school terms\. Enrolment Services will offer extended hours of phone support during the registration periods in June and July\.

### Top reasons to connect

-   Get help with managing your finances or creating a [financial plan](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/)\.
-   Talk to someone about [scholarships, bursaries, awards](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/), and [student loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/)\.
-   Walk through the ways you can pay your [tuition and fees](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/paying-tuition/)\.
-   Understand UBC regulations and processes\.
-   Find support for [course registration](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/) issues\.
-   Access and update your [student records](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/)\.
-   Request letters, complete forms, or gather signatures required from the Registrar’s office\.

## Contact us[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/enrolment\-services\-advisors/\#contact\-us](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/#contact-us)

Enrolment Services is closed on all [statutory holidays](https://hr.ubc.ca/working-ubc/statutory-holidays) observed by UBC\.

### Connect online

-   **If you’re an undergraduate student,** learn how to [find your ES Advisor’s email](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/ubc-advisor-contacts/finding-your-enrolment-services-advisors-contact-information/) in Workday\. Your ES Advisor is your main point of contact in Enrolment Services\. Please contact them directly with questions\.
-   **If you’re a graduate, postgraduate, other type of student, or an alumni,** submit your question through the [online contact form](https://www.askme.ubc.ca/form/s/)\.

### Reach out by phone

Contact Enrolment Services by phone during opening hours\. Please have your student number ready when you call\.

-   **Phone**: [604 822 9836](tel:6048229836)
-   **Toll\-free**: [1 877 272 1422](tel:18772721422)

### Visit in person

Drop by the Enrolment Services Advising Centre in [Brock Hall](https://www.maps.ubc.ca/PROD/index_detail.php?locat1=112-1) \(1874 East Mall\) during opening hours:

title: International Student Advising
content_markdown:
## About International Student Advising[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/international\-student\-advising/\#about\-international\-student\-advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/#about-international-student-advising)

If you have questions about life as an international student, International Student Advising is here to help\. International Student Advisors are Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultants \(RCICs\) or Regulated International Student Immigration Advisors \(RISIAs\) who can support you in your experience as a UBC international student\.

### Top reasons to connect

-   Get help with your [visa](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/), [study permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/), and [work permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/) application\.
-   Ask about part\-time or full\-time [work requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/)\.
-   Learn about your [health insurance coverage](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/)\.
-   Talk to someone about transitioning to life in Canada\.

## International Student Guide[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/international\-student\-advising/\#international\-student\-guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/#international-student-guide)

Find everything you need to know about life as an international student at UBC’s Vancouver campus\.

[View the guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/)

## Immigration FAQs[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/international\-student\-advising/\#immigration\-faqs](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/#immigration-faqs)

Get the [latest updates on immigration](https://students.ubc.ca/news/category-ircc-policy-updates/), and answers to common immigration and health insurance questions in the [Frequently Asked Questions](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-immigration-health-insurance-faq/) \(FAQ\)\.

## Online application review courses[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/international\-student\-advising/\#online\-application\-review\-courses](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/#online-application-review-courses)

Advisors are not able to fully review immigration applications\. Before applying for your initial study permit, study permit extension, Temporary Resident Visa, or Post\-Graduation Work Permit, sign up for the [Canvas application review courses](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/tutorials/#online-application-review-courses) to go over your application and avoid common mistakes\.

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/international\-student\-advising/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/#additional-resources)

International Student Advising is unable to help with the following topics, but you can find information at the links below:

-   [Permanent Residence](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/prepare-leave-ubc#staying-in-canada)
-   [Prospective student inquiries](https://www.ubc.ca/prospective-students/)
-   [Postdoctoral fellows immigration documents](https://hr.ubc.ca/contact/contact-housing-and-relocation-services)
-   [Parent, extended family, or friend’s immigration documents](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/inviting-friends-family-visit/) \(International Student Advising can only support spouses, common\-law partners, and children\)
-   [Work permits unrelated to studies](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/#other-types-of-work-permits-unrelated-to-studies)
-   [Influencing processing times](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/check-processing-times.html)
-   [Contacting IRCC on your behalf](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/tips-communicating-immigration-refugees-citizenship-canada-ircc/)
-   [Taxes](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/)
-   [Starting your own business](https://smallbusinessbc.ca/)
-   [US immigration](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas.html)
-   Advising non\-UBC students \(contact your institution’s international student office\)

## Contact us[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/international\-student\-advising/\#contact\-us](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/#contact-us)

Please review the [International Student Guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/) before connecting with our office\.

-   **Phone**: [604 822 5021](tel:6048225021)
-   **Address**: Room 1200, UBC Life Building \([6138 Student Union Boulevard](https://goo.gl/maps/sLxUUvBedGh5uA8eA)\)

### Submit a question

Leave a message for an International Student Advisor to get advice\. Be sure to include your UBC student number and as much detail about your situation as possible\.  
  

[Submit a question](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0J8VRJgJQkuO2b4)

### In\-person advising

Visit the International Student Advising office in the UBC Life Building at room 1200 of [6138 Student Union Boulevard](https://goo.gl/maps/sLxUUvBedGh5uA8eA), located on the main floor across from Starbucks\.

Before arriving at the office, you can sign in to the [virtual line](https://vue.comm100.com/joinqueue/80000265/location?locationId=0bd862af924b401d8f888a4afdb195ac) to save your spot\. You can also join the virtual line at the office by using a QR code\.

International Student Advising is closed on all [statutory holidays](https://hr.ubc.ca/working-ubc/statutory-holidays) observed by UBC\.

-   **Monday**: 9:30 am to 12:00 pm, 1:00 pm to 4:00 pm
-   **Tuesday**: 9:30 am to 12:00 pm, 1:00 pm to 4:00 pm
-   **Wednesday**: 1:00 to 4:00 pm
-   **Thursday**: 9:30 am to 12:00 pm, 1:00 pm to 4:00 pm
-   **Friday**: 9:30 am to 12:00 pm, 1:00 pm to 4:00 pm

### Zoom advising

International Student Advising is available to meet virtually on Zoom\. Join the [virtual line](https://vue.comm100.com/joinqueue/80000265/location?locationId=0bd862af924b401d8f888a4afdb195ac) with your email address and Canadian or US phone number, if you have one, and you’ll receive the Zoom link when it’s your turn in line\. You will get updates about your place in the line by email and text message, if providing a Canadian or US phone number\. 

If you do not have a Canadian or US phone number, you can still join the virtual line, but you will not receive text messages with updates\.

While waiting to connect with our office, you can check your place in line, push your appointment back, leave the line, or get an update when it’s almost your turn\.

Find [step\-by\-step instructions](https://support.zoom.us/hc/en-us/articles/201362193-Joining-a-Meeting) on how to download and use Zoom\.

Zoom advising hours are as follows\. Advising is closed on statutory holidays\.

-   **Monday**: 9:30 to 11:30 am, 2:00 to 4:00 pm
-   **Tuesday**: 9:30 to 11:30 am, 2:00 to 4:00 pm
-   **Wednesday**: 2:00 to 4:00 pm
-   **Thursday**: 9:30 to 11:30 am, 2:00 to 4:00 pm
-   **Friday**: 9:30 to 11:30 am, 2:00 to 4:00 pm

While we strive to support as many students as possible, when there is high volume, we may not be able to connect with you\. If you are in the queue and there are a large number of students in front of you before Zoom advising hours end, you will be removed from the line\. We apologize for not being able to assist you at that time\. Please rejoin the queue when we re\-open or send us a [webform](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0J8VRJgJQkuO2b4)\.

## Get immigration reminders[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/international\-student\-advising/\#get\-immigration\-reminders](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/#get-immigration-reminders)

Add your document expiry dates to the confidential [UBC Reminder System](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/immigration-documents-reminder-system/) and receive notifications for when you need to extend your documents\. You can also get helpful tips on how to prepare your application\. 

## Subscribe to the International Student Life Newsletter[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/international\-student\-advising/\#subscribe\-to\-the\-international\-student\-life\-newsletter](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/#subscribe-to-the-international-student-life-newsletter)

Stay informed through biweekly updates for international students at UBC Vancouver\. The newsletter features campus events, workshops, immigration updates, helpful resources, and student stories\. Learn more and [subscribe online](https://blogs.ubc.ca/ubcisa/international-student-life-newsletter/)\.

content_markdown:
> > Temporary service change

> > Due to renovations, the Career Centre’s physical location is closed\. All appointments and in\-person services for the Career Centre will be virtual until **Sep 14, 2026**\.

## About the Centre[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/ubc\-career\-centre/\#about\-the\-centre](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/ubc-career-centre/#about-the-centre)

The Career Centre helps UBC Vancouver students and recent graduates explore possibilities, gain confidence, and take the first or next step in their career\.

Whether you’re attending a career fair, exploring job opportunities, or looking for support with your resume and cover letter, we’re here to guide you through the process\.

Browse the services we offer:

-   [One\-on\-one appointments](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/ubc-career-centre/#book-appointment)
-   [Career events, workshops, and fairs](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/)
-   [Work Learn program](https://students.ubc.ca/career/work-learn-program/)
-   [Undergraduate research opportunities](https://students.ubc.ca/career/undergraduate-research/)
-   [CareersOnline Job board](https://ubc-csm.symplicity.com/)

[A UBC student with a Career Educator at the Career Centre space during a one\-on\-one advising appointment](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/career_centre_unit_introduction-1024x391.jpg)

## Contact us[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/ubc\-career\-centre/\#contact\-us](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/ubc-career-centre/#contact-us)

-   **Phone**: [tel:604 822 4011](tel:604%20822%204011)[604 822 4011](tel:604%20822%204011)
-   **Email:** [mailto:career\.centre@ubc\.ca](mailto:career.centre@ubc.ca)[career\.centre@ubc\.ca](mailto:career.centre@ubc.ca)

## Book a career appointment

Book a one\-on\-one discussion with a Career Educator to explore future career possibilities or to walk through your job application\.

Appointments are held virtually at this time and can be scheduled for 15, 30, or 45 minutes\. Current students and recent graduates up to 12 months after graduation can book an appointment\.

1.  Log into [CareersOnline](https://ubc-csm.symplicity.com/index.php) with your CWL\. 
2.  Select “Appointments” in the top menu\. 
3.  Choose “Book New Appointment”\.
4.  If you have a specific date, time, advising topic, or advisor you’d like to meet, fill out the fields\. Otherwise, leave the fields empty and click “Check availability”\.
5.  Select your preferred appointment time and complete the information requested\.

Once you’ve booked an appointment, you will no longer be able to see the times to book another appointment\.

If you need to cancel or reschedule, please call [604 822 4011](tel:6048224011) or email [career\.centre@ubc\.ca](mailto:career.centre@ubc.ca)\.

title: Wellness Centre
content_markdown:
## About the Wellness Centre[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/wellness\-resources/wellness\-centre/\#about\-the\-wellness\-centre](https://students.ubc.ca/health/wellness-resources/wellness-centre/#about-the-wellness-centre)

The Wellness Centre believes that a healthy mind, body, and spirit are foundations for students to achieve their personal and academic goals\. Located in the [UBC Life Building](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/ubc-life-building/), the Wellness Centre is a peer\-hosted space that offers many wellbeing programs, services and resources for students\. For regular updates about our programs and services, follow the Wellness Centre on Instagram at [@ubcwellnesscentre](https://instagram.com/ubcwellnesscentre)\.

The Wellness Centre does not offer crisis support or medical advice\. Consult [crisis support options](https://students.ubc.ca/health/crisis-support-services/) for what to do during emergency situations\.

### About the Health Promotion Team

The Student Health and Wellbeing’s Health Promotion Team leads health education and promotion initiatives to enhance the health equity and wellbeing of individual students and communities of students at UBC\.

Learn more about their goals and the work they do at UBC on the [Faculty and Staff website](https://facultystaff.students.ubc.ca/health-wellbeing/health-equity-promotion-education)\.

## Contact us[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/wellness\-resources/wellness\-centre/\#contact\-us](https://students.ubc.ca/health/wellness-resources/wellness-centre/#contact-us)

-   **Phone:** [604 822 8450](tel:604%20822%208450)
-   **Address:** [UBC Life Building](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/ubc-life-building/), Room 1400 \([6138 Student Union Boulevard](https://maps.app.goo.gl/ZoYsuzaB6A63orUm6)\)

Drop by the Wellness Centre in the UBC Life Building or [ask us a question](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3JyO1ZHby4ZrbD0) you may have about health and wellness resources\.

### Opening hours

The Wellness Centre is closed on all [statutory holidays](https://hr.ubc.ca/working-ubc/statutory-holidays) observed by UBC\.

-   **Monday**: 11:00 am to 3:00 pm
-   **Tuesday**: 11:00 am to 3:00 pm
-   **Wednesday**: 11:00 am to 3:00 pm
-   **Thursday**: 11:00 am to 3:00 pm

## Ask the Wellness Info Desk about resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/wellness\-resources/wellness\-centre/\#ask\-the\-wellness\-info\-desk\-about\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/health/wellness-resources/wellness-centre/#ask-the-wellness-info-desk-about-resources)

Wellness Centre Assistants can answer your questions about health, mental health and wellbeing resources, services, and support options\.

Get connected through one of the following options:

-   **Drop by in person**  
    Visit the Wellness Centre Info Desk in the [UBC Life Building](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/ubc-life-building/) during opening hours\.
-   **Submit a question online**  
    You can also [complete the online form](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3JyO1ZHby4ZrbD0) and receive an email response within 3 to 5 business days\. Please review the [Privacy Statement](https://students.ubc.ca/health/wellness-resources/wellness-centre/#privacy-statement) before submitting your question\.
-   **Connect with us through phone**  
    You can also call us during our opening hours at [604 822 8450](tel:6048228450)\.

## Pick up harm reduction supplies: Naloxone training and fentanyl test strips[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/wellness\-resources/wellness\-centre/\#pick\-up\-harm\-reduction\-supplies\-naloxone\-training\-and\-fentanyl\-test\-strips](https://students.ubc.ca/health/wellness-resources/wellness-centre/#pick-up-harm-reduction-supplies-naloxone-training-and-fentanyl-test-strips)

In response to the accidental drug poisoning crisis in British Columbia, naloxone and fentanyl test strips are available for free and anonymously at the UBC Wellness Centre and at many other locations [across campus](https://www.ams.ubc.ca/support-services/student-resources/ubc-harm-reduction-resources/)\.

Naloxone is a medication that can reverse accidental drug poisoning from fentanyl\. Kits are available for people who could experience accidental drug poisoning from the toxic drug supply in British Columbia or those who might witness a family member or friend experience drug poisoning\.

Fentanyl test strips check substances for the presence of fentanyl\. You can pick up test strips from the front table at the Wellness Centre and get naloxone training during opening hours\.

## Visit the Sexual Health Shop[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/wellness\-resources/wellness\-centre/\#visit\-the\-sexual\-health\-shop](https://students.ubc.ca/health/wellness-resources/wellness-centre/#visit-the-sexual-health-shop)

The Sexual Health Shop is a welcoming and inclusive sexual health space where you can learn more about sexual wellbeing or purchase accessible safer sex, sexual health, and sex toy products\. Drop by in person or order online\.

[Find out how](https://students.ubc.ca/health/sexual-health/wellness-centre-sexual-health-shop/)

## Wellbeing Training and Education[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/wellness\-resources/wellness\-centre/\#wellbeing\-training\-and\-education](https://students.ubc.ca/health/wellness-resources/wellness-centre/#wellbeing-training-and-education)

Wellness Centre offers a range of self\-directed learning courses on Canvas accessible to all UBC students with a CWL\. Topics include health resource navigation, mental health, substance use health, and more\.

You can also book wellbeing workshops, activities, and events led by staff and students for student groups, club events, and more\.

[Get details](https://students.ubc.ca/health/wellness-resources/wellbeing-training-education/)

## UBC Student Recovery Community \(SRC\)[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/wellness\-resources/wellness\-centre/\#ubc\-student\-recovery\-community\-src](https://students.ubc.ca/health/wellness-resources/wellness-centre/#ubc-student-recovery-community-src)

The [UBC Student Recovery Community](https://students.ubc.ca/health/substance-use-health-harm-reduction/ubc-student-recovery-community/) is a safe, welcoming, and inclusive space for students who are in recovery, or curious to explore their relationship with substance use and/or behavioural addictions, including disordered eating, gaming, gambling, and more\.

## Privacy Statement[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/wellness\-resources/wellness\-centre/\#privacy\-statement](https://students.ubc.ca/health/wellness-resources/wellness-centre/#privacy-statement)

To speak with a Wellness Centre Assistant through the online form, you will be asked for your name, email, and location to identify resources relevant to where you’re located\.

The personal information and any other information you provide during this session are collected under the authority of section 26\(c\) of the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act \(FIPPA\)\.

Your information will be kept confidential except if your information is required to provide you with the assistance you have requested, or as required for health, safety, or legal reasons\. If you have questions about the collection of this information, please email [wellness\.centre@ubc\.ca](mailto:wellness.centre@ubc.ca)\.
