title: Wellness Centre Sexual Health Shop
content_markdown:
## About the shop[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/sexual\-health/wellness\-centre\-sexual\-health\-shop/\#about\-the\-shop](https://students.ubc.ca/health/sexual-health/wellness-centre-sexual-health-shop/#about-the-shop)

Since 2006, the Wellness Centre Sexual Health Shop \(or the “Shop”\) has aimed to be a sex\-positive, inclusive, welcoming, and safer space for all members of the UBC community\. The Shop exists to provide sexual health information for all UBC students and increase access to sexual health and pleasure products\.

Drop by the [Wellness Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/health/wellness-resources/wellness-centre/) to browse the Shop and make a purchase in person or [place an order online](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_9no9nGaL5UheBlY)\. Peer Health Educators; trained UBC student volunteers, or other trained Wellness Centre student staff, will be available to answer questions and to share resources\.

## Available products[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/sexual\-health/wellness\-centre\-sexual\-health\-shop/\#available\-products](https://students.ubc.ca/health/sexual-health/wellness-centre-sexual-health-shop/#available-products)

The Shop offers products made of body\-safe materials, and all sexual health and sex toys are compatible with water\-based lubricant\. Products are specifically chosen to be gender inclusive, shame\-free, pleasure\-focused, and to celebrate the diversity of sexual experiences and identities at UBC\.

Prices are listed in Canadian dollars\. All purchases are **cash only** and returns are not accepted\.

The Shop currently offers sexual health products, such as external condoms, lubricants, menstrual products, and pregnancy tests, as well as a variety sex toys, including vibrators, masturbation sleeves and eggs, c\-rings, and anal plugs and beads\.

Check out the [cleaning guides](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/sexual_health_shop_cleaning_guide.pdf) \(pdf\) for tips on how to safely use, clean, and store products\.

[Browse all products \(pdf\)](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/sexual_health_shop_products.pdf)

## How to place an order[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/sexual\-health/wellness\-centre\-sexual\-health\-shop/\#how\-to\-place\-an\-order](https://students.ubc.ca/health/sexual-health/wellness-centre-sexual-health-shop/#how-to-place-an-order)

There are 2 ways you can purchase products from the Shop: 

-   Visit the Shop at the [UBC Wellness Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/health/wellness-resources/wellness-centre/) during open hours\. 
-   Place an order [through the online form](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_9no9nGaL5UheBlY) and pick up in person at the [UBC Wellness Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/health/wellness-resources/wellness-centre/)\. You will receive an email notification for pick up in 2 business days\.

## Contact us[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/sexual\-health/wellness\-centre\-sexual\-health\-shop/\#contact\-us](https://students.ubc.ca/health/sexual-health/wellness-centre-sexual-health-shop/#contact-us)

-   **Email**: [wellness\.centre@ubc\.ca](mailto:wellness.centre@ubc.ca)
-   **Address**: [UBC Life Building](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/ubc-life-building/), Room 1400 \([6138 Student Union Boulevard](https://maps.app.goo.gl/ZoYsuzaB6A63orUm6)\)
-   **Phone**: [604 822 8450](tel:6048228450)

### Opening hours

The Wellness Centre Sexual Health Shop is closed on all [statutory holidays](https://hr.ubc.ca/working-ubc/statutory-holidays) observed by UBC\.

-   **Monday**: 11:00 am to 3:00 pm
-   **Tuesday**: 11:00 am to 3:00 pm
-   **Wednesday**: 11:00 am to 3:00 pm
-   **Thursday**: 11:00 am to 3:00 pm

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/sexual\-health/wellness\-centre\-sexual\-health\-shop/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/health/sexual-health/wellness-centre-sexual-health-shop/#if-you-have-questions)

Learn about sexual health and resources through our [Sex and Sexual Health guide](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-topics/sex-sexual-health/)\.

For additional questions, drop by the Sexual Health Shop to speak with a Peer Health Educator, contact us through phone, or email wellness\.centre@ubc\.ca\.

title: Support for unanticipated circumstances
content_markdown:
If you’ve been impacted by a significant event or unanticipated circumstances, there are services and resources to help you\.

## Courses, assignments, and exams[https://students\.ubc\.ca/support\-unanticipated\-circumstances/\#courses\-assignments\-and\-exams](https://students.ubc.ca/support-unanticipated-circumstances/#courses-assignments-and-exams)

Find the academic support options available to you\.

-   Check your course syllabus to see what options you have\.
-   Apply for an [academic concession](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-concessions/)\.
    -   Undergraduate students can contact their [academic advising](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) office\.
    -   Graduate students can speak to their program [graduate advisor](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/current-students/supervision-advising/program-advising) or supervisor\.
    -   Indigenous students can find a list of [program advisors](https://fnhl.ubc.ca/students/student-resources/program-advisors/)\.

## Mental and physical health[https://students\.ubc\.ca/support\-unanticipated\-circumstances/\#mental\-and\-physical\-health](https://students.ubc.ca/support-unanticipated-circumstances/#mental-and-physical-health)

Access resources for mental and physical health\.

-   Call or chat with a [crisis responder](https://crisiscentre.bc.ca/) 24/7\.
-   Access 24/7 mental health counselling using [Here2Talk](https://here2talk.ca/main)\.
-   Book an appointment with a [mental health](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/) or [medical provider](https://students.ubc.ca/health/medical-care-on-campus/) on campus\.
-   Connect with a spirituality or faith group through a [chaplain at UBC](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/)**\.**

## Financial support[https://students\.ubc\.ca/support\-unanticipated\-circumstances/\#financial\-support](https://students.ubc.ca/support-unanticipated-circumstances/#financial-support)

Get help if you’re experiencing financial difficulties\.

-   See if you’re eligible for [emergency funding](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/emergency-funding/)\.
-   Talk to an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) about your financial support options\.
-   Indigenous students can reach out to the [Indigenous Student Support Team](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-support-indigenous/)\.

## Sexual assault support[https://students\.ubc\.ca/support\-unanticipated\-circumstances/\#sexual\-assault\-support](https://students.ubc.ca/support-unanticipated-circumstances/#sexual-assault-support)

Help is available if you have experienced sexual assault or sexual violence\. We believe you\.

-   Book a consultation or appointment with a [Support Specialist](https://svpro.ubc.ca/)\.
-   Access [Sexual Assault Support Centre](https://amssasc.ca/) for support and educational resources\.

## Visas and study or work permits[https://students\.ubc\.ca/support\-unanticipated\-circumstances/\#visas\-and\-study\-or\-work\-permits](https://students.ubc.ca/support-unanticipated-circumstances/#visas-and-study-or-work-permits)

Get support if you’re an international student\.

-   Check out the [International Student Guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/)\.
-   Connect with an [International Student Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/)\.

## Other student supports[https://students\.ubc\.ca/support\-unanticipated\-circumstances/\#other\-student\-supports](https://students.ubc.ca/support-unanticipated-circumstances/#other-student-supports)

Explore the full list of student services available to you\.

[View all services](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/)

title: Information for international students with family
content_markdown:
## Activities for Spouses and Partners[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/information\-international\-family/\#activities\-for\-spouses\-and\-partners](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/information-international-family/#activities-for-spouses-and-partners)

Here are some ways to get involved in community events and activities that make the transition to life in Vancouver more enjoyable:

-   Sign up for English classes\. View the “English As An Additional Language \(EAL\) Resources” handout\.
-   Enrol in a course through [UBC Extended Learning Studies](https://cstudies.ubc.ca/)\.
-   Take advantage of [athletics and recreation programs](http://www.recreation.ubc.ca/) and facilities on campus\. Most are open to the public for an additional cost\.
-   Attend activities at your local community centre or neighbourhood house\.
-   If you live in student residence on campus, get involved in Residence Life activities\.
-   Consider volunteering \(informally\)\.
-   Attend [UBC events](http://www.events.ubc.ca/)\.

## Association of Neighbourhood Houses of BC[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/information\-international\-family/\#association\-of\-neighbourhood\-houses\-of\-bc](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/information-international-family/#association-of-neighbourhood-houses-of-bc)

British Columbia’s non\-profit organization [The Association of Neighbourhood Houses](http://www.anhbc.org/) offers the following community services at various Neighbourhood Houses located throughout BC, such as:

-   **Community**:  
    Low income tax clinics, monthly community potlucks, Neighbourhood Small Grants, Volunteer training and volunteer opportunities, computer tutorials, Pocket Market, Westside Food Collaborative, Steeves Manor Resource Room, information and referrals
-   **Childcare**:  
    Bumbletree Childcare, Kits and Dunbar Kids Club \(Out of School Care\)
-   **Youth**:  
    Youth Leadership, Citizen U, Westside Youth Plan Alliance, Expressive Art for Newcomer Preteens
-   **Families**:  
    Parent and Tot Drop\-in, Mama & Papa Goose, Nobody’s Perfect parenting program, My Tween & Me, Food Skills for Families, Family Camp, Neighbourhood Connections
-   **Seniors**:  
    Affordable housing for seniors and individuals with spinal cord injuries, Seniors Resource Centre, Seniors Links, Seniors Peer Counselling, Seniors Drop\-in, Osteofit, Seniors Outreach, Intergenerational Knitting Circles
-   **Newcomers**:  
    English Conversation Circles, Multicultural Women’s Support Program, Westside Newcomers Hub

The Neighbourhood House closest to UBC is [Kitsilano Neighbourhood House](http://www.kitshouse.org/) at 3683 West 4th Ave, Vancouver, BC, V6R 4N6 \(Temporary Office Location during Redevelopment\)\. You can call the organization at [604\-736\-3588](tel:604-736-3588) or email [frontdesk@kitshouse\.org](mailto:frontdesk@kitshouse.org)\.

## Community Recreation Centres[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/information\-international\-family/\#community\-recreation\-centres](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/information-international-family/#community-recreation-centres)

The [City of Vancouver Board of Parks and Recreation](http://www.vancouver.ca/community_profiles/RecGuideInfo.htm) operates 24 community recreation centres open to all residents of the city\. They offer a wide variety of programs and facilities\.

## Vaccinations \(also known as Immunizations\)[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/information\-international\-family/\#vaccinations\-also\-known\-as\-immunizations](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/information-international-family/#vaccinations-also-known-as-immunizations)

Vaccinations protect people of all ages from harmful bacteria and viruses\. Doctors, pharmacists and nurses provide vaccinations at local public and private health facilities\. 

Be sure to keep complete records of immunizations for you and your family\. A child’s immunization record is usually requested when he or she is registered to enter day care, preschool, kindergarten, school and certain programs in post\-secondary institutions\.

This schedule, listing [vaccines provided free to residents of BC](https://www.healthlinkbc.ca/bc-immunization-schedules), can help you determine when you or your family needs to be immunized\. If you have any questions about immunizations, speak with your health care provider\.

The closest Child Health Clinic to UBC is the [Pacific Spirit Community Health Centre](http://www.vch.ca/locations-services/result?res_id=1336)\. You can bring your baby for immunizations and general check\-ups\. Contact the Health Centre directly for more information\.

## Resources for parents[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/information\-international\-family/\#resources\-for\-parents](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/information-international-family/#resources-for-parents)

Caring for children far from extended family support systems can be an isolating experience\. There are a number of ways to reach out and receive support as a parent:

-   Attend events sponsored by the [UBC Graduate Student Society](https://gss.ubc.ca/) where you might meet other UBC parents\.
-   Bring your children to the [Graduate Life Centre](https://gss.ubc.ca/graduate-life-centre-glc/) where there is a child friendly area\.
-   Attend a class or activity at a community centre or organization with your child and other parents\.
-   Attend a parenting support group provided by a community organization\.
-   Connect with other parents in your area by posting notes on community bulletin boards or through online sites like [Craigslist](https://vancouver.craigslist.ca/)\. You can also meet other parents through activities you enjoy \(such as a hiking or a book club\)\. You can try [“Meetup” groups](https://www.meetup.com/)\. When meeting strangers from the internet, be sure to meet in public places \(at least initially\) and consider your safety\. 

Single parents can access programs and resources through organizations such as the YWCA or consider becoming involved with a group such as Single Parents On Campus \(SPOC\)\. SPOC raises awareness about experiences of single parents attending UBC and facilitates lobbying efforts both on campus and within the Metro Vancouver community\.

Find out more about [programs, resources and initiatives](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/resources-who-are-parents/) that are available to students who are parents\.

## Applying for documents together as a family[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/information\-international\-family/\#applying\-for\-documents\-together\-as\-a\-family](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/information-international-family/#applying-for-documents-together-as-a-family)

For many IRCC forms, there is an option of filling out only one application for the entire family\. For example, eligible accompanying spouses or common\-law partners of study permit holders can [apply for open\-work permits](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/help-your-spouse-common-law-partner-work-canada.html) that last as long as the study permits of their student partners, if the student is studying full\-time at the time of application\. 

When the study permit holder extends their study permit using the online MyCIC system, applications for new, or extension of, documents of accompanying spouses and all dependents can be made at the same time\. There will be a fee for each document requested\. For more information, visit the [IRCC website](http://www.cic.gc.ca/)\. 

## Child care on campus[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/information\-international\-family/\#child\-care\-on\-campus](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/information-international-family/#child-care-on-campus)

UBC Child Care Services offers professional, on\-campus child care for infants to school\-age children\. Due to the high demand, it is encouraged that you apply before you arrive in Vancouver\. For children under the age of 5, the wait time is 6 to 12 months, and possibly 2 or more years for children under 3 years old\. The child’s age and time of year greatly affect the waiting time\. You can [find more information](http://www.childcare.ubc.ca/) on waiting times, the type of programs offered, and how to apply\. You can also call [604\-822\-5343](tel:604-822-5343) for more information\.

The [Westcoast Child Care Resource Centre](https://www.wstcoast.org/) provides information, referrals, training and resources to families who are seeking the best care and early learning for children\. They maintain a comprehensive list of all registered child care facilities in Metro Vancouver and also offer an online guide for choosing child care as well as resources and help in many languages\. You can call them at [604\-709\-5661](tel:604-709-5661)\. 

More information about child care and other services is also available at:

-   [Immigrant Services Society of BC](http://www.issbc.org/) 
-   [MOSAIC](http://www.mosaicbc.com/)
-   [Pacific Immigrant Resources Society](http://www.pirs.bc.ca/) 
-   [ChildCareBC](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/family-social-supports/caring-for-young-children)

## Enrolling children in school[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/information\-international\-family/\#enrolling\-children\-in\-school](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/information-international-family/#enrolling-children-in-school)

In Canada, the school year runs from September to June\. There is a 2\-week break in December and a 2\-week break in March\. Children can enter kindergarten as young as age 5\. The Vancouver School Board operates the public elementary and secondary schools in Vancouver\. These schools offer elective programs in business, visual and graphic arts, choir, orchestra, physical education, drama, and languages\. For more information, visit the [Vancouver School Board](http://www.vsb.bc.ca/) website\. 

Many schools offer English as a Second Language \(ESL\) classes for their students as part of the regular curriculum\. For information about these programs, contact the Immigrant Services Society of BC at [604\-684\-2561](tel:604-684-2561)\. 

If your study permit is valid for at least one year and you are enrolled at a publicly funded institution such as UBC, your minor children \(18 years of age and younger\) are eligible to attend elementary and secondary school as if they were Canadian residents\. They will not be required to pay international student fees\. You should begin the enrolment process for your children as early as possible after your arrival in Vancouver\. You will need the following to enroll your child in school:

-   Passport
-   Passport stamp or visitor record indicating the day your child entered Canada
-   Copies of the parents’ study or work permits 

The following documents should be translated into English \(if necessary\):

-   Immunization documents
-   Birth certificate
-   Copies of school report cards, grades, and evaluations from the past two years 

For more information, visit the [Vancouver School Board](http://www.vsb.bc.ca/) website or the [IRCC website](http://www.cic.gc.ca/)\.

## The information on this page may change[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/information\-international\-family/\#the\-information\-on\-this\-page\-may\-change](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/information-international-family/#the-information-on-this-page-may-change)

The immigration information on this page has been reviewed and endorsed by Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultants \(RCICs\) or Regulated International Student Immigration Advisors \(RISIAs\) in compliance with the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and Regulations\. However, this is not a legal document and information may change without notice\. Always refer to [Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada](http://www.cic.gc.ca/) \(IRCC\) for the most up\-to\-date information\.

## International Student Guide[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/information\-international\-family/\#international\-student\-guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/information-international-family/#international-student-guide)

Find everything you need to know about life as an international student at UBC’s Vancouver campus\.

You can connect with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for questions related to immigration, health insurance, and life as an international student in Canada\.

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/information\-international\-family/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/information-international-family/#additional-resources)

title: Travelling to Canada
content_markdown:
If you’re an international student planning to come to UBC, we are here to help\.

There are important steps to take before you plan your trip\. It’s important for you to carefully review the guide and understand the process and requirements before you travel\.

## Check before you make travel plans[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/travelling\-to\-canada/\#check\-before\-you\-make\-travel\-plans](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/#check-before-you-make-travel-plans)

Before making travel arrangements, there are a few things you will need to consider:

-   Understand travel documents you need\.
-   Consider when to travel\.
-   Get advice on whether to travel\.

[Start the guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/check-eligible/)

## Before you travel to Canada[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/travelling\-to\-canada/\#before\-you\-travel\-to\-canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/#before-you-travel-to-canada)

Before you travel to Canada, you must make sure you prepare the right documents\.

-   Get a new immigration medical exam, if required\.
-   Confirm your health insurance coverage\.
-   Complete the optional Advance Declaration\.

[Read requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/before-you-travel/)

## Know what to bring[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/travelling\-to\-canada/\#know\-what\-to\-bring](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/#know-what-to-bring)

Prepare the documents you should bring and learn about restrictions\.

-   Learn what to pack\.
-   See documentation to bring\.

[Get the checklist](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/what-bring-canada/)

## While you travel to Canada[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/travelling\-to\-canada/\#while\-you\-travel\-to\-canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/#while-you-travel-to-canada)

Know what to expect at the airport or border, follow arrival steps, and ensure your study permit has conditions to work\.

[Read details](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/while-you-travel/)

## After arriving in Canada[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/travelling\-to\-canada/\#after\-arriving\-in\-canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/#after-arriving-in-canada)

There are a few things you need to do as soon as you arrive in Canada\.

-   Apply for MSP and check that you have iMED\.
-   Complete the after arrival checklist\.
-   Learn about life in Canada\.
-   Find helpful resources to get settled\.

[Find resources](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/after-arriving/)

title: Introduction to UBC classes
content_markdown:
## About UBC courses[https://students\.ubc\.ca/new\-to\-ubc/introduction\-ubc\-classes/\#about\-ubc\-courses](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/introduction-ubc-classes/#about-ubc-courses)

Most UBC undergraduate courses amount to 3 hours of class time per week\. This does not include the number of hours you may spend on assignments, projects, tutorials, or lab work outside of lectures\. Classes that are 3 hours long are referred to as 3\-credit classes or 3\-credit hours\.

Generally, 100\-level courses are first\-year courses, 200\-level courses are second\-year courses, and so on\. 500\- and 600\-level courses are considered graduate\-level and are only available to undergraduates with the permission of the department and the Faculty of Graduate Studies\.

Some courses require prerequisites which are courses you must complete before enrolling in a specific course or program\.

Similarly, corequisites are courses you must enrol in at the same time as another course or program, or complete beforehand\.

## Course formats[https://students\.ubc\.ca/new\-to\-ubc/introduction\-ubc\-classes/\#course\-formats](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/introduction-ubc-classes/#course-formats)

At UBC, courses are offered in various formats\. Before registering for a course, it is important to check your course to confirm how it is being delivered\. Read about how [courses are delivered](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/course-modes-delivery/) at UBC\.

### Lectures

Most courses are offered as lectures, which are either 50 or 80 minutes each\. For example, if your schedule says your class is from 10:00 to 11:00 am, the class will end at 10:50 am\. This allows you enough time to get to your next class or lecture\.

### Tutorials

Tutorials are generally held weekly\. They are commonly taken with lecture courses and provide an opportunity for smaller group discussions or learning\. If a course has a tutorial section, you must register for the tutorial in addition to the lecture\. In some cases, grades are given for attendance and active participation\.

### Labs

Many science, math, and engineering courses have a laboratory \(lab\) component\. Labs involve practical projects done in small groups under the direction of a Teaching Assistant \(TA\)\. You must pass the lab to pass the course\. If a course has a lab section, you must register for the lab in addition to the lecture\.

### Seminars and discussions

Seminar courses are smaller, less formal classes than lectures\. They encourage discussions and sometimes involve presentations\. Students are graded on presentations and participation\.

## Student evaluation[https://students\.ubc\.ca/new\-to\-ubc/introduction\-ubc\-classes/\#student\-evaluation](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/introduction-ubc-classes/#student-evaluation)

On the first day of class, your instructor will present a course outline or syllabus that you will follow throughout the term\. It will outline important details on class readings, exams, assignments, due dates, and grading criteria\.

In university, you are expected to take charge of your own learning and success\. Be sure to contact your professor for the syllabus if you missed the first lecture\. You will also be responsible for catching up on any course material you may miss during the term\.

There are 3 main methods of student evaluation at UBC:

-   Class participation
-   Assignments
-   Exams

### Class participation

In many courses, you will be expected to discuss your opinions, ideas, and perspectives related to the coursework, readings, and assignments\.

The goals of class participation are to develop academic skills such as critical thinking, connecting and creating ideas, and defending perspectives or arguments\. Memorizing lecture notes and course material is important but often not sufficient to achieve the best results\.

### Assignments

Instructors may assign term papers, essays, problem sets, or other assignments like group projects, class presentations, or lab projects\. Read your syllabus at the start of the term for assignment due dates and grading criteria, and consider adding your deadlines to a calendar to help you stay on track\.

### Exams

Many courses have 2 major exams: midterms and final exams\. Your courses may have one midterm halfway through the course or several midterms throughout the term\.

Exams will test your knowledge using varying formats, such as short or long answers, essay questions, true or false, and multiple choice\.

## Final exams[https://students\.ubc\.ca/new\-to\-ubc/introduction\-ubc\-classes/\#final\-exams](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/introduction-ubc-classes/#final-exams)

Final exams happen at the end of each term during exam periods in December and April\. Review [important term dates](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/dates-and-deadlines) for the exam period\.

Exam schedules are posted to your [Workday account](http://www.myworkday.ubc.ca/) and are available in the [Exam Schedule tool](https://legacy.students.ubc.ca/exam-schedule/) in mid\-October \(Term 1\) and mid\-February \(Term 2\)\.

You must be available to take your exams during the entire exam period\. Do not plan trips until you know your exam schedule\.

### Exam clashes and hardships

When your exam schedule is released, check that you don’t have any [exam clashes or hardships](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/exams/exam-clashes-hardships-cancellations/)\.

### Missing an exam

If you need to miss an exam, or have missed an exam due to a legitimate reason, contact your [academic advising office](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) as soon as possible, and check if you’re eligible for an [academic concession](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-concessions/)\.

## Instructors[https://students\.ubc\.ca/new\-to\-ubc/introduction\-ubc\-classes/\#instructors](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/introduction-ubc-classes/#instructors)

Most undergraduate classes are taught by professors\. Some courses will have Teaching Assistants \(TAs\)\. Be sure to speak to your instructor for any of the following situations:

-   You cannot submit your assignment on time\.
-   You don’t understand a concept that was covered in class\.
-   You’re feeling overwhelmed by your course load due to circumstances outside of the course\.
-   You need more information about an essay, project, or other assignment\.

### Office hours

Most instructors hold office hours, which are dedicated times when you can drop by to discuss course material, assignments, questions, and other concerns\. You can also schedule one\-on\-one appointments with your instructor\. Consult your course syllabus for specific instructions\.

### Conduct

Student\-faculty relationships may be different at university than they are in secondary school or in other countries:

-   Relationships are informal and you may hear students call some instructors by their first name\.
-   Students may respectfully challenge and question their instructors in class or office hours\.
-   It’s considered inappropriate for instructors to date their students\.

## Academic integrity[https://students\.ubc\.ca/new\-to\-ubc/introduction\-ubc\-classes/\#academic\-integrity](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/introduction-ubc-classes/#academic-integrity)

In a nutshell, academic integrity means completing your academic work honestly\. This can include doing and submitting your original work, acknowledging the contributions of others, such as through citations, and avoiding tools and services like artificial intelligence software unless permitted\.

As a UBC student, you’re expected to uphold [academic integrity](https://academicintegrity.ubc.ca/student-start/) throughout your degree\. Learn more about the topic, resources and support available to you, and types of academic misconduct to avoid\.

### Plagiarism

Plagiarism is the act of submitting the intellectual property of another person as your own\. It is one of the most serious of academic offences\. Penalties for plagiarism may range from a failing grade in a course to suspension from UBC\. Learn how to [avoid plagiarism](https://learningcommons.ubc.ca/academic-integrity/)\.

Plagiarism may include:

-   Copying any part of another person’s work and presenting it as your own
-   Purchasing a written paper from someone or a website and presenting it as your own
-   Re\-submitting your work from one course to fulfill a requirement in another course
-   Generating work using AI and submitting it as your own

### Citation

Intellectual property includes ideas, arguments, phrases, sentences, paragraphs, or results of research\. When you use excerpts from someone else’s work in your essay, paper, or presentation, you must acknowledge the original author in a footnote or another accepted manner of citation\. The UBC Library can help you with [proper citation](https://help.library.ubc.ca/evaluating-and-citing-sources/how-to-cite/)\. If you do not properly cite your work, it may be considered plagiarism\.

### University regulations

It is your responsibility to be aware of University regulations\. Review the [list of academic regulations](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations) that apply to every student at UBC\.

## Academic resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/new\-to\-ubc/introduction\-ubc\-classes/\#academic\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/introduction-ubc-classes/#academic-resources)

UBC offers a variety of [academic and learning resources](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/) to help you succeed in your studies\.

title: After arriving in Canada
content_markdown:
There are steps you need to take before you start your studies\.

## After arriving in British Columbia[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/travelling\-to\-canada/after\-arriving/\#after\-arriving\-in\-british\-columbia](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/after-arriving/#after-arriving-in-british-columbia)

-   Apply for the [BC Medical Services Plan](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/apply-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/) \(MSP\)
-   Check that you have [iMED health insurance](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international/) for your first three months in BC \(or longer if you are not a degree\-seeking student\)
-   Apply for a [Social Insurance Number](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/) \(SIN\)
-   Add your immigration document expiry dates into the [UBC reminder system](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/immigration-documents-reminder-system)
-   Sign up to receive the [International Community Update newsletter](https://blogs.ubc.ca/ubcisa/international-student-life-newsletter/)
-   Learn how your [enrolment impacts immigration](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/immigration-impacts-part-time-studies-withdrawing-courses/), including part\-time studies and taking time away from studies
-   Get a [BCID card](https://www.icbc.com/driver-licensing/getting-licensed/Apply-for-a-bcid) to avoid carrying your passport for identification

## If you need a temporary mailing address[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/travelling\-to\-canada/after\-arriving/\#if\-you\-need\-a\-temporary\-mailing\-address](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/after-arriving/#if-you-need-a-temporary-mailing-address)

If you don’t have a mailing address, you can [rent a Post Office Box](https://www.canadapost.ca/cpc/en/personal/receiving/alternative-delivery/post-office-box.page) from Canada Post or use the mailing address of your friend or relative who is in Canada\. You should not use the address of a friend who lives in UBC residence since they only accept mail for current residents\.

You can use International Student Advising as your temporary mailing address when you first arrive in Canada\.

International Student Advising  
UBC Life Building  
1200 – 6138 Student Union Blvd\.  
Vancouver, BC V6T 1Z1

International Student Advising is not responsible for your mail\. Mail will be publicly accessible in the office, so there is no way to ensure that your mail will be secure\. International Student Advising does not accept packages on behalf of students as there is no secure storage space\. 

After you’ve moved into your place of residence, remember to change all of your mailing addresses\.

## Learning about life in Canada[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/travelling\-to\-canada/after\-arriving/\#learning\-about\-life\-in\-canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/after-arriving/#learning-about-life-in-canada)

-   iPREP immigration and health insurance courses:
    -   [Undergraduate students](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/NJFRY4)
    -   [Graduate students](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/77NDCK)
    -   [Non\-degree seeking students](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/NCK6XM)
-   [New to UBC guide for first years](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/)
-   [Interactive checklist for graduate students](https://community.grad.ubc.ca/newly-admitted#:~:text=interactive%20new%20student%20checklist)
-   [Health insurance for international students](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/)
-   [Working in Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/)
-   [Guide to banking in Canada](https://www.canada.ca/en/financial-consumer-agency/services/banking.html)
-   [Getting to know Canada](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/new-immigrants/learn-about-canada.html)
-   [Welcome to Canada: publications for newcomers \(IRCC\)](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/publication-welcome-canada-what-you-should-know.html)
-   [EduCanada’s pre\-departure guide](https://www.educanada.ca/study-plan-etudes/before-avant/guide.aspx?lang=eng)
-   [BC’s Newcomers’ Guides](https://www.welcomebc.ca/Start-Your-Life-in-B-C/Newcomers-Guides) \(available in 13 languages\)

title: Before you travel to Canada
content_markdown:
## Get a new medical exam, if required[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/travelling\-to\-canada/before\-you\-travel/\#get\-a\-new\-medical\-exam\-if\-required](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/before-you-travel/#get-a-new-medical-exam-if-required)

**

If you applied for a study permit or TRV outside Canada

**

[Immigration medical exam](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/medical-police/medical-exams.html) \(IME\) results are valid for 12 months and your medical exam must be valid when you enter Canada\.

If you completed an immigration medical exam for your study permit application and you will enter Canada more than 12 months after you completed your medical exam, you must take another medical exam before travelling to Canada\. If you need to take a second medical exam, be sure to complete this well in advance of travelling to Canada and send a copy of your new E\-medical \(the document you receive from your panel physician with your photo\) to IRCC through a [webform](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/contact-ircc/web-form.html) as soon as you receive it\. Select “Add a document to your application” as the request category to submit your E\-medical\. When you travel to Canada bring both your previous and new E\-medical copies with you\.

If you get a request in your online IRCC account for a medical exam it is important to complete the medical exam or provide an explanation for why you cannot complete the medical exam by the deadline\. See our [medical exam FAQ](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-immigration-health-insurance-faq/#medical-exam) for details\.

If a medical exam was not required for your study permit application, you do not need to complete one unless your situation has changed since you applied and you now [require a medical exam](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/medical-police/medical-exams/requirements-temporary-residents.html#needs)\. This could apply to you, if, for example, you lived in a [designated country](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/medical-police/medical-exams/requirements-temporary-residents/country-requirements.html) for 6 months or longer consecutively in the year before you travel to Canada\. In this case, complete the medical exam with a panel physician well in advance of travelling, send a copy of your E\-medical to IRCC through a [webform](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/contact-ircc/web-form.html) as soon as you receive it\. Select “Add a document to your application” as the request category to submit your E\-medical\. Bring a copy of the E\-medical with you when you travel to Canada\.   

In addition, if you are a medical student, will work, or complete a Co\-op or student work placement in [jobs which require a medical exam](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/#if-you-work-with-children-or-seniors-in-healthcare-settings-or-in-agriculture), check that your study and/or work permit conditions allow you to work in such jobs\. You cannot work in jobs that require a medical exam until you have received a study or work permit with the appropriate conditions and are [eligible to work](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/)\.

**

If you are a continuing student with a valid study permit who has been outside Canada for more than 6 months

**

If you’ve been in a [designated country](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/medical-police/medical-exams/requirements-temporary-residents/country-requirements.html) for 6 months or longer in the past 12 months, you will need to complete a medical exam with a [panel physician](https://secure.cic.gc.ca/pp-md/pp-list.aspx) before travelling to Canada\. You should take the medical exam well in advance before you plan to travel to Canada, send a copy of your new E\-medical to IRCC through a [webform](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/contact-ircc/web-form.html) as soon as you receive it\. Select “Other” as the request category to submit your E\-medical\. Bring a copy of the E\-medical with you when you travel to Canada\.

In addition, if you are a medical student, will work, or complete a Co\-op or student work placement in [jobs which require a medical exam](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/#if-you-work-with-children-or-seniors-in-healthcare-settings-or-in-agriculture), check that your study and/or work permit conditions allow you to work in jobs which require a medical exam\. If your study and/or work permit do not have conditions which allow you to work in jobs which require a medical exam, complete a medical exam and [apply to change conditions](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/extend-study-permit-within-canada/) on your study and/or work permit\. You cannot work in jobs that require a medical exam until you have received a study or work permit with the appropriate conditions and are [eligible to work](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/)\. If your study and/or work permit conditions are correct but you later lived in a designated country for 6 months or longer consecutively, please contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support\. 

## Confirm your health insurance coverage[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/travelling\-to\-canada/before\-you\-travel/\#confirm\-your\-health\-insurance\-coverage](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/before-you-travel/#confirm-your-health-insurance-coverage)

### If you’re new to UBC

**

Students in programs longer than 6 months \(including degree\-seeking, two\-term exchange, and VIRS students studying more than 6 months\)

**

As a new international student who will be studying for more than 6 months, who has registered in one or more on\-campus courses, and is charged AMS/GSS student fees, you have temporary, private health insurance coverage for your first 3 months through [iMED](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international/)\.

iMED is designed to cover your 3\-month waiting period before you are eligible for the British Columbia \(BC\) government Medical Services Plan \(BC MSP\) – you must [apply for MSP](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/apply-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/) as soon as you enter BC\. Learn more about [health insurance for international students](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/)\.

Your iMED coverage dates depend on when you start your program:

-   Winter Term 1 \(September to December\): coverage will start on August 10
-   Winter Term 2 \(January to April\): coverage will start on December 10
-   Summer Term 1 \(May to August\): your coverage will start on April 10

If you are a Go Global exchange student or a VIRS student, please connect directly with [Go Global](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/contact) if you need to change your coverage dates\. 

For all other students, [see what to do](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international/#coverage-dates) if you will arrive in Canada before your coverage dates, or in the calendar month after your iMED insurance starts\.

**

One\-term exchange and non\-degree\-seeking students studying less than 6 months

**

As a new international student who will be studying for less than 6 months, who is registered in one or more on\-campus courses, and who is charged AMS/GSS student fees, you have temporary health insurance coverage through iMED for the entire duration of your program of studies\.

**One\-term exchange students** have set iMED [coverage dates](https://sites.guard.me/ubc/department/go-global-_-virs) for 130 days \(approximately one academic term\) which cannot be changed\.

If you will arrive in Canada before your iMED coverage start date, contact [Go Global](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/contact) directly for support\.

If you plan to stay in Canada after your iMED coverage dates, contact [GuardMe](https://sites.guard.me/ubc/contact) or another private health insurance provider for options\. Ensure you always have sufficient health insurance during your stay in Canada\. You also need to ensure you have valid immigration status in Canada – contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support\.  

**VIRS students** studying for less than 6 months have iMED coverage dates based on their research period\. If you need to change your research period, learn about changing your iMED [coverage dates](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international#changing-your-imed-coverage-dates)\.

For other non\-degree seeking students such as unclassified, access studies and visiting students, please check the [iMED page](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international/) for details or [contact GuardMe](https://sites.guard.me/ubc/contact) to ask about your options\.

#### Getting your iMED card

Your welcome email from GuardMe will contain instructions for accessing your iMED card and account\. Check that the iMED coverage period on your iMED card is correct\.

If you have not received your welcome email by the start of the iMED coverage period, check your Workday student account to make sure you have been charged iMED fees\. If you do not see iMED fees in your student account, contact [International Student Advising](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0J8VRJgJQkuO2b4) for support\. Learn more about accessing your iMED card and account\.

Learn more about [accessing your iMED card and account](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international/#logging-into-your-guardme-account)\.

### Returning students

Before you travel, check whether you have valid [BC Medical Services Plan](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/) \(MSP\) coverage\.

**

If you’ve been outside of Canada for six months or less

**

If you have been outside of Canada for **less than six months** and you did not cancel your MSP, ensure your MSP coverage has not expired\. You should be eligible to continue to be covered under MSP; however, you should [contact BC MSP](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents-contact-us) to confirm that this is the case\.

**

If you’ve been outside of Canada for more than six months

**

If you have been outside of Canada for **more than six months** in a calendar year, [contact BC MSP](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents-contact-us) to confirm your eligibility for MSP coverage\.

-   If you can still be covered under MSP, no further action is required until your MSP expires\.
-   If you are no longer covered under MSP, please check the instructions provided below\.

#### If you don’t have MSP

If you are not eligible to be covered under MSP, you will need to get private health insurance to cover you during the MSP 3\-month waiting period\. You can contact [GuardMe](https://sites.guard.me/ubc/contact), the provider of iMED, to discuss your options, or you may find and purchase your own private insurance\.

As soon as you re\-enter BC, [apply for the BC MSP online](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/apply-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/)\.

## Complete the optional Advance Declaration[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/travelling\-to\-canada/before\-you\-travel/\#complete\-the\-optional\-advance\-declaration](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/before-you-travel/#complete-the-optional-advance-declaration)

If you are flying to Canada and will first arrive in Vancouver, Toronto, Montreal, or other participating airports, you can use [Advance Declaration](https://www.canada.ca/en/border-services-agency/services/arrivecan.html) to submit your customs and immigration declaration in advance \(up to 72 hours before your scheduled arrival\) to save time at the airport\.

## The information on this page may change[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/travelling\-to\-canada/before\-you\-travel/\#the\-information\-on\-this\-page\-may\-change](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/before-you-travel/#the-information-on-this-page-may-change)

The immigration information on this page has been reviewed and endorsed by Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultants \(RCICs\) or Regulated International Student Immigration Advisors \(RISIAs\) in compliance with the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and Regulations\. However, this is not a legal document and information may change without notice\. Always refer to [Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada](http://www.cic.gc.ca/) \(IRCC\) for the most up\-to\-date information\.

title: Check before you make travel plans
content_markdown:
## Travelling as an international student[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/travelling\-to\-canada/check\-eligible/\#travelling\-as\-an\-international\-student](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/check-eligible/#travelling-as-an-international-student)

Before making travel plans, check that you have the right documents and understand when to travel\.

COVID\-19 emergency border measures ended on October 1, 2022\.

Travel restrictions may be announced without notice\. Be sure to check the [latest updates](https://travel.gc.ca/travel-covid)\.

## Immigration documents[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/travelling\-to\-canada/check\-eligible/\#immigration\-documents](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/check-eligible/#immigration-documents)

To travel to Canada for studies, you must have two types of documents:

1.  Valid documents to study in Canada
2.  Valid documents to travel to Canada

### Have valid documents to study in Canada

First, you must fall into one of the following categories:

-   You have an original, [valid study permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/study-permits#maintaining-your-student-status)\.
-   You have a valid [Letter of Introduction](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/#get-your-study-permit-approval) \(study permit approval letter\)\.
-   You will study in a [short\-term program](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/study-permits#about-study-permits) for less than 6 months as a visitor, and can study without a study permit\.
-   You are a US citizen or lawful US permanent resident, or a resident of Greenland or St\. Pierre and Miquelon, and will [apply for a study permit on arrival](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/study-permits#important-considerations) in Canada\.

If you will study in Canada for more than 6 months, **do not travel to Canada** until you have received your Letter of Introduction, even if you have an eTA or TRV\.

### Have valid documents to travel to Canada

Second, you must fall into one of the following categories:

-   You have a valid [Temporary Resident Visa \(TRV\)](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/) \(a sticker in your passport\)
-   You have a valid [Electronic Travel Authorization \(eTA\)](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/eta.html)  
-   You are a US citizen or [lawful US permanent resident](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/entry-requirements-country.html#lawful-pr-us) who holds valid status in the US \(you do not require a TRV or an eTA\)\.

Find [entry requirements](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/entry-requirements-country.html) by country or territory\.

### About your Temporary Resident Visa \(TRV\)

If you travel from Canada to the US and back without travelling to a third country, you could [re\-enter Canada without a TRV](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/travelling-outside-canada#visiting-the-united-states) if you have a valid study or work permit, or are returning before your initial visitor status \(e\.g\., usually 6 months starting on the day you first enter Canada\) ends\. You may print out section 190\(3\)\(f\) of [Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations](https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2002-227/page-25.html#docCont:~:text=%28f%29%C2%A0to%20re%2Denter%20Canada%20following%20a%20visit%20solely%20to%20the%20United%20States%20or%20St.%20Pierre%20and%20Miquelon%2C%20if%20they) to carry with you in case the border officer has questions about your re\-entry to Canada\.

### About your Electronic Travel Authorization \(eTA\)

If you are from an [eTA expansion country](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/eta/eligibility/eta-x.html), your eTA can be used to board flights to Canada, however you would need to have a TRV to enter Canada by land \(car, bus or train\) or sea \(boat or cruise ship\)\. For example, if you travel from your home country to the US, then drive from the US to Canada, a TRV would be required to enter Canada by car\. If you travel from Canada to the US and back without travelling to a third country, you could re\-enter Canada without a TRV as per above\. For students from Mexico, please see the [Feb 29, 2024, policy changes](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/campaigns/eta-work-visa-mexico.html)\.

## When you can travel[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/travelling\-to\-canada/check\-eligible/\#when\-you\-can\-travel](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/check-eligible/#when-you-can-travel)

There is no specific earliest date you can travel\. However, an officer may have concerns if you are travelling several months before you begin your studies\. Arriving a month before you begin or resume studies should be considered reasonable\. You cannot work in Canada until you have begun full\-time studies and [meet the requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/)\. 

If you must travel earlier, prepare a detailed explanation and supporting documents, if possible, in case the airline or border officer asks\. The Canada Border Services Agency \(CBSA\) officer you meet at the airport/border crossing will make the final decision on whether or not to admit you to Canada\.

If you took a [gap in studies](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/taking-time-away-school-international/) and are not currently enrolled, you should avoid travelling to Canada more than a month before you resume studies\. Contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support\.

Do not travel or purchase non\-refundable flight tickets or make non\-refundable accommodation deposits until you have received the right documents to study and travel to Canada \([see above](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/check-eligible/#:~:text=Have%20valid%20documents%20to%20travel%20to%20Canada)\)\.

### Booking your flight\(s\)

Be aware of local rules if you are transiting airports in other countries en route to Canada\. Check the transit country’s immigration department website and see the [International Air Transport Association \(IATA\) page](https://www.iatatravelcentre.com/) for guidance on international visa and passport requirements\.

You will need to get your study permit at the **first** airport you arrive to in Canada\. For example, if you arrive in Toronto and then take another flight to Vancouver, you must get your study permit in Toronto\. Consider booking flights which have a long layover to allow time for immigration\.

#### Getting to UBC or your final destination

UBC does not offer airport pick\-up services\. For transportation options from YVR airport, check [YVR’s transportation information](https://www.yvr.ca/en/passengers/transportation)\. You can also plan your trip via public transit by using [Translink’s trip planner](https://www.translink.ca/trip-planner) or [Google maps](https://maps.google.com/)\. 

To get to UBC by public transit, consider taking the Canada Line train from the airport to the Oakridge\-41st Avenue station then take the R4 express bus to UBC, or get off at the Broadway\-City Hall station, then take the 99 B\-line express bus to UBC\.

### Driving across the border

The largest border crossing near UBC is the [Douglas \(Peace Arch\) border crossing](https://do-rb.cbsa-asfc.cloud-nuage.canada.ca/?lang=en_CA&id=405), which is open 24 hours\. See the list of [border crossings and hours](https://do-rb.cbsa-asfc.cloud-nuage.canada.ca/?lang=en_CA)\.

Also, see considerations when [temporarily importing a vehicle](https://tc.canada.ca/en/road-transportation/importing-vehicle/temporarily-importing-vehicles)\.

## Get advice on whether you should travel[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/travelling\-to\-canada/check\-eligible/\#get\-advice\-on\-whether\-you\-should\-travel](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/check-eligible/#get-advice-on-whether-you-should-travel)

If you have unusual circumstances, to receive advice on documents for travel or timing of travelling, you may email or call the [Canada Border Services Agency](https://www.cbsa-asfc.gc.ca/contact/bis-sif-eng.html) \(CBSA\)\. If you are calling, please ask for and take note of the agent’s badge number, the date and time you speak with the agent, and record notes of your conversation in case you need to refer to this in the future\. Please note the CBSA officer you meet with when you arrive in Canada will make the final decision on whether you can enter Canada\.

You may also consider contacting your airline to confirm what documentation they will request from you when boarding your flight\.

## The information on this page may change[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/travelling\-to\-canada/check\-eligible/\#the\-information\-on\-this\-page\-may\-change](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/check-eligible/#the-information-on-this-page-may-change)

The immigration information on this page has been reviewed and endorsed by Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultants \(RCICs\) or Regulated International Student Immigration Advisors \(RISIAs\) in compliance with the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and Regulations\. However, this is not a legal document and information may change without notice\. Always refer to [Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada](http://www.cic.gc.ca/) \(IRCC\) for the most up\-to\-date information\.

title: What to bring to Canada
content_markdown:
## Documents to bring[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/travelling\-to\-canada/what\-bring\-canada/\#documents\-to\-bring](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/what-bring-canada/#documents-to-bring)

There are important documents you should be sure to have in your carry\-on luggage as you travel\.

### All students

-   **UBC Proof of Enrolment Letter**  
    If you’ve already registered in courses, you can bring a current [Letter of Enrolment](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/extend-study-permit-within-canada/gather-required-documents-study-permit-extension/#:~:text=Letter%20of%20Enrolment%20%28listed%20as%20%E2%80%98Letter%20of%20Acceptance%E2%80%99%20on%20your%20MyCIC%20checklist%29) as proof that you are a current, enrolled student\. This letter should ideally be issued the week before you travel\.
-   **Advance Declaration \(optional\)**  
    You can bring your completed [Advance Declaration](https://www.canada.ca/en/border-services-agency/services/arrivecan.html) on your phone or bring a printout\.
-   **Passport**  
    Always keep [your passport](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/passports/) with you when travelling\. 
-   **Visa or eTA**  
    Depending on your country of citizenship, you will need a valid [Temporary Resident Visa](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/) \(TRV\) or [Electronic Travel Authorization](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/eta.html) \(eTA\) — [US citizens and lawful US permanent residents](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/entry-requirements-country.html#lawful-pr-us:~:text=American%20citizens,how%20you%E2%80%99re%20travelling.) are exempt\.
-   **Proof of health insurance**  
    Bring proof of health insurance\. This might include your MSP card, virtual [iMED card](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international/) or other basic insurance\. See [Before you travel to Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/before-you-travel/) for details\. If your iMED card does not arrive in time for your travels, you can show a Border Services Officer the [iMED page](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international#when-am-i-covered) with details on coverage\.
-   **Your spouse/common law partner and/or children’s documents \(if applicable and you are travelling together\)**  
    Bring relevant [documents for your family](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/documentation-family/), such as Letters of Introduction for their study or work permits \(if applicable\), proof of relationship, their passport with valid TRV or eTA, and proof of health insurance\. Check additional documentation you may need when travelling with a [minor](http://cbsa-asfc.gc.ca/travel-voyage/td-dv-eng.html#children)\. 

### Current students with study permits

In addition to the above list, all students continuing to study at UBC who already have a study permit must bring with them:

-   **Study permit**  
    You need to have your original, [valid study permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/study-permits#maintaining-your-student-status) with you\.
-   **A letter from your program explaining any required student work placements \(if applicable\)**  
    You will need this letter if your required work placement is not already mentioned in your letter of admission\. If you have one, you should also bring a current, valid job offer\.
-   **Proof of funds for yourself and any accompanying dependents**  
    We recommend your bank documents be issued within 30 days before traveling\. See [proof of means of financial support](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/extend-study-permit-within-canada/gather-required-documents-study-permit-extension/) for sample documents\. If you have paid for tuition, download your [proof of payment](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/downloading-your-proof-of-tuition-payment-account-statement/) in Workday*\.* There is no specific minimum amount required\. However, ideally you would show you have access to **at least $22,895**\. The amount required for [additional family members](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/get-documents/financial-support.html#:~:text=If%20you%20apply%20on%20or%20after%20September%201%2C%202025) depends on how many dependents you have\.
-   **Medical exam, if required**  
    If you’ve been in a [designated country](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/medical-police/medical-exams/requirements-temporary-residents/country-requirements.html) for 6 months or more consecutively in the past year, are a medical student or will work in [jobs which require a medical exam](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/#if-you-work-with-children-or-seniors-in-healthcare-settings-or-in-agriculture), bring a copy of your medical exam \(“e\-medical”\) completed within 12 months before travelling\. See the [Before you travel to Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/before-you-travel/) page for details\. 

### New students and current students who need a new study permit

In addition to the above list, if you are a new student, or a current student who applied for a new study permit from outside of Canada, you’ll also need to bring:

-   **A Letter of Introduction**  
    This is your electronic study permit approval, or [Letter of Introduction](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/#get-your-study-permit-approval)\. 
-   **Your UBC Letter of Admission \(new students only\)**  
    This is also known as your offer letter or Letter of Acceptance\. How you [get your Letter of Admission](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/tutorial-apply-initial-study-permit-required-documents/) depends on your program\.
-   **Proof of funds for yourself and any accompanying dependents**  
    We recommend you bring copies of the financial documents you provided in your study permit application\. In addition, we recommend you bring recent financial documents which are issued within 30 days before traveling and proof of tuition payment, if you have paid for tuition\. See [proof of means of financial support](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/tutorial-apply-initial-study-permit-required-documents/) for sample documents\. Download your [proof of tuition payment](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/downloading-your-proof-of-tuition-payment-account-statement/) from Workday*\.* You should be able to show proof of **at least $22,895**\. The amount required for [additional family members](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/get-documents/financial-support.html#:~:text=If%20you%20apply%20on%20or%20after%20September%201%2C%202025) depends on how many dependents you have\.
-   **Valid medical exam, if required**  
    Bring a copy of your medical exam \(e\-medical\) if you required one for your study permit application, or get a medical exam if your situation changed since you applied and you now [require one](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/medical-police/medical-exams/requirements-temporary-residents.html#needs)\. Your medical exam should be completed within 12 months before travelling\. If it has been more than 12 months since you took your exam, you must take another medical exam before travelling\. See the [Before you travel to Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/before-you-travel/) page for details\. 
-   **English language test results, if you have them \(recommended\)**  
    If you provided English language test results in your study permit application, bring a copy of your results, if applicable\.

### Other helpful documents to carry on the plane

-   Driver’s license
-   Medical or immunization records, including proof of COVID\-19 vaccination\(s\)
-   Marriage certificate and notarized copies
-   Documents for dependents accompanying you: passports, birth certificates, children’s immunization and school records
-   National identity document from your country

## What to pack[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/travelling\-to\-canada/what\-bring\-canada/\#what\-to\-pack](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/what-bring-canada/#what-to-pack)

There are some things you cannot bring to Canada or will need to declare when you arrive, such as cash over CAD $10,000 and food or animal products\.

Refer to the Canada Border Services Agency’s [visitors to Canada](https://www.cbsa-asfc.gc.ca/travel-voyage/ivc-rnc-eng.html) and [restricted and prohibited goods](https://www.cbsa-asfc.gc.ca/travel-voyage/rpg-mrp-eng.html) pages for details\.

Learn what to do if you plan to [travel with your pet\(s\)](https://inspection.canada.ca/importing-food-plants-or-animals/pets/eng/1326600389775/1326600500578)\.

Also, we recommend you bring snacks in case of a long wait upon arrival\.

### Medication

Keep your medication in your carry\-on bag in its original packaging, along with a prescription from the doctor\. If you are planning on bringing medication or health products with you, check that the quantity or type is not [restricted](https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/drugs-health-products/compliance-enforcement/importation-exportation/personal-use-health-products-guidance/document.html) or if they have [controlled substances](https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/health-concerns/controlled-substances-precursor-chemicals/controlled-substances/compliance-monitoring/travelling-into-and-out-of-canada-with-prescription-medication-containing-controlled-substances.html)\. 

It’s a good idea to bring a copy of your medical records for you and the family members who travel with you\. If you have a chronic medical condition, have your doctor write a short medical history, preferably in English, for your new doctor in Vancouver\. Bring records including the dates of any immunizations and medical tests you have done\.

## The information on this page may change[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/travelling\-to\-canada/what\-bring\-canada/\#the\-information\-on\-this\-page\-may\-change](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/what-bring-canada/#the-information-on-this-page-may-change)

The immigration information on this page has been reviewed and endorsed by Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultants \(RCICs\) or Regulated International Student Immigration Advisors \(RISIAs\) in compliance with the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and Regulations\. However, this is not a legal document and information may change without notice\. Always refer to [Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada](http://www.cic.gc.ca/) \(IRCC\) for the most up\-to\-date information\.
