| Robert H\. Lee Alumni Centre | 16 | On East Mall at west end of the Alumni Centre |
| Ponderosa Commons | 17 | On West Mall, at the south end of the layby in front of Ponderosa Commons North |

Other areas of campus can be accessed via nearby [accessible parking](https://parking.ubc.ca/) or public transit\. Learn more about [public transit](https://planning.ubc.ca/transportation) on the UBC campus\.

## UBC Accessibility Shuttle policies

### Shuttle pick\-up and drop off

-   The shuttle stops only at designated stops\. Please check the [shuttle service map](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/ubc-accessibility-shuttle/#areas-served-by-the-accessibility-shuttle) for a list of campus stops\.
-   Passengers who do not arrive on time or fail to cancel their booking before their pick\-up will be flagged\. Repeated missed rides may result in the suspension of riding privileges\.
-   Accessibility Shuttle passengers are limited to 3 rides per day\.

#### Situations where service may be denied

Employees reserve the right to deny service if:

-   The passenger is intoxicated and shuttle staff determine they are unable to care for themselves or provide informed consent\.
-   The shuttle staff, passenger, or property is at risk of harm\.
-   The passenger fails to comply with program policies or treat staff respectfully\.

### Food and drink on the shuttle

Open food or beverages are not permitted on the shuttle\. You are allowed to have a beverage in a closed container\. 

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/centre\-for\-accessibility/ubc\-accessibility\-shuttle/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/ubc-accessibility-shuttle/#additional-resources)

-   [Translink trip planner](https://www.translink.ca/)  
    Map out your bus route to campus, making sure to check if your TransLink stop is wheelchair\-accessible\.
-   [HandyDART](https://www.translink.ca/rider-guide/transit-accessibility/handydart)  
    Take advantage of TransLink’s door\-to\-door shared ride service, available for those who are unable to safely navigate public transit\.
-   [UBC Campus and Community Planning](https://planning.ubc.ca/vancouver/transportation-planning/transportation-options/transit/ubc-community-shuttle-routes)  
    Get details about transportation on campus, including UPass information, campus maps, and more\.
-   [UBC Wayfinding map tool](http://maps.ubc.ca/PROD/index.php)  
    View a detailed map of campus buildings with information on accessible entrances and locations of power and manual doors\.
-   [SPARC decal parking permits](https://www.sparc.bc.ca/parking-permits/)  
    Apply for a SPARC parking permit to access designated accessible parking spaces across campus and throughout BC\.
-   [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility)  
    Contact the Centre for details on a special needs parking permit that will allow you to park in UBC parkades at reduced rates\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/centre\-for\-accessibility/ubc\-accessibility\-shuttle/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/ubc-accessibility-shuttle/#if-you-have-questions)

-   For additional assistance or to book a ride, call [604 822 9929](tel:6048229929)\.
-   For comments, feedback, and inquiries, email [accessibility\.shuttle@ubc\.ca](mailto:accessibility.shuttle@ubc.ca)\.

title: Student code of conduct
content_markdown:
## About the Code of Conduct[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/student\-code\-conduct/\#about\-the\-code\-of\-conduct](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/student-code-conduct/#about-the-code-of-conduct)

The Student Code of Conduct sets out the standards of conduct expected of students\. It holds individuals and groups responsible for the consequences of their actions\. Failure to fulfill these responsibilities may result in the withdrawal of privileges or the imposition of sanctions\.

UBC is a community of students, faculty and staff involved in learning, teaching, research and other activities\. In accordance with the [UBC Respectful Environment Statement](http://www.hr.ubc.ca/respectful-environment/), all members of this community are expected to conduct themselves in a manner that contributes positively to an environment in which respect, civility, diversity, opportunity and inclusiveness are valued, so as to assure the success of both the individual and the community\. The Student Code of Conduct reflects a concern for these values and tries to ensure that members of UBC and the public can make use of and enjoy the activities, facilities and benefits of UBC without undue interference from others\.

The information provided on this page is an overview of the Student Code of Conduct\. It is not, nor is it intended to be, a substitute for the Code itself or UBC’s full policies and regulations regarding non\-academic student misconduct\. Students are responsible for reading, understanding and abiding by the Code\. The entire Student Code of Conduct is available in the Policies and Regulations section of the UBC Vancouver Academic Calendar under [Student Conduct and Discipline](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/student-conduct-and-discipline/discipline-non-academic-misconduct-student-code-conduct)\.

## When does the code apply?[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/student\-code\-conduct/\#when\-does\-the\-code\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/student-code-conduct/#when-does-the-code-apply)

The Student Code of Conduct applies to any student enrolled in a credit course at UBC, including co\-op and exchange students\.

The Code applies to conduct that occurs on or near the premises of UBC\. It also applies to conduct that occurs elsewhere if it is related to University\-sponsored programs or activities, \(such as travelling athletic teams\), or if it occurs in the context of a relationship between the student and a third party that involves the student’s standing, status or academic record at UBC\.

The Code does not apply to conduct that is assigned to another disciplinary body at the University, allegations regarding a student’s failure to meet standards of professional conduct, or conduct committed by a student solely in their capacity as an employee of UBC\.

Students living in residence may also be subject to a separate residence policy for conduct that occurs in any buildings managed by Student Housing and Community Services or the property surrounding these residences\. For further information, please review the applicable [Residence Contract/Residential Agreement](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/residence-contracts/)\.

### Sexual Misconduct Policy

Sexual misconduct is a form of non\-academic misconduct that is prohibited conduct and can give rise to discipline\. However, the applicable UBC policy that specifically governs sexual misconduct is UBC’s [Sexual Misconduct Policy](https://universitycounsel.ubc.ca/policies/sexual-misconduct-policy/) \(SC17\)\. 

The Sexual Misconduct Policy sets out the definition of sexual misconduct, applicable principles, and process as to how the University responds to and investigates allegations of sexual misconduct\. As such, it is the Sexual Misconduct Policy that applies to allegations of sexual misconduct rather than the Student Code of Conduct\. This means that allegations of conduct that is sexual misconduct as defined in the Sexual Misconduct Policy will be addressed under the Sexual Misconduct Policy and its investigatory process, rather than the process set under the Student Code of Conduct\. 

If a student is alleged to have engaged in multiple instances of misconduct that would engage both the Sexual Misconduct Policy and Student Code of Conduct, the responsible offices will work together to determine the appropriate next steps\. 

Additional information can be obtained from the [Sexual Violence Prevention and Response Office](https://svpro.ubc.ca/) \(SVPRO\), which provides confidential services for UBC community members who have experienced, or been impacted by, any form of sexual or gender\-based violence, harassment, or harm, regardless of where or when it took place\. 

Allegations of sexual misconduct can be reported to the [UBC Investigations Office](https://io.ubc.ca/) \(IO\), with specific information as to the reporting process found on the IO’s website\.

### UBC Residence Standards

Students living in residence may also be subject to a separate residence policy for conduct that occurs in any buildings managed by Student Housing and Community Services or the property surrounding these residences\. For further information, please review the applicable [Residence Contract/Residential Agreement](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/residence-contracts/)\.

## Prohibited conduct[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/student\-code\-conduct/\#prohibited\-conduct](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/student-code-conduct/#prohibited-conduct)

All municipal, provincial, and federal laws apply on campus\.

Prohibited conduct under the Code includes but is not limited to:

-   Assaulting, harassing, intimidating, or threatening another individual or group
-   Endangering the health or safety of others
-   Stealing, misusing, destroying, defacing or damaging UBC property or property belonging to someone else
-   Disrupting University activities
-   Using UBC facilities, equipment, services or computers without authorization
-   Making false accusations against any member of UBC
-   Supplying false information to UBC or forging, altering or misusing any UBC document or record
-   Storing, possessing or using real or replica firearms or other weapons, explosives \(including fireworks\), ammunition, or toxic or otherwise dangerous materials on University grounds
-   Using, possessing or distributing illegal drugs
-   Violating provincial liquor laws or UBC alcohol policies
-   Hazing
-   Encouraging, aiding, or conspiring in any prohibited conduct
-   Failing to comply with a disciplinary measure or disciplinary measures imposed under the procedures of this Code

## Disciplinary measures[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/student\-code\-conduct/\#disciplinary\-measures](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/student-code-conduct/#disciplinary-measures)

Disciplinary measures that may be imposed under the Code include but are not limited to: 

-   Written warning or reprimand
-   Probation, during which certain conditions must be fulfilled and good behaviour must be demonstrated
-   Payment of costs or compensation for any loss, damage or injury caused by the conduct
-   Issuance of an apology, made publicly or privately
-   Loss of certain privileges
-   Restriction or prohibition of access to, or use of, UBC facilities, services, activities, or programs
-   Fines or loss of fees
-   Relocation or exclusion from residence
-   Suspension
-   Expulsion

## Student resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/student\-code\-conduct/\#student\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/student-code-conduct/#student-resources)

-   [UBC Vancouver Academic Calendar Student Code of Conduct](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/student-conduct-and-discipline/discipline-non-academic-misconduct-student-code-conduct)
-   [UBC Office of the University Counsel](https://universitycounsel.ubc.ca/guides-and-resources/student-discipline)
-   [The Office of the Ombudsperson for Students](http://ombudsoffice.ubc.ca/)
-   [The AMS Advocacy Office](https://www.ams.ubc.ca/support-services/student-services/advocacy/) 
-   [The GSS Advocacy Office](https://gss.ubc.ca/advocacy/)
-   [http://communitysafety\.ubc\.ca/](http://communitysafety.ubc.ca/)[Community Safety](http://communitysafety.ubc.ca/)
-   [Equity & Inclusion Office](http://equity.ubc.ca/)
-   [Student Housing Services](http://www.housing.ubc.ca/)

title: Religion and spirituality
content_markdown:
## The importance of spirituality[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/\#the\-importance\-of\-spirituality](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/#the-importance-of-spirituality)

Learning about or joining a spiritual practice can help you feel connected to a greater purpose—something bigger than yourself\.

Spirituality is as important to student health as regular exercise and good eating habits\. It is not limited to mono\- or poly\-theistic religions, and can be described as the means by which a person may find the core of their being, their values, and the big picture\. 

Spirituality is also thought of as having a connection to those around you, your environment, and the universe that affects the way you perceive the world and is a force of inspiration\. It can help you solve problems with a greater sense of happiness, inner peace, and understanding, contributing to living a more fulfilled student life\.

## Spiritual practices[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/\#spiritual\-practices](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/#spiritual-practices)

Spiritual practices may include: 

-   Participating in a religious community
-   Joining a Humanist organization
-   Meditation, prayer, ceremony, or contemplation
-   Writing in a journal, playing music, painting
-   Activities to let your creativity flow and allow you to become more comfortable with yourself
-   Community involvement and volunteering

## Spiritual resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/\#spiritual\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/#spiritual-resources)

-   [Guide to Religious and Spiritual Accommodations](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/student_religious_spiritual_accommodations_guide.pdf)  
    Learn how to request faith\-based accommodations at UBC\.
-   [Chaplains at UBC](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/)  
    If you’re curious about a specific faith or want to talk to someone in the religious community on campus, find a chaplain at UBC\.
-   [Multifaith prayer rooms](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/ubc-multifaith-prayer-rooms/)  
    UBC provides multifaith prayer rooms for UBC Vancouver students of all faiths to pray, meditate, reflect or find quiet on campus\.
-   [Brock Commons South Community Space](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/brock-commons-south-community-space/)  
    Book the Community Space for your faith\-based or spiritual event or program\.
-   [Student\-run organizations](https://www.ams.ubc.ca/student-life/clubs/campusbase/)The AMS has a list of student\-run religious organizations on campus if you’re interested in joining a club and talking to peers about beliefs and spirituality\.

title: Chaplains
content_markdown:
The term “chaplain” has become a widely used and accepted term to refer to individuals who represent any religion or philosophical tradition\.

Chaplains are usually, but not always, ordained in a religious or spiritual tradition and work within a certain group or community\. They can be found in many places such as hospitals, the armed forces and universities\. The role of a chaplain varies depending on the community to which they belong\.

## Chaplains at UBC[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/\#chaplains\-at\-ubc](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/#chaplains-at-ubc)

Opportunities for religious observance are available under the guidance of Chaplains representing a variety of faiths\. Chaplains are an important spiritual resource for students, but they are not UBC employees and are completely separate and independent from UBC\. They are accountable to and financially supported by their own religious constituencies, and they do not act under the direction or authority of UBC\.

-   [Anglican](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/anglican-chaplain/)
-   [Anglican Church of Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/anglican-church-canada-chaplain/)
-   [Baptist](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/baptist-chaplains/)
-   [Brethren Tradition](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/brethren-tradition-chaplain/)
-   [Buddhist](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/buddhist-chaplain/)
-   [Chabad\-Jewish](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/chabad-jewish-chaplain/)
-   [Christian and Missionary Alliance](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/christian-missionary-alliance-cma-chaplain/)
-   [Every Nation](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/every-nation-chaplain/)
-   [Jewish](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/jewish-chaplain/)

-   [Mennonite Brethren](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/mennonite-brethren-chaplain/)
-   [UBC Thaqalayn Muslim Association](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/ubc-thaqalayn-muslim-association/)
-   [Muslim Students’ Association Chaplain](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/muslim-association-chaplain/)
-   [Pentecostal](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/pentecostal-chaplain/)
-   [Presbyterian](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/presbyterian-chaplain/)
-   [Roman Catholic](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/roman-catholic-chaplain/)
-   [Sikh](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/sikh-chaplain/)
-   [United Church of Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/united-church-canada-chaplain/)
-   [Zen Buddhist](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/zen-buddhist-chaplain/)

## What do the chaplains do?[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/\#what\-do\-the\-chaplains\-do](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/#what-do-the-chaplains-do)

The main function of the chaplains is to guide members of the UBC community in engaging with their spirituality and faith\. The details of each of the chaplains’ work are slightly different depending on the faith community they serve\. Most chaplains offer one\-on\-one pastoral and spiritual counseling, and opportunities to engage in the faith tradition they represent\. Most of the chaplains have student groups that include some combination of fellowship groups, meals, worship, faith exploration, and training or study in the traditions of their respective faith\. These groups are a good way to explore some of the “big questions” of life, as well as just have some fun and get to know your peers\.

Besides serving their own faith communities, chaplains cooperate on several fronts\. They participate in international student orientations, [Imagine UBC](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/orientations/imagine-ubc/), the Wellness Fair, and Convocation\. Chaplains participate in special programs, as well as occasionally sponsor workshops and lectures, film festivals, and art displays\. They also sometimes partner with others on campus to develop programs on social and ethical issues\.

### University Multifaith Chaplains Association

Chaplains generally have a professional graduate degree beyond a basic baccalaureate\. To become part of the [University Multifaith Chaplains Association](http://www.facebook.com/UMCAssociation/), members are expected to fulfill the conditions required by their religious body, whether this be ordination or its equivalent through education or training\.

The University Multifaith Chaplains Association makes a vital contribution to the wellbeing of the UBC community by engaging people in faith and spirituality, and meditation and emotional healing\. The Association also encourages community, including intercultural dialogue and collaboration, citizenship and leadership, and friendship\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/#if-you-have-questions)

The University Multifaith Chaplains Association office is in UBC Life Room 1303, but most chaplains also have other spaces they use\. If you are looking for a particular faith tradition, the contact information for each chaplain can be found on their individual pages\.

If you are looking for more general information \(or are not sure which chaplain offers what you are looking for\), you are welcome to contact the Coordinating Chaplain, Craig O’Brien, at [pastorcraigobrien@gmail\.com](mailto:pastorcraigobrien@gmail.com)\.

title: UBC Multifaith Prayer Rooms
content_markdown:
UBC provides multifaith prayer rooms on campus for students of all faiths to pray, meditate, reflect, or find quiet\.

Multifaith prayer rooms are generally available on a drop\-in basis during the building’s open hours, unless otherwise stated\. You may have to wait for a space in the room to become free\.

Find a prayer room on the Vancouver campus:

-   [Brock Commons South Multifaith Prayer and Quiet Contemplation Room](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/ubc-multifaith-prayer-rooms/brock-commons-south-multifaith-prayer-and-quiet-contemplation-room/)
-   [Wesbrook Building Prayer Room](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/ubc-multifaith-prayer-rooms/wesbrook-building-prayer-room/)
-   [West Mall Swing Space Prayer Room](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/ubc-multifaith-prayer-rooms/west-mall-swing-space-prayer-room/)
-   [Marine Drive Residence Prayer Room](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/ubc-multifaith-prayer-rooms/marine-drive-residence-prayer-room/)
-   [AMS Prayer Space in the AMS Student Nest](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/ubc-multifaith-prayer-rooms/ams-prayer-space/)

If you’re a UBC Okanagan student, find [spiritual or multi\-faith spaces](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/health-wellness/spiritual-multi-faith-space/) for your campus\.

## Ablution stations[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/ubc\-multifaith\-prayer\-rooms/\#ablution\-stations](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/ubc-multifaith-prayer-rooms/#ablution-stations)

Individual and single\-occupancy ablution stations are available for student use in the Brock Commons South, Wesbrook, and West Mall Swing Space Prayer Rooms for those who need to perform ritual washing of oneself before prayer, also known as “wudu”\.

Ablution stations can be accessed for individual and private use in the following rooms:

-   Rooms 4110A and 4110B in Brock Commons South
-   Rooms 132A and 132B in the Wesbrook Building
-   Room 209 in the West Mall Swing Space

## Prayer room rules and responsibilities[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/ubc\-multifaith\-prayer\-rooms/\#prayer\-room\-rules\-and\-responsibilities](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/ubc-multifaith-prayer-rooms/#prayer-room-rules-and-responsibilities)

All prayer rooms are shared and rely largely on the respect of users\. They are open only to UBC students, not external individuals or organizations\.

Please also review UBC’s [Student Code of Conduct](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/student-code-conduct/) and [Respectful Environment Statement for Students, Faculty, and Staff](https://hr.ubc.ca/working-ubc/respectful-environment) and follow the regulations of use\.

-   Leave the room tidy for the next user\.
-   Take personal items of religious practice with you\.
-   Do not block others from using the room for long periods\.
-   Keep noise to a minimum\. No general conversations\.
-   No eating or drinking in the rooms\.
-   No mobile phone calls or use of other devices\.
-   No collecting of money without permission\.
-   No candles, incense, or open flames of any kind\.
-   No distribution of flyers or posters\.
-   No holding meetings\.
-   No sleeping\.

### Other guidelines

-   **Footwear**  
    Please remove footwear upon entering the prayer room\.
-   **Speakers**  
    The use of speakers is not permitted unless otherwise stated under the specific room rules and regulations\.
-   **Events**  
    Multifaith prayer rooms are intended for drop\-in use during opening hours, unless otherwise stated\. The multifaith prayer rooms are not available for drop\-in events\. To book alternative rooms, refer to UBC’s [general events or room booking process](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/organizing-campus-events/booking-an-event-space/)\.
-   **Other potential users of multifaith prayer rooms**  
    The opportunity for space, quiet, retreat, and refuge may help many in managing life, health, and wellbeing\. During a traumatic event, such as bereavement, these spaces can be useful places of calm recollection\. Users for whom religion may be of no obvious significance are equally welcome\.
-   **Ablution stations**  
    Ablution facilities are for individual student\-use only\. Any excessive water on the floor and/or seat should be dried off after use\.

## Reporting a problem about the facilities[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/ubc\-multifaith\-prayer\-rooms/\#reporting\-a\-problem\-about\-the\-facilities](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/ubc-multifaith-prayer-rooms/#reporting-a-problem-about-the-facilities)

If you encounter any issues with the prayer room or its use, please report it as soon as possible to the Office of the Vice\-President, Students at [vpsassist@mail\.ubc\.ca](mailto:vpsassist@mail.ubc.ca)\.

Concerns may include cleanliness, damage, lighting, misuse of these facilities, or complaints about other users\.

### Urgent concerns

In case of fire or emergency evacuation, follow the procedures posted in the rooms\. In the event of an incident or concern that requires attention, contact [UBC Security](https://security.ubc.ca/) by calling [604\.822\.2222](tel:6048222222)\. For emergencies that require an immediate response, call 911\.

title: Campus safety
content_markdown:
## If you’re injured[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/campus\-safety/\#if\-youre\-injured](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/campus-safety/#if-youre-injured)

**For medical emergencies**, please call [911](tel:911)\. 

If you’re injured, you can visit [UBC Student Health and Wellbeing](https://students.ubc.ca/health/student-health-service/) on campus, or go to [Urgent Care](http://www.vch.ca/Locations-Services/result?res_id=991) at the UBC Hospital\.

If you need help getting to a class or another location on campus due to mobility issues, book a ride on the [Accessibility Shuttle](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/ubc-accessibility-shuttle/)\.

## Contact Community Safety anytime[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/campus\-safety/\#contact\-community\-safety\-anytime](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/campus-safety/#contact-community-safety-anytime)

Community Safety is available 24/7\. They provide first aid support, can accompany you across campus anytime, and are here to help if you need assistance, feel unsafe, or notice suspicious activity\. Call [604 822 2222](tel:6048222222)\. For emergencies, call [911](tel:911)\.

You can also reach them immediately on a [Blue Phone](https://security.ubc.ca/home/safety-prevention-resources/emergency-blue-phones/), one of more than 85 blue\-coloured poles on campus that have the word “Assistance” printed on them\.

## Know the signs of an accidental drug poisoning[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/campus\-safety/\#know\-the\-signs\-of\-an\-accidental\-drug\-poisoning](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/campus-safety/#know-the-signs-of-an-accidental-drug-poisoning)

Many illegal substances in Canada can have unknown mixes of drugs in them, like fentanyl or benzodiazepines\. This has resulted in many deaths in British Columbia and across the country\. If you plan to use substances, [make a plan to reduce harm](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-topics/substance-use-health-harm-reduction/) and know how to [respond to accidental drug poisoning](https://towardtheheart.com/opioid-od-awareness)\.

You can get a free and confidential naloxone kit from [Wellness Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/health/wellness-centre/), at [AMS SASC](https://www.amssasc.ca/), or at any [participating BC pharmacy](http://www.naloxonetraining.com/training)\. There are also [fentanyl test strips](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-topics/substance-use-health-harm-reduction/) available on campus\.

## Keeping your stuff safe[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/campus\-safety/\#keeping\-your\-stuff\-safe](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/campus-safety/#keeping-your-stuff-safe)

Don’t leave valuables like your phone or computer unattended in libraries and other public spaces\. It can only take a few seconds for them to disappear\.

As a preventative measure, upload free device location software like [Find My iPhone](https://support.apple.com/en-ca/explore/find-my-iphone-ipad-mac-watch) to track your phone or computer if it should ever be lost or stolen\.

If you bike to campus, investing in a high\-quality lock goes a long way to preventing bike theft\. Check out [helpful tips](https://planning.ubc.ca/transportation/cycling/cycling-tips-and-resources) on keeping your bike safe and cycling to campus\. 

If you lose something on campus, you can search the [Lost and Found Database](https://lostandfound.ubc.ca/all-items) to check if your item has been turned in\. Most lost items will typically be brought to the on\-campus [Lost and Found desk](https://lostandfound.ubc.ca/)\.

## Walking at night on campus[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/campus\-safety/\#walking\-at\-night\-on\-campus](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/campus-safety/#walking-at-night-on-campus)

If you don’t feel comfortable walking around campus by yourself, particularly in the dark, plan to walk with friends, or contact [AMS Safewalk](https://www.ams.ubc.ca/support-services/student-services/safewalk/) for a co\-ed team to walk with you or drive you to your destination\.

AMS Safewalk is available until **2:00 am**\. [UBC Campus Security](http://security.ubc.ca/) is available 24/7 and will gladly provide the same service\.

## Staying safe online[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/campus\-safety/\#staying\-safe\-online](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/campus-safety/#staying-safe-online)

Watch out for emails that do not seem legitimate as they can be [phishing emails](https://privacymatters.ubc.ca/phishing-emails), which try to steal your personal info by inviting you to click on links\.

Remember that UBC will **never** send you an email asking for your Campus\-Wide Login or password\. 

Visit [Privacy Matters @ UBC](https://privacymatters.ubc.ca/) to learn more about how to stay safe online, including how to encrypt your computer and mobile devices\.​​

## Frauds and scams[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/campus\-safety/\#frauds\-and\-scams](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/campus-safety/#frauds-and-scams)

Unfortunately, there are many different frauds and scams out there, such as those impersonating government departments like the [Canada Revenue Agency](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html)\.

Visit the [RCMP website](http://bc.rcmp-grc.gc.ca/ViewPage.action?siteNodeId=2081&languageId=1&contentId=-1) for valuable tips on how to protect your money and remember that if something sounds too good to be true, it probably is\.

If you suspect a phone call, email, rental, job offer, or anything else may be a scam, or if you have been the victim of a scam, the best thing to do is call the police at 911\.

## Reach out for sexual assault support[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/campus\-safety/\#reach\-out\-for\-sexual\-assault\-support](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/campus-safety/#reach-out-for-sexual-assault-support)

If you have experienced sexual violence or if you know someone who has, call [604 822 1588](tel:6048221588) to contact the [Sexual Violence Prevention and Response Office](http://svpro.ubc.ca/) \(SVPRO\) for support\.

## Get safety alerts[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/campus\-safety/\#get\-safety\-alerts](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/campus-safety/#get-safety-alerts)

Sign up for the [UBC Alert system](https://srs.ubc.ca/emergency/get-notified/) to receive safety news and information from the university through the UBC Safe Vancouver app\. [Alertable](https://metrovancouver.org/services/emergency-management/emergency-notification-system) is a free app used by emergency management agencies across BC to issue regional alerts like wildfires, severe weather, and more\. Use this to stay informed about events that may impact your commute or region\.

## Preparing for emergencies[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/campus\-safety/\#preparing\-for\-emergencies](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/campus-safety/#preparing-for-emergencies)

Emergencies like earthquakes, fires, or severe weather can happen when you least expect them\. Knowing what to do ahead of time can make a big difference\.

Visit the [UBC Safety & Risk Services](https://srs.ubc.ca/) website to learn how to stay safe on campus in a variety of situations\. You’ll find simple checklists, emergency kit guides, evacuation tips, and more\.

## Reporting building or classroom issues[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/campus\-safety/\#reporting\-building\-or\-classroom\-issues](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/campus-safety/#reporting-building-or-classroom-issues)

Please contact [UBC Facilities](https://buildingoperations.ubc.ca/) if you notice broken lights, heating or air conditioning problems, unsafe building infrastructure, or overgrown landscaping\.

## About the Anglican Diocese of Canada[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/anglican\-chaplain/\#about\-the\-anglican\-diocese\-of\-canada](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/anglican-chaplain/#about-the-anglican-diocese-of-canada)

The Anglican tradition was formed after the Reformation when the Church of England embraced the theology of the Reformers, whose teachings were rooted in the early church\. It retained the ancient liturgical traditions that had been preserved by the church through the centuries\.

Our worship follows the traditional liturgical pattern centred on the preaching of the Word and the celebration of the Sacrament of Holy Communion\. We use the 2019 Book of Common Prayer\. 

The Anglican Diocese of Canada \(ADoC\), is affiliated with the [Anglican Church in North America](http://www.anglicanchurch.net/) and is part of the global [Fellowship of Confessing Anglicans](http://fca.net/), which affirms the [Jerusalem Declaration](http://www.anglicannetwork.ca/jerusalem_declaration_0608.htm)\.

## About the chaplains[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/anglican\-chaplain/\#about\-the\-chaplains](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/anglican-chaplain/#about-the-chaplains)

### Fr Geoff Chapman \(St\. Thomas Mission\)

[Headshot of Chaplain Geoff](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/3_fr.-geoff.jpg)

In South Africa, Fr Geoff completed two degrees in psychology before beginning a career in human resources management\. He became the founder and CEO of a remuneration consultancy and outsourced payroll administration company\. At age 38, he left this career to pursue a Master of Divinity degree \(M\.Div\) at Regent College in Vancouver\. He has been in pastoral ministry since 2003 and an Anglican Priest at St\. Thomas Mission since 2013\. He is currently pursuing doctoral studies at Emory University in Atlanta, Georgia\.

Fr Geoff’s journey of faith began at the age of 13, encountering Jesus while on a church retreat in 1977\. Through many years of highs and lows in his walk with God, he has learned to rely on the power and love of the Holy Spirit and to trust that God’s way is always best, no matter how rocky the road\. He has learned to appreciate the wisdom and grace of God as revealed in His Holy Word, and that He can be trusted in all things\.

As an ever\-growing disciple of Jesus, it is Fr Geoff’s privilege to share his faith and knowledge of God with all interested\. He would love to meet you for a chat anytime\.

You can contact Fr Geoff at [604 505 9992](tel:6045059992) or by email at [geoff@stthomasmission\.ca](mailto:geoff@stthomasmission.ca)\.

## Services and events[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/anglican\-chaplain/\#services\-and\-events](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/anglican-chaplain/#services-and-events)

Check out weekly events being offered in the Chapel at Carey Theological College on UBC campus, located at 1815 Wesbrook Mall\. Find [more information](http://stthomasmission.ca/) online\.

-   **Sunday Holy Communion**   
    Attend worship at Carey Chapel on Sundays at 6 pm, usually followed by supper\.
-   **Midweek Holy Communion**  
    On special occasions, we have a short communion service on Wednesdays at 7:30 am, followed by a simple breakfast\.
-   **Catechism**  
    We run Catechism classes on a weekday evening\. Anyone who wants to know more about Christian faith is welcome to join\. For more information, speak to Fr Geoff\.
-   **Bible Study**  
    Attend small, mid\-week Bible Study groups to read the Bible and pray together\. For more information email Fr Geoff at [geoff@stthomasmission\.ca](mailto:geoff@stthomasmission.ca)\.

## Find St\. Thomas Mission online[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/anglican\-chaplain/\#find\-st\-thomas\-mission\-online](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/anglican-chaplain/#find-st-thomas-mission-online)

-   [Website](https://www.stthomasmission.ca/)
-   [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@st.thomasmission)
-   [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/stthomasmissionvancouver) 
-   [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/st.thomasmission/)

## About the Anglican Church of Canada[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/anglican\-church\-canada\-chaplain/\#about\-the\-anglican\-church\-of\-canada](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/anglican-church-canada-chaplain/#about-the-anglican-church-of-canada)

As a partner in the worldwide Anglican Communion and in the Universal Church, the Anglican Church of Canada proclaims and celebrates the gospel of Jesus Christ in worship and action\.

We value our heritage of biblical faith, reason, liturgy, tradition, bishops and synods, and the rich variety of our life in community\. We acknowledge that God is calling us to greater diversity of membership, wider participation in ministry and leadership, better stewardship in God’s creation, and a stronger resolve in challenging attitudes and structures that cause injustice\. Guided by the Holy Spirit, we commit ourselves to respond to this call in love and service, and to more fully live the life of Christ\.

This chaplaincy is a welcoming community that embraces diversity and inclusivity\. Our doors are open to all, regardless of background, age, or identity\. Come as you are, with as many questions as you have, and find a welcome in the Anglican Church of Canada\.

## About the chaplains[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/anglican\-church\-canada\-chaplain/\#about\-the\-chaplains](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/anglican-church-canada-chaplain/#about-the-chaplains)

### Rev\. Alecia Greenfield

Alecia Greenfield is the rector at St Anselm’s Church, the UBC Anglican Parish\. She is active in eco\-justice ministries\. You can contact Rev\. Alecia at rector@stanselms\.ca\. 

### Rev\. Dr\. Rob James

Rob James is the Associate Professor of Anglican Formation and Studies at the Vancouver School of Theology\. He was ordained in the Church of England, and before coming to Canada, was a parish priest in Gloucestershire and then worked at Wells Cathedral, in Somerset\. You can contact Rev\. Dr\. Rob James at [rjames@vst\.edu](mailto:rjames@vst.edu)\.

### Rev\. Alisdair Smith

Alisdair Smith is the Chaplain at the Vancouver School of Theology\. He is a Deacon in the Anglican Church of Canada and served for over 20 years as Deacon and Business Chaplain at Christ Church Cathedral in Vancouver\. You can contact Alisdair at [asmith@vst\.edu](mailto:asmith@vst.edu)\. 

## Services and events[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/anglican\-church\-canada\-chaplain/\#services\-and\-events](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/anglican-church-canada-chaplain/#services-and-events)

-   **Midday Eucharist**  
    Attend midday Eucharist at Epiphany Chapel \([6030 Chancellor Boulevard](https://maps.app.goo.gl/arWvHScEVNrHVZDs8), accessible via Iona Drive\) on Tuesdays at 12:15 pm\. This service runs from Sep 12 to Dec 5, 2023, excluding Oct 24\. Bring your own lunch if you’re able to stay for conversation\.
-   **Student evening gatherings**  
    Meet other students at Epiphany Chapel \([6030 Chancellor Boulevard](https://maps.app.goo.gl/arWvHScEVNrHVZDs8), accessible via Iona Drive\) and enjoy conversation, discussion, prayer, and free food\. Gatherings are held at 6:00 pm on Wednesday evenings\.
-   **Sunday Eucharist**  
    Attend a Eucharist held at St\. Anselm’s Church \([5210 University Boulevard](https://maps.app.goo.gl/gCKDnpb4YiCyZeD29)\), just opposite the University Golf Club, at 10:30 am every Sunday\.

title: Baptist Chaplains
content_markdown:
## About the Baptist faith tradition[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/baptist\-chaplains/\#about\-the\-baptist\-faith\-tradition](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/baptist-chaplains/#about-the-baptist-faith-tradition)

Baptists are Christian people who share beliefs about God and mankind’s relationship to Him\. We believe the Bible is God’s authoritative word to us, and that Jesus is the only hope for a lost and broken world\. We also subscribe to a theology of believer’s baptism \(as opposed to infant baptism\), salvation through faith alone, Scripture alone as the rule of faith and practice, and the autonomy of the local church\. In Canada, there are several Baptist churches and groups who associate voluntarily with each other for common causes\. These include the Canadian National Baptist Convention and the Canadian Baptists of Western Canada\.

At UBC, we offer several ways for you to interact with and discuss the Bible, learn about Jesus, and find hope in your individual situation\. University is a great time to explore what you believe and ask your questions about God and what differences He can make in your life\. Baptist chaplains are available to support you in this journey, and provide a safe atmosphere where you can wrestle with the big questions and grow your personal faith\. Our groups are open to everyone, so you do not have to be a Baptist to participate\.

### Our beliefs

We believe that the Scriptures of the Old and New Testaments are inspired by God and without error, and that they are our supreme and final authority in faith and life\. We believe in one God, the Creator, eternally existing in three persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit\. We believe that Jesus Christ was conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of the virgin Mary—100% God and man\.

We believe that the Holy Spirit gives spiritual life to all believers, enabling them to understand Biblical truth, empowering them for godly living, and equipping them for service and witness\.

We believe that God created Adam and Eve in His divine image, that they sinned resulting in the spiritual, physical, and emotional fall of humanity\. We believe that all people by their own decisions have chosen to sin and thereby stand guilty before God and are in need of a Saviour\.

We believe that the Lord Jesus Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, as a representative and substitution sacrifice\. We believe that all who by faith receive the Lord Jesus Christ are born again of the Holy Spirit and thereby become children of God\.

We believe that every person from every language, tribe, and nation is valuable and loved by God, who offers special privileges and gifts to anyone who puts their faith in His Son, Jesus\. 

## Meet the chaplains[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/baptist\-chaplains/\#meet\-the\-chaplains](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/baptist-chaplains/#meet-the-chaplains)

[Headshot of Chaplain Craig O Brien](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/4_craig-obrien.jpg)

### Craig O’Brien

Craig is glad to be part of the UBC campus community sharing life with students who are the heartbeat of the community\. They bring their energy, ambitions, and passions to life at UBC\. During his own university years, Craig remembers enjoying the opportunities available to him while also feeling some anxiety as he explored what to study and what to aim his life at\. He found himself asking questions like, “What vision of success is going to shape my life?” In the process of discovery, he changed majors several times, used the summers as a way of exploring possible vocations, and talked a lot with friends and mentors about the future\.

While it is important to learn about oneself, Craig also discovered he needed something more\. Through these transitions, he began to entrust himself to Jesus Christ and to explore the implications of life with Him in all relationships\. His childhood faith began to change, expand, and mature\. His earnest desire is for others to know the joy of having purpose and living loved in a relationship with God\.

Craig obtained his Bachelor’s of Arts in Speech Communications from the University of Georgia in 1990\. He later received his Master of Divinity from Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary in 1993 and then his Doctor of Ministry from Golden Gate Baptist Theological Seminary in 2003\.

Craig currently serves as a pastor with Origin Church which gathers in the UBC campus community and is the co\-ordinating chaplain for the University Multifaith Chaplains Association at UBC\.

You can reach Craig by emailing [pastorcraigobrien@gmail\.com](mailto:pastorcraigobrien@gmail.com), or by calling [604 644 3961](tel:604%20644%203961)\.

[Profile of Suzanne from Baptist Chaplain](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/baptist_church_chaplain_suzanne.jpg)

### Suzanne Perry

Since 2006, Suzanne Perry has served as a Chaplain and International Student Minister at UBC, helping people in the international community on campus adjust to life in Canada\. She also encourages students who are searching for God\. Suzanne is happy to welcome new international students to UBC\. She recognizes moving to a new country requires great courage and she holds a great deal of admiration for the brave students who have chosen to study abroad\. English Corner is one of the groups she organizes, along with other special interest groups\. Some of which are religious in nature, some are not\. Everyone is welcome\!

To register for English Corner, email [speakinglisteningexploring@gmail\.com](mailto:speakinglisteningexploring@gmail.com)\.

Suzanne’s bachelor’s degree is in Human Resources Counseling: Specialization in Services to the Deaf \(1992\)\. Ten years later, she followed the call to pursue an international ministry career and enrolled in the Southwestern Seminary, earning a Master of Divinity \(MDivBL\) degree\. 

You can reach Suzanne by emailing [suzanneperry\.ca@gmail\.com](mailto:suzanneperry.ca@gmail.com), or by calling [604 839 0484](tel:604%20839%200484)\. 

[Profile of Susan Guo from Baptist Chaplain](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/baptist_church_susan_guo.jpg)

### Susan Guo

Susan was born in China \(fluent in Mandarin\) and immigrated to Canada with her family at the age of 10\. While she was striving to find meaning and happiness in achievements, relationships and material things, she experienced guilt, shame, fear and hopelessness\. Susan’s life was transformed in her third year of university when she heard the good news of Jesus and received Him as her personal Lord and Savior\. She began to experience God’s unfailing love, abundant grace, unexplainable peace, and living hope\.

Susan obtained her Bachelor’s of Science in Civil Engineering with a specialization in Energy and Environmental Engineering from the University of Calgary in 2019\. During her three years of working in the engineering field, God stirred within her a holy discontentment for her job and a deep longing for young adults to meet Jesus and experience transformation\. In 2022, Susan committed herself to a new role where she can meet students where they are\. She enjoys listening to people’s stories and walking with them in their faith journey amidst the realities of everyday life\. Susan delights in gathering people around the table to share food and do life together – and there is a seat for you\!

You are invited and welcome to connect with Susan by emailing [shushanguo@gmail\.com](mailto:shushanguo@gmail.com), or by calling [403 869 9368](tel:403%20869%209368)\.

[baptist church joshua smith](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/baptist_church_joshua_smith.jpg)

### Joshua Smith

Joshua finds great joy in serving as a Chaplain at UBC\. He enjoys spending time with people, making friends, laughing lots, and caring for the needs of others\. Board games, ice cream, and praying for others also bring him great joy\.

He is not exempt from past hurts and personal challenges\. He has faced the loss of family, bullying during childhood, financial mistakes, feelings of failure, and of being a hypocrite at times\.

That is why he loves his job—he cares for students through the love of Jesus, in many ways\. Experiencing that care from others has changed him\. Now, he desires to care for students who face greater challenges that he did and hopes to invest in their faith journeys\.

To help equip him in his career and love for others, he attended the Canadian Baptist Theological Seminary and College, where he graduated with a Bachelor of Christian Studies\. 

Fun fact, Joshua is married to the lovely Susan Guo who also serves as Chaplain at UBC\. Please do say hello to Joshua and he will be glad to connect\.

You can email him at [joshuamsmith98@gmail\.com](mailto:joshuamsmith98@gmail.com) or text him at [5878340668](tel:5878340668) anytime\.

## Services and events[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/baptist\-chaplains/\#services\-and\-events](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/baptist-chaplains/#services-and-events)

-   For the latest updates on all services, gathering, Bible studies and volunteer opportunities, please refer to the [Origin Church linktree](https://linktr.ee/originchurch)\. You can also learn more about [Origin Church](https://originchurch.ca/)\.
-   English Corner conversation group meets weekly\. Visit the English Corner at UBC [Facebook page](https://www.facebook.com/English-Corner-at-UBC-197473193619924) or email [speakinglisteningexploring@gmail\.com](mailto:speakinglisteningexploring@gmail.com) to register or for more information\.

title: Brethren Tradition Chaplain
content_markdown:
## About the Brethren Tradition[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/brethren\-tradition\-chaplain/\#about\-the\-brethren\-tradition](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/brethren-tradition-chaplain/#about-the-brethren-tradition)

University Chapel is an interdenominational Christian church on the UBC campus that has its roots in the Brethren tradition\. Three of our pastors serve as UBC chaplains\. The Brethren Tradition grew out of the Anglican church in England in the 1830’s\. The Brethren tradition emphasizes that every Christian is equally called to live the Christian life and serve Jesus Christ in all they do\. It countered the idea that ministry was only done by ordained ministers, and that everyone else was just a spectator\. The idea of “the priesthood of all who believe” in Jesus has now become part of mainstream thinking in many denominations where laypeople actively serve and minister in their areas of gifting\.

## University Chapel on the UBC Campus[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/brethren\-tradition\-chaplain/\#university\-chapel\-on\-the\-ubc\-campus](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/brethren-tradition-chaplain/#university-chapel-on-the-ubc-campus)

University Chapel is an interdenominational and intercultural Christian community held together by our common belief in the God of the Bible\. We believe that the Bible is the inspired Word of God, that Jesus was the Messiah, and that through him every person may enter into a relationship with God empowered by the Holy Spirit\. Our core beliefs are outlined in the Nicene and Apostles’ Creeds\.

Our church community, “Three Families Under One Roof”, is made up of three different language worshipping congregations: English, Mandarin Chinese, and Korean\. Each Sunday morning, our “families” gather together for separate language services to experience God through sung worship, prayer, teaching, communion, and fellowship\. These three services all take place at the same time in different spaces within the church building\. Once or twice every quarter all three services come together in one single joint service to worship in all three languages together\.As Christians, we believe in the reliability and authority of the Bible as the Word of God\. Our core beliefs are outlined in a number of creeds \(statements of belief\) developed by the early church\. These include the Nicene Creed, the Apostles’ Creed and the Athanasian Creed\.

## Meet the chaplains[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/brethren\-tradition\-chaplain/\#meet\-the\-chaplains](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/brethren-tradition-chaplain/#meet-the-chaplains)

[Headshot of Chaplain Karen Daniels](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/2_karen-daniels_edited_hayley.jpg)

### Karen Daniels

Karen originally came to Vancouver to pursue a Masters Degree in Music Theory at UBC and enjoyed being part of a number of campus clubs\. She was involved with and served in leadership with InterVarsity Campus Ministries\. Karen has been a part of the University Chapel community for many years, serving on staff in a number of different roles since 2002\. It was through these different roles that she felt called to pursue an MDiv at Regent College\. Since that time, she has served in several pastoral roles and currently as the Executive Coordinating Pastor at UC\.

One of her passions is to help create spaces and events that help people build deeper relationships within their community, relationships that help to build a sense of belonging and a greater understanding of what it means to be the body of Christ, and relationships that encourage one another to continue to seek and know Christ more deeply\. 

You can contact Karen by emailing [karen@universitychapel\.org](mailto:karen@universitychapel.org), or by calling her at [604\-916\-5325](tel:%20604-916-5325)\. 

[Headshot of Chaplain Michael Low](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/1_michael-low.jpg)

### Michael Low

Michael is a graduate of the Faculty of Law, National University of Singapore\. He spent two decades in the marketplace, first as a litigator, before moving into wealth management, where he worked with high net worth clients to help them with their estate and succession planning\. It was in this role that he really found himself helping his clients to exercise stewardship of their resources\. It was also in this season that Michael began to ask the question of what his work meant to his Christian faith, and how that integration would look\. This led him to Regent College, where he graduated with an MA in Theological Studies, with a concentration in Marketplace Theology\. 

Michael has spent 20 years of lay ministry working with young adults of college age and older, and is passionate about helping them navigate the most tumultuous season of their lives, as they graduate and enter the workforce\. He has served as a Youth and Young Adult Pastor, lectured at a seminary in Singapore, as well as sat on the board of three churches and several non\-profits\. He is currently serving as the English Language Congregation Pastor at University Chapel\. He is also conversant in Mandarin and Cantonese, and in his spare time, is an avid scuba diver \(but only in tropical waters\!\)\. 

You can contact Michael by emailing [michael@universitychapel\.org](mailto:michael@universitychapel.org), or by calling him at [604\-353\-9920](tel:%20604-353-9920)\.

[Headshot of Chaplain Bruce Nie](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/5_bruce-nie.jpg)

### Bruce Nie

Bruce is originally from Qingdao, China where he was a human resource executive manager at several multinational companies\. He also served as a pastor for a church in Qingdao for many years\. 

In 2019 Bruce moved to Vancouver with his family to pursue theological studies at Regent College\. Bruce has served as the Chinese Language Pastor at University Chapel since 2022\. 

You can contact Bruce by emailing [bruce@universitychapel\.org](mailto:bruce@universitychapel.org), or by calling him at [778\-917\-9196](tel:%20604-353-9920)\.

title: Buddhist Chaplain
content_markdown:
## About Buddhism[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/buddhist\-chaplain/\#about\-buddhism](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/buddhist-chaplain/#about-buddhism)

The word “Buddha” is not a name, but a title designated to “one who has woken up\.” It refers to a being who has awakened to the true knowledge of the world and found release from suffering\. His enlightenment involves the deepest insight into the inter\-being of phenomenon and the Four Noble Truths \(the nature of suffering or unsatisfactoriness\)\. While anyone can practice towards enlightenment, some may not want to\. An analogy likens the Buddha to a doctor with a cure, but it is up to the patient to take the medicine\.

The Buddha is human, but an extraordinary one\. He is not a savior but a teacher, known as “satthar”, as it appears in the ancient Pāli texts\. He teaches out of compassion and sympathy the path of the end of suffering for the benefit and wellbeing of all living things\. The Buddha set in motion the wheel of “dhamma” with his teachings and established a community of disciples, the “saṅgha”\. Buddhism is in essence the learning and practice of the Buddha’s teachings of compassion and wisdom\. It is a continuous practice in search of sustainable happiness\.

Learn more about Buddhism below:

-   [Buddhistdoor Global](https://www.buddhistdoor.net/)
-   [Online Dictionary by Buddhistdoor](https://www2.buddhistdoor.net/dictionary/)

## About the Buddhist Chaplaincy[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/buddhist\-chaplain/\#about\-the\-buddhist\-chaplaincy](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/buddhist-chaplain/#about-the-buddhist-chaplaincy)

At UBC, Buddhist Chaplains offer you resources and support to integrate Buddhist teachings and practices with your study, work, and relationships\. Our events invite you to experience mindfulness, deep listening, and compassionate speech together\. Everyone in the UBC community with or without Buddhist background or practice is welcome\.

## Meet the chaplain[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/buddhist\-chaplain/\#meet\-the\-chaplain](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/buddhist-chaplain/#meet-the-chaplain)

[Profile of Ernest from Buddhist chaplain](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/chaplain_buddhism_ernest.jpg)

### Rev\. Dr\. Ernest C\.H\. Ng

*BA, MA  \(UChicago\), MBuddhStud, PhD \(HKU\), *CSCP, CPST, PSE \(CASC\)**, *Mindfulness \(MBCT, MPIM, TSM, MiSP\), CFRE, MFA\-P*

Ernest Ng is a Buddhist Chaplain with the UMCA at UBC and Multifaith Centre at SFU\. He focuses on the wellbeing of communities by volunteering at universities and charities\. He engages in religious and spiritual care, teaches mindfulness, and guides forest therapy\.

Ernest became a Buddhist and received the Five Precepts and Yogacara Bodhisattva vows under the Ch’an tradition\. He received the Three Jewels, the Five Mindfulness Trainings and the Fourteen Mindfulness Trainings with the Plum Village\. He is also a Certified Spiritual Care Practitioner, Certified Psychospiritual Therapist, and Provisional Supervisor\-Educator under Canadian Association of Spiritual Carehas \(CASC\)\. He completed Buddhist Chaplaincy Training, received Sixteen Precepts, and was ordained as Lay Minister with the Upaya Zen Center\.

Ernest is the CEO of [Tung Lin Kok Yuen, Canada Society](https://tlkycs.buddhistdoor.com/index.php?lang=en) \(TLKYCS\)\. TLKYCS is a Buddhist charity in Vancouver\. It has been dedicated to Buddhist teachings, education, and community services for 30 years\. Ernest specializes in applying wisdom tradition and spirituality into contemporary decision\-making\. His research publications include *Leveraging Happiness*, *Self\-sufficiency*, and *Introduction to Buddhist Economic*s\.

You can contact Ernest at [ernestngch@gmail\.com](mailto:ernestngch@gmail.com) or through his [Linktree](https://linktr.ee/ernestngch)\.

title: Chabad-Jewish Chaplain
content_markdown:
## About the Chabad Jewish Student Centre[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/chabad\-jewish\-chaplain/\#about\-the\-chabad\-jewish\-student\-centre](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/chabad-jewish-chaplain/#about-the-chabad-jewish-student-centre)

Chabad Jewish Student Centre Vancouver serves the Jewish student population at UBC and local community colleges with religious, educational, social, and recreational programming\. We strive to create a space where “Every Jew is Family” on campus for Jews of all backgrounds through a partnership between students and staff to help create cutting edge programming, plan social action projects, and offer volunteer opportunities\.

As a haven you can turn to when you are stressed or lonely and need a true friend, Chabad is a place where students can socialize in a comfortable home\-like setting filled with friends, superb food, and stimulating discussions\. It also acts as a forum where you can question your faith and not be afraid of judgment\. 

As a place for prayer and study, you can gain a deeper understanding and appreciation of your Jewish heritage\. The Centre provides texts and teachers for those who seek to learn, and has been recognized as one of the fastest growing and most vibrant, innovative and all\-inclusive organizations for Jewish students in North America\. 

Through all its growth and changes, Chabad’s warmth and intimacy remain the same\. At Chabad you will always find a friend\. Find us on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/chabadubc), [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/chabadubc/) or visit our [Chabad website](https://www.chabadubc.com/)\.

### Our philosophy

The Chabad Jewish Student Centre is based on the ideology of Chabad \(Chassidic Philosophy\) and fueled by the inspiration and teachings of the Lubavitcher Rebbe, Rabbi Menachem M\. Schneerson O\.B\.M, which have at their foundation the encompassing Mitzvah “to love every Jew as one loves himself” through Acts of Kindness and Mitzvahs\. It is our belief that every individual Jew makes an indispensable contribution to the whole of the Jewish people\. Chabad welcomes all Jews at their own pace and comfort level through innovative educational programs in all areas of Jewish life\.  
   
The vision for Chabad is a vibrant student centre that offers a meaningful Jewish experience to all who come in contact with it\. The values that lie at the heart of the Chabad Jewish Student Centre are embodied in Torah and Jewish tradition\. These values include spiritual growth and practice and Jewish learning to create a sense of belonging\.

## About Rabbi Chalom Loeub[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/chabad\-jewish\-chaplain/\#about\-rabbi\-chalom\-loeub](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/chabad-jewish-chaplain/#about-rabbi-chalom-loeub)

[Rabbi Chalom Loeub](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/chabad_chaplain_chalom_loeub.jpg)

Rabbi Chalom Loeub was born and raised in Montreal, Canada\. He spent three years studying in the Rabbinical College of Canada, followed by a two\-year Rabbinic internship in Singapore where he received his Rabbinical Ordination\. He served as the Associate Rabbi and program director at Chabad at Florida State University in Tallahassee, Florida for four years\.  
   
He speaks, reads, and writes English, French and Hebrew\. Chalom enjoys cooking, playing his musical instruments, having a good shmooze with students, and playing with his kids\.

You can contact Chalom by emailing [rabbi@chabadubc\.com](mailto:rabbi@chabadubc.com), or by calling him at [778 712 7703](tel:778%20712%207703)\.

## About Esti Loeub[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/chabad\-jewish\-chaplain/\#about\-esti\-loeub](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/chabad-jewish-chaplain/#about-esti-loeub)

Mrs\. Esti Loeub was born in Long Island, NY\. She studied at the Lubavitch Girls High School in Chicago, Illinois, and at the Ohel Chana Seminary in Melbourne, Australia\.  
After working for various Chabad institutions in Philadelphia and Westchester areas and serving as the program director for Chabad of the Upper East Side in Manhattan for three years, Esti is now co\-director of the Chabad Jewish Student Centre Vancouver\. She speaks English, Hebrew and Yiddish\. Esti enjoys biking, baking, and teaching Torah classes\.  
   
You can contact her by emailing [esti@chabadubc\.com](mailto:esti@chabadubc.com)\.

## Services and events[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/chabad\-jewish\-chaplain/\#services\-and\-events](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/chabad-jewish-chaplain/#services-and-events)

-   **Weekly Shabbat Dinners**  
    Meet other Jewish students over [Shabbat Dinner](https://www.chabadubc.com/templates/articlecco_cdo/aid/3515100/jewish/Shabbat-Chabad.htm) at the Chabad Jewish Student Centre \(view [Google Map](https://goo.gl/maps/iwkd6g9FH3LWtZpR6)\), on Friday evenings at 6:30 pm during the winter and 7:30 pm during the summer\.
-   **Ongoing Torah Classes**  
    Join Chabad for weekly Torah classes offered on and off campus, online and in person\. All relevant info about these offerings can be found on their [Instagram](http://instagram.com/chabadubc)\.
-   **Jewish Holidays**  
    If you’re wondering what to do for the Jewish High Holidays, Chanukah, Purim, Pesach \(Passover\) and all the other Jewish holidays in between, contact Rabbi Chalom for information on a full schedule of services, meals and more to help you celebrate\.
-   **One\-on\-one meetings**  
    Rabbi Chalom and Esti Loeub are both available to talk about anything over coffee\. Reach out to them to set up a time that works\.

## About Christian & Missionary Alliance \(C&MA\)[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/christian\-missionary\-alliance\-cma\-chaplain/\#about\-christian\-missionary\-alliance\-cma](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/christian-missionary-alliance-cma-chaplain/#about-christian-missionary-alliance-cma)

The Christian and Missionary Alliance \(the C&MA\) represents a group of approximately 440 local churches across Canada that aims to be Christ\-centred, Spirit\-empowered, and Mission\-focused in everything we do\.

There are two chaplains at UBC under the Christian and Missionary Alliance that you may be interested in joining:

-   Tenth Church, UBC
-   Athletes in Action Sports Chaplain

### Tenth Church\. UBC Pt Grey

We are a place where people of all different backgrounds can discover Christ, a community of spiritual transformation that seeks social justice for all\.

We are the 5th site for Tenth Church, a large multi\-ethnic community in Vancouver\. Our UBC Pt Grey site is made up of students, faculty, families, and neighbourhood residents\. The Canadian Broadcasting Corporation \(CBC\) has described Tenth as “a resting place for people from all walks of life\.”

Tenth UBC is a community gathering on campus and working to create a place of meaningful connection and relationship, we’d love to have you join us\.

### Athletes in Action Sports Chaplain

UBC student athletes are encouraged to engage with the Christian faith and integrate it with their life and sport\. The Athletes in Action sports chaplain fosters athletic fellowship among varsity athletes at UBC and SFU\.

## Site Pastors of Tenth UBC Pt Grey[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/christian\-missionary\-alliance\-cma\-chaplain/\#site\-pastors\-of\-tenth\-ubc\-pt\-grey](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/christian-missionary-alliance-cma-chaplain/#site-pastors-of-tenth-ubc-pt-grey)

Reverends Michele and Anthony Yackel are the Site Pastors for Tenth UBC Pt Grey\. Previously, they served as Co\-Lead Pastors of UrbanRoad, a faith community they started in 2010 in Langley\.

[Profile of Michele Yackel from CMA Chaplain](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/cma_chaplain_michele_yackel.jpg)

### Reverend Michele Yackel

Over the years, Michele has served as a youth pastor, a global worker in India teaching theology and music, and worked in various pastoral and leadership roles\. She has led and been a part of over 30 international mission endeavors, and served on various boards\. She has a Bachelor’s degree in Theology and Cross\-Cultural Communications, and hopes to finish her Master of Arts in the coming years\. She has been licensed and ordained with PAOC since 1996, and recently with C&MA\.

You can contact Michele by emailing [michele@tenth\.ca](mailto:michele@tenth.ca) or calling [604 817 5705](tel:604%20817%205705)\. 

[Profile of Anthony from CMA Chaplain](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/cma_chaplain_anthony.jpg)

### Reverend Anthony Yackel

Over the last twenty\-five years, Anthony has led people through vision, strategy, and communications, having served as a pastor, consultant, facilitator, and communications director in a number of different ministry environments and roles\. Anthony received his Master of Arts in Leadership and Innovation in 2017 from Kilns College in Bend, Oregon\. He is also a 2005 graduate of the Arrow Leadership Program\. He has been ordained and licensed since 1996, serving with both PAOC and C&MA\.

You can reach Anthony by emailing [anthony@tenth\.ca](mailto:anthony@tenth.ca) or calling [604 839 6987](tel:604%20839%206987)\.

Michele and Anthony have been married since 2002 and enjoy life with their 2 teens\. As a family, they enjoy travelling, sunshine, movies, laughter, and exploring the world of coffee\.

## Athletes in Action Sports Chaplain[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/christian\-missionary\-alliance\-cma\-chaplain/\#athletes\-in\-action\-sports\-chaplain](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/christian-missionary-alliance-cma-chaplain/#athletes-in-action-sports-chaplain)

[Profile of Rod Alm from CMA Chaplain](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/cma_chaplain_rod_alm.jpg)

### Rod Alm

Since earning a Bachelor of Science from the University of Saskatchewan, Rod Alm has devoted 46 years to Campus Ministry with his wife, Kathy—9 at UBC and 36 at the University of Saskatchewan and University of Regina\. In 2022, they returned to Vancouver to focus on a sports ministry of mentoring varsity athletes and coaches, the Athletes in Action Sports Chaplain\.

Rod is devoted to assisting varsity athletes in exploring and growing in their Christian faith, teaching them to integrate it into their sports, studies, and social lives\. Contact Rod at [roda@athletesinaction\.ca](mailto:roda@athletesinaction.ca)\.

## Services and events[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/christian\-missionary\-alliance\-cma\-chaplain/\#services\-and\-events](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/christian-missionary-alliance-cma-chaplain/#services-and-events)

### Tenth Church, UBC

-   **[In\-person service](https://www.tenth.ca/locations/ubc-pt-grey)**  
    Drop in to the Centre for Interactive Research on Sustainability \(CIRS\) on Sundays at 10:00 am\.
-   **[UBC Life Groups](http://www.tenth.ca/UBClife)**  
    Life Groups \(small groups\) meet at least twice a month in a welcoming environment and focus on spiritual growth and building relationships with each other\. 
-   **[If you’re new to Tenth UBC](https://www.tenth.ca/helloUBC)**  
    Get more information, or grab a coffee with Pastor Michele or Pastor Anthony\.
-   Find Tenth Church on their [website](http://www.tenth.ca/locations/ubc-pt-grey), through [Instagram](http://www.instagram.com/tenthubcptgrey), or on [Facebook](http://www.facebook.com/groups/tenthubcptgrey)\.

Email Rod at [roda@athletesinaction\.ca](mailto:roda@athletesinaction.ca) to request more information or sign up for the following:
