content_markdown:
## About Every Nation[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/every\-nation\-chaplain/\#about\-every\-nation](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/every-nation-chaplain/#about-every-nation)

Every Nation is a global family of churches that exist to honour God by establishing Christ\-centered, Spirit\-empowered, socially responsible churches and campus ministries in every nation\. It lands within the orthodox evangelical protestant faith tradition\. The foundational values are lordship, evangelism, discipleship, leadership, and family\.

## Every Nation Campus UBC[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/every\-nation\-chaplain/\#every\-nation\-campus\-ubc](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/every-nation-chaplain/#every-nation-campus-ubc)

Every Nation Campus \(ENC\) UBC is a church\-based campus ministry passionate about helping students grow in their relationships with God, one another, and the world\. They do this by meeting in large group settings to build a sense of community, and in small groups to pursue truth, love, and a deeper connection with God and each other, together\. As a group, they do their best to help students connect with their community on campus, get connected to a local church family, and create spaces where students can navigate the big questions of life from a Christian perspective, such as:

-   What is the meaning of life?
-   Does God exist?
-   Do all religions lead to God?
-   Why is there evil?
-   Is there life after death?

## About Tyler Mitchell[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/every\-nation\-chaplain/\#about\-tyler\-mitchell](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/every-nation-chaplain/#about-tyler-mitchell)

[Profile of Tyler Mitchell from Every Nation Chaplain](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/every_nation_chaplain_tyler_mitchell.png)

During his undergrad, Tyler came face to face with some big existential questions, such as who am I? Who is God? How can I be loved? What is my purpose? It was a critical time for his relationship  with God and Christian maturity\. It was during those years he decided to take his faith seriously and was discipled by older Christian mentors\. His university years were formative, which inspired him to create spaces for others to do the hard but fulfilling work of spiritual formation\. He considers it his greatest privilege to walk alongside students on their journeys of faith\.

As an Every Nation Chaplain, Tyler walks with students who are wanting to investigate existential and faith\-centered questions, eager to learn how to read the Bible contextually, and curious to discover what apprenticeship under the person of Jesus looks like\. 

Additionally, he is passionate about creating spaces for students to engage with each other as they pursue spiritual formation together\.

Born and raised in Vancouver, Tyler studied at Langara College and the University of British Columbia\. He now holds a Bachelor of Arts majoring in Psychology from UBC\. He is currently serving as a full\-time campus minister with Every Nation Campus and gratefully spends a majority of his time at UBC\.

You can contact Tyler by emailing [tyler\.mitchell@envan\.ca](mailto:tyler.mitchell@envan.ca)\.

## Services and events[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/every\-nation\-chaplain/\#services\-and\-events](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/every-nation-chaplain/#services-and-events)

-   **Campus hangouts**  
    Join the Every Nation Campus community in the Life Building to hang out, meet students, and play games together\. Regardless of where you’re at on your faith journey, this is a space to simply connect\. Come meet some lovely people\!
-   **Engage groups**  
    Our Engage groups are places for students to explore deeper questions of faith and life in a small group with other students\. We get to know each other as friends and build deeper relationships, and we open up the Bible together to see how it can help us know God and grow as loving people in all aspects of life\. Come get connected\!
-   **Monthly ENC events**  
    Join the Every Nation Campus community on the last Friday of each month for a special event\. These are spaces for students to gather to enjoy good times and build connections\. There’s often food, games or some fun activity, and always great people\. You don’t wanna miss it\! 
-   **Sunday Gathering with Every Nation Church Vancouver**  
    Every Nation Vancouver \(ENV\) rents their space from Langara College\. Visit Room A130 at 11 am for their weekly Sunday Service\.

## Find Every Nation online[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/every\-nation\-chaplain/\#find\-every\-nation\-online](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/every-nation-chaplain/#find-every-nation-online)

Connect with Every Nation through the [online directory](https://linktr.ee/ENC_Vancouver), which includes our Instagram, events, calendar, and more\.

## About Hillel BC[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/jewish\-chaplain/\#about\-hillel\-bc](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/jewish-chaplain/#about-hillel-bc)

Serving campuses across British Columbia, [Hillel BC](https://www.hillelbc.com/) promotes Jewish life on campus and beyond, providing a warm, welcoming environment where British Columbia students are able to grow religiously, culturally, socially, and ethically\. Whether it’s a monthly Shabbat dinner, our Jewish Learning Fellowship \(JLF\), our holiday programming, weekly kosher Hot Lunch, or Lunch and Learn, Hillel BC has something for everyone\.

## About the Jewish faith[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/jewish\-chaplain/\#about\-the\-jewish\-faith](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/jewish-chaplain/#about-the-jewish-faith)

Judaism is one of the oldest monotheistic religions in the world\. Much of its basis deals with engaging with the text of the Written Torah \(the Torah, Prophets and Writings\) and the Oral Torah, a rich tradition of laws, stories, and logic\. 

Another important aspect of Judaism is the “covenantal” relationship between God and the Children of Israel \(later to be known as Jews\) that is found in the Hebrew Bible\. Judaism believes that that “covenant” is still very much in effect today\.

As a religion, one of the most important aspects of Judaism is its theology that understands the Creator \(God\) as a single entity that has no human, animal, or physical aspects\. In a word, God within Judaism is “unseen” physically but manifests as a presence in numerous ways through interaction with people and the world\.

Although Judaism is for many, primarily a religion, it is also seen by many others as a culture, an ethnicity, and/or a peoplehood, in which elements of language \(Hebrew, Yiddish, Ladino, Aramaic, and others\), land \(Israel as the foundational land of Judaism as well as a modern State\), music, art, food, and literature also play a very important part\.

Judaism can be seen also as a way of life that includes philosophy, psychology, diet, and perhaps most importantly our behavior towards one another\.

### Birthright Israel

If you’re a Jewish young adult between the ages of 18 and 32, you have the opportunity to visit Israel on a free educational trip\. Check out [Birthright Israel](https://www.birthrightisrael.com/) for more details and to find out if you are eligible\.

She spent undergrad studying languages at Northern Michigan University where she was active in a small and mighty Soref Initiative Hillel\. Before attending Hebrew Union College \(HUC\), she lived in Chicago studying Talmud and Hebrew with Svara\.

She has served at Kodesh V’Hol in Holon, Israel; United Hebrew Congregation in Terre Haute, Indiana; Temple Sholom in Blue Ash, Ohio; B’ShERT in Brooklyn, New York; The New Jewish Home’s Sarah Neuman campus, and virtually at Central Reform Congregation in St\. Louis, Missouri\. She is excited to be out west and the new adventure in Vancouver, where free time will be spent doing jigsaw puzzles and going on new and exciting Pacific Northwest walks with her wife Cantor Shani Cohen\.

You can reach Rabbi Kylynn Cohen by emailing [kylynn@hillelbc\.com](mailto:kylynn@hillelbc.com) or calling [604 224 4748](tel:604%20224%204748)\.

content_markdown:
## About the Mennonite Brethren[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/mennonite\-brethren\-chaplain/\#about\-the\-mennonite\-brethren](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/mennonite-brethren-chaplain/#about-the-mennonite-brethren)

### We have a passion:

-   To pursue His heart
-   To serve this needy world
-   For His creation
-   For the lost, lonely, and hurting

As Christians, we believe in God as eternal Father, Son, and Holy Spirit\. We believe God created and sustains the universe and that He became human in Jesus Christ\. Jesus came to restore the world because humans rejected God in disobedience\. He died on the cross, making it possible for us to accept a renewed relationship with God\. Jesus rose from the dead, broke the power of sin and death and freed us to live in obedience to God’s will\. We believe that God the Holy Spirit invites all people to be reconciled with God and to join the global family of faith\.

“As Christians, we are called to turn:  
from ignorance of God to a personal relationship with God\.  
from the bondage of sin and past mistakes to freedom, forgiveness, and healing\.  
from individualism to interdependence with others in fellowship\.  
from lifestyle choices that harm us, others, and the earth to choices that nurture wholeness,  
healing, and joy\.”  
  
International Community of [Mennonite Brethren](https://www.mennonitebrethren.ca/directory/partners/international-community-of-mennonite-brethren-icomb-confession-of-faith/) \(ICOMB\) Confession of Faith

## Meet the chaplains[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/mennonite\-brethren\-chaplain/\#meet\-the\-chaplains](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/mennonite-brethren-chaplain/#meet-the-chaplains)

[Michael and Amy Weidman](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/mennonite_chaplain_michael_amy_weidman.jpeg)

Michael and Amy are Power to Change Staff doing international student ministry with Bridges International \(p2c\) at the University of British Columbia\. We attend [Westside Church](https://www.wchurch.ca/) \(Mennonite Brethren\) in Downtown Vancouver\. We look forward to meeting you\! We welcome you to join our International student communities on campus: Bridges International Fellowship and Bridges Mandarin Fellowship\. We also have lunch bible studies and one\-on\-one meetups over coffee or tea\. Michael and Amy speak Mandarin, German, Minnan \(Taiwanese\), and French\.

### Amy Weidman

Amy is a minister and life coach\. Her passion is to mentor people to become the best version of themselves\. Her vision is to enable and empower disciples to become disciple\-makers, mentoring other people at their workplace and communities\. Amy received her Master of Arts in History of Christian Thought from Trinity Evangelical Divinity School\. She has teaching credentials in History and Mandarin from the state of California\. She taught in a public high school in California\. Amy loves music, reading, writing, photography, hiking, and swimming\.  
   
You can contact Amy by emailing [Amy\.weidman@p2c\.com](mailto:Amy.weidman@p2c.com) or by calling her at [604 445 1687](tel:604%20445%201687)\.

### Michael Weidman

A graduate of Spring Arbor University, Michael worked with Youth for Christ\. Then he pursued a Master of Divinity degree in Biblical Theology at Trinity Evangelical Divinity School in Deerfield, Illinois, and a Master of Linguistics at the University of Illinois\. After graduate studies, Michael became Lecturer at Fu Jen University in Taiwan and studied Chinese\.  He continued his study of Chinese in the Stanford Inter\-University Program\.   
   
In Taiwan, Michael met his wife, Amy, who was a full\-time minister with Campus Evangelical Fellowship \(InterVarsity\)\. They subsequently returned to the States to pursue further theological studies\. Michael received his Master of Theology in Systematic Theology\. They joined the Overseas Missionary Fellowship \(founded by Hudson Taylor\) in 1993 and ministered to students and scholars in Germany\. They lived in two cities, Munich \(“Go Bayern\!”\) and Heidelberg\. In the year 2000, Michael did research at the University of Cambridge in Ethics\. In 2002, he became Pastor of English Ministries in Southern California\. Michael received his Doctor of Ministry from the Talbot School of Theology \(Biola\) in 2012\.   
   
Michael loves languages, fluent in Chinese \(Mandarin\) and German and reads French, Greek, Hebrew and Latin\. He also loves mountain biking, tennis, hiking, skiing, philosophical and theological reading and classical music\.  
   
You can contact Michael by emailing [Michael\.weidman@p2c\.com](mailto:Michael.weidman@p2c.com), or by calling him at [604 441 5467](tel:604%20441%205467)\.

## About Islam[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/muslim\-association\-chaplain/\#about\-islam](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/muslim-association-chaplain/#about-islam)

Commonly, Islam refers to the monotheistic religion revealed to Muhammad ibn Abdullah between 610 and 632 AD\. Much of a word in Arabic can be deduced from its linguistic meaning\. The term Islam is derived from the three\-letter Arabic root, S \(س\), L \(ل\), M \(م\), which generates words with meanings, including “submission”, “commitment,” “peace”\. So an adherent to Islam, or a Muslim, achieves peace with one’s self through wholly submitting to God and accepting His guidance\.

A Muslim believes in the existence of God, His angels, His scriptures, His messengers, the Day of Judgement and Predestination\.

Prophet Muhammad mentioned the best summary of the core of Islam:

“Islam means that you should bear witness that there is no god but Allah \(The One God\) and that Muhammad is God’s final messenger, that you should perform the ritual prayer, pay the annual charitable donation, fast during the month of Ramadan, and make the pilgrimage to the Ka’bah if you are able to go there\.”

The term Islam was instituted by the Qur’an, the sacred scripture revealed to Muhammad, the Last and Final Prophet\. However, for Muslims, Islam is not a new religion\. Rather, it represents the final and comprehensive explanation of God’s Oneness, a theme found in earlier monotheistic religious traditions\.

### Beyond the faith

Although Islam can be described as a religion, it is viewed by its adherents, which make up a fifth of the world’s population, in much broader terms\. Beyond belief in specific doctrines and performance of important ritual acts, Islam is practiced as a complete and natural way of life, designed to bring God into the center of one’s consciousness and life\. In essence, Islam is a world view centered around belief in the One God and commitment to His commandments\.

## About Shaheer Muhammad[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/muslim\-association\-chaplain/\#about\-shaheer\-muhammad](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/muslim-association-chaplain/#about-shaheer-muhammad)

[Profile of Shaheer Muhammad from Muslim Chaplain](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/muslim_chaplain_shaheer_muhammad.jpg)

Shaheer Muhammad, the Muslim Students’ Association Chaplain, is a long\-time UBC resident and the owner of Willowbrook Pharmacy\. His interest in combining health care and entrepreneurship has led him to pursue the Doctor of Pharmacy Degree from UBC\. He previously obtained his Bachelor of Science Degree and Master of Business Administration from UBC and Thompson Rivers University\.

Shaheer believes that success in life is an outcome achieved through faith\-centred service\. He has participated in community building and youth empowerment through his role with the Canadian Muslim Chaplaincy organization\. He has organized numerous community events, established mentorship programs and shared Islamic Knowledge for over ten years\.

Shaheer has been a long\-time executive member of the Muslim Students’ Association \(MSA\) throughout his university life and has served as MSA president at both UBC and Thompson Rivers University\. He is currently a board member of the White Rock Muslim Association\.

In his spare time, Shaheer enjoys looking for pristine bodies of water for boating and underrated eateries to review\. He hopes to publicize a travel vlog channel and fulfill his dream of running a cafe\.

If you would like to speak to Shaheer about an academic, personal or faith\-related matter, you are more than welcome to email him at [shaheer\.mu@gmail\.com](mailto:shaheer.mu@gmail.com) or find him on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/shaheer.chaplain/)\.

## About the Pentecostal Church[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/pentecostal\-chaplain/\#about\-the\-pentecostal\-church](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/pentecostal-chaplain/#about-the-pentecostal-church)

The Pentecostal Church is found within the mainstream of orthodox evangelical protestant faith\. As a movement, the church is just over 100 years old\. While Pentecostals emphasize the physical expression of God’s inner dwelling through spiritual and supernatural gifts, we are also known for our ministry to the fringes of society, cultural diversity, and passion for talking about God to others\.

### University Christian Ministries at UBC

At UBC, the Pentecostal ministry is made up of more than just Pentecostals\. Virtually every Christian denomination has been represented in our community at one time or another\. Through the Pentecostal Chaplaincy, we sponsor an interdenominational Christian student group on campus\. We are a community who desires to walk alongside students through the contours of university life, and we hope to be a place where students can discover what it means to integrate what you learn in the classroom with the Christian faith\.  
   
[University Christian Ministries](http://www.ucmatubc.com/) \(UCM\) at UBC is a student community passionate about Christ, excited about His transforming power at work in our lives, and open to God’s life\-changing presence through the Holy Spirit\.

## About Paul Engels[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/pentecostal\-chaplain/\#about\-paul\-engels](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/pentecostal-chaplain/#about-paul-engels)

[Image of Paul Engels from the Pentecostal chaplain](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/pentecostal_chaplain_paul_engels.jpg)

Paul’s life was transformed after he was in a car accident and experienced a severe traumatic brain injury when he was 18 years old\. This left him comatose for a month and a half\. His miraculous healing came through his reception of God, so now Paul lives to share the same life\-giving power of love with others\. Paul serves as campus director University Christian Ministries at UBC, by regularly providing spiritual care for students, multiplying groups which seek to grow in faith, and mobilizing missional initiatives to create peace and reconciliation on campus\.

You can contact Paul by emailing him at [paul\.engels@paoc\.org](mailto:paul.engels@paoc.org), or by texting him at [604 679 3520](tel:604%20679%203520)\.

## About the Presbyterian Church[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/presbyterian\-chaplain/\#about\-the\-presbyterian\-church](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/presbyterian-chaplain/#about-the-presbyterian-church)

People of diverse cultural backgrounds and languages comprise over 1000 Presbyterian congregations across Canada\. We seek to be in loving relationships with God, others, ourselves and creation\. Together, we strive to reflect the inclusive love of Jesus by embracing people of all backgrounds – regardless of age, gender, race or ability\. We believe each person is a unique sacred creation, cherished by God, and invited to participate fully in the communities of those who follow Christ Jesus\. The Bible guides our shared journey, but we do not require members to follow a fixed set of doctrines, but respect those willing to seek, question, and grow\. We honour the spiritual paths of others and trust that God’s Spirit moves not just in our midst, but in many voices, many places, and many prayers\.

Presbyterians share many beliefs with others in Christian denominations\. Learn more about [The Presbyterian Church in Canada](https://presbyterian.ca/) on the denomination’s website\.

### St\. Andrew’s Hall at UBC

Life is precious and the road of life is often complicated and messy, with many voices vying for attention and many difficult choices to make\. At [St\. Andrew’s Hall](https://www.standrews.edu/), the Presbyterian College on the UBC campus, we desire to create a safe space for you during your time at UBC\. We support you in voicing your thoughts, testing out what you believe, growing in faith, strengthening friendships, practicing love of neighbour, and journeying together with those who seek to follow the way of Jesus in everyday life\. Everyone, regardless of background, is invited to attend our events\.

## About Sumarme Goble[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/presbyterian\-chaplain/\#about\-sumarme\-goble](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/presbyterian-chaplain/#about-sumarme-goble)

[Headshot of Chaplain Sumarme Goble](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/6_sumarme-goble_edited_hayley.jpg)

The Reverend Sumarme serves as Chaplain and Community Life Director at St\. Andrew’s Hall\. She holds degrees in Christian Education \(BA, Seattle Pacific University\), English Language Learning \(Seattle University\), and a Master of Divinity \(Fuller Theological Seminary\)\. Her past work includes service in Ban Vinai refugee camp in Thailand and pastoral roles in two Seattle congregations\.

Initially focused on achievement and perfection as identity markers throughout her university years, Sumarme’s journey through failure taught her resilience and that we are human beings not “human doings\.” She benefited from mentors who prioritized nonjudgmental and attentive listening while helping her address the big questions of life and grow through life’s challenges\. She wants to come alongside students in similar ways as they form their identities\.  

As chaplain, she cares for students holistically – encouraging spiritual growth, vocational purpose, and compassion\. She guides them in integrating faith, learning, and service, and invites them into communities shaped by love, peace, and gospel\-centered hope\.

## Services and events[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/presbyterian\-chaplain/\#services\-and\-events](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/presbyterian-chaplain/#services-and-events)

Attend community worship at [St\. Andrew’s Hall](https://www.standrews.edu/) in the Community Center \(view [Google map](https://goo.gl/maps/Hh19BVaogzFGXWsT9)\) from 12:00 pm to 1:00 pm on Tuesdays during the UBC Winter Session\. For more information and a current listing of programs and events, email [sgoble@standrews\.edu](mailto:sgoble@standrews.edu)\.

## About the Roman Catholic faith tradition[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/roman\-catholic\-chaplain/\#about\-the\-roman\-catholic\-faith\-tradition](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/roman-catholic-chaplain/#about-the-roman-catholic-faith-tradition)

The faith life of the Catholic community on campus is diverse in character and expression\. Including students, staff and faculty of the UBC community we are both local and international\. Our activities seek to support the spiritual life of the university community with a commitment to the dialogue between faith and reason and the promotion of a faith that seeks harmony and justice\. 

The Roman Catholic core religious beliefs are summarized in creeds\. The following is the Apostles Creed:

*We believe in God, the Father Almighty,  
Creator of heaven and earth,  
And in Jesus Christ, his only Son, our Lord,  
Who was conceived by the Holy Spirit, born  
Of the Virgin Mary, Suffered under Pontius Pilate, was crucified,  
Died and was buried;  
He descended to the dead; on the third day he  
Rose again; He ascended into heaven, and is seated at  
The right hand of God the Father almighty;  
From there he will come to judge the living  
And the dead\.  
We believe in the Holy Spirit,  
The holy catholic church,  
The communion of saints,  
The forgiveness of sins,  
The resurrection of the body,  
And life everlasting\. Amen\.*

See the Nicene Creed for a more expansive version\.

### Roman Catholic community on campus

Catholic chaplaincy activities at UBC include weekday and Sunday liturgies, sacramental preparation and faith study programs for Catholics and for those interested in knowing more about the life of the Church\. Ongoing activities include spiritual formation and retreats in the Ignatian tradition, Bible study, and Science and Faith discussion groups\. Those interested in knowing more about the Catholic Church may wish to consider the Rite of Christian Initiation for Adults \(RCIA\) program\. For information on ongoing programs we encourage you to visit St\. Mark’s chapel and to follow events on our websites\. 

In addition to UBC Catholic Chaplaincy activities, the Catholic colleges of Corpus Christi and St\. Mark’s provide additional, welcoming spaces of learning and celebration\.  

Come and experience different forms of prayer and worship that will deepen your understanding of how God’s love and grace are at work in your life\.

## Meet Father Robert Allore S\.J\.[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/roman\-catholic\-chaplain/\#meet\-father\-robert\-allore\-s\-j](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/roman-catholic-chaplain/#meet-father-robert-allore-s-j)

[Image of Robert Allore from Catholic Chaplain](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/catholic_chaplian_robert_allore.jpg)

Trained initially in the life sciences, Robert is a member of the Society of Jesus \(Jesuits\) and, since 2012, the pastor of St\. Marks and the chaplain at UBC\. Blessed by a university community of talented and faith\-filled students, staff and faculty, the Catholic community at UBC provides a place to grow in faith, wisdom and service\. Inspired by the life of the Spirit in our faith community, it is his hope that the university chaplaincy will be a place of welcome where question and challenge, faith, reason and service are nurtured as graces for the journey\.  

You can contact Fr\. Robert Allore S\.J\. by emailing [parish\.smark@rcav\.org](mailto:parish.smark@rcav.org) or calling [604 822 0261](tel:604%20822%200261)\.

## About Sikhs on campus at UBC[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/sikh\-chaplain/\#about\-sikhs\-on\-campus\-at\-ubc](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/sikh-chaplain/#about-sikhs-on-campus-at-ubc)

Sikhs On Campus at UBC is a collective of community volunteers with the goal to help students become confident as mature and proud Sikhs\. As like\-minded friends, we support Sikh students and their families with a home away from home\. All students, regardless of where they may be on their Sikh journey, are invited to join our extended family as we celebrate our faith, community, culture, and commonly\-held values\. We are all one\.  
   
At Sikhs on Campus, Sikh students and families know they can reach out for help and guidance\. With the generous backing of local Sikhs, we help with tasks as simple as answering questions for first\-time students, introducing students to a network of local families, and sponsoring various faith\-centric activities\.  
   
Join us in the practice of selfless community service \(Seva\) as we feed the homeless in Vancouver alongside an award\-winning and long\-standing local Sikh charity, Guru Nanak’s Free Kitchen\. Come along with us to celebrate the colours, flavours, and proud history of Baisakhi with 500,000 local Sikhs at the world’s largest Nagar Kirtan outside India\. Sikhs on Campus is a place where being part of the Sikh community is fun\.

## About the Sikh faith[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/sikh\-chaplain/\#about\-the\-sikh\-faith](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/sikh-chaplain/#about-the-sikh-faith)

In the true Sikh spirit of inclusiveness, everyone is welcome and nobody is ever turned away from Sangat \(fellowship\)\. Through Seva and a faith\-based celebration of Chardi\-Kala \(eternal optimism and joy\), Sikhs on Campus fosters a spirit of peace \(Sukhmani\) and joy \(Anand\)\. We always share the principles and teachings of Sikhism with anyone who wishes to learn\. Of course, in accordance with Sikh ideals, we never push religious conversion\.  
   
The word Sikh means ‘one who learns’ \(a disciple or student\)\. Sikhs are on a spiritual journey to learn about, master, and adopt a set of universal values\.

-   Equality \(Ekta, no discrimination of gender and religion\)
-   Charity \(Seva, community service\)
-   Protection and Empathy \(Daya, understand and help the vulnerable\)
-   Truth \(Sat, see the world as it is and speak to it truthfully\)
-   Contentment; \(Santokh, free the mind from fear and worry by accepting reality for what it is\)
-   Humility \(Nimrata, know that you are not superior or above others\)
-   Love \(Pyar, love all of God’s creation unconditionally and see goodness in all\)

### Our philosophy

Sikhs believe that all creation is attributed to a single, universal, shapeless, timeless, and genderless Creator referred to as ‘WaheGuru’\.

**Wa** \(or Va\): Wonder in the divine light\.

**Guru**: Spiritual darkness \(Gu\) is illuminated \(Ru\)\.

Sikhs view humanity as one, with no single religion claiming superiority over another\. Various religious beliefs are separate pathways leading all believers to the same Creator\. This belief of the one\-and\-only Creator is referred to as ‘Ik\-Onkar’\.

**Ik**: One and only one

**Oang**: Creator

**Kar**: Creation

## About the Sikh Chaplain[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/sikh\-chaplain/\#about\-the\-sikh\-chaplain](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/sikh-chaplain/#about-the-sikh-chaplain)

[Profile of Inderjeet Singh from Sikh Chaplain](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/sikh_chaplain_inderjeet_singh.jpg)

Mr\. Inderjeet Singh \(Indy\), a proud father of two, has devoted more than 35 years to building and driving education, community support, and faith\-centric programs for Sikh youth in North America and Asia\. His passion is to connect the divide between today’s youth interests and traditionally\-inspired spiritual practices\. 

Mr\. Singh blends modern\-western with conventional\-eastern pedagogic methods to create a holistic, relevant, and engaging experience for students\. Through this approach, he has coordinated Sikh youth camps which run in Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, the United States, and Canada since the early 1990’s\.

For the past 10 years, Mr\. Singh has been developing and conducting his latest programs for 200 youth in New Westminster, BC \(Sukh Sagar Gurdwara\)\. He coaches and mentors youth volunteers, educating and empowering them to run camps, classes, and events focused on religious philosophy, citizenship, culture, and social and communications skills\.

Mr\. Singh also serves as a volunteer coordinator for Guru Nanak’s Free Kitchen, an award\-winning program to feed the homeless in Vancouver’s Eastside, serving nearly 50,000 meals per year to the less fortunate\.

MADD Canada \(Vancouver chapter\), appointed Mr\. Singh to their Board in 2022 to serve as their South\-Asian Liaison, and to help bring awareness of the dangers of impaired driving\.

Mr\. Singh holds a Master of Education degree and Bachelor of Arts in Communication from Bowling Green University \(BGSU – Ohio, USA\), where he advised student groups on good governance and ethics while supervising 16 graduate House Directors as Area Coordinator for Greek Affairs in the Office of Residence Life\. For over 15 years, Mr\. Singh has worked as a Senior Instructor, Corporate Trainer and Coach, and Marketing Manager in Canada and Malaysia\.

Mr\. Singh is a practicing Sikh and community advocate, fluent in written and spoken English, Punjabi, Hindi, and Bahasa Malaysia and Bahasa Indonesia\.

You can contact Mr\. Singh by emailing [chaplain@sikhsoncampus\.com](mailto:chaplain@sikhsoncampus.com), or by calling him at [604 723 8850](tel:604%20723%208850)\.

## Services and events[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/sikh\-chaplain/\#services\-and\-events](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/sikh-chaplain/#services-and-events)

Visit [Sikhs on Campus](http://sikhsoncampus.com/) to connect with the Sikh community at UBC and learn about upcoming events\.

title: UBC Thaqalayn Muslim Association
content_markdown:
## About the Islamic faith[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/ubc\-thaqalayn\-muslim\-association/\#about\-the\-islamic\-faith](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/ubc-thaqalayn-muslim-association/#about-the-islamic-faith)

The word “Islam” is an Arabic word that means “submission to the will of God”\. To be called a Muslim, one has to affirm that God \(Allah\) who is the Creator of all, is the only one worthy of worship, that Muhammad is a last prophet of God, and that the Holy book \(the Qur’an\) is revealed on the Prophet Muhammad\(sa\) and has been shared through both oral recitation and as a written book\. One also has to believe in the Day of Judgment and the four pillars of Islam which include five daily prayers, a certain amount of obligatory charity \(zakat\), fasting once in a year in the month of Ramadan \(siyam\), and performing a ritual journey to the house of God in Makkah \(hajj\)\.  
   
Islam emphasizes three dimensions, which are jurisprudential, moral and intellectual\. The basic message of Islam is to spread love, peace and harmony in human society\. Spiritual and moral development of the human being, purification of the soul and tranquility of the heart are important aspects and the ultimate objectives of Islam\.

### Our philosophy

The universal message of the Qur’an is that religion cannot be imposed on anyone\. Human beings are like family members as all are sons and daughters of Adam \(as\) and Eve\. If someone kills an innocent person, it is like they have killed all of mankind\. If someone saves a life, it is like they have saved all of mankind\. It is believed that all good and bad deeds will be manifested in the Day of Judgment in their true face\. Those who do good will be rewarded and those who commit evil will be punished\.  
   
Followers of all religions should gather on a single focal point which is oneness of God, and focus on their commonalities\. No one is allowed to use abusive language to the beliefs of the followers of other faiths\.

## About Dr\. Syed Nasir Zaidi[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/ubc\-thaqalayn\-muslim\-association/\#about\-dr\-syed\-nasir\-zaidi](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/ubc-thaqalayn-muslim-association/#about-dr-syed-nasir-zaidi)

[Profile of Syed Zaidi from Muslim Chaplain](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/muslim_chaplain_syed_zaidi.jpg)

Dr\. Zaidi is also a Spiritual Care Practitioner and Muslim Chaplain at Vancouver General Hospital \(VGH\)\. Dr\. Zaidi believes that Islam, in its true spirit, has strong universal messages for all religious and spiritual communities\. He aims to promote the true picture of Islam by highlighting its moral, ethical and spiritual aspects by connecting students to the spiritual wellbeing of the UBC community\. He hopes to make evident the effectiveness of Islam’s ethical and spiritual principles, and the promotion of interfaith harmony\.  
   
Dr\. Zaidi understands that university life can cause spiritual complications for students as they face several intellectual, spiritual and psychological problems in their individual, social and academic lives\. He is a proponent of one\-on\-one or group counselling based on students’ spiritual and religious traditions\. Like all students, Muslim students have theological and philosophical questionsrelating to their social and academic environment\. 

Dr\. Zaidi would like to address these critical questions on a philosophical, psychological and theological basis\. It is also important for him to demonstrate the capability of Islamic spirituality in enriching other faiths and religious traditions\.

Dr\. Zaidi holds a PhD and Masters in Islamic Philosophy and Theology from the University of Tehran in Iran, as well as a Masters in Arabic from the University of Punjab in Pakistan\. All of these achievements are evaluated and approved by ICES, Canada\.  
   
Prior to his current role as Research Scholar and Spiritual Consultant at the [Az\-Zahraa Islamic Centre](https://az-zahraa.org/), Dr\. Zaidi acted as the former Director General \(Research\) of the Counsel of Islamic Ideology at Islamabad Pakistan from 2007 to 2010\. He was also a Visiting Professor at University of Bonn in Germany from 2006 to 2007, and an Assistant Professor at the International Islamic University in Islamabad, Pakistan from 2003 to 2005\.  
   
You can contact Dr\. Zaidi by emailing [dr\.nasirzaidi@gmail\.com](mailto:dr.nasirzaidi@gmail.com), or by calling him at [604 369 3571](tel:604%20369%203571)\. You can also learn more on his website at [www\.drnasirzaidi\.com](http://www.drnasirzaidi.com/)\.

## Services and events[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/ubc\-thaqalayn\-muslim\-association/\#services\-and\-events](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/ubc-thaqalayn-muslim-association/#services-and-events)

-   [UBC Thaqalayn Muslim Association](https://tmaubc.wixsite.com/tmaubc)  
    Join the UBC Thaqalayn Muslim Association on Mondays, Fridays and weekends\. Spiritual counselling is also provided on Mondays and Fridays\. 
-   [Thursday night program](https://az-zahraa.org/)  
    Join the Az\-Zahraa Islamic Centre’s \(view [Google map](https://goo.gl/maps/mTk3NHW2e33uxYjCA)\) night program on the last Thursday of every month\. You can also call [604 274 7869](tel:604%20274%207869) for more information\.
-   **[Fatimia Community Services Society of BC](https://www.fatimia.org/)**  
    Join Fatimia Community Services Society of BC to listen to lectures from Dr\. Zaidi on the first three Thursday nights of every month\.
-   [Sunday morning program](https://az-zahraa.org/)  
    Join the Az\-Zahraa Islamic Centre every Sunday morning\. You can also call [604 274 7869](tel:604%20274%207869) for more information\.

title: United Church of Canada Chaplain
content_markdown:
## About The United Church of Canada[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/united\-church\-canada\-chaplain/\#about\-the\-united\-church\-of\-canada](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/united-church-canada-chaplain/#about-the-united-church-of-canada)

The United Church of Canada is the largest Protestant Christian denomination in Canada\. We minister close to 3 million people in over 3500 congregations across the country\. The United Church was formed in 1925 as a union of Methodists, Presbyterians and Congregationalist Christians\. We continue to enjoy a diversity of faith expressions while communing as a single body\.  
   
The United Church strives to be open and welcoming as Jesus was, regardless of age, race, class, gender, or physical ability\. We view each person as a unique, loved creation of God and welcome all people to the full life of the Christian community\. The Bible is the shared standard for our faith, but members are not required to adhere to a particular creed or formulation of doctrine\. The United Church views the religious practices of all people of goodwill with respect and gratitude\. We believe the Spirit of God is at work in many different faith communities\.

## About Aaron Miller[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/united\-church\-canada\-chaplain/\#about\-aaron\-miller](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/united-church-canada-chaplain/#about-aaron-miller)

[Profile of Aaron Miller from United Chaplain](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/united_church_chaplain_aaron_miller.jpg)

Aaron Miller is an ordained minister in the United Church of Canada, and the Campus Minister for the [Pacific Mountain Regional Council](https://pacificmountain.ca/)\. He has been serving in full\-time ministry since 2009 in Ontario and at UBC with [University Hill \(U Hill\)](https://www.uhill.net/) Congregation\. Aaron completed his undergraduate degree at Brock University in English Language and Literature\. He received his Masters of Divinity from Emmanuel College in Toronto\.

For more information about [Campus United](https://campusunited.ca/) at UBC, you can [find us on Instagram](http://www.instagram.com/campusunited.ubc)\.

You can also contact Aaron by emailing [aaronmiller@united\-church\.ca](mailto:aaronmiller@united-church.ca) or calling and texting [604 779 8720](tel:604%20779%208720)\. His office is located in room 127 at the [Vancouver School of Theology](https://www.maps.ubc.ca/?code=VST)\.

title: Zen Buddhist Chaplain

## About Zen Buddhism[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/zen\-buddhist\-chaplain/\#about\-zen\-buddhism](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/zen-buddhist-chaplain/#about-zen-buddhism)

Zen practice contributes to the world by bringing harmony, compassion and ethical integrity into the lives of individuals and communities\. Zen transforms how we live with one another and on the earth we share\. In a university setting, Zen meditation can help students concentrate on their work and study, cope with the pressures of campus life, and better relate to the diversity of people they encounter daily\.  
   
Zen develops our potential as human beings by cultivating our innate wisdom\. This is realized and actualized in meditation practice, and extends into everyday life\. Zen emphasizes self\-realization, which is realization of the true self, through a simple but concentrated practice of contemplation and actualization\. Zen practice builds confidence in the self that is ever\-changing and inherently interconnected to the world we live in\.  
   
Learn more about [Buddhism and Zen](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/zen_buddhism_learn_more.pdf) \(pdf\)\.

## About Gareth Sirotnik[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/zen\-buddhist\-chaplain/\#about\-gareth\-sirotnik](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/zen-buddhist-chaplain/#about-gareth-sirotnik)

[Profile of Gareth Sirotnik from Zen Chaplain](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/zen_buddhist_chaplain_gareth_sirotnik.jpg)

Gareth holds a Bachelor of Arts in History from Reed College in Portland, Oregon\. He has been a writer and communication consultant based in Vancouver since 1972\. Gareth is also a long\-time practitioner and formerly an ordained monk at the Zen Centre of Vancouver\. For Gareth, hearing UBC students say that Zen meditation practice helps them reduce stress, focus better, and find a stronger core of being in a responsive relationship to the world and people around them, makes this the most satisfying work he has ever done\.  
   
You can contact Gareth by emailing [gareth\.ubczen@gmail\.com](mailto:gareth.ubczen@gmail.com)\.

## Services and events[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/chaplains/zen\-buddhist\-chaplain/\#services\-and\-events](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/chaplains/zen-buddhist-chaplain/#services-and-events)

Drop in to Zen Meditation in the [UBC Life Building](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/ubc-life-building/) twice a week, except for statutory holidays:

-   Mondays in Room 2109 from 5:00 pm to 6:00 pm
-   Thursdays in Room 2109 from 5:00 pm to 6:00 pm

If you are joining for the first time, please arrive 15 minutes early for a brief introduction\. To connect to the session via Zoom, [email Gareth](mailto:gareth.ubczen@gmail.com) for the meeting information\.

Gareth is also available by appointment for one\-on\-one spiritual guidance one hour before or one hour after the Zen Meditation time\. [Email Gareth](mailto:gareth.ubczen@gmail.com) for an appointment\.

title: Child care and school registration
content_markdown:
Browse on\-campus or community resources and services for child care\. The British Columbia government also offers [provincial resources and tips](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/family-social-supports/caring-for-young-children) on finding child care\.

If you’re an international student, please familiarize yourself with the Canadian laws about the [rights and responsibilities of parents](https://family.legalaid.bc.ca/children/parenting-guardianship/guardianship/guardianship-parenting-time-and-parental) in British Columbia\. They may be different from those in your home country\.

An [immunization record](https://www.healthlinkbc.ca/health-library/immunizations/information-and-safety/records) is usually requested when your child is registered to enter daycare, preschool, kindergarten, school and certain programs in post\-secondary institutions\. 

## Child care resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/equity\-diversity\-inclusion\-resources/resources\-who\-are\-parents/child\-care\-school\-registration/\#child\-care\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/resources-who-are-parents/child-care-school-registration/#child-care-resources)

### On\-campus child care

[UBC Child Care](http://www.childcare.ubc.ca/)

Join the waitlist for licensed child care for infants through elementary school age children\. Apply early as spaces are limited\.

[Berwick Child Development Centre](http://www.develop.bc.ca/for-families/children-and-youth/)

Find licensed child care spaces for children ages 3 to 5, including those with special needs\. Children of UBC Students receive priority placements\.

### Off\-campus child care

The following services can provide guidance and referrals to off\-campus child care facilities:

-   [Westcoast Child Care Resource Centre](http://www.wstcoast.org/)
-   [Immigrant Support Services of BC](https://issbc.org/about-us)
-   [SUCCESS](http://www.successbc.ca/)
-   [Pacific Immigrant Resources Society](http://pirs.bc.ca/about-us/)

### Financial support for child care

[$10 a Day ChildCareBC Centres](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/family-social-supports/caring-for-young-children/childcarebc-programs/10-a-day-childcarebc-centres)

Learn more about province\-run affordable child care options near you\.

[Affordable Child Care Benefit](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/family-social-supports/caring-for-young-children/childcarebc-programs/child-care-benefit)

Apply for a monthly payment to help you with the cost of child care\.

[UBC scholarships and bursaries](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/)

Browse awards and funding opportunities available to eligible students\.

## About the British Columbia school system[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/equity\-diversity\-inclusion\-resources/resources\-who\-are\-parents/child\-care\-school\-registration/\#about\-the\-british\-columbia\-school\-system](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/resources-who-are-parents/child-care-school-registration/#about-the-british-columbia-school-system)

In Canada, the school year runs from September to June\. There is typically a two\-week break in December and a two\-week break in March for elementary and secondary schools\. Children can start kindergarten at age 4\.

The [Vancouver School Board](http://www.vsb.bc.ca/) operates the public elementary and secondary schools in Vancouver\. Suburbs of Vancouver have their own school boards\.

### International student information

If your study permit is valid for at least one year, and you are enrolled at a publicly funded institution such as UBC, your minor children aged 18 years or younger are eligible to attend elementary and secondary school as if they were Canadian residents\. They will not be required to pay international student fees\. 

### English classes for children

Many schools offer ESL classes for their students as part of the regular curriculum\.

For information about these programs, contact the [Immigrant Services Society of BC](http://www.issbc.org/) by phone at [604 684 2561](tel:6046842561) or through email at [iss@issbc\.org](mailto:iss@issbc.org)\.

## Registering your children in school[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/equity\-diversity\-inclusion\-resources/resources\-who\-are\-parents/child\-care\-school\-registration/\#registering\-your\-children\-in\-school](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/resources-who-are-parents/child-care-school-registration/#registering-your-children-in-school)

You should enroll your children in school as soon as you’ve accepted your offer to study at UBC\. If you’ll be living on\-campus or in Vancouver, visit the Vancouver School Board’s [Newcomer Welcome Centre](https://www.vsb.bc.ca/nwc) online for more information\.

### **For children born outside of Canada**

If you meet all of the following requirements, please review the [Vancouver School Board resources](https://www.vsb.bc.ca/nwc/page/11332/registration) to register your child for school:

-   Your child was born outside of Canada
-   Your primary language at home is not English
-   You and your child are currently living in Vancouver and have a confirmed address in Vancouver

### **For children born in Canada**

If your child was born in Canada and English is their first language, please [register online](https://vsbapplynow.vsb.bc.ca/) with the Vancouver School Board\.

title: Responding to discrimination
content_markdown:
UBC is committed to providing a safe, supportive, and inclusive living and learning environment, with resources and services to support all students\.

## About discrimination[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/equity\-diversity\-inclusion\-resources/responding\-discrimination/\#about\-discrimination](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/responding-discrimination/#about-discrimination)

Discrimination is treatment that burdens or disadvantages someone with no reasonable justification, where these disadvantages are related to one’s race, colour, place of origin, ancestry, sexual orientation, gender identity or gender expression, mental disability, physical disability, sex, age, religion, family status, and marital status\. Discrimination involves unfair or different treatment for reasons unrelated to academic or employment performance\. 

Discrimination can be a comment or behaviour that is unwelcome or that has a negative impact on the person whether the person intended it or not\. Harassment can be either a single, serious incident or a pattern of related, repeated incidents\.

Examples of discrimination include:

-   Racist, sexist, or homophobic jokes or remarks
-   Repeated advances from someone after you have indicated a lack of interest \(verbally, by email, texting or through other forms of social media\)
-   Being mocked for your accent, culture, or religion
-   Consistently being misgendered or intentionally referred to with the wrong pronouns
-   Not being allowed to reschedule an exam when the exam date conflicts with your religious or spiritual observance
-   Being denied the appropriate accommodations if you have a disability
-   Receiving a negative evaluation because the instructor disapproves of your sexual orientation or cultural perspective

## If you experience discrimination[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/equity\-diversity\-inclusion\-resources/responding\-discrimination/\#if\-you\-experience\-discrimination](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/responding-discrimination/#if-you-experience-discrimination)

### First, understand you do not deserve what is happening

Harassment is unlikely to stop or go away if you ignore it\. In fact, harassing behaviour may increase if the harasser feels that they can get away with it\. It takes courage to address what is happening and the first step is to acknowledge that it doesn’t have to be this way\.

### Keep records

Remembering all the details of what happened can be challenging\. Do not rely on your memory\. Carefully record the details of the harassment as soon as it occurs\. Also record any attempts to tell the person that the behaviour is unwelcome\. Keep all harassing letters, gifts, emails, texts, voice mail messages, and more as evidence\.

### Seek advice and resources

UBC offers many services that can help you with your situation: 

-   If you believe you or others are in physical danger, contact [Community Safety](http://communitysafety.ubc.ca/) \(call [604 822 2222](tel:6048222222)\) or the police \(call [911](tel:911)\) immediately\. 
-   You can [request an advising appointment](https://equity.ubc.ca/what-we-do/human-rights-advising/) with an impartial human rights advisor at the Equity and Inclusion Office\.
-   You may also want to contact the [Office of the Ombudsperson for Students](https://ombudsoffice.ubc.ca/who-we-are/), an independent, impartial, and confidential service that supports students in addressing and resolving concerns about unfair treatment at UBC\.
-   Other UBC staff members are available to help, such as [academic advisors](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) from your faculty or program\. You can also contact staff and faculty members in your department\.
-   The University provides a wide range of [health and wellness resources](https://students.ubc.ca/health/), including [Counselling Services](https://students.ubc.ca/health/counselling-services/)\.

## If you witness an act of discrimination[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/equity\-diversity\-inclusion\-resources/responding\-discrimination/\#if\-you\-witness\-an\-act\-of\-discrimination](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/responding-discrimination/#if-you-witness-an-act-of-discrimination)

A bystander is someone who observes a conflict, unacceptable behaviour, or an unsafe situation\. By taking steps to make a difference, you can be an **active** **bystander** and support those in the situation\.

If you witness an act of discrimination, depending on the situation or your feeling of safety, you can employ any of the 5 Ds of bystander intervention: Distract, Delegate, Document, Delay, or Direct\.

-   [The 5 Ds to bystander intervention](https://righttobe.org/guides/bystander-intervention-training/)
-   [Free anti\-harassment training sessions](https://righttobe.org/our-training/)
-   [Five tips on tackling racism](https://equity.ubc.ca/news-and-stories/solidarity-action-five-tips-to-shut-down-racism/)
-   [How to be an active witness](https://beyond.ubc.ca/active-witness/)

## UBC Policies[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/equity\-diversity\-inclusion\-resources/responding\-discrimination/\#ubc\-policies](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/responding-discrimination/#ubc-policies)

Familiarize yourself with the policies set out by the University, which are applicable to all students, staff, and faculty\.

-   [Discrimination Policy SC7](https://universitycounsel.ubc.ca/policies/discrimination-policy/)  
    The policy prohibits discrimination on a number of protected grounds including age, family status, physical or mental disability, race, Indigenous identity, religion, sex, or sexual orientation\. 
-   [UBC’s Respectful Environment Statement](https://hr.ubc.ca/working-ubc/respectful-environment)  
    This statement provides guiding principles to support an environment in which respect, civility, diversity, opportunity and inclusion are valued\. It also addresses bullying and harassment not related to human rights grounds\.
-   [Conflict of Interest and Conflict of Commitment Policy SC3](https://universitycounsel.ubc.ca/policies/coi-policy/)  
    Policy SC3 describes how faculty, staff, and students must act during research, teaching, and learning activities\.

## Getting advice and support[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/equity\-diversity\-inclusion\-resources/responding\-discrimination/\#getting\-advice\-and\-support](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/responding-discrimination/#getting-advice-and-support)

-   [Equity & Inclusion Office Human Rights Advising](https://equity.ubc.ca/how-we-can-help/human-rights-advising/)
-   [Health and wellness resources](https://students.ubc.ca/health/)
-   [UBC Counselling Services](https://students.ubc.ca/health/counselling-services/)
-   [Office of the Ombudsperson for Students](https://ombudsoffice.ubc.ca/who-we-are/)
-   [AMS Ombudsperson](https://www.ams.ubc.ca/support-services/ombuds/)
-   [UBC Sexual Violence Prevention and Response Office \(SVPRO\)](https://svpro.ubc.ca/)
-   [Equity, diversity, and inclusion resources for students](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/)

title: UBC Orientation and Transition Leadership opportunities
content_markdown:
Each year, UBC welcomes thousands of new students to campus\. Become a student leader and guide them through orientation programs\. These programs allow students to meet friends, learn about their academic experience, and connect with professors from their faculty\.

## What you can expect[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/ubc\-orientation\-transition\-leadership/\#what\-you\-can\-expect](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/ubc-orientation-transition-leadership/#what-you-can-expect)

-   Learn about building respectful and inclusive communities\.
-   Develop leadership, facilitation, and teamwork skills\.
-   Meet other students in your faculty or school\.
-   Find out about involvement opportunities and resources in the UBC community\.

[imagine orientation transition leaders](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/imagine_orientation_transition_leaders-1.jpg)

## Apply for a position[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/ubc\-orientation\-transition\-leadership/\#apply\-for\-a\-position](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/ubc-orientation-transition-leadership/#apply-for-a-position)

Get involved in leadership positions and support students in their transition to UBC\.

title: Jump Start and Collegia Leader opportunities
content_markdown:
## About the roles[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/ubc\-orientation\-transition\-leadership/jump\-start\-collegia\-leader/\#about\-the\-roles](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/ubc-orientation-transition-leadership/jump-start-collegia-leader/#about-the-roles)

As a Jump Start Leader or Collegia Advisor, you’ll support new students as they transition into university life, helping to build connection, confidence, and community\. You’ll work closely with the [Centre for Student Development and Leadership](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-student-development-leadership/) staff and other student leaders to create welcoming, engaging experiences where students connect with others and learn what to expect in their first year\. These roles will support programs including [Jump Start](https://you.ubc.ca/jump-start-vancouver/), [Collegia](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/ubc-collegia/), and [Imagine UBC](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/orientations/imagine-ubc/)\.

### Jump Start roles 

Jump Start Senior Orientation Leaders, Jump Start Orientation Leaders, and Jump Start Events Crew focus on the delivery of the Jump Start program for a one\-week period leading up to the beginning of classes in September\. 

### Collegia roles

Collegia Advisors and Senior Collegia Advisors focus on year\-long community\-building and student support, beginning with Jump Start and continuing throughout the Winter Term\.

## Position requirements[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/ubc\-orientation\-transition\-leadership/jump\-start\-collegia\-leader/\#position\-requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/ubc-orientation-transition-leadership/jump-start-collegia-leader/#position-requirements)

-   You must be in good academic and non\-academic standing
-   You must be available for all time commitments as outlined in the job description
-   You must meet all eligibility and employment requirements listed for the role on CareersOnline

## Skills and qualifications[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/ubc\-orientation\-transition\-leadership/jump\-start\-collegia\-leader/\#skills\-and\-qualifications](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/ubc-orientation-transition-leadership/jump-start-collegia-leader/#skills-and-qualifications)

To be eligible for the roles, you must demonstrate the following:

-   Strong leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills
-   Excellent organization and time management
-   Ability to lead and facilitate programs, activities, or group experiences with students
-   Ability to adapt to new experiences and challenges with a positive mindset
-   Comfort working independently and collaboratively with peers and staff
-   Ability to build welcoming, inclusive communities for students from diverse backgrounds and lived experiences
-   An interest to engage in ongoing personal and professional development opportunities
-   The ability to represent UBC and its student leadership programs in a positive and professional manner

## Time commitment[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/ubc\-orientation\-transition\-leadership/jump\-start\-collegia\-leader/\#time\-commitment](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/ubc-orientation-transition-leadership/jump-start-collegia-leader/#time-commitment)

Please see the position descriptions on [CareersOnline](https://ubc-csm.symplicity.com/) for full details about time commitment expectations\.

All positions start in August\.

## What will you get out of the role?[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/ubc\-orientation\-transition\-leadership/jump\-start\-collegia\-leader/\#what\-will\-you\-get\-out\-of\-the\-role](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/ubc-orientation-transition-leadership/jump-start-collegia-leader/#what-will-you-get-out-of-the-role)

Jump Start Leaders and Collegia Advisors build hands\-on leadership skills and help shape the first\-year student experience at UBC\.

As a leader or advisor, you will:

-   Build confidence in your leadership, facilitation, and teamwork skills
-   Strengthen your ability to connect with and support diverse student communities
-   Gain insight into how orientation and transition programs shape the first\-year experience
-   Make a tangible, positive impact on incoming students while growing as a leader yourself

title: Booking a general teaching space on campus
content_markdown:
Students can book general teaching spaces on campus if they are part of an AMS\-constituted club or if they are a booking representative for an authorized student group\. All students must read and follow UBC’s [Respectful Environment Statement](http://www.hr.ubc.ca/respectful-environment/files/UBC-Statement-on-Respectful-Environment-2014.pdf) \(pdf\) and [Booking Guidelines for General Teaching Space](https://enrolmentservices.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/media-uploads/files/GTS%20Booking%20Guidelines%20w%20Rental%20Rates%20-%20011725.pdf) \(pdf\)\.

Use the [Learning Spaces search tool](https://learningspaces.ubc.ca/find-space) to find the perfect classroom with the right amenities for your event, workshop, or activity\. Check that building hours align with your event schedule\. Bookings are subject to availability\.

## Required forms[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/organizing\-campus\-events/booking\-general\-teaching\-space\-campus/\#required\-forms](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/organizing-campus-events/booking-general-teaching-space-campus/#required-forms)

Submit the [UBC Vancouver Student Booking Representative Form](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_b1R19lL5qq1SKQS) **before** submitting room booking requests\. You must update your forms each academic year\.

Students who are affiliated with the AMS must complete and upload the [AMS booking representatives form](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/ams_booking_representatives_form.pdf) \(pdf\)\.

Students who are not affiliated with the AMS but would like to establish a student organization must first fill out the [authorization form](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/student_organization_authorization_form.pdf) \(pdf\)\. To operate, you will need the permission of the department head\.

After you have been authorized by the department head, complete the [student booking representatives form](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/student_organization_booking_representatives_form.pdf) \(pdf\)\. Both forms must be completed and uploaded\.

## Rules and policies[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/organizing\-campus\-events/booking\-general\-teaching\-space\-campus/\#rules\-and\-policies](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/organizing-campus-events/booking-general-teaching-space-campus/#rules-and-policies)

-   Room bookings are scheduled to begin and end on the hour or half\-hour\. The activity should end 10 minutes prior to the scheduled end time to allow for transition to the next activity\. 
-   Food, alcohol, non\-alcoholic drinks are not permitted in general teaching spaces \(classrooms\)\. 
-   If a room is not returned to its original condition, Custodial Services may charge fees to restore it\.
-   Limit your requests for specific buildings, layouts, and features when booking a space\.
-   All bookings must adhere to the following policies:
    -   [Policy \#UP9 Booking and Rental of UBC Space](https://universitycounsel.ubc.ca/policies/space-rental-policy/)
    -   [Policy \#UP5 Ownership and Use of UBC Equipment and UBC Support Services](https://universitycounsel.ubc.ca/policies/equipmentservices-use-policy)
    -   [Policy \#UP8 Posting of Notices, Posters, and Signs](https://universitycounsel.ubc.ca/policies/signage-policy/)
    -   [UBC’s Respectful Environment Statement](http://www.hr.ubc.ca/respectful-environment/files/UBC-Statement-on-Respectful-Environment-2014.pdf)

## Booking release dates[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/organizing\-campus\-events/booking\-general\-teaching\-space\-campus/\#booking\-release\-dates](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/organizing-campus-events/booking-general-teaching-space-campus/#booking-release-dates)

In order to allow time to book credit courses and/or exams in general teaching spaces, all other booking requests can only be made on and after the release date for the corresponding room booking period\.

### 2026 Summer release dates

| Time Period | Booking Period | Release Date |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026 Summer Term 1 | Apr 26 to Jun 21, 2026 | Jan 21, 2026 \(refer to collection week below\) |
| June 2026 Exams | Jun 22 to 26, 2026 | Jun 3, 2026 |
| 2026 Summer Term 2 | Jun 27 to Aug 16, 2026 | Jan 21, 2026 \(refer to collection week below\) |
| August 2026 Exams | Aug 17 to 21, 2026 | Jul 29, 2026 |
| End of Summer | Aug 22 to Sept 6, 2026 | Jan 21, 2026 \(refer to collection week below\) |

### 2026/27 Winter release dates

| Time Period | Booking Period | Release Date |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2026/27 Winter Term 1 | Sep 7 to Dec 10, 2026 | Jul 29, 2026 \(refer to collection week below\) |
| December 2026 Exams | Dec 11 to 22, 2026 | Nov 18, 2026 |
| 2026/27 Winter Term 2 | Jan 4 to Apr 15, 2027 | Oct 1, 2026 \(refer to collection week below\) |
| April 2027 Exams | Apr 16 to 27, 2027 | Mar 24, 2027 |

### Collection week

Booking requests for winter and summer sessions will be collected for a one\-week period called collection week \(e\.g\., Wednesday to Tuesday\) for each respective session\. Requests received within the one\-week collection period will be booked in accordance with their respective priority\. Booking requests received after the one\-week periods will be processed on a first come, first serve basis\.

For example, if January 25 is the release date, then January 25 to 31 is the collection week\. Anything submitted on February 1 onwards will be processed on a first come, first serve basis\.

## Making a room booking request[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/organizing\-campus\-events/booking\-general\-teaching\-space\-campus/\#making\-a\-room\-booking\-request](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/organizing-campus-events/booking-general-teaching-space-campus/#making-a-room-booking-request)

1.  Read the [policies and procedures](https://facultystaff.students.ubc.ca/sites/facultystaff.students.ubc.ca/files/GTS%20Booking%20Guidelines%20w%20Rental%20Rates%20-%20011725.pdf) \(pdf\) in place for general teaching space booking requests carefully\. If you have any questions, contact [room\.bookings@ubc\.ca](mailto:room.bookings@ubc.ca)\.

3.  Complete the [Room Booking Request Form](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3vHf0CNAatJGRRc) at least **4 weeks** before your requested booking date\.
4.  Scheduling Services will process the request and email you about your room booking confirmation within 15 business days except between January and March, and September and October, where response times may be longer\.

Please **do not** advertise your event until you have received a final booking confirmation\.

Rooms are rented for a minimum of 4 hours\. Additional time is charged on a per\-hour basis\. GST tax is not included\.

If a room is not returned to its original state, you may be subject to a charge for Custodial Services to restore the room back to its original condition\.

title: Events with food
content_markdown:
Food is a great way to build community and attract event attendance, however it is also important to be aware of how food may make an event less inclusive for certain groups in the community\.

Many members of the university community have important dietary restrictions related to their religious or cultural background\. Others have common allergies that should be taken into consideration when planning the menu, preparation, and serving food at events\.

## Providing food at public events[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/organizing\-campus\-events/events\-food/\#providing\-food\-at\-public\-events](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/organizing-campus-events/events-food/#providing-food-at-public-events)

For public events, you may need to fill out a [Temporary Food Services Application Form](https://www.vch.ca/en/service/temporary-events-markets-permits) with Vancouver Coastal Health\.

Learn more about [organizing outdoor events](https://planning.ubc.ca/outdoorevents) at UBC\.

## Know your food[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/organizing\-campus\-events/events\-food/\#know\-your\-food](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/organizing-campus-events/events-food/#know-your-food)

Work with your organizing team to brainstorm a range of food options that will ensure the event is inclusive\.

-   Do your research to fully understand cultural and religious dietary restrictions as they can apply not only to how the food is served, but also how the food is prepared\.
-   When advertising your event, make sure you share the different options of food that will be available at the event \(e\.g\. “pork\-free”, “vegetarian”, “vegan” options will be available at the event\)\.
-   Ensure that vegetarian and non\-vegetarian food is separated, and distinct types of meats are also separated if you plan to offer halal or kosher options\.
-   Ensure that separate utensils are also used for serving\. If you are having a BBQ, have separate BBQ plates as well\.
-   Label food options clearly and provide a list of ingredients whenever possible\.
-   Try to include dairy and gluten free options where possible\.

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/organizing\-campus\-events/events\-food/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/organizing-campus-events/events-food/#additional-resources)

-   [Bookable spaces on campus](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/organizing-campus-events/booking-an-event-space/)  
    Find the application procedures for booking an on\-campus event space\.
-   [Serving alcohol at campus events](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/organizing-campus-events/serving-alcohol-campus-events/)  
    Before planning to serve alcohol at your event, familiarize yourself with UBC policies\.
