-   [Dialectical Behaviour Therapy \(DBT\) Skills Group](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/dialectical-behavior-therapy-skills-group/)
-   [Dungeons and Dragons Social Skills Group](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/social-skills-group-counselling/)
-   [Grad Student Support Group](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/grad-student-support-group/)
-   [I am Stronger than My Depression: CBT Skills Group](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/i-am-stronger-than-my-depression-cbt-skills-group/)
-   [International Students Support Group](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/international-support-group/)
-   [Navigating Anxiety Group](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/acceptance-commitment-therapy-anxiety-group/)
-   [Rooted and Resilient Group](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/rooted-resilient-group-counselling/)
-   [Strengthening Connections Group](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/strengthening-connections-group/)
-   [Understanding your Emotions \(AEDP\) Group](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/understanding-your-emotions-aedp-group/)

## Other UBC support groups[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/\#other\-ubc\-support\-groups](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/#other-ubc-support-groups)

There are a variety of groups and meetings on campus which offer a sense of community and support for mental health and wellness related concerns\.

-   **[Kaleidoscope](https://the-kaleidoscope.com/)**  
    The Kaleidoscope offers weekly peer led support groups for undergraduate and graduate students living with the experience of mental health concerns\.
-   **[UBC Student Recovery Community \(SRC\)](https://students.ubc.ca/health/substance-use-health-harm-reduction/ubc-student-recovery-community/)**  
    For students who are in recovery, or curious to explore their relationship with alcohol, drugs, and/or addictive behaviours such as disordered eating, the SRC offers peer led support meetings\.
-   **[UBC Sexual Assault Support Centre \(SASC\)](https://www.amssasc.ca/support/support-services-available/)**  
    SASC Support and Advocacy staff facilitate support groups for people of all genders and identities who have experienced any form of sexualized violence\. These groups are open to all members of the UBC community\.

title: Community and Healing: A 2STGD and Gender Questioning Support Group
content_markdown:
## About the group[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/2stgd\-and\-gender\-questioning\-support\-group/\#about\-the\-group](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/2stgd-and-gender-questioning-support-group/#about-the-group)

This group is about building community connections, sharing resources, and supporting you to thrive as your most authentic self\. The primary focus of the group will be to create meaningful and supportive connections with other students, ourselves, and with trans histories and solidarities across time and space\.

The group is centred on the values and teachings of intersectionality, neuroqueering, decolonization and the Disability Justice movement\. The facilitators want to uplift and honour the unique and intersecting identities of students across a range of gender identities\.

Topics will be determined by the interests of the participants\. Some possible topics include:

-   Gender Identity and Mental Health: Supporting You to Thrive
-   Information and Support for Accessing Gender: Affirming Care and Services
-   Relationships of All Kinds\!
-   Navigating Your Unique and Shifting Gender Identity and Presentation
-   Solidarity, Resistance, and the Legacy of Community Resilience
-   Transphobia and Safety
-   Navigating University Life and Academic Demands as a Non\-Cis Student
-   Gender Struggles and Gender Euphoria

## Eligibility[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/2stgd\-and\-gender\-questioning\-support\-group/\#eligibility](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/2stgd-and-gender-questioning-support-group/#eligibility)

This group is open to UBC Vancouver students who identify as Two\-Spirit, trans, gender diverse, non\-binary, genderqueer, and those who are exploring their unique gender identity\. This list is non\-exhaustive\. Facilitators are grateful for the wonderful diversity of genders in existence, and students who are not cisgender but have explored or are exploring a gender identity not listed here are very welcome to join\. 

Group sessions will be held in person\. To safeguard the group, the location will be shared with participants following an intake with the facilitators\. 

We recognize the unique individual needs of each student and aim to provide an accessible group experience\.

title: Dialectical Behavior Therapy Skills Group
content_markdown:
## About the group[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/dialectical\-behavior\-therapy\-skills\-group/\#about\-the\-group](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/dialectical-behavior-therapy-skills-group/#about-the-group)

When emotions feel too intense, or your reactions create more problems than solutions, Dialectical Behavior Therapy \(DBT\) can offer a way forward\.

DBT is an evidence\-based approach that teaches practical, step\-by\-step skills to manage emotions, tolerate distress, and navigate relationships more effectively\. It’s built on the idea that two things can be true at once – you can accept yourself as you are and still work toward meaningful change to build your better life\.

Structured like an interactive class, this 8\-week, in\-person group is where you can learn and practice strategies\. Alongside the group, you would take part in regular individual check\-ins with your health professional to support your progress\. 

This group is designed for students who want to:

-   Respond to emotions without feeling overwhelmed
-   Cope better with crisis moments
-   Build stronger, healthier relationships
-   Stay grounded and present, even under stress

## Eligibility[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/dialectical\-behavior\-therapy\-skills\-group/\#eligibility](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/dialectical-behavior-therapy-skills-group/#eligibility)

Group sessions will be held in person\. Student Health and Wellbeing recognizes the unique individual needs of each student and will provide alternate options if group programming is not an appropriate referral option or fit\.

## How to register[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/dialectical\-behavior\-therapy\-skills\-group/\#how\-to\-register](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/dialectical-behavior-therapy-skills-group/#how-to-register)

This group is by referral only\.

Find more information by connecting with a professional at Student Health and Wellbeing, such as a counsellor, physician, mental health nurse, or a Wellness Advisor\.

title: International Students Support Group
content_markdown:
## About the group[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/international\-support\-group/\#about\-the\-group](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/international-support-group/#about-the-group)

Join Global Connections, UBC’s in\-person international student support group, to meet other international students in a safe and relaxing space, connect and build a community of support on campus, and learn ways to navigate the unique challenges often experienced by international students\.

Participants are encouraged to bring a variety of relevant topics to the group meetings\. Past group topics have included:

-   Adjusting to Canadian culture
-   Language concerns and challenges
-   Making connections and new friendships
-   Coping with academic stress and demands
-   Facing uncertainty and unknowns in a new country
-   Building resilience and self\-compassion

## Eligibility[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/international\-support\-group/\#eligibility](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/international-support-group/#eligibility)

**Schedule**: Thursdays beginning on Sep 17, 2026

**Time:** 2:00 to 3:30 pm

You can join the support group at any point during the term, although we recommend regular attendance as it builds community\.

title: Strengthening Connections Group
content_markdown:
## About the group[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/strengthening\-connections\-group/\#about\-the\-group](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/strengthening-connections-group/#about-the-group)

This group is designed for students seeking to develop the important skills needed for healthy, meaningful relationships\. Through a focus on self\-awareness, communication, values, boundaries, conflict resolution, and navigating grief and goodbyes, participants will gain practical tools to improve how they connect with themselves and others\.

Whether you’re looking to build new friendships, deepen existing relationships, or better manage difficult emotions and conversations, this supportive space will help you grow both personally and relationally\.

This is a drop\-in group so students are free to attend as many or as few sessions as they may need\.

Group session topics include: 

-   Foundations of healthy relationships
-   Self\-awareness and emotional regulation in relationships
-   Communication skills that build connection
-   Conflict resolution and boundaries
-   Grief and goodbyes

## Eligibility[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/strengthening\-connections\-group/\#eligibility](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/strengthening-connections-group/#eligibility)

Any currently registered UBC Vancouver student is eligible to participate\.

## Group session details[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/strengthening\-connections\-group/\#group\-session\-details](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/strengthening-connections-group/#group-session-details)

-   **Schedule:** Mondays, from Oct 19 to Nov 16, 2026
-   **Time:** 2:15 pm to 3:45 pm
-   **Location:** UBC Vancouver Campus

The location of the meeting will be emailed to registered students before the session\.

## How to register[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/strengthening\-connections\-group/\#how\-to\-register](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/strengthening-connections-group/#how-to-register)

If you are already working with a UBC health professional such as a Wellness Advisor, counsellor, physician, or nurse practitioner, they can register you for the group\.

Alternatively, you can register for group sessions through the booking portal below\. Select “Counselling – Counselling Services” from the list of Counselling options\.

title: Meet the counsellors
content_markdown:
## About the team[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/meet\-the\-counsellors/\#about\-the\-team](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/meet-the-counsellors/#about-the-team)

UBC Student Health and Wellbeing has a diverse team of mental health professionals and trainees who can provide a wide range of services while you attend university:

-   [Wellness Advising Team](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/meet-the-counsellors/#wellness-advising-team)
-   [Counselling Team](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/meet-the-counsellors/#counselling-team)
-   [Indigenous Mental Health and Wellbeing Team](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/meet-the-counsellors/#indigenous-mental-health-and-wellbeing-team)
-   [Embedded Counsellors](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/meet-the-counsellors/#embedded-counsellors)
-   [Leadership Team](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/meet-the-counsellors/#leadership-team)

## Wellness Advising Team[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/meet\-the\-counsellors/\#wellness\-advising\-team](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/meet-the-counsellors/#wellness-advising-team)

[Headshot of Jenna Borisevich](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/wellness_advising_jenna_borisevich-1.jpg)

#### Jenna Borisevich, MSW, RSW \(she/her\)

Jenna is a Registered Social Worker holding a Master of Social Work from the University of Toronto\. Jenna offers a holistic and integrative approach as well as a warm and compassionate space for individuals to safely share their emotions and experiences\. Jenna endeavors to leave students feeling heard, valued, and supported – equipped with practical tools and a collaborative plan that endorses their wellness goals\.

[A tree branch dappled with sunlight\. The generic image used for Counselling Services team members who don't have headshots\.](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_services_generic_avatar.jpg)

#### Anna Ho, MA, CCC \(she/her\)

Anna is a Certified Canadian Counsellor registered with the Canadian Counselling and Psychotherapy Association\. With an emphasis on compassion, Anna provides a warm and inclusive space for individuals to feel heard and cared for\. Anna is dedicated towards providing a safe environment for students that cultivates acceptance and understanding through an integrative and humanistic approach\.  

[Headshot of Amman Shahi](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/wellness_advising_amman_shahi.jpg)

#### Amman Shahi, BA, MSW, RSW \(she/her\)

Amman is a first generation Canadian\-Punjabi practitioner\. While English is her mother tongue, Punjabi and Hindi are her additional languages\. Her practice philosophy is that everyone is the narrator of their own lived experience, and that the human interaction is one of interwoven story\. She believes in an emotion\-focused, narrative approach, and emphasizes behavioral activation through the lens of cultural humility, decolonization, and mindfulness practice\. Amman holds a Master of Social Work from the UBC Okanagan Campus \(Sylix Nation\), a community in which she was born and raised in\.

[A tree branch dappled with sunlight\. The generic image used for Counselling Services team members who don't have headshots\.](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_services_generic_avatar.jpg)

#### Michelle Lim, MSW, RSW \(she/her\)

Michelle is a Registered Social Worker with the BC College of Social Workers\. With cultural humility, she strives to foster a welcoming, caring, and trauma\-informed space where students can express themselves and feel heard\. Her counselling approach emphasizes the mind\-body connection, and is responsive to her students’ needs\.

[A tree branch dappled with sunlight\. The generic image used for Counselling Services team members who don't have headshots\.](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_services_generic_avatar.jpg)

#### Kristen Yang, CCC, RCC

Kristen is a clinical counsellor with a Master’s degree in Counselling Psychology from the University of Victoria\. Kristen seeks to create a welcoming space where thoughts, emotions, physical sensations, and parts of self can be explored with compassion and curiosity, including those that have previously been rejected or neglected\. Using an attachment\-based approach, Kristen believes that our emotions can act as guides to our inner wants and needs and listening to them and allowing ourselves to process them without resistance or judgment can provide valuable insight into thoughtful next steps\.

[A tree branch dappled with sunlight\. The generic image used for Counselling Services team members who don't have headshots\.](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_services_generic_avatar.jpg)

#### Kathryn Kryska, M\. Ed, CCC

Kathryn holds a Master of Education in Counselling Psychology from the University of Lethbridge and is a Certified Canadian Counsellor\. She brings a relational and culturally responsive approach to her work and meets students with openness and curiosity\. Kathryn aims to create an approachable space where students can explore their concerns, recognize their strengths, and leave with strategies and resources that support their personalized wellness plan\.

## Counselling Team[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/meet\-the\-counsellors/\#counselling\-team](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/meet-the-counsellors/#counselling-team)

[Headshot of Karen Flood](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_karen_flood.jpg)

#### Karen Flood, PhD, RCC, R\. Psych \(she/her\)

Karen is a Registered Psychologist with over 25 years’ experience\. Informed by her philosophy of life\-long learning and the possibility of change, Karen works collaboratively to build a safe and supportive environment within which to create change\. Therapeutic work is guided by presenting concerns and goals, but likely to include working with thoughts, emotions, and values\. Therapy may involve increasing understanding of experiences and behaviours, mind\-body connection, gentle challenges, mindfulness and compassion, revisiting strengths and supports, and learning new information, skills, and ways of being\. Karen holds a special place in her heart for the graduate student experience\.

[A tree branch dappled with sunlight\. The generic image used for Counselling Services team members who don't have headshots\.](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_services_generic_avatar.jpg)

#### Jacky Grüter\-Andrew, MA, RCC\-ACS \(she/her\)

Jacky works with her students to create a safe, welcoming space to explore their concerns and strengths\. She recognizes the uniqueness of every individual and collaboratively tailors a therapy approach to support students to move towards their goals\. She strives to practice cultural humility and her therapy style is based on attachment, trauma\-informed approaches, the mind\-body connection, acceptance, and mindful self\-compassion\. Jacky uses humor, warmth, and gentle challenges to help students move from feeling stuck to a sense of choice\.

[A tree branch dappled with sunlight\. The generic image used for Counselling Services team members who don't have headshots\.](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_services_generic_avatar.jpg)

#### Rebecca Lalonde, MEd\., R\. Psych \(she/her\)

Rebecca is a Registered Psychologist holding a Master’s degree in School and Counselling Psychology from the University of Saskatchewan\. She aims to create an atmosphere of openness and non\-judgment where students can become more aware of their thoughts and feelings, connect to their strengths, and feel empowered to take action that feels meaningful in their lives\. Her collaborative and practical approach is rooted in a humanistic and evidence\-based framework to support students in navigating life’s challenges\.

Rebecca is currently unavailable for counselling\.

[Headshot of Sharon Lee](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_sharon_lee.jpg)

#### Sharon Lee, MCP, CCC \(she/her\)

Sharon is a counsellor who incorporates a strengths\-based approach towards exploring the connections between thoughts, behaviours, and emotions\. Sharon believes that students are the experts in their own lives, and that it is important to understand and acknowledge each student’s diversity and intersectionality\. Sharon also believes that including mindfulness and grounding into counselling is important to keeping therapeutic work present focused\. Collaboration with students is a key element within Sharon’s work as this creates opportunities for students to discover their own solutions to their concerns\.

[Headshot of Karen Moss](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_karen_moss.jpg)

#### Karen Moss, MA, MC, RCC \(she/her\)

Karen believes that everyone deserves to have a safe space to explore who they are, their concerns, and their goals\. She brings social justice concerns into the therapy room and strives to practice cultural humility\. Karen uses an integrative therapy style which can include mind\-body, attachment and trauma\-informed approaches\. She seeks to create a welcoming environment for students with her caring, creative, and person\-centered approach to wellbeing\.

[Headshot of Gordon Lai](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/embedded_counselling_gordon_lai.jpg)

#### Gordon Lai, MEd, RCC \(he/him\)

Gordon is a Registered Clinical Counsellor with a Master of Education in Counselling Psychology from UBC\. His therapeutic approach integrates acceptance and commitment while also taking a strengths\-based and solution focused approach when working with students\. While Gordon appreciates the outdoors and nature, he is described as an “indoor cat” who loves the modern conveniences that the indoors provide\.

[Headshot of Alysha Chan Kent](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_alysha_chan_kent.jpg)

#### Alysha Chan Kent, PhD, CCC \(she/her\)

Alysha Chan Kent is a Canadian Certified Counsellor with UBC Student Health and Wellbeing who holds a PhD in Counselling Psychology from the University of Calgary\. Her therapeutic practice is rooted in the provision of a warm, non\-judgmental space for each student to work through life’s challenges, helping them to uncover personal strengths and create meaningful change\. In her practice, Alysha adopts an integrative approach, drawing from various evidence\-based approaches\. Navigating this process may include exploring students’ thoughts, feelings, and behaviours, identifying their values and strengths, and untangling narratives that might be holding them back\.

[Headshot of Rachel Walker](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_rachel_walker.jpg)

#### Rachel Walker, PsyD, R\. Psych, HSP, CMPC \(she/her\)

Rachel is a Registered Psychologist who earned her doctorate at Springfield College in Massachusetts majoring in Counselling Psychology and a concentration in Athletic Counselling\. Rachel places great importance on fostering a strong therapeutic alliance with her students and assisting them to understand what is no longer working in their lives\. She invites students to explore challenging yet vital places of growth in the service of what is most important to them\. Through humility, compassion, play, and curiosity, Rachel looks forward to supporting students on their journey towards healing, growth, and flourishing\.

[Headshot of Nicole Adoranti](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/embedded_counselling_nicole_adoranti.jpg)

#### Nicole Adoranti, MEd, CCC \(she/her\)

Nicole is a Canadian Certified Counsellor with an Master of Education in Counselling Psychology from the University of Toronto\. Her counselling approach is based first and foremost on the clinician\-student relationship, as she feels an authentic connection creates the platform for meaningful change\. With years of experience working with people in different countries and from a variety of cultures, she aims to remain humble in her approach while integrating trauma\-informed and decolonial practices into her work\.

[Headshot of Polly Cheng](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_polly_cheng.jpg)

#### Polly Cheng, PhD

Polly is a psychologist and earned her PhD in Counselling Psychology from McGill University\. She practices within an anti\-oppressive and trauma\-informed framework\. Polly’s approach to therapy facilitates a collaborative exploration of both individual and systemic factors to encourage students to thicken their understanding of themselves and their challenges\. Drawing from a range of evidence\-based approaches, she aims to support students in developing emotion regulation skills and fostering a deeper connection with themselves\. Polly strives to motivate change through her warmth, compassion, and curiosity\.

[A tree branch dappled with sunlight\. The generic image used for Counselling Services team members who don't have headshots\.](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_services_generic_avatar.jpg)

#### D, Queer and Gender\-Affirming Counsellor, RCC \(they/them\)

D is currently unavailable for counselling\.

Please contact Student Health and Wellbeing at [604 822 3811](tel:6048223811) for queer and gender affirming counselling options\.

[Headshot of Craig Lee](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_craig_lee.jpg)

#### Craig Lee, MCP, RCC \(he/him\)

Craig is a Registered Clinical Counsellor and a Professional Art Therapist\. His approach to therapy is to create a safe and non\-judgmental space for students to collaboratively explore their goals with the belief that people generally wish to improve their situation\. He practices therapy through an integration of different techniques including a person\-centered approach, asks students to foster a different relationship with their thoughts and feelings, and utilizes art\-based approaches in healing\. Additionally, he recognizes the intersectionality of diverse identities, and acknowledges the importance this has in the therapy process\. 

[A tree branch dappled with sunlight\. The generic image used for Counselling Services team members who don't have headshots\.](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_services_generic_avatar.jpg)

#### Kelly Lyons, MA, MEd, RCC \(she/her\)

Kelly is a Registered Clinical Counsellor with a Master’s in Sport Psychology from UofA and a Master’s in Counselling Psychology from UBC\. Her aim is to create a warm, autonomous, environment for students to feel heard and hopeful about their work together\. She offers a trauma\-informed practice utilizing anti\-oppressive principles to build connection\. Kelly works with cultural humility demonstrating comfort and genuine curiosity to explore how each part of our cultural identities intersects, making us who we are\. She believes it is important for students to be included and empowered to create the changes they want in their lives\.

[A tree branch dappled with sunlight\. The generic image used for Counselling Services team members who don't have headshots\.](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_services_generic_avatar.jpg)

#### Rachel Kerzner, PsyD \(she/her\)

Rachel completed her doctoral training in Clinical Psychology at the University of Prince Edward Island and has applied for registration with the BC College of Psychologists\. Rachel’s approach to working with students is collaborative, flexible, and person\-centered\. She strives to offer a warm and non\-judgemental space, help student’s set manageable goals, practice coping skills, and process emotions and experiences\. Rachel draws from various evidence\-based and trauma\-informed interventions grounded in exploring the connection between thoughts, feelings, and behaviours, and adapted to the student’s unique values, goals, and preferences\. Outside of work, Rachel enjoys spending time outside with her two rescue dogs\. 

[Headshot of Sae Aizawa](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/wellness_advising_sae_aizawa.jpg)

#### Sae Aizawa, MC, RCC \(she/her\)

Sae is a Registered Clinical Counsellor who completed her undergraduate degree at UBC and holds a Master of Counselling from City University of Seattle\. Sae takes a student\-centered approach and believes that the student is the expert in their lives\. Through this approach, Sae supports students to be psychologically flexible towards their emotions and connect to their values\. Sae also believes that being present and grounding ourselves in the current day is a helpful way to cultivate the here\-and\-now through mindfulness practice\.

## Indigenous Mental Health and Wellbeing Team[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/meet\-the\-counsellors/\#indigenous\-mental\-health\-and\-wellbeing\-team](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/meet-the-counsellors/#indigenous-mental-health-and-wellbeing-team)

[Headshot of Hali McLennan](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/indigenous_mental_health_wellbeing_hali_mclennan.jpg)

#### Hali McLennan, MSW, RSW \(she/her\)

Hali is a member of the Métiis Nation of British Columbia\. She was born in the Yukon but as a child, moved to the unceded territories of the Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil\-Waututh\. She completed both her Social Work degrees at UBC’s School of Social Work and is grateful to get the chance to support current UBC students through the challenges they may face while at school\.

[A tree branch dappled with sunlight\. The generic image used for Counselling Services team members who don't have headshots\.](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_services_generic_avatar.jpg)

#### Anne Sinclair, MCP, RCC \(she/her\)

Anne is of Peguis First Nation ancestry and has lived experience working in the remote Heiltsuk First Nation community of Bella Bella\. She holds a Master of Counselling Psychology from Adler University and a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology from UBC\. Her practice is grounded in a holistic approach that honours mind, body, and spirit, while providing a culturally safe and supportive space for each client\. Anne draws on Rational Emotive Behaviour Therapy \(REBT\), Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing \(EMDR\), Narrative Therapy, Solutions\-Focused Therapy, and other creative, client\-centred approaches to support personal growth and healing\.

## Embedded Counsellors[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/meet\-the\-counsellors/\#embedded\-counsellors](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/meet-the-counsellors/#embedded-counsellors)

[Image](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/embedded_counselling_asmae_el-bouhali.jpg)

#### Asmae El\-Bouhali, MEd, MSc, CCPA member \(she/her\)

Asmae is the Embedded Counsellor within the Faculty of Medicine \(FoM\) dedicated to the clinical care and support of FoM undergraduate students\. She offers a collaborative, safe, compassionate therapeutic space in which students can explore self\-awareness, mindfulness, and personal growth\. Asmae facilitates change and goal attainment utilizing a trauma\-informed lens and several theoretical and research\-based methodologies\. Asmae also has extensive experience in cross\-cultural therapy and is able to offer services in Moroccan\-Arabic and Dutch\.

[A tree branch dappled with sunlight\. The generic image used for Counselling Services team members who don't have headshots\.](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_services_generic_avatar.jpg)

#### Laura Harvey, MSW, RSW \(she/her\)

Laura is the counsellor embedded in the Faculty of Arts\. She believes that meaningful connection with others is essential and that we can heal and grow in connection with community\. She is committed to student success in all its forms\. She strives to provide a safe space for students to show up just as they are\. She works with each student to identify practical and effective coping strategies that are unique to them\. Students have shared that they felt fully seen, heard and validated in their sessions with her\. Laura also facilitates wellbeing workshops through the [Arts Compass](https://www.arts.ubc.ca/student-support/compass/)\.

[Headshot of Lisa John](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/embedded_counselling_lisa_john.jpg)

#### Lisa John, MEd, RCC \(she/her\)

Lisa is a Registered Clinical Counsellor with a Master of Education in Counselling Psychology from UBC\. Lisa works from a person\-centred and strength\-based therapeutic approach which focuses on bringing awareness to thoughts and felt experiences\. She works collaboratively and seeks to create a safe and supportive space in which students can share, reflect, and integrate their self\-knowledge in ways that are helpful and aligned with their values, needs, and goals\.

[Headshot of Sabina Lupasco](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/embedded_counselling_sabina_lupasco.jpeg)

#### Sabina Lupasco, MEd, RCC \(she/her\)

Sabina is a Registered Clinical Counsellor holding a Master of Education in Counselling Psychology from UBC\. Sabina’s focus in therapy is to create a space where students feel safe, validated, and accepted; where students feel comfortable to share and explore all the parts of their identities, as well as the internal and external barriers preventing them from reaching their goals\. Sabina believes that people get hurt and healed in relationships with others, and her approach includes helping students develop a sense of connection and belonging within themselves and with others\. Sabina’s counselling style integrates person\-centered and strengths\-based approaches\.

[Headshot of Thoko Moyo](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/embedded_counselling_thoko_moyo.jpg)

#### Thoko Moyo, MC, RCC \(she/they\)

Thoko is currently unavailable for counselling\.

Please contact Student Health and Wellbeing at [604 822 3811](tel:6048223811) for counselling options for the scholarship programs\.

[Headshot of Whitney Sedgwick](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/embedded_counselling_whitney_sedgwick.jpg)

#### Whitney Sedgwick, PhD, R\. Psych\. \(she/her\)

Whitney is a Registered psychologist and the Mental Performance/Mental Health lead for UBC Athletics\. She has degrees in sport and clinical psychology and has worked with various sport organizations\. Whitney works collaboratively with students to clarify their concerns, identify their strengths and further their effective coping strategies\. She believes that mental performance skills transfer outside of sport and assists students toward value\-driven lives\. Whitney is also committed to helping students increase their awareness of mental and physical interconnection\. She strives to be compassionate, kind, and genuine and is grateful to work in this role\.

[Headshot of Cassie Smith](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/embedded_counselling_cassie_smith.jpg)

#### Cassie Smith, MC, MBET, RP, CCC

Cassie is a Registered Psychotherapist and Counsellor who serves as the Embedded Counsellor in the Faculty of Pharmaceutical Sciences in addition to her role within the main Student Health and Wellbeing at UBC\. She has spent over a decade working in post\-secondary counselling services at multiple universities with a particular focus on supporting students studying in professional programs\. She is passionate about taking a curious and collaborative approach to her work with students in creating meaningful and sustainable change\.

[Headshot of Nafiza Ali](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/embedded_counselling_nafiza_ali.jpg)

#### Nafiza Ali, MA, RCC \(she/her\)

Nafiza is the embedded counsellor for the Sauder School of Business\. She is a Registered Clinical Counsellor with a Master of Arts in Counselling Psychology from Adler University\. Nafiza is a first\- generation Fijian\-Canadian clinician who believes in authentic and genuine connections to create safety, belonging, and community\. Nafiza takes a person\-centered and strength\-based therapeutic approach where she brings focus to mind and body and encourages student success to come from a place of healthy self\-worth\. Nafiza works collaboratively to create a safe space for her students to explore their wellbeing, ensuring they feel validated, heard, and accepted\. Outside of work, Nafiza loves to explore other countries and cultures and play sports with her husband when she’s not chasing her two wonderful kiddos around\.

[Headshot of Myra Mangadap](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/embedded_counselling_myra_mangadap.jpg)

#### Myra Mangadap, MA PSYCH, RCC

Myra Mangadap is a Registered Clinical Counsellor with experience spanning 26 years across health systems in mental health and substance use\. She has a longstanding passion for, and commitment to diverse populations, rooted in Indigenous and Black communities and knowledge systems\. Myra provides culturally responsive and holistic evidence\-based counselling that is person\-centred, strengths\-based, and honours traditional ways of knowing and cultural identity in healing\. Mindfully, she has chosen a helping profession in mental health, where her actions reflect her belief that access to equitable health services is a human right\. 

[Headshot of Stephanie Seo from embedded counsellors page](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/stephanie_seo_headshot.jpg)

#### Stephanie Seo, MA, RCC

Stephanie is a Registered Clinical Counsellor and the embedded counsellor at the Faculty of Science\. A first\-generation Canadian with a decade of experience supporting post\-secondary students, she is committed to creating a safe, inclusive space where all students feel heard, valued, and supported\. With a humanistic, strength\-based approach, Stephanie provides practical tools to enhance self\-awareness, build resilience, manage stress, and improve overall well\-being\. She is passionate about empowering students to navigate personal, academic, and life challenges while advocating for accessible mental health support in post\-secondary settings\.

[Profile of Danya from Embedded Counselling](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/dayna.jpg)

#### Dayna McCracken MA, RCC \(She/Her\)

Dayna is a Registered Clinical Counsellor, and is the Embedded Counsellor for Faculty of Education and School of Kinesiology students\. Her practice experience has spanned across a variety of settings including universities, government mental health clinics, non\-profit agencies and residential mental health treatment centres\. Dayna strives to offer a warm, safe, caring space where students can express themselves, collaboratively navigate challenges, and feel heard\. She places great importance on each students’ right to self\-determination of personal goals, simultaneously recognizing the colonial systems that are profoundly impacting student health and wellness\. It is paramount in her practice that students feel empowered and enhanced in their sense of peace and clarity\. Outside of work, you might find Dayna wakesurfing, skiing or boarding, singing 90s music or getting lost in an epic fantasy novel\.

[A tree branch dappled with sunlight\. The generic image used for Counselling Services team members who don't have headshots\.](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_services_generic_avatar.jpg)

#### Stephanie Craven, MSW, RSW \(she/her\)

Steph is a Registered Social Worker who holds a Master’s degree in Clinical Social Work from the University of Calgary\. She is dedicated to fostering a supportive and inclusive environment where students can explore their experiences, process emotions, and grow at a pace that feels right for them\. Guided by the values of curiosity, presence, and compassion, she believes that healing emerges through human connection and that every individual is already whole just as they are\. Steph’s approach is grounded in holistic, experiential, and relational methods, integrating mind\-body connection to help students navigate challenges and deepen self\-awareness\.

[Headshot of Fernanda Bruce](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/embedded_counselling_fernanda_bruce.jpg)

#### Fernanda McConnell, MA, RCC

Fernanda is currently unavailable for counselling\.

Please contact Student Health and Wellbeing at [604 822 3811](tel:6048223811) for other counselling options\.

[counselling jackie kopacek](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_jackie_kopacek.jpg)

#### Jackie Kopacek, MCP, RCC \(She/Her\) 

Jackie is a Registered Clinical Counsellor dedicated to providing a warm and collaborative space for personal growth and meaningful change\. Grounded in a strengths\-based, person\-centered therapeutic approach, she values each student’s unique experiences and believes in their innate capacity for development\. She strives to create a safe, inclusive environment where students feel heard, empowered, and supported as they move toward greater well\-being and clarity\.

[counselling elena latushkina](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_elena_latushkina.jpg)

#### Elena Latushkina \(she/her\), PhD, RCC, PCC

Elena is a Registered Clinical Counsellor, Professional Certified Coach, and the Embedded Counsellor for the Graduate and Postdoctoral Education Office in the Faculty of Medicine\. She holds a Master’s degree in Psychology and a Doctorate in Psychological Science\. With a background in psychology research, Elena integrates evidence\-based counselling, strength\-based and solution\-focused coaching into her work, grounded in a person\-centered, responsive, and inclusive approach\. Her practice emphasizes whole\-person, mind–body integration, supporting students in navigating complex challenges, exploring their strengths, building emotional resilience and authentic leadership, fostering deeper connections with themselves and others, and enhancing overall wellbeing\.

[embedded counselling helena morris](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/embedded_counselling_helena_morris.jpg)

#### Helena Morris \(she/her\), MA

Helena received her MA in Counselling at the University of Victoria where she also completed her BA in Psychology\. She has worked in diverse settings including in\-patient treatment programs and acute services as well as public health clinics and private practices\. She has worked with clients of all ages and backgrounds and various presenting concerns but does have a special interest in working with emerging adults and those engaged in education and career development\.

## Leadership Team[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/meet\-the\-counsellors/\#leadership\-team](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/meet-the-counsellors/#leadership-team)

[Headshot of Lauren McBride](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_leadership_lauren_mcbride.jpg)

#### Lauren McBride, EdD, R\. Psych, Director, Student Health and Wellbeing \(she/her\)

Lauren is a Registered Psychologist in British Columbia and the Director of Student Health and Wellbeing\. Her therapeutic approach is grounded in cognitive\-behavioural therapy and draws upon principles of mindfulness and self\-compassion\. Lauren also provides supervision to clinical staff and pre\-doctoral interns\. Her clinical supervision style can be described as developmentally integrative, collaborative, and relational\. Lauren approaches her work with compassion, curiosity and humour\.

[A tree branch dappled with sunlight\. The generic image used for Counselling Services team members who don't have headshots\.](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_services_generic_avatar.jpg)

#### Kirk Beck, PhD, R\. Psych, Associate Director, Training \(he/him\)

Kirk is a Registered Psychologist in British Columbia and the Associate Director, Director of Training\. Kirk has been at Student Health and Wellbeing for the past 25 years and uses a collaborative, student\-centered approach to help others achieve their identified goals\. His clinical practice is grounded in evidence based approaches including cognitive behavioural, narrative, and compassion focused therapy\. Kirk provides clinical supervision to staff and doctoral interns and he works within a developmental and strength\-based model\. Some of Kirk’s clinical and research interests are in ethics/legal issues in counselling, counsellor training and development, decision making, and grief and loss\.

[Headshot of Anna Kline](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_leadership_anna_kline.jpg)

#### Anna Kline, M\. Psych, RCC\-ACS, Associate Director, Embedded Counselling \(she/her\)

Anna is a Registered Clinical Counsellor and an Approved Clinical Supervisor with the BC Association of Clinical Counsellors\. She has a Master of Psychology degree in Counselling Psychology from Monash University in Australia\. As a counsellor, Anna uses a person\-centered perspective believing in unconditional respect for the individual and their experiences\. As a clinical supervisor, Anna works alongside counsellors in a collaborative way to encourage growth\. Anna honours a trusting relationship and strives to build this in all aspects of her work\.

[A tree branch dappled with sunlight\. The generic image used for Counselling Services team members who don't have headshots\.](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_services_generic_avatar.jpg)

#### Longena Ng, PhD, C\. Psych, Associate Director, Equity \(she/her\)

Longena is a Clinical Psychologist and the Associate Director, Equity\. She is a first\-generation Canadian and has worked at various academic hospitals in Canada\. She specializes in the assessment and treatment of posttraumatic stress disorder, anxiety, and mood disorders and operates from a place of cultural humility\. She provides supervision to clinical staff and pre\-doctoral interns\. She takes a developmental and collaborative approach in her work with clients, staff, and trainees\.

[Headshot of Tracy Gard](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/counselling_leadership_tracy_gard.jpg)

#### Tracy Gard, PhD, R\. Psych, Associate Director, Group Counselling \(she/her/hers\)

Tracy is a Registered Psychologist in British Columbia and the Associate Director of Group Counselling at Student Health and Wellbeing\. She has more than 20 years of clinical, supervisory and leadership experience in mental health and substance use treatment\. She is experienced using cognitive behavioral therapy, motivational interviewing, person\-centered therapy, and psychodynamic psychotherapy\. Her clinical and supervisory style is strengths based, and she approaches her work with curiosity, humility, and openness\. She challenges herself to utilize an anti\-oppressive lens in clinical practice, supervision, and program development\.

title: Mental health care at UBC
content_markdown:
## Connect to support[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/\#connect\-to\-support](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/#connect-to-support)

Student Health and Wellbeing is your first point of contact at UBC for all mental health concerns, whether you’d like to see a doctor, a counsellor, or get more information about what’s available\.

Student Health and Wellbeing can help you navigate challenges like:

-   Feeling anxious, depressed, overwhelmed, or noticing changes in your mental health
-   Support when experiencing emotional distress, thoughts of self\-harm, or concerns about safety
-   Relationships \(family, friends, or partners\), grief, or loss
-   Life transitions or cultural adjustment
-   Gender or sexual identity
-   Discrimination or sexual violence
-   Difficulty with concentration, procrastination, or test anxiety
-   Difficulties sleeping
-   Documentation or support related to academic functioning
-   Prescriptions and medication questions
-   Support with ADHD assessment pathways
-   Referrals to psychiatry

If you have a mental health provider you already see within your community, we encourage you to connect with them before booking an appointment with Student Health and Wellbeing\. This can support your continuity of care throughout your time at UBC and after you graduate\.

### Specialized services

Student Health and Wellbeing offers counselling tailored to your identity and background, with mental health professionals who are connected to or have similar lived experiences\.

Our health professionals may be able to work with you in your first language\. Please speak with our Welcome Desk staff about this possibility\.

When making an appointment, you can request:

-   Queer and gender\-affirming counselling
-   Neuro\-affirming care and counselling
-   [Indigenous Mental Health and Wellbeing](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/indigenous-mental-health-wellbeing-program/)
-   Affirming and culturally responsive support for Black students, as well as students from other equity\-deserving communities 
-   Varsity student athlete counselling
-   Counsellors who work closely with and are located in your faculty or program, or counsellors focused on supporting specific identities and students in UBC residences

## Mental health crisis or urgent help[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/\#mental\-health\-crisis\-or\-urgent\-help](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/#mental-health-crisis-or-urgent-help)

If you or someone you know is experiencing severe distress, feeling hopeless, or at risk of harm, get immediate support using one of the options below:

-   Call [911](tel:911)\.
-   Visit the [emergency department](https://www.vch.ca/your-care/emergency-care) at your nearest hospital\.
-   Visit the [UBC Urgent Primary Care Centre](https://www.vch.ca/en/location/ubc-urgent-and-primary-care-centre-upcc/plan-your-visit) during open hours\.
-   Call or chat online with a [crisis line](https://crisiscentre.bc.ca/get-help/)\.
-   Call or text [988](tel:988) toll\-free to reach [Suicide Crisis Helpline](https://988.ca/)\.

Vancouver residents can connect with the [Access and Assessment Centre](https://www.vch.ca/en/location-service/access-and-assessment-centre-aac-vancouver-general-hospital) between 7:30 am and 9:30 pm for walk\-in services, or call between 7:30 am and 10:00 pm\. If you live outside of Vancouver but in British Columbia, you can visit a [Rapid Access Clinic](https://www.fraserhealth.ca/Service-Directory/Services/mental-health-and-substance-use/mental-health---community-services/rapid-access-clinic) in your area\.

## Book an appointment[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/\#book\-an\-appointment](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/#book-an-appointment)

### Visit in person

Drop by the Student Health and Wellbeing Welcome Desk located on **Level 3** of the **Gateway Building** at [5955 University Boulevard](https://maps.app.goo.gl/ULJj4mKNdVSRvBcG6) during opening hours, excluding [statutory holidays](https://hr.ubc.ca/working-ubc/statutory-holidays):

-   **Monday**: 8:00 am to 5:00 pm
-   **Tuesday**: 8:00 am to 5:00 pm
-   **Wednesday**: 8:00 am to 6:00 pm
-   **Thursday**: 8:00 am to 5:00 pm
-   **Friday**: 8:00 am to 5:00 pm

### Call to book

Call [604 822 3811](tel:6048223811) during the opening hours above to schedule an in\-person or virtual appointment\.

### Book online

At this time, online booking is available for faculty, program, or population\-specific counselling appointments, and counsellors in residence\.

Find your faculty, program, or counsellors in residence on the online booking platform\. If it’s not listed, call [604 822 3811](tel:6048223811) to book an appointment\.

[Book online](https://ubcshw.inputhealth.com/ebooking#new/locations)

## Inclusive and equitable care[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/\#inclusive\-and\-equitable\-care](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/#inclusive-and-equitable-care)

### Confidentiality of information

Information you share with Student Health and Wellbeing is confidential\. Your personal health information is protected and is not shared with your faculty or your Workday Student account\.

Aggregate information may be used within Student Health and Wellbeing and shared more broadly at UBC for service planning, quality improvement, and reporting\. This means your information is combined with other students’ information, without names,  to improve programs and services\.

Personal information about you and your health can only be shared outside UBC with your permission, or when safety concerns or legal requirements arise\.

If you have any questions about confidentiality, or anything else, please ask during your appointment\.

### Equitable support for all students

At Student Health and Wellbeing, we respect that students have unique identities, personalities, cultures, and lived experiences\. We strive to bring a culturally responsive, anti\-oppressive, and social justice orientation to the ways we support you\.

Our providers represent a broad diversity of identity and human experience\. We value and respectfully recognize Indigenous history, culture, traditional values, stories, and the lands we work on\. Meet the [counsellors on our team](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/meet-the-counsellors/)\.

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/#additional-resources)

[AMS/GSS student health benefits](https://studentcare.ca/plan/en-CA/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS/understanding-my-coverage)

Students registered in the plan have full coverage for psychotherapy and eligible ADHD, autism, and psychoeducational assessments up to a set amount\.

[International student health benefits](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/)

International students are automatically enrolled in health insurance for the first 6 months of their program, covering a range of health services\.

[Group Counselling](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/)

Connect with other students in a confidential, staff\-facilitated group setting for specific topics throughout the school year\.

[Wellness resources](https://students.ubc.ca/health/wellness-resources/)

Find tools and virtual counselling options you can access whenever you need to, at your own pace\.

[https://stgstudents\.wpenginepowered\.com/health/wellness\-resources/](https://stgstudents.wpenginepowered.com/health/wellness-resources/)[Finding a private counsellor](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/finding-private-counsellor/)

Learn how to choose a private counsellor for long\-term care who matches your needs, preferences, and budget\.

title: Health insurance for domestic students
content_markdown:
## Basic health insurance[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-domestic/\#basic\-health\-insurance](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-domestic/#basic-health-insurance)

If you’re a domestic student, you must have basic health insurance, such as the [British Columbia Medical Services Plan](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents) \(MSP\) or health coverage under another provincial or territorial basic health plan during your studies at UBC\. British Columbian residents are not charged for BC MSP\.

Health care in Canada can cost thousands of dollars per day if you do not have valid health insurance\. Basic health insurance covers doctor visits, hospital visits, and medical tests\. Your health coverage runs for as long as you remain enrolled and eligible for MSP or your home province or territory health plan\.

### How to enrol

Before enrolling, make sure you meet the [eligibility requirements](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents/eligibility-and-enrolment/are-you-eligible) for the plan\.

Some things to consider before you enrol:

-   You can [enrol with BC MSP](http://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents/eligibility-and-enrolment/how-to-enrol) directly\.
-   You may already be covered under one or both of your parents’ plans\.
-   You do not need to switch to MSP if you are covered under another Canadian provincial or territorial health plan, as long as you remain a student\.
-   If you are Canadian but don’t have a provincial health plan, you will need to enrol in the [Global Campus Health Plan](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/global-campus-health-plan/) so you have health coverage while you wait for your BC MSP\.

## Extended health insurance[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-domestic/\#extended\-health\-insurance](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-domestic/#extended-health-insurance)

### AMS/GSS Health and Dental Plan

All UBC students are automatically enrolled in the [AMS/GSS Health and Dental Plan](https://www.ams.ubc.ca/support-services/health-dental/) each year\. You may also enrol in a similar extended health insurance from another source if it provides equivalent coverage to the AMS/GSS Health and Dental Plan\. If you are covered under another extended health insurance, you can opt out of the AMS/GSS Health and Dental Plan during the [opt\-out period](https://www.studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_ChangeofCoverage_ChangeofCoveragePeriod)\.

Under the plan, you can [submit claims](https://studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_Health_HealthCoverage_HealthPractitioners_Psychologists) up to a certain amount for services from a licensed psychologist, registered clinical counsellor, or therapist with a Master’s in Social Work\. The plan also covers psycho\-education assessments, such as ADHD assessments\. Learn how to find a [private mental health professional](https://students.ubc.ca/health/counselling-services/finding-private-counsellor/) for your concerns\.

The AMS/GSS Health and Dental Plan covers the following at an [annual rate](https://www.studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_Cost_HowMuchDoesItCost):

-   [Certain health care](http://www.studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_Health_HealthCoverage&random=487) \(e\.g\., up to 80% of eligible [prescription drugs](http://www.studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_Health_HealthCoverage_PrescriptionDrugs)\)
-   [Dental care](http://www.studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_Dental_DentalCoverage&random=346)
-   [Vision care](http://www.studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_Vision_VisionCoverage&random=909)
-   [Health Practitioner care](http://www.studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_Health_HealthCoverage_HealthPractitioners)
-   [Travel health coverage](http://www.studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_Travel_TravelCoverage&random=956) \(outside of the home country\)

#### Coverage period

-   If you enrol in Term 1, the fee is $338 for 12 months of coverage from September 1, 2023 to August 31, 2024\.
-   New students beginning in Term 2 \(January 2024\) pay a prorated fee of $225\.33 for coverage from January 1 to August 31, 2024\.

Check your [Account Activity](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/viewing-your-financial-account-activity-tuition-amount-and-payments/) in Workday to make sure you’ve been charged for the fees and will be enrolled\.

If you think you should be covered but you are missing the fee, contact the [Care Centre](https://www.studentcare.ca/plan/en-CA/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS/assistance-centre)\.

### BC PharmaCare

If you’re a resident of British Columbia, the [BC PharmaCare program](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/pharmacare-for-bc-residents) helps pay for the cost of certain prescription drugs, pharmacy services, and medical supplies\. 

In most cases, your AMS/GSS Health and Dental Plan will cover up to 80% of eligible prescriptions\. You may also choose to apply for BC Pharmacare to cover more expensive prescriptions for chronic health conditions that are not covered by the AMS/GSS Health and Dental Plan\. It is recommended for most students to apply for the “Fair PharmaCare Plan”\.

title: Health insurance for Non-Status First Nations, Métis, and Inuit students
content_markdown:
## AMS/GSS Health and Dental Coverage at UBC[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-indigenous/health\-insurance\-non\-status\-first\-nations\-metis\-inuit/\#ams\-gss\-health\-and\-dental\-coverage\-at\-ubc](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-indigenous/health-insurance-non-status-first-nations-metis-inuit/#ams-gss-health-and-dental-coverage-at-ubc)

All UBC students are automatically enrolled in the [AMS/GSS Health and Dental Plan](https://www.ams.ubc.ca/support-services/health-dental/) every academic year when they register for courses\. This includes all Indigenous students\. Please review the [fees for the plan](https://www.vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/?tree=14,267,785,0) depending on your coverage period\.

Get more information about the AMS/GSS Plan:

-   [Pay\-Direct Card print\-out](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/pay-direct_card_print-out.pdf) \(pdf\)
-   [AMS Health Care coverage](https://www.studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_DownloadCentre_YourPlanataGlance)
-   [Couple and Family Enrolment](https://studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_ChangeofCoverage_CoupleFamilyEnrolments)
-   [Studentcare Assistance contact](https://www.studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_NeedHelp_ContactUs)

### Opting out of the fee

Some students have extended health coverage through other plans, and therefore choose to opt out of the AMS/GSS Health and Dental Plan\. If you choose to do so, make sure to opt out of the plan during the [change\-of\-coverage period](https://www.studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_ChangeofCoverage_ChangeofCoveragePeriod)\. You are required to do this **every year** at the start of term\.

If you are a sponsored student covered by your band for tuition and living expenses, it’s likely that they won’t cover this additional health coverage fee for you\. Please connect with your Education Coordinator through your band regarding potential coverage for this fee\. If they don’t cover it, please opt out or be prepared to cover this fee yourself\.

If you’ve missed the deadline to opt out, please contact the Indigenous Student Support team at [es\.indigenous@ubc\.ca](mailto:es.indigenous@ubc.ca)\.

### Staying enrolled on the plan

Depending on your health and dental needs and costs, you may decide that it could be worthwhile to have coverage through both your Indigenous Health Authority and the AMS/GSS Health and Dental plan\. In this case, you can have reimbursements of health costs from both insurance providers\.

Example situations where you may want to be covered for both plans:

-   You need prescription glasses or contacts\.
-   You often get medical prescriptions\.
-   You have ongoing health concerns\.
-   You want to maximize chiropractor, physiotherapist, or massage therapy benefits\.
-   You have dental concerns\.
-   You are planning to travel or go on exchange\.

## Maximizing your coverage[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-indigenous/health\-insurance\-non\-status\-first\-nations\-metis\-inuit/\#maximizing\-your\-coverage](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-indigenous/health-insurance-non-status-first-nations-metis-inuit/#maximizing-your-coverage)

To make sure you’re getting the most out of your extended health care coverage, consider asking your doctor, dentist, optometrist, or medical provider the following questions:

-   Are you registered with Pacific Blue Cross or PharmaCare?
-   Do you require payment upfront for services?

### If you have more than one health insurance plan

When students have access to another third\-party health insurance, such as AMS/GSS Health and Dental coverage, they should submit claims to that plan first\. One exception is the pharmacy benefit, where clients should submit claims to PharmaCare first\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-indigenous/health\-insurance\-non\-status\-first\-nations\-metis\-inuit/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-indigenous/health-insurance-non-status-first-nations-metis-inuit/#if-you-have-questions)

For information about the AMS/GSS Health and Dental plan, contact the [AMS/GSS Studentcare Team](https://www.studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_NeedHelp_ContactUs)\.

title: Health insurance for Status First Nations students
content_markdown:
## If you’re a British Columbia resident[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-indigenous/health\-insurance\-status\-first\-nations/\#if\-youre\-a\-british\-columbia\-resident](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-indigenous/health-insurance-status-first-nations/#if-youre-a-british-columbia-resident)

As a UBC student, you are required to have basic medical insurance and extended health care insurance so that you have health coverage when you need it\. The First Nations Health Authority \(FNHA\) covers the basic BC Medical Services Plan \(MSP\) and other extended health insurance coverage for Status First Nations students\.

If you’re not currently enrolled, you can read the FNHA Health Benefits [eligibility and enrolment details](https://www.fnha.ca/benefits/eligibility)\. The Health Benefits Program provides clients with back\-dated coverage of unpaid MSP premiums up to a maximum of five years\. Call Health Benefits at [1 855 550 5454](tel:1%20855%20550%205454) for help with unpaid MSP premiums\.

For a full list of exclusions under the FNHA Health Benefits Program, read the [FNHA Health Benefits Information Package](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/fnha_health_benefits_guide.pdf) \(pdf\)\.

MSP covers regular doctor’s appointments, hospital visits, some lab and x\-ray services, and surgeries performed in a hospital\. You can use your Care Card when accessing these health services\.

In addition to covering your BC Medical Services Plan \(MSP\) as your basic health insurance, the FNHA Health Benefits Program provides full or partial coverage of your extended health needs, including:

-   **Ambulance invoices**: Trips in an ambulance to go to the hospital
-   **Pharmacy**: Prescription medication
-   **Vision**: Eye exams, glasses, and contact lenses
-   **Dental**: Yearly dental visits and teeth cleaning
-   **Medical supplies and equipment**: Crutches, walking boot, and supplies after surgery
-   **Medical transportation**
-   **Mental health support**: Psychologist or counsellor visits

FNHA Health Benefits do not cover physiotherapy, chiropractic treatment, massage therapy, naturopathy, or other paramedical or supplementary services\.

Find more information about FNHA Health Benefits:

-   [FNHA Health coverage details](https://www.fnha.ca/benefits/coverage-details)
-   [Health Benefits Guide](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/fnha_health_benefits_guide.pdf) \(pdf\)
-   [Mental Health and Counselling Benefit and programs](https://www.fnha.ca/benefits/mental-health)
-   [FNHA Mental Health Provider List](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/fnha_first_nations_health_benefits_mental_health_provider_list.pdf) \(pdf\)

### Confirming your Health Benefits enrolment

If you’d like to confirm whether you’re enrolled in the Health Benefits, or if you’d like to register for the first time, please have your status number ready and call [1 855 550 5454](tel:1%20855%20550%205454) or email [healthbenefits@fnha\.ca](mailto:healthbenefits@fnha.ca)\.

## If you’re not a British Columbia resident[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-indigenous/health\-insurance\-status\-first\-nations/\#if\-youre\-not\-a\-british\-columbia\-resident](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-indigenous/health-insurance-status-first-nations/#if-youre-not-a-british-columbia-resident)

If you’re a Status First Nations student arriving from a Canadian province or territory outside of British Columbia, there are certain steps you’ll need to take: 

-   Have your status number, date of birth, school start date, and expected graduation date ready, then call the BC First Nations Health Authority \(FNHA\) Eligibility Team at [1 855 550 5454](tel:18555505454)\.
-   Contact the health services plan from your respective province or territory to ensure that you have active health services while studying in British Columbia \(BC\)\. You are **not** eligible for BC Medical Services Plan \(MSP\) in British Columbia as you are not a BC resident\.
-   Inform providers, such as pharmacists, dentists, and eye doctors, that you are an out\-of\-province resident\. Providers will need to access benefits through Health Canada for services\.

### What the First Nations Health Authority will do

Once you call the BC First Nations Health Authority Eligibility team, they will advise Indigenous Services Canada that you are an out\-of\-province resident studying in BC\.

FNHA will request for you to be added to the Non\-Insured Health Benefits Safelist \(NIHB\)\. The NIHB Safelist will enable you to claim services in British Columbia with no issues\.

## AMS/GSS Health and Dental Coverage at UBC[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-indigenous/health\-insurance\-status\-first\-nations/\#ams\-gss\-health\-and\-dental\-coverage\-at\-ubc](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-indigenous/health-insurance-status-first-nations/#ams-gss-health-and-dental-coverage-at-ubc)

All UBC students are automatically enrolled in the [AMS/GSS Health and Dental Plan](https://www.ams.ubc.ca/support-services/health-dental/) every academic year when they register for courses\. This includes all Indigenous students\. Please review the [fees for the plan](https://www.vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/?tree=14,267,785,0) depending on your coverage period\.

Get more information about the AMS/GSS Plan:

-   [Pay Direct\-Card print\-out](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/pay-direct_card_print-out.pdf) \(pdf\)
-   [AMS Health Care coverage](https://www.studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_DownloadCentre_YourPlanataGlance)
-   [Couple and Family Enrolment](https://studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_ChangeofCoverage_CoupleFamilyEnrolments)
-   [Studentcare Assistance contact](https://www.studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_NeedHelp_ContactUs)

### Opting out of the fee

Some students have extended health coverage through other plans, and therefore choose to opt out of the AMS/GSS Health and Dental Plan\. If you choose to do so, make sure to opt out of the plan during the [change\-of\-coverage period](https://www.studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_ChangeofCoverage_ChangeofCoveragePeriod)\.You are required to do this **every year** at the start of term\. You may use your status card as proof of other coverage during the opt\-out process\. 

If you are a sponsored student covered by your band for tuition and living expenses, it’s likely that they won’t cover this additional health coverage fee for you\. Please connect with your Education Coordinator through your band regarding potential coverage for this fee\. If they don’t cover it, please opt out or be prepared to cover this fee yourself\.

If you’ve missed the deadline to opt out, please contact the Indigenous Student Support team at [es\.indigenous@ubc\.ca](mailto:es.indigenous@ubc.ca)\.

### Staying enrolled on the plan

Depending on your health and dental needs and costs, you may decide that it could be worthwhile to have coverage through both your Indigenous Health Authority and the AMS/GSS Health and Dental plan\. In this case, you can have reimbursements of health costs from both insurance providers\.

Example situations where you may want to be covered for both plans:

-   You need prescription glasses or contacts\.
-   You often get medical prescriptions\.
-   You have ongoing health concerns\.
-   You want to maximize chiropractor, physiotherapist, or massage therapy benefits\.
-   You have dental concerns\.
-   You are planning to travel or go on exchange\.

## Maximizing your coverage[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-indigenous/health\-insurance\-status\-first\-nations/\#maximizing\-your\-coverage](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-indigenous/health-insurance-status-first-nations/#maximizing-your-coverage)

To make sure you’re getting the most out of your extended health care coverage, consider asking your doctor, dentist, optometrist, or medical provider the following questions:

-   Are you registered with Pacific Blue Cross, PharmaCare, or FNHA direct billing?
-   Do you require payment upfront for services?

### If you have more than one health insurance plan

When students have access to another third\-party health insurance, such as AMS/GSS Health and Dental coverage, they should submit claims to that plan first and then to FNHA Health Benefits\. One exception is the pharmacy benefit, where clients should submit claims to PharmaCare first\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-indigenous/health\-insurance\-status\-first\-nations/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-indigenous/health-insurance-status-first-nations/#if-you-have-questions)

Please contact the [First Nations Health Authority](https://www.fnha.ca/contact-us) for questions about the FNHA Health Benefits\.

For information about the AMS/GSS Health and Dental plan, contact the [AMS/GSS Studentcare Team](https://www.studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_NeedHelp_ContactUs)\.

title: Health insurance for international students
content_markdown:
## About health insurance[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/\#about\-health\-insurance](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/#about-health-insurance)

In Canada, medical care can be extremely expensive if you don’t have insurance and have to pay from your own pocket\. Health insurance is a plan that will pay some or all of the cost of medical treatment in Canada if you get sick or injured\. You pay a monthly, annual, or one\-time fee for this coverage\.

All international students are required to have basic and extended health insurance for the duration of their studies at UBC\.

In addition, accompanying family members should have appropriate basic and extended health insurance coverage for the duration of their stay in Canada\.

## Overview of health insurance[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/\#overview\-of\-health\-insurance](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/#overview-of-health-insurance)

All UBC international students will need 2 kinds of health insurance:

-   Basic health insurance
-   Extended health insurance

### Basic health insurance

Basic health insurance covers most medically required services, such as doctor’s visits, hospital visits, and medically required services provided by a provincially licensed physician\.

#### iMED temporary health insurance

iMED, provided by GuardMe, covers your first 3 months in British Columbia until you become eligible for the BC provincial health plan, the Medical Services Plan of BC \(MSP\)\. 

If you are a visiting or exchange student who will study in Canada for less than 6 months, you will be covered by iMED for the duration of your studies\.

All new\-to\-UBC international students are automatically enrolled in the plan, and no application is required\.

[Learn about iMED](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international/)

#### Medical Services Plan of BC \(MSP\)

The British Columbia public health insurance plan, [BC MSP](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/), is required for everyone who lives in BC for 6 months or longer\. MSP covers the cost of basic medical care within Canada, including most physician and hospital services\.

You will need to [apply for MSP](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/apply-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/) after arriving in BC\. If you extend your study permit at any point, you’ll also need to apply to extend your MSP then\. 

[Read about MSP](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/)

### Extended health insurance

Extended health insurance covers some fees and services not covered by basic health insurance, such as vision and dental care, some prescription drugs, and private mental health services\.

The [AMS/GSS Health and Dental Plan](https://www.studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_Home) is an extended health insurance plan designed to cover some fees and services not covered by iMED\.

Most students are enrolled in the plan automatically for the duration of their studies\. However, if you are an exchange student or if you’re starting your studies in the summer, you’ll need to [self\-enrol in the plan](https://www.studentcare.ca/rte/en/SelfEnrolment%2811%29)\. 

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/#additional-resources)

-   [iMED: Temporary health insurance for international students](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international/)
-   [BC Medical Services Plan \(MSP\)](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/)
-   [AMS/GSS Health and Dental Plan](http://www.studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_Home)
-   [Health and wellbeing support options](https://students.ubc.ca/health)
