title: iMED: Temporary health insurance for international students
content_markdown:
GuardMe Enhanced@UBC iMED is a temporary basic health insurance plan for international students who are new to UBC\. At UBC, the plan is referred to simply as iMED\. Managed by [GuardMe](https://guard.me/en.html), iMED provides international students with basic health insurance during the three\-month waiting period before you qualify for the British Columbia government\-run [Medical Services Plan](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/) \(MSP\), or for the duration of your studies if your program is shorter than 6 months, such as a one\-term exchange program\.

iMED covers emergency hospitalization and required medical services for an unexpected sickness or injury, including treatment at a doctor’s clinic\. Full details of what is covered by iMED can be found on the Policy Wording document in your [GuardMe account](https://www.guard.me/login.php)\.

Learn more about [health insurance for international students](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/), including the differences between iMED, MSP, and the AMS/GSS Health and Dental Plan\.

## Eligibility for iMED[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/imed\-temporary\-health\-insurance\-international/\#eligibility\-for\-imed](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international/#eligibility-for-imed)

All new international students who are charged AMS/GSS student fees, as well as Go Global exchange and Visiting International Research students \(VIRS\), are eligible and automatically enrolled in iMED when they register in their first on\-campus, in\-person course\. 

Domestic students, including Canadian citizens and permanent residents, and students who are registered only in off\-campus courses are not eligible to be covered by iMED\.

Check your [financial account activity](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/viewing-your-financial-account-activity-tuition-amount-and-payments/) in Workday to confirm you are charged for iMED\. You will receive a welcome email from GuardMe with detailed information about the plan before your coverage begins\. 

If you’re enrolled at UBC, but are not eligible for iMED, you may need to purchase private temporary insurance to cover you until you qualify for MSP\. Contact [GuardMe](https://sites.guard.me/ubc/contact) to discuss your options\.  

## iMED costs[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/imed\-temporary\-health\-insurance\-international/\#imed\-costs](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international/#imed-costs)

The cost for your iMED coverage depends on the length of your program or studies at UBC\.

Your iMED fee will be charged as a part of your student fees, which you can [view in your Workday account](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/viewing-your-financial-account-activity-tuition-amount-and-payments/)\. Please note that the direct billing fee applies only to UBC Vancouver students\.

**

Students in programs of study that are longer than 6 months

**

iMED costs **$204\.30** for three months of coverage, plus a one\-time direct billing fee of $11\.15\.

This amount also applies to degree\-seeking students, two\-term exchange students, and VIRS students studying more than 6 months\.

**

One\-term exchange or one\-term non\-degree students

**

For the 2026/27 academic year, iMED costs **$295\.10** for 130 days of coverage, plus a one\-time direct billing fee of $11\.15\.

**

Visiting International Research Students \(VIRS\) studying 6 months or less

**

iMED is available on a monthly basis and costs **$68\.10** per month, plus a one\-time direct billing fee of $11\.15\.

## Coverage dates[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/imed\-temporary\-health\-insurance\-international/\#coverage\-dates](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international/#coverage-dates)

The details of your coverage dates and how to change them depend on the length of your program or studies at UBC\.

**

Students in programs of study that are longer than 6 months

**

This information also applies to degree\-seeking students, two\-term exchange students, and VIRS students studying more than 6 months\.

iMED is designed to cover you during the waiting period before you become eligible for the British Columbia government\-run [Medical Services Plan](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/) \(MSP\)\. The MSP waiting period includes the remainder of the month you arrive in BC, plus the next 2 calendar months\. For example, if you arrived in BC on Aug 19, you would be eligible for MSP on Nov 1\.

Your iMED coverage dates depend on when you start your program:

-   Winter Term 1 \(Sep to Dec\): coverage starts on Aug 10
-   Winter Term 2 \(Jan to Apr\): coverage starts on Dec 10
-   Summer Session \(May to Aug\): coverage starts on Apr 10

Check the iMED coverage dates on your iMED card to ensure they’re consistent with your planned arrival date\.

Note that VIRS students’ coverage will depend on when your research period begins\.

If you are a Go Global exchange student or a VIRS student, please connect directly with [Go Global](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/contact) if you need to change your coverage dates\. 

For all other students, if you plan to arrive in Canada before the earliest iMED coverage start date available for your UBC program \(e\.g\., your coverage starts Aug 10, but you arrive in July\), you should purchase [Early Arrival coverage](https://sites.guard.me/ubc/department/international-students/early-arrivals) directly from GuardMe\.

If you plan to arrive in Canada in the calendar month **after** your iMED coverage starts \(e\.g\., your coverage starts Aug 10 but you arrive in September\), you must [submit a date change request](https://sites.guard.me/ubc/page/international-students/date-change-request) to have your iMED coverage shifted to cover your 3\-month waiting period for MSP\.

**

One\-term exchange or one\-term non\-degree students

**

One\-term exchange or non\-degree students have iMED coverage for a period of 130 days, equivalent to one academic term\. The duration of iMED coverage takes the move\-in date for UBC residence into consideration\.

Your iMED coverage dates are based on the academic term you’re enrolled in:

-   Winter Session Term 1 \(Sep to Dec 2026\): Aug 26, 2026 to Jan 2, 2027
-   Winter Session Term 2 \(Jan to Apr 2027\): Dec 23, 2026 to May 1, 2027

Your iMED coverage dates are fixed and cannot be changed\. However, you can purchase additional days of coverage directly from GuardMe if you will arrive in BC before, or leave after, the dates indicated above\. 

To discuss your options and purchase additional days of coverage, [contact GuardMe](https://sites.guard.me/ubc/contact) directly or log into your [GuardMe account](https://myaccount.guard.me/login.php)\.

**

Visiting International Research Students \(VIRS\) studying 6 months or less

**

A monthly rate is available for VIRS students, and you will have iMED coverage for the duration of the research period\. 

The start date of your iMED coverage depends on when your research period begins\. UBC will automatically assess the iMED coverage period based on your program and your research period at UBC\. Check your iMED coverage dates in [your account](https://myaccount.guard.me/login.php) and ensure they are correct\.

If you need to shift your program start or end dates, or you plan to arrive in Canada before your coverage start date, please reach out directly to [Go Global](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/contact) for assistance\. 

## Logging into your GuardMe account[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/imed\-temporary\-health\-insurance\-international/\#logging\-into\-your\-guardme\-account](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international/#logging-into-your-guardme-account)

Once you register for your courses, you will be automatically enrolled in iMED and receive a welcome email from GuardMe within 2 to 4 weeks of your program start date\. Be sure to check your spam folder\.

Follow the instructions in your welcome email to log into your account and download your card\. In your GuardMe account for iMED, you can review your coverage, submit a claim, and view other important information\.

During your coverage period, print your iMED card and keep it with you in case you need medical attention, along with your student ID and a copy of your study permit, if you have one\. You can also access your card through the [GuardMe mobile app](https://news.guard.me/GuardMe_Mobile_App.html)\. 

## Accessing health care services with iMED[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/imed\-temporary\-health\-insurance\-international/\#accessing\-health\-care\-services\-with\-imed](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international/#accessing-health-care-services-with-imed)

Students covered under iMED may seek medical care at any licensed medical clinic or hospital\. Medical expenses that are eligible under the iMED policy can be submitted to GuardMe either directly by the medical facility, or by you\. You are usually billed for treatment at a hospital after you are discharged from the hospital \(e\.g\., when you have finished treatment\), while you will likely be asked to pay up front for consultations with a doctor\.

If you need care, you should always show your iMED card and your study permit \(if you have one\) when you’re being admitted and ask if the hospital or clinic will agree to bill expenses to GuardMe\. You must also [contact GuardMe](https://sites.guard.me/ubc/contact) immediately with the policy number on your iMED card if you are being admitted to a hospital\.

If you need to pay out of pocket for medical services, or you receive an invoice from a clinic or hospital, you will need to [submit a claim](https://guard.me/en/submit-a-claim.html) through your account or the GuardMe mobile app to request reimbursement\.

On the mobile app or [GuardMe site](https://sites.guard.me/ubc/clinicSearch/), you can search for a clinic that bills to GuardMe directly, as well as view their live wait times, hours, and contact details\.

### Additional health care services

GuardMe provides a [Mobile Doctor](https://www.guard.me/en/mobile-doctor.html) service which offers you 24/7 access to Canadian doctors via Maple on your phone, tablet, or computer\. This is a fast and convenient way to access medical care in minutes, even when outside of Canada\.

You can also access the [Student Support Program](https://sites.guard.me/ubc/gmssp) for 24/7, culturally\-matched, and confidential mental health support for any challenges you may be experiencing\. This program is available during your entire first year at UBC, even after your iMED coverage ends\.

### Important tips

-   If you are hospitalized, you or someone on your behalf must [contact GuardMe customer care](https://sites.guard.me/ubc/contact) immediately with the policy number on your iMED card\. Coverage for certain medical services requires that you contact GuardMe to request pre\-authorization\. Examples include surgery, specialist consultation, and specialized diagnostic tests like an MRI or CT scan\.
-   Carry a photocopy or digital copy of your study permit, if you have one\. You must present a copy of your study permit with your iMED card if you are treated at a hospital to ensure you are billed fees as a British Columbia resident\.
-   You don’t have to hold a study permit to use your iMED plan\. If you and/or your dependents are in Canada as a visitor or worker and you and/or your dependents are enrolled in iMED, bring your iMED card, photo ID, and any immigration documents you have when seeking medical services\.

## If you withdraw from or defer your program[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/imed\-temporary\-health\-insurance\-international/\#if\-you\-withdraw\-from\-or\-defer\-your\-program](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international/#if-you-withdraw-from-or-defer-your-program)

If you decide to withdraw from your studies, or defer your program to another academic term, it’s important to [drop your courses](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/) before the [registration add/drop deadline](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/dates-deadlines/) for the term in order to receive a refund on your tuition and student fees\. 

If you drop your courses before the add/drop deadline, your iMED fees will be refunded to you along with your other fees\. If you register for courses in a future term, you will automatically be enrolled in iMED once you register in courses\.

## Enrolling your family in iMED[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/imed\-temporary\-health\-insurance\-international/\#enrolling\-your\-family\-in\-imed](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international/#enrolling-your-family-in-imed)

Your spouse, partner, or dependent children can also be covered by iMED for the duration of their stay or until they qualify for MSP\. You can [purchase iMED for them](https://sites.guard.me/ubc/dependents/dependents/current-students) directly through GuardMe\. If you aren’t currently covered by iMED, GuardMe offers other [health insurance options](https://sites.guard.me/ubc/department/dependents/students-with-msp) for your dependents\. 

## Opting out of iMED[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/imed\-temporary\-health\-insurance\-international/\#opting\-out\-of\-imed](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international/#opting-out-of-imed)

It is mandatory to have basic health insurance coverage while enrolled at UBC\. If you meet the eligibility criteria, you may be able to [opt out of iMED](https://sites.guard.me/ubc/optout/international-students/opt-out) by submitting a request before the deadline\. Go Global exchange and VIRS students should contact [Go Global](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/contact) directly for information about opting out\. 

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/imed\-temporary\-health\-insurance\-international/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international/#if-you-have-questions)

-   To learn more about your iMED insurance policy, how to understand and use your coverage, and how to access medical care, review the [GuardMe Virtual Orientation](https://guard.me/en/virtual-orientation---guardme-.html) or the policy overview available in your [GuardMe account](https://myaccount.guard.me/login.php)\.
-   For questions about your iMED coverage, getting your iMED card, enrolling family members, or submitting claims, contact [GuardMe customer care](https://sites.guard.me/ubc/contact) by chat, phone, or email\.
-   If you have other questions related to international health insurance, connect with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/)\. Go Global exchange students and VIRS students should contact [Go Global](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/contact) for support\.
-   UBC Okanagan students should contact the [UBC\-O International Student Advising office](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/international/international-student-advising/) with any questions or concerns\. 
-   For questions about your student fees, payments or refunds, contact [Enrolment Services](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

## International Student Guide[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/imed\-temporary\-health\-insurance\-international/\#international\-student\-guide](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international/#international-student-guide)

Find everything you need to know about life as an international student at UBC’s Vancouver campus\.

[View the guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/)

title: Medical Services Plan (MSP) for international students
content_markdown:
## About the BC Medical Services Plan \(MSP\)[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/medical\-services\-plan\-msp\-international/\#about\-the\-bc\-medical\-services\-plan\-msp](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/#about-the-bc-medical-services-plan-msp)

The British Columbia \(BC\) government Medical Services Plan \(BC MSP\) is a mandatory public health insurance plan for everyone who lives in BC for 6 months or longer\. Applying for the BC MSP allows you to benefit from the health care available to all BC residents\. The plan covers the cost of basic medical care within Canada, including most physician and hospital services\. If you are not enrolled, you will have to pay for medical expenses independently\.

See [health insurance for international students](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/) to learn about the differences between iMED, MSP, and the AMS/GSS Health and Dental Plan\.

## Who is eligible and how do I apply? [https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/medical\-services\-plan\-msp\-international/\#who\-is\-eligible\-and\-how\-do\-i\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/#who-is-eligible-and-how-do-i-apply) 

If you will live in BC for **6 months or longer**, you are required by law to enrol in MSP\. If you are a study permit holder, you’re required to pay the plan’s health\-care coverage fee\.

You must apply for MSP **as soon as you arrive in BC**\. You cannot apply for MSP before you arrive\.

You can apply for the Fair PharmaCare plan to enhance your coverage at the same time you apply for MSP\. Check the “[Register for BC PharmaCare](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/#register-for-bc-fair-pharmacare)” section below for details\.

[Apply for MSP](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/apply-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/)

## When am I covered? [https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/medical\-services\-plan\-msp\-international/\#when\-am\-i\-covered](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/#when-am-i-covered) 

There is a 3\-month waiting period before MSP coverage begins: this is the balance of the month in which you arrive in British Columbia \(BC\), plus two full calendar months\. For example, if you arrive in BC on August 25, you are eligible for MSP coverage starting November 1\.

To cover the waiting period for MSP, most new\-to\-UBC international students are covered by [iMED health insurance](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international/) for their first 3 months in Canada\. Returning international students who no longer have iMED are advised to purchase private temporary health insurance, such as the [GuardMe Canada plan](https://sites.guard.me/ubc/department/interim-coverage)\.

BC MSP coverage will be provided to the same expiry date as your status in Canada \(such as your study or work permit\), unless you [leave BC for an extended period](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international#msp-coverage-outside-of-bc)\.

If you extend your study permit or get a Post\-Graduation Work Permit, you must apply to [extend your MSP online](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/extend-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/), otherwise you will not be covered\. 

If you applied for a new study or work permit and your study permit expires before you receive it, you will have [maintained status](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/maintained-status/)\. It’s important to take action and request [temporary MSP coverage](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international#how-having-maintained-status-impacts-your-msp-coverage) while under maintained status\.

## MSP coverage fees[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/medical\-services\-plan\-msp\-international/\#msp\-coverage\-fees](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/#msp-coverage-fees)

All study permit holders are charged a $75 health\-care coverage fee per month called [the International Student Health Fee](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/accessing-health-care/health-fee-international-students)\. You will receive a bill from the British Columbia government, and must pay the [BC government](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/accessing-health-care/health-fee-international-students/pay) directly\. The fee is not included in your UBC student fees\. You can [pay online](https://billing-and-payment.revenueservicesbc.gov.bc.ca/international-student-health-fee) and set up online services, such as seeing your balance, setting up paperless invoicing, and autopayments\.

If your family is with you in Canada, they will only be charged the new health\-care coverage fee if they also hold study permits\. If they hold work permits or are here as visitors, they will not be charged the fee\.

The fees are subject to change\. Check the [MSP website](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/accessing-health-care/health-fee-international-students) for the most up\-to\-date information\.

### Changing from study permit to Post\-Graduation Work Permit \(PGWP\)

Even if your MSP coverage has not expired, once you get your PGWP, [contact MSP by phone](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents-contact-us) to receive instructions for updating your account and removing the international student health fee\. As a work permit holder, you do not need to pay the health\-care coverage fee\.  

## Getting your MSP card[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/medical\-services\-plan\-msp\-international/\#getting\-your\-msp\-card](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/#getting-your-msp-card)

When your application is processed, your MSP card, or [BC Services Card](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/governments/government-id/bc-services-card) \(formerly known as “BC CareCard”\), will be mailed to the address you provided in your application\. Your BC Services Card will indicate your coverage period, which should match the expiration date of your status in Canada \(such as your study or work permit\)\. Note that your card will not include your photo if you are a study or work permit holder, or are under the age of majority in BC, which is 19 years old\.

## Using your MSP insurance[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/medical\-services\-plan\-msp\-international/\#using\-your\-msp\-insurance](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/#using-your-msp-insurance)

In most cases, you will not have to pay at the time you seek care for medically required services when you show your BC Services Card\. 

MSP does not cover dental care, prescription drugs, routine vision care such as eye examinations or corrective lenses, or travel\. The [AMS/GSS Extended Health and Dental Plan](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/#extended-health-insurance-ams-gss-health-and-dental-plan) is designed to cover some of these costs\.

See a full list of your [medical and health care benefits](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents/benefits) provided by MSP\.

In general, you should go to clinics for non\-urgent medical care, and hospitals for emergencies\. For emergencies and for an ambulance, call 911\. Learn about when to go to an [Emergency Department](https://www.vch.ca/en/health-topics/emergency-care) or Urgent & Primary Care Centre, [finding services in BC](https://www.healthlinkbc.ca/health-services/search-services-your-area), and explore the [BC Newcomers’ Guide](https://www.welcomebc.ca/Start-Your-Life-in-B-C/Newcomers-Guides) to learn about healthcare in BC, which is available in 13 languages\. You can also call 811 to reach [Health Link BC](https://www.healthlinkbc.ca/find-care/healthlink-bc-8-1-1-services) 24/7 for assistance and to speak to healthcare professionals such as a nurse\.  

UBC’s [Student Health Service](https://students.ubc.ca/health/student-health-service/) offers a range of health assessments and treatments on\-campus\.

## Register for BC Fair PharmaCare[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/medical\-services\-plan\-msp\-international/\#register\-for\-bc\-fair\-pharmacare](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/#register-for-bc-fair-pharmacare)

It is recommended for most students to register for the [BC Fair PharmaCare program](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/pharmacare-for-bc-residents/who-we-cover/fair-pharmacare-plan#eligibility), which may provide additional coverage for prescription drugs, medical devices and pharmacy services\. BC Fair PharmaCare registration may be required for [prescription coverage](https://www.studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_Health_HealthCoverage_PrescriptionDrugs_BCFairPharmaCare) through the AMS/GSS Health and Dental plan\.

Since coverage is based on income, the application requires proof of your previous income based on taxes filed in Canada 2 years ago\. If you are a new resident of Canada, recently turned 19, or were exempt from filing taxes in Canada 2 years ago, you might be able to submit a [Fair PharmaCare Proof of Income Affidavit](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/assets/gov/health/forms/5357fil.pdf)—[contact MSP](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents-contact-us) for assistance\.

You can register for the BC Fair PharmaCare plan at the same time you [apply for MSP](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/apply-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/)\. It is also possible to [register for Fair PharmaCare](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/pharmacare-for-bc-residents/who-we-cover/fair-pharmacare-plan) separately\.

You need to provide a [Social Insurance Number \(SIN\)](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/) to apply\. If you don’t have a SIN yet, consider applying for MSP separately as soon as you arrive in BC, then register for Fair PharmaCare once you have your SIN\.

If you have questions about enrollment with Fair PharmaCare, [contact MSP](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents-contact-us)\.

## Once your MSP coverage begins[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/medical\-services\-plan\-msp\-international/\#once\-your\-msp\-coverage\-begins](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/#once-your-msp-coverage-begins)

MSP will send you an invoice in the mail each month\. You need to [start making payments](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/accessing-health-care/health-fee-international-students/pay) after you receive the invoice\.

Remember to tell MSP if you change your address, change your name, leave BC permanently, or need to add/remove dependents to or from your coverage \(for example you get married, divorced, have a common\-law partner, or have children\)\. See the [Managing your MSP Account page](http://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents/managing-your-msp-account)\.

Remember to keep your MSP valid by [extending yo](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/extend-bc-medical-services-plan-msp)[ur MSP](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/extend-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/) coverage each time you extend your temporary residency in Canada \(for example, when you extend your study permit or get a Post\-Graduation Work Permit\)\. Be sure to understand how [having maintained status](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/#how-having-maintained-status-impacts-your-msp-coverage) can affect your coverage, if your study or work permit will expire while you are in Canada\.

## Maintaining your MSP coverage[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/medical\-services\-plan\-msp\-international/\#maintaining\-your\-msp\-coverage](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/#maintaining-your-msp-coverage)

Generally, your MSP coverage will have the same expiry date as your status in Canada, such as the expiry date of your study permit or Post\-Graduation Work Permit\. 

If you extend your immigration documents, make sure you extend your MSP coverage as soon as you get your new study or work permit\.

[Extend your MSP](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/extend-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/)

## How having maintained status impacts your MSP coverage[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/medical\-services\-plan\-msp\-international/\#how\-having\-maintained\-status\-impacts\-your\-msp\-coverage](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/#how-having-maintained-status-impacts-your-msp-coverage)

You will have “[maintained status](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/maintained-status/)” \(formerly called “implied status”\) if all of the following applies to you:

-   You applied for a new immigration document, such as a study or work permit, before the old one expired\.
-   You won’t receive a new immigration document before your old one expires\.
-   You remain in Canada beyond the expiry of your old documents\.

### If you are waiting for your study permit extension or Post\-Graduation Work Permit \(PGWP\)

**

Before you get your new immigration document

**

If you have applied to renew your study permit or applied for a PGWP before your study permit expired and you are still waiting for the approval while your current study permit has expired, you have “maintained status” and can legally stay in Canada\. You should [call MSP](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents-contact-us) to request [temporary coverage](https://news.gov.bc.ca/releases/2022HLTH0132-000679#:~:text=Effective%20May%201%2C%202022%2C%20Medical,on%20their%20application%20for%20extension.) for an initial 6 months while you are on maintained status\. This is particularly important if you have a pre\-existing condition which may not be covered by private health insurance, such as pregnancy\.

Separately, if you currently take prescription medications that are classified as [Controlled Prescription Program Drugs,](https://www.bcpharmacists.org/cpp) pharmacies may refuse to dispense your prescription if you do not have an active personal health number, even if you have private insurance\. 

Temporary health insurance coverage with MSP is available to those on maintained status who meet [MSP’s eligibility requirements](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents/eligibility-and-enrolment/are-you-eligible/maintained-status-holders)\. This also applies to your dependents who are currently residents of BC\. 

**If MSP approves your request for temporary coverage**  
Ask them to confirm your coverage start and end date\. If you and your family members are study permit holders, you will continue to be charged the monthly healthcare coverage fee\. 

You will need to submit an [MSP extension application](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/extend-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/) and provide all of the following documents instead of a copy of your study or work permit:

-   A letter written by yourself explaining your status and your request for temporary coverage, such as, “I would like to request temporary coverage of BC MSP as I applied to extend my immigration documents before my BC MSP and immigration status expired and was advised by a Health Insurance BC agent that I am eligible for coverage during maintained status”\. Review the [MSP Temporary Coverage Sample Letter](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/msp_temporary_coverage_sample_letter.pdf) \(pdf\)\.
-   A copy of the IRCC submission confirmation \(PDF\) confirming that IRCC received your immigration application\. To find your confirmation, log into your [IRCC online account](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/account.html)\.

If it has been **4 weeks or longer** since your previous study permit expired, you must provide recent documentation from IRCC from **within the past 4 weeks** showing that your study or work permit application is still being processed\. Examples of supporting documents include:

-   A screenshot or PDF of your [IRCC online account](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/account.html) webpage showing the current status of your study or work permit application and timestamp \(e\.g\., the date and time your screenshot was recorded *—* capture the full window of your computer screen to display the timestamp\)\. The screenshot must be from within 4 weeks of the date you submit the request\. Click “check status and messages” under the “View my submitted applications or profiles” section\.
-   The most recent correspondence received by IRCC regarding your study or work permit application status issued within the past 4 weeks, such as a PDF letter in your [IRCC online account](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/account.html) under “[messages](https://www.cic.gc.ca/english/helpcentre/answer.asp?qnum=851&top=23)”\.

**If MSP is not able to provide temporary coverage**

Purchase temporary private health insurance, such as the [Guard Me Canada Plan](https://sites.guard.me/ubc/department/interim-coverage), to cover you until you can reinstate your MSP coverage\.

**

After you get your new immigration document

**

Once you get your new immigration document, you will need to extend or reapply for MSP\. 

**If you were approved for MSP temporary coverage**, apply to [extend your MSP online](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/extend-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/) with a copy of your new study or work permit\.

**If you were not approved for MSP temporary coverage**, depending on the length of the gap in MSP coverage, you will either be able to get an extension of your MSP, or you will need to reapply for MSP\. You must [contact MSP by phone](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents-contact-us) to confirm your eligibility, as it will depend on your individual circumstances\.

If you will need to [reapply for MSP](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/apply-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/) and serve the 3\-month MSP waiting period again, be sure to purchase temporary private health insurance to cover you during the 3\-month waiting period\.

If you can [extend your MSP](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/extend-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/) and you hold a study permit, you will continue to be charged the monthly healthcare coverage fee\.

## MSP coverage outside of BC[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/medical\-services\-plan\-msp\-international/\#msp\-coverage\-outside\-of\-bc](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/#msp-coverage-outside-of-bc)

### Maintaining your MSP eligibility

If you’re leaving British Columbia \(BC\) temporarily due to a co\-op placement or travel plans, you will continue being billed for your health\-care coverage fee\. 

To remain eligible for MSP, you need to live in BC for a minimum of 6 months in one calendar year\. If you are absent from BC for more than 6 months, you may need to re\-apply when you return to the province and go through the approximately 3\-month waiting period again\. Be sure to get temporary private health insurance for your waiting period\.

For example, if you live outside of BC between May and December in a particular year, you may need to reapply for your health insurance\. However, if you are away from BC between September and April of the following year, you remain eligible for MSP because you are only absent from the province for 4 months in each calendar year\.

For more information, visit [Leaving BC Temporarily](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents/managing-your-msp-account/leaving-bc-temporarily)\. 

**

Before leaving BC

**

Make sure you understand [MSP’s residency requirements](http://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents/eligibility-and-enrolment/are-you-eligible) and [call MSP](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents-contact-us) to discuss how your coverage could be impacted by travel plans\. It will help if you know the exact dates when you will be traveling outside BC\.

**

If you will be in another Canadian province or territory

**

You might be able to continue to use MSP coverage for 3 months outside of BC, which could be used to cover your waiting period in another province or territory\. To confirm your eligibility for coverage outside of BC and options to cancel your MSP, [contact MSP by phone](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents-contact-us)\.

Different provinces and territories in Canada have their own health insurance plans and not all of them provide coverage for international students\. Check with the [province or territory’s health insurance plan](https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/health-cards.html) to confirm if you are eligible to join and how to apply\. If you are not eligible, be sure to purchase temporary private health insurance\.

**

If you will be outside of Canada

**

**If you will be outside Canada for less than 6 months**, you have the option to keep or cancel MSP\. 

**If you will be outside of Canada for more than 6 months** in a calendar year, [contact MSP by phone](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents-contact-us) to confirm your eligibility\. You might need to cancel your MSP coverage, or you might be given the option to keep MSP\.    

If you’re eligible and you decide to keep MSP, you do not have to reapply or have a 3\-month waiting period when you return, but you will need to continue to pay the monthly fee for MSP while you are away\.

If you cancel your MSP, you will have to [reapply when you return to BC](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/apply-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/) and get temporary private health insurance before you return to Canada to cover you during the MSP 3\-month waiting period\. 

Ensure you have sufficient health insurance outside of Canada\. If you are enrolled in the [AMS/GSS Health and Dental Plan](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/#extended-health-insurance-ams-gss-health-and-dental-plan), you must have basic insurance, such as MSP, to be eligible for [travel coverage](https://www.studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_Travel_TravelCoverage&random=956), and you cannot be covered in your country of origin\.

**

Upon return to British Columbia

**

If you aren’t sure whether or not you are eligible for coverage, you must [call MSP](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents-contact-us) to confirm, particularly if you have been outside of BC for more than 6 months in a calendar year\. 

If you must [re\-apply for MSP](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/apply-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/) and go through the 3\-month waiting period for MSP again, be sure to obtain temporary private health insurance to cover you until you are covered under MSP\.

## Enrolling your family[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/medical\-services\-plan\-msp\-international/\#enrolling\-your\-family](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/#enrolling-your-family)

If your family members plan to reside in BC for 6 months or more, they may also be [eligible for MSP](http://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents/eligibility-and-enrolment/are-you-eligible)\.

If your family members arrive in BC with you within the same calendar month, you can all [apply for MSP](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/apply-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/) at the same time\. 

If your family members arrive in BC at a later date \(outside of the same calendar month\), use the [MSP Account Change](https://my.gov.bc.ca/msp/deam/home) form to add them to your existing MSP\. 

Remember to include photocopies of every family members’ Canadian status document, such as a study permit, visitor record, or work permit, that is valid for 6 months or more in the application\. Some visitors will only have an entry stamp in their passports; use this as their status document\.

Also remember that your family members will need to go through the 3\-month waiting period and should purchase a temporary private health insurance plan\.

If your child is born in BC, you can add them to your MSP\.

Learn more about [adding or removing dependents](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents/managing-your-msp-account/adding-and-removing-dependents)\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/medical\-services\-plan\-msp\-international/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/#if-you-have-questions)

To confirm your eligibility and coverage, [contact MSP](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents-contact-us)\.

For all other questions related to international health insurance, connect with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/)\.

## International Student Guide[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/medical\-services\-plan\-msp\-international/\#international\-student\-guide](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/#international-student-guide)

Find everything you need to know about life as an international student at UBC’s Vancouver campus\.

[View the guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/)

title: How to apply for your BC Medical Services Plan (MSP)
content_markdown:
## Overview of process[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/medical\-services\-plan\-msp\-international/apply\-bc\-medical\-services\-plan\-msp/\#overview\-of\-process](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/apply-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/#overview-of-process)

- **Row 1**

  - **Header cell 1:**
  
    Topic
  
  - **Header cell 2:**
  
    Details

- **Row 2**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    When to apply
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Immediately after arriving in British Columbia

- **Row 3**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Cost
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    $75 per month for study permit holders

- **Row 4**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Processing time
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    1 to 2 months  
    Coverage begins after a waiting period \(the remainder of the month of arrival plus 2 full calendar months\)

- **Row 5**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    How to apply
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    [Apply online](http://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents/eligibility-and-enrolment/how-to-enrol) \(recommended\) or by mail\.  
    Review the [UBC MSP Application Guide](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/ubc_msp_application_tutorial_slides.pdf) \(pdf\) to prepare your MSP online application\.

- **Row 6**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Supporting documents
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    **International students:** Copy of valid study permit **or** work permit \(such as Post\-graduation or spouse/partner work permit\)  
    **Canadian students:** Copy of proof of status \(such as Canadian permanent resident card, record of landing, confirmation of permanent residence letter, Canadian passport, Canadian birth certificate, front and back of Canadian citizenship card, certificate of Canadian citizenship, First Nations status card, or Métis status card\)  
    **Family members:** Copy of visitor record, study permit, spouse/partner work permit, or passport stamp showing arrival date to Canada  
    Additional documents may be needed\.

## Tips for the process[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/medical\-services\-plan\-msp\-international/apply\-bc\-medical\-services\-plan\-msp/\#tips\-for\-the\-process](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/apply-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/#tips-for-the-process)

The easiest way to apply is to [submit an application online](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents/eligibility-and-enrolment/how-to-enrol#:~:text=best%20for%20you.-,Apply%20online,-Apply%20in%20person)\.

If you decide to submit a [paper application](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/ahdc#mail:~:text=You%20can%20also%20apply%20by%20mail%20using%20a%20paper%C2%A0form) by mail, consider using a secure mailing method such as Canada Post Xpresspost\.

### International students

If you are reapplying for MSP after no longer being covered by the plan, you will need to go through the approximately 3\-month waiting period again\. Be sure to get temporary private health insurance to cover you until you can reinstate your MSP coverage\. You can [contact GuardMe](https://sites.guard.me/ubc/department/interim-coverage), the provider of [iMED](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international/), to discuss your options for temporary health insurance, or you can find and purchase your own private temporary health insurance\.

Temporary BC residents \(such as international students and workers\) will typically be issued a BC Services Card \(formerly known as “BC CareCard”\) without a photo\. Carry your card with you as well as a digital or paper copy of your valid study permit or work permit\.

You can also apply for a [BC driver’s license](https://www.icbc.com/driver-licensing/moving-bc/Pages/Default.aspx) and/or [BCID card](https://www.icbc.com/driver-licensing/getting-licensed/Apply-for-a-bcid) \(which includes your photo\) by submitting a separate application to the [Insurance Corporation of BC](https://www.icbc.com/Pages/default.aspx) \(ICBC\)\.

### Domestic students

As of 2018, to complete MSP enrolment, adult Canadian citizens and permanent residents will need to obtain a BC Services Card with a photo by visiting an [Insurance Corporation of BC](https://www.icbc.com/Pages/default.aspx) \(ICBC\) driver licensing office\. 

Apply for MSP, wait for your letter of instruction, then bring the letter and primary and secondary photo ID document such as your driver’s license or your BCID Card to an ICBC office near you\.

## Get important information on MSP[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/medical\-services\-plan\-msp\-international/apply\-bc\-medical\-services\-plan\-msp/\#get\-important\-information\-on\-msp](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/apply-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/#get-important-information-on-msp)

Learn about how to maintain your MSP coverage, how to make payments, what happens if you will be outside of BC and more\.

[Review details](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/)

## Register for BC Fair PharmaCare[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/medical\-services\-plan\-msp\-international/apply\-bc\-medical\-services\-plan\-msp/\#register\-for\-bc\-fair\-pharmacare](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/apply-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/#register-for-bc-fair-pharmacare)

It is recommended for most students to register for the [BC Fair PharmaCare program](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/pharmacare-for-bc-residents/who-we-cover/fair-pharmacare-plan#eligibility), which may provide additional coverage for prescription drugs, medical devices, and pharmacy services\. PharmaCare registration may be required for [prescription coverage](https://www.studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_Health_HealthCoverage_PrescriptionDrugs_BCFairPharmaCare) through the AMS/GSS Health and Dental plan\. 

Since coverage is based on income, the application requires proof of your previous income based on taxes filed in Canada 2 years ago\. If you are a new resident of Canada, recently turned 19, or were exempt from filing taxes in Canada 2 years ago, you might be able to submit a [Fair PharmaCare Proof of Income Affidavit](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/assets/gov/health/forms/5357fil.pdf)—[contact MSP](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents-contact-us) for assistance\.

You can register for the BC Fair PharmaCare plan at the same time you [apply for MSP](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/apply-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/)\. It is also possible to [register for Fair PharmaCare](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/pharmacare-for-bc-residents/who-we-cover/fair-pharmacare-plan) separately\.

You need to provide a [Social Insurance Number \(SIN\)](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/) to apply\. If you don’t have a SIN yet, consider applying for MSP separately as soon as you arrive in BC, and then register for Fair PharmaCare once you have your SIN\.

If you are a Canadian citizen or permanent resident who has resided in Canada for at least the past 12 months, you might also be eligible for [supplementary benefits](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents/benefits/services-covered-by-msp/supplementary-benefits)\.

If you have questions about enrollment with Fair PharmaCare, [contact MSP](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents-contact-us)\.

## Related resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/medical\-services\-plan\-msp\-international/apply\-bc\-medical\-services\-plan\-msp/\#related\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/apply-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/#related-resources)

-   [Health insurance for international students](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/)  
    All international students are required to have basic and extended health insurance for the duration of their studies\.
-   [iMED: Temporary health insurance for international students](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international/)  
    iMED is a temporary basic health insurance plan required for new international students, and will provide you with health insurance coverage during the 3 month waiting period for BC’s Medical Services Plan \(MSP\) or for the full duration of your program if you are a one\-term exchange student or Visiting International Research Student \(VIRS\)\.
-   [Medical Services Plan \(MSP\) for international students](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/)  
    MSP is BC’s provincial health insurance plan\. Anyone living in BC for six months or longer \(including international students\) is required by law to enrol in MSP and pay the plan’s monthly healthcare coverage fee \(i\.e\., the International Student Health Fee\)\.
-   [How to extend your BC Medical Services Plan \(MSP\)](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/extend-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/)  
    Find helpful tips for extending your BC Medical Services Plan \(MSP\)\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/medical\-services\-plan\-msp\-international/apply\-bc\-medical\-services\-plan\-msp/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/apply-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/#if-you-have-questions)

To confirm your eligibility and coverage, [contact MSP](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents-contact-us)\.

For all other questions related to international health insurance, please connect with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/)\.

## International Student Guide[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/medical\-services\-plan\-msp\-international/apply\-bc\-medical\-services\-plan\-msp/\#international\-student\-guide](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/apply-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/#international-student-guide)

    **Family members:** Copy of visitor record, study permit, spouse/partner work permit, or passport stamp showing arrival date to Canada  
    Additional documents may be needed\.

## How having maintained status impacts your MSP coverage[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/medical\-services\-plan\-msp\-international/extend\-bc\-medical\-services\-plan\-msp/\#how\-having\-maintained\-status\-impacts\-your\-msp\-coverage](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/extend-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/#how-having-maintained-status-impacts-your-msp-coverage)

You will have “[maintained status](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/maintained-status/)” \(formerly called “implied status”\) if **all** of the following applies to you:

-   You applied for a new immigration document, such as a study or work permit, before your [study permit became invalid or expired](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/#maintaining-your-student-status); or your work permit/visitor status expired\.
-   You won’t receive a new immigration document before your old one expires\.
-   You remain in Canada beyond the expiry of your old document\.

Since your BC MSP will end on the expiry date of your current immigration document, you **must take action to get health insurance coverage before your MSP expires**\. Without valid health insurance, you will need to pay for any health services\. Check how to get [MSP temporary coverage](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international#how-having-maintained-status-impacts-your-msp-coverage)\.

**If you were approved for MSP temporary coverage**, apply to extend your MSP online with a copy of your new study or work permit\.

**If you were not approved for MSP temporary coverage**, depending on the length of the gap in MSP coverage, you will either be able to get an extension of your MSP, or you will need to reapply for MSP\. You must [contact MSP by phone](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents-contact-us) to confirm your eligibility, as it will depend on your individual circumstances\.

If you will need to [reapply for MSP](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/apply-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/) and complete the 3\-month MSP waiting period again, be sure to purchase temporary private health insurance to cover you during the 3\-month waiting period\. You can [contact GuardMe](https://sites.guard.me/ubc/contact), the provider of [iMED](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international/), to discuss your options for temporary health insurance, or you can find and purchase your own private insurance\.

If you can extend your MSP and you hold a study permit, you will continue to be charged the monthly health\-care coverage fee\.

## Tips for the process[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/medical\-services\-plan\-msp\-international/extend\-bc\-medical\-services\-plan\-msp/\#tips\-for\-the\-process](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/extend-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/#tips-for-the-process)

The easiest way to apply is to [submit an application online](http://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents/eligibility-and-enrolment/how-to-enrol)\.

If you decide to submit a [paper application](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/assets/gov/health/forms/203fil.pdf) by mail, consider using a secure mailing method such as Canada Post Xpresspost\. You should also include a cover letter along with other supporting documents if requesting [MSP temporary coverage](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international#how-having-maintained-status-impacts-your-msp-coverage)—check the [MSP Temporary Coverage Sample Letter](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/msp_temporary_coverage_sample_letter.pdf) \(pdf\)\.

### International students

Temporary BC residents \(such as international students and workers\) will typically be issued a [BC Services Card](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/governments/government-id/bc-services-card) \(formerly known as “BC CareCard”\) without a photo\. Carry your card with you as well as a digital or paper copy of your valid study permit or work permit\.

You can also apply for a [BC driver’s license](https://www.icbc.com/driver-licensing/moving-bc/Pages/Default.aspx) and/or [BCID Card](https://www.icbc.com/driver-licensing/getting-licensed/Apply-for-a-bcid) \(which includes your photo\) by submitting a separate application to the [Insurance Corporation of BC](https://www.icbc.com/Pages/default.aspx) \(ICBC\)\.

## Get important information on MSP[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/health\-insurance/health\-insurance\-international/medical\-services\-plan\-msp\-international/extend\-bc\-medical\-services\-plan\-msp/\#get\-important\-information\-on\-msp](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/extend-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/#get-important-information-on-msp)

Learn about how to maintain your MSP coverage, how to make payments, what happens if you will be outside of BC and more\.

title: Flu and colds
content_markdown:
## About the flu[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/medical\-care\-on\-campus/flu\-colds/\#about\-the\-flu](https://students.ubc.ca/health/medical-care-on-campus/flu-colds/#about-the-flu)

The flu, also known as Influenza, is an infection of your nose and throat, or upper airway, caused by an influenza virus\. The flu can cause serious illness and health complications, especially for young children, pregnant people, the elderly, or people with certain medical conditions\. A cold is caused by a viral infection of the upper respiratory tract\. Most viral infections are self\-limiting and resolve on their own\.

## What to do if you’re sick[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/medical\-care\-on\-campus/flu\-colds/\#what\-to\-do\-if\-youre\-sick](https://students.ubc.ca/health/medical-care-on-campus/flu-colds/#what-to-do-if-youre-sick)

### Managing your symptoms

Many cold and flu symptoms such as fever, muscle pain, and sore throat can be managed at home with over\-the\-counter medications such as Tylenol or Advil\. Read about the [flu symptoms](https://www.healthlinkbc.ca/healthlinkbc-files/facts-about-influenza-flu) you can manage at home on your own, and the ones that require medical attention\.

If you experience severe symptoms, like difficulty breathing, confusion, persistent fever, or chest pain, you should visit your nearest emergency department or urgent care\.

Visit [Student Health and Wellbeing](https://students.ubc.ca/health/medical-care-on-campus/) if you do not start to feel better in a few days or your symptoms worsen\.

Call HealthlinkBC at [811](tel:811) for free health information and advice from a registered nurse, dietician, pharmacist, or a qualified exercise professional\.

### If you have to miss class or an exam

If you’re feeling unwell and cannot attend class, follow the instructions in your syllabus\. Your course instructor should not need you to present a sick note\. They may simply ask you to email them about your situation and make up the work you missed\.

You may want to consider an [academic concession](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-concessions/) if a medical circumstance is preventing you from completing graded work or exams\. Contact your [academic advising office](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) if you have to miss class or coursework for an extended time due to illness\.

If your medical condition is ongoing and affecting your studies for more than one term, you can request an [academic accommodation](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/)\.

### If you’re unable to work

UBC offers [emergency funding](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/emergency-funding/) for students who encounter an unexpected situation that impacts their finances\. An [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) can work with you to review your personal finances and connect you to helpful resources\.

## Protecting yourself and others from getting sick[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/medical\-care\-on\-campus/flu\-colds/\#protecting\-yourself\-and\-others\-from\-getting\-sick](https://students.ubc.ca/health/medical-care-on-campus/flu-colds/#protecting-yourself-and-others-from-getting-sick)

Colds and flus spread easily through coughing, sneezing, or having face\-to\-face contact\. The risk of getting sick can be higher in spaces with large numbers of people, such as lecture halls, indoor campus spots, and on the bus\.

Follow the tips below to protect yourself and others from getting sick:

-   Cover your mouth when you cough or sneeze\.
-   Wash your hands frequently\.
-   Stay home if you are unwell\.
-   If you’re sick, wear a mask when around others\.
-   Avoid touching your eyes, mouth, or nose\.
-   Get your flu shot at a local pharmacy or clinic\.

## Get your flu shot[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/medical\-care\-on\-campus/flu\-colds/\#get\-your\-flu\-shot](https://students.ubc.ca/health/medical-care-on-campus/flu-colds/#get-your-flu-shot)

The flu shot, also known as [flu vaccine](https://immunizebc.ca/influenza), is available during late October or early November\. In British Columbia, the flu shot is recommended and free for everyone aged 6 months or older\. If you’re registered with the [Get Vaccinated](https://www.getvaccinated.gov.bc.ca/s/) system, you’ll receive a notification when it’s time to book your next flu vaccine\.

You can also call and book an appointment for your flu vaccine at [UBC Student Health and Wellbeing](https://students.ubc.ca/health/medical-care-on-campus/)\.

### COVID\-19 Vaccine

Several pharmacies and clinics also offer the COVID\-19 vaccine with the flu shot during the same appointment\. Please call ahead to confirm availability if you decide to walk in\.

If you’re registered with the [Get Vaccinated](https://www.getvaccinated.gov.bc.ca/s/) system, you’ll receive a notification when it’s time to book both of these vaccines\. If you don’t have MSP or a Personal Health Number \(PHN\), you can call [1 833 838 2323](tel:18338382323) \(toll free\) to register for the system\.

### On\-campus locations

| On\-campus pharmacy | Address | Bookable vaccine\(s\) | How to book |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Shoppers](https://www1.shoppersdrugmart.ca/en/store-locator/store/2273/?_ga=2.268510708.44450994.1634162807-1881830948.1634162807) | 5940 University Boulevard | Flu and COVID\-19 | Register online with the [Get Vaccinated system](https://www.getvaccinated.gov.bc.ca/s/) or walk in\. |
| [IDA University Pharmacy](https://www.universitypharmacy.net/) | 5754 University Boulevard | Flu and COVID\-19 | Register online with the [Get Vaccinated system](https://www.getvaccinated.gov.bc.ca/s/) or walk in\. |
| [Save\-On\-Foods](https://www.saveonfoods.com/sm/pickup/rsid/1982/ubc/) | 5945 Berton Avenue | Flu and COVID\-19 | Register online with the [Get Vaccinated system](https://www.getvaccinated.gov.bc.ca/s/)\. |

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/medical\-care\-on\-campus/flu\-colds/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/health/medical-care-on-campus/flu-colds/#additional-resources)
