title: How to apply for your initial study permit
content_markdown:
## Overview of the process[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/apply\-initial\-study\-permit/\#overview\-of\-the\-process](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/#overview-of-the-process)

### When to apply

You must apply for your initial study permit from outside of Canada and it must be approved before you come to Canada\. Study permits are issued by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada \(IRCC\), the government department that handles immigration\.

You should apply for your study permit as soon as you receive your Letter of Admission and [Provincial Attestation Letter](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-documents-required-study-permit/) \(PAL\), if applicable\.

**If you are a U\.S\. citizen or permanent resident**, or a resident of Greenland or St\. Pierre and Miquelon, you have the option to [apply upon entry](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/study-permits#important-considerations) into Canada, either at the Canada\-US border crossing or at an airport upon arrival in Canada\. You will need a PAL for your application unless you are enrolled in a Master’s or Doctoral degree program\. 

**If you are inside Canada** only some people are eligible to apply through the [inside Canada process](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/extend-study-permit/)\. Contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support\. 

Check current estimated [processing times](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/check-processing-times.html)\.

## First, learn about study permits[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/apply\-initial\-study\-permit/\#first\-learn\-about\-study\-permits](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/#first-learn-about-study-permits)

Before preparing your application, [review important information](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/) about what a study permit is, who needs one, study permits for minors, and other important considerations\.

If you have a spouse, common\-law partner, or children, it’s possible to submit your family’s applications together with your study permit application\. Learn more about [documents for your family](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/documentation-family/)\. 

## Next, prepare your application[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/apply\-initial\-study\-permit/\#next\-prepare\-your\-application](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/#next-prepare-your-application)

1.  [Create your document checklist](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/tutorial-apply-initial-study-permit-document-checklist/)
2.  [Gather your required documents](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/tutorial-apply-initial-study-permit-required-documents/)
3.  [Complete the application form](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/tutorial-apply-initial-study-permit-fill-application/)

### Medical exams

You may be required to complete an [immigration medical exam](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/medical-police/medical-exams/requirements-temporary-residents.html)\. In general, it is faster for study permit processing if you take an “upfront” medical exam, meaning you take a medical exam before you apply for a study permit, and submit the medical exam document \(e\-medical\) in your study permit application\.

You can also submit your study permit application first and wait for a notice asking you to take a medical exam, which may take longer\. Generally, if you do not take an upfront medical exam, you will have to provide results within 30 days of receiving a request for a medical exam\.

Costs of medical exams vary depending on the individual panel physician \(a doctor authorized by Canadian Immigration to conduct immigration medical exam\)\.

Check out the “documents you might need” section on the [Gather your required documents page](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/tutorial-apply-initial-study-permit-required-documents/) for further information\.

### Complete the application review course

Before you submit your application, review the online [application review Canvas course](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/EXWLA4) to go over your application with helpful videos and to learn about common mistakes\.

## Then, apply for your initial study permit[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/apply\-initial\-study\-permit/\#then\-apply\-for\-your\-initial\-study\-permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/#then-apply-for-your-initial-study-permit)

The application fee is $150\.

It’s highly recommended to **apply online**\.

### Alternate options

-   Apply in person at a [Visa Application Centre \(VAC\)](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/contact-ircc/offices/find-visa-application-centre.html)\.
-   Apply [by paper](https://ircc.canada.ca/english/information/applications/student.asp#apply-paper) if you have a disability which prevents you from applying online, or you hold an identity or travel document for non\-national residents, refugees or stateless persons\.
-   US citizens, US permanent residents, and residents of Greenland or St\. Pierre and Miquelon can also [apply in person](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/#important-considerations) upon entry to Canada at the border or airport\.

### If a representative will apply for you on your behalf

Only [certain people](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/find-regulated-immigration-consultant-or-lawyer/#get-help-from-an-authorized-representative) can represent or advise you with a Canadian immigration proceeding or application\. Working with a representative or agent who is not authorized to provide immigration advice could have a negative impact on your application, as well as future immigration applications\. See how to [find a regulated immigration consultant or lawyer](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/find-regulated-immigration-consultant-or-lawyer/#get-help-from-an-authorized-representative)\.

## Submit biometrics and medical exams, if applicable[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/apply\-initial\-study\-permit/\#submit\-biometrics\-and\-medical\-exams\-if\-applicable](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/#submit-biometrics-and-medical-exams-if-applicable)

Submit your biometrics \(fingerprints and photo\) in\-person at the nearest [biometrics collection site](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/information/where-to-give-biometrics.asp) after you apply for your study permit within 30 days of receiving a request for biometrics\. Book an appointment to provide biometrics as soon as you get your Biometrics Instruction Letter \(request for your biometrics\)\. A fee of $85 will be required at the time you submit your study permit application\. IRCC will not start processing your application until you have submitted your biometrics, if applicable\. Your application may be returned to you if you do not complete your biometrics by the deadline stated in your instruction letter\.

Some students may need to travel within their home country or in some cases, apply for a visa to travel to another country to submit biometrics\. 

If you provided biometrics in the past 10 years or if you are a U\.S\. citizen, you are exempt\. Find out more on [who needs to provide biometrics](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/biometrics/who-needs-to-give.html)\. 

## Get your study permit approval[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/apply\-initial\-study\-permit/\#get\-your\-study\-permit\-approval](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/#get-your-study-permit-approval)

If your study permit application is approved, IRCC will email you a **Letter of Introduction**\.

You will need to print and present this letter to the Canada Border Services Officer when you first enter Canada\. They will then issue your study permit \(a piece of paper\) at the airport or border crossing\.

Review the [Travelling to Canada Guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/) before making travel plans\. Do not book travel until you have received your Letter of Introduction, or book travel that can be changed or refunded\.

**

Sample Letter of Introduction

**

Below is a sample letter of introduction\.

[Screenshot of a sample Letter of Introduction](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/study_permit_letter_introduction_sample.jpg)

**

If your application is refused

**

If you receive a refusal on your application, inform [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) through our [webform](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0J8VRJgJQkuO2b4) as soon as possible so we can help you resolve the issue\. Make sure to upload a copy of your refusal letter and all documents submitted with your application\.

## Get your TRV/eTA, if applicable[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/apply\-initial\-study\-permit/\#get\-your\-trv\-eta\-if\-applicable](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/#get-your-trv-eta-if-applicable)

After your study permit has been approved, you will automatically be issued one of these documents to travel to Canada depending on your country of citizenship:

-   Temporary Resident Visa \(TRV\), or 
-   Electronic Travel Authorization \(eTA\)

If you are from a [TRV\-required country](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/entry-requirements-country.html#visaRequired), normally, IRCC will contact you to ask for your passport once your study permit is approved\. You will then send your passport to your visa office or a Visa Application Centre \(VAC\) so they can attach your TRV \(a sticker\) on a page inside your passport\.

If you are from an [eTA country](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/entry-requirements-country.html#visaExempt), once your study permit is approved, IRCC will automatically include your eTA number in your Letter of Introduction\. No action is required by you\. You can [check your eTA status online](https://onlineservices-servicesenligne.cic.gc.ca/eta/applicationQuery?lang=en)\.

U\.S\. citizens and permanent residents are exempt from requiring a TRV or an eTA\.

## When you arrive in Canada[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/apply\-initial\-study\-permit/\#when\-you\-arrive\-in\-canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/#when-you-arrive-in-canada)

Read the guide to ensure you are prepared for your arrival in Canada and steps you should follow\.

[Get details](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/get-study-permit-enter-canada/)

## After entering Canada[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/apply\-initial\-study\-permit/\#after\-entering\-canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/#after-entering-canada)

Once you’re in Canada, there are a few steps to complete, such as applying for your BC Medical Services Plan \(MSP\), maintaining your student status, applying for a Social Insurance Number \(SIN\) and more\.

1.  Apply for [BC Medical Services Plan \(MSP\)](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/apply-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/) as soon as you arrive in British Columbia\.
2.  Check that you have [iMED health insurance](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international/) for your first three months in BC\.
3.  Apply for a [Social Insurance Number \(SIN\)](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/), which is required to work in Canada\.
4.  Add your immigration document expiry dates into the [UBC Reminder System](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/immigration-documents-reminder-system/)\.
5.  Keep your study permit valid and remain enrolled in classes until program completion\.  Learn about how your [enrolment impacts immigration](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/immigration-impacts-part-time-studies-withdrawing-courses/)\.
6.  To avoid carrying your passport for identification, [get a BCID](https://www.icbc.com/driver-licensing/getting-licensed/Apply-for-a-bcid)\.

### Learn about life in Canada

-   [International Student Guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/)
-   iPREP pre\-arrival immigration and health insurance course:
    -   [Undergraduate students](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/NJFRY4)
    -   [Graduate students](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/77NDCK)
    -   [Non\-degree seeking students](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/NCK6XM)
-   [New to UBC guide for first years](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/)
-   [Getting to know Canada](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/new-immigrants/learn-about-canada.html)
-   [Health insurance for international students](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/)
-   [Working in Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/)
-   [Guide to banking in Canada](https://www.canada.ca/en/financial-consumer-agency/services/banking.html)
-   [Driving in BC](https://www.welcomebc.ca/start-your-life-in-b-c/daily-life#Driving)
-   [Resources if you have children](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/resources-who-are-parents/)
-   [Scams and fraud](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/campaigns/fraud-scams.html)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/apply\-initial\-study\-permit/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/#if-you-have-questions)

You can connect with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for questions related to immigration, health insurance, and life as an international student in Canada\.

## The information on this page may change[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/apply\-initial\-study\-permit/\#the\-information\-on\-this\-page\-may\-change](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/#the-information-on-this-page-may-change)

The immigration information on this page has been reviewed and endorsed by Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultants \(RCICs\) or Regulated International Student Immigration Advisors \(RISIAs\) in compliance with the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and Regulations\. However, this is not a legal document and information may change without notice\. Always refer to [Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada](http://www.cic.gc.ca/) \(IRCC\) for the most up\-to\-date information\.

title: Get your study permit when you enter Canada
content_markdown:
## Preparing to arrive in Canada[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/apply\-initial\-study\-permit/get\-study\-permit\-enter\-canada/\#preparing\-to\-arrive\-in\-canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/get-study-permit-enter-canada/#preparing-to-arrive-in-canada)

Follow our detailed [Travelling to Canada Guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/) to learn about making travel plans, what you must bring, arrival steps to ensure you get a study permit with conditions to work, and more\.

## When you arrive in Canada[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/apply\-initial\-study\-permit/get\-study\-permit\-enter\-canada/\#when\-you\-arrive\-in\-canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/get-study-permit-enter-canada/#when-you-arrive-in-canada)

Be sure to get your study permit when you **first enter Canada**\. In other words, present your Letter of Introduction to the Canada Border Services Officer at the **first place** you arrive in Canada and request a study permit\.

For example, if you arrive in Toronto, then take another flight to Vancouver, you must get your study permit in Toronto\. If you have connecting flights, try to schedule a layover for a few hours to allow time for immigration\.

1.  **Answer questions on the electronic [Primary Inspection Kiosk](https://www.cbsa-asfc.gc.ca/services/border-tech-frontiere/pik-bip-eng.html), if arriving by plane**\.  
    You must declare if you have packed currency equal to or greater than CAD$10,000 and/or any food, plant or animal products\.
2.  **Present your kiosk receipt to an officer**\.  
    Let them know you need a study permit, then the officer will direct you to immigration\.
3.  **Pick up your checked luggage, if applicable\.**
4.  **Proceed to immigration and present your Letter of Introduction\.**
5.  **Check your study permit before you leave the officer’s desk\.**
    -   Confirm that all personal information and conditions are correct\. If they are not, notify the officer right away\.
    -   To prevent delays in starting a job, ensure your study permit includes **at least one of the following conditions:** 
        -   “May accept employment on or off campus if meeting eligibility criteria, per paragraph R186\(f\), \(v\) or \(w\) and must cease working if no longer meeting these criteria”
        -   “May work 24 hours per week off campus or full time during regular breaks if meeting criteria outlined in paragraph 186\(v\) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations” \(study permits issued before Nov 8, 2024, would indicate 20 hours a week\)
        -   “May accept employment on the campus of the institution at which registered in full\-time studies”
    -   Before leaving the officer’s desk, ensure the information on your study permit is correct and that it states you ‘may work’ or ‘may accept employment\.’ If these words are not present, respectfully request they be added\. If they are not, you will not be able to work on your study permit for many months while you apply for a correction\.

If you arrive by car, there are no kiosks\. Answer the officer’s questions, let them know you need a study permit, then proceed to secondary examination for your study permit\.

## Complete the iPREP pre\-arrival course[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/apply\-initial\-study\-permit/get\-study\-permit\-enter\-canada/\#complete\-the\-iprep\-pre\-arrival\-course](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/get-study-permit-enter-canada/#complete-the-iprep-pre-arrival-course)

Learn about your immigration documents, health insurance, banking in Canada, getting a phone, scams and more\.

-   [Undergraduate students](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/NJFRY4)
-   [Graduate students](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/77NDCK)
-   [Exchange students](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/NCK6XM)

For more information on what to expect when you arrive in Canada, please see Step 4 of our Travelling to Canada Guide, [While you travel to Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/while-you-travel/)\.

## Study permit example[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/apply\-initial\-study\-permit/get\-study\-permit\-enter\-canada/\#study\-permit\-example](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/get-study-permit-enter-canada/#study-permit-example)

Below is a screenshot of an example study permit:

[Screenshot of a sample study permit](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/study_permit_example_screenshot.jpg)

title: Create your document checklist for your initial study permit application
content_markdown:
The documents you need to provide with your study permit application vary according to your country of citizenship along with other factors\.

## Choose your application method[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/apply\-initial\-study\-permit/tutorial\-apply\-initial\-study\-permit\-document\-checklist/\#choose\-your\-application\-method](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/tutorial-apply-initial-study-permit-document-checklist/#choose-your-application-method)

**

Apply online \(recommended\)

**

**Step 1**

Create an [IRCC secure account](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/account.html) if you do not have one already\. You will be prompted to answer a set of questions\. Ideally you would use the same account for all applications, so keep this information safe\. If you can’t remember your account information, it’s possible to create a new account\.

For help creating an account, review the [Creating an IRCC secure online account guide](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/study_permit_creating_ircc_account.pdf) \(pdf\)\.

**Step 2**

After you are logged into your IRCC Secure Account, select “apply to come to Canada”\. You will need to answer a series of questions in a questionnaire\. For assistance with the questionnaire, check our video in our [Canvas application review course](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/EXWLA4)\.

Note that for the question “Is work an essential component of your studies?”, this refers to whether your program has a mandatory work component to graduate, such as a Co\-op, internship or practicum\.

-   Most undergraduate degree programs require that you first begin your program before you can [apply for Co\-op](https://coop.ubc.ca/students/how-co-op-works), then you will be issued a Co\-op letter if you are accepted into the Co\-op option\. Select “no” to this question\. You may still be able to participate in a Co\-op or student work placement after you arrive in Canada and are issued a Co\-op confirmation letter\. If you are not sure if your program has a mandatory work component, please contact your faculty’s [Academic Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) office or your [graduate program staff](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/current-students/supervision)\.
-   If your program **does** have a mandatory work component and you have been issued a Co\-op confirmation letter, you can select “yes” to this question\. Then, you will need to upload a letter from your program/faculty about your required work component in your study permit application\.
-   If your program **does** have a mandatory work component, but you have not been issued a confirmation letter, select “no” for this question\. You may still be able to participate in a Co\-op or student work placement after you arrive in Canada and are issued a confirmation letter\.
-   If your program **does not** have a mandatory work component, select “no” to this question\. You do not require a Co\-op work permit to work in Canada during studies and can [work on and/or off campus](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/) based on your study permit, if you are eligible\.

When you have completed the questionnaire, you’ll be guided to a screen entitled “*Your document checklist*” that lists your required documents based on your answers from your questionnaire\. If you’ve made a mistake, it’s possible to go back and change your answers to update your document checklist\. 

**Step 3**

**Important**: In addition to your document checklist generated by IRCC, you need to add any additional documents required by the Canadian visa office in your country\.

Get the full list of documents required by the Canadian visa office in your country:

1.  Go to the [IRCC website](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/information/applications/student.asp) for paper applications and select your country/territory from the drop\-down list\.
2.  Then select “*Visa office instructions*“\. This will launch a PDF specifying requirements from your visa office\.

Any documents required by your visa office which are not already included in your online document checklist will need to be provided along with your letter of explanation in the “client information” section, under *optional documents* in your document checklist\.

**

Apply at a Visa Application Centre \(VAC\)

**

Visa Application Centres \(VACs\) are private companies that have contracts with the Canadian government to provide application support services for a fee\. They do not provide immigration advice or make decisions on your study permit application\. Check the [Visa Application Centre’s website](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/contact-ircc/offices/find-visa-application-centre.html) for more information about their services\.

If you will apply in person at a VAC, follow the same steps as applying on paper to create your document checklist\.

**

Apply on paper

**

You can only apply by paper if you have a disability which prevents you from applying online **or** you hold an identity or travel document for non\-national residents, refugees or stateless persons\.

To apply by paper:

1.  Go to the “Apply on paper” section of the [IRCC website](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/information/applications/student.asp)\.
2.  Select your country/territory from the drop\-down menu and click “Get documents”\.
3.  You’ll notice a list of links:
    -   Click on the first link to review a general document checklist\.
    -   Click on the second link to view visa office instructions for your country\. These instructions include a document checklist showing additional supporting documents required by your country’s visa office\.
    -   The remaining links in the list will open the forms listed in the general document checklist\.
4.  Submit your application through a [Visa Application Center \(VAC\)](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/contact-ircc/offices/find-visa-application-centre.html) that serves your area\.

**

Apply on arrival

**

Only US citizens or permanent residents, and residents of Greenland or St\. Pierre and Miquelon, can [apply in\-person](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/#important-considerations) on arrival in Canada at the airport or border crossing\.

If you are eligible for this option, follow the same steps as applying online to create your document checklist\. Print all documents and bring your completed application form and supporting documents with you\.

Be sure to check if you need a medical exam, custodianship, or biometrics in advance\.

The immigration information on this page has been reviewed and endorsed by Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultants \(RCICs\) or Regulated International Student Immigration Advisors \(RISIAs\) in compliance with the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and Regulations\. However, this is not a legal document and information may change without notice\. Always refer to [Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada](http://www.cic.gc.ca/) \(IRCC\) for the most up\-to\-date information\.

title: Complete your initial study permit application
content_markdown:
## About the application form[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/apply\-initial\-study\-permit/tutorial\-apply\-initial\-study\-permit\-fill\-application/\#about\-the\-application\-form](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/tutorial-apply-initial-study-permit-fill-application/#about-the-application-form)

Your application form is an important part of your study permit application\. Missing or incorrect information can negatively impact the outcome of your application\. Below are 4 steps to help create a comprehensive application\.

Note that some people are “[inadmissible](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/inadmissibility.html)” to Canada, which means they are not allowed to enter or remain in Canada for reasons such as having committed a crime, [medical reasons](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/inadmissibility/reasons/medical-inadmissibility.html), or for [misrepresentation](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/protect-fraud/consequences-fraud.html) \(not being honest in an application\)\. It is very important to carefully read and accurately answer all questions on the application form\. Contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) if you have concerns about inadmissibility\.

Below are 4 steps to help create a comprehensive application\.

## First, download the newest form[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/apply\-initial\-study\-permit/tutorial\-apply\-initial\-study\-permit\-fill\-application/\#first\-download\-the\-newest\-form](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/tutorial-apply-initial-study-permit-fill-application/#first-download-the-newest-form)

Use the “Application for a Study Permit Made Outside of Canada \[IMM 1294\]” form\.

IRCC makes periodic updates to their application forms\. Always make sure you are using the most current application form by downloading the application form from your Document Checklist on your IRCC online account\.

[Screenshot of the application form to download in your IRCC online account](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/study_permit_download_form_screenshot.png)

If you see the “Please wait…” message when downloading the form, click on the download arrow at the top right to save the file onto your computer, such as in your documents folder or desktop, and then open it from where you saved it on your computer with Adobe Reader\. You will not be able to open it from a browser\. If you do not see the arrow, move your cursor to the top of the screen and it will appear\.

[Screenshot of the please wait message from IRCC](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/ircc_please_wait_screenshot-1024x345.png)

## Get help with commonly asked questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/apply\-initial\-study\-permit/tutorial\-apply\-initial\-study\-permit\-fill\-application/\#get\-help\-with\-commonly\-asked\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/tutorial-apply-initial-study-permit-fill-application/#get-help-with-commonly-asked-questions)

**

What is a UCI?

**

UCI stands for “Unique Client Identifier,” also known as “Client ID\.” It is an eight\-digit or ten\-digit number\. **If you do not have a UCI, leave this section blank\.**

[Screenshot of the "UCI" section on your initial study permit application](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/study_permit_uci_screenshot.png)

**

What is UBC’s Designated Learning Institution \(DLI\) number?

**

UBC’s DLI is **O19330231062**\. It starts with the letter “O” and not zero\.

[Screenshot of the "DLI" section on your initial study permit application](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/study_permit_dli_number.png)

**

How do I answer “Duration of expected study”?

**

Your study permit length will usually match your program duration plus 90 days, unless your passport expires sooner\.

-   **In the “From” field**: use the “Program Start Date” shown on your Letter of Acceptance\.
-   **In the “To” field**: Add 90 days after your anticipated program completion date\.

[Screenshot of how to fill out "Duration of study" in IRCC form](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/study_permit_duration_study.png)

**

How do I fill out the “the cost of my studies” section?

**

Provide information on your expenses including your first\-year tuition fees, rent and food, travel expenses, and other estimated costs for one year\. 

For “tuition”, check your Letter of Admission for tuition costs for one year\. You should provide proof of funds which exceed the minimum of the tuition fee range, if one was provided\. 

For “room and board”, add the minimum for cost\-of\-living expenses for one year\. You should indicate at least $22,895 for the [cost\-of\-living financial requirement](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/get-documents/financial-support.html#) as of 2025\. The cost\-of\-living amount will be adjusted each year based on Statistics Canada’s low\-income cut\-off\. The amount required for [additional family members](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/get-documents/financial-support.html) depends on how many dependents you have\.

You can use these two cost calculators to help you estimate your costs:

-   [Undergraduate students](http://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/cost/)
-   [Graduate students](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/prospective-students/tuition-fees-cost-living/cost-living)

[Screenshot of the "Cost of studies" section on your initial study permit application](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/study_permit_cost_studies.png)

**Note**: exchange students coming through [Go Global](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc/coming-ubc-exchange) should indicate ‘$0’ in the ‘tuition’ field as you will not pay tuition fees to UBC, you will pay your home university\. Include a letter of explanation to address your tuition fees as an inbound exchange student and provide supporting documents, if available\. One\-term exchange students may provide estimated costs based on one term only and prorate the cost\-of\-living amount\.

**

How do I fill out the “funds available for my stay” section?

**

The amount you indicate in “*Funds available for my stay \(CAD\)*” should match the total amount of funds you are providing in your application from all sources\.

For example, if you have a combination of $20,502 in your bank account, $10,000 from your scholarship, and $63,843 from your parents, you would indicate $94,345\.

Remember, you **must** show that you have enough funds to cover your first year tuition fees, travel expenses, and the minimum for cost\-of\-living expenses\. So the amount provided under box 5 “funds available for my stay \(CAD\)” must be greater than the total amounts for tuition, room and board and other under box 4 “the cost of my studies”\.​​​​​

[Screenshot of how to fill out "Funds available" section on initial study permit application](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/study_permit_funds_available_screenshot.png)

**

How do I fill out the “Employment” section?

**

The information you provide in this section helps IRCC have a fuller picture of your activities within the last ten years:

-   Include all part\-time and full\-time jobs as well as any internships and practicum placements, even if they were unpaid\.
-   Under “*current activity*”, if you are not currently working/employed, but you are a student, write “student” as activity and your school name as “employer”\. Your ‘to’ date can be the month and year of your study permit application; for example, if you are applying in April 2026, indicate this in your ‘to’ field\. 
-   If you are working at the time of application, write the month and year of your application submission as your ‘To’ date\.
-   Fill out the form in reverse chronological order, with the most recent job/activity first\.
-   If you need more space, provide additional information in a Letter of Explanation\.

**

How do I answer “Background” questions?

**

It is very important to carefully read these questions and answer truthfully and honestly\.

Please contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) if you answered “yes” to any of the questions so that you are aware of possible implications\.

**Important:** If you have previously applied for any Canadian immigration application, including a Canadian study permit, a Temporary Resident Visa \(TRV\), a work permit, or permanent residence, whether it is approved or rejected, you must report it to IRCC by checking the box “Yes” on 2\(c\) and writing down what you applied for and what year you applied for each type of document in the box in addition to any details\.

**

How can I sign the form if I apply online?

**

You do not need to sign your name in the signature field on the bottom of page 5, but you will need to type in the date of your application if applying online\. Upload the form **without** printing or signing\.

-   After uploading all your documents, you will be asked to electronically sign your application by typing your name\.
-   **Do not** print and sign the form because you will not be able to upload it to the site\.

## Validate your form[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/apply\-initial\-study\-permit/tutorial\-apply\-initial\-study\-permit\-fill\-application/\#validate\-your\-form](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/tutorial-apply-initial-study-permit-fill-application/#validate-your-form)

When you finish filling out your application form, click the blue “Validate” button \(found on the first or last page\)\. This will highlight any missing information that is required and create an additional page with barcodes\.

-   You can make changes after the application is successfully validated – just remember to validate again\.
-   You can edit and validate as many times as you need\.

Once your application has been successfully validated, it will show the following:

[Screenshot of the barcode required to validate your TRV application](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/validate_form_screenshot.png)

If you don’t see any barcodes when you validate your application, please visit the [CIC help page](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/helpcentre/answer.asp?qnum=767&top=23)\.

## Review the Canvas course[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/apply\-initial\-study\-permit/tutorial\-apply\-initial\-study\-permit\-fill\-application/\#review\-the\-canvas\-course](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/tutorial-apply-initial-study-permit-fill-application/#review-the-canvas-course)

Sign up for the [initial study permit application review Canvas course](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/EXWLA4) to go over required documents, learn how to fill out the form, avoid common mistakes, and be ready to submit your application\.

## If applying online, take screenshots as you apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/apply\-initial\-study\-permit/tutorial\-apply\-initial\-study\-permit\-fill\-application/\#if\-applying\-online\-take\-screenshots\-as\-you\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/tutorial-apply-initial-study-permit-fill-application/#if-applying-online-take-screenshots-as-you-apply)

In case there are issues with your application submission, take screenshots of these screens:

1.  The “Your document checklist” page after all your documents have been successfully uploaded to your IRCC online account\.
2.  The “Acknowledgment of receipt” page after the application has been submitted\.
3.  After [uploading or submitting](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/helpcentre/answer.asp?qnum=1310&top=23) any ‘after\-the\-fact’ documents that an IRCC officer has requested after your original application has been submitted\.

Save your screenshots to a safe place where you can access them easily\.

Learn how to take screenshots if you’re [using a PC](http://support.microsoft.com/en-us/help/13776/windows-use-snipping-tool-to-capture-screenshots#1TC=windows-7) or [on your Mac](http://support.apple.com/en-ca/HT201361)\.

## The information on this page may change[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/apply\-initial\-study\-permit/tutorial\-apply\-initial\-study\-permit\-fill\-application/\#the\-information\-on\-this\-page\-may\-change](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/tutorial-apply-initial-study-permit-fill-application/#the-information-on-this-page-may-change)

The immigration information on this page has been reviewed and endorsed by Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultants \(RCICs\) or Regulated International Student Immigration Advisors \(RISIAs\) in compliance with the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and Regulations\. However, this is not a legal document and information may change without notice\. Always refer to [Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada](http://www.cic.gc.ca/) \(IRCC\) for the most up\-to\-date information\.

title: Gather required documents for your initial study permit application
content_markdown:
## Documents all students need[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/apply\-initial\-study\-permit/tutorial\-apply\-initial\-study\-permit\-required\-documents/\#documents\-all\-students\-need](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/tutorial-apply-initial-study-permit-required-documents/#documents-all-students-need)

All students coming to UBC will need all of the following documents\.

When possible, documents should be issued within **30 days** before submitting your application to be considered recent\. 

If you must provide several documents in a section, combine them into one file \(such as a PDF\) before uploading\. The size limit is 4MB per file; you may need to [reduce the file size](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/helpcentre/answer.asp?qnum=1213&top=23)\. 

If your documents are not in English or French, they must be accompanied by:

-   the English or French official translation; and
-   an [affidavit](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/helpcentre/glossary.asp#affidavit) from the person who completed the translation

Below are Certified Translators in British Columbia:

-   [Society of Interpreters and Translators of British Columbia](https://www.stibc.org/)
-   [MOSAIC](https://www.mosaicbc-lsp.org/)

**

Letter of Admission

**

Even if your [Letter of Admission](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-documents-required-study-permit/), or offer letter, has admission conditions that you still have left to complete, you may use your conditional Letter of Admission for your study permit application\. We do not recommend that you wait to meet the conditions before applying; “full acceptance” letters are not automatically issued\.

If you are applying for your study permit with a conditional Letter of Admission, add a section to your letter of explanation to explain how the conditions have been or will be met and provide proof if you can\.

Find out how to get your UBC Letter of Admission for your program on the [UBC PAL webpage](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-provincial-attestation-letter/#how-and-when-to-get-your-pal)\.

**

Provincial Attestation Letter

**

As of Jan 22, 2025, all students submitting study permit applications from outside Canada must include a Provincial Attestation Letter \(PAL\) with their study permit application, except for Master’s and Doctoral degree students, and exchange students through [Go Global](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc/coming-ubc-exchange)\. Find out [how to get a PAL](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-provincial-attestation-letter/)\. After you receive your PAL, you will need to upload it in your document checklist as part of your study permit application\.

If you are an incoming Master’s or Doctoral degree student you are exempt from providing a PAL with your application\. On your document checklist, you will be asked to upload proof of your exemption\. Download the [PAL exemption template](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/study_permit_pal_exemption_template.docx) \(docx\) for graduate students and personalize it with your own information\. Combine this letter with your letter of admission into one file, then upload this file in your document checklist where they request a PAL or proof of exemption\. This means you will be uploading your letter of admission in two different places on the document checklist\.

**

Proof of financial support

**

It is crucial to show strong [proof of financial support](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/get-documents/financial-support.html) from yourself and/or your sponsors, such as family members or organizations supporting you\. 

Most Canadian immigration officers interpret “evidence of sufficient funds” to mean 6 months of bank statements, savings account statements, bank drafts, or other proof that indicates you have sufficient available funds to cover the cost of 1 year in Canada including:

-   Your first year of tuition fees as indicated on your Letter of Admission
-   Travel expenses to get to and from Canada, and
-   Minimum cost\-of\-living
    -   The minimum for one year of [cost\-of\-living expenses](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/get-documents/financial-support.html) is $22,895 for an individual as of 2025, in addition to tuition fees for the first year and travel costs\. The cost\-of\-living amount will be adjusted each year based on Statistics Canada’s low\-income cut\-off\. The amount required for [additional family members](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/get-documents/financial-support.html) depends on how many dependents you have\.

You are only required to show the minimum proof of funds for tuition, cost\-of\-living expenses and return travel expenses to cover your first year of studies, even if your program is more than 1 year\. For example, if you are an undergraduate student, you do not need to provide proof of funds for all 4 years\. However, the officer who reviews your application must be satisfied that the probability of funding for future years does exist, such as if you are being supported by your parents that you provide proof of their employment, or if you have a scholarship, that it is for more than 1 year\.

For more details, please see [IRCC’s website](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/get-documents/financial-support.html)\.

Below are examples of what you can submit as proof of financial support\. Provide as many of them as apply to your situation\.

-   Your bank statements from a Canadian or overseas bank with a stamp
-   A letter from UBC that proves you are receiving financial aid/scholarship/award/teaching assistantship/research assistantship
-   Bank statements of your parents/sponsor from a Canadian or overseas bank with a stamp
-   Proof of employment for yourself/your parents/sponsor
-   Proof of business ownership/income for yourself/your parents/sponsor
-   A [Guaranteed Investment Certificate \(GIC\)](https://www.canada.ca/en/financial-consumer-agency/services/rights-responsibilities/rights-investing/rights-guaranteed-investment-certificates.html) from a participating Canadian financial institution
-   Approval for an educational loan
-   Proof of ownership of properties for yourself/your parents/sponsor 
-   Proof of any other type of income, stock, dividend etc\. for yourself/your parents/sponsor
-   It is not possible to pre\-pay tuition fees to UBC – you should show you have sufficient funds to cover your tuition fees in your application\. It is recommended that you apply for your study permit as soon as possible and do not wait for [registration](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/registration-dates/) to open\. If you have already registered in courses and paid tuition, you can provide your proof of tuition payment from Workday\. Learn how to access your [financial account activity](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/viewing-your-financial-account-activity-tuition-amount-and-payments/)\. It may take 1 to 5 days for tuition payments to appear on your account\.

If the balance\(s\) in any of the documentation above is in foreign currency, provide a screenshot of the [Bank of Canada currency converter](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/rates/exchange/currency-converter/) result \(if your currency is not listed, use [xe\.com](https://www.xe.com/)\)\.

If the proof of funds is from another person’s bank account, such as a parent or family member who is sponsoring you, they must provide proof of where their funds are coming from, for example proof of employment\. Additionally, they must write a letter \(preferably notarized\) stating that they will support you during your studies in Canada\. Providing proof of relationship and their passport is recommended\. To write a letter of financial support, they can [download our template](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/letter_financial_support_international_students.docx) \(docx\)\.

Include a summary or an index page of all the documents you are submitting for this section\. This will also allow you to clarify or explain the connection between documents, if applicable\. You can download a [Word template for the summary](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/ubc_summary_proof_funds_template.docx) \(docx\)\.

**

Passport

**

Provide a copy of the bio\-data page \(the page with your name, date of birth, passport number, expiration date, etc\.\) and a copy of every page of your passport that has stamps, visas, or markings from any country\. Most visa offices require copies of your current passport and all expired passports that you have held; be sure to check your visa office instruction guide for the requirements you must meet\.

**Important**: Your study permit will not be issued beyond your passport’s expiry date\.

-   If you do not have a passport, **apply for one immediately**\.
-   If your passport will expire soon, extend it before you apply for your study permit\.
    -   If this is not an option or passport processing time is too long, apply for a study permit with your current passport\. If you get the new passport before your application is processed, you can request to add your new passport to your application through the [IRCC’s webform](https://secure.cic.gc.ca/ClientContact/en/Application)\.
    -   If you can’t get a new study permit in time, after you arrive in Canada, extend your passport and then [extend your study permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/extend-study-permit/) from within Canada before your study permit expires\. 

**

Passport photo

**

Make sure your photo meets the specifications for the application method you’re using\.

-   **Applying online**Find digital photo specifications on the*Your document checklist* page by clicking on the question mark, in the “Instructions” column, for “Digital photo”\.
-   **At a Visa Application Centre or applying on paper  
    **You need 2 photos which meet the [IRCC’s photo specifications](https://www.canada.ca/content/dam/ircc/migration/ircc/english/pdf/photospecs-e.pdf)

**

Documents specific to your visa office

**

In addition to the documents required for students from all countries, some visa offices require additional documents\. Remember to check for **any additional documents** required by your country’s visa office\.

To get the full list of documents required by your country’s visa office:

1.  Go to the [IRCC website](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/information/applications/student.asp) for paper applications and select your country/territory from the drop\-down list\.
2.  Then select “Visa office instructions”\. This will launch a PDF specifying requirements for your visa office\.

**To avoid delays or rejection**, submit the required documents listed on the *Your document checklist* page in your [IRCC secure account](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/account.html) plus any visa office\-specific documents\.

-   For any visa office specific documents you have not already provided in your online document checklist, add them to your Letter of Explanation\. Merge your Letter of Explanation and all visa office\-specific documents into one file \(such as a PDF\) then upload the file in the “Client Information” section under *Optional Documents* in your online checklist\. If you have multiple documents, consider adding an index or table of contents in a cover page\. The file must be within 4MB in size\.

**

Letter of Explanation

**

A letter of explanation is a letter you will write yourself to describe additional factors, and a place to include additional documents to support your application\. An important part of your application is to provide an explanation and supporting documents to show the officer that you have strong ties to your home country and will leave Canada before the end of your authorized stay\. See the guideline below on how to write a letter of explanation\. 

Your letter of explanation could include:

-   Issues you would like to clarify or that the officer might find useful
-   Supporting documents, screenshots, or any other proof to support your explanation
-   Documents showing how you will meet the conditions of your Letter of Admission, if applicable
-   Additional employment history if you have run out of space in your application form
-   Additional documents required by your visa office which you have not provided elsewhere in your application
-   An explanation about your status in the country you are applying from, if you are not applying from your country of citizenship, and copies of your status documents
-   Details about your ties to your home country 

For further guidelines, check out the [How to write a Letter of Explanation guide](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/how_to_write_letter_explanation.pdf) \(pdf\)\.

You may also download our [template to write a letter of explanation](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/ubc_letter_explanation_template_word.docx) \(docx\)\. Upload this document under “Client Information” in the *Optional Documents* section of your online checklist\.

The letter of explanation that you will write should be the first page, followed by supporting documents which you then combine into one PDF to upload a single file\. 

**

Study Plan

**

To address the purpose of your studies, write a detailed study plan that is concise, clear and genuine \(see template below\)\. This may be required by your visa office and could include specific points to address\. A study plan is particularly recommended for graduate students\.

For further guidelines, check out the [How to write a Study Plan](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/how_to_write_study_plan.pdf) guide \(pdf\)\.

You may also use our [study plan Word template](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/study_plan_template.docx) \(docx\)\. Upload this document under “Client Information” in the *Optional Documents* section of your online checklist if applying online\.

**

Biometrics

**

If you apply for a study permit from outside Canada, you will be required to submit your biometrics \(fingerprints and a photo\) in\-person at a biometrics collection point outside of Canada\. 

The time it takes to submit your biometrics is not included in the processing time for your study permit and your application will not be processed until biometrics are received by the visa office\. You only need to give biometrics once every 10 years\.

American citizens, those who have provided biometrics in the past 10 years, as well as [certain individuals](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/biometrics/who-needs-to-give.html) are exempt from providing biometrics\. 

1.  Pay the biometrics fee at the same time you submit your study permit application for faster processing\.
2.  Receive your Biometrics Instruction Letter \(BIL\) online\. You will typically receive the PDF biometrics instruction letter soon after submitting your study permit application\. If you pay the biometrics fee and do not receive the biometrics instruction letter within 3 business days of submitting your application, you should submit a [webform on technical difficulties](https://secure.cic.gc.ca/enquiries-renseignements/canada-case-cas-eng.aspx) to follow up and request your BIL\.
3.  Submit your biometrics within 30 days after receiving your biometrics instruction letter\. If you are not able to provide your biometrics within 30 days of receiving your biometrics instructions letter, you need to [submit a webform to IRCC](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/biometrics/where-to-give.html) to explain why you need more time and request an extension\.

Find out where to [submit biometrics](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/biometrics/where-to-give.html)\.

**Note**: If there is no biometrics collection service point in your home country, you may need to travel to another country to give biometrics\.

## Documents you might need[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/apply\-initial\-study\-permit/tutorial\-apply\-initial\-study\-permit\-required\-documents/\#documents\-you\-might\-need](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/tutorial-apply-initial-study-permit-required-documents/#documents-you-might-need)

Depending on your specific circumstances, you may need one or more of the following documents\.

**

Medical exam

**

You will require a medical exam when applying for a study permit if you:

1.  Have lived in a [designated country or territory](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/medical-police/medical-exams/requirements-temporary-residents/country-requirements.html) for more than 6 months in the 12 months immediately before you apply\. Canada is not a designated country or territory, so this does not apply to you if you have been in Canada for more than 6 months in the past year\.
2.  Would like to work in [certain jobs](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/#if-you-work-with-children-or-seniors-in-healthcare-settings-or-in-agriculture) in Canada which bring you into close contact with vulnerable people, such as positions working with children or in healthcare settings, or if you are a medical student\.

If the above scenario applies to you, you will need a medical exam conducted by an IRCC\-approved [Panel Physician](https://www.cic.gc.ca/pp-md/pp-list.aspx)\. The doctor will send the full results to IRCC automatically\. Ask the doctor for a copy of your medical exam report \(referred to as your “e\-medical”\), which you will need to upload in your document checklist\.

You have 2 options:

1.  Take an upfront medical exam before submitting your initial study permit application, then include your e\-medical report in your application\. We recommend this option as it will save you time\. 
2.  Alternatively, apply for your study permit first and wait for a visa officer to send you a medical exam request, then provide medical exam results within 30 days of the request\. This may delay the processing of your application\.

If you are submitting a medical exam in order to work in [certain jobs](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/#if-you-work-with-children-or-seniors-in-healthcare-settings-or-in-agriculture), be sure to mention this in your letter of explanation, and request that appropriate conditions be placed on your study permit to allow you to work in restricted occupations\.

Medical exams are valid for 12 months and must be valid at the time you enter Canada\. If you will travel to Canada more than 12 months after your medical exam, you will need a new one before you travel\. Check the [travelling to Canada guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/before-you-travel/) for more details\.

**

Family Information Form \[IMM5707 or IMM5645\]

**

This form is required if it is included in your document checklist \(see sample below\) or if it is required by your visa office \(upload under *Client Information* along with your letter of explanation if it is required but does not appear in your document checklist\)\. Check [IRCC’s instruction guide](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/application-forms-guides/imm5707.html)\.

[Screenshot of the "Family information form" section of the Supporting Documents for an initial study permit application](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/study_permit_family_information_form_screenshot.jpg)

**

Co\-op/internship/practicum letter

**

If your program has a mandatory work component, such as a Co\-op, practicum, or student work placement and you have received a confirmation letter from your faculty or program, you can include it with your study permit application\.

For more information about whether you need a Co\-op or student work placement letter, check the “[apply online](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/tutorial-apply-initial-study-permit-document-checklist/#choose-your-application-method)” section of our tutorial\.

**

Schedule 1: Application for Temporary Residence \[IMM5257B\]

**

This document is required **only if** you answer “Yes” to questions 3, 4, 5 or 6 in the “*Background Information*” section of the “*Application for a Study Permit Made Outside of Canada*” form \[IMM1294\], or if it is required by your visa office\.

Most students will **not** require Schedule 1\. That is why it is listed in the “*Optional Documents*” section in your IRCC online account, if you are applying online\.

## The information on this page may change[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/apply\-initial\-study\-permit/tutorial\-apply\-initial\-study\-permit\-required\-documents/\#the\-information\-on\-this\-page\-may\-change](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/tutorial-apply-initial-study-permit-required-documents/#the-information-on-this-page-may-change)

The immigration information on this page has been reviewed and endorsed by Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultants \(RCICs\) or Regulated International Student Immigration Advisors \(RISIAs\) in compliance with the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and Regulations\. However, this is not a legal document and information may change without notice\. Always refer to [Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada](http://www.cic.gc.ca/) \(IRCC\) for the most up\-to\-date information\.

title: About study permit extensions
content_markdown:
> > Latest updates from IRCC
> 
> > Read the most [up\-to\-date IRCC updates](https://students.ubc.ca/news/2025-07-14/july-2025-latest-study-permit-information/) on topics related to study permits\.

## When should I apply?[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/extend\-study\-permit/\#when\-should\-i\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/extend-study-permit/#when-should-i-apply)

### Current students inside Canada

You can only extend your study permit if you are physically inside Canada\.

It’s recommended that you apply 5 to 6 months before your current study permit expires\. Check estimated [processing times](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/check-processing-times.html)\.

If you need to apply more than 6 months in advance for personal reasons, such as upcoming travel plans, contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support\.

To maintain status in Canada, you must submit your application before 11:59 pm [Coordinated Universal Time](https://time.is/UTC) \(UTC\), not local time, on the day your study permit expires, or change or extend your status within 90 days after your letter of completion becomes available if you’ve finished your program—whichever comes first\.

#### **If you are changing institutions**

As of Nov 8, 2024, if you [change institutions](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/change-schools.html), you must apply for a study permit extension for your new institution and most students need to receive the new study permit before beginning studies at your new institution\. If you are coming to UBC from a Canadian high school or from another post\-secondary institution, be sure to apply for a study permit extension with your UBC Letter of Admission and [Provincial Attestation Letter](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-documents-required-study-permit/) as soon as you receive them\. 

On July 4, 2025, IRCC published an update for students transferring from Canadian high schools to post\-secondary institutions\. As long as you apply for your UBC [study permit extension](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/extend-study-permit-within-canada/) inside Canada before your study permit expires or within 90 days of finishing high school – whichever comes first – you can begin studies at UBC while your study permit extension application is being processed\. If you apply then leave Canada after your [study permit becomes invalid](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/#maintaining-your-student-status), you will lose [maintained status](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/maintained-status/) and will not be able to study until you receive your study permit\. Students transferring to UBC from another post\-secondary institution must wait to receive their new study permit before beginning studies at UBC\. Check [important considerations](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/#important-considerations) for details\.

#### **If you changed institutions before Nov 8, 2024**

If you transferred to UBC from a Canadian high school or another post\-secondary institution in Canada before Nov 8, 2024, send International Student Advising a [webform](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0J8VRJgJQkuO2b4) with details about your situation before applying to extend your study permit\. An assessment must be made to determine if a PAL will be required as part of your application\. 

### New students inside Canada

Some students might be able to apply for their first study permit through the inside Canada process\. Select “[inside Canada](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/apply.html)” under “Get specific instructions on how to apply” to see the list of who is eligible to apply through the inside Canada process\. 

If you are studying at a Canadian high school on a secondary school study permit and are applying to extend your study permit to study at UBC, you can apply for a study permit extension through the inside Canada process\. Be sure to apply before your study permit expires and within 90 days of finishing high school – whichever comes first\.

If you are eligible to apply for your first study permit through the inside Canada process, review our tutorial and Canvas application review course for study permit extensions below to prepare your application, and apply as soon as you receive your Letter of Admission and [Provincial Attestation Letter](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-documents-required-study-permit/), if needed\. 

## How to extend your study permit[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/extend\-study\-permit/\#how\-to\-extend\-your\-study\-permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/extend-study-permit/#how-to-extend-your-study-permit)

Visit our tutorial for step\-by\-step instructions, a list of required documents, and other important info that will help you complete your application\.

[Go to the study permit extension tutorial](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/extend-study-permit-within-canada/)

## Before submitting your application[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/extend\-study\-permit/\#before\-submitting\-your\-application](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/extend-study-permit/#before-submitting-your-application)

Sign up for the new Canvas application review course to go over required documents, learn how to fill out the form, avoid common mistakes, and be ready to submit your application\.

[Sign up now](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/XH6JG3)

## If you will travel after applying or are outside of Canada[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/extend\-study\-permit/\#if\-you\-will\-travel\-after\-applying\-or\-are\-outside\-of\-canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/extend-study-permit/#if-you-will-travel-after-applying-or-are-outside-of-canada)

See our FAQ on the differences between applying for a study permit from [inside or outside of Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-immigration-faq/)\.

Be sure to review our [Travelling to Canada Guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/) before making travel plans\.

## If your permit expires after IRCC receives your application[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/extend\-study\-permit/\#if\-your\-permit\-expires\-after\-ircc\-receives\-your\-application](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/extend-study-permit/#if-your-permit-expires-after-ircc-receives-your-application)

If you and your family members applied for your immigration documents \(e\.g\. study permit, or work permit, visitor record, etc\.\) before they became invalid, then they expire **after** Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada \(IRCC\) **has received** your application to extend your status, you will still be considered a temporary resident of Canada until a decision about your application is made\. This is known as “[maintained status](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/maintained-status/)” \(formerly known as ‘implied status’\)\.

**

Staying in Canada with “maintained status”

**

With maintained status, you may continue studying \(and working, if eligible\) under the same conditions **as long as you remain in Canada\.** You must take action on your health insurance and request a [temporary extension of your Medical Services Plan](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/maintained-status/#medical-services-plan-msp)\.

**If you leave Canada with “maintained status”** 

You cannot resume studies or work until you have received your new study permit\.

See [travelling outside Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/travelling-outside-canada/) for more information and [contact International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support\.

## If your study permit expires and you haven’t applied for an extension[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/extend\-study\-permit/\#if\-your\-study\-permit\-expires\-and\-you\-havent\-applied\-for\-an\-extension](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/extend-study-permit/#if-your-study-permit-expires-and-you-havent-applied-for-an-extension)

If your permit expires **before** Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada \(IRCC\) receives your extension application, you will be “**out of status**”\.

### What to do if you are out of status

You must stop studying and working immediately\. You are not authorized to attend classes or work while you are out of status\.

You must [apply for restoration](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/restoration-status/) within 90 days of having lost your status\. Contact [International Student Advising for support](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) and to discuss your options\. An International Student Advisor should review your application before you submit it\.

## International Student Guide[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/extend\-study\-permit/\#international\-student\-guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/extend-study-permit/#international-student-guide)

Find everything you need to know about life as an international student at UBC’s Vancouver campus\.

[View the guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/extend\-study\-permit/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/extend-study-permit/#if-you-have-questions)

You can connect with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for questions related to immigration, health insurance, and life as an international student in Canada\.

## The information on this page may change[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/extend\-study\-permit/\#the\-information\-on\-this\-page\-may\-change](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/extend-study-permit/#the-information-on-this-page-may-change)

The immigration information on this page has been reviewed and endorsed by Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultants \(RCICs\) or Regulated International Student Immigration Advisors \(RISIAs\) in compliance with the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and Regulations\. However, this is not a legal document and information may change without notice\. Always refer to [Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada](http://www.cic.gc.ca/) \(IRCC\) for the most up\-to\-date information\.
