title: UBC documents required for your study permit
content_markdown:
## List of required documents[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/ubc\-documents\-required\-study\-permit/\#list\-of\-required\-documents](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-documents-required-study-permit/#list-of-required-documents)

Depending on your situation, you will need certain documents from UBC before you submit your immigration application\. These documents may need to be included in your study permit application, among other requirements:

-   Letter of Admission \(required for all new students\)
-   Provincial Attestation Letter \(required for most new undergraduate students\)
-   Letter of Enrolment \(for current, continuing, and returning students\)

If your program is 6 months or less in duration, you do not need to apply for a study permit\.

## Letter of Admission[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/ubc\-documents\-required\-study\-permit/\#letter\-of\-admission](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-documents-required-study-permit/#letter-of-admission)

You must [apply to UBC](https://www.ubc.ca/prospective-students/) and receive your Letter of Admission, also known as an offer letter, before you can apply for your study permit\. Depending on your program or faculty, you will need to accept your offer and might need to pay a deposit to get your Letter of Admission\.

You can use your Letter of Admission to apply for your study permit even if it has conditions\. Include a section on your [letter of explanation](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/tutorial-apply-initial-study-permit-required-documents/) to address how you will meet the condition\(s\) and provide supporting documents, if possible\.

You should be able to download your Letter of Admission from the online platform you used to apply to UBC, or it may have been sent to you by your program\. Check the [Provincial Attestation Letter](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-provincial-attestation-letter/#how-and-when-to-get-your-pal) page to find out how to get your Letter of Admission for your program\.

## Provincial Attestation Letter[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/ubc\-documents\-required\-study\-permit/\#provincial\-attestation\-letter](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-documents-required-study-permit/#provincial-attestation-letter)

A Provincial Attestation Letter \(PAL\) is a document which confirms a student has a spot in the provincial allocation for study permits and is included in the yearly federal cap to submit a study permit application\.

Learn more about the [Provincial Attestation Letter](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-provincial-attestation-letter/) and find out if you need it for your study permit application\.

## Letter of Enrolment[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/ubc\-documents\-required\-study\-permit/\#letter\-of\-enrolment](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-documents-required-study-permit/#letter-of-enrolment)

Your Letter of Enrolment shows your current registration at UBC\. This letter can be used to explain details about your studies, show current and future enrolment, and indicate the remaining time you need to complete your program\. You can only obtain one after registration has opened and you are registered\. Review [registration dates](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/registration-dates/) for the term\.

You will need a current Letter of Enrolment issued within the past 30 days for many inside Canada immigration applications, such as:

-   [Study permit extension](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/extend-study-permit/)
-   [Temporary Resident Visa \(TRV\)](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/)
-   If you’re outside Canada applying for a [study permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/about-initial-study-permits/tutorial-apply-initial-study-permit-overview/) to return as a current/returning student
-   For your [family’s applications](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/documentation-family/)

In many applications, the officer will determine the length of the immigration document based on your letter of enrolment\. Therefore, it’s important to ensure you use the correct letter with the right information\.

### Important tips for your Letter of Enrolment

**Do not** use the Letter of Admission you received when you were first accepted to UBC \(unless you are a new student or are about to start a second program at UBC\)\.

Learn how to [get your Letter of Enrolment](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/student-documents/downloading-your-confirmation-of-enrolment-letter/), known as a “Confirmation of Enrolment Letter” in Workday\. Be sure to select the most recent academic session \(Winter or Summer Session\)\. If the letter does not indicate you are enrolled [full\-time for immigration purposes](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#full-time), contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support\.

Your Letter of Enrolment indicates your remaining program length\. For undergraduate students, this is based on your Class Standing \(previously known as your “year level” in the Student Service Centre\)\. For example, if you issue your Letter of Enrolment in December 2026, and your letter states you have Class Standing 3, this indicates you would complete your program in April 2028\.

Contact an [Academic Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) from your faculty or your [graduate program staff](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/current-students/supervision) to request a customized Letter of Enrolment if:

-   You need additional time to finish your program requirements than what your Workday Letter of Enrolment indicates, for example your letter indicates you are enrolled until the end of the current academic session in April but you will need additional terms to finish your program requirements, you are in a Co\-op program, you transferred credits to UBC, you are in a thesis\-based program, or you need more time based on your anticipated course load\.
-   You are applying at the end of the Winter Session Term 2 \(Jan\-Apr\) or during the Summer Session \(May\-Aug\) before [registration opens](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/registration-dates/) for the following Winter Session \(Sep\-Apr\)\.
-   You are on a [gap in studies](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/taking-time-away-school-international/)\. Contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support with your application\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/ubc\-documents\-required\-study\-permit/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-documents-required-study-permit/#if-you-have-questions)

For support with obtaining your Letter of Admission:

-   **Undergraduate students**: contact [undergraduate admissions](https://you.ubc.ca/contact-us/)\.
-   **Graduate students**: contact your [graduate program staff](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/current-students/supervision)\.
-   **Current and returning students**: contact [Academic Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) or your [graduate program staff](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/current-students/supervision) for your Letter of Enrolment\.
-   **VIRS and exchange students**: contact [Go Global](https://global.ubc.ca/go-global/contact-go-global)\.
-   **Unclassified, access studies and visiting students:** contact [Enrolment Services Advisors](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

For support with getting your Provincial Attestation Letter, contact [ubc\.pal@ubc\.ca](mailto:ubc.pal@ubc.ca)\.

For support with your study permit application, travel documents, or other immigration questions, contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/)\.

## International Student Guide[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/ubc\-documents\-required\-study\-permit/\#international\-student\-guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-documents-required-study-permit/#international-student-guide)

Find everything you need to know about life as an international student at UBC’s Vancouver campus\.

[View the guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/)

title: Taking time away from school for international students
content_markdown:
## About gaps in studies[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/taking\-time\-away\-school\-international/\#about\-gaps\-in\-studies](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/taking-time-away-school-international/#about-gaps-in-studies)

You may need time away from studies, whether it be for health reasons, a family emergency, because you are in\-between programs, or other reasons\.

All reasons for taking time away from studies will be referred to as “gaps” in the sections below\.

As an international student, you have specific considerations to think about when taking a gap\. Taking a gap could negatively impact:

1.  Your current [student status](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/#maintaining-your-student-status) in Canada
2.  Your current [eligibility to work](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/) on and off campus
3.  Your future eligibility for the [Post\-Graduation Work Permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/post-graduation-work-permit/) \(PGWP\)

As of Nov 8, 2024, if you [change institutions](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/change-schools.html), you must apply for a study permit extension for your new institution and most students need to receive the new study permit before beginning studies at your new institution\.

If you are thinking of withdrawing from courses, see [immigration impacts of part\-time studies and withdrawing from courses](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/immigration-impacts-part-time-studies-withdrawing-courses/)\.

## Types of gaps[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/taking\-time\-away\-school\-international/\#types\-of\-gaps](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/taking-time-away-school-international/#types-of-gaps)

You must “actively pursue studies” in order to [maintain your student status](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/#maintaining-your-student-status) in Canada and your eligibility for the [Post\-Graduation Work Permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/post-graduation-work-permit/)\. The length and type of gap determine whether you are considered to be actively pursuing studies during that time\.

### Gaps considered actively pursuing studies if 150 days or less

-   UBC authorized leaves of absences \(see below to learn more\)
-   [Deferring your program start date](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#deferred-enrolment) after arrival in Canada 
-   Undergraduate students on a [scheduled break](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#scheduled-break) in the summer session
-   Strike or school closure

Your 150\-day period begins during the following times depending on your situation:

-   **Undergraduate students on authorized leave**  
    If it is not your first term of study and you dropped all courses before the [add/drop deadline](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/course-change-dates/), your leave would start the first day of classes for the term\. If you withdraw with a “W”, your leave would start on the day you withdrew from all courses\. 
-   **Graduate students on an authorized leave**  
    Your leave begins on either the first day of classes of the term, or the day your leave was approved by G\+PS —whichever comes last\. For more details, review the [leave of absence policy](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/current-students/managing-your-program/leave-absence) for graduate students\.
-   **Changing programs at UBC after finishing your program**  
    The day your [letter of completion](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/post-graduation-work-permit/#when-to-apply-for-a-pgwp) first becomes available
-   **Deferring your start date after arrival in Canada**  
    Contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support\.

### Gaps which are not considered actively pursuing studies

-   Approved leaves that are longer than 150 days
-   Gaps beyond 150 days when deferring program start date after arrival in Canada 
-   Gaps as a result of changing programs at UBC without finishing your program
-   Any other gap not on the approved list above
-   Gaps beyond 150 days due to a strike or school closure

## Next steps[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/taking\-time\-away\-school\-international/\#next\-steps](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/taking-time-away-school-international/#next-steps)

**

If you have taken a gap in the past

**

If your study permit is [still valid](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/), no immediate action is necessary until you make your next immigration application, such as for a post\-graduation work permit\. However, if your study permit is no longer valid, or you are unsure if your study permit is still valid, contact International Student Advising for support\.

Collect as many documents as you can related to the reason for your gap in studies\. See “documents to prepare” below for more information\.

**If you took a gap in studies during Winter Term 2 2019 \(January to April 2020\) or Summer Session 2020 \(September to May 2020\)**

There was a temporary IRCC policy for these terms due to the onset of COVID\-19\. See our [FAQs for details](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-immigration-health-insurance-faq/#online-courses-and-pgwp)\.

**If you are an undergraduate student who took a gap in studies in Winter Session 2020 \(September 2020 to April 2021\) or earlier**

Authorized leave for undergraduate students was not available at this time and you would not have been considered actively pursuing studies\. Connect with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support\.

**If you are an undergraduate student who took a gap in studies in **or after September** 2021**

Starting September 2021, under the International Undergraduate Leave Procedure, students in good academic standing could request a leave letter to show they were on leave for one or both winter terms\. If you took one or both terms off, request a letter through your academic advising office as soon as possible\. If you have a leave letter, keep it until you need to show it to IRCC\. If you are unable to get a leave letter, or your leave was longer than 150 days, contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support\.

**

If you take a gap which is considered actively pursuing studies

**

**Status in Canada and eligibility to stay**

You are considered to be [maintaining your student status](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/#maintaining-your-student-status) and can stay in Canada for up to 150 days if your gap is considered to be active pursuit of studies\. No immediate action is necessary if you will be on a gap that is less than 150 days or before your study permit expires, whichever comes first\. 

Summer is considered a [scheduled break](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#scheduled-break) for undergraduate students, and no enrolment in courses is required\. You do not need to request an approved leave in order to take a gap during the summer, and you may be eligible to work full time during the summer scheduled break if you meet the eligibility criteria\. The summer scheduled break is considered an active pursuit of study for undergraduate students\.

**Working during your gap**

As soon as you are no longer enrolled in full\-time studies, you are not eligible to [work in Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/) during an academic term, and also not eligible to work during scheduled breaks before and after the term in which you are taking a gap\. If you have a co\-op work permit, you cannot use it for work unrelated to studies\. To be eligible to work while you are on a gap, you must have a valid work permit which is unrelated to studies, which in general can be difficult to obtain\. 

**Impact on your Post\-Graduation Work Permit \(PGWP\) in the future**

In general, your eligibility for the [PGWP](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/post-graduation-work-permit/) should not be impacted if you are on a gap which is considered actively pursuing studies for less than 150 days, however the officer who reviews your application will make the final decision\. You should collect as many documents as you can related to the reason for your gap in studies\. See “documents to prepare” below for more information\. 

When you apply for the PGWP, write a letter of explanation about the reason for your gap in studies and provide as many supporting documents as possible\. Contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for assistance\.

**

If you take a gap that is an authorized leave of absence longer than 150 days

**

**Status in Canada and eligibility to stay**

A gap that is longer than 150 days is not considered to be actively pursuing studies\. 

This applies even if you have a UBC authorized leave of absence that is longer than 150 days, for example, an authorized leave for one year\. Because a gap that is longer than 150 days is not considered to be an active pursuit of studies, you must take action in order to remain compliant with the conditions of your study permit\. 

Before the first 150\-day period is over, you must do **one** of the following:

-   Apply for a [Visitor Record](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/extend-stay.html) to stay in Canada as a visitor, which does not allow you to work\.
-   Hold a [work permit](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/permit.html) unrelated to studies \(if eligible\)\. In general, these are difficult to qualify for and you may find an [authorized immigration representative](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/find-regulated-immigration-consultant-or-lawyer/) outside UBC for advice\.
-   Leave Canada\.
-   Start or resume studies\. If you [change institutions](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/change-schools.html), as of Nov 8, 2024, you must apply for a study permit extension for your new institution and most students need to receive the new study permit before beginning studies at your new institution\. Contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support\. If you plan to return to UBC, check with an [Academic Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) from your faculty to see if your credits can be transferred back to UBC or count towards your program requirements\.

If your authorized leave is longer than 150 days, your study permit may become invalid\. This could impact your eligibility to remain in Canada, as well as your ability to return to your studies\. Contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) to discuss your situation and options\.

**Exception**: UBC undergraduate students on authorized leave beginning in Winter Term 2 do not need to take further action on your status in the summer scheduled break since UBC considers undergraduate students during summer to be on a [scheduled break](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#scheduled-break) for immigration purposes\.

**Working during your gap**

As soon as you are no longer enrolled in full\-time studies, you are not eligible to [work in Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/) during an academic term, and also not eligible to work during scheduled breaks before and after the term in which you are taking a gap\. If you have a co\-op work permit, you cannot use it for work unrelated to studies\. To be eligible to work while you are on a gap, you must have a valid work permit which is unrelated to studies, which in general can be difficult to obtain\. 

**Impact on your Post\-Graduation Work Permit \(PGWP\) in the future**

Taking gaps which are not considered actively pursuing studies can impact your PGWP eligibility\. You should collect as many documents as you can related to the reason for your gap in studies\. See “documents to prepare” below for more information\. 

When you apply for the PGWP, write a letter of explanation about the reason for your gap in studies and provide as many supporting documents as possible\. You can still submit a PGWP application; however, unfortunately, there is no guarantee the application will be approved\. The officer who reviews your application will decide whether or not to approve the application on a case\-by\-case basis based on your individual circumstances and will make the final decision\.

**

If you take a gap which is not considered actively pursuing studies

**

**Status in Canada and eligibility to stay**

You are not considered to be meeting your requirements as a student and cannot remain in Canada during the gap without taking further action\.

You must do **one** of the following before your gap begins:

-   Apply for a [Visitor Record](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/extend-stay.html) to stay in Canada as a visitor, which does not allow you to work or study in Canada\. You should submit your application for a visitor record before your gap begins\.
-   Hold a [work permit](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/permit.html) unrelated to studies \(if eligible\)\. In general, these are difficult to qualify for and you may find an [authorized immigration representative](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/find-regulated-immigration-consultant-or-lawyer/) outside UBC for advice\.
-   Leave Canada for the duration of the gap\.
-   Start or resume studies\. As of **Nov 8, 2024**, if you [change institutions](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/change-schools.html), you must apply for a study permit extension for your new institution and most students need to receive the new study permit before beginning studies at your new institution\. Contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support\. If you plan to return to UBC, ask an [Academic Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) from your faculty if your credits can be transferred back to UBC or count towards your program requirements\. If you will need to take a gap because you have been required to withdraw from UBC due to a failed year, contact International Student Advising as soon as possible for support\. 

If you are not actively enrolled at UBC or on an approved academic leave, your study permit may become invalid\. This could impact your eligibility to remain in Canada, as well as your ability to return to your studies\. Contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) to discuss your situation and options\.

**Work eligibility**

As soon as you are no longer enrolled in full\-time studies, you are not eligible to [work in Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/) during the academic term, and are also not eligible to work during scheduled breaks before and after the term in which you are taking a gap\. If you have a co\-op work permit, you cannot use it for work unrelated to studies\. To be eligible to work you must have a work permit which is unrelated to studies, which in general can be difficult to obtain\.

**Impact on your Post\-Graduation Work Permit \(PGWP\) in the future**

Taking gaps which are not considered actively pursuing studies can impact your PGWP eligibility\. You should collect as many documents as you can related to the reason for your gap in studies\. See “documents to prepare” below for more information\. 

When you apply for the PGWP, write a letter of explanation about the reason for your gap in studies and provide as many supporting documents as possible\. You can still submit a PGWP application; however, unfortunately, there is no guarantee the application will be approved\. The officer who reviews your application will decide whether or not to approve the application on a case\-by\-case basis based on your individual circumstances and will make the final decision\.

**

If you might take a gap in the future: Authorized Leave

**

**Undergraduate students**

Starting from the 2021/22 Winter Session, UBC offers a procedure for international undergraduate students to document their authorized leaves\. The undergraduate leave procedure allows you to take time away from studies and still be considered to be actively pursuing studies, maintaining the conditions of your study permit and maintaining eligibility for the Post\-Graduation Work Permit program for leaves that are up to 150 days\.

UBC Vancouver Senate’s  [Academic Leave Policy](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/academic-leave) enables students in good academic standing to take up to a year away from studies without having to reapply for admission, though note that leaves longer than 150 days may have an immigration impact\.

If you want to prove to IRCC that you were on an authorized leave, you must request the leave and receive a letter from UBC confirming that you are authorized to take the leave\.

**When to drop or withdraw from courses**

-   If it is your first term in your program:
    -   If Winter Term 1 is your first term in your program and you drop all courses before the [last day to drop courses without a W](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/course-change-dates/), and you are registered in Term 2, you would be considered to have deferred enrolment for immigration purposes\. You would not need and would not be eligible for an authorized leave in Term 1\.
    -   If in your first term in your program you withdraw from all courses after the [Course change dates](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/course-change-dates/) with a W, you might qualify for the Academic Leave Policy\. The leave would start on the day you withdraw\.
-   If it is not your first term in your program:
    -   If you drop all courses before the [last day to drop courses without a W](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/course-change-dates/), then your leave would start on the first day of classes for that term, or 
    -   If you withdraw from courses before the [deadline to drop a course with a W](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/course-change-dates/), then your leave would start on the day you withdrew from all courses\.

**If you withdraw** ***after*** **the deadline to drop a course with a W**, you will not be eligible for an authorized leave for that term\.

**When to request a leave letter**

You can request a leave letter as soon as registration opens for the term\(s\) for which you are requesting a leave letter\. We recommend you request a leave letter by mid\-October for leaves starting Term 1, or mid\-February for leaves starting Term 2, so your leave will be recorded accurately in the Immigration Report which IRCC requires from UBC each winter term\.

**Eligibility for a leave letter**

To be eligible to request a leave letter, you must meet all of the following requirements:

-   Request a leave letter for one or more winter terms in Winter Session 2021 \(starting September 2021\) or later
-   Be eligible to register as of the first day of classes for each term for which you’re requesting a leave letter
-   Have no active registration in the term\(s\) for which you’re requesting a leave letter
-   Request a leave letter for a maximum of one full academic session \(Winter Term 1 \+ 2\) plus any number of one\-term leaves per program; however, programs reserve the right to deny leave letters if sufficient academic progress is not being made
-   Be an international student in a program that leads to a UBC degree, diploma or certificate and to which *graduate* student leave policies don’t apply
-   Have withdrawn from courses in time \(read “when to drop or withdraw from courses” above\)
-   Meet eligibility as specified by your faculty’s academic advising office

**How to request a leave letter**

If you are considering taking a gap in studies, follow these steps:

1.  After reading this page, carefully consider whether you will take Term 1, Term 2, or both terms away from studies\.
2.  Talk to an [Academic Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) to check your program requirements and discuss your options for taking a gap and returning to studies later\. You must meet all academic regulations of your program\. Taking a leave does not guarantee courses will be available when you return to studies\. 
3.  Carefully review how taking time away from studies impacts your immigration and other potential impacts on this page, particularly if you will be on leave for more than 150 days and will be in Canada during your leave\. Contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) if you have any questions about the immigration and health insurance impacts of taking a gap\.
4.  After you withdraw from all courses in Term 1, Term 2, or both terms, send a request to your [Academic advising office](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/)\. Tell them you are requesting a leave and for which term\(s\)\.
5.  If they agree, the authorized leave letter will be emailed to you\. The leave will not appear on your transcript\. Keep the authorized leave letter on file, and include it with future IRCC applications as needed\.

Your authorized leave letter will say when your leave began\. You can remain in Canada for 150 days after that date\.

Leaves longer than 150 days affect your Post\-Graduation Work Permit eligibility and status in Canada\.

**If you are not eligible for an authorized leave**

If you take a gap in your studies and are not eligible for an authorized leave, there could be serious impacts to your status in Canada and the validity of your study permit\. Please connect with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) as soon as possible for support\.

**Graduate students and students in the Diploma in Accounting and Juris Doctor programs**

If your leave of absence is approved, you could remain in Canada for 150 days after:

-   The day your leave was approved, or
-   The first day of classes of the term in which your leave starts, whichever comes last\.

If you plan to take a gap:

1.  After reading this page, carefully consider which in term\(s\) you plan to take time away from studies\.
2.  If you are a graduate student, review UBC’s [Graduate Student Leaves of Absence policy](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-graduate-and-postdoctoral-studies/classification-students/leave-status)\.
3.  Talk to your [program staff](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/current-students/supervision-advising/program-advising) to discuss your options for taking a gap and returning to studies later, as well as any impacts on funding\.
4.  Contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) if you have any questions about the immigration and health insurance impacts of taking a gap\. 

## Documents to prepare[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/taking\-time\-away\-school\-international/\#documents\-to\-prepare](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/taking-time-away-school-international/#documents-to-prepare)

Whether you have had a gap in studies in the past, are currently on a gap, or plan to take a gap in studies in the future, you are **not** required to notify IRCC right away\. 

However, no matter the reason or length of your gap, you **must keep documentation** in case you are asked to show why you took the leave and/or include them in your future Post\-Graduation Work Permit application\. Prepare the below documents and connect with an International Student Advisor before submitting your application\.

### Step 1\. Download the UBC Acknowledgment Letter

This [UBC Acknowledgement Letter](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/ubc_acknowledgment_letter.pdf) \(pdf\) affirms UBC’s policy towards time taken away \(e\.g\., gaps\) from studies\.

### Step 2\. Create a timeline

Create a list in chronological order of all decisions, events, and action steps leading up to your gap in studies\. Include key dates which would be helpful for the officer to understand your circumstances; for example, the date that you withdrew from courses, received approval for a deferral, left and returned to Canada, received medical care, had a family emergency occur, etc\. Keep this timeline for your records in case you are asked for information from IRCC or need to write a letter of explanation for a future immigration application\.  

### Step 3\. Gather supporting documents

Gather as many documents as possible related to your reason for your gap in studies and keep scanned and original paper copies \(if applicable\) in an accessible, safe place\. 

Examples include a doctor’s recommendation for treatment, hospital documents, flight tickets showing when you left and returned to Canada, letters issued by your program or faculty, documents relating to a family emergency, confirmation of your internship or military service, etc\. Any documents which are not in English or French will need an official translation if you submit them to IRCC\.

#### Letter of support

If possible, request a letter of support with the below guidelines:

-   The person should be aware of the reasons you took a gap, for example a doctor, counsellor, or advisor\.
-   The letter should contain factual information to attest to the reason for your gap in studies\.
-   Individuals can only attest to things they have not observed or witnessed themselves\.

## Potential impacts of taking a gap[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/taking\-time\-away\-school\-international/\#potential\-impacts\-of\-taking\-a\-gap](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/taking-time-away-school-international/#potential-impacts-of-taking-a-gap)

### Traveling on a gap

Ensure your [study permit is valid](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/) and that your entry document \([Temporary Resident Visa](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/) or [Electronic Travel Authorization](https://onlineservices-servicesenligne.cic.gc.ca/eta/applicationQuery)\) is valid to return to Canada\. See our [Travelling to Canada guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/) to learn about what documents to prepare before you travel\. If you had a gap that is not considered “actively pursuing studies”, are changing institutions, or had a gap of more than 150 days, contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support\. 

If you have not registered for courses before returning to Canada, request a letter from your academic advisor or graduate staff before re\-entering Canada\. This letter should state that you are eligible to return to your program of studies at the end of your gap\. Upon return to Canada, if you are asked by an officer, present this letter along with any documentation of your break \(e\.g\., leave approval from G\+PS if applicable, copies of plane tickets proving when you left Canada, etc\.\)\.

### Study permit validity and extension during a gap

After your gap, you can resume studies on your current study permit if it is [still valid](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/)\. If you had a gap that is not considered “actively pursuing studies”, are changing institutions, or had a gap of more than 150 days, contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support\.

If your study permit will expire or become invalid during your gap, contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) to discuss your options to apply for a study permit from inside or outside Canada\. You may need to provide additional documents to explain how you plan to resume your studies\.

### Medical Services Plan \(MSP\)

It is very important to maintain valid health insurance at all times to avoid medical bills and to help you access health support when you need it\. Your MSP coverage is usually valid for the same length as your study permit\.

If you will leave Canada for an extended time or your study permit will expire during your gap, see our [MSP page](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/) for information on next steps\.

### AMS/GSS/UBCSUO Health and Dental

Check if you maintain eligibility for the [Alma Mater Society \(AMS\)](https://www.ams.ubc.ca/student-services/health-dental/), [Graduate Student Society \(GSS\)](http://gss.ubc.ca/health-dental/), or [UBC Students’ Union Okanagan \(UBCSUO\)](https://www.suo.ca/health-dental/) Health and Dental Plan\. Coverage ends on August 31 each year and you must have basic health insurance, such as MSP, to be able to make a claim\. 

### Social Insurance Number

Your [Social Insurance Number \(SIN\)](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/) remains valid until the expiry date, however you can only [work in Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/) if you are enrolled full\-time for immigration purposes, or are eligible to work on a scheduled break\. Having a valid SIN is not sufficient to work in Canada\.

### Dependents’ status

If your common\-law partner or spouse has a work permit as a result of your study permit, it remains valid until the expiry date indicated on the work permit unless there is a condition which says otherwise\.

If you have children, they may continue to study with or without a study permit while your study permit is valid, even if you have applied for visitor status\. 

However, if you are on visitor status due to taking a gap of 150 days or more and your study permit and your spouse’s open study or work permit will expire, your children must obtain their own study permit\.

See [documentation for your family](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/documentation-family/) for more information and contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support\.

### Scholarships/awards or other funding

If you are currently receiving funding, such as a fellowship, scholarship or award, check with your funding agency to see if taking a gap will impact your eligibility\.

If you are an undergraduate student and have financial assistance or awards, check with an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) to see if taking a gap will affect your funding\.

If you are a graduate student and receive funding, check with your [graduate program staff](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/current-students/supervision-advising/program-advising) to see if taking a gap will affect your funding\.

### Eligibility for on\-campus housing

Ask about your eligibility to remain in on\-campus housing with [Student Housing and Community Services](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/eligibility/)\.

## International Student Guide[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/taking\-time\-away\-school\-international/\#international\-student\-guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/taking-time-away-school-international/#international-student-guide)

Find everything you need to know about life as an international student at UBC’s Vancouver campus\.

[View the guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/taking\-time\-away\-school\-international/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/taking-time-away-school-international/#if-you-have-questions)

You can connect with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for questions related to immigration, health insurance, and life as an international student in Canada\.

## The information on this page may change[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/taking\-time\-away\-school\-international/\#the\-information\-on\-this\-page\-may\-change](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/taking-time-away-school-international/#the-information-on-this-page-may-change)

The immigration information on this page has been reviewed and endorsed by Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultants \(RCICs\) or Regulated International Student Immigration Advisors \(RISIAs\) in compliance with the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and Regulations\. However, this is not a legal document and information may change without notice\. Always refer to [Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada](http://www.cic.gc.ca/) \(IRCC\) for the most up\-to\-date information\.

title: Temporary Resident Visa (TRV)
content_markdown:
## About the Temporary Resident Visa \(TRV\)[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv/\#about\-the\-temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/#about-the-temporary-resident-visa-trv)

A Temporary Resident Visa \(TRV\), also referred to as a “visitor visa” or “entry visa”, is a travel document that is placed in your passport and is used to enter or re\-enter Canada\.

It does not give you any status inside Canada and is usually issued for the same length of time as your study or work permit\. A TRV allows you to **travel to Canada \(that is, to the border\)** while a [study permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/) allows you to stay and study inside Canada\. A study permit is the document showing your status inside Canada, but you must have a valid TRV in order to enter Canada if you are a citizen of a visa\-required country\.

## Do I need a TRV?[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv/\#do\-i\-need\-a\-trv](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/#do-i-need-a-trv)

If you’re a citizen of a visa\-required country, you will need a TRV to travel to or re\-enter Canada\.

If you are from a visa\-exempt country, you will need an [Electronic Travel Authorization \(eTA\)](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/eta.html) to travel to Canada by air\.

U\.S\. citizens and lawful permanent residents of the US do not require TRVs or eTAs\.

Check [entry requirements by country](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/entry-requirements-country.html) and IRCC’s [“Find out if you need a visa to travel to Canada”](https://www.cic.gc.ca/english/visit/visas.asp) tool for more information\. Once you are in Canada, you are not required to have a valid TRV since it is only needed for entry to Canada\. However, it is highly recommended to always have a valid TRV in case you have an unexpected trip abroad\. Otherwise you must apply for a TRV from outside Canada, which may take a long time, and you may not be able to return to Canada in time to resume studies or work\.

## Getting a TRV[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv/\#getting\-a\-trv](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/#getting-a-trv)

### If you apply for an initial study permit or Post Graduation Work Permit \(PGWP\) from outside of Canada

You do not need to apply for a TRV separately if you apply for an initial study permit or a Post\-Graduation Work Permit \(PGWP\) from outside Canada\. When your [initial study permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/) or [PGWP](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/post-graduation-work-permit/) is approved, you will automatically be issued a TRV along with your study or work permit\.

### If you are in Canada

When you apply to [extend your study permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/extend-study-permit-within-canada/) or apply for a PGWP from inside Canada, a new TRV is not automatically issued\. You have to wait until you have received a new study permit or PGWP, then apply for a TRV from within Canada\. Your TRV will normally be issued with the same expiry date as your new study or work permit\.

It is best to receive your new TRV before leaving Canada\. In general, estimated [processing times](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/check-processing-times.html) for applications outside of Canada are longer and you will need to provide more documents\.

Apply for a TRV well in advance of travel\. Be cautious about booking non\-refundable travel plans before you receive your TRV\. The published processing times do not include the time it takes to mail your passport to Ottawa—usually the process takes around 1 month\. If you must provide [biometrics](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/campaigns/biometrics/facts.html), apply for your TRV earlier to allow for this extra step\.

[Go to the TRV tutorial](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial/)

### Before submitting your application

Sign up for the Canvas application review course to go over your application with helpful videos and learn about common mistakes\.

[Sign up now](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/CAFA9F)

## If your TRV expires before you return to Canada[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv/\#if\-your\-trv\-expires\-before\-you\-return\-to\-canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/#if-your-trv-expires-before-you-return-to-canada)

You can apply for a TRV from outside of Canada with a digital copy of your study or work permit\. Review our [TRV tutorial](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial/), then review the [TRV from outside of Canada guide](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/about-visitor-visa.html) since applications for TRVs from outside Canada are different\. Be sure to include any additional documents required by your visa office\.

To find the instructions for your visa office, go to [IRCC’s TRV page](https://www.cic.gc.ca/english/information/applications/visa.asp), select your country in the “apply on paper” section, then see the visa office instructions PDF\. Make sure to write a letter of explanation and make it clear that you are applying for a TRV to return to Canada to continue studying or working\. Include any additional documents required from your visa office along with your letter of explanation in the “Client Information” section, under “Optional Documents” in your online application\.

## Important considerations[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv/\#important\-considerations](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/#important-considerations)

### Exchange, VIRS, visiting and unclassified students

If you will study at UBC for **less than six months**, apply for a TRV as soon as you receive your Letter of Admission by [completing the steps](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/about-visitor-visa.html) provided by the Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada \(IRCC\)\.

### Visitors

If you change to visitor status or your dependent family members are in Canada as visitors, you are not able to apply for a TRV through the inside Canada process\. Visitors in Canada can only [apply for a TRV](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/about-visitor-visa.html) through the Canadian visa office responsible for their country of citizenship\.

### Travelling outside of Canada during your studies

You must have a valid Temporary Resident Visa \(TRV\) or [Electronic Travel Authorization \(eTA\)](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/eta.html) to re\-enter Canada if you’re planning to travel outside of Canada during your studies\. US citizens and lawful permanent residents of the US do not require TRVs or eTAs\.

Before making any travel plans, check [travelling outside of Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/travelling-outside-canada/) and the [Travelling to Canada Guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/) to prepare for your return\.

### If you get a new passport

If you have received a new passport or you will renew your passport while abroad and your TRV is in your previous passport, you can continue using your TRV until it expires\. You will need to travel with both your old passport with the TRV and your new passport\. 

### TRV validity and change of status 

TRVs are valid until the expiry date listed on the document, unlike [study permits](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/), which become automatically invalid 90 days after your letter of completion first becomes available\. 

You can also continue using your TRV if it says ‘visitor’ \(V\-1\), ‘student’ \(S\-1\) or ‘worker’ \(W\-1\), even if that is not your status\. For example if you previously had a study permit and now have a Post\-Graduation Work Permit, your TRV is normally valid if it has not expired\. 

You may be issued a TRV with a ‘V\-1’ code, even if you applied for a study or work permit\. This is not an error and you can use your TRV until the expiry date\.

### Travelling to the United States

You may not need a valid TRV to re\-enter Canada if you meet all of the following:

-   Have a valid study permit or work permit, or hold valid visitor status in Canada
-   Leave Canada to visit only the United States
-   Return to Canada by the end of the authorized period of your stay in Canada

Please note that re\-entry to Canada is always at the discretion of the officer at the border\. You can reference the [TRV exemptions](https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/sor-2002-227/section-190.html) from the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations Section 190\(3\)\(f\)\. 

In addition, be sure to meet [US immigration requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/travelling-outside-canada#visiting-the-united-states)\. Note that we cannot provide US immigration advice\.

## If your passport containing a TRV is lost or stolen[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv/\#if\-your\-passport\-containing\-a\-trv\-is\-lost\-or\-stolen](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/#if-your-passport-containing-a-trv-is-lost-or-stolen)

You must first replace your passport if your passport with a valid TRV is lost or stolen\.

Once you have a new passport, you can apply for a new TRV\. Include a letter of explanation that contains the police report number and a brief explanation about why you are applying\.

## The information on this page may change[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv/\#the\-information\-on\-this\-page\-may\-change](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/#the-information-on-this-page-may-change)

The immigration information on this page has been reviewed and endorsed by Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultants \(RCICs\) or Regulated International Student Immigration Advisors \(RISIAs\) in compliance with the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and Regulations\. However, this is not a legal document and information may change without notice\. Always refer to [Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada](http://www.cic.gc.ca/) \(IRCC\) for the most up\-to\-date information\.

## International Student Guide[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv/\#international\-student\-guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/#international-student-guide)

Find everything you need to know about life as an international student at UBC’s Vancouver campus\.

[View the guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/#if-you-have-questions)

You can connect with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for questions related to immigration, health insurance, and life as an international student in Canada\.

title: Complete your TRV application from within Canada
content_markdown:
Your application form is an important part of your application\. Missing or incorrect information can negatively impact the outcome of your application\. Below are five steps to a comprehensive application\.

## First, download the newest form\(s\)[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv/apply\-temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv\-within\-canada\-tutorial/apply\-temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv\-within\-canada\-tutorial\-application\-form/\#first\-download\-the\-newest\-forms](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial-application-form/#first-download-the-newest-forms)

IRCC makes periodic updates to their application forms\. Always make sure you are using the most current application form\(s\) by downloading the application form\(s\) directly from your MyCIC Document Checklist\.

[Screenshot of the document checklist for the TRV application](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/1.-document-checklist-trv.jpg)

1.  Download applicable forms by putting your cursor over the document name\. You’ll see a note that says “\(Opens a new window\)”; this indicates a form can be downloaded\.
2.  If you see a “Please wait…” message when you’re downloading a form:
    -   Click on the download arrow at the top right to save the file onto your computer and then open it with [Adobe Reader](https://get.adobe.com/reader/)\.
    -   If you do not see the arrow, move your cursor to the top of the screen and it will appear\.

[Screenshot of the "Please wait" message on screen from IRCC](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/ircc_please_wait_screenshot-1.jpg)

## Next, review your application form\(s\)[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv/apply\-temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv\-within\-canada\-tutorial/apply\-temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv\-within\-canada\-tutorial\-application\-form/\#next\-review\-your\-application\-forms](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial-application-form/#next-review-your-application-forms)

**Required for all applicants:** “Application for Visitor Visa \(Temporary Resident Visa\) \[IMM5257E\]” form

The “Family information \[IMM5707\]” form is only required for some applicants\. **You cannot sign this form electronically\.** Instead, you should fill out the form, print it out and sign the applicable section\(s\) before uploading your completed form\.

## Get help with commonly asked questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv/apply\-temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv\-within\-canada\-tutorial/apply\-temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv\-within\-canada\-tutorial\-application\-form/\#get\-help\-with\-commonly\-asked\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial-application-form/#get-help-with-commonly-asked-questions)

**

What is a UCI?

**

UCI stands for “Unique Client Identifier,” also known as “Client ID\.” It is an eight or ten\-digit number on your study permit; your UCI has this format: 0000\-0000 or 00\-0000\-0000\.

[Screenshot of the UCI number for the TRV application](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/trv_uci_screenshot.jpg)

**

What visa am I applying for?

**

Choose Visitor Visa

[Screenshot of how to answer your "Visa required" section for the TRV application](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/trv_visa_screenshot.jpg)

**

How do I fill out the “Current mailing address” section?

**

Inaccurate or incomplete information will negatively impact your ability to get your passport returned, if your TRV is approved\.

-   A [P\.O\. Box](https://www.canadapost.ca/web/en/products/details.page?article=postal_boxes) is a lockable mailbox located in a post office station\. Your mailbox number is **not** a P\.O\. Box number\.
-   A street number is the main number on the outside of a building\. Some “street names” also contain numbers, such as *West 10\[th\] Ave*, but this number is a street name\.
-   If you live in a residence on campus, you may have an assigned mailbox number\. You may put your mailbox number in brackets before the street name and spell out “mailbox: your mailbox number”\.
-   If you do not have an assigned mailbox number, you can put your apartment number under Apt/Unit\.

[Screenshot of what to fill out for the address section during the TRV application](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/trv_address_screenshot.jpg)

**

How do I fill out the “Details of Visit to Canada” section?

**

-   If you are a study permit holder, you are a “returning student”\. You may type in “UBC” as “my school”\.
-   If you are a work permit holder, you are a “returning worker”\. You may type in your company’s name as “my employer”\.

[Screenshot of the "Details of Visit to Canada" section](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/details_of_visit_screenshot.jpg)

**

How do I fill out the “Indicate how long you plan to stay” section?

**

-   **In the “From” field**: type in the date when you will submit this application
-   **In the “To” field**: type in the expiry date of your current study permit/work permit

[Screenshot of how to fill out the length of your stay for the TRV application](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/trv_stay_length_screenshot.jpg)

**

How do I fill out the “Funds available” section?

**

The amount you indicate in “funds available for my stay \(CAD\)” should match the total amount of funds you are showing as proof\. Remember, you must show you have proof of funds to cover at least $20,635 for the cost\-of\-living financial requirement in 2024 and one year of tuition fees\.

[Screenshot of how to fill out the Funds Available section for the TRV application](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/trv_funds_available_screenshot.jpg)

**

How do I fill out the “Education” section?

**

The information you provide in this section helps IRCC have a fuller picture of your current post\-secondary education\.

-   Indicate ‘yes’ to the education section as you are currently studying \(or completed your studies, if applying for a work permit\) at UBC\. Type in the current year and month in the “to” field\. If you completed your studies, indicate the relevant month and year\.
-   Type in your current program \(e\.g\. level, Bachelor, field, Arts\) at UBC\.
-   You may include your other studies at the post\-secondary level \(e\.g\., university, college, apprenticeship training, etc\.\)\.
-   If you need more space, download the [Letter of Explanation](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/ubc_letter_explanation_template_word.docx) Word document template \(docx\), provide additional information, and upload this document in the “Client Information” section under “Optional Documents”*\.*

[Screenshot of how to fill out the Education section for the TRV application](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/trv_education_screenshot-1.jpg)

**

How do I fill out the “Employment” section?

**

The information you provide in this section helps IRCC have a fuller picture of your employment activities within the last ten years\.

Include the following activities for the past ten years, with the most recent activities listed first, whether you did them in or outside of Canada:

-   For all students, the first section under employment is “current activity”; therefore, fill your current status as a student\. If you are currently employed, fill your employment in the next section\. Remember to include:
-   Part\-time job\(s\)
-   Full\-time job\(s\)
-   Internship\(s\)/Co\-op\(s\)/Practicum\(s\)
-   Studies at the post\-secondary level \(e\.g\., university, college, etc\.\)
-   If you need more space, download the [Letter of Explanation](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/ubc_letter_explanation_template_word.docx) Word document template \(docx\), provide additional information, and upload this document in the “Client Information*“* section under “Optional Documents*“\.*

[Screenshot of how to fill out the Employment section for the TRV application](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/trv_employement_screenshot.jpg)

**

How do I answer the “Background” questions?

**

**2 \(a\) Have you remained beyond the validity of your status, attended school without authorization or worked without authorization in Canada?**

**2 \(b\) Have you ever been refused a visa or permit, denied entry or ordered to leave Canada or any other country?**

**2 \(c\) Background information: Have you previously applied to enter or remain in Canada?**

You must provide honest answers to these questions\. Please speak with an International Student Advisor if you answered “yes” to questions 2\(a\) or 2\(b\) so that you are fully aware of any implications\.

**Important:** If you have applied for a study permit, a Temporary Resident Visa \(TRV\), or a work permit, whether it is approved or rejected, you must report that to IRCC by checking the box “Yes” to 2\(c\)\. You must also write down when you applied for each type of document in the box and provide additional details\.

[Screenshot of how to fill out the Background section for the TRV application](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/trv_background_questions_screenshot-1.jpg)

**

How can I sign the \[IMM5257E\] form if I apply online?

**

You do not need to print or sign your name in the signature field on the bottom of page 5 of \[IMM5257E\] if applying online\. Simply validate, save, and upload the form without signing\.

You will be prompted to electronically sign your application later in the online application process after you have uploaded all documents

## Validate your form[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv/apply\-temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv\-within\-canada\-tutorial/apply\-temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv\-within\-canada\-tutorial\-application\-form/\#validate\-your\-form](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial-application-form/#validate-your-form)

When you finish filling out your application form, click the blue “Validate” button \(found on the first or last page\)\. This will highlight any missing information required on your application\.

-   You can make changes after the application is successfully validated\. You can edit and validate as many times as you need\.
-   Remember to save and upload the final form\.

Once your application has been successfully validated it will show the following\. If you don’t see any barcodes when you validate your application, please visit the [CIC help](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/helpcentre/answer.asp?qnum=767&top=23) [p](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/helpcentre/answer.asp?qnum=767&top=23)[age](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/helpcentre/answer.asp?qnum=767&top=23)\.

[Screenshot of the barcode required to validate your TRV application](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/trv_validate_barcode.jpg)

## Take screenshots as you apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv/apply\-temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv\-within\-canada\-tutorial/apply\-temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv\-within\-canada\-tutorial\-application\-form/\#take\-screenshots\-as\-you\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial-application-form/#take-screenshots-as-you-apply)

It is a good practice to take screenshots as you apply in case there are issues after you submit your application\. You are welcome to take screenshots of all screens; however, these are the most important:

-   The **“Your document checklist”** page after all your documents have been successfully uploaded to your MyCIC account
-   The “**Acknowledgment of receipt**” page after the application has been submitted
-   After uploading/submitting any ‘**after\-the\-fact**’ documents that an IRCC officer has requested after your original application has been submitted

Save your screenshots to a safe place where you can access them easily\.

Learn how to take screenshots if you’re [using a PC](http://support.microsoft.com/en-us/help/13776/windows-use-snipping-tool-to-capture-screenshots#1TC=windows-7) or [on your Mac](http://support.apple.com/en-ca/HT201361)\.

## The information on this page may change[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv/apply\-temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv\-within\-canada\-tutorial/apply\-temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv\-within\-canada\-tutorial\-application\-form/\#the\-information\-on\-this\-page\-may\-change](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial-application-form/#the-information-on-this-page-may-change)

The immigration information on this page has been reviewed and endorsed by Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultants \(RCICs\) or Regulated International Student Immigration Advisors \(RISIAs\) in compliance with the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and Regulations\. However, this is not a legal document and information may change without notice\. Always refer to [Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada](http://www.cic.gc.ca/) \(IRCC\) for the most up\-to\-date information\.
