title: How to apply for a Temporary Resident Visa (TRV) from within Canada
content_markdown:
## Overview of the process[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv/apply\-temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv\-within\-canada\-tutorial/\#overview\-of\-the\-process](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial/#overview-of-the-process)

- **Row 1**

  - **Header cell 1:**
  
    Topic
  
  - **Header cell 2:**
  
    Details

- **Row 2**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Eligibility
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Visit the [Temporary Resident Visa \(TRV\) page](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/)\.

- **Row 3**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    When to apply
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    If you are from a visa\-required country and have [travel plans](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/travelling-outside-canada/), you will need a TRV \(along with your valid study permit and passport\) to re\-enter Canada\.  
    Apply at least 3 months before your planned departure from Canada or immediately after you have extended your study/work permit\.

- **Row 4**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Cost
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    $100\.00 CAD and $85\.00 CAD for biometrics, if applicable

- **Row 5**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Processing time
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Check the [Canadian government website](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/check-processing-times.html) for weekly updates\. Please note that these are estimates only\.

- **Row 6**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    How to apply
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Online through the [Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada \(IRCC\) website](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/e-services/account.asp)  
    **Alternate option**: You can only apply by paper if you are unable to apply online because of a disability, or your identity or travel document was issued to a refugee, stateless person or a non\-citizen\. Fill out the forms, gather all required documents and send to the [IRCC Case Processing Centre](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/visit/cpp-o-apply.asp) in Ottawa, Ontario  
    **Applying for family members:** When generating your checklist for your family members through IRCC’s online system, the correct forms \(e\.g\. **\[IMM5257\]**\) **will not** be triggered for your family members\. Unfortunately, the system generates a different form: **\[IMM5708\]\.**  
    If you submit this form, you will be asking for your family members’ status to change, not applying for a TRV\. **Therefore, please submit separate applications for each family member\.** Please speak with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) to go through this process in more detail\.

- **Row 7**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Application form
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    To avoid delays with your application, always download the most current form from the [IRCC website](http://cic.gc.ca/english/information/applications/visa.asp)\.  
    **Applying online**: Application for Temporary Resident Visa Made Outside of Canada \[**IMM5257E**\] \(Choose this form even if you are applying from within Canada\.\)  
    **Applying by paper:** Application for Visitor Visa \(Temporary Resident Visa\) \[**IMM5257E**\]

## Create your document checklist[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv/apply\-temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv\-within\-canada\-tutorial/\#create\-your\-document\-checklist](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial/#create-your-document-checklist)

### Applying online

1.  Create an IRCC Secure Account on the [IRCC website](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/e-services/account.asp)\.
2.  Complete the questionnaire to generate a checklist of application forms and required documents\.
    -   When answering the question “what would you like to do in Canada?” on the online questionnaire, please answer “study”\.
    -   Answering “visit” will generate the wrong document checklist\.
3.  After completing the questionnaire, you will be guided to a screen titled “Your document checklist”\.

### Applying by paper

Download the [document checklist](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/pdf/kits/forms/IMM5721E.PDF) **\[IMM5721\]**\.

## Gather your required documents[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv/apply\-temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv\-within\-canada\-tutorial/\#gather\-your\-required\-documents](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial/#gather-your-required-documents)

You’ll need to prepare your transcript, Letter of Enrolment, a copy of your passport, and more\.

[Get details](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial-required-documents/)

## Complete the application form[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv/apply\-temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv\-within\-canada\-tutorial/\#complete\-the\-application\-form](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial/#complete-the-application-form)

Your application form is an important part of your application\. Missing or incorrect information can negatively impact the outcome of your application\. Follow five steps to a comprehensive application\.

[Follow instructions](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial-application-form/)

## Get your TRV[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv/apply\-temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv\-within\-canada\-tutorial/\#get\-your\-trv](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial/#get-your-trv)

You will need to mail your passport to get your TRV\. **Do not** send your passport before IRCC sends you a written request to send your passport\.

### How to mail your passport

1.  Purchase two Canada Post Xpresspost prepaid 24 x 32 cm Xpresspost\-National envelopes at any Canada Post location\. \(e\.g\., the University Village pharmacy at 5754 University Blvd\.\)
2.  Put one envelope with your address inside the other so that the IRCC can return your passport securely\.
    -   [Online application mailing instructions](http://www.cic.gc.ca/submit-envoyer/offices-bureaux-eng.asp)
    -   [Paper application mailing instructions](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/visit/cpp-o-apply.asp)

If your contact information changes after submitting your application, be sure to update it via [IRCC’s webform](https://secure.cic.gc.ca/enquiries-renseignements/canada-case-cas-eng.aspx)\.

## After you receive your TRV[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv/apply\-temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv\-within\-canada\-tutorial/\#after\-you\-receive\-your\-trv](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial/#after-you-receive-your-trv)

Add the expiry date of your new TRV into the [UBC Reminder System](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/immigration-documents-reminder-system/)\.

## If you need help[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv/apply\-temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv\-within\-canada\-tutorial/\#if\-you\-need\-help](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial/#if-you-need-help)

### Before submitting your application

Sign up for the Canvas application review course to go over your application with helpful videos and learn about common mistakes\.

[Sign up now](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/CAFA9F)

### Contact international Student Advising

You can connect with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for questions related to immigration, health insurance, and life as an international student in Canada\.

## International Student Guide[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv/apply\-temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv\-within\-canada\-tutorial/\#international\-student\-guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial/#international-student-guide)

Find everything you need to know about life as an international student at UBC’s Vancouver campus\.

[View the guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/)

## The information on this page may change[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv/apply\-temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv\-within\-canada\-tutorial/\#the\-information\-on\-this\-page\-may\-change](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial/#the-information-on-this-page-may-change)

The immigration information on this page has been reviewed and endorsed by Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultants \(RCICs\) or Regulated International Student Immigration Advisors \(RISIAs\) in compliance with the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and Regulations\. However, this is not a legal document and information may change without notice\. Always refer to [Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada](http://www.cic.gc.ca/) \(IRCC\) for the most up\-to\-date information\.

title: Gather documents for your TRV application from within Canada
content_markdown:
## Documents all students need[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv/apply\-temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv\-within\-canada\-tutorial/apply\-temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv\-within\-canada\-tutorial\-required\-documents/\#documents\-all\-students\-need](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial-required-documents/#documents-all-students-need)

All students applying for a TRV will need all of the following documents\. 

When possible, documents should be issued within 30 days of submitting your application to be considered recent\. If you must provide several documents in a section, combine them into one file \(such as a PDF\) before uploading\. The size limit is 4MB per file; you may need to [reduce the file size](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/helpcentre/answer.asp?qnum=1213&top=23)\.

**

Recent education transcript

**

-   [Order your transcript online](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-transcript/)\.
-   If you have just started your program and your transcript is not available, you may want to write an explanation of your current circumstances and upload it as a ‘Letter of Explanation’\.

**

Canadian study permit or work permit

**

-   If you are a study permit holder, you will need a scanned copy of your study permit\.
-   If you are a work permit holder, you will need a scanned copy of your work permit\.

**

Letter of Enrolment \(listed as ‘Letter of Acceptance’ on your MyCIC checklist\)

**

Your Letter of Enrolment shows your current registration at UBC\. This letter is necessary to explain details about your studies, show current and future enrolment, and help an officer determine the remaining time you need to complete your program\. You can only obtain one after registration has opened and you are registered\. Review [registration dates](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/registration-dates/) for the term\.

Make sure to get a recently issued Letter of Enrollment issued within the past 30 days\. **Do not use** the Letter of Acceptance you received when you were first accepted to UBC \(unless you are a new student\)\. 

**Undergraduate Students**

Learn how to [get your Letter of Enrolment](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/student-documents/downloading-your-confirmation-of-enrolment-letter/), known as a “Confirmation of Enrolment Letter” in Workday\. Be sure to select the most recent academic session \(Winter or Summer Session\)\.  If the letter does not indicate you are enrolled [full\-time for immigration purposes](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#full-time), contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support\.                                                                                           

Your Class Standing \(previously known as your “year level” in the Student Service Centre\) indicates your remaining program length on your Letter of Enrolment\. For example, if you issue your Letter of Enrolment in December 2025, and your letter states you have Class Standing 3, this indicates you would complete your program in April 2027\.   

Contact an [Academic Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) from your faculty to request a Customized Enrolment Letter only if:

-   Need additional time to complete your program than what your Workday Letter of Enrolment  indicates\. For example, you are in a co\-op program, you transferred credits to UBC or your letter indicates you are in Class Standing 4 but you will need additional terms to finish your program requirements based on your anticipated course load, or
-   You are applying at the end of Winter Session Term 2 \(Jan\-Apr\) or during the Summer Session \(May\-Aug\) before [registration opens](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/registration-dates/) for the following Winter Session \(Sep\-Apr\)\.
-   You are on [authorized leave](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/taking-time-away-school-international/) and need to extend your TRV\. Contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support with your application\.

Your Customized Enrolment Letter should include your program, your current status as a student, and your expected completion date\. 

**Graduate Students**

Learn how to [get your Letter of Enrolment](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/student-documents/downloading-your-confirmation-of-enrolment-letter/), known as a “Confirmation of Enrolment Letter” in Workday\. Be sure to select the most recent academic session \(Winter or Summer Session\)\.

Your Letter of Enrolment indicates your remaining program length\. For example, if you issue your Letter of Enrolment in December 2025, and your letter states you are enrolled until April 2026, this indicates you are completing your program in April/May 2026\.

Contact your [graduate program staff](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/current-students/supervision/program-advising) to request a Customized Enrolment Letter only if:

-   You need additional time to complete your program than your Workday letter indicates\. For example, your letter indicates you are enrolled until the end of the academic session but you will need additional terms to finish your program requirements\.
-   You are applying at the end of the Winter Session Term 2 \(Jan\-Apr\) or during the Summer Session \(May\-Aug\) before [registration opens](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/registration-dates/) for the following Winter Session \(Sep\-Apr\)\.
-   You receive funding \(such as a teaching assistantship or research assistantship\) as part of your program\. This letter could also be uploaded in your proof of financial support documents
-   You are on a [leave of absence](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/taking-time-away-school-international/) and need to extend your TRV\. Contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support with your application\. 

Your Customized Enrolment Letter should include your program, your current status as a student, and your expected completion date\.

**Students coming from another Canadian school or applying for your first study permit**

If you are applying for your TRV based on your admission to UBC, and you haven’t registered for courses at UBC, you will need to show an official Letter of Acceptance \(LOA\) from UBC\. Find out how to get your [Letter of Acceptance](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-documents-required-study-permit/)\. You can also include a Letter of Enrolment if you have already registered in courses as mentioned above\. 

**

Proof of means of financial support

**

As part of your application you must prove that you can support yourself and any dependent family members with you in Canada for a year\.

**Increase to proof of funds requirement**

As of September 1, 2025, the minimum cost\-of\-living financial requirement for one year has [increased](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/get-documents/financial-support.html) from $20,635 to $22,895 for 2025\. The cost\-of\-living amount will be adjusted each year based on Statistics Canada’s low\-income cut\-off\. The amount required for [additional family members](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/get-documents.html#doc3) depends on how many dependents you have\.

**What to provide**

In your Temporary Resident Visa application, you should show proof of funds which would be sufficient to cover:

-   **One year of living expenses**: The cost\-of\-living amount for 2025 is $22,895 for a single person\. The cost\-of\-living amount will be adjusted each year based on Statistics Canada’s low\-income cut\-off\. If you have dependents \(spouse, common\-law partner, and/or children\), you’ll need to show additional proof of funds based on the number of [family members](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/get-documents/financial-support.html)\. If you have less than a year remaining to finish your program, you can prorate this amount to $1,907\.91 a month\. 
-   **One year of tuition fees**: You need to show proof of funds to cover one year of tuition fees\. If you have less than a year remaining to finish your program, you could show proof of funds for the remaining tuition fees\.

You may provide a combination of financial documents and sources, as long as the total exceeds the minimum cost\-of\-living financial requirement for yourself and any dependents plus one year of tuition fees, such as:

-   An official bank statement issued within the past 30 days that has been stamped or signed by your Canadian bank account showing the balance\.
-   A letter from parent\(s\) stating their relationship to you and that they will financially support you along with their financial documents\. The letter should be signed by your parent\(s\)\. You must also provide an official bank statement\(s\) of your parent\(s\) issued by their bank and that has been signed or stamped\. It must also be in English or French \(or accompanied by an official translation\)\. To write a letter of financial support, they can [download our template](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/ubc_financial_support_template_word.docx) \(docx\)\.
-   A letter from your sponsor \(e\.g\. sponsorship organization, scholarships, loans\) or employer \(e\.g\., teaching assistantships, research assistantships\) stating their relationship to you and the amount that they will provide you\.
-   If you have already paid tuition fees for a future term, get proof of payment from Workday\. Learn how to get your [account statement](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/downloading-your-proof-of-tuition-payment-account-statement/)\.

See IRCC’s [proof of financial support page](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/get-documents/financial-support.html) for further examples\.

While you only need to show proof of funds for one year, the officer must be satisfied that the possibility of funding for additional years of studies exists, such as your parents are employed or that your scholarship is for more than 1 year\.   

If providing a combination of financial documents and sources, include a summary or an index page of all the documents you are submitting for this section\. This will also allow you to clarify or explain the connection between documents, if applicable\. You can download a [template for the summary](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/ubc_summary_proof_funds_template.docx) \(docx\)\.

If you are having challenges with providing proof of funds, contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support\.

**Important:** If the balances in any of the documentation above are in foreign currency, provide a screenshot of the [currency converter](http://www.bankofcanada.ca/rates/exchange/currency-converter/) result\. \(if your currency is not listed, use [xe\.com](http://xe.com/)\)\.

**

Passport

**

The scanned copy of your passport pages provides information about your travel history and the expiry date of your passport\.

You must provide a copy of the bio\-data page \(the page with your name, date of birth, passport number, expiry date, etc\.\) AND a copy of every page in your passport that has stamps, visas, or markings from either Canada or other countries\. Make sure you merge all the pages into one PDF document and upload it\.

**Important:** Your TRV will not be issued past your study permit \(or work permit\) expiry date\. If your passport will expire soon, extend it before you apply for your TRV\.

If you need help scanning your documents, go to the [Irving K\. Barber Chapman Learning Commons](http://learningcommons.ubc.ca/tech-support/print-copy-scan/)\.

**

Digital photo

**

Make sure your photo meets the correct [specifications](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/application-forms-guides/temporary-resident-visa-application-photograph-specifications.html)\.

## Documents you might need[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv/apply\-temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv\-within\-canada\-tutorial/apply\-temporary\-resident\-visa\-trv\-within\-canada\-tutorial\-required\-documents/\#documents\-you\-might\-need](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial/apply-temporary-resident-visa-trv-within-canada-tutorial-required-documents/#documents-you-might-need)

Depending on your specific circumstances, you may need one or more of the following documents\.

**

Letter of Explanation

**

A letter of explanation is a good way to describe additional factors or include additional documents in your application\. It could include:

1.  The purpose of your application
2.  Issues you would like to clarify or that the officer might find useful
3.  Supporting documents, screenshots or any other proof to support your explanation
4.  Additional employment history if you have run out of space in your application

Download the [Word document template](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/ubc_letter_explanation_template_word.docx) for your use\.

**

Provincial Attestation Letter

**

Temporary Resident Visa applications do not require a [Provincial Attestation Letter \(PAL\)](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-documents-required-study-permit/)\. Some students get a request for a PAL in their TRV application checklists\. 

Download the [PAL exemption template](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/trv_pal_exemption_template.docx) \(docx\)\. Combine this letter with the suggested supporting documents into one file, then upload this file in your document checklist where they request a PAL or proof of PAL exemption\.

**

Medical exam

**

If you have been studying in Canada for the past 12 months, you do not need proof of a medical exam unless:

1.  You have lived in a [designated country or territory](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/medical-police/medical-exams/requirements-temporary-residents/country-requirements.html) for more than 6 months in the past 12 months or,
2.  You would like to [work](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/) in a job that will bring you into close contact with people including patients, children, the elderly, etc\. This includes public health, health sciences or agriculture\-related fields \(e\.g\., health care workers, primary and secondary school teachers\)\. See [this page](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/information/medical/medexams-temp.asp) to find out if you need a medical exam\.

If the above applies to you, you will need a medical exam conducted by an [IRCC\-approved Panel Physician](http://www.cic.gc.ca/pp-md/pp-list.aspx)\. Your medical exam report \(referred to as your ‘e\-medical’\) can be submitted with your TRV application\. You cannot start the position until you have received a study or work permit with appropriate conditions\.

**

Schedule 1: Application for Temporary Residence \[IMM5257B\]

**

**Most students will not require this form\.**

This document is required only if you answer “Yes” to any of the following questions: 3, 4, 5 or 6 in the “Background Information” section of the *“*Application to change of conditions, extend my stay or remain in Canada as a student” \[IMM5709\]” form*\.*

**Important:** If you answered “Yes” to any question in the “Background information” section other than 2\(c\), please speak to [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/)\.

**

Biometrics

**

If you have not previously provided [biometrics](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/campaigns/biometrics/facts.html) \(fingerprints and a photo\), you must submit them in\-person at a designated Service Canada location\. 

The processing time for your application does not include the time it takes to submit your biometrics\. Your application will not be processed until biometrics are received\. You only need to give biometrics once every 10 years\.

U\.S\. citizens and people who have provided biometrics in the past 10 years and [certain other individuals](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/visit/biometrics.asp) are exempt from providing biometrics\. 

1.  Pay the biometrics fee at the same time you submit your TRV application for faster processing\.
2.  Receive your biometrics instruction letter\. If you applied online you will receive an electronic biometrics instruction letter within 24 hours\.  
3.  Book an appointment as soon as possible at a designated Service Canada location\.
4.  Submit your biometrics within 30 days of receiving your biometrics instruction letter\.

title: Tips on communicating with Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC)
content_markdown:
## Communicating with IRCC[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/tips\-communicating\-immigration\-refugees\-citizenship\-canada\-ircc/\#communicating\-with\-ircc](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/tips-communicating-immigration-refugees-citizenship-canada-ircc/#communicating-with-ircc)

### By IRCC’s Web Form

Enter your case\-specific enquiry using the [online web form](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/contacts/web-form.asp)\.

If you have an application in progress, take care in selecting whether your application was:

-   an in\-Canada application or 
-   an application made to a visa office outside of Canada \(normally you would select the [visa office](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/contact-ircc/offices/international-visa-offices.html) responsible for your country\) 

Your enquiry will be sent to the relevant office\.

Be sure to fill out all applicable fields and provide a clear explanation in the ‘your enquiry’ text box\. After you click ‘next’, you will have an opportunity to upload documents, if necessary\. 

**Note**: If you have an application in progress, there is no guarantee that the information will be seen by the officer who will assess your application\. 

#### If your question is about a technical error:

1.  Describe the information you were looking for
2.  The nature of the problems
3.  Send screenshots of:
    -   The page you are attempting to access
    -   The error message that you receive

### By phone

Call the IRCC Call Centre at [1\-888\-242\-2100](tel:1-888-242-2100)*,* from within Canada only, Monday to Friday, 8am to 4pm local time, except for statutory holidays\.

Try calling early in the morning and prepare to wait on hold for some time\. Due to the heavy volume of calls received, you may need to try calling back several times\. For your records, write down the date and time you called, the agent’s name, and the exact information they provide\. Ask the agent if they can email the information they provided\. If you have submitted an immigration application, note that the agent you speak with is different from the officer who will review your application and make the final decision\.

title: Travelling outside Canada
content_markdown:
Whether you plan to travel for a few days or a few months, if you’re an international student, there are things to consider before you make plans to leave and re\-enter Canada\.

## Have your documents in order[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/travelling\-outside\-canada/\#have\-your\-documents\-in\-order](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/travelling-outside-canada/#have-your-documents-in-order)

You need the right documents to re\-enter Canada if you leave, so be sure to check your document expiration dates and renew them if necessary before you travel\.

Learn what immigration documents you need to return to Canada and what documents to bring by visiting the [Travelling to Canada guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/)\.

In general, it’s best to renew your immigration documents before you leave Canada, if possible\. If your immigration document\(s\) will expire while you are outside Canada, or you’ve applied for an extension of your document\(s\) before they expired and you must leave Canada, contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) before travelling for support\.

If you’ve applied for a study permit extension before it expired and your application is still being processed, you will lose maintained status when you leave Canada and will not be able to resume studies until your study permit has been issued\. Check [maintained status](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/maintained-status/) to learn more\.

Check Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada \(IRCC\)’s estimated [processing times](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/information/times) to plan ahead\.

## Visiting the United States[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/travelling\-outside\-canada/\#visiting\-the\-united\-states](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/travelling-outside-canada/#visiting-the-united-states)

#### Entering the United States

Citizens of some countries require a US visa\. Citizens of other countries may be required to get an [ESTA](https://esta.cbp.dhs.gov/esta/) and/or complete a [Form I\-94/I\-94W](https://www.cbp.gov/travel/international-visitors/i-94-instructions)\. Always check with the US Consulate for the most up\-to\-date information before beginning your visa application\. See the [US Department of State website](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/us-visas.html) and [United States Consulate\-General Vancouver](https://ca.usembassy.gov/visas/) for more information\. All US immigration questions should be directed to the [United States Consulate\-General Vancouver](https://ca.usembassy.gov/visas/contact-information/)\. UBC does not provide advice on US immigration issues\.

#### Reentering Canada after travelling to the United States

If you have a valid study permit or work permit, or hold valid visitor status in Canada, and you leave Canada and visit only the United States, you do not need a valid Temporary Resident Visa \(TRV\) to re\-enter Canada, provided you return to Canada by the end of the authorized period of your stay in Canada\. See the [Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations, Part 9, Division 5, Section 190\(3\)\(f\)](https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/sor-2002-227/section-190.html)\.

If you are waiting for your study permit extension application \([maintained status](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/maintained-status/)\) and need to travel to the United States, connect with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) before traveling\.

## Resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/travelling\-outside\-canada/\#resources](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/travelling-outside-canada/#resources)

title: UBC definitions for immigration purposes
content_markdown:
During your studies at UBC, there may be different definitions for different purposes, such as academic, tax, funding, financial aid, and more\.

UBC’s enrolment definitions for immigration purposes clarify when international students are in active pursuit of studies, and when you are eligible to work on and off campus or post\-graduation\.

## Importance of enrolment status[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/ubc\-definitions\-immigration\-purposes/\#importance\-of\-enrolment\-status](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#importance-of-enrolment-status)

Having a study permit comes with [certain responsibilities](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/#maintaining-your-student-status)—that is, to actively pursue studies and make reasonable progress towards completing your program\.

Your enrolment status impacts whether you can:

-   [Remain in Canada as a student](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/#maintaining-your-student-status)
-   [Work in Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/)
-   Remain eligible for a [post\-graduation work permit \(PGWP\)](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/post-graduation-work-permit/)

Learn about the impacts if you are considering [part\-time studies](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/immigration-impacts-part-time-studies-withdrawing-courses/) or [taking time away from studies](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/taking-time-away-school-international/)\.

Twice a year or more, UBC is required to report on your enrolment status to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada \(IRCC\) based on the definitions below\.

### Four\-letter codes that define your student status for immigration purposes

The record of your enrolment status is on the Student Information Service Centre \(SISC\), which is accessed by UBC staff\. If you are unclear about your student status for immigration purposes, you can confirm with your [graduate program staff](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/current-students/supervision-advising/program-advising), [academic advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/), or [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) to see what is on record in the SISC\. The following definitions include the 4\-letter code that is on your record as your enrolment status in the SISC\.

## “Regular academic session”[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/ubc\-definitions\-immigration\-purposes/\#regular\-academic\-session](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#regular-academic-session)

UBC has two [academic sessions](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/academic-year-202324) per year that are divided into two terms:

-   Winter Session: Term 1 \(September to December\) and Term 2 \(January to April\) 
-   Summer Session: Term 1 \(May to June\) and Term 2 \(July to August\) 

**Undergraduate, Diploma \(other than the Diploma in Accounting\), Certificate, Juris Doctor, exchange, VIRS, visiting students, and unclassified students**

You must be enrolled in Winter Term 1 and Winter Term 2\. Summer is a scheduled break and courses are optional\.

**Graduate students and students in the Diploma in Accounting Program**

You must be enrolled throughout the year \(Winter Term 1, Winter Term 2, and the Summer Session\)\.

## “Scheduled Break”[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/ubc\-definitions\-immigration\-purposes/\#scheduled\-break](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#scheduled-break)

This definition is for immigration purposes to denote students who are not required to be enrolled during program breaks\. Students are considered to be ‘actively pursuing studies’ while on a scheduled break\.

Dates are based on the [UBC Vancouver](http://www.calendar.ubc.ca/vancouver/) and [Okanagan Calendar](http://www.calendar.ubc.ca/okanagan/index.cfm)

Scheduled breaks include:

| Term 1 Midterm Break | First day of Midterm Break | Last day of Midterm Break |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Term 1 Midterm Break | First day of Midterm Break | Last day of Midterm Break |
| Winter Break | Day after posted final exam period for Winter Term 1 | Day before the start of classes for Winter Term 2 |
| Term 2 Midterm Break | First day of Midterm Break | Last day of Midterm Break |
| Break between Winter Term 2 and Summer | Day after posted final exam period for Winter Term 2 | Day before the start of classes for Summer Term 1 |
| Summer Session \(not available for students in graduate programs or the Diploma in Accounting Program \[DAP\]\) | Start of classes for Summer Term 1 | Last day of posted final exam period for Summer Term 2 |
| Break between Summer Session and Winter Term 1 | Day after posted final exam period for Summer Term 2 | Day before the start of classes for Winter Term 1 |

#### Exception to the Scheduled Break

If your academic program has start and end dates which differ from those specified in the applicable academic calendar, the program dates will apply\.

Students in graduate programs or the Diploma in Accounting Program \(DAP\) in summer are deemed to be on an academic summer session, not a scheduled break\.

### Working during a scheduled break

You might be eligible to work full\-time on or off campus during a scheduled break\. Work refers to work which is authorized by a study permit\. Students who also hold work permits may be able to work supplemental days/hours in addition to work authorized by study permits\.

Registered, eligible, or continuing students in **UBC degree, diploma, certificate, and Juris Doctor programs** are considered to be eligible to work while on a scheduled break if you meet all of the following criteria:

-   You are eligible to [work on and/or off campus](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/)
-   You were full\-time for immigration purposes in the term immediately before the break\.
-   Your degree has not been conferred\.
-   You will resume full\-time studies in the term immediately following the break\.

#### If you meet the above requirements

You are permitted to work full\-time on or off campus during a scheduled break for a total of 180 days per calendar year, but not more than 150 consecutive days\.

#### If you do not meet the above requirements

You are **not eligible to work** during a scheduled break\. For further clarification, exchange, VIRS, visiting students, and unclassified students are not eligible to work during scheduled breaks\.

**Undergraduate, diploma, certificate, and Juris Doctor students** on a scheduled summer break who do not meet the above requirements may only work up to 24 hours a week \(20 hours before Nov 8, 2024\) and unlimited hours on campus during the Summer Session only if enrolled in a full\-time course load in the Summer Session\. If you are enrolled in a part\-time course load in summer, you are not eligible to work on or off campus\. 

## “Full time”[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/ubc\-definitions\-immigration\-purposes/\#full\-time](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#full-time)

This definition is for immigration purposes to denote students who are actively pursuing studies and who may be eligible to work on or off campus\. Full\-time status is the minimum requirement to work on or off campus, among [other requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/)\.

Work refers to work which is authorized by a study permit\. Students who also hold work permits may be able to work additional days/hours in addition to work authorized by study permits\.

Students with full\-time status can start work on the first day of the term as per the [UBC Vancouver](http://www.calendar.ubc.ca/vancouver/) or [UBC Okanagan](http://www.calendar.ubc.ca/okanagan/index.cfm) academic calendar\. You must stop work on the last day of the posted final exam period according to the academic calendar or when you no longer meet [requirements to work](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/)\.

**Exception:** If your academic program has start and end dates which differ from those specified in the applicable academic calendar, you can start work on the first day of your program’s term, and you must stop work on the last day of your program’s term\.

### Additional information

-   Students who meet the “full time” definition in summer and are not eligible for a scheduled break during the summer session will be deemed full time from May 1 to August 31\. 
-   Courses spanning two terms are counted as half the credit value per term \(e\.g\. a 6 credit course counts as 3 credits in Term 1 and 3 credits in Term 2\)\.

### Definitions for being “full time”

UBC students are considered by UBC to be “full time for immigration purposes” if they meet **any one** of the following definitions:

**

Graduate students \(enrolled in a UBC graduate program\)

**

-   **Registered** \(“REGI” on the SISC\), or
-   **Continuing** \(“CONT” on the SISC\)

**

Undergraduate, post\-baccalaureate, diploma, and other students

**

This category also includes **Diploma in Accounting** \(“DAPP” on the SISC\), **Juris Doctor** \(JD\), **Unclassified** \(“UNCL” on the SISC\), **Access Studies** \(“ACES” on the SISC\), **Exchange** \(“EXCH” on the SISC\), and **Visiting** \(“VISI” or “VISO” on the SISC\) students\.

Students taking graduate\-level courses but not enrolled in a UBC graduate program also fall into this category, including graduate exchange students\.

**Winter Term 1 or 2**:

-   **Registered** \(“REGI” on the SISC\) in 9 or more credits per winter term

**​Summer \(May to August\)**:

-   **Registered** \(“REGI” on the SISC\) for 9 or more credits, and
-   Do not meet the definition of “scheduled break”

**Final academic term**

-   Registered \(“REGI” on the SISC\) in any number of credits in the “final” term—“final” as determined by your academic advising office and denotes that you will have satisfied all program requirements upon successful completion of the current term’s activities\.
-   If a final course spans two terms \(e\.g\. 6 credits\), each term may be determined to be a final term\.
-   If final coursework is taken during the summer session \(May to August\), you can be registered for any number of credits during this period\. Your full\-time status continues until your letter of completion is available\.

**

Visiting International Research Students and Visiting Research Exchange Students

**

Visiting International Research Students \(VIRS or VIRO\) and Visiting Research Exchange Students are considered by UBC to be “full time for immigration purposes” if you are **registered** \(“REGI” on the SISC\)\. Please check with [Go Global](https://global.ubc.ca/go-global) if you think this applies to you\.

**

Students with academic accommodations

**

Students with academic accommodations are considered to be “full time for immigration purposes” if you are registered in the minimum number of credits for your reduced course load accommodation as determined by the Centre for Accessibility \(Vancouver\), or the Disability Resource Centre \(Okanagan\) in line with [Disability Accommodation Policy LR7](https://universitycounsel.ubc.ca/policies/disability-accommodation-policy/)\.

**

Outbound exchange students

**

UBC students away on exchange term\(s\) abroad are considered “full\-time for immigration purposes” if you are **registered** \(“REGI” on the SISC\)\.

**

Co\-op students

**

UBC students on a co\-op work term, internship, practicum, or other program\-required work are considered by UBC to be “full\-time for immigration purposes” if you are **registered** \(“REGI” on the SISC\)\.

**

UBC Okanagan English Foundation Program students

**

UBC students enrolled in the UBC Okanagan English Foundation Program are considered by UBC to be “full\-time for immigration purposes”\.

**

Graduating students

**

UBC students who have completed program requirements and whose program completion letter is not yet available are considered by UBC to be “full\-time for immigration purposes”\.

## “Part\-time”[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/ubc\-definitions\-immigration\-purposes/\#part\-time](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#part-time)

UBC students are considered by UBC to be “part\-time for immigration purposes” if they meet both of the following criteria:

-   They are **registered** \(“REGI” on the SISC\)\.
-   They do not meet the “full time” or “scheduled break” definition\.

No minimum number of credits is required to have “part\-time” status\.

Part\-time students are considered actively pursuing studies but cannot work on or off campus\. Work refers to work which is authorized by a study permit\. Students who also hold work permits may be able to work additional days/hours in addition to work authorized by their study permits\.

Part\-time studies \(except during a final term\) also impact eligibility for the [Post\-Graduation Work Permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/post-graduation-work-permit/)\.  Learn more about [immigration impacts](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/immigration-impacts-part-time-studies-withdrawing-courses/) of part\-time studies or withdrawing from courses\. 

## “Authorized leave”[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/ubc\-definitions\-immigration\-purposes/\#authorized\-leave](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#authorized-leave)

UBC students are considered to be on an “authorized leave for immigration purposes” in a given term if you meet one of the following:

-   You are on leave \(“OLVE” on the SISC\)
-   You have been issued a leave letter under the [International Undergraduate Authorized Leave Procedure](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/taking-time-away-school-international/), which began in 2021/22 Winter Session\.

Some authorized leaves can be considered “actively pursuing studies”\. Learn more about [taking time away from studies](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/taking-time-away-school-international/)\.

## “Deferred enrolment”[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/ubc\-definitions\-immigration\-purposes/\#deferred\-enrolment](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#deferred-enrolment)

UBC students are considered by UBC to have “deferred enrolment” if they meet all of the following criteria:

-   The Letter of Acceptance was issued\.
-   The offer was not revoked\.
-   UBC allows your start date to be delayed to a subsequent term or session, because UBC postponed the program of study or you initiated a delay\.

Deferred enrolment is determined by Admissions, the Faculty, or program\.

## “Academic suspension”[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/ubc\-definitions\-immigration\-purposes/\#academic\-suspension](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#academic-suspension)

UBC students are considered to be on “academic suspension for immigration purposes” when they are suspended due to poor academic performance or violation of the institution’s policies\. The student is allowed to return after the period of suspension\.

Learn more about [taking time away from studies](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/taking-time-away-school-international/)\.

## “No show”[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/ubc\-definitions\-immigration\-purposes/\#no\-show](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#no-show)

UBC students are considered to be “no\-shows for immigration purposes” if all of the following happen:

-   The Letter of Acceptance was issued\.
-   Your offer was not revoked\.
-   The Add/Drop date for the first term has passed\.
-   Enrolment was not deferred\.
-   You never registered or enrolled in the current program of study at UBC\.

## “Not started”[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/immigration/ubc\-definitions\-immigration\-purposes/\#not\-started](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#not-started)

This status applies to students who are enrolled in a program of studies that begins the following semester\. They have not yet started their studies\.

title: Applying to graduate
content_markdown:
To graduate, students must submit a formal application for graduation\. If you plan to graduate, you must apply, regardless of whether or not you intend to participate in the scheduled ceremonies\.

Before applying to graduate, make sure you’ll have completed all program requirements by the specified dates below\.

## If you’re graduating in November[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/graduation/applying\-graduate/\#if\-youre\-graduating\-in\-november](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/graduation/applying-graduate/#if-youre-graduating-in-november)

If you plan to graduate in Fall 2026, you must apply for graduation by **Aug 28, 2026**\. For important dates and deadlines, refer to the Fall graduation timeline on this page\.  
  
Your parchment will be printed with a conferral date of November 2026 and will be available at or after the Fall graduation ceremonies\. Your parchment refers to your diploma\. 

## Graduation timeline[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/graduation/applying\-graduate/\#graduation\-timeline](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/graduation/applying-graduate/#graduation-timeline)

There are 2 graduation periods, one in spring, and another in fall: 

-   **Spring graduation:** May 20 to 22, 2026 and May 25 to May 28, 2026
-   **Fall graduation:** November 25 to 27, 2026

You can find the graduation ceremony schedule on the [UBC Graduation website](https://graduation.ubc.ca/schedule/)\. Please review the important dates and information below to ensure you are eligible to graduate at your desired time\. 

You are required to apply for graduation, even if you don’t plan on attending the ceremony\.

[View detailed schedule](https://graduation.ubc.ca/schedule/)

### Fall graduation in November 2026

If you are completing Term 1 courses in December, you are not eligible for November graduation and should wait to apply for May graduation\. If you have questions about your degree requirements, contact your [academic advising office](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/)\.

## Eligibility to graduate[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/graduation/applying\-graduate/\#eligibility\-to\-graduate](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/graduation/applying-graduate/#eligibility-to-graduate)

-   If you are graduating in May, you must complete your program requirements by the end of April\.
-   If you are graduating in November, you must complete your program requirements by the end of October\.
-   If you’re a graduate student, there are [specific deadlines](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/deadlines) for you\.
-   If you are completing Term 1 courses in December, you are not eligible for November graduation and should wait to apply for May graduation\. If you have questions about your degree requirements, contact your [academic advising office](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/)\.
-   You will not receive a parchment or be able to order transcripts if you have an outstanding balance of fees\.

## How to apply to graduate[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/graduation/applying\-graduate/\#how\-to\-apply\-to\-graduate](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/graduation/applying-graduate/#how-to-apply-to-graduate)

### Before you apply

Make sure your financial account with UBC is settled\. You will not receive a parchment or be able to order transcripts with an outstanding balance of fees\. You will still be able to apply to graduate and attend the ceremony, but will not receive your parchment when you cross the stage\. If you have questions about your finances, contact your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\. If you don’t have an assigned advisor, they’re still available to help\.

If you are an international student, and you plan to invite family from abroad to attend your graduation, be sure to apply for the [necessary travel documents](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/inviting-friends-family-visit/) for your family in advance\.

If you are a student completing a double major, you will be assigned to the ceremony for the major that is listed first on your student record \(e\.g\., a double major in French and Economics will be assigned to French\)\. To check your student record, log into [Workday](https://myworkday.ubc.ca/) and select “Academic history” under *Academics*\. For any changes to your programs of study, or the major that is listed first, contact your faculty or departmental [advising office](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) before you apply to graduate\.

### Use of names on parchments and graduation ceremonies

While completing your application, check your legal name and your listed program of studies for accuracy\. Unless specified, the name on your official student record will be the name printed on your parchment\.

Find out what to do if you’d like to [change your name](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/changing-name-parchment-diploma/) on your parchment\.

-   **May graduation:** You must submit your name change requests for your parchment by **Fri, Apr 17, 2026**\.
-   **November graduation:** You must submit your name change request for your parchment by **Fri, Oct 9, 2026**\.

### Applying for November 2026 graduation

You’ll need to complete two parts to your application: 

-   **Graduation application:** This is required to ensure you can attend your graduation ceremony and receive your parchment\. You’ll also find your ceremony details and procession number closer to the ceremony date\. Your procession number is your place in line and indicates the order of when you will cross the stage\.
-   **Program completion application**: You’ll need to review your academic record and enter your expected completion date\.

Follow [step\-by\-step instructions](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/degree-planning/applying-for-graduation-or-program-completion/) to submit your application for November 2026 graduation\.

### When you can expect an approval decision

Your faculty will assess and approve your graduation application status if you have met your program requirements\. You are welcome to check your application status on Workday\. Approval decisions will be updated by your faculty on Workday by mid\-May or mid\-November, and earned credentials will appear on Workday about a week before the ceremony\.

If you have concerns about your application status or whether you’ve met your degree requirements, please contact your [academic advising office](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/)\.

## About the graduation ceremony[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/graduation/applying\-graduate/\#about\-the\-graduation\-ceremony](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/graduation/applying-graduate/#about-the-graduation-ceremony)

Review the [graduation checklist](http://graduation.ubc.ca/students/your-graduation-checklist/) to find the ceremony schedule, ticket, and gown ordering information, as well as ceremony instructions for students and guests\.

You will be notified by email when you can check your personal ceremony date and time on your Graduation Application tool\.

## Getting your parchment[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/graduation/applying\-graduate/\#getting\-your\-parchment](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/graduation/applying-graduate/#getting-your-parchment)

Parchments are not printed until just before the May and November ceremonies\. Parchments will only be available at the ceremony or by pick up or courier delivery in early June and December for all students\.

-   **If you’re attending the ceremony**  
    You can start planning using the Graduation checklist on the [Graduation at UBC website](http://graduation.ubc.ca/students/your-graduation-checklist/)\. You’ll receive your parchment on the day of your ceremony\.
-   **If you’re not attending the ceremony**  
    You can pick up your parchment or pay for your parchment to be couriered\.
-   **Changing to courier delivery**  
    To switch your selection on the grad application from pick\-up to courier, please edit your application by **Fri, Aug 28** or email [graduation@ubc\.ca](mailto:graduation@ubc.ca)\. Make sure to include your UBC student number\.

**

In\-person pick up

**

If you’re graduating in November 2026, you can pick up your parchment starting **Mon, Dec 7, 2026** from the Advising Centre in [Brock Hall](http://www.maps.ubc.ca/PROD/index_detail.php?locat1=112-1)\.

You may pick up your parchment or have it picked up by someone else on your behalf with a [third party pick up form](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/third_party_document_authorization_form.pdf) \(pdf\)\.

Alternatively, if the person picking up your document is authorized on your Workday account, they must have your student number and authorization code in addition to their ID\.

Learn about [third\-party authorization](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/third-party-authorization/)\.

**

Courier delivery

**

Couriers cannot deliver to PO boxes\.

If you’ve selected the courier option on your graduation application, you’ll receive an email for when you can pay the courier fee\. You won’t be able to pay online until your degree has been conferred\.

Once graduation ceremonies end, parchments will be packaged and sent out via courier\.

**Courier costs**

| **Destination** | **Cost** | **Estimated delivery time after your request has been processed** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Within Canada | $23\.20 | 1 to 2 business days, depending on destination |
| United States | $45\.20 | 1 to 3 business days, depending on destination |
| International locations | $45\.20 | 3 to 5 business days, depending on destination |

## Changing your ceremony attendance[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/graduation/applying\-graduate/\#changing\-your\-ceremony\-attendance](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/graduation/applying-graduate/#changing-your-ceremony-attendance)

You can change your selection for the Fall graduation in your Graduation Application Tool until **Fri, Aug 28, 2026**\.

If you miss the deadline and would like to change your selection to attending, please email [graduation@ubc\.ca](mailto:graduation@ubc.ca)\. Please include your full name and UBC student number\.

### Important information about late requests to attend the ceremony

The Ceremonies Office cannot guarantee ticket availability\.

Your parchment may not be available at the ceremony, but will be available for pickup or courier in either December \(if you are graduating in November\) or June \(if you are graduating in May\)\.

### If you can’t make the ceremony

If you indicated that you were attending the ceremony on the application but can no longer make it, you can pick up your parchment at the Enrolment Advising Centre at [Brock Hall](http://www.maps.ubc.ca/PROD/index_detail.php?locat1=112-1) in early December for the Fall ceremony or early June for the Spring ceremony\. If you prefer courier delivery, email [graduation@ubc\.ca](mailto:graduation@ubc.ca)\.

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/graduation/applying\-graduate/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/graduation/applying-graduate/#additional-resources)

-   [Ordering a parchment \(diploma\)](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-parchment-diploma/)
-   [Changing the name on your parchment \(diploma\)](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/changing-name-parchment-diploma/)
-   [Graduation FAQ](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/graduation/graduation-faq/)
-   [Ordering a transcript](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-transcript/)
-   [Graduation at UBC](https://graduation.ubc.ca/)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/graduation/applying\-graduate/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/graduation/applying-graduate/#if-you-have-questions)

For information regarding graduation application and parchments, contact: 

-   **UBC Vancouver:** [graduation@ubc\.ca](mailto:graduation@ubc.ca)
-   **UBC Okanagan**: [gradapps\.okanagan@ubc\.ca](mailto:gradapps.okanagan@ubc.ca)

Contact the Graduation Ceremonies Office by emailing [ceremonies\.graduation@ubc\.ca](mailto:ceremonies.graduation@ubc.ca) for information about tickets, gown rentals, guests, or the ceremony schedule\.

title: Graduation FAQ
content_markdown:
## Browse frequently asked questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/graduation/graduation\-faq/\#browse\-frequently\-asked\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/graduation/graduation-faq/#browse-frequently-asked-questions)

### Applying to graduate

**

When will I know when my application has been approved?

**

Your application to graduate will be reviewed by your faculty in October for the fall ceremony and in April for the spring ceremony\. The final approval will be noted in Workday on the Academics app, under the graduation tab about a week prior to the congregation ceremony\.

**

I just looked at my graduation application and the status has changed\. What does this mean?

**

In the Workday Academics app, under the “Graduation” tab, you can view your Program of Study Status and Program Completion Status\. There are a number of statuses that may appear on your academic record once you have applied to graduate\. Your program of study status will also be reflected on your [graduation application](https://ubc.appiancloud.com/suite/sites/graduation-management-application)\. Please review the [tutorials](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/degree-planning/applying-for-graduation-program-completion/#step-3-verify-your-application) for more information\.  
 

- **Row 1**

  - **Header cell 1:**
  
    Application term
  
  - **Header cell 2:**
  
    Description

- **Row 2**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Applied for Completion
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Your application has been received\. Applications will be reviewed once the graduation application closes\. Please ensure that all requirements are met by the [deadline for graduation](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/graduation/applying-graduate/)\.

- **Row 3**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Evaluation Deferred
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Your application will remain pending until all final grades are in, and your file has been approved by the Dean of your faculty\.

- **Row 4**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Denied
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    1.  Your application has been withdrawn and will not be evaluated for graduation\. You must reapply for a subsequent session\.
      
    3.  Your application for graduation has not been approved by your faculty or school\. Contact your faculty or school if you believe that you have met graduation requirements and should be eligible to graduate\. Otherwise, you will need to **reapply** for graduation in a subsequent session when you become eligible to graduate\.

- **Row 5**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Approved for Completion
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Your application has been approved by your faculty\. Your credential will not appear on your transcript until Senate meets to approve all graduates and confer their degrees\.

- **Row 6**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Program completed
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Your degree has been conferred \(awarded\) by Senate and your credentials will appear on your transcript\. Senate usually confers degrees during its regular monthly meeting about a week before graduation ceremonies\.

**

My degree is not noted on my transcript yet, but I need proof that I’ve completed all my requirements\. What should I do?

**

Contact your program or faculty [advising office](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) to request a letter of completion\.

**

I have missed the deadline to apply for graduation\. Can I still graduate?

**

Please contact your faculty or departmental [advising office](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/)\.

**

I have applied for Program Completion in Workday and submitted my Graduation Application through the Graduation Application Tool\. Why does the status checker at the top of my Graduation Application indicate that my Program Completion in Workday is missing?

**

Please note that there may be a delay in syncing between the two portals, which can cause this discrepancy\. Once the systems have synced, your Graduation Application will display the correct Program Completion status\.

**

How can I apply for my graduation?

**

To graduate from UBC, you must complete a formal application process that consists of two components:  

1.  **The** [**Graduation Application**](https://ubc.appiancloud.com/suite/sites/graduation-management-application)  
    -   This application must be submitted to receive your parchment and to indicate whether or not you plan to attend the ceremony\. 
2.  **The** [**Program Completion Application**](https://myworkday.ubc.ca/)  
    -   This application must be submitted to have your program requirements reviewed by your faculty or school, and have your degree conferred \(awarded\) by the Senate\. 

Please review the [tutorials](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/degree-planning/applying-for-graduation-program-completion/#step-3-verify-your-application) for more information\. 

### Graduation and your degree specialization

**

My degree specialization listed on Workday is not correct\. What should I do?

**

Contact your faculty or departmental [advising office](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising)\.

**

I am doing a double major but I’m only seeing my primary Program of Study on the Graduation Application\.

**

When you submit your Graduation Application via the [Graduation Application Tool](https://ubc.appiancloud.com/suite/sites/graduation-management-application), only your primary major will be displayed\. Please note, however, that both majors will be printed on your degree parchment\.

**

I am currently taking a course at another university or college for credit toward my UBC degree\. What do I need to do to graduate?

**

To apply for graduation and process transfer credit from another institution, you must follow the steps below:

1.  Arrange for an official transcript from the other institution that includes your final course grade to be sent directly to Enrolment Services at UBC, via email to [final\.grades@ubc\.ca](mailto:final.grades@ubc.ca) including your student number or to:  
      
    UBC Enrolment Services  
    ATTN: Transfer Credit  
    1874 East Mall  
    Vancouver, BC V6T 1Z1  
    Canada
2.  Before you started taking courses at the other institution, you should have received a [Letter of Permission](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/letter-permission/) \(LOP\) from your faculty\. Send your LOP and student number to Enrolment Services at [academicrecord\.support@ubc\.ca](mailto:academicrecord.support@ubc.ca)\. Alternatively, you can ask your faculty to send the LOP directly to Enrolment Services via campus mail\.

The approximate processing time is 6 to 8 weeks\.

**

I am registered as a master’s or doctoral student\. What will happen to my award when I complete my degree requirements?

**

Graduate students who are award recipients will have their award prorated to the end of the month in which they complete their degree requirements, including submission of their thesis to the UBC Library\. Students will be required to return any amounts issued to them for the time period after their effective completion date\. Please contact [Enrolment Services](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) with any additional questions\.

### Graduation ceremony

**

When will I know my ceremony date and time?

**

The fall schedule is available in October and the spring schedule is available in March on the [UBC Graduation](http://graduation.ubc.ca/) website\.

**

I am doing a double major\. Which group of Majors will I graduate with?

**

If you are a student completing a double major, you will be assigned to the ceremony for the primary Program of Study \(e\.g\., someone with a primary program of study in History and a Secondary Pathway in Psychology will be assigned to the History ceremony\)\. To check your student record, log into Workday and select “Academic History” under Academics\. 

Please note that if you are completing an Honours program, it must be listed as your primary major, and you will be assigned to the corresponding ceremony\. 

Contact your faculty or departmental advising office if this needs to be changed before the application deadline\. 

**

I don’t plan on attending the ceremony\. Do I still need to apply to graduate?

**

Yes, you are required to apply for graduation regardless of whether you are able to attend the ceremony\. If you do not apply, you will not graduate nor receive your parchment\.

**

Why are the Ceremony Details blank on my Graduation Application? When will I see my ceremony information?

**

Ceremony information is expected to begin appearing on Graduation Applications in April for May ceremonies, and in October for November ceremonies\.

**

I will not complete my degree requirements until December\. Which ceremony do I apply for?

**

If you do not complete your degree requirements by December, you will not meet the fall congregation deadline\. You must apply to graduate in the spring ceremony following the completion of your degree requirements\. If you will not meet degree requirements by the deadline for spring graduation, you must apply for the following fall graduation\.

### Your parchment \(diploma\)

**

How do I change the name on my parchment?

**

Read about options to [change the name on your parchment](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/changing-name-parchment-diploma/)\. There is a deadline to submit preferred name change and legal name change requests for graduation\.

**

What’s included in my parchment \(diploma\)?

**

The following details will be included on your parchment\.  

-   Faculty 
-   Student’s name 
-   Credential \(Bachelor of Arts, Bachelor of Education, etc\.\) 
-   Primary Program of Study and Secondary Pathway \(If applicable\)  
-   Co\-operative Education \(if you completed a co\-op program\) 
-   Degree Standing \(“With Distinction” and “with Honours”, etc\., if applicable\)\. To dispute your standing, please contact your program or faculty\. 
-   Minors are not printed on parchments\. However, this will be displayed on your transcript\. 

**

I couldn’t attend my graduation ceremony and was going to pick up my parchment, but I can’t make it to campus\. Can someone pick it up for me?

**

Yes\. If you would like someone to pick up your parchment on your behalf, download and complete the [Third\-Party Document Pick Up Form](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/es_third_party_pickup_form.pdf) \(pdf\), then give it to the person who will be picking up your parchment for you\. Make sure you have filled out the form correctly and that the person picking the parchment up can present the identification specified in the form\. Alternatively, you can assign [third\-party authorization](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/third-party-authorization/) via your Workday account\.

**

Where can I get a UBC parchment frame?

**

You can purchase a UBC parchment frame during the graduation ceremonies outside near the Chan Centre\. You can also purchase one online through [Alumni Affairs](https://alumni.ubc.ca/services/ubc-degree-frames/) or in person at the [UBC Bookstore](http://bookstore.ubc.ca/home)\.

**

If I buy a parchment frame from UBC Alumni Affairs, does my purchase support this association?

**

Yes, a portion of the frame purchase is donated to [UBC Alumni Affairs](https://alumni.ubc.ca/services/ubc-degree-frames/)\.

### If you’re not graduating

**

I am not ready to graduate\. Why am I being prompted to apply for graduation?

**

Some degree or diploma and certificate programs do not have year levels so the system cannot determine when you’ll be completing your program\. For some programs, students may take from 8 months to 5 years to graduate\. We want to make sure that those who are eligible to graduate know they should apply\.

**

I have applied for graduation by mistake\. How can I withdraw my application?

**

Before the [application deadline](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/graduation/applying-graduate), you can withdraw your graduation application by sending in a written request to [graduation@ubc\.ca](mailto:graduation@ubc.ca)\. Please include your UBC student number\. When you are ready to graduate, please remember to apply again\.

After the [application deadline](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/graduation/applying-graduate/), you can withdraw your graduation application by sending in a written request to your faculty or departmental [advising office](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/)\.

Please include your full name and UBC student number\. When you are ready to graduate, please remember to apply again\.
