title: Academic accommodations for students with disabilities
content_markdown:
## About academic accommodations[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/\#about\-academic\-accommodations](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/#about-academic-accommodations)

Academic accommodations reduce barriers in the learning environment to support equitable access for students with disabilities or ongoing medical conditions\.

UBC’s [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/) determines a student’s eligibility for accommodations in accordance with the university’s [Disability Accommodation Policy LR7](https://universitycounsel.ubc.ca/policies/disability-accommodation-policy/)\.

The types of conditions supported by the Centre for Accessibility include, but are not limited to:

-   Mental health conditions such as depression, anxiety disorders, or bipolar disorder
-   Neurological disabilities such as attention deficit and hyperactivity disorder, learning disabilities, head injuries, and Autism Spectrum Disorder
-   Chronic health conditions including ongoing medical conditions such as arthritis, chronic pain, Crohn’s disease, or migraines
-   Physical or sensory disabilities, such as visual impairment, hearing loss, or mobility impairments

[Read types of accommodations](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/types-academic-accommodations/)

## How to request an academic accommodation[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/\#how\-to\-request\-an\-academic\-accommodation](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/#how-to-request-an-academic-accommodation)

The Centre for Accessibility typically works with students to arrange an academic accommodation for permanent, chronic, or long\-term conditions\. To request an academic accommodation, you must register with the [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/)\. An Accessibility Advisor will determine the accommodations you are eligible for\. 

If you are experiencing a temporary injury or acute medical condition that is not expected to persist for longer than one term, please connect with [Academic Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/)\.

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/#additional-resources)

-   [Types of academic accommodations](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/types-academic-accommodations/)
-   [Exam accommodation guidelines and expectations](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/exam-accommodation-guidelines-expectations/)
-   [Documentation Guidelines](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/documentation-guidelines/)
-   [Learning disabilities documentation standards](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/learning-disabilities-documentation-standards/)
-   [Registering with the Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/registering-centre-accessibility/)
-   [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/#if-you-have-questions)

The [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/) facilitates disability\-related accommodations and supports that are designed to remove barriers for students with disabilities and ongoing medical conditions\.

Contact the Centre by email at [info\.accessibility@ubc\.ca](mailto:info.accessibility@ubc.ca) or call [604 822 5844](tel:6048225844)\.

title: Documentation guidelines
content_markdown:
If you are seeking accommodations, you are required to provide the [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/) with current documentation of your medical condition or disability\.

It is your responsibility to cover any expenses related to obtaining documentation of disability\.

## Documentation copies[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/documentation\-guidelines/\#documentation\-copies](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/documentation-guidelines/#documentation-copies)

Medical documentation does not have to be created specifically for UBC\. If you have medical documentation that was obtained for another purpose \(e\.g\., for another institution\), the Centre can accept a copy if it contains sufficient information and meets the requirements outlined on this page\.

If you have applied or are in the process of applying for government funding based on disability, the Centre can accept a copy of your **Verification of Disability** **form** specific to your home province\. For example, students in British Columbia who are eligible for permanent disability programs under StudentAid BC can provide a copy of the Verification of Disability form in the [StudentAid BC Appendix 8 form](https://studentaidbc.ca/sites/all/files/form-library/disability-verification.pdf) \(pdf\) as their medical documentation\.

## Types of documentation[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/documentation\-guidelines/\#types\-of\-documentation](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/documentation-guidelines/#types-of-documentation)

You can provide documentation from certified and licensed medical doctors, psychologists, or other health professionals who have specific training, expertise, and experience in the diagnosis of conditions for which accommodation is being requested\.

The Centre for Accessibility treats documentation as confidential in accordance with [Freedom of Information Guidelines](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/governments/about-the-bc-government/open-government/open-information/freedom-of-information)\.

### Documentation requirements

Medical documentation must meet all of the following requirements:

-   It should be up to date and recent, preferably created within the last 3 years\.
-   It is legible and preferably typed and submitted on letterhead
-   Includes the practitioner’s name, license number, title, phone or fax, mailing and email addresses, and signature
-   Indicates the length of time you have been under the practitioner’s care
-   Describes the nature of your medical condition or disability, along with a detailed explanation of the functional impact of the disability\. A diagnosis alone is not sufficient to support a request for an accommodation\.
-   Provides sufficient detail so the Centre can determine appropriate accommodations
-   Describes the symptoms that formed the basis for the practitioner’s diagnosis
-   Includes relevant test results and supporting documentation if the practitioner is verifying an existing diagnosis
-   Describes the timelines for rehabilitation and recovery if the diagnosis is of a temporary nature
-   Identifies side effects of medications that may adversely affect academics

### Informational requirements

Certain disabilities have specific informational requirements, including the following:

-   Completion of a psycho\-educational assessment for a learning disability\. View [documentation standards](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/learning-disabilities-documentation-standards/) for psycho education assessments\.
-   Neuropsychological assessment for a traumatic brain injury
-   Audiology report for a hearing disability
-   Ophthalmology report for a visual disability

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/documentation\-guidelines/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/documentation-guidelines/#if-you-have-questions)

The [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/) facilitates disability\-related accommodations and supports that are designed to remove barriers for students with disabilities and ongoing medical conditions\.

Contact the Centre by email at [info\.accessibility@ubc\.ca](mailto:info.accessibility@ubc.ca) or call [604 822 5844](tel:6048225844)\.

title: Exam accommodation guidelines and expectations
content_markdown:
Exam accommodations allow you to demonstrate your knowledge of the course materials in cases where a disability or ongoing medical condition may impact your ability to access exams under standard conditions\.

If you are a student with a disability or ongoing medical conditions, you must be [registered with the Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/registering-centre-accessibility/) for exam accommodations\.

## Booking an exam[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/exam\-accommodation\-guidelines\-expectations/\#booking\-an\-exam](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/exam-accommodation-guidelines-expectations/#booking-an-exam)

If you are eligible for exam accommodations, you will likely write your exams with the [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/) because it is not always possible for your instructor or faculty to arrange exam accommodations\.

However, in some situations, you might be able to request your exam accommodation through your department\.

Whether you are writing an exam with the Centre or requesting accommodations from the department, you must book your exam according to the following steps:

1.  Complete an entry on the [Exam Registration System](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/)\. Book the exam for the same day and time as your class exam\.
2.  The online registration system will contact your instructor to obtain information for your exam\.
3.  Log into the system to review your exam date and time under “upcoming events” before the exam period\.

## Exam details[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/exam\-accommodation\-guidelines\-expectations/\#exam\-details](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/exam-accommodation-guidelines-expectations/#exam-details)

### Exam dates and deadlines

-   **Midterms, quizzes, or summer finals**  
    You must book exams at least 7 days in advance of the exam date\. This includes quizzes, in\-class tests, and any exams that have timed components\.
-   **Winter term final exams**  
    Final exams must be booked at least 7 days in advance of the start of the formal examination period, April and December only\. Late requests are not accepted by the system\.

### Exam hours

The Centre for Accessibility’s exam hours are from 8:00 am to 9:30 pm\.

#### Evening exams

The Centre does not schedule exams past 9:30 pm\. Students whose evening exam starts at 7:00 pm or later will have their exam moved up to finish at 9:30 pm\. 

### Exam location

-   Midterms and Summer term finals are held in the Accommodated Exam Writing Centre in Room 3080, Brock Commons South \([6180 Walter Gage Road](https://www.maps.ubc.ca/?show=y,n,y,n,n,y&bldg2Search=n&locat1=121-1&locat2=)\)\.
-   April and December final exams will be scheduled in Room 201, [Buchanan D](http://www.maps.ubc.ca/PROD/index_detail.php?show=y,n,y,n,n,y&bldg2Search=n&locat1=121-1&locat2=)\.

## Rules and expectations for the exam[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/exam\-accommodation\-guidelines\-expectations/\#rules\-and\-expectations\-for\-the\-exam](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/exam-accommodation-guidelines-expectations/#rules-and-expectations-for-the-exam)

Familiarize yourself with the rules and expectations for students writing exams with the Centre for Accessibility:

-   Arrive 15 minutes early and be fully prepared to start the exam\.
-   Check in with your UBC card\.
-   Students who arrive more than 30 minutes after the class start time will not be permitted to start the exam\. Students who arrive late but prior to the class start time will be able to write with deducted time\. Students will not be permitted to leave until 30 minutes after the class has started\. 
-   If your evening exam is moved up and you finish it early, you must stay in the exam room under exam conditions until 30 minutes after your original class exam time\.
-   Start and stop times for examinations will be strictly followed\.
-   Only bring material authorized by your instructor and as indicated on the exam\. Notes, books, calculators, and formula sheets will not be allowed in without explicit written authorization from the professor\.
-   You are not permitted to bring your bags or personal items into the private rooms\. Odourless food and drink are allowed\. Please do not bring foods with a strong smell, nuts, or other common allergens\.
-   No electronic devices are allowed without written permission from the instructor on the exam form, such as cell phones, MP3 players, smart watches, bluetooth headphones\.
-   You may bring your own watch or clock to keep track of time during the exam, as long as it does not have an audible alarm\.
-   Note that the invigilator will track your start and end time with the Centre’s clock, rather than your personal one\.
-   Work only within the Word document pertaining to your exam\. The use of any other function or software program requires advance authorization in writing to the Centre for Accessibility from the instructor\. 
-   If you experience a flare up during your exam, alert your invigilator\.
-   Stay in the exam room at all times\. You may leave only with the permission of the exam invigilator\.
-   Hand in all material including scrap booklets, formula sheets, and the exam question sheet at the specified end time for the exam\. Copies of the exam will not be provided\.
-   Cheating is not tolerated and will be subject to the disciplinary processes outlined by [UBC’s Student Conduct and Discipline policy](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/student-code-conduct/)\. 
-   Exam information is confidential\. If you are granted permission from your professor and Accessibility Advisor to write your exam before or after the scheduled exam for the class, do not disclose any information about the exam to anyone else\. You will be required to sign an Exam Confidentiality Agreement form\.
-   Students who are eligible for private space will write alone in an exam room with regular checks by an invigilator\. Because an invigilator is not present at all times, students will be required to undergo a security check\. Before entering the private room, lock up any unauthorized materials\. If any unauthorized materials are found once you have entered the exam room, the exam will be stopped\. The Centre for Accessibility may contact your professor and department head, and provide a report to them\. 
-   Students who are not eligible for private exam space will sit in an exam room with other students and an invigilator will be present at all times\. A security check will take place to ensure you do not have unauthorized materials in your pencil case or in your clothing\.

## Group exam components[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/exam\-accommodation\-guidelines\-expectations/\#group\-exam\-components](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/exam-accommodation-guidelines-expectations/#group-exam-components)

Academic accommodations generally do not apply to group components, which are to be written with the class

If you have an exam with a group component, then email [exam\.coordinator@ubc\.ca](mailto:exam.coordinator@ubc.ca) to schedule the individual portion of your exam with enough time to return to class to complete the group component\.

## Other exams[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/exam\-accommodation\-guidelines\-expectations/\#other\-exams](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/exam-accommodation-guidelines-expectations/#other-exams)

### Distance education exams

You can book distance exams written on campus as usual\. Final exam dates for these courses will show up on your Workday profile\. Please ensure the exam date and time are correct when you submit your booking\.

### Deferred exams

If you’re writing formal [Standing Deferral \(SD\) exams](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/exams/standing-deferred-supplemental-exams/) through the Centre for Accessibility, you must apply to write in Workday, and indicate that you would like to write your exam with the Centre\. Your information will be sent to the Centre and your exam will be booked automatically\.

Please **do not** apply through the Centre for Accessibility’s Exam Booking System unless it is a special arrangement with instructor permission on a different date and time\.

You can check your exam booking a couple of weeks before the writing date by logging in and selecting “Upcoming Events” on the Exam Booking System\. Your writing date will be the same as the rest of the class\.

### Exam scheduling exceptions

Exams for Real Estate, Continuing Education and non\-credit courses will not be scheduled online\. Contact the [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/) to make a booking\.

Real Estate students still need to contact the [Sauder School of Business Real Estate office](https://www.sauder.ubc.ca/programs/real-estate/real-estate-contact-us) to register and pay the necessary fees for writing their exams\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/exam\-accommodation\-guidelines\-expectations/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/exam-accommodation-guidelines-expectations/#if-you-have-questions)

The [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/) facilitates disability\-related accommodations and supports that are designed to remove barriers for students with disabilities and ongoing medical conditions\.

Contact the Centre by email at [info\.accessibility@ubc\.ca](mailto:info.accessibility@ubc.ca) or call [604 822 5844](tel:6048225844)\.

title: Learning disabilities documentation standards
content_markdown:
This page outlines the documentation you need to request an accommodation for a learning disability\.

## Qualified assessors[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/learning\-disabilities\-documentation\-standards/\#qualified\-assessors](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/learning-disabilities-documentation-standards/#qualified-assessors)

You must provide a qualified assessor’s report that is complete, typed on official letterhead, and signed and dated by the qualified assessor\.

A qualified assessor is one of the following:

-   A Registered Psychologist with an expertise in diagnosing Learning Disabilities \(LD\) and making educational recommendations\.
-   A Certified School Psychologist who must be or was employed by a provincially funded school board, college, or university at the time of the LD assessment\. If they are in British Columbia \(BC\), they must be a member in good standing with the [BC Association of School Psychologists](http://www.bcasp.ca/)\.

## Current Documentation[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/learning\-disabilities\-documentation\-standards/\#current\-documentation](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/learning-disabilities-documentation-standards/#current-documentation)

The qualified assessor’s report must be complete, typed on official letterhead, and signed and dated by the qualified assessor\.

The qualified assessor’s report must also include:

-   The qualified assessor’s name, title, professional credentials, address and phone, fax number, or email
-   The client’s case history
-   Review of documentation and previous testing, if any
-   Discussion of Standardized Test results including Intelligence, Aptitudes and Achievement, and Emotional Functioning
-   Appropriate Norm\-Referenced Assessment Instruments
-   Test results in Standard scores and/or percentiles
-   Conclusions and recommendations that might include specific and realistic educational accommodations accompanied by a rationale

## Learning Disability \(LD\) diagnosis[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/learning\-disabilities\-documentation\-standards/\#learning\-disability\-ld\-diagnosis](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/learning-disabilities-documentation-standards/#learning-disability-ld-diagnosis)

The Learning Disability \(LD\) diagnosis must contain and report on the following diagnostic features:

-   Diagnosis of the client’s achievement on individually administered, standardized tests in reading, mathematics, or written expression as substantially below norms\. This may include any additional factors such as an associated disorder in cognitive processing, a co\-morbid mental disorder, or general medical condition\.
-   Statement that the learning problems significantly interfere with academic achievement or occupational function that requires reading, mathematical, or writing skills
-   Description of the level of severity and how the disability interferes with academic function \(e\.g\., reading, memorizing, writing, note\-taking, test taking\)\.

The report should contain recommendations for specific reasonable accommodations needed to address the current and substantial impact of the LD on the client’s academic functioning\. Recommendations must be supported by test scores and must be included in the report\. 

The report should be current and not more than 3 to 5 years old\. Students should be at least 17 years old at the time of the testing\.

If there are any questions about LD documentation, please contact the [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/)\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/learning\-disabilities\-documentation\-standards/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/learning-disabilities-documentation-standards/#if-you-have-questions)

The [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/) facilitates disability\-related accommodations and supports that are designed to remove barriers for students with disabilities and ongoing medical conditions\.

Contact the Centre by email at [info\.accessibility@ubc\.ca](mailto:info.accessibility@ubc.ca) or call [604 822 5844](tel:6048225844)\.

title: Request an accommodation
content_markdown:
## Eligibility for accommodations[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/request\-accommodation/\#eligibility\-for\-accommodations](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/request-accommodation/#eligibility-for-accommodations)

Academic accommodations help students with a disability or ongoing medical condition overcome challenges that may affect their academic success\.

UBC’s [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/) determines a student’s eligibility for accommodations in accordance with the university’s [Disability Accommodation Policy LR7](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/Disability_Accomodation-_Policy_LR7.pdf) \(pdf\)\.

The types of conditions supported by the Centre for Accessibility include, but are not limited to:

-   Mental health conditions such as depression, anxiety disorders, or bipolar disorder
-   Neurological disabilities such as attention deficit and hyperactivity disorder, learning disabilities, head injuries, and Autism Spectrum Disorder
-   Chronic health conditions including ongoing medical conditions such as arthritis, chronic pain, Crohn’s disease, or migraines
-   Physical or sensory disabilities, such as visual impairment, hearing loss, or mobility impairments

Academic accommodations are not determined by your instructor\. However, your instructor may consult with the Centre for Accessibility should the accommodations affect the essential learning outcomes of a course\. 

### If you have a temporary injury or condition

The Centre for Accessibility typically works with students with permanent, chronic or long term conditions\. If you are experiencing a temporary injury or acute medical condition that is not expected to persist for longer than 1 term, please connect with [Academic Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/)\.

## How to request an accommodation[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/request\-accommodation/\#how\-to\-request\-an\-accommodation](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/request-accommodation/#how-to-request-an-accommodation)

To request an accommodation, you must [register with the Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/registering-centre-accessibility/) by booking an appointment with an Accessibility Advisor\. You are encouraged to register as soon as you have accepted your UBC offer of admission\.

There is typically a 1\- to 3\-week waiting period for new client appointments\. Please contact your [Academic Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) if you have a time\-sensitive, urgent academic issue such as an exam or assignment deadline before your appointment with the Centre\.

After your appointment, your Accessibility Advisor will determine the academic accommodations you’re eligible for\.

All intake appointments are scheduled for 1 hour except for prospective students and those in the Real Estate program or affiliate colleges, which are scheduled for 30 minutes\.

## Changing your academic accommodations[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/request\-accommodation/\#changing\-your\-academic\-accommodations](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/request-accommodation/#changing-your-academic-accommodations)

Meet with your Accessibility Advisor as early as possible to request new accommodations or changes to your current ones\. Depending on the nature of the accommodation and the timing of the request, it may not be possible to implement the changes immediately\.

## Confidentiality[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/request\-accommodation/\#confidentiality](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/request-accommodation/#confidentiality)

You are **not required to share information** or documentation about your disability or ongoing medical condition with your instructor or any other UBC office\. Your transcript and other student records will not show your registration with the Centre for Accessibility\.

By registering with the Centre for Accessibility, you give permission for the Centre to share the minimum information necessary to provide their service\.

The Centre for Accessibility is committed to keeping your documentation confidential in accordance with [BC’s Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act](https://www.oipc.bc.ca/for-the-public/what-are-my-rights.aspx)\.

### Inform your instructor

Once you are registered with the Centre for Accessibility, you will be able to download your Letter of Accommodation that should be given to the instructor of the class that you are seeking the accommodation in as soon as possible and preferably within the first 2 weeks of the class\.

If additional information about the nature of your disability or documentation is required, please direct your instructor or other UBC units to the Centre for Accessibility\.

## Student resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/request\-accommodation/\#student\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/request-accommodation/#student-resources)

-   [Enrolment Services support for finances, including loans and awards](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)
-   [Academic and learning resources](http://learningcommons.ubc.ca/)
-   [Resources for students with disabilities](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/resources-disabilities/)

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/request\-accommodation/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/request-accommodation/#additional-resources)

-   [Policy LR7: Academic Accommodation for Students with Disabilities](https://universitycounsel.ubc.ca/policies/disability-accommodation-policy/)
-   [Academic concessions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-concessions/)
-   [Disability information for prospective students](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/disability/)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/request\-accommodation/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/request-accommodation/#if-you-have-questions)

The [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/) facilitates disability\-related accommodations and supports that are designed to remove barriers for students with disabilities and ongoing medical conditions\.

Contact the Centre by email at [info\.accessibility@ubc\.ca](mailto:info.accessibility@ubc.ca) or call [604 822 5844](tel:6048225844)\.

title: Types of academic accommodations
content_markdown:
## Academic accommodations[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/types\-academic\-accommodations/\#academic\-accommodations](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/types-academic-accommodations/#academic-accommodations)

Academic accommodations are intended to provide students with a disability or ongoing medical condition access to the academic environment\. They do not apply to temporary injuries or acute medical conditions that are not expected to persist for longer than one term\.

While this page describes the common types of academic accommodations at UBC, the specific accommodations you’re eligible for will be determined by your Accessibility Advisor\. You must register with the [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/) to request an academic accommodation\.

View the [Accommodation Inventory](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/cfa_accommodation_inventory.pdf) \(pdf\) for a comprehensive list of accommodation examples and information on the accommodation decision\-making process\.

## Alternate format materials[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/types\-academic\-accommodations/\#alternate\-format\-materials](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/types-academic-accommodations/#alternate-format-materials)

Alternate format materials allow students with print disabilities to access academic materials in other formats such as digital audio, accessible PDF, and electronic text\.

If you are eligible for this accommodation, submit your [Alternate Format Request Form](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0Tbtus5o0IoZpDU) following the instructions provided in your alternate format welcome letter\.

Production times for materials vary depending on the format\. If possible, please send all requests **4 to 6 weeks** before the start of the course to avoid delays\. Materials will be sent to the email address you have on file, so make sure your contact information is up to date\.

## Assistive technology[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/types\-academic\-accommodations/\#assistive\-technology](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/types-academic-accommodations/#assistive-technology)

The Centre for Accessibility facilitates access to a range of assistive technology\. If you require software or other specialized equipment, please contact your Accessibility Advisor to explore your options\. You may be eligible for funding support\.

## Captioning and ASL interpreting[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/types\-academic\-accommodations/\#captioning\-and\-asl\-interpreting](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/types-academic-accommodations/#captioning-and-asl-interpreting)

ASL interpreting, real\-time captioning, and captioning media are available for eligible Deaf and hard of hearing students\.

### If you are eligible for this accommodation

If you require this accommodation, you must register with the Centre for Accessibility as early as possible or as soon as you have been offered admission and before the start of your program\.

You’ll be required to submit a [Request for Classroom Captioning or Interpreting Form](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3PigwE9Ian5OBOm) if you are eligible\. 

## Requesting Note\-taking support[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/types\-academic\-accommodations/\#requesting\-note\-taking\-support](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/types-academic-accommodations/#requesting-note-taking-support)

Your eligibility to request Note\-taking support is determined by your Accessibility Advisor\. It does not replace your attendance requirements\.

Most students will be provided with a free subscription to Genio note\-taking software\. This software supports autonomous note\-taking through customizable features, including audio recording, transcription, and integration of course notes\. Genio Notes allow quick access to your class notes immediately after class while supporting active engagement with course materials during class\. You will be required to sign an agreement to use the software\. 

If Genio Notes does not meet your accessibility needs, please contact your Accessibility Advisor to explore alternate options\.

Once you are assigned Genio Notes as your note\-taking support, please follow the steps below:

1.  Access the [ClockWork student portal](https://clockwork.as.it.ubc.ca/ClockWork/custom/misc/home.aspx) and navigate to “Online Forms”\.
2.  Carefully review and complete all sections of the “Student Agreement for using Genio Notes” and submit it\. You will receive a confirmation email while your submission is under review\.
3.  Once we have received and approved the Agreement form, you will receive an activation email from Genio with instructions on how to access Genio and set up your account\.

Your Genio account will be linked to your UBC student number and the email you have listed in Workday\.

If you have previously signed up for a Genio demo account, this can be linked to your licensed account\. Please contact [access\.assistants@ubc\.ca](mailto:access.assistants@ubc.ca) for support\.

If you no longer need Genio Notes, please email access\.assistants@ubc\.ca as soon as possible\.

## How to request an academic accommodation[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/types\-academic\-accommodations/\#how\-to\-request\-an\-academic\-accommodation](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/types-academic-accommodations/#how-to-request-an-academic-accommodation)

The Centre for Accessibility typically works with students to arrange an academic accommodation for permanent, chronic, or long\-term conditions\. To request an academic accommodation, you must register with the [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/)\. An Accessibility Advisor will determine the accommodations you are eligible for\. 

If you are experiencing a temporary injury or acute medical condition that is not expected to persist for longer than one term, please connect with [Academic Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/)\.

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-accommodations\-disabilities/types\-academic\-accommodations/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/types-academic-accommodations/#additional-resources)

title: Academic concessions
content_markdown:
An academic concession may be granted for a student when an unexpected situation or circumstance prevents them from completing graded work or exams within a term\. Please read the [UBC Academic Calendar](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/academic-concession) for complete details on academic concessions\.

Academic concessions may include:

-   Later deadline for an assignment
-   Make\-up test or quiz
-   [Deferred standing](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/grading-practices/standings) for coursework and exams
-   Late [withdrawal](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/withdrawal/introduction#251) from a course

If you have a disability or ongoing medical condition that affects your studies for **more than one term**, you may request an [academic accommodation](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/) through the [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/)\.

## Eligibility for academic concessions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-concessions/\#eligibility\-for\-academic\-concessions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-concessions/#eligibility-for-academic-concessions)

You may request an academic concession for:

-   **Unanticipated changes in personal responsibilities that create a conflict**  
    These may include family care, paid employment, religious practices, or military duty that conflict with academic requirements and are beyond your control\.
-   **Medical circumstances**  
    This can cover a mental or physical health issue that emerges or recurs during a term\.
-   **Compassionate grounds**  
    A concession may be granted when a student experiences a traumatic event, sexual assault, or death in the family or of a close friend\.

## Requesting a concession[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-concessions/\#requesting\-a\-concession](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-concessions/#requesting-a-concession)

Requests should be made as early as reasonably possible\. We understand that some issues may make it impossible for you to report until you’ve received medical attention or support for a traumatic event\.

Depending on the situation, your academic advising office or course instructor will manage your request\.

### Read the course syllabus

First, check the course syllabus to determine the options you have for making up missed work in your course\.

If the work you missed is optional \(e\.g\., it’s one of several quizzes and two can be missed without penalty\), you may not need to make up for the missed work\.

### Check with your advising office

Find information from your faculty about requesting an academic concession:

-   [Arts](https://students.arts.ubc.ca/advising/academic-performance/help-academic-concession/)
-   [Commerce](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/academic-concession)
-   [Engineering](https://academicservices.engineering.ubc.ca/exams-grades/academic-concession/)
-   [Kinesiology](https://kin.educ.ubc.ca/undergraduate/supports-resources/?login)
-   [Land and Food Systems](https://www.landfood.ubc.ca/current/undergraduate/wellness-support-and-advising/medical-personal-difficulties/)
-   [Science](https://science.ubc.ca/students/advising/concession)

If you don’t see your faculty in the list above, contact your faculty’s [academic advising office](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/)\.

You can also contact your faculty’s academic advisor if the following applies to you:

-   You’re unsure whether you’re eligible for an academic concession\.
-   Your circumstance or situation lasts more than a few days\.
-   You continue to face difficult life events repeatedly\.

## Submitting documentation[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-concessions/\#submitting\-documentation](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-concessions/#submitting-documentation)

Talk to your [academic advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) about your specific situation and to find out your options\. In some cases, submitting a “self\-declaration of absence” to your faculty’s [academic advising office](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) or your instructor may be enough\.

Example cases include, but are not limited to:

-   A sudden illness that keeps you from attending an exam
-   An arm injury the week a paper is due
-   Death in the family 
-   Mental health crisis

## Tuition adjustment or refund[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-concessions/\#tuition\-adjustment\-or\-refund](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-concessions/#tuition-adjustment-or-refund)

If you’ve received an academic concession, or withdrawn from a course under extenuating circumstances, you may be eligible for a [tuition adjustment or refund](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/tuition-refunds/)\. 

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/academic\-learning\-resources/academic\-concessions/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-concessions/#if-you-have-questions)

Talk to your [academic advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) for questions related to academic concessions and next steps\.

title: Auditing courses
content_markdown:
## What does auditing mean?[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/auditing\-courses/\#what\-does\-auditing\-mean](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/auditing-courses/#what-does-auditing-mean)

Auditing means taking a course without seeking a grade or credit\. Students usually audit courses for self\-interest and academic exploration\.

When you audit a course, your participation in the course is set by the instructor\. In general, if you’re auditing a course, you’ll be expected to complete all course requirements except the final exam, and your transcript will show a statement of audit for the course\.

If you choose to audit a course, you will still be assessed [regular tuition and mandatory student fees](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/undergraduate-tuition-fees/)\. Read more about the Audit \(AUD\) course standing in the [Academic Calendar](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/grading-practices/standings)\.

## Registering to audit a course[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/auditing\-courses/\#registering\-to\-audit\-a\-course](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/auditing-courses/#registering-to-audit-a-course)

The following instructions are for undergraduate students\. Graduate students should refer to the [Faculty of Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/current-students/managing-your-program/audit) website for information\. 

1.  Download the [Registration or Change of Registration \(Add/Drop\) Form](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/registration_adddrop_form_2024_fall.pdf) \(pdf\)\. You can also pick up a paper copy from your [faculty advising office](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) or the [Enrolment Services Advising Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) in Brock Hall\.
2.  Fill out the “Course Section Add” section of the form and check off “Audit” in the left\-hand column\.
3.  Ask your course instructor to sign the form\.
4.  Follow the instructions on the form to submit it to the appropriate office\.

## Application deadlines[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/auditing\-courses/\#application\-deadlines](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/auditing-courses/#application-deadlines)

Submit your form by the [add/drop deadline](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/course-change-dates/) to update your status to “Auditing”\.

For course\-specific add/drop deadlines, [view your course information](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/viewing-the-course-schedule/) in Workday\.

| Course type | Deadline for changing auditing status |
| --- | --- |
| 2026/27 Winter Term 1 courses | Mon, Sep 21, 2026 |
| 2026/27 Winter Term 1 and 2 courses | Mon, Sep 28, 2026 |
| 2026/27 Winter Term 2 courses | Mon, Jan 18, 2027 |

## Additional signatures you may need[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/auditing\-courses/\#additional\-signatures\-you\-may\-need](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/auditing-courses/#additional-signatures-you-may-need)

Follow the form instructions for the required signatures\. Depending on your program, you’ll need to connect with either your [faculty advising office](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) or the [Enrolment Services Advising Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

If you’re auditing a graduate\-level course, you’ll need to receive a form and signature from [Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/current-students/managing-your-program/audit)\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/auditing\-courses/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/auditing-courses/#if-you-have-questions)

For help with finances, registration, records, and more, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

title: Course modes of delivery
content_markdown:
## About UBC courses[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/course\-modes\-delivery/\#about\-ubc\-courses](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/course-modes-delivery/#about-ubc-courses)

Before registering for a course, it is important to [check the Course Schedule](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/viewing-the-course-schedule/) to learn how the course is being delivered\. At UBC, a single course may include multiple instructional formats, such as lectures, labs, seminars, or other activity types\.

Review the [guide to UBC classes](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/introduction-ubc-classes/) to learn about course formats and assessment at UBC\.

## How UBC courses are delivered[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/course\-modes\-delivery/\#how\-ubc\-courses\-are\-delivered](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/course-modes-delivery/#how-ubc-courses-are-delivered)

In the [Course Schedule](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/viewing-the-course-schedule/) in Workday, each course activity will show a “Mode of Delivery”, which describes how each individual component \(e\.g\., lecture, lab, tutorial, discussion\) within a course is going to be delivered\.

UBC offers the following course modes of delivery:

-   **In\-Person:** The course activity takes place in\-person\.
-   **Online**: The course activity is fully online and does not require any in\-person attendance to complete\.
-   **Hybrid**: The course activity has a mixture of mandatory in\-person and online activities as designed by the instructor\.
-   **Multi\-Access:** The course activity gives students the choice to attend either in person or online, as designed by the instructor\.

Make sure to check the “Notes” of each course activity on the Course Schedule to confirm how the course will be delivered\. When the term begins, read the syllabus for the most up\-to\-date and accurate course information\.

Confirm the Mode of Delivery for **all** the courses on your worklist before registering\. The Course Schedule may continue to change up until the registration date\.

## Registering for courses[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/course\-modes\-delivery/\#registering\-for\-courses](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/course-modes-delivery/#registering-for-courses)

You can [view your registration appointment](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/viewing-your-registration-appointment/) for the Winter Session in early June\. You’ll receive an email when your appointment is available in [Workday](https://myworkday.ubc.ca/)\.

Learn how to create your saved schedule and prepare for your course registration\.

[Read the guide](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/register-courses/)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/course\-modes\-delivery/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/course-modes-delivery/#if-you-have-questions)

If you’re having problems with registration, read the [Workday tutorials](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/) first\.

If you still have questions, please connect with your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

title: Credit/D/Fail grading
content_markdown:
## About Credit/D/Fail[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/creditdfail\-grading/\#about\-credit\-d\-fail](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/creditdfail-grading/#about-credit-d-fail)

The [Credit/D/Fail \(CR/D/F\) grading policy](https://senate.ubc.ca/vancouver/policies/credit-d-fail-standing/) was created to encourage students’ curiosity and learning in subjects outside of their own programs of study, and to introduce them to diverse fields\.

The policy was supported by the AMS Council and approved by the UBC Vancouver Senate in March of 2009\.

Credit/D/Fail is available to students in some direct\-entry undergraduate programs of study\. They can take eligible elective courses for Credit, D, or Fail standing instead of percentage grades\.

## How it appears on your transcript[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/creditdfail\-grading/\#how\-it\-appears\-on\-your\-transcript](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/creditdfail-grading/#how-it-appears-on-your-transcript)

If you choose the Credit/D/Fail option, you’ll be expected to complete all of the coursework and exams\. You will be assigned a percentage grade, but only the standing will be displayed on your grades record or official transcript\. These documents won’t display any percentage or letter grade\. 

You’ll get credit for courses with a Credit or D standing, but not for a Fail standing\. Courses that you take for CR/D/F won’t be counted toward your grade average calculations used for the purpose of academic performance evaluations\. However, these courses will still be considered when determining your overall [academic standing](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/academic-standing)\. If you receive a Fail standing in too many courses, including those taken as CR/D/F, you could be placed on academic probation or asked to withdraw\.

The standings are awarded for the following percentage grades:

-   **CR:** 55% or higher
-   **D:** 50 to 54\.9%
-   **F:** less than 50%, or below the passing grade

For courses or programs that define a passing grade as higher than 50%, only **CR** or **F** may be awarded\.

## Eligibility checklist[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/creditdfail\-grading/\#eligibility\-checklist](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/creditdfail-grading/#eligibility-checklist)

You’ll be eligible to take courses for Credit/D/Fail \(CR/D/F\) grading if all of the following apply:

-   You’re in a direct\-entry undergraduate program, with the exception of Applied Science\.
-   Your program allows CR/D/F courses \(check with the [Academic Advising office](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) for your program or degree\)\.
-   You understand the possible [awards implications](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/maintaining-awards-loan-eligibility/)\.
-   Your course doesn’t require a percentage grade as a prerequisite to a course you may want to take in the future\.
-   The course is an elective in your program and you are otherwise meeting all other degree requirements\.
-   You’re not taking more than 6 CR/D/F credits in one Session \(Winter or Summer\)\.
-   You don’t take more than 12 CR/D/F credits in total toward your degree program\.

### Future programs

If you’re thinking of applying to a particular graduate or other program in the future, you should consider the possible impact of CR/D/F grading on that program’s admission requirements\.

## Awards implications[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/creditdfail\-grading/\#awards\-implications](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/creditdfail-grading/#awards-implications)

### Scholarships

Students must meet the minimum course load requirements to maintain scholarship eligibility\. These requirements are based on percentage\-graded credits so Credit/D/Fail \(CR/D/F\) grading, which is not percentage graded, may affect your scholarship eligibility\.

Read [UBC’s Regulations Governing University Awards](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/university-awards) to get full details on minimum requirements for your award type\.

If you’re not sure how CR/D/F might affect your award eligibility, contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) to understand your eligibility and options\.

### Bursaries 

Credit/D/Fail grading does not impact your eligibility for bursaries, which are awarded based on financial need\. 

## Signing up for CR/D/F grading[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/creditdfail\-grading/\#signing\-up\-for\-cr\-d\-f\-grading](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/creditdfail-grading/#signing-up-for-cr-d-f-grading)

Learn how to find and get approval for [Credit/D/Fail courses](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/finding-credit-d-fail-courses/) in Workday\.

## Switching your course back to percentage grading[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/creditdfail\-grading/\#switching\-your\-course\-back\-to\-percentage\-grading](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/creditdfail-grading/#switching-your-course-back-to-percentage-grading)

Please contact the [Academic Advising office](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) of your undergraduate degree program prior to the add/drop deadline to change your course from Credit/D/Fail to percentage grading\. You cannot complete this on your own in Workday\.

### Switching after the add/drop date

Normally, switching from CR/D/F to percentage grading after the add/drop deadline is not permitted\. If you are experiencing extenuating circumstances, reach out to your faculty to discuss your options\.

## If you’ve changed your program of study[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/creditdfail\-grading/\#if\-youve\-changed\-your\-program\-of\-study](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/creditdfail-grading/#if-youve-changed-your-program-of-study)

Review the [Academic Calendar](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/grading-practices/creditdfail-grading-elective-undergraduate-courses) for more information on how changing your program of study, including adding a declared specialization, may affect your Credit or D standing\.

Learn how to use Workday for [degree planning](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/degree-planning/)\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/creditdfail\-grading/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/creditdfail-grading/#if-you-have-questions)

For help with finances, registration, records, and more, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

title: Grades
content_markdown:
## Grading practices[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/grades/\#grading\-practices](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/grades/#grading-practices)

In most faculties, individual courses are normally graded as follows\. For a complete list of grading practices, please visit the [Academic Calendar](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/grading-practices)\.

| Letter Grade | Percentage \(%\) |
| --- | --- |
| A\+ | 90 to 100 |
| A | 85 to 89 |
| A\- | 80 to 84 |
| B\+ | 76 to 79 |
| B | 72 to 75 |
| B\- | 68 to 71 |
| C\+ | 64 to 67 |
| C | 60 to 63 |
| C\- | 55 to 59 |
| D | 50 to 54 |
| F \(Fail\) | 0 to 49 |

## View your grades[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/grades/\#view\-your\-grades](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/grades/#view-your-grades)

For 2024/25 Winter Session and beyond, learn how to [view your grades](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/degree-planning/viewing-your-grades-and-academic-record/) in Workday\.

If you don’t have access to Workday, you can download an [unofficial transcript](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-transcript/#unofficial-transcript) to view your grades\.

## Release dates[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/grades/\#release\-dates](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/grades/#release-dates)

For the Winter Session, Term 1 grades are available in late December and Term 2 grades are available in late April\. Full\-year course grades are available in late April\.

Summer Session grades are available a few weeks after the course ends\.

## Review of Assigned Standing \(RAS\)[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/grades/\#review\-of\-assigned\-standing\-ras](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/grades/#review-of-assigned-standing-ras)

If you are not satisfied with your assigned standing, you are encouraged to first discuss your standing with your course instructor, when possible\.

If you still believe that your assigned standing has not been correctly evaluated, you may apply for a [Review of Assigned Standing \(RAS\)](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/review-assigned-standing):

1.  Complete the [online application form](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5BHJPuQxj9qSWWy)
2.  Pay the [RAS fee](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/fees/application-and-administrative-fees#18103)\. The fee payment is part of the online application process and is a requirement for submission\.

In the online application, you will also be required to include all course materials related to your current assigned standing\. Certain course materials such as live performances, live presentations, graduate\-level theses, doctoral dissertations, or class participation are **not** eligible for review\.

[Apply now](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5BHJPuQxj9qSWWy)

## Credit/D/Fail grading[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/grades/\#credit\-d\-fail\-grading](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/grades/#credit-d-fail-grading)

The Credit/D/Fail \(CR/D/F\) grading policy was created to encourage students’ curiosity and learning in subjects outside of their own programs of study and to introduce them to diverse fields\.

The policy was supported by the AMS Council and approved by the UBC Vancouver Senate in March 2009\.

The [Credit/D/Fail option](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/creditdfail-grading/) is available to students in some direct\-entry undergraduate programs of study\. They can take eligible elective courses and receive *Credit*, *D*, or *Fail* standing instead of percentage grades\.

title: Non-Degree Studies
content_markdown:
Non\-Degree Studies provide study options for individuals wishing to take UBC credit\-based courses without pursuing a UBC degree, diploma, or certificate\.

Non\-Degree Studies are an option for you if you meet one of the following:

-   You want to take courses for general interest\.
-   You want to take a course for professional development, upgrading or academic advancement\.
-   You are completing an undergraduate degree at another institution\.
-   You have already completed a degree\.

If you would like to take courses at the UBC Okanagan campus, please contact [UBC Okanagan Non\-Degree Studies](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/non-degree-studies/)\.

## Types of Non\-Degree Studies[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/\#types\-of\-non\-degree\-studies](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/#types-of-non-degree-studies)

[Unclassified](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-unclassified/)

This option is for students who have already completed an undergraduate degree\.

[Visiting](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-visiting/)

This option is for students who are currently enrolled in a Bachelor’s degree program at another institution\.

[Access studies](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-access-studies/)

This option is for students who have not completed an undergraduate degree and are interested in taking courses for general interest, not towards a UBC degree\.

## Enrolling in Non\-Degree Studies[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/\#enrolling\-in\-non\-degree\-studies](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/#enrolling-in-non-degree-studies)

The admission process differs based on your academic background\. However, you can follow these steps for all 3 types of Non\-Degree Studies\.

1.  Review the program requirements and submit an application for the type of Non\-Degree Studies category you want to enroll in:
    -   [Unclassified students](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-unclassified/)
    -   [Visiting students](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-visiting/)
    -   [Access Studies](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-access-studies/)
2.  Pay the application fee\.
3.  Wait for a confirmation email including next steps\.

title: Student Directed Seminars
content_markdown:
The Student Directed Seminars program provides upper\-year undergraduate students \(in third year or later\) the opportunity to propose, coordinate, and lead their own 3\-credit seminar class with a small group of peers on a topic not currently offered at UBC\-Vancouver\. Student Directed Seminars run from January to April in Winter Term 2\.

Each seminar brings together a group of highly\-motivated students to explore and investigate a topic through learning activities including group discussions, research papers, presentations, guest lectures, applied problem\-solving, and Community Service Learning\. 

If you’re a student from UBC Okanagan, please review the [Okanagan Student Directed Seminars guide](https://fass.ok.ubc.ca/student-resources/undergrad/student-directed-seminars)\.

## Get involved[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/student\-directed\-seminars/\#get\-involved](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/student-directed-seminars/#get-involved)

### Become a student coordinator

Student Directed Seminars are an expansion of the directed studies option offered by most departments and are a great way to enhance your own learning experience while gaining facilitation and leadership skills\. You will also have the unique opportunity to work closely with a faculty member to develop the course proposal and syllabus\.

[Find out more](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/student-directed-seminars/creating-student-directed-seminar/)

### Be a student participant

Student participants have a role in shaping many aspects of the course\. From helping to edit the course syllabus and choose readings, to peer marking, facilitating learning activities, and leading individual classes, each student builds their own learning experience and contributes to the learning outcomes for their peers\.

You must be a third or fourth\-year undergraduate student to register in a Student Directed Seminar\.

Registration for [Student Directed Seminars](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/student-directed-seminars/student-directed-seminar-courses/) is now open\. Review the [program guide](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/student_directed_seminar_program_guide.pdf) \(pdf\) for all available seminars\.

## Past Student Directed Seminars[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/student\-directed\-seminars/\#past\-student\-directed\-seminars](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/student-directed-seminars/#past-student-directed-seminars)

Check out [previous Student Directed Seminars](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/past_student_directed_seminars.pdf) \(pdf\) that have been successfully facilitated at UBC from 1999 to 2025\.

## Advisory committee[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/student\-directed\-seminars/\#advisory\-committee](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/student-directed-seminars/#advisory-committee)

The Student Directed Seminars Advisory Committee is made up of faculty members from various departments, staff from the Centre for Community Engaged Learning, the Alma Mater Society \(AMS\), and former Student Director Seminars Student Coordinators\.

The committee reviews all course proposals thoroughly for academic rigor, quality of course plans, appropriate marking schemes and assignments, and the overall qualifications and suitability of the student coordinator\(s\)\.
