title: Creating your Student Directed Seminar
content_markdown:
If you are an upper\-year undergraduate student \(in your third year or beyond\), you are eligible to coordinate a Student Directed Seminar\. UBC students can register in 2 Student Directed Seminars during their degree: once as Coordinator and once as a participant\. You can view [current seminars](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/student-directed-seminars/student-directed-seminar-courses/) or explore past seminars and previous faculty sponsors\.

Student Coordinators must complete mandatory training in Winter Term 1 and be prepared to facilitate their seminars in Winter Term 2 of the same academic year\.

## Application timeline[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/student\-directed\-seminars/creating\-student\-directed\-seminar/\#application\-timeline](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/student-directed-seminars/creating-student-directed-seminar/#application-timeline)

| Date | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Mar 19, 2026 | Applications open |
| May 16, 2026 at 11:59 pm | Application deadline |
| Early July | Applications are reviewed by the Advisory Committee\. Applicants are notified of the status of their application\. |
| Late July | Resubmissions are due\. |
| Early August | Applicants hear final decisions\. |
| September to December | Students attend mandatory 6 weekly program training sessions\. The sessions will take place Tuesdays from 1:00 to 3:00 pm\. Coordinators are expected to arrange their schedules around training hours\. |
| January to April | Students run their seminar\. |

## Before you submit your proposal[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/student\-directed\-seminars/creating\-student\-directed\-seminar/\#before\-you\-submit\-your\-proposal](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/student-directed-seminars/creating-student-directed-seminar/#before-you-submit-your-proposal)

There are a few things that you will need to prepare and submit a proposal\. [Read the FAQ](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/student-directed-seminars/creating-student-directed-seminar/#frequently-asked-questions) before starting your proposal\.

If you need one\-on\-one support, please book an advising session by reaching out to [student\.seminars@ubc\.ca](mailto:student.seminars@ubc.ca)\.

## Create your Student Directed Seminar[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/student\-directed\-seminars/creating\-student\-directed\-seminar/\#create\-your\-student\-directed\-seminar](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/student-directed-seminars/creating-student-directed-seminar/#create-your-student-directed-seminar)

Once you have a topic in mind for your Student Directed Seminar, you will need to complete the following steps\. You must complete and submit all components of the application package by **May 16, 2026**\. The application can take time, so don’t leave it until the last minute\.

### Step 1\. Reflect on your suitability for being a seminar coordinator

Student Coordinator roles are suited to academically motivated students who have a strong academic background and leadership experience that can translate to a classroom environment\. Student Coordinators must be willing to engage in a peer\-based learning environment and share responsibility with the participants for achieving course outcomes\. Becoming a Student Coordinator requires a significant amount of time and strong time management skills\.

All Student Coordinators must complete mandatory training in Winter Term 1 and be prepared to facilitate their seminars in Winter Term 2 of the same academic year\.

### Step 2\. Find a Faculty Sponsor

A supportive faculty member is an important part of your application process\. They can provide advice and guidance and help shape your idea into a clear and intentional course plan\. Your Faculty Sponsor must be a tenured professor or tenure\-stream who has expertise in your proposed seminar’s discipline or a closely related discipline\. An ideal Faculty Sponsor is someone who is interested in mentoring you the through course design and facilitation process\.

Finding a Faculty Sponsor can be the most difficult part of your application process, so start your search early\. Reach out to potential faculty sponsors with information about who you are, your qualifications, and your ideas about the course\.

You may want to direct your potential Faculty Sponsor to [FAQs for faculty](https://ubc.yul1.qualtrics.com/ControlPanel/File.php?F=F_9sHkIyeYrvtYLoq) \(pdf\)\.

**

Choosing a Faculty Sponsor

**

Your Faculty Sponsor should be a tenured or tenure\-stream faculty member\. Sponsoring a Student Directed Seminar requires additional work that may not be included in the work terms for faculty with other appointments\. However, with the support and approval of a Department Head, the Student Directed Seminar Advisory Committee will consider seminars supported by colleagues other than tenure or tenure\-stream faculty\. In this case, it is important that such faculty members agree to take on this supervisory role voluntarily and understand that it is not a condition of their UBC employment\.

**

If you don’t know who to approach

**

Responsibility for finding a faculty sponsor rests with aspiring student coordinators\. You should connect with a faculty sponsor whose interests align with yours and with whom you’d like to develop a close working relationship\.  When ‘cold\-calling’ professors to express interest in collaborating on an Student Directed Seminar, consider setting up a meeting to explain your interest, providing links to the Student Directed Seminar program and an abstract of your course idea\.

### Step 3\. Develop a seminar proposal

The seminar proposal is a series of questions which helps demonstrate the academic value of your proposed course in a way that links academic literature and peer\-based learning\. Your proposal also helps to contextualize why your seminar would be an asset to the scholarly community at UBC\.

A strong course proposal clearly demonstrates how your proposed course is unique, including how the material has not been offered before and how it does not duplicate an existing UBC course\.

The proposal is also an opportunity to build your idea into a concise and thoughtful plan that links an idea to implementation\. The proposal questions take a significant amount of time and effort to complete and require students to be in constant communication with their faculty sponsor\. Please keep this in mind when applying\.

Review the [Student Directed Seminar Proposal Guide](https://ubc.yul1.qualtrics.com/ControlPanel/File.php?F=F_5GAwqTX6XrQREUO) \(pdf\) for detailed instructions\.

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/student\-directed\-seminars/creating\-student\-directed\-seminar/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/student-directed-seminars/creating-student-directed-seminar/#how-to-apply)

Applications for 2026/27 Student Directed Seminars are now closed\. Check back in 2027\.

There are several components to submit as part of your application\. Review the details for each component below\.

### Required application components

**

Seminar proposal

**

The committee is looking for academically rich, challenging, and well thought\-out courses that will create an exceptional learning environment for students\. 

Once you’ve created your seminar proposal following the instructions above, submit it through the [online application form](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0d2ml3jb3akJZEq)\.

**

Unofficial transcripts \(all years\)

**

To ensure that coordinators have the academic background to undertake this rigorous form of study\. All applicants must to submit unofficial transcripts for all academic years at UBC\. Learn how to [download your unofficial transcript](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/student-documents/ordering-a-transcript/) from Workday\.

If you studied at another institution for a portion of your degree, please include those transcripts as well\. If you are not able to retrieve transcripts from other institutions, please reach out to [student\.seminars@ubc\.ca](mailto:student.seminars@ubc.ca)\.

Your unofficial transcript\(s\) must be uploaded with your online application form when you are ready to submit\.

**

Faculty sponsor form

**

This form confirms that your Faculty Sponsor has agreed to supervise your coordination of a Student Directed Seminar and can verify your qualifications to take on the role of Seminar Coordinator\. Ask your Faculty Sponsor to complete the [2026/27 Student Directed Seminars Faculty Sponsor Form](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_aeOe4xwyMo6iMRM) online by the application deadline\.

The sponsor form is only available online during the application period\. You can share [a preview of the form](https://ubc.yul1.qualtrics.com/ControlPanel/File.php?F=F_IdY93XgeQO6r1kn) \(pdf\) for their reference\.

## Sample Seminar Proposals[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/student\-directed\-seminars/creating\-student\-directed\-seminar/\#sample\-seminar\-proposals](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/student-directed-seminars/creating-student-directed-seminar/#sample-seminar-proposals)

The sample proposals shown here are for guiding purposes only\. You do not need to use this format or style for your proposal\. Application components change annually, so be sure to review all application criteria listed as you prepare your application\.

-   **2020/21 Seminar:** [BIOL 490A 201 – Ethics of Genetic Engineering](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/SDS_seminar_syllabus_ethics_genetic_engineering_2020-21.pdf) \(pdf\)
-   **2019/20 Seminar:** [LFS 490 001 – Food Justice: Eating our way towards equity](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/SDS_seminar_syllabus_food_justice_2019-20.pdf)  \(pdf\)

## If you need help with your proposal[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/student\-directed\-seminars/creating\-student\-directed\-seminar/\#if\-you\-need\-help\-with\-your\-proposal](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/student-directed-seminars/creating-student-directed-seminar/#if-you-need-help-with-your-proposal)

You may book a one\-on\-one advising session to walk through your Student Directed Seminar Proposal through email at [student\.seminars@ubc\.ca](mailto:student.seminars@ubc.ca)\.

## After your seminar is approved[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/student\-directed\-seminars/creating\-student\-directed\-seminar/\#after\-your\-seminar\-is\-approved](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/student-directed-seminars/creating-student-directed-seminar/#after-your-seminar-is-approved)

If your proposal is approved, you should begin consultation with your faculty sponsor for in\-depth seminar planning\. The mandatory training sessions will provide facilitation training, however, you should be in frequent contact with your faculty sponsor for syllabus development\.

You will be required to attend 6 in\-person training sessions during Winter Term 1 \(September to December\)\. There, you’ll gain skills on seminar facilitation, coordination, syllabus development, and promotional strategies to fill up your course\. You will also need to schedule a class meeting time, book a classroom, and identify any guest speakers you might want\.

Once you have completed your training, your seminar will be available for registration to UBC Vancouver students as a 3\-credit, upper level course\. The minimum enrolment for each seminar is 7 student participants \(including the coordinator\), and the maximum is 15\.

## Frequently asked questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/student\-directed\-seminars/creating\-student\-directed\-seminar/\#frequently\-asked\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/student-directed-seminars/creating-student-directed-seminar/#frequently-asked-questions)

**When do Student Directed Seminars run?** 

Student Directed Seminars are expected to run in Term 2 of the year your proposal is accepted, after you have completed mandatory training in Term 1\.

**

Do I have to participate in training? When does training take place?

**

All seminar coordinators **must** participate in mandatory training in Term 1 of the year their proposal is accepted\. Training is a requirement for running an SDS course\. Training takes place in Term 1 and the dates and times are decided by each cohort\.

**

I am graduating in the fall\. Can I be a student coordinator?

**

All student coordinators must be undergraduate students for the full\-year of the year their proposal is accepted \(Sept to May\) in order to complete training prior to course facilitation\. This means if you submit a proposal in the summer and are graduating in Term 1 of the same year, you are unfortunately ineligible to participate in the program\.

**

Is there a grade cut\-off to participate in the Student Directed Seminar program? My grades aren’t perfect, can I still participate?

**

The Student Directed Seminar program works with students from all academic backgrounds\. While there is no specific grade requirement, the SDS adjudication committee looks for students with a strong academic background\. Aspiring student coordinators need to demonstrate both the capacity to undertake the time commitments of coordinating an SDS and the ability to facilitate a rigorous upper\-level course\. Academic performance is one component of the adjudication process\.

**

How do I approach a Faculty Sponsor? Can you help me find a Faculty Sponsor?

**

Some best practices to consider when soliciting a faculty sponsor include:

-   Providing background information about the SDS program, including a link to the program website
-   Providing some initial ideas about your proposed course, like an abstract
-   Providing a link to the Faculty FAQ page
-   Scheduling a chat or meeting to introduce yourself

Responsibility for finding a faculty sponsor rests with aspiring student coordinators\. We suggest you look to connect with a faculty sponsor whose interests align with yours and with whom you’d like to develop a close working relationship\. When ‘cold\-calling’ professors to express interest in collaborating on an SDS, consider setting up a meeting to explain your interest, providing links to the SDS program and an abstract of your course idea\. If you’re really stuck, have a look through the list of [previous SDS faculty sponsors](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/student-directed-seminars/student-directed-seminar-courses/) or ask one of your current professors for ideas\.

**

Who makes a good Student Directed Seminar Coordinator?

**

SDS coordinators come from all backgrounds, disciplines and experiences\. Some of the characteristics which make for a successful SDS coordinator experience include:

-   Strong time\-management skills
-   A willingness to learn
-   Leadership experience
-   Strong communication skills
-   Critical thinking skills

Training is provided to help develop facilitation, teaching and communication skills\.

**

I’m not an expert in the idea I am proposing\. Is this okay?

**

Potential Student Directed Seminar coordinators are not expected to be experts in the areas they are proposing; however, background knowledge and curiosity in the topic proposed is important\. We look for proposals which demonstrate an academically rigorous knowledge base \(e\.g\., academic literature and media\)\.

**

I’m a graduate student\. Can I participate in this program?

**

Unfortunately, the Student Directed Seminars program is only available to undergraduate students in good academic standing\.

**

How are proposals adjudicated?

**

  
All proposals are reviewed by a committee of faculty, staff and alumni coordinators\. The committee looks for many qualifications, including:

-   Academic rigour
-   Demonstrated gap in the UBC curriculum
-   Qualifications of the seminar coordinator\(s\)
-   Proposed learning environment and processes

All proposals receive feedback after their first review and some proposals may require resubmission before acceptance into the program\.

Please contact the Student Directed Seminar team at [student\.seminars@ubc\.ca](mailto:student.seminars@ubc.ca)\.

title: Student Directed Seminar courses
content_markdown:
## 2025/26 Student Directed Seminars[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/student\-directed\-seminars/student\-directed\-seminar\-courses/\#2025\-26\-student\-directed\-seminars](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/student-directed-seminars/student-directed-seminar-courses/#2025-26-student-directed-seminars)

If you’re a student interested in taking a Student Directed Seminar course in the 2025/26 Winter Session, browse the course descriptions below for information\. Student Directed Seminar courses are only available to third or fourth\-year undergraduate students\. Students are allowed to enrol in a Student Directed Seminar once during their undergraduate degree\.

To register for a Student Directed Seminar course, log into your [Course Schedule](https://wd10.myworkday.com/ubc/d/faceted-search2/c55/fs1/recover-current-state.htmld) and search the course code, or contact the student coordinator directly for more information\. Some courses may have specific requirements and instructions you need to follow in order to register for the course\. Please read each course description carefully\.

Some seminars may have a selection process due to limited seating\. If you’re unable to register for a seminar through the [Course Schedule](https://wd10.myworkday.com/ubc/d/task/1422$5132.htmld), reach out to the Student Coordinator\(s\) for assistance\.

The UBC Okanagan Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences is currently developing a Student Directed Seminars course for its students\. For further information, please email [fasscurriculum\.ubco@ubc\.ca](mailto:fasscurriculum.ubco@ubc.ca)\.

## UBC Vancouver Winter Term 2 courses[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/student\-directed\-seminars/student\-directed\-seminar\-courses/\#ubc\-vancouver\-winter\-term\-2\-courses](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/student-directed-seminars/student-directed-seminar-courses/#ubc-vancouver-winter-term-2-courses)

### ASTU 400K\-001: Biochemical Pathways of Human Emotions

-   **Student Coordinator:** Lillian Pernitsky 
-   **Student Coordinator email:** [lpernits@student\.ubc\.ca](mailto:lpernits@student.ubc.ca)
-   **Faculty Sponsor:** Eden Fussner\-Dupas

This seminar is scheduled for Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays from 2 to 3 pm\. You can view this seminar on the [Workday Course Schedule](https://wd10.myworkday.com/ubc/d/inst/15$365714/15194$464866.htmld)\.

Biochemical Pathways of Human Emotions explores how emotions such as fear, bonding, and happiness arise from molecular signaling networks, neurochemical pathways, and endocrine systems\. Students will analyze the biochemistry and neurophysiology of emotional states through scientific literature, pharmacological case studies, and interactive peer learning\. Designed for students with a background in biochemistry, biology, or neuroscience, this seminar offers a rigorous, interdisciplinary investigation into the molecular basis of what we feel and why\. 

### ISCI 490\-202: The Neuroscience of Free Will

-   **Student Co\-coordinators:** Kiara Sun and Alyssa Aguason
-   **Student Co\-coordinator’s emails:**
    -   Kiara: [ksun11@student\.ubc\.ca](mailto:ksun11@student.ubc.ca)
    -   Alyssa: [aaguason@student\.ubc\.ca](mailto:aaguason@student.ubc.ca)
-   **Faculty Sponsor:** Angela O’Neill

This seminar is scheduled for Wednesdays from 5:00 to 8:00 pm\. You can view this seminar on the [Workday Course Schedule](https://wd10.myworkday.com/ubc/d/inst/15$365714/15194$452888.htmld)\.

This course will explore free will, a controversial topic that lies at the interface between philosophy and neuroscience\. Starting from the foundational philosophical arguments, students will be encouraged to share their own conceptions of free will, which will then be challenged through classical and contemporary neuroscientific experiments; from lesion case studies to priming effects to the neural underpinnings of decision\-making\. Additionally, the implications of free will will be explored at the individual and societal levels with particular emphasis placed on the criminal justice system\. In this way, the seminar will uniquely approach a traditional philosophical topic from a neuroscience perspective, underscoring the capacity for neuroscience to inform philosophical discourse\.

### ASTU 400J\-001: The Brain in Balance: Exploring Wellness Through a Neuroscientific Lens

-   **Student Coordinator:** David Roberts
-   **Student Coordinator email:** [drober05@student\.ubc\.ca](mailto:drober05@student.ubc.ca)
-   **Faculty Sponsor:** Todd Handy

This seminar is scheduled for Mondays and Wednesdays from 4 to 5:30 pm\. You can view this seminar on the [Workday Course Schedule](https://wd10.myworkday.com/ubc/d/inst/15$365714/15194$464829.htmld)\.

The Brain in Balance: Exploring Wellness Through a Neuroscientific Lens is a student\-directed seminar that investigates the intersection of neuroscience, wellness, and technology\. It explores how neuroscience informs understandings of mental health, resilience, and healing, focusing on neuroplasticity, stress regulation, and the mind\-body connection\. Attention is given to digital culture—particularly social media—examining both risks \(e\.g\., digital addiction, cyberbullying\) and emerging wellness tools \(e\.g\., mindfulness apps, biofeedback, virtual therapy\)\. 

### ASTU 400E\-001: Neuroaesthetics: Your Brain on Art

-   **Student Co\-coordinators:** Leo Chung and Betty Bao
-   **Student Co\-coordinator’s emails:** 
    -   Leo: [ljchung@student\.ubc\.ca](mailto:ljchung@student.ubc.ca)
    -   Betty: [bettybao507@gmail\.com](mailto:bettybao507@gmail.com)
-   **Faculty Sponsor:** Steven Barnes

This seminar is scheduled for Tuesdays and Thursdays from 5:00 to 6:30 pm\. You can view this seminar on the [Workday Course Schedule](https://wd10.myworkday.com/ubc/d/inst/15$365714/15194$464845.htmld)\.

What makes something beautiful? How universal is the experience of beauty? This SDS will explore the field of neuroaesthetics – scientific study of the neural mechanisms of hedonic valuation, artistic creation, and aesthetic appreciation – allowing students to explore how their brains perceive and experience art \(visual art, music, architecture, film, literature, etc\.\), and how art can affect their brain\. The proposed SDS will include student\-led discussions, multimodal generative assignments and in\-class activities \(e\.g\., visual art, reflective writing—both solo and collaborative\), and visits by guest speakers\. 

### ASTU 400L\-001: Biopsychosocial Model in Medicine: Integrating Mind, Body, and Society

-   **Student Coordinator:** Lavleen Walia
-   **Student Coordinator email:** [lavleenw28@gmail\.com](mailto:lavleenw28@gmail.com)
-   **Faculty Sponsor:** Benjamin Cheung

This seminar is scheduled for Mondays and Wednesdays from 12:30 pm to 2:00 pm\. You can view this seminar on the [Workday Course Schedule](https://wd10.myworkday.com/ubc/d/inst/15$365714/15194$464883.htmld)\. 

Through case studies, reflective writing, and dialogue with peers and community voices, students will explore how biological, psychological, and social factors intersect in health and illness, with particular attention to the experiences of marginalized communities\. The course fosters collaborative learning, respectful discussion, and the development of patient\-centered, integrative approaches to care\. Although the biopsychosocial model is widely recognized in theory, its application in healthcare often falls short, with biomedical approaches dominating diagnosis and treatment\. This student\-led seminar critically examines the gap between theory and practice, drawing on psychology, biology, sociology, cultural studies, and medical ethics\.

### ASTU 400C\-001: Contemporary Feminism in Chinese Media

-   **Student Coordinator:** Clair Tang
-   **Student Coordinator email:** [clairtang9628@gmail\.com](mailto:clairtang9628@gmail.com)
-   **Faculty Sponsor:** Jiaqi Yao

This seminar is scheduled for Mondays and Wednesdays from 4:00 pm to 5:30 pm\. You can view this seminar on the [Workday Course Schedule](https://wd10.myworkday.com/ubc/d/inst/15$365714/15194$464809.htmld)\.

What is the state of feminism in today’s China? How shall one interpret its complex development and \(increasingly\) sensitive associations in a media context? In this seminar, we will engage with the most raw, compelling, and fascinating aspects of contemporary Chinese feminism through hands\-on examinations of women’s experiences as depicted and reflected in many facets of popular media\. Topics covered range from the creation and reception of feminist filmmaking, TV, literature, and video games to how feminism in China navigates media censorship, expressions of sexuality, queer cultures, and more\. We aim to gather a nuanced understanding of how Chinese women today pursue social justice\. Anyone interested is welcome to the discussion, regardless of prior knowledge of the Chinese languages\. 

### ASTU 400F\-001: Postcolonial Considerations of Literature from the Caucasus and Central Asia

-   **Student Coordinator**: Selin Berktas
-   **Student Coordinator email:** [selinberktash9@gmail\.com](mailto:selinberktash9@gmail.com)
-   **Faculty Sponsor:** Katherine Bowers

This seminar is scheduled for Tuesdays and Thursdays from 4:00 to 5:30 pm\. You can view this seminar on the [Workday Course Schedule](https://wd10.myworkday.com/ubc/d/inst/15$365714/15194$464769.htmld)\.

This seminar considers Central Asian and Caucasian literature, as readily available resources to self\-map and understand from the inside, through a postcolonial lens\. It utilizes a postcolonial approach to center the so\-called periphery\. Specific themes include citizenship, identity, empire, and how they construct one another\. How does literature inform or mirror these concepts? How does literary form build narratives, break them, and simultaneously revise them? Taking note of collective knowledge, literature acts as resistance through tangible practices of observation, note\-taking, and documenting\. How can we use literature in the field to map various texts out contrapuntally, as sums of a whole, moving beyond the “insularity and provincialism” of literature as stated by Edward Said? 

### ASTU 400H\-001: Understanding Loss and Grief: An Interdisciplinary Approach 

-   **Student Coordinator:** Atrina Shadgan
-   **Student Coordinator email:** [mailto:atrinashadgan@gmail\.com](mailto:atrinashadgan@gmail.com)[atrinashadgan@gmail\.com](mailto:atrinashadgan@gmail.com)
-   **Faculty Sponsor:** Sunaina Assanand

This seminar is scheduled for Wednesdays from 4:00 pm to 7:00 pm\. You can view this seminar on the [Workday Course Schedule](https://wd10.myworkday.com/ubc/d/inst/15$365714/15194$464837.htmld)\.

What happens when we lose someone or something important to us? How do such painful losses shape our lives and communities? Grief is a complex and multidimensional response to many different forms of loss\- not just death\. In this seminar, we will explore the psychological, sociocultural, and neurobiological dimensions of grief, while considering how individual experiences of grief are shaped by broader systemic forces and contexts\. Through engagement with diverse models of grief, in\-class discussions, and interdisciplinary projects, students will develop a deep understanding of how loss and grief are experienced, expressed, and supported across different individuals and communities\. 

### ENGL 336A\-001: Unhidden Currents: Media, Propaganda and the Architecture of Influence

-   **Student Coordinator:** Alicia Matthews
-   **Student Coordinator email:** [aliciajanetmatthews@gmail\.com](mailto:aliciajanetmatthews@gmail.com)
-   **Faculty Sponsor:** Richard Cavell

This seminar is scheduled for Mondays from 2:00 pm to 5:00 pm\. You can view this seminar on the [Workday Course Schedule](https://wd10.myworkday.com/ubc/d/inst/15$365714/15194$464805.htmld)\.

How can cognitive autonomy survive under the attention economy? In an age of increasing technocracy and polarization, how might we mitigate widening ideological gaps, confront social atomization and question our own media consumption habits? These are pertinent questions discussed in popular culture, yet the societal and psychological effects of media in the digital age remain understudied in academia\. This seminar aims to bridge that gap through an interdisciplinary inquiry into the often\-invisible infrastructures of propaganda and persuasion in contemporary Western culture\. Assignments involve critical readings, field research, and a collaborative digital humanities project\.

title: Taking a break from your courses
content_markdown:
## About academic leave[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/taking\-break\-courses/\#about\-academic\-leave](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/taking-break-courses/#about-academic-leave)

In accordance with the [Academic Calendar](http://www.calendar.ubc.ca/vancouver/index.cfm?tree=3,289,0,0), for most programs, students in “Good Standing” may take an Academic Leave \(time away from UBC studies\) of up to one full year or 12 months\. 

Students in some programs are required to seek permission for an academic leave before leaving\. All students should discuss their plans with an academic advisor in their faculty or school before requesting a leave\.

For example, a student in “Good Standing” after completing the 2025/26 Winter Session will automatically be eligible to register in the same program for the 2026 Summer, 2026/27 Winter, 2027 Summer and 2027/28 Winter Sessions\.

### Consequences of not being in good standing

If you’re placed on academic probation, you may be restricted to register in a maximum number of credits in the following term\. Please see your faculty’s academic regulations or contact your faculty’s [advising office](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) for more information\.

### Programs requiring approval for Academic Leave

If you are in a cohort\-based or a limited enrolment program, you are required to seek permission for an academic leave before taking time away due to the limited ability to accommodate leaves in such programs\.

However, for all other programs, you are highly encouraged to notify your faculty to ensure you understand the implications and next steps\. Please [contact your faculty or school](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) before taking an academic leave\.

## Requesting an Academic Leave[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/taking\-break\-courses/\#requesting\-an\-academic\-leave](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/taking-break-courses/#requesting-an-academic-leave)

### Undergraduate students

If you are an undergraduate student and want to take time off, complete the steps below:

1.  Review UBC’s policy on [academic leave](http://www.calendar.ubc.ca/vancouver/index.cfm?tree=3,289,0,0)\.
2.  Talk to an [academic advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) in your program or faculty for program\-specific requirements\.
3.  Check with an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) to see if taking a break will affect your financial assistance or awards\.

### International students

If you’re an international student, there are special considerations around taking time off\. Read the [important steps to take](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/taking-time-away-school-international/) for requesting time away from your studies and contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) if you are planning to take a break\.

### Graduate students

If you’re a graduate student, you’ll have to apply for a leave of absence from [Graduate and Post\-doctoral Studies](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/)\.

## Returning from academic leave[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/taking\-break\-courses/\#returning\-from\-academic\-leave](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/taking-break-courses/#returning-from-academic-leave)

If you have been away for one year, there are specific instructions for returning to your studies depending on your situation\.

**

You did not attend school elsewhere

**

You will automatically receive a registration appointment and be sent an email with your registration date and time\. If you do not register by Term 2 of the Winter session in which you are expected to return, your record will be discontinued\.

**

You would like to return to a new program

**

1.  Log into your [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/)\.
2.  Click the blue “Re\-Admission/Change Program” button on the right\.
3.  Under “First Program Selection”, choose the program you would like to apply to using the drop\-down\.

## Extending an academic leave[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/taking\-break\-courses/\#extending\-an\-academic\-leave](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/taking-break-courses/#extending-an-academic-leave)

If you decide to extend your academic leave beyond one year, discuss your plans with a [Faculty Academic Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) and your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\. If you’re an international student, connect with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) first\.

You will need to submit an application for readmission to resume your studies when you are ready through the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/)\. Each faculty has different readmission deadlines, and there may be financial implications if you have awards, scholarships or government student loans\.

If you cannot log into [Workday](https://myworkday.ubc.ca/), you will regain access once you are readmitted to UBC\. If you need to download your [unofficial transcript](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-transcript/#unofficial-transcript) or order an [official transcript](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-transcript/#pdf-transcript), you can complete this request through the [UBC Official Documents tool](https://ubc.appiancloud.com/suite/sites/ubc-official-documents)\.

title: Academic concessions for Non-Degree Studies
content_markdown:
## About academic concessions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/academic\-concessions\-non\-degree\-studies/\#about\-academic\-concessions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/academic-concessions-non-degree-studies/#about-academic-concessions)

An [academic concession](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/academic-concession) is an accommodation for students who are unable to fulfill course requirements due to extenuating circumstances\.

You may be eligible for an academic concession in your course if medical or personal difficulties prevent you from continuing your studies\. You will need to submit a request for concession as soon as possible\.

An academic concession may be a [deferred standing](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/exams/standing-deferred-supplemental-exams/) \(SD\) or a late withdrawal from a course\.

## Eligibility for academic concessions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/academic\-concessions\-non\-degree\-studies/\#eligibility\-for\-academic\-concessions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/academic-concessions-non-degree-studies/#eligibility-for-academic-concessions)

You may be eligible for an academic concession when you’re not able to complete an assignment, write an exam on time, or participate in classes due to one or more of the conditions below:

-   [Medical circumstances](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/academic-concession#26588)
-   [Compassionate grounds](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/academic-concession#26589)
-   [Conflicting responsibilities](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/academic-concession#26587)

You must apply for your academic concession as early as possible\.

## Deadlines to apply for an academic concession[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/academic\-concessions\-non\-degree\-studies/\#deadlines\-to\-apply\-for\-an\-academic\-concession](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/academic-concessions-non-degree-studies/#deadlines-to-apply-for-an-academic-concession)

You must apply for an end\-of\-term concession by the following deadlines:

| Date | Session |
| --- | --- |
| January 15 | Winter Session, Term 1 |
| May 15 | Winter Session, Term 2 |
| September 15 | Summer Session |

## How to apply for an academic concession[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/academic\-concessions\-non\-degree\-studies/\#how\-to\-apply\-for\-an\-academic\-concession](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/academic-concessions-non-degree-studies/#how-to-apply-for-an-academic-concession)

1.  Complete the [academic concession form](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0ixlx9Vh6cuMF7w) so that an advisor can review your case\. Your concession cannot be processed until the form is filled out\. You don’t need to contact the Non\-Degree Studies team or speak to an advisor before filling out the form\.
2.  You will receive a decision or instructions for next steps within 5 to 7 business days\.

## Late withdrawal[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/academic\-concessions\-non\-degree\-studies/\#late\-withdrawal](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/academic-concessions-non-degree-studies/#late-withdrawal)

You are not permitted to withdraw from a course after the [course/drop/withdrawal deadline](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/course-change-dates/), unless you qualify for an academic concession due to extenuating circumstances\.

Requests to withdraw due to anticipation of an unsatisfactory academic outcome or neglect of the coursework will be refused\.

If you are approved for a late withdrawal from a course, the university’s normal policy of [refund of tuition fees](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/fees/tuition-fees/refund-tuition-fees#18000) applies\. You will be assessed the full tuition and student fees for the course\. The concession will be noted on your transcript with a [W standing](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/grading-practices/standings) for the course\.

## Deferred standing[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/academic\-concessions\-non\-degree\-studies/\#deferred\-standing](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/academic-concessions-non-degree-studies/#deferred-standing)

Before applying, please read through details about [Standing Deferred and Supplemental exams](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/exams/standing-deferred-supplemental-exams/)\.

Follow the steps below if your academic concession for a deferred standing is approved and an “SD” has been added to your student record:

1.  Apply through your [Workday](https://myworkday.ubc.ca/) account to write your exam\(s\) in the application period outlined by Enrolment Services\.
2.  Write your deferred exam as scheduled by Enrolment Services\. Deferred exams for Winter Session courses are held the following July or August\. Deferred exams for Summer Session courses are held in November\.
3.  Submit incomplete coursework as per your instructor’s directions and deadlines\.

## Missed midterm work[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/academic\-concessions\-non\-degree\-studies/\#missed\-midterm\-work](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/academic-concessions-non-degree-studies/#missed-midterm-work)

Any incomplete work during the term must be handled between you and your instructor, in accordance with written guidelines given at the start of the course\. Review [UBC grading practices](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/grading-practices/introduction) and your course syllabus for guidelines\.

If you want an extension for incomplete work, contact your instructor directly and arrange to make up or complete the work, if permitted\.

Your instructor is not required to make allowance for any missed test or incomplete work that is not satisfactorily accounted for\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/academic\-concessions\-non\-degree\-studies/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/academic-concessions-non-degree-studies/#if-you-have-questions)

Contact Enrolment Services by phone at [604 822 9836](tel:6048229836) or email [non\.degree@ubc\.ca](mailto:non.degree@ubc.ca)\.

title: Non-Degree Studies for Access Studies
content_markdown:
## Eligibility for Access Studies[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/non\-degree\-studies\-access\-studies/\#eligibility\-for\-access\-studies](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-access-studies/#eligibility-for-access-studies)

If you haven’t completed a degree but you’d like to take courses for general interest at UBC outside of a degree program, you can apply as an Access Studies student\.

To be eligible, you must meet all the following requirements:

-   You fulfill the [English language requirement](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/english-language-competency/)\.
-   You meet UBC’s [criteria for Access Studies](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/admissions/classification-students) students\.
-   You do not hold a bachelor’s degree from a recognized institution\.

If you’re a senior citizen or a current high school student, there are additional steps you’ll need to follow\. Review the information in the sections below\.

## Considerations for Access Studies students[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/non\-degree\-studies\-access\-studies/\#considerations\-for\-access\-studies\-students](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-access-studies/#considerations-for-access-studies-students)

-   Enrolment for Access Studies students is limited to 6 credits per term and a lifetime maximum of 24 credits\.
-   Being admitted to UBC as an Access Studies student does not guarantee enrolment in requested courses or admission to a degree program at UBC\.
-   You may be able to transfer your course credits to a future UBC degree program at the discretion of the faculty you apply to\.
-   To register, you’ll need to meet course prerequisites through previous study, relevant experience, or instructor permission\.

## Application dates[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/non\-degree\-studies\-access\-studies/\#application\-dates](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-access-studies/#application-dates)

| Course start date | Application deadline |
| --- | --- |
| September for Winter Session Term 1 | July 15 |
| January for Winter Session Term 2 | October 15 |
| May for Summer Session Term 1 or 2 | March 15 |

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/non\-degree\-studies\-access\-studies/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-access-studies/#how-to-apply)

### Select your courses

1.  Use the [Course Search](https://courses.students.ubc.ca/course-search) to find eligible courses in Arts, Forestry, Land and Food Systems, or Science\.
2.  Select “Course Search” and enter the subject area or keywords for your area of interest, making sure that you meet the stated course restrictions and prerequisites\.

### Apply online

All new and previously registered students must complete the steps below:

1.  Create an [Education Planner BC account](https://apply.educationplannerbc.ca/) online\. 
2.  Fill in your personal information and academic history\.  
3.  Click *Start Applying* and select “University of British Columbia” as the institution\.
4.  Select the appropriate Admissions Category based on your academic history\.
5.  Select “Access Student” under *First Program Choice*\. You do not need to select a second program choice\.
6.  When asked, make sure to include the list of course\(s\) you’re interested in taking or the specific program under which you would like to take courses\.
7.  UBC Admissions will email you with a confirmation of your application and next steps\.
8.  After completing your application, email any additional and required documents to [non\.degree@ubc\.ca](mailto:non.degree@ubc.ca)\.

## Senior citizens[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/non\-degree\-studies\-access\-studies/\#senior\-citizens](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-access-studies/#senior-citizens)

If you’re a Canadian citizen or permanent resident that is 65 years of age or older, you are eligible to apply through Access Studies to take courses for general interest if you meet the following requirements:

-   You are a British Columbia resident\.
-   You do not hold a bachelor’s degree from a recognized institution\. If you completed a bachelor’s degree, you need to apply as an [unclassified student](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-unclassified/)\.

### Tuition costs for senior citizens

Normally, senior citizens do not pay [tuition or student fees](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/fees/policies-fees#18205), except for programs within Dentistry, Law, Medicine, Nursing, Pharmacy, or any faculty or school where existing facilities and resources are limited\.

If you wish to opt in to the full suite of student fees, please email [non\.degree@ubc\.ca](mailto:non.degree@ubc.ca)\.

Expect to pay about $100 to $150 per course for course materials, which are available through the [UBC Bookstore](http://www.bookstore.ubc.ca/)\.

### How to apply as a senior citizen

Follow the same application instructions as mentioned above, then email [non\.degree@ubc\.ca](mailto:non.degree@ubc.ca) with proof of your date of birth as well as British Columbia \(BC\) residency, such as a photocopy of your BC driver’s license\. Include your UBC reference or student number\.

## Concurrent high school students[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/non\-degree\-studies\-access\-studies/\#concurrent\-high\-school\-students](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-access-studies/#concurrent-high-school-students)

To be considered for concurrent studies at UBC as an Access Studies student, you must meet all of the following requirements:

-   You are in good academic standing and have a [superior academic record](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/admissions/applicants-following-bcyukon-secondary-school-curriculum/concurrent-enrolment-policy)\.
-   You are enrolled in a British Columbia secondary school in a program that meets [regular UBC entry requirements](http://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/canadian-highschools)\.
-   You are 16 years of age or older at the start of studies\.
-   You can provide a written recommendation from your high school principal\.
-   You have the written consent of your parent or legal guardian\.

### How to apply as a high school student

Submit your application and required materials by the deadline, and UBC Admissions will submit them to your chosen faculty for evaluation\.

Once you have been approved by the faculty for enrolment in courses at UBC, you will receive an email with confirmation and registration instructions\. Submit supporting documentation to [non\.degree@ubc\.ca](mailto:non.degree@ubc.ca) with your full name and UBC reference \(student\) number\.

Access studies is not intended for recent high school graduates who have already applied to an undergraduate degree program at UBC or wish to pursue one in the near future\.

## UBC’s inclusive post\-secondary education initiative[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/non\-degree\-studies\-access\-studies/\#ubcs\-inclusive\-post\-secondary\-education\-initiative](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-access-studies/#ubcs-inclusive-post-secondary-education-initiative)

If you have developmental or intellectual disabilities and are interested in attending post\-secondary education in a way that supports your strengths and learning style, consider applying for UBC’s inclusive post\-secondary education initiative with the [STEPS Forward program](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/how-to-apply/disability/#component-3)\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/non\-degree\-studies\-access\-studies/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-access-studies/#if-you-have-questions)

Contact Enrolment Services by phone at [604 822 9836](tel:6048229836) or email [non\.degree@ubc\.ca](mailto:non.degree@ubc.ca)\.

title: Non-Degree Studies tuition and fees
content_markdown:
## Application fee[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/non\-degree\-studies\-tuition\-fees/\#application\-fee](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-tuition-fees/#application-fee)

Students enrolled in [Non\-Degree Studies](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/) are required to pay an [application fee](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/fees/application-and-administrative-fees)\.

## Tuition fees[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/non\-degree\-studies\-tuition\-fees/\#tuition\-fees](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-tuition-fees/#tuition-fees)

Your [tuition fees](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/fees/tuition-fees/undergraduate#17997) are assessed on a per\-credit basis and depend on the level of the course\.

Most undergraduate courses are 3 or 6 credits, with some exceptions\. You can check the [Course Search](https://courses.students.ubc.ca/course-search) for specific course information, including number of credits, when and where the course is offered, and who the course instructor is\.

Like degree\-seeking students, you are assessed [student fees](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/fees/student-fees)\. While some student fees are prorated based on the number of credits you are registered in, most are assessed on a one\-time basis\. There are some student fees that you can choose to [opt out](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/fees/student-fees/refunds-and-opting-out-student-fees) of\.

Non\-Degree Studies students are held to the same policies surrounding registration and tuition as degree seeking students at UBC\. It is the [student’s responsibility](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/student-declaration-and-responsibility) to periodically check their student account for any changes and to ensure that their registration and finances are up to date\.

## Course materials[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/non\-degree\-studies\-tuition\-fees/\#course\-materials](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-tuition-fees/#course-materials)

Expect to pay about $100 to $150 per course for course materials, such as textbooks or online educational software, which are available through the [UBC Bookstore](http://bookstore.ubc.ca/home)\.

## Exceptions for tuition and fees[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/non\-degree\-studies\-tuition\-fees/\#exceptions\-for\-tuition\-and\-fees](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-tuition-fees/#exceptions-for-tuition-and-fees)

### Senior citizens

BC residents 65 years of age and older who are Canadian citizens or permanent residents normally do not pay tuition, application, or student fees\.

However, fees may be assessed for programs within Dentistry, Law, Medicine, Nursing, Pharmacy, or any faculty or school where existing facilities and resources are limited\.

If you wish to opt into the full suite of student fees, please email [non\.degree@ubc\.ca](mailto:non.degree@ubc.ca)\.

### UBC faculty and staff members

UBC’s faculty and staff [tuition waiver](https://hr.ubc.ca/benefits/benefit-plan-details/tuition-waivers) covers tuition fees **only**\. Other fees that may be associated with each course, like assessed [student fees](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/fees/student-fees), are not covered by the waiver\.

The tuition waiver is not managed by Non\- Degree Studies\. Please connect with UBC Human Resources to facilitate the tuition waiver process once you are registered in courses\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/non\-degree\-studies\-tuition\-fees/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-tuition-fees/#if-you-have-questions)

Contact Enrolment Services by phone at [604 822 9836](tel:6048229836) or email [non\.degree@ubc\.ca](mailto:non.degree@ubc.ca)\.

title: Non-Degree Studies for unclassified students
content_markdown:
## Eligibility for Unclassified Studies[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/non\-degree\-studies\-unclassified/\#eligibility\-for\-unclassified\-studies](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-unclassified/#eligibility-for-unclassified-studies)

As an unclassified student, you can continue to take courses at UBC even after completing a recognized 4\-year bachelor’s degree program\.

To be eligible, you must meet all of the following requirements:

-   You meet the [English language requirement](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/english-language-competency/)\.
-   You have completed a bachelor’s degree from a recognized institution\.
-   You can provide a final official transcript showing your degree conferral\.

If you’re a senior citizen, there are additional steps you’ll need to follow, which you can review in [the section below](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-unclassified/#senior-citizens)\.

If you plan to take Faculty of Education courses only as an unclassified student, apply directly to the [Faculty of Education](http://teach.educ.ubc.ca/admissions/visiting-and-unclassified-students/)\.

## Considerations for unclassified students[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/non\-degree\-studies\-unclassified/\#considerations\-for\-unclassified\-students](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-unclassified/#considerations-for-unclassified-students)

-   Depending on the time of year, it may take several weeks for your documents to reach UBC Admissions and be processed\.
-   Being admitted as an unclassified student does not guarantee enrolment in requested courses or admission to a degree program at UBC\.
-   Credits from your courses may be transferable to a future UBC degree program at the discretion of the faculty you apply to\.
-   Non\-Degree students are not eligible for [Credit/D/Fail grading](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/creditdfail-grading/)\. However, you may consider [auditing courses](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/auditing-courses/)\.

Make sure you include the following information:

title: Non-Degree Studies for visiting students
content_markdown:
## Eligibility for visiting students[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/non\-degree\-studies\-visiting/\#eligibility\-for\-visiting\-students](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-visiting/#eligibility-for-visiting-students)

Non\-Degree Studies are available for students enrolled in a bachelor’s degree at another institution\.

You can apply to be considered a visiting student if you meet all the following requirements:

-   You meet the [English language requirement](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/english-language-competency/)\.
-   You are in good academic standing\.
-   You are enrolled in a bachelor’s degree program at a recognized institution\.
-   You can provide a [Letter of Permission](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-visiting/#letter-of-permission)\.

If you are enrolled in a graduate degree and would like to take graduate level courses or pursue research at UBC, apply directly as a [Visiting Graduate Student](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/current-students/student-status-classification/visiting-graduate-students)\.

## Considerations for visiting students[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/non\-degree\-studies\-visiting/\#considerations\-for\-visiting\-students](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-visiting/#considerations-for-visiting-students)

-   Being admitted as a visiting student does not guarantee your enrolment in requested courses or admission to a degree program at UBC\.
-   Your credits from courses may be transferable to a future UBC degree program at the discretion of the faculty you apply to\.
-   Non\-Degree students are not eligible for [Credit/D/Fail grading](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/creditdfail-grading/) but you may consider [auditing courses](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/auditing-courses/)\.
-   Visiting students are admitted to UBC for one academic session, either Winter or Summer, at a time\. If you want to continue studying at UBC as a visiting student in the next session, please email [non\.degree@ubc\.ca](mailto:non.degree@ubc.ca)\.

## Eligible courses[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/non\-degree\-studies\-visiting/\#eligible\-courses](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-visiting/#eligible-courses)

Visiting students can take courses in the following faculties:

-   [Arts](https://www.arts.ubc.ca/)
-   [Science](https://science.ubc.ca/)
-   [Forestry](https://forestry.ubc.ca/)
-   [Land and Food Systems](https://www.landfood.ubc.ca/)
-   [Applied Science](https://apsc.ubc.ca/)
-   [Faculty of Education](http://educ.ubc.ca/)

If you’re taking Applied Science courses, you will not receive an admission decision until after degree\-seeking students have registered and shortly before the start of classes\.

If you plan to take Faculty of Education courses only, please apply directly to the [Faculty of Education](http://teach.educ.ubc.ca/admissions/visiting-and-unclassified-students/)\.

You can use the [Course Search](https://courses.students.ubc.ca/course-search) to view current course offerings\.

## Application deadlines[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/non\-degree\-studies\-visiting/\#application\-deadlines](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-visiting/#application-deadlines)

| Course start date | Application deadline |
| --- | --- |
| September for Winter Session Term 1 | July 15 |
| January for Winter Session Term 2 | July 15 |
| May for Summer Session Term 1 or 2 | March 15 |

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/non\-degree\-studies\-visiting/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-visiting/#how-to-apply)

All new and previously registered students must complete the steps below:

1.  Create an [Education Planner BC account](https://apply.educationplannerbc.ca/) online\. 
2.  Fill in your personal information and academic history\.  
3.  Click *Start Applying* and select “University of British Columbia” as the institution\.
4.  Select the appropriate Admissions Category based on your academic history\.
5.  Select “Visiting Student” under *First Program Choice*\. You do not need to select a second program choice\.
6.  UBC Admissions will email you a confirmation of your application and next steps\.
7.  After completing your application, email any additional and required documents to [non\.degree@ubc\.ca](mailto:non.degree@ubc.ca)\.

## Letter of Permission[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/non\-degree\-studies\-visiting/\#letter\-of\-permission](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-visiting/#letter-of-permission)

Visiting students are required to provide a Letter of Permission \(LOP\) issued by their home institution\. This letter does not need to be submitted at the time of the application\.

Your Letter of Permission is only valid for one session\. You will need to submit a new letter for additional sessions you might register in\.

### Requirements for the letter

-   The letter must be typed on official university letterhead or written on an appropriate university form\.
-   You must include a list of all the courses you are planning to take\.
-   You must note the academic session you are applying to \(e\.g\., 2026/27 Winter or 2027 Summer\)\.
-   You must indicate your current bachelor’s program and academic standing\.
-   The letter must be in PDF format\.

Please have the issuing office of your home institution email the Letter of Permission to [non\.degree@ubc\.ca](mailto:non.degree@ubc.ca)\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/non\-degree\-studies\-visiting/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-visiting/#if-you-have-questions)

Contact Enrolment Services by phone at [604 822 9836](tel:6048229836) or email [non\.degree@ubc\.ca](mailto:non.degree@ubc.ca)\.

title: Registration for Non-Degree students
content_markdown:
## About Non\-Degree Studies[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/registration\-non\-degree/\#about\-non\-degree\-studies](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/registration-non-degree/#about-non-degree-studies)

Non\-Degree Studies provide study options for individuals wishing to take UBC credit\-based courses without pursuing a UBC degree, diploma, or certificate\.

Non\-Degree Studies are an option for you if you meet one of the following:

-   You want to take courses for general interest\.
-   You want to take a course for professional development, upgrading or academic advancement\.
-   You are completing an undergraduate degree at another institution\.
-   You have already completed a degree\.

If you would like to take courses at the UBC Okanagan campus, please contact [UBC Okanagan Non\-Degree Studies](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/non-degree-studies/)\.

## How to register for courses[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/registration\-non\-degree/\#how\-to\-register\-for\-courses](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/registration-non-degree/#how-to-register-for-courses)

Once your application for Non\-Degree Studies has been approved, you’ll be able to register for courses\.

1.  Log into [Workday](https://myworkday.ubc.ca/) with your Campus\-wide Login \(CWL\)\.
    -   If you don’t have a Student CWL, you can create one after accepting your offer and receiving a student number\. You can [set up a Student CWL](https://it.ubc.ca/services/accounts-passwords/campus-wide-login-cwl/how-create-account) through UBC IT\.
    -   If you do not have Multi\-factor Authentication set up, [follow instructions](https://it.ubc.ca/services/accounts-passwords/multi-factor-authentication-mfa#getting-started) online, then log into Workday\.
2.  Learn how to [view the course schedule](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/viewing-the-course-schedule/) and find course sections\.
3.  [Register for individual courses](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/registering-for-individual-course-sections/) when your course opens\.
4.  Pay your [tuition and student fees](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/paying-tuition/) in Workday by the [deadline](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/dates-deadlines/)\. Non\-Degree Studies students are held to the same policies surrounding registration and tuition as degree\-seeking students at UBC\.

It is your responsibility to periodically check your student account for any changes and to ensure that your registration and finances are up\-to\-date\. Once you register in your courses, you must pay both the regular [tuition fees](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/fees/tuition-fees/undergraduate#17997) and all related [student fees](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/fees/student-fees)\.

## If you’re having trouble registering[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/registration\-non\-degree/\#if\-youre\-having\-trouble\-registering](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/registration-non-degree/#if-youre-having-trouble-registering)

### Prerequisites and Transfer Credit

Non\-Degree students do not receive transfer credit from other institutions\. Your student information system will not automatically show transfer credits even though you may have provided transcripts for the purpose of an admission decision\.

If a course that you are trying to register in requires a prerequisite and you are unable to register yourself, you will need to complete and submit a [Registration Form](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/registration_adddrop_form_2024_fall.pdf) \(pdf\) to Enrolment Services\.

If you are able to obtain permission from the instructor or the department via email, you may forward this communication to [non\.degree@ubc\.ca](mailto:non.degree@ubc.ca)\.

### If your desired course is full

-   Some courses have waitlists in the student information system that you can register for\. There is no guarantee of getting into the course, so continue to check registration regularly\. Follow [online instructions](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/adding-a-course-waitlist-to-your-saved-schedule/) for getting on a waitlist in Workday\.
-   Some instructors have informal waitlists and may sign Registration Forms during the registration period for students on their waitlists or for those who request it\. This is at the instructor’s discretion and may not be granted\.
-   Keep checking Workday for course openings since students add or drop courses throughout the registration period\.

## Helpful information[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/registration\-non\-degree/\#helpful\-information](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/registration-non-degree/#helpful-information)

-   Generally, students are admitted to an entire [academic session](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/dates-and-deadlines) \(Winter or Summer\) and may choose to register either in one term or both terms\.
-   UBC registration occurs on a sessional basis\. If you’re admitted for the Winter session, you will register for courses in both Term 1 and Term 2 at the same time\.
-   If you’re an international student and not a Canadian citizen or permanent resident, you may need to follow additional steps after you are admitted to UBC\. You can review the information on [study permits and visas](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/)\.
-   Read the [online guide](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/register-courses/) for how to register for courses, create worklists, or add, drop, and switch classes\.
-   Prepare for course registration with [Workday tutorials](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/)\.
-   Non\-Degree students are not eligible for [Credit/D/F grading](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/creditdfail-grading/)\. However, you can consider [auditing courses](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/auditing-courses/)\.

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/registration\-non\-degree/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/registration-non-degree/#additional-resources)

-   [Non\-Degree Studies](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/)
-   [Non\-Degree Studies tuition and fees](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-tuition-fees/)
-   [Academic concessions for Non\-Degree Studies](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/academic-concessions-non-degree-studies/)
-   [Register for graduate\-level courses as a Non\-Degree student](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/forms/enrolment-non-degree-students-graduate-course)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/non\-degree\-studies/registration\-non\-degree/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/registration-non-degree/#if-you-have-questions)

Contact Enrolment Services by phone at [604 822 9836](tel:6048229836) or email [non\.degree@ubc\.ca](mailto:non.degree@ubc.ca)\.

title: Exam clashes, hardships, and cancellations
content_markdown:
While the information on this page provides helpful guidelines, refer to the [official rules and policies](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/academic-assessment) on exams for the most up\-to\-date information, including the following topics:

-   Student conduct during exams
-   Exam hardships and clashes
-   Deferred and Supplemental exams

## Exam clashes[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/exams/exam\-clashes\-hardships\-cancellations/\#exam\-clashes](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/exams/exam-clashes-hardships-cancellations/#exam-clashes)

An exam clash happens when more than one is scheduled on the same day at the same time\.

If you have an exam clash, contact your instructor immediately to see if you can find an alternate writing time\. If the instructor is unable to resolve the examination clash, then the department head, dean or director will be contacted\.

If an alternate writing time is not available at the faculty level, students must contact their [Academic Advisors](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) to make alternate arrangements\.

## Exam hardships[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/exams/exam\-clashes\-hardships\-cancellations/\#exam\-hardships](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/exams/exam-clashes-hardships-cancellations/#exam-hardships)

An exam hardship is defined as having **3 or more** end\-of\-term exams in less than 24 hours \(e\.g\., from 8:00 a\.m\. to 7:59 a\.m\. the following day\)\.

Read more about [exam hardships](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/academic-assessment/examination-hardships-and-clashes) in the UBC Academic Calendar\.

## Exam cancellations[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/exams/exam\-clashes\-hardships\-cancellations/\#exam\-cancellations](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/exams/exam-clashes-hardships-cancellations/#exam-cancellations)

Always check [ubc\.ca](http://ubc.ca/) for the most up\-to\-date information about campus closures and weather advisories\.

If exams are cancelled:

-   A notice will be posted on [ubc\.ca](http://ubc.ca/)\.
-   Enrolment Services will email affected students, instructors, and exam representatives to let them know that the exam is cancelled and what to expect next\.

### Rescheduling cancelled exams

If a Winter Term 1 final exam is cancelled, it will be rescheduled for the Saturday after the first full week of classes in Term 2, or on Sunday when necessary\.

If a Winter Term 2 and/or Summer Term exam is cancelled, it will be scheduled for the day\(s\) following the last date of formal exams for that term\.

If you are unable to attend a rescheduled exam, follow your faculty procedures to review your options\. Contact your [faculty advising office](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) for details\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/exams/exam\-clashes\-hardships\-cancellations/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/exams/exam-clashes-hardships-cancellations/#if-you-have-questions)

Contact your [Academic Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) for more information\.

For help with finances, registration, records, and more, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

title: Off-campus exams
content_markdown:
Students writing Standing Deferred \(SD\) or Supplemental \(S\) exams outside of the Vancouver campus must apply to write their exams\. A separate application is required for each exam\.

You are eligible to apply for an off\-campus exam if: 

-   You have Standing Deferred \(SD\) or Supplemental \(S\) standing in a course from the previous winter session\.
-   You’re located outside Metro Vancouver during the exam period\. Metro Vancouver extends as far north as Squamish, and as far east as Chilliwack\. 

## Application dates for SD and supplemental exams[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/exams/off\-campus\-exams/\#application\-dates\-for\-sd\-and\-supplemental\-exams](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/exams/off-campus-exams/#application-dates-for-sd-and-supplemental-exams)

View [Standing Deferred and Supplemental Exams](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/exams/standing-deferred-supplemental-exams/#application-and-exam-periods) for upcoming application dates\. The summer exam application period only applies to exams from the winter session immediately preceding it\. For example, only exams from the 25W session can be written in the 2026 summer exam period\. 

You **cannot** write Standing Deferred or Supplemental exams from Summer Session courses off\-campus\.

## If you miss the application deadline[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/exams/off\-campus\-exams/\#if\-you\-miss\-the\-application\-deadline](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/exams/off-campus-exams/#if-you-miss-the-application-deadline)

You cannot submit an application for an off\-campus exam through the Exam Application Tool after the application period ends\. Applications submitted outside the application period are reviewed on a case\-by\-case basis\. Contact [student\.exams@ubc\.ca](mailto:student.exams@ubc.ca) if you need to submit a late application\.

## Application fees[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/exams/off\-campus\-exams/\#application\-fees](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/exams/off-campus-exams/#application-fees)

### Deferred examination

| Location | Fee per paper in Canadian dollars |
| --- | --- |
| Canada or USA | $116\.80 |
| International | $163\.70 |

### Supplemental examination

| Location | Fee per paper in Canadian dollars |
| --- | --- |
| Canada or USA | $116\.80 |
| International | $163\.70 |

## Before you apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/exams/off\-campus\-exams/\#before\-you\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/exams/off-campus-exams/#before-you-apply)

To write an off\-campus exam at a UBC partner exam centre, check if there is one in your area from the list below\.

    Region

- **Row 2**

    British Columbia

    -   Chetwynd
