title: Special circumstances for students receiving awards
content_markdown:
Most undergraduate students who earn scholarships and other merit\-based awards are required to meet the minimum credit\-load and academic performance criteria, according to the [Regulations Governing University Awards](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/university-awards)\. There are, however, there are some special circumstances in which exceptions apply\.

## Exceptions to minimum credit rules[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/special\-circumstances\-receiving\-awards/\#exceptions\-to\-minimum\-credit\-rules](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/special-circumstances-receiving-awards/#exceptions-to-minimum-credit-rules)

To earn a scholarship or other academic award, undergraduate students must be registered in 24 percentage\-graded credits in a Winter session\. Students may be able to earn and maintain an award with a reduced credit load in the following cases:

**

Varsity athletes

**

If you are a UBC varsity athlete, you may receive and earn scholarships and academic awards on as few as 18 percentage\-graded credits in the Winter session\. You will need to provide a letter from Athletics confirming your commitment to the varsity team and the need to study at a reduced course load\.

**

Students with a disability

**

-   **If you are registered with the Centre of Accessibility**   
    You will need a letter or email from an Accessibility Advisor confirming your registration and the need to study at a reduced course load\. The letter must indicate the number of credits you can take each term, which would be equivalent to a full\-time course load\.
-   **If you are not registered with the Centre of Accessibility**  
    You will need a letter from a medical professional confirming your medical condition and the need to study at a reduced course load\.

**

Final year of study

**

If you are registered in fewer than 24 percentage\-graded credits in your last year of study, you may retain renewable scholarships and be eligible for academic\-merit based awards normally requiring percentage\-graded 24 credits\. You will need to provide a letter from your faculty advising office confirming exactly how many credits are required for you to meet the May graduation requirements at the end of the Winter session\.

**

Special circumstances

**

If there are other extenuating circumstances impacting your ability to meet the minimum requirements under Senate Regulations, you will be required to submit supporting documentation to Enrolment Services\.

Depending on the situation, the documentation can be from a physician, counsellor, academic advisor, or other appropriate professional\.

If you’ve already provided documentation to another UBC unit or faculty, you may not need to submit documentation again to Enrolment Services\. Enrolment Services staff can make a decision based on communication received from another UBC unit or faculty\.

## Students on exchange terms[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/special\-circumstances\-receiving\-awards/\#students\-on\-exchange\-terms](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/special-circumstances-receiving-awards/#students-on-exchange-terms)

A number of [scholarships and awards](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/new-programs-ubc-students/new-student-resources/awards-students-participating-go-global) are available specifically to students going on exchange\. 

**

Maintain your award while on exchange

**

Students registered in exchange for only one academic term must complete a minimum of 12 percentage\-graded credits during the UBC academic term to maintain their award and renewable award eligibility\.

**

Eligibility for renewable scholarships after exchange

**

Recipients of renewable scholarship may continue to receive funding while registered in an exchange program\. Students on exchange are expected to be enrolled in a full\-time course load at the exchange institution\. Since UBC scholarships are based on results from your previous Winter Session at UBC, you won’t receive automatic eligibility because UBC will not have grades or credit information from your time away on exchange\. You’ll be required to submit an exchange transcript to [Enrolment Services](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) and meet the [UBC award credit and academic requirements](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/university-awards)\.

**

Eligibility for non\-renewable scholarships after exchange

**

Students participating in an approved exchange program may be eligible to receive scholarships and other academic awards if they meet [UBC Senate Regulations](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/university-awards) and the following special conditions:

-   For scholarships in the following Winter session, students on exchange must be registered in a minimum of 24 percentage\-graded credits overall at UBC and their exchange institution during the current Winter session\.
-   For [faculty recommended awards](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/faculty-recommended-awards/), students normally need to submit an exchange transcript to their faculty or department\. You can connect with [Academic Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) for more information\.
-   For [awards managed by Enrolment Services](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/), students must submit a copy of their exchange transcript by the award program deadline\. For competitive scholarships, grades from exchange terms will be compared and converted to UBC grades so that a GPA can be calculated for award eligibility, where required\.

## Students on co\-op terms[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/special\-circumstances\-receiving\-awards/\#students\-on\-co\-op\-terms](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/special-circumstances-receiving-awards/#students-on-co-op-terms)

Students in a Co\-op program may be eligible for scholarships in the following academic term, as long as they meet the [UBC Senate Regulations](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/university-awards) and the special conditions below\.

### Non\-renewable scholarships

**Co\-op term during a Winter Session** 

If you have one Co\-op work term and are enrolled in classes for one academic term in the same Winter Session, your eligibility for scholarships will be affected in the following ways:

#### For scholarships during a Co\-op year

-   You must be registered in at least 12 percentage\-graded credits during the academic term to receive the scholarship\.
-   The full amount will be paid during the academic term, even if it would normally be split over both terms\.

#### Scholarship eligibility for the following year

-   Co\-op courses will not count toward academic averages when calculating awards eligibility for the following year\.
-   Since you will have taken fewer credits during the year with one Co\-op term, the average for scholarships will be calculated on the best 12 percentage\-graded credits\.
-   Because you will have only completed half a full course load during the Co\-op year, you will only be eligible for scholarships at half its value the following year\. This eligibility should balance out over the course of the degree, as it will take a year longer to complete and you will have an additional year of scholarship eligibility as a result\.

Consider the following example scenario\. A student receiving a $2,000 scholarship this school year was on Co\-op for Term 1\. They received the entire $2,000 in Term 2, since they were registered in at least 12 credits\.

The same student is now being considered for a $3,000 scholarship for the following year\. Their academic average is based on their best 12 credits, not counting the Co\-op course\. If the student is eligible, they will receive $1,500 of the scholarship, because they completed only half an academic course load this year\.

**

Two Co\-op terms during a Winter Session

**

You will have your award deferred to your next academic term during the Winter Session after your Co\-op year\.

Co\-op courses will not count toward academic averages when calculating awards eligibility for the following year\.

Consider the following example scenario\. A student is registered in 24 percentage\-graded credits during the 2025 Winter Session\. Based on the grades in this session, they earn a Trek award for the 2026 Winter Session\. They decide to complete two co\-op terms in the 2026 Winter session, from September to December 2026 and January to April 2027\. Their award will be deferred to the 2027 Winter Session, where they will once again be enrolled in academic studies\.

### Renewable scholarships

If you are a Co\-op student with a renewable entrance scholarship, you will receive the same total monetary value, but the funding will be spread equally over the Winter Session academic terms only, unless otherwise specified in your award offer letter\. You will still need to meet the renewal criteria specific to your scholarship\.

## Sign up for Direct Deposit[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/special\-circumstances\-receiving\-awards/\#sign\-up\-for\-direct\-deposit](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/special-circumstances-receiving-awards/#sign-up-for-direct-deposit)

University awards are normally applied to your tuition first\. If your award is greater than your tuition, the credit will remain on your account for future tuition, unless you have added direct deposit information in Workday\. Learn how to [sign up for direct deposit](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/setting-up-your-direct-deposit/) to receive your credit refund in your bank account\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/special\-circumstances\-receiving\-awards/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/special-circumstances-receiving-awards/#if-you-have-questions)

For help with finances, registration, records, and more, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

title: Trek Excellence Scholarship
content_markdown:
## About the scholarship[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/trek\-excellence\-scholarship/\#about\-the\-scholarship](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/trek-excellence-scholarship/#about-the-scholarship)

The Trek Excellence Scholarship offers $1,500 awards to domestic students in the top 5% in their undergraduate year, faculty, and school\.

Rankings are based on a student’s top 24 percentage\-graded credits, as per [Senate award regulations](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/university-awards)\. Eligible students will automatically be considered for the scholarship and do not need to submit an application\. 

## Eligibility requirements[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/trek\-excellence\-scholarship/\#eligibility\-requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/trek-excellence-scholarship/#eligibility-requirements)

To be eligible for the scholarship, you must meet all the requirements below:

-   You must be a Canadian citizen or a permanent resident of Canada\.
-   You must be registered in at least 24 percentage\-graded credits in your previous winter session\. If you’re registered in more than 24 percentage\-graded credits, your average will be based on your top 24 credits\.
-   You must be continuing in the same faculty or school in your current winter session\.

The following courses will not be counted towards your average:

-   Audited courses
-   Wait\-listed courses
-   Summer courses
-   Credit/D/Fail courses

### Retaining the scholarship

To keep your scholarship, you must meet all the requirements below:

-   You must be registered in 24 credits in your current winter session\.
-   You must be continuing in the same faculty and school\.

### Exceptions

#### Students on Co\-op or Exchange

Most undergraduate students who earn scholarships and other merit\-based awards are required to meet minimum credit load and academic performance criteria, according to the [regulations governing university awards](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/university-awards)\. However, if you are on a Co\-op or Exchange term or in your final year of study, please refer to the [special circumstances](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/special-circumstances-receiving-awards/) for students receiving awards, or contact your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) directly for more information\.

#### Post\-baccalaureate programs

If you’re in a post\-baccalaureate program such as Medicine, Dentistry, Law, or Education, you will not be eligible\. You may qualify for substantial faculty\-recommended scholarships\. Contact your faculty’s scholarship representative or check your faculty website to find out more\.

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/trek\-excellence\-scholarship/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/trek-excellence-scholarship/#how-to-apply)

You do not need to submit an application for this scholarship\.

Students are automatically considered based on their grades from the prior Winter session\. Recipients will be notified from late\-August to late\-October\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/trek\-excellence\-scholarship/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/trek-excellence-scholarship/#if-you-have-questions)

For help with finances, registration, records, and more, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

title: UBC Bursary Program
content_markdown:
## About the bursary[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/ubc\-bursary\-program/\#about\-the\-bursary](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/#about-the-bursary)

The UBC Bursary program is designed to help fill the gap between your assessed educational and living costs, and your available government assistance and expected financial contributions\.

The bursary program follows the framework set out by [StudentAid BC](https://studentaidbc.ca/) to give eligible domestic students access to financial resources to help meet their needs\.

Being eligible for a bursary does not guarantee that you will receive the full amount of funding to cover all costs\.

### How funding amounts are determined

Several factors are considered to determine the amount of bursary funding you may be eligible to receive\.

For most programs, the following is used to determine your funding amount:

-   **Loan assessment:** Your individual financial need as determined by your provincial student loan assessment\.
-   **Family demographics:** Total family size and the previous year’s total income\.
-   **Applicant volume:** The total number of bursary applicants within your specific program\.
-   **Comparative need:** The unmet financial need of other eligible students\.
-   **Program\-specific allocation:** UBC Bursary eligibility and the total funds reserved for your program\.

## Eligibility requirements[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/ubc\-bursary\-program/\#eligibility\-requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/#eligibility-requirements)

To be eligible for the UBC Bursary program, you must meet all of the following requirements:

-   You are a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or have refugee status\.
-   You are enrolled in an eligible program with a full\-time [course load](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/course-load-guide/)\.
-   You must be receiving full\-time Canadian government student loans for a study period that is a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks in length and matches the period for which you’re applying for bursary support\.
-   You must have received confirmation of enrolment for your Canadian government student loan by the bursary application deadline\.
-   You must have an unmet financial need as determined by UBC’s evaluation process\.

You are not eligible for the bursary if you are currently registered in UBC Co\-op or Certificate, Diploma, Unclassified, Qualifying, Visiting, or Access Studies\.

UBC Bursary applications are subject to verification\. Read [UBC Bursary Verifications](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/#bursary-verifications) below for more details\.

## UBC Access Promise for eligible BC students[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/ubc\-bursary\-program/\#ubc\-access\-promise\-for\-eligible\-bc\-students](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/#ubc-access-promise-for-eligible-bc-students)

The UBC Access Promise program automatically assesses bursary funding for eligible British Columbia students meeting the program criteria below\.

Students who were eligible as Access Promise in one session may not automatically qualify as Access Promise students in subsequent or future session\(s\)\.

### Access Promise student eligibility requirements

-   You must meet the UBC Bursary Program eligibility requirements\.
-   You must be registered in any undergraduate degree program at UBC Vancouver campus, except for JD, MD, PHRMD, and DMD\.
-   You must have received the maximum [Canada Student Grant for Full\-Time Students](https://studentaidbc.ca/explore/grants-scholarships/canada-student-grant-full-time-students)\.
-   You must have received a full\-time student loan through [StudentAid BC](https://studentaidbc.ca/)\.
-   You must be classified by StudentAid BC as a [Dependent student](https://studentaidbc.ca/apply/eligibility) who is considered to be dependent on a financial sponsor, such as parent\(s\), or self\-identify as an Indigenous person\.

## Application period[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/ubc\-bursary\-program/\#application\-period](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/#application-period)

There are 2 main bursary application periods: winter and summer\. An additional winter Term 2\-only bursary application is available to students with a Term 2\-only student loan\. To be eligible, you must apply for the bursary and enrolment must be confirmed with your province for your Canadian government student loan by the application deadline\.

| Important dates | Application information |
| --- | --- |
| Fri, Aug 14, 2026 | 2026/27 Winter applications open |
| Tues, Sep 15, 2026 | 2026/27 Winter applications close |
| Tues, Dec 15, 2026 | 2026/27 Winter Term 2\-only applications open |
| Fri, Jan 15, 2027 | 2026/27 Winter Term 2\-only applications close |

### Important information about student loans

Students are encouraged to apply for student loans and grants as early as possible\.

Your enrolment must be confirmed with your provincial loan provider before the bursary application deadlines above to be eligible for UBC bursaries\.

To meet this bursary deadline, you are strongly encouraged to apply for your provincial student loan by the following dates, depending on the application period during which you are applying:

-   For **winter bursary** applications, apply by July 31\.
-   For **winter Term 2\-only bursary** applications, apply by November 15\.
-   For **summer bursary** applications, apply by April 15\.

## How to apply for the bursary[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/ubc\-bursary\-program/\#how\-to\-apply\-for\-the\-bursary](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/#how-to-apply-for-the-bursary)

Follow [step\-by\-step instructions](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/applying-to-the-ubc-bursary-program/) to apply to the UBC Bursary program on the [LFSM portal](https://lfsm.ubc.ca/)\.

Information in the application is collected under the authority of section 26\(c\) of the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act\.

## If there are changes to your financial situation[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/ubc\-bursary\-program/\#if\-there\-are\-changes\-to\-your\-financial\-situation](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/#if-there-are-changes-to-your-financial-situation)

If you are facing an unexpected [financial emergency](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-emergencies/) or have had a significant change to your financial situation, contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\. They can help you navigate these changes and connect you to relevant support\.

If you have been awarded a bursary and have since received additional resources not reported on your bursary application, you must report this to your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

## How bursary funds are issued[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/ubc\-bursary\-program/\#how\-bursary\-funds\-are\-issued](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/#how-bursary-funds-are-issued)

Bursaries issued by UBC are applied first toward tuition and student fees\. When the amount of the bursary is greater than the outstanding fees in any term:

-   If you have provided banking information on Workday, the surplus funds are paid to your bank account through [direct deposit](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/setting-up-your-direct-deposit/), normally within 3 to 5 business days of the payment being issued\.
-   If banking information has not been provided, any remaining funds will stay on your tuition account as a credit toward future tuition\.

Students are required to [sign up for direct deposit](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/setting-up-your-direct-deposit/) to ensure timely access to bursary funds\.

## UBC Bursary Verifications

All UBC bursary support is subject to financial reviews and verifications\.

Keep all relevant receipts and documents for 18 months after you apply\. Information provided on your bursary application can be verified before and after the bursary decision, and up to 18 months after you receive your funding\.

**

If your application is selected for verification

**

If your application is selected for verification, you may be asked to provide additional supporting documents, including:

-   Housing documentation, such as rental agreement and proof of payment \(cash receipts are not accepted as proof of payment\)
-   Bank statements for the student, parent, and/or dependents
-   Notice of Assessment issued by the Canada Revenue Agency for the most recently available tax year \(including line 150\)
-   Proof of address for student and family members living in the same household

Failure to provide the requested documents in a timely manner may result in the delay or cancellation of your UBC bursary funding, and/or a reassessment of your application\.

**

If you’re claiming child care expenses in your bursary application

**

Before applying for bursary support:

-   You must apply for government funding\.
-   You may be asked to submit a confirmation letter from the BC Child Care Service Centre indicating Affordable Child Care Benefits \(ACCB\) eligibility or ineligibility\.
-   You may be eligible for the [Child Care Fee Reduction Initiative](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/family-social-supports/caring-for-young-children/running-daycare-preschool/child-care-operating-funding/child-care-fee-reduction-initiative-provider-opt-in-status) without an application\.
-   You need to submit an application for the Affordable Child Care Benefit every year\. The BC Child Care Service Centre estimates that it takes 10 business days to process an electronic application\. Please ensure that you apply early to allow time for your application to be processed before the start of the academic year\.

**Supporting documentation**

You may be asked to submit proof of expenses, including:

-   A letter from child care service providers
-   Proof of payment to child care service providers \(cash receipts are not accepted as proof of payment\)
-   Confirmation of child care benefits from BC Child Care Service Centre

## Other financial support programs[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/ubc\-bursary\-program/\#other\-financial\-support\-programs](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/#other-financial-support-programs)

If you apply for the UBC Bursary, you may be eligible to apply for other UBC and government bursary programs\.

### UBC Bursary programs

-   [Affiliation Bursaries](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/affiliation-bursaries/)
-   [Awards for Indigenous students](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-indigenous/)
-   [Awards for students with disabilities](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-disabilities/)

### Government bursary programs

-   **Students from BC**: Access [StudentAid BC](https://studentaidbc.ca/explore/grants-scholarships) for details\.
-   **Students from outside BC**: Visit your home province’s government funding website\.

## FAQs[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/ubc\-bursary\-program/\#faqs](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/#faqs)

**

I haven’t applied for my student loan yet\. Can I submit a bursary application?

**

Yes\. You can apply for the UBC Bursary Program before your loan application is complete\. However, UBC will need to confirm your enrolment by the bursary application deadline\.

**

I have loans from a province other than BC\. How do I ensure my bursary eligibility?

**

If you are receiving a student loan through Quebec, Northwest Territories, or Nunavut Student Financial Assistance you will be required to upload your Notice of Assessment before your bursary application can be assessed\. UBC will let you know when and how to submit any required documents\.

Students receiving student loans from other provinces will need to make sure their loan has been confirmed by the bursary deadline, but are not required to upload their Notice of Assessment\.

**

Are there any programs at UBC that aren’t eligible for bursary support?

**

The following student categories are not eligible for bursary funding:

-   All Non\-Degree Studies students registered in Certificate, Diploma, Unclassified Qualifying, Visiting, or Access Studies
-   Students enrolled in a UBC Co\-op term

**

Am I eligible for bursary support during my Co\-op term?

**

Students enrolled in an approved UBC Co\-op term are not eligible for bursary funding during their Co\-op term\(s\)\.

Students who have received bursary funds before Co\-op registration has been added for the current study period will have their bursary reassessed accordingly and funds will be recovered\.

**

Am I eligible for bursary support if my loan starts in January?

**

Yes, UBC offers a bursary for Winter Term 2 only for students with full\-time Canadian government student loans starting in January\. The application is open from December 15 to January 15 in [Workday](https://myworkday.ubc.ca/)\. Students are encouraged to apply for their Term 2 loans by November 15\. Confirmation of enrolment for your Canadian government student loan must be completed by January 15 to be considered for bursary eligibility\. If January 15 falls on a weekend, the deadline will be the next working day\. Students who have full\-year loans starting in September are not eligible to apply for the Term 2\-only bursary\.

**

Is there any bursary support for high\-cost professional degree programs?

**

Graduate programs [designated as professional programs](https://academic.ubc.ca/bursary-support-designated-graduate-programs) are eligible for faculty\-funded or donor\-funded bursaries specifically identified to their particular program\. Faculty\-funded bursaries are subject to faculty budget approval, and therefore, are not guaranteed\.

All graduate students who wish to be considered for bursary support must submit a bursary application through [Workday](https://myworkday.ubc.ca/) by the deadline\.

**

What happens if I forget to accept my bursary offer?

**

Students are required to accept their bursary offer as soon as possible and no later than the last day of the study period for which they’re receiving funding\. Students who do not accept their bursary within their loan study period will have their bursary cancelled\.

**

What happens if I finish my program early?

**

Students who complete their studies earlier than the end date of the study period for which they are receiving funding will have their bursary recalculated to match the new, shorter study period dates and may be required to repay some of the bursary funds they have received\.

**

Is my bursary confidential?

**

For the purpose of maintaining donor relations and informing the donor about the impact of their generosity, UBC may disclose the following information to award donors:

-   Your name
-   Contact information including your mailing address, telephone number, and email address
-   Your year and program of study
-   Other information relevant to the requirements of the award

Information about your award may also be shared with University faculty and staff on a “need to know” basis but it will otherwise be kept confidential to the extent authorized by law\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/ubc\-bursary\-program/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/#if-you-have-questions)

For help with finances, registration, records, and more, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

If you’re a UBC Okanagan student, please contact [Enrolment Services Advising](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/advising/)\.

If you are experiencing issues with the application platform, please check [UBC Status](https://status.it.ubc.ca/) for any scheduled maintenance or unexpected outages\.

title: Student Housing Supplement Grant
content_markdown:
## About the grant[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/student\-housing\-supplement\-grant/\#about\-the\-grant](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/student-housing-supplement-grant/#about-the-grant)

The UBC Vancouver Student Housing Supplement Grant is a one\-time grant of up to $1,700 that supports living costs for undergraduate students starting their first winter session at UBC\. To be eligible, you must be living in UBC\-managed housing designated for first\-year undergraduate students\. The program is meant to support students who wish to attend UBC and participate in the residence experience\. Eligible students will automatically be considered for the grant, and do not need to submit an application\.  

## Eligibility requirements[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/student\-housing\-supplement\-grant/\#eligibility\-requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/student-housing-supplement-grant/#eligibility-requirements)

Applicants must meet all of the following requirements: 

-   You are a Canadian citizen or permanent resident\.
-   You are starting your studies at UBC by September 2026\.
-   You will be living in UBC\-managed housing designated for first\-year undergraduate students, with a mandatory meal plan for the duration of Winter Session\. If your stay in UBC Housing is less than the duration of the Winter Session, you may be ineligible for the grant or eligible for only a certain amount\. This may affect your student account and you will have to pay the remaining housing costs\.
-   You have received full\-year, full\-time [Canadian government student loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/), as confirmed by September 15, 2026\.
-   You must maintain your eligibility for loans during the 2026/27 Winter session or throughout your stay in UBC Housing\.
-   You have received the maximum [Canada Student Grant](https://studentaidbc.ca/explore/grants-scholarships/canada-student-grant-full-time-students) for full\-time students\.
-   You have not been awarded the Student Housing Assistance Grant\.
-   You will be enrolled full\-time in a degree or eligible program\. You are not eligible if you are enrolled in Certificate Programs, Diploma Programs, and/or Non\-Degree Studies, including Unclassified, Visiting, Qualifying, and Access Studies\.

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/student\-housing\-supplement\-grant/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/student-housing-supplement-grant/#how-to-apply)

No application is required\. All eligible students will be automatically considered for the grant\. 

Successful recipients will be notified by email by the end of February\. Funds will be sent by [direct deposit](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/setting-up-your-direct-deposit/)\.

### Financial review and audit

All eligible students may be subject to financial review and audits\. If you are selected for a financial review or audit, you may be asked to provide additional supporting documents, such as the following:

-   Student loan notice of assessment
-   Bank statements for you, your parents, and/or your dependents
-   Tax returns, child care receipts, and other similar documents demonstrating financial need

If you’re unable to provide the requested documents in a timely manner, you may no longer be eligible for the grant\.

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/student\-housing\-supplement\-grant/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/student-housing-supplement-grant/#additional-resources)

-   [Student housing for prospective students](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/getting-started/prospective/)
-   [Vancouver student housing](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/)
-   [First\-year housing guarantee](http://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/how-we-assign-rooms/first-year-guarantee/)
-   [Benefits of living in residence](http://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/reasons-to-live-in-residence/)
-   [Housing FAQs](http://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/faq/)
-   [Funding your studies](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/student\-housing\-supplement\-grant/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/student-housing-supplement-grant/#if-you-have-questions)

For help with finances, registration, records, and more, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

title: UBC Vancouver Technology Bursary
content_markdown:
## About the bursary[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/ubc\-vancouver\-technology\-bursary/\#about\-the\-bursary](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-vancouver-technology-bursary/#about-the-bursary)

The UBC Vancouver Technology Bursary is a one\-time needs\-based bursary\. It is intended for students who find themselves in financial distress and cannot meet their basic technology requirements, such as headphones, web cameras, specialized accessibility technology, or Internet access\.

## Eligibility requirements[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/ubc\-vancouver\-technology\-bursary/\#eligibility\-requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-vancouver-technology-bursary/#eligibility-requirements)

-   You must be enrolled and registered in an undergraduate, graduate, or post\-baccalaureate degree program at the UBC Vancouver campus\.
-   You must demonstrate why other publicly available technology resources on the UBC Vancouver campus \(e\.g\., library, computer lab\) are insufficient\.
-   You must demonstrate you have financial need due to unforeseen circumstances, and that you do not have access to any alternative funding to cover the costs requested through this bursary\.
-   You must outline how the technology is needed for you to engage in and complete UBC coursework\.
-   You must confirm how you otherwise planned to cover the cost of the item\(s\) being requested through this bursary\.

## What’s not included in the funding[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/ubc\-vancouver\-technology\-bursary/\#whats\-not\-included\-in\-the\-funding](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-vancouver-technology-bursary/#whats-not-included-in-the-funding)

This funding is not intended for the following:

-   Improvements to physical workspaces such as ergonomic keyboards, desks, or chairs
-   Upgrades to older technology
-   Supplemental technological needs for employment

Employers should provide necessary resources for staff to perform their work\. Students are also expected to provide the technology required for their program of study, such as a laptop or special software\. Learn more about [technology requirements](https://lthub.ubc.ca/student-support/tech-requirements/) that students should plan for\.

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/ubc\-vancouver\-technology\-bursary/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-vancouver-technology-bursary/#how-to-apply)

There are 2 ways to apply for the technology bursary\. Choose the option that works best for you\.

### Option 1: Contact an Enrolment Services Advisor

If you’re an undergraduate student, contact your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) to discuss your situation\.

If you’re a graduate or post\-baccalaureate degree student, you can call 604 822 9836, visit [Brock Hall](http://www.maps.ubc.ca/PROD/index_detail.php?locat1=112-1), or submit an [online form](https://www.askme.ubc.ca/form/s/)\.

If you’re an Indigenous student, please contact your assigned ES Advisor or reach out to the Indigenous Student Support team by emailing es\.indigenous@ubc\.ca\.

### Option 2: Submit an online application

You can also [complete an online application](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_2lwwp4hKZ09IPrL) for funding\.

Your application will be reviewed by an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) and you may be contacted by email or phone if more information is required\. If you are an undergraduate student, please note that your application will be reviewed by your assigned Enrolment Services Advisor\.

## Bursary verifications[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/ubc\-vancouver\-technology\-bursary/\#bursary\-verifications](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-vancouver-technology-bursary/#bursary-verifications)

All UBC bursary support is subject to financial review and verification\. Please keep all your relevant receipts and documents for 18 months after applying\. 

If you fail to provide the requested documents in a timely manner, your funding may be delayed, cancelled, or reassessed\.

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/ubc\-vancouver\-technology\-bursary/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-vancouver-technology-bursary/#additional-resources)

-   [Borrow UBC technology](https://services.library.ubc.ca/computers-technology/technology-borrowing/)
-   [BC Technology for Learning Society](https://www.reusetechbc.ca/)
-   [Computers for Schools Plus](https://www.ic.gc.ca/eic/site/cfs-ope.nsf/eng/home)
-   [Canadian and US Student Loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/awards\-scholarships\-bursaries/ubc\-vancouver\-technology\-bursary/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-vancouver-technology-bursary/#if-you-have-questions)

For help with finances, registration, records, and more, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

title: Financial Wellness Training and Education
content_markdown:
## Financial Wellness Workshops[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-wellness\-training\-education/\#financial\-wellness\-workshops](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-wellness-training-education/#financial-wellness-workshops)

UBC student groups, staff, and faculty members are invited to book workshops organized by [Enrolment Services Advisors](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) \(ES Advisors\)\.

ES Advisors offer workshops to student groups by request\. They focus on financial planning, understanding financial and other resources at UBC, and student loan support\. ES Advisors are unable to provide tax or financial investment advice\.

Fill out the [workshop request form](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_cH2hYUpno4pmguy) if you are interested in having an ES Advisor come to one of your meetings or events\.

## Learn at your own pace[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-wellness\-training\-education/\#learn\-at\-your\-own\-pace](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-wellness-training-education/#learn-at-your-own-pace)

If you’re a UBC student, you can take self\-guided courses to learn about financial wellness\. Log into Canvas using your CWL to enrol\.

[Understanding Your Financial Picture](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/GGWED8)

Develop practical skills for managing your finances and explore financial wellness topics like budgeting\.

[Food Budgeting and Meal Planning](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/RA3A6C)

Learn how to budget for groceries realistically, plan meals that fit your schedule, and make the most of your food budget throughout the term\.

[Understanding Your Financial Credit Score](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/MKD89J)

Understand how credit works in Canada, what affects your credit score, and how to make informed decisions about credit cards and borrowing\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-wellness\-training\-education/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-wellness-training-education/#if-you-have-questions)

Email [financial\.wellness@ubc\.ca](mailto:financial.wellness@ubc.ca) if you have questions about the workshops or Canvas courses\.

If you have specific questions about your student account or personal finances, please contact your assigned [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

title: Financial emergencies
content_markdown:
## How we can help[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/financial\-emergencies/\#how\-we\-can\-help](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-emergencies/#how-we-can-help)

If you are experiencing financial concerns, you can schedule a confidential advising appointment with an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) \(ES Advisor\)\. They will work with you to develop the best course of action and review resources available to you\.

Learn how to find your [ES Advisor’s contact](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/ubc-advisor-contacts/finding-your-enrolment-services-advisors-contact-information/) in Workday\.

ES Advisors can help you create or adapt your financial plan and find financial support options when unexpected situations arise, such as:

-   An unexpected change in living situation
-   Food insecurity
-   Delays in transferring funds out of a country
-   Illness or death in the family
-   An exceptional medical situation
-   Other unforeseen circumstances

## Emergency Funding[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/financial\-emergencies/\#emergency\-funding](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-emergencies/#emergency-funding)

Sometimes, even with the best planning, you may run into a situation that is out of your control and you may need help to deal with the problem\. One option might be short\-term, generally one\-time, emergency funding to help cover a temporary shortfall due to an unexpected emergency situation when no other financial options are available\.

[Learn more](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/emergency-funding/)

## What to expect[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/financial\-emergencies/\#what\-to\-expect](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-emergencies/#what-to-expect)

ES Advisors are not here to tell you how to spend your money\. They are here to support you with immediate, short, and long\-term financial wellbeing\. When meeting with an ES Advisor, you can expect to be heard without judgment\.

An ES Advisor will work with you to review your personal finances and make sure you are aware of all the financial resources available to you in your particular situation\. This can include exploring resources like [student loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/), [scholarships and bursaries](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/), and/or [Work Learn](https://students.ubc.ca/career/work-learn-program/) and student employment\.

## Other financial resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/financial\-emergencies/\#other\-financial\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-emergencies/#other-financial-resources)

[Funding your studies](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/)

Explore funding resources, such as loans, awards, and part\-time work\.

[Financial support options](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/)

Get financial support through scholarships, bursaries, and other assistance programs\.

[Financial planning](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/)

Develop a financial plan for your time at UBC\.

[AMS Food Bank](https://www.ams.ubc.ca/student-services/food-bank/)

Use the on\-campus food bank for groceries and toiletries, up to 16 times per term\.

[Food Hub Market](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/food-hub-market/)

Shop for affordable grocery essentials and build your food literacy\.

[Crisis support](https://students.ubc.ca/health/crisis-support-services/)

Reach out for immediate help if you or someone else is in danger, or at risk of harming yourself or others\.

[Student support and resources](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/)

Learn who to contact for assistance with academics, money, health, and more\.

[UBC Vancouver Technology Bursary](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-vancouver-technology-bursary/)

Apply for a one\-time, needs\-based bursary towards costs of equipment needed for online learning\.

## If you need help[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/financial\-emergencies/\#if\-you\-need\-help](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-emergencies/#if-you-need-help)

If you’re an undergraduate student, please contact your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) directly\.

Graduate, postgraduate, and all other students can contact an Enrolment Services Advisor by calling [604 822 9836](tel:6048229836) or submitting a question through the [online form](https://www.askme.ubc.ca/form/s/)\.

If you’re an Indigenous student, please contact your assigned ES Advisor or reach out to the ES Indigenous Student Support Team at [es\.indigenous@ubc\.ca](mailto:es.indigenous@ubc.ca)\.

title: Emergency funding
content_markdown:
Sometimes, even with the best planning, you may run into a situation that is out of your control and may need short\-term financial help\. UBC may be able to provide emergency financial support to help cover a temporary shortfall due to an unexpected situation when all other financial options have been exhausted\. All requests for financial support are confidential and separate from your academic record\.

Examples of costs that may be considered for financial support include:

-   Rent or temporary emergency housing 
-   Food and essential items 
-   Childcare 
-   Emergency medical costs not covered through AMS/GSS extended health coverage or Indigenous Health Authority coverage
-   Unexpected travel expenses

Items that UBC does not provide funding for include \(but are not limited to\) costs such as tuition, student fees, credit card payments, car payments, loan payments, and pet care\. Emergency funding is not intended to support family or friends\.

## Eligibility requirements[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/emergency\-funding/\#eligibility\-requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/emergency-funding/#eligibility-requirements)

Degree\-seeking students must be enrolled and registered in an undergraduate, graduate or post\-baccalaureate degree program at the UBC Vancouver campus\.

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/emergency\-funding/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/emergency-funding/#how-to-apply)

There are 2 ways to apply for emergency funding:

1.  Contact an Enrolment Services Advisor\.
2.  Submit an online application\.

### Contact an Enrolment Services Advisor 

If you’re an undergraduate student, contact your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) to discuss your situation\.

If you’re a graduate or post\-baccalaureate degree student, you can call [604 822 9836](tel:6048229836), visit [Brock Hall](http://www.maps.ubc.ca/PROD/index_detail.php?locat1=112-1), or submit an [online form](https://www.askme.ubc.ca/form/s/)\.

If you’re an Indigenous student, please contact your assigned ES Advisor or reach out to the Indigenous Student Support team by emailing [es\.indigenous@ubc\.ca](mailto:es.indigenous@ubc.ca)\.

### Submit an online application

Alternatively, you can fill out an online application for funding\. Your application will be reviewed by an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) and you may be contacted by email or phone if more information is required\. If you are an undergraduate student, please note that your application will be reviewed by your assigned Enrolment Services Advisor\.

[Apply online](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4U9KW535QR2W8Z0)

title: Financial planning
content_markdown:
Part of your success at UBC involves proactive financial planning\. Review the resources below and connect with an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) if you would like guidance on how to start\.

## Understand your costs[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/\#understand\-your\-costs](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/#understand-your-costs)

### Tuition and student fees

The first step is to understand how much a school year will cost you and what the related expenses are\. Knowing your costs will give you the foundation to build your financial plan\. Start by understanding the costs for tuition, student fees, and books:

-   [Undergraduate student tuition and fees](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/undergraduate-tuition-fees/)
-   [Graduate student tuition and fees](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/prospective-students/tuition-fees-cost-living/graduate-tuition-fees)

### Living costs

Next, consider how much it will cost to live in Vancouver\.

-   If you are living on campus, you’ll need to cover [residence fees and a meal plan](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/fees-payments/)\.
-   If you’re off\-campus, you’ll want to consider rent, groceries, and utilities\.

Be sure to account for your personal expenses, such as your phone bill, subscriptions, and social expenses\. If it’s in your financial plan, you won’t be caught off\-guard\. Use the [cost calculator](http://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/cost#cost-calculator) to help you calculate your first year finances\.

If you’re a graduate student, use the [graduate cost calculator](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/prospective-students/tuition-fees-cost-living/cost-living) to develop your financial plan\.

## Know your resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/\#know\-your\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/#know-your-resources)

After determining your educational costs, you’ll need to find resources to cover those costs\.

Domestic and US students may be eligible for [government student loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/)\.

International students must ensure they have sufficient financial resources for their studies at UBC\. Unless you have received a scholarship, plan to cover the full cost of your degree\. 

Learn more about [financial assistance programs](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/) for students studying at UBC\.

## Map your timeline[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/\#map\-your\-timeline](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/#map-your-timeline)

Enrolment Services is committed to helping you, but it is your responsibility to meet important deadlines\. Review key [dates and deadlines](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/dates-deadlines/)\.

You’re strongly recommended to apply for your [student loan](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/) by mid\-July\.

## Build a financial plan[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/\#build\-a\-financial\-plan](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/#build-a-financial-plan)

Every student should have a financial plan\. Once you’ve gathered the information above, you’ll be ready to make one and find what works best for you\.

These tools and tips can help you get started on your financial plan:

-   [How to budget](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/budget/)
-   [Spending Plan Template](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/financial_planning_spending_plan_template.xlsx) \(Excel\)
-   [Budget\-Planning Worksheet](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/ubc_budget_planning_worksheet.pdf) \(pdf\)
-   [Sticking to the Plan](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/sticking_to_the_plan.pdf) \(pdf\)
-   [Student Loans and Graduation](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/financial_planning_repayment_graduation.pdf) \(pdf\)

## Maintaining your financial plan[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/\#maintaining\-your\-financial\-plan](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/#maintaining-your-financial-plan)

Once you have a plan, it’s important to use it\. Sometimes this is easier said than done\. If it’s not working, making adjustments as needed is okay\. Stay on top of your loan obligations and be prepared for your [loan repayment](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/repaying-my-student-loans/)\.

If you’re facing an unexpected [financial emergency](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-emergencies/) or experiencing a significant change in your financial situation, contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) to discuss your options\.

## Financial Wellness workshops[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/\#financial\-wellness\-workshops](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/#financial-wellness-workshops)

During the summer months, Enrolment Services Advisors host free Financial Wellness workshops for students who are new to UBC\. Other workshops open to all students are available throughout the year\. Browse upcoming sessions and register through the [event schedule](https://events.ubc.ca/organizer/enrolment-services/?eventDisplay=past)\.

Additional workshops for student groups are available by request\. Visit [Financial Wellness Training and Education](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-wellness-training-education/) to learn more or [request your workshop](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_b46Ysa4gmInv7nM) online\.

## Financial resources Canvas courses[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/\#financial\-resources\-canvas\-courses](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/#financial-resources-canvas-courses)

Take [financial wellness Canvas courses](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-wellness-training-education/#learn-at-your-own-pace) to learn more about topics like budgeting and credit scores\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/#if-you-have-questions)

For help with finances, registration, records, and more, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

title: How to budget
content_markdown:
## What does budgeting mean?[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/budget/\#what\-does\-budgeting\-mean](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/budget/#what-does-budgeting-mean)

Think about the last $100 that you spent\. Where did it go? Did it stretch as far as you thought it would? Budgeting means reflecting on your spending habits, learning how to balance your finances, and managing your spending\.

Put simply, a budget is a list of your total income compared to your total expenses over a fixed period of time, such as a school term, a month, or a year\.

## Reasons to budget[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/budget/\#reasons\-to\-budget](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/budget/#reasons-to-budget)

The little things can make a difference\. For example, if you buy a regular latte each day from Monday to Friday, you’ll spend more than $1,000 over the school year\. Budgeting allows you to recognize the small ways you may be spending much more than you realize\.

Plan your finances by checking your [undergraduate tuition fees](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/undergraduate-tuition-fees/) and using the [cost calculator](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/cost/), which is based on a first\-year student course load\.

## How to budget[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/budget/\#how\-to\-budget](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/budget/#how-to-budget)

Deciding that you want to budget is the first step you can take towards managing your finances\. Follow the steps below to get you started on your budgeting journey\.

### Step 1\. Download the Spending Plan Template

Download the [Spending Plan Template](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/financial_planning_spending_plan_template.xlsx) \(Excel\) to track your budget\. This template will automatically update your monthly balance as you input your income and expenses\.

### Step 2\. Determine your income

First, calculate your total income\. When creating your budget, make sure to include all sources of income\. Be as accurate as you can, such as deducting taxes from your payroll figures\.

Consider both repayable and non\-repayable sources of income\. Repayable sources of income refer to money you’ll have to pay back, while non\-repayable sources of income do not need to be repaid\.

On the spreadsheet, input this information in the “Income/Resources” table\. 

- **Row 1**

  - **Header cell 1:**
  
    Type of income
  
  - **Header cell 2:**
  
    Examples

- **Row 2**

  - **Header cell 1:**
  
    Repayable income
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    -   Student loans
    -   Line of credit or bank loan
    -   Money borrowed from family or friends

- **Row 3**

  - **Header cell 1:**
  
    Non\-repayable income
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    -   Job earnings and tax refunds
    -   Family contributions and savings
    -   Grants, bursaries, and awards

### Step 3\. List all your fixed expenses

Fixed expenses are those that you expect on a regular schedule, such as:

-   Rent payments
-   Tuition and student fees
-   Utilities and bills \(e\.g\., internet, phone\)
-   Gym or other membership fees
-   Subscriptions

On the spreadsheet, input this information in the “Expenses” table\. 

### Step 4\. List all your variable expenses

Variable expenses are all the other things you purchase that do not occur regularly\. These expenses can be essential, but they may still change month to month\.

Variable expenses can include:

-   Groceries and snacks
-   Entertainment
-   Travelling
-   Clothes, shopping, and personal care

On the spreadsheet, input this information in the “Expenses” table\.

### Step 5\. Compare your income and expenses

Review the “Monthly Balance” row on the spreadsheet\.

If you have more income than expenses, congratulations\! Your budget is balanced and you can consider putting some of your extra money into savings\.

If your income and your expenses are equal, consider some ways to give yourself a little breathing room\. You can do this by either lowering your expenses, increasing your income, or both\.

If your income is less than your expenses, it is time to re\-balance your budget\. That means increasing your income or decreasing your expenses\. There are many resources you can access for help\. Reach out and make a plan for your finances\.

### Step 6\. Balance your budget

Whenever possible, your expenses should not exceed your income\. There are 2 ways to balance your budget:

-   Increase your income by applying for a student loan, working part\-time, starting a side gig based on your skillset, and applying for awards\.
-   Decrease your expenses by cutting unnecessary spending, purchasing used or discount items, or consolidating loans while paying off higher interest amounts first\.

Another way to balance your budget is to make a strict spending plan for the month, then compare your expenses at the end of the month with your plan\. Were you exactly right with your numbers? Did you underestimate or overestimate in some areas? You can learn from your current situation and make a more accurate budget for the next month\. This approach helps you think about your expenses, but also identifies exactly what your costs are rather than guessing each month\.

Even small changes can have a big impact, especially over time\. Balancing your budget allows you to plan for emergencies and any unexpected fees or expenses\.

## Plan for success[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/budget/\#plan\-for\-success](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/budget/#plan-for-success)

Beyond the considerations above, there are additional steps you can take towards financial success:

-   Set 3 goals for balancing your budget and including specific actions to achieve those goals\.
-   Create your own personal budget and keep track of your numbers for a month\. Estimate how much you will have left in your savings at the end of the month, then compare this with your actual bank account balance\. Repeat the process for the next month\.
-   Review your monthly budget and identify your top 3 spending weaknesses\.
-   Give yourself a specific amount of cash for the next 2 weeks to spend on variable expenses and stick to that amount\.

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/budget/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/budget/#additional-resources)

-   [Financial planning](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/)
-   [Financial support options](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/)
-   [Financial Wellness Training and Education](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-wellness-training-education/)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/budget/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/budget/#if-you-have-questions)

For help with finances, registration, records, and more, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

title: Financial planning for post-baccalaureate students
content_markdown:
## About the program[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/financial\-planning\-post\-baccalaureate/\#about\-the\-program](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/financial-planning-post-baccalaureate/#about-the-program)

Post\-baccalaureate programs include Law, Dentistry, Medicine and Education\. These programs involve significant cost and time commitments\. As a post\-baccalaureate student, it’s important to make sure you are financially prepared\.

## Tuition and living costs[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/financial\-planning\-post\-baccalaureate/\#tuition\-and\-living\-costs](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/financial-planning-post-baccalaureate/#tuition-and-living-costs)

Each post\-baccalaureate program is unique\. Find specific information on tuition and living costs associated with your program:

-   [Medicine](http://mdprogram.med.ubc.ca/student-resources/financial-support/cost-of-an-md-student/)
-   [Law](https://allard.ubc.ca/programs/juris-doctor-jd-program/costs-and-funding/tuition-and-program-fees)
-   [Dentistry](http://www.dentistry.ubc.ca/dmd/dmd-financial-info/)
-   [Education](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/financial-planning-post-baccalaureate/funding-bachelor-education/)
-   [Pharmacy \(Entry to Practice\)](https://pharmsci.ubc.ca/programs/entry-practice-pharmd-degree/entry-practice-doctor-pharmacy-pharmd-program)

## Student loans and bursaries[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/financial\-planning\-post\-baccalaureate/\#student\-loans\-and\-bursaries](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/financial-planning-post-baccalaureate/#student-loans-and-bursaries)

Government student loans and bursaries may be available to help supplement your financial resources\. It is important to note that these resources will not cover all of your costs for your program\. Read more about [types of loans and eligibility](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/)\.

-   Check your loan assessment for exact amounts and disbursement dates\.
-   Ensure you have met the minimum [credit load requirements](https://tools.students.ubc.ca/course-load-guide/) to maintain your loan\. 
-   Apply for your student loan by **Fri, Jul 31, 2026** to be eligible for a one\-month tuition deferral

Learn more about the [UBC bursary program](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/) and how to apply\.

## Scholarships and awards[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/financial\-planning\-post\-baccalaureate/\#scholarships\-and\-awards](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/financial-planning-post-baccalaureate/#scholarships-and-awards)

Scholarships and awards recognize outstanding student achievement\. You do not need to apply for most scholarships and awards, since your faculty directly recommends students\.

As a post\-baccalaureate student, you may also apply for:

-   [Affiliation scholarships](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/affiliation-scholarships/)
-   [Affiliation bursaries](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/affiliation-bursaries/)
-   [Awards for Indigenous students](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-indigenous/)
-   [Awards for students with disabilities](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-disabilities/)
-   [Premier Undergraduate and Wesbrook scholarships](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/premier-undergraduate-wesbrook-scholarships/)

## Professional line of credit[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/financial\-planning\-post\-baccalaureate/\#professional\-line\-of\-credit](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/financial-planning-post-baccalaureate/#professional-line-of-credit)

You may want to consider a professional student line of credit to fulfil any gaps in funding\. Many financial institutions offer lines of credit and have packages specifically designed for students in professional programs\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/financial\-planning\-post\-baccalaureate/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/financial-planning-post-baccalaureate/#if-you-have-questions)

For help with finances, registration, records, and more, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

title: Funding your Bachelor of Education
content_markdown:
The Bachelor of Education \(BEd\) is an intensive program with significant costs\. Understanding your costs is essential to building a good financial plan and a successful year of study\.

## Understanding your costs[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/financial\-planning\-post\-baccalaureate/funding\-bachelor\-education/\#understanding\-your\-costs](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/financial-planning-post-baccalaureate/funding-bachelor-education/#understanding-your-costs)

Start by using the [cost calculator](http://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/cost/#cost-calculator) to estimate your costs for the year, including tuition, fees, and living expenses\. Next, consider the resources available to you\. You are expected to prepare for the costs of the Bachelor of Education program by accessing all resources available, including but not limited to:

-   Parent and family support
-   Summer earnings
-   Personal savings
-   Government student loans
-   Bursaries
-   Part\-time work

## Awards[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/financial\-planning\-post\-baccalaureate/funding\-bachelor\-education/\#awards](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/financial-planning-post-baccalaureate/funding-bachelor-education/#awards)

There are a limited number of awards available that you may be eligible for\. These include [Faculty of Education awards](http://teach.educ.ubc.ca/students/awards/) for both new and continuing Education students, as well as other [general awards for UBC students](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/)\.

## Bursaries[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/financial\-planning\-post\-baccalaureate/funding\-bachelor\-education/\#bursaries](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/financial-planning-post-baccalaureate/funding-bachelor-education/#bursaries)

You are encouraged to apply for the [UBC Bursary Program](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/) as another type of financial support\.

To be eligible for the UBC Bursary Program, you must apply for your full\-time government student loan by Jul 31, and apply for the bursary through [Workday](https://myworkday.ubc.ca/) between Aug 15 and Sep 15\.

-   The Bachelor of Education \(BEd\) program is eligible for a limited number of bursaries and therefore your full unmet need may not be filled\.
-   By applying for the Winter Bursary Program between Aug 15 and Sep 15, you will be considered for the full length of the 11\-month program\. You will not be eligible for more assistance in the Summer Bursary program, as your unmet need will have already been considered for the full year\.

## Student loans[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/financial\-planning\-post\-baccalaureate/funding\-bachelor\-education/\#student\-loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/financial-planning-post-baccalaureate/funding-bachelor-education/#student-loans)

Government student loans are available to help supplement your financial resources\. It is important to note that these loans will not cover all of your costs for the Bachelor of Education \(BEd\) program\. Read more about [types of loans and eligibility](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/)\.

-   Your student loan will be disbursed in 2 unequal installments\.
-   Check your loan assessment for exact amounts and disbursement dates\.
-   By applying for your loan by Jul 31, your tuition will be deferred until after your loan disbursement dates in early September and mid\-February\.
-   Please ensure you have met the minimum credit load requirements to maintain your loan\. As this is an intensive program, the minimum credit loads are different between terms and are higher than the standard 9\-credit minimums\. Refer to the email you will receive in early July titled “Important student loans and bursary information for Education Students”\.

## Student line of credit[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/financial\-planning\-post\-baccalaureate/funding\-bachelor\-education/\#student\-line\-of\-credit](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/financial-planning-post-baccalaureate/funding-bachelor-education/#student-line-of-credit)

A student line of credit may be an option for you to make sure you have enough money to cover your costs\.

You can apply for a student line of credit at any private bank\. Bring your letter of acceptance or a proof of enrolment letter to the bank when you apply\.

Learn how to [download your proof of enrolment letter](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/student-documents/downloading-your-confirmation-of-enrolment-letter/) in Workday\.​

## Work opportunities[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/financial\-planning\-post\-baccalaureate/funding\-bachelor\-education/\#work\-opportunities](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/financial-planning-post-baccalaureate/funding-bachelor-education/#work-opportunities)

The Bachelor of Education \(BEd\) program involves an intense course load so finding time to work may be difficult\.

A [Work Learn position](https://students.ubc.ca/career/work-learn-program/) may be your best option if you choose to work during your studies\. It’s a great way to earn extra money part\-time during the academic year\. There are also other [part\-time jobs on campus](https://students.ubc.ca/career/campus-jobs/) that you can explore\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/funding\-studies/financial\-planning/financial\-planning\-post\-baccalaureate/funding\-bachelor\-education/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/financial-planning-post-baccalaureate/funding-bachelor-education/#if-you-have-questions)

Contact the Enrolment Services Education Support Advisor at [es\.edusupport@ubc\.ca](mailto:es.edusupport@ubc.ca)\.
