title: Financial support options
content_markdown:
UBC recognizes the significant contribution you and your family make toward your degree\. [Enrolment Services Advisors](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) are here to advise you on finances and resources like scholarships, bursaries, and other assistance programs\.

## Setting yourself up for financial wellness[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/\#setting\-yourself\-up\-for\-financial\-wellness](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/#setting-yourself-up-for-financial-wellness)

Financial wellness at UBC involves proactive planning\. Review the [financial planning guide](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/) and drop into [financial wellness workshops](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-wellness-training-education/), or connect with an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) to discuss your financial plan\. You can also learn how to stay on top of your finances with the [guide to budgeting](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/budget/)\.

## Your responsibilities as a student[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/\#your\-responsibilities\-as\-a\-student](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/#your-responsibilities-as-a-student)

Make sure you have a clear understanding of your financial responsibilities as a student and take the proper steps to access available resources, such as:

-   Talking with your family about financial support
-   Applying for government [student loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/)
-   Meeting deadlines for funding programs
-   Making sure you take the minimum number of courses required for financial aid
-   Maintaining a good credit history

If you’re facing an unexpected [financial emergency](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-emergencies/) or experiencing a significant change to your financial situation, contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) to discuss your options\.

## Domestic student support[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/\#domestic\-student\-support](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/#domestic-student-support)

UBC is strongly committed to supporting domestic students which include Canadian citizens and permanent residents of Canada\. For this reason, UBC established the [UBC Bursary Program](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/), which aligns with the [Financial Aid Policy for domestic students](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-aid-policy-domestic/) \(Policy LR10\)\.

Beyond financial support from the UBC Bursary, there are other ways you can fund your studies:

-   Merit\-based awards: [scholarships and bursaries](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/)
-   Wage subsidy programs like [Work Learn](https://students.ubc.ca/career/work-learn-program/)
-   Repayable funding: [government student loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/), private loans, or lines of credit
-   Non\-repayable funding: bursaries and [student grants](https://www.canada.ca/en/services/benefits/education/student-aid/grants-loans.html)
-   Other UBC case\-specific funding

## International student support[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/\#international\-student\-support](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/#international-student-support)

UBC recognizes the academic achievement of outstanding students from around the world by devoting more than $35 million annually to awards, scholarships, and other forms of financial support for international undergraduate students, such as:

-   Merit\-based [scholarships and awards](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-international/)
-   Wage subsidy programs like [Work Learn](https://students.ubc.ca/career/work-learn-program/)

## Indigenous student support[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/\#indigenous\-student\-support](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/#indigenous-student-support)

As an Indigenous student, you can finance your education at UBC in many ways\. Browse [financial support options](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-support-indigenous/) specific to you, Indigenous student awards, job opportunities and training programs, band or community sponsorship, and more\.

## Students with disabilities[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/\#students\-with\-disabilities](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/#students-with-disabilities)

Enrolment Service Advisors coordinate with the [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/) to help students with disabilities manage their financial challenges\. If you are a student with a disability, you may be eligible for all standard programs, but there is additional information you need to know\.

### Student loans for students with disabilities

Both the federal and provincial governments have special programs administered through student loan agencies\. These programs support eligible students with disabilities and include non\-repayable grants to help with living expenses, as well as funding for specialized educational equipment and services\.

Find more information about these programs through the [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/) or by [StudentAid BC’s list of programs](https://studentaidbc.ca/explore/grants-scholarships)\.

### Disability Programs application

#### British Columbia residents

BC residents who are student loan\-approved and have a permanent disability or persistent or prolonged disability are encouraged to submit a [Disability Programs Application](https://studentaidbc.ca/sites/all/files/form-library/appendix_8.pdf) to StudentAid BC\. Once approved, you may be eligible for additional grants and additional financial support for services and equipment\. You may also be approved for studying at 40% of a full [course load](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/course-load-guide/)\.

If you are taking less than 40% of a full course load, you can apply for grant funding through the [StudentAid BC Part\-Time Studies application](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/part-time-funding-british-columbia/)\.

#### Students outside of BC

For government student loans for students with permanent disability or persistent or prolonged disability, the application process is different in each province\. Contact your home province loan provider to ensure that you are submitting the correct information and forms\. See information about [loans for students from other provinces](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/loans-full-time-other-provinces/)\.

### Awards for students with a disability

Awards in the form of scholarships and bursaries are available for students with disabilities\. Each award has different values and eligibility requirements\. You must register with the [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/) to be eligible\.

[Browse awards](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-disabilities/)

## Helpful resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/\#helpful\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/#helpful-resources)

-   [Funding your studies](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/)
-   [Student loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/)
-   [Awards: scholarships and bursaries](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/)
-   [Planning for your finances at UBC](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/)
-   [Financial Wellness workshops](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-wellness-training-education/)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/#if-you-have-questions)

Contact your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\. Even if you do not have an assigned Advisor, they are still able to help\.

title: Financial Aid Policy for domestic students
content_markdown:
## About the policy[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/financial\-aid\-policy\-domestic/\#about\-the\-policy](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-aid-policy-domestic/#about-the-policy)

The [Financial Aid Policy](https://universitycounsel.ubc.ca/policies/financial-aid-policy/) \(Policy LR10\) was created to ensure that UBC is financially accessible to all domestic students, meaning that full\-time domestic students—Canadian citizens or permanent residents of Canada—are not prevented from starting or continuing their studies for financial reasons alone\.

It is your responsibility to understand if you are eligible and follow the steps to apply to [financial support options](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/) under the policy\. This includes, but is not limited to, demonstrating financial need, meeting deadlines for funding programs, and making sure you are taking the minimum number of courses required for financial assistance\.

## How aid is determined[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/financial\-aid\-policy\-domestic/\#how\-aid\-is\-determined](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-aid-policy-domestic/#how-aid-is-determined)

UBC determines your financial need based on the BC Student Assistance Program assessment mechanism\. This is the difference between your assessed total cost of study and your available resources, such as government assistance and expected financial contributions\.

If you are considered a dependent student, UBC will also consider your family’s resources\. Learn what it means to be a [dependent student](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/loans-full-time-british-columbia/)\.

## Policy flexibility[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/financial\-aid\-policy\-domestic/\#policy\-flexibility](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-aid-policy-domestic/#policy-flexibility)

Not every student’s financial situation fits within UBC’s guidelines\. That’s why Policy LR10 allows exceptions in certain situations:

-   A student, domestic or international, faces a [financial emergency](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-emergencies/)\.
-   The standard assessment method does not realistically reflect a student’s situation\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/financial\-aid\-policy\-domestic/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-aid-policy-domestic/#if-you-have-questions)

For help with finances, registration, records, and more, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

title: Financial support for Indigenous students
content_markdown:
## Creating a financial plan[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/financial\-support\-indigenous/\#creating\-a\-financial\-plan](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-support-indigenous/#creating-a-financial-plan)

Deciding to pursue university studies is exciting, and the Indigenous Student Support Team is glad you have chosen UBC to be a part of it\!

Part of preparing for and successfully completing your program is planning for the costs of post\-secondary education\. Creating a financial plan can help you take control of your finances while attending UBC, which can lead to a positive and stress\-free experience\.

As this can be a new situation for many, there are people and resources at UBC to support you as you navigate your options\.

## Academic and personal costs[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/financial\-support\-indigenous/\#academic\-and\-personal\-costs](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-support-indigenous/#academic-and-personal-costs)

If you are planning to attend UBC, you may need to consider the following costs: 

-   Tuition and student fees
-   Books and other classroom material
-   Housing
-   Utilities \(cellphone, power and heat\)
-   Groceries and meals
-   Entertainment and subscriptions
-   Personal items
-   Child care

### Getting started

1.  To calculate your expenses, including tuition and other costs for specific programs, follow the [UBC financial planning guide](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/), or use the [first\-year cost calculator](http://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/cost#cost-calculator)\.
2.  Connect with an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/), who can help you create a personalized financial plan and walk through resources with you\.
3.  Learn about standard [tuition payment options](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/paying-tuition/)\.

## Funding resources for Indigenous students[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/financial\-support\-indigenous/\#funding\-resources\-for\-indigenous\-students](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-support-indigenous/#funding-resources-for-indigenous-students)

There are many ways to fund your education at UBC\. If you are an Indigenous student, you can request funds from several funding sources, depending on your situation\.

### First Nation, Band or community sponsorship

At UBC, some Indigenous students are eligible to receive support from their band to pay for their post\-secondary education, including First Nations communities, Métis Associations, or community organizations like the [BC Association of Aboriginal Friendship Centres](https://bcaafc.com/)\. Depending on your band, they may be able to offer support with tuition and fees, as well as monthly living expenses\.

Get in touch with your band early to determine if this is an option for you\.

#### Tuition and student fees

Your band must fill out a [Sponsorship Billing Agreement](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_dg7icsLodwcOdeu) for tuition and student fees before the start of every academic year\. Learn more about the [Sponsorship Billing process](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/sponsorship-billing/)\.

#### Living expenses

If your sponsorship includes housing and meal plan coverage, your sponsor must fill out a [Sponsorship Billing Agreement](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_8q9foXnpnROykLA) with UBC Housing\. Learn more about [Student Housing sponsorship](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/student-housing-sponsorship/)\.

### Government student loans and grants

Government student loans are offered by every province and territory in Canada, and you can apply through your province or territory of residence\.

These loans remain interest\-free while you are a full\-time student\. You are also not required to pay this loan back until you’re no longer in full\-time studies\. It’s the most ideal type of credit or loan for students who need to borrow funding for post\-secondary education\. Read about the [types of student loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/) and how you can apply\.

When you apply for student loans, you’re also considered for [government grant funding](https://www.canada.ca/en/services/benefits/education/student-aid/grants-loans.html), depending on your family size, income, and more\. Grants do not have to be paid back and you’re only eligible for them if you apply for government assistance\.

#### Things to consider

-   If you’re applying for a student loan in British Columbia, the amount of sponsorship funding you receive will not impact your loan assessment\. You are encouraged to apply for both sponsorship funding and student loan funding at the same time\.
-   Outside of British Columbia, sponsorship funding may be counted as an asset towards your loan calculation\. Please verify this with your [Provincial Loan Provider](https://www.canada.ca/en/services/benefits/education/student-aid/grants-loans/province-apply.html)\.
-   If you are eligible for and are receiving government student loans, you are also eligible to apply for the [UBC Bursary Program](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/)\. If your application is successful, you do not need to pay back bursary funds\.
-   For part\-time students, there are specific [loan options](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/part-time-funding-british-columbia/) and grant funding that can cover the cost of tuition, books, and classroom materials\. Part\-time loans provide you with the option to only take non\-repayable grant funding\.
-   A common way for students to finance their post\-secondary course work is through government student loans\. That said, it is also quite common for students to have negative opinions and/or fears around the idea of student loans and/or debt in general\. Having these ideas and feelings is normal, and the Indigenous Student Support Team is here to discuss your options with you\.

### UBC scholarships and bursaries for Indigenous students

The university offers many scholarships and awards based on different criteria, including academic standing, involvement in extracurricular activities, or financial need\. You may wish to check if you’re eligible for the following awards:

-   [Entrance awards for undergraduate Indigenous students](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/scholarships-awards-canadian-students/indigenous-students/)
-   [Entrance funding and information for graduate Indigenous students](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/prospective-students/indigenous-students)
-   [Awards for current Indigenous students](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-indigenous/)
-   [General scholarships, awards, and bursaries for all UBC students](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/)
-   [UBC Bursary program for students with student loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/)
-   [UBC needs\-based Technology Bursary for online learning](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-vancouver-technology-bursary/)
-   [Indigenous Awards for Health Science Students](https://health.aboriginal.ubc.ca/students/student-awards/)

You can also use the [UBC Award Search Tool](https://tools.students.ubc.ca/award-search/) to explore the general awards and scholarships by faculty and year level\.

### International Tuition Exemption for Indigenous students

Certain American Indigenous international students may be eligible to pay domestic fees\. Learn more about the [International Tuition Exemption](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-support-indigenous/international-tuition-exemption/)\.

### Former youth in care waiver program

UBC is committed to supporting the academic and personal achievements of [former and current youth in care](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/former-youth-in-care/)\. If you have been a youth in care within British Columbia, you may qualify for the [UBC Post\-Care Tuition Waiver Program](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/loans-bursaries/youth-in-care-funding/) or the [BC Provincial Tuition Waiver Program](https://studentaidbc.ca/explore/grants-scholarships/provincial-tuition-waiver-program)\.

## Jobs and career resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/financial\-support\-indigenous/\#jobs\-and\-career\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-support-indigenous/#jobs-and-career-resources)

UBC offers many job opportunities for students to build work experience and earn money\.

[Work Learn program](https://students.ubc.ca/career/work-learn-program/)

Work part\-time while still taking classes\.

[Community Based Work Learn](https://students.ubc.ca/career/work-learn-program/)

Self\-identifying Indigenous students are encouraged to apply for Work Learn positions with a paid training program\.

[UBC Co\-op program](https://students.ubc.ca/career/co-op/)

Gain work experience in the industry through a full\-time position during your degree\. 

[Other on\-campus jobs](https://students.ubc.ca/career/campus-jobs/)

Check out places at UBC that regularly hire students\.

[Career resources for Indigenous graduates](https://students.ubc.ca/career/career-resources/career-resources-historically-marginalized-students/career-resources-indigenous-graduates/)

Read the guide to help you move through the next steps of your career journey\.

[Job Search](https://students.ubc.ca/career/career-resources/job-search/)

Learn how to be strategic in finding job opportunities\.

## Emergency funding[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/financial\-support\-indigenous/\#emergency\-funding](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-support-indigenous/#emergency-funding)

Sometimes, even with the best planning, you may run into a situation that is out of your control and you may need help to manage the problem\. When no other financial options are available, you may wish to consider [short\-term emergency funding](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/emergency-funding/) to help cover a temporary shortfall due to an unexpected emergency situation\.

Contact your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) about the funding\. If you do not have an assigned Advisor, please email [es\.indigenous@ubc\.ca](mailto:es.indigenous@ubc.ca)\.

## If you need help[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/financial\-support\-indigenous/\#if\-you\-need\-help](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-support-indigenous/#if-you-need-help)

The Indigenous Student Support and Advising Team in Enrolment Services works closely with other teams on campus, including the following:

-   [First Nations House of Learning](https://indigenous.ubc.ca/longhouse/fnhl/)
-   [Indigenous Student Academic Advising team](https://indigenous.ubc.ca/students/current-students/student-resources/program-advising/)
-   [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/)

### How Enrolment Service Advisors can help

From the beginning of your UBC journey until graduation, Enrolment Services Advisors can support you when you need it in the following ways:

-   Creating a financial plan with you
-   Helping you understand the different funding options
-   Developing a scholarship or award application

All undergraduate students have an assigned [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) for personalized advising\. If you do not have an assigned advisor, you can email the Indigenous Advising Team \([es\.indigenous@ubc\.ca](mailto:es.indigenous@ubc.ca)\) for help\.

### Book an appointment

If you have an assigned [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/), please contact them directly through email or phone\. Otherwise, you can email [es\.indigenous@ubc\.ca](mailto:es.indigenous@ubc.ca) and book a one\-on\-one advising appointment with a member of the Indigenous Student Support Team\.

If you’re a UBC Okanagan student, please contact the [UBC Okanagan Indigenous Student Advising Team](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/academic-success/academic-advising/aboriginal-student-advising)\.

### In\-person drop\-in support

On **Tuesdays** from **10:00 am to 3:00 pm**, speak with an Enrolment Services Advisor on the Indigenous Student Support Team at the [UBC First Nations Longhouse](https://fnhl.ubc.ca/longhouse)\. Find us in the Sty\-Wet\-Tan Great Hall during lunch or ask the front desk about us\.

title: Paying tuition
content_markdown:
## First, review your balance[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/tuition\-fees/paying\-tuition/\#first\-review\-your\-balance](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/paying-tuition/#first-review-your-balance)

You are responsible for paying the tuition and fees assessed in Workday\. Learn how to find your [tuition and fee amounts](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/viewing-your-financial-account-activity-tuition-amount-and-payments/)\. The earliest you can pay your tuition and fees through TouchNet is 30 days from the due date\.

If there are any changes to your registration, program of study, or citizenship on your account, your account balance will be updated the following day\. Your Account Activity does not refresh in real time\. Tuition and student fees are assessed nightly\.

### Unaccepted in\-person payments

While in\-person services are available, Enrolment Services cannot accept cash, personal cheques from a Canadian financial institution, and debit or credit card payments in person\. Only external awards and US dollar cheques are accepted for in\-person tuition and student fee payment\.

## Online payment options[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/tuition\-fees/paying\-tuition/\#online\-payment\-options](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/paying-tuition/#online-payment-options)

### Online banking

Set up online banking to pay your UBC tuition and fees like any other bill\. Payments take 2 to 3 business days to process and appear on Workday\. Enrolment Services will honour the payment date\.

To pay with online banking, follow the steps below:

1.  Open a bank account at a Canadian financial institution
2.  Add “UBC Tuition” or “UBC Tuition Fees” as a bill payee
3.  Use your student number as the bill’s account number
4.  Enter the amount you’d like to pay for your UBC tuition and fees

#### Student housing and meal plan payments

For information about paying student housing and meal plan fees, please visit [Student Housing Fees and Payments](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/fees-payments/)\.

### Pre\-Authorized Debit

UBC does not automatically withdraw funds from your bank account through Pre\-Authorized Debit \(PAD\) to pay the balance you owe\. Once your account is set up, you have to initiate every PAD transaction to make a payment\. Payments are posted immediately on your student account, but can take several days to be processed in your bank account\. Please keep sufficient funds in your bank account until the funds have been withdrawn by UBC\.

Follow the tutorials for paying by Pre\-Authorized Debit in Workday: 

-   [Setting up your Pre\-Authorized Debit Account](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/setting-up-your-pre-authorized-debit-account-in-touchnet/)
-   [Paying your tuition and fees with Pre\-Authorized Debit](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/paying-your-tuition-and-student-fees-in-touchnet-pre-authorized-debit/)

Pre\-Authorized Debit payments may be returned by your financial institution similar to a bounced cheque in the following situations:

-   There are insufficient funds or funds are not available\.
-   You entered incorrect account details\.
-   The account doesn’t have chequing privileges\.
-   The account has been closed\.

If your payment is returned, the funds will be reversed out of your student account\. This may place your account on financial hold\. You will be charged an insufficient funds penalty of $35 and may also be charged additional interest\.

### International Funds Transfer \(IFT\) using TransferMate

You can pay your UBC tuition and fees from a foreign bank account with non\-Canadian currency using International Funds Transfer \(IFT\)\.

Follow the [online Workday tutorial](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/paying-your-tuition-and-student-fees-in-touchnet-transfermate-payment/) for paying your tuition and student fees using TransferMate payment\.

For further support while paying via TransferMate, please contact [TransferMate](https://transfermateeducation.com/customerservice.aspx)\.

Completed payments made through TransferMate may take 3 to 10 days to appear on Workday\.

### Credit Card or Signature Debit Card

You can pay your tuition and student fees using an accepted credit card or signature debit card\.

Follow the [online Workday tutorial](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/paying-your-tuition-and-student-fees-in-touchnet-credit-card-and-signature-debit-card-payment/) to pay by credit card or signature debit card\.

This payment method is subject to a non\-refundable convenience fee, as listed below\.

| Payment type | Convenience fee |
| --- | --- |
| Visa or Mastercard | 2\.65% of the full payment **or** a minimum flat fee of $3\.00, whichever is greater |
| Visa Debit or Mastercard Debit | 1\.65% of the full payment **or** a minimum flat fee of $3\.00, whichever is greater |

## Other payment options[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/tuition\-fees/paying\-tuition/\#other\-payment\-options](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/paying-tuition/#other-payment-options)

**

Paying with your Registered Education Savings Plan \(RESP\)

**

A proof of enrolment, also known as a confirmation of enrolment letter, is often needed to redeem RESPs\.

You can download your [Confirmation of Enrolment Letter](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/student-documents/downloading-your-confirmation-of-enrolment-letter/) from Workday\.

Most RESP providers accept the UBC proof of enrolment directly downloaded from Workday\. If your RESP provider does not accept the UBC proof of enrolment downloaded from Workday, please contact [Enrolment Services](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

**

Paying by US dollar cheques in person

**

You can pay your tuition and student fees in person at [Enrolment Services](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) in Brock Hall with a US dollar cheque\. Payments received by cheque at Enrolment Services in Brock Hall will take up to 10 business days to process\.

1.  Make sure your cheque is correctly filled out, and that your student number is written on the front of the cheque on the memo line\.
2.  Fill out a [Tuition Fee Payment Form](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/tuition_fee_payment_form.pdf) \(pdf\) and attach it to your cheque\. No post\-dated cheques will be accepted\.
3.  Bring your cheque and payment slip to [Enrolment Services Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

Payment using US dollar cheques will use the UBC currency exchange rate of the day it is processed and not the day it is received by UBC\. To lock in an exchange rate, consider paying via [International Funds Transfer with TransferMate](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/paying-your-tuition-and-student-fees-in-touchnet-transfermate-payment/)\.

**

Tuition fee deferral for full\-time Canadian student loan holders

**

An automatic, one\-month tuition fee deferral is available to students who apply for a full\-time Canadian [student loan](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/) by April 15 for the Summer session and July 31 for the Winter session\. Your loan will be issued to you directly, and then payment to UBC can be made through online banking or pre\-authorized debit\.

**

Tuition fee deferral for TAs or RAs

**

A tuition fee deferral is available to graduate students employed by UBC as Teaching or Research Assistants \(TAs or RAs\)\.

You can find detailed eligibility and application instructions on the [Tuition Fee Deferral Application](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_cw0JHfpA16wf2RM)\. Proof of employment is required\. You can submit a screenshot of your Compensation page from your Workday account or a letter from your department stating your start and end date of employment\.

Below are the online application periods for tuition fee deferral:

-   **Summer session**: March 1 to April 30
-   **Winter Term 1**: July 15 to August 31
-   **Winter Term 2**: November 1 to December 31

**

Paying by cheque at any RBC branch

**

You can pay your tuition fees at any Royal Bank of Canada \(RBC\) branch using a personal cheque, without a service charge\.

Your payment will be applied first to any fees that you owe from previous academic sessions\. Please make sure your account is fully paid to avoid late charges\.

You must have your student number recorded on the face of the cheque payable to UBC\.

**How to make your payment**

The steps below are only for paying your tuition fees, not for depositing external award cheques\.

1.  Pick up an RBC Deposit slip at the [Enrolment Services Advising Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) or at the RBC branch\.
2.  Fill out your Student ID, followed by your Last Name and First Name in the “Narrative box” space provided at the top of the deposit slip\. If you don’t have a “Narrative box”, write your details in the empty space on the top left as shown in the second screenshot\.
3.  All student tuition cheques should be deposited into RBC Tuition Account \#18076\.

[paying by cheque](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/paying_by_cheque.jpg)

[paying by cheque 2](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/paying_by_cheque_2-2.jpg)

**

Tuition Waivers

**

Tuition waivers are employment benefits available to UBC staff and faculty only\. Learn about [tuition waivers](https://finance.ubc.ca/payroll/your-benefits/tuition-waivers), eligibility requirements, and how to submit them to UBC\.

Once your tuition waiver is approved by [UBC Benefits](https://hr.ubc.ca/contact/contact-benefits), the waiver information will be updated in Workday\.

The waivers do not cover student fees\. Make sure you pay for your student fees in Workday\. Learn how to view your [tuition amount and payments](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/viewing-your-financial-account-activity-tuition-amount-and-payments/)\.

If you have any questions, contact the [ISC Helpdesk](https://isc.ubc.ca/)\.

**

Private lenders

**

UBC does not accept deposits from most private lenders or unauthorized third\-party service providers for the payment of tuition and/or student fees unless specifically listed as an exception below\.

Transactions from private lenders will be rejected and students will be responsible for any fees incurred as a result of the payment or return of funds\. If you have unpaid tuition and fees because of rejected transactions, you may be put on financial hold and charged an [interest penalty](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/late-payment-fees/)\.

Exceptions:

-   US students can apply for [private loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-private-student-loans/)\.
-   UBC has a working agreement with [Windmill Microlending](https://www.windmillmicrolending.org/?r=0) and eligible students can connect directly with Windmill Microlending for more information\.
-   Students or applicants pursuing specific full\-time Sauder School of Business graduate programs \(Master of Business Administration, Master of Management, and Master of Business Analytics\) may be eligible for loans from Prodigy Finance and should [contact Sauder](https://www.sauder.ubc.ca/contact-ubc-sauder) directly\.

## Scholarships[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/tuition\-fees/paying\-tuition/\#scholarships](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/paying-tuition/#scholarships)

**

Claiming your UBC scholarship

**

If you are a UBC scholarship recipient, the scholarship amount will be applied to your student account against any fees owed after you’ve accepted the award in Workday\. Awards that have not been accepted will not be disbursed\.

For scholarships paid in installments, funds will be credited to your tuition account on the date specified in the award legal agreement\.

If your award amount is less than the total amount you owe, you’re required to pay the difference by the fee deadline to avoid late charges\. If your award amount exceeds your tuition you must pay for the term, please [set up your direct deposit](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/setting-up-your-direct-deposit/) before accepting the award to receive the balance directly\.

Scholarships cannot be applied towards acceptance or registration deposits\.

**

Redeeming a BC Provincial scholarship

**

Follow the instructions to redeem BC Provincial scholarships, such as:

-   BC Achievement
-   District/Authority
-   BC Excellence
-   Pathway to Teacher Education
-   Graduation Program Examination

**Online verification**

Submit the following documents through the [Scholarship Redemption online form](https://www.bcedextranet.gov.bc.ca/secure_forms/Scholarship_Redemption.html):

-   **Provincial Scholarship Voucher**  
    Write your Social Insurance Number \(SIN\) and email address on the voucher\. Check that your mailing address is correct\. If it isn’t, provide your current address\.
-   **Verification or Proof of Enrolment**  
    Download your [Confirmation of Enrolment Letter](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/student-documents/downloading-your-confirmation-of-enrolment-letter/) in Workday\.
-   **Proof of Tuition Fee Payment**  
    Download your [proof of tuition payment](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/downloading-your-proof-of-tuition-payment-account-statement/), also known as your Account Statement, in Workday\. 

**In\-person option**

1.  **Gather your Provincial Scholarship Voucher**  
    Write your Social Insurance Number \(SIN\) and email address on the voucher\. Check that your mailing address is correct\. If it isn’t, provide your current address\.
2.  **Verify your document**  
    Have your Provincial Scholarship Voucher stamped and signed at [Enrolment Services Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.
3.  **Submit your verified voucher**  
    Scan or take a photo of your verified voucher and submit it through the [Scholarship Redemption online form](https://www.bcedextranet.gov.bc.ca/secure_forms/Scholarship_Redemption.html)\.

**

Depositing external award cheques

**

**Mailing cheques to Enrolment Services**

Undergraduate students who have received an external award should ask the granting agency or organization to send the cheque directly to [Enrolment Services](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) for processing with the subject line “Attention: External Awards Processing”\.

In some cases, the granting agency or organization may require supporting documentation from the student before the cheque can be released\.

If you’ve received the cheque directly from the organization, include your student number and Confirmation of Enrolment letter in your mail with the cheque to Enrolment Services\. Allow at least 4 weeks for processing\.

**Bringing your external award cheque and payment slip to Enrolment Services**

Make sure your cheque is correctly filled out, and that your student number is written on the front of the cheque on the memo line\. Bring your cheque and payment slip to [Enrolment Services Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) at Brock Hall\.

Payments made by external award cheque at Enrolment Services Advising in Brock Hall will take at least 4 weeks to appear on your tuition account\.

## Sponsorship Billing[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/tuition\-fees/paying\-tuition/\#sponsorship\-billing](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/paying-tuition/#sponsorship-billing)

Some UBC students have a sponsor who pays a portion of their UBC fees\. Sponsors can be an Indigenous community, employer, or government agency\. When UBC sends a bill for fees to sponsors, this is called “third\-party billing”\.

Learn more about [sponsorship billing](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/sponsorship-billing/) and how the application or payment process works\.

## Late payment of fees[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/tuition\-fees/paying\-tuition/\#late\-payment\-of\-fees](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/paying-tuition/#late-payment-of-fees)

Your fees must be paid in full by the [payment deadlines](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/fees/policies-fees#15539-pay-and-due)\. Otherwise, you may be placed on a financial hold and charged a processing fee, as well as an interest penalty\. Your financial hold will be removed when you pay the outstanding balance in full\.

Learn about [late payment of fees](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/late-payment-fees/)\.

## Tuition adjustments and refunds[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/tuition\-fees/paying\-tuition/\#tuition\-adjustments\-and\-refunds](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/paying-tuition/#tuition-adjustments-and-refunds)

If you are planning to drop or withdraw from a course, you may be eligible for a [tuition refund](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/tuition-refunds/) or adjustment\. To be eligible for a 100% refund of tuition, you must drop your classes by the [course drop deadline](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/course-change-dates/)\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/tuition\-fees/paying\-tuition/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/paying-tuition/#if-you-have-questions)

For help with finances, registration, records, and more, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

title: Late payment of fees
content_markdown:
If your fees are not fully paid by the [payment deadlines](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/fees/policies-fees#15539-pay-and-due), your account may be placed on financial hold\. Read more about overdue student fees on the [Academic Calendar](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/fees/policies-fees#17941) and [Policy FM1](https://universitycounsel.ubc.ca/policies/late-payment-policy/)\.

If you’re a UBC Okanagan student, read [UBC Okanagan information](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/finances/tuition-and-fees/) on late payment of fees\.

## Financial holds[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/tuition\-fees/late\-payment\-fees/\#financial\-holds](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/late-payment-fees/#financial-holds)

A student may be placed on financial hold as a result of outstanding fees, including tuition and student fees, parking and library fines, and Student Housing and Community Services fees\. The hold will be removed once the outstanding balance, including penalties, is paid in full\.

If you are put on financial hold, you will be blocked from the following registration activities:

-   Registering in new courses
-   Enroling in course waitlists
-   Switching course sections

### What happens during a financial hold

If you are placed on hold, you will not be dropped from class automatically and your professors will not be notified\. However, the following will happen:

-   Your registration will be blocked\. You can still drop or withdraw from courses before the [course change dates](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/course-change-dates/)\.
-   A $35\.00 processing fee will be assessed\.
-   You will be assessed [financial interest](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/late-payment-fees/#financial-interest) near the end of every month\.
-   You will not be able to order transcripts and parchments\.
-   You will not be able to download a program completion letter\.
-   UBC Student Housing and Community Services may refuse your admission to residences, withdraw your residence and dining privileges, and/or require you to vacate the premises\.
-   UBC Parking may withdraw your parking privileges and tow your parked vehicles\.
-   The Library may withdraw your borrowing privileges and electronic access\.
-   Accounts that are still outstanding after the session end date are subject to be sent to a collection agency\.

### Removing a financial hold

The financial hold will be removed when the outstanding balance is paid in full\. You can make partial payments until the entire balance has been paid\. Try to pay as soon as possible to avoid being charged further interest\.

Payment processing times vary depending on your [payment method](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/paying-tuition/)\.

## Financial interest[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/tuition\-fees/late\-payment\-fees/\#financial\-interest](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/late-payment-fees/#financial-interest)

Interest will be charged at a [rate of prime](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/rates/daily-digest/) plus 6% per annum\. Interest is calculated near the end of each month and charged on all outstanding amounts that are past due\.

Anything else in this section notwithstanding and any amounts charged as penalties for the late payment of fees and accounts \(including the Interest Penalty and the processing fee\) will not exceed 60% per annum\.

### How to calculate interest rates charged

Follow the steps below to find the interest charged at the end of each month:

1.  Find the [rate of prime](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/rates/daily-digest/)
2.  Add 6 percent to the rate of prime to get your interest per year
3.  Divide your interest per year by 12 months

The total will be the interest charged on all outstanding amounts past due\.

If you’re facing an unexpected [financial emergency](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-emergencies/), or have had a significant change to your financial situation, contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) to discuss your options and learn how UBC can help\.

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/tuition\-fees/late\-payment\-fees/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/late-payment-fees/#additional-resources)

-   [Funding your studies](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/)
-   [Financial support options](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/)
-   [Financial planning](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/funding-studies/financial-planning/)
-   [Financial emergencies](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-emergencies/)
-   [Accessing crisis support and services](https://students.ubc.ca/health/crisis-support-services/)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/tuition\-fees/late\-payment\-fees/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/late-payment-fees/#if-you-have-questions)

For help with finances, registration, records, and more, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

Some UBC students have a portion of their UBC fees paid by a sponsor such as an Indigenous community, employer, or government agency\. This is called sponsorship billing\.

title: Information for sponsored students
content_markdown:
## About sponsorship billing[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/tuition\-fees/sponsorship\-billing/information\-sponsored\-students/\#about\-sponsorship\-billing](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/sponsorship-billing/information-sponsored-students/#about-sponsorship-billing)

Some UBC students have a portion of their UBC fees paid by a sponsor, such as an Indigenous community, employer, or government agency\. This is called sponsorship billing\.

To have an organization sponsor your studies at UBC, they must meet the required criteria and apply before the start of the term\. Please notify the Sponsorship Billing Office immediately if there are changes to your sponsoring agency or the coverage amount\.

### Housing sponsorship

Enrolment Services does not coordinate sponsorship billing for UBC\-managed residences\. If your sponsor has indicated they can support you with your on\-campus residence fees, please email the Vancouver Student Residence office at [information@housing\.ubc\.ca](mailto:information@housing.ubc.ca) or the Okanagan Student Residence office at [information@housing\.okanagan\.ubc\.ca](mailto:information@housing.okanagan.ubc.ca)\.

Find out more about [student housing sponsorships](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/student-housing-sponsorship/) at UBC\.

## Sponsorship invoicing[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/tuition\-fees/sponsorship\-billing/information\-sponsored\-students/\#sponsorship\-invoicing](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/sponsorship-billing/information-sponsored-students/#sponsorship-invoicing)

We will invoice your sponsor only for the tuition and fees they agree to pay, up to the coverage limit specified for the academic session or term they selected\.

Your sponsor\(s\) will receive an invoice after each Winter Term’s [course change date](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/course-change-dates/), also known as the add/drop deadline\. That way, an accurate invoice will be generated after you finalize your course schedule\. 

If you are taking summer courses, UBC will only issue one invoice in mid\-July for both Summer Session terms\. If you are registered for Summer Term 1 courses, you will not be placed on financial hold as long as an active sponsorship contract is in place by the term’s tuition deadline\.

### Invoice delivery times

-   **Winter Session Term 1**: late September
-   **Winter Session Term 2**: late January
-   **Summer Session**: mid\-July

### Books and supplies

If your sponsor has indicated that they will cover books and supplies, the UBC Bookstore will generate an invoice for that amount\. Bookstore sponsorship is not available for international sponsors\. Email the Sponsorship Billing Office at [ubc\.sponsorship@ubc\.ca](mailto:ubc.sponsorship@ubc.ca) or the UBC Bookstore at [ar\.bookstore@ubc\.ca](mailto:ar.bookstore@ubc.ca) if you have any questions\.

## Your responsibilities as a sponsored student[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/tuition\-fees/sponsorship\-billing/information\-sponsored\-students/\#your\-responsibilities\-as\-a\-sponsored\-student](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/sponsorship-billing/information-sponsored-students/#your-responsibilities-as-a-sponsored-student)

### Communicate with your sponsor

As a sponsored student, you must contact your sponsor to negotiate the terms and length of your sponsorship agreement\. UBC will not do this on your behalf\.

Please also be mindful that you will be responsible for informing your sponsor\(s\) of any changes to your situation which may affect your level of sponsorship \(e\.g\., awards\) and any fees that your sponsor does not cover, including but not limited to, interest charges, late fees, U\-Pass, and the AMS/GSS or SUO Health and Dental plan\.

### Pay other required fees

You are responsible for paying any charges and student fees not covered by your sponsor, such as your [student health and dental coverage](https://www.ams.ubc.ca/support-services/health-dental/)[,](https://www.ams.ubc.ca/support-services/health-dental/) by the published tuition due dates in Workday\.

Any late payment charges you accumulate before your sponsorship contract is authorized will not be reversed\. Sponsors typically do not cover late fees, unless the fees result from their own delayed submission, in which case they may agree to cover the penalties\. Learn more about [paying tuition and student fees](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/paying-tuition/)\.

If your sponsor doesn’t pay the invoice by the deadline, or if there is an outstanding balance on the amount you are responsible for, your student account will be placed on [financial hold](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/fees/policies-fees#17924)\. You won’t be able to register for new courses, view grades, audit a course, or order transcripts while on hold\. You’ll also be charged [late payment fees](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/late-payment-fees/) to your account\.

Please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) if you’re unsure about the fees that you owe\.

### Review your sponsorship contract

You are strongly encouraged to review the terms and coverage limits set out by your sponsor so you understand what your sponsor is covering and what you owe if your sponsor isn’t covering all charges\. You may also request this information from your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/), as it will not be available in Workday\.

### Academic information

If your sponsor requires your academic information, such as transcripts, you are responsible for providing it\. Learn how to [order an official transcript](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-transcript/) for a small fee, or order an unofficial transcript free of charge by logging into the UBC Official Documents tool \(ODMT\)\.

### Submit your student declaration

You must complete the [Sponsor Student Declaration](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_9G3ZP9bQHIjpNAO) as soon as possible to confirm the sponsorship contract\. The declaration only needs to be completed once per program\.

## Granting third\-party authorization[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/tuition\-fees/sponsorship\-billing/information\-sponsored\-students/\#granting\-third\-party\-authorization](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/sponsorship-billing/information-sponsored-students/#granting-third-party-authorization)

UBC complies with the British Columbia [Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act](https://www.bclaws.gov.bc.ca/civix/document/id/complete/statreg/96165_00) \(the “FIPPA”\)\. As a result, UBC requires your permission to disclose details of your financial account to your sponsor\.

### Add your sponsor\(s\) information to Workday

1.  Log in to [Workday Student](https://myworkday.ubc.ca/) and click on the icon on the top right of the screen\. 
2.  Click on “View Profile”, then “Personal”, then “Additional Data”\. 
3.  Complete the details on the “Third\-Party Authorization Form” to authorize your sponsor to receive applicable information about you\.
4.  Select “Yes” for the statement “I acknowledge that I have read, understand and agree to the Terms of Use and Agreement for Third Party Authorization\.”
5.  Type your sponsor organization into the “Name of the person you are authorizing” section\.
6.  From the dropdown options, select “Sponsorship Billing” in the “Person’s relationship to me”\.
7.  Select “Yes” to the statement, “I consent to the release of information pertaining to my financial assistance and award status, including but not limited to student loans, bursaries, scholarships and financial need\. As related to this status, registration, grades, fees and enrolment status may also be released\.” 
8.  Click “Save\.”

By entering into a sponsorship agreement and setting up third\-party authorization, you agree to UBC sharing information from your student account directly with your sponsor\. Information that can be shared with your sponsor includes, but is not limited to, your registered courses, program information, tuition and fee assessments, awards, bursaries or scholarships, grade information, and any other items related to your studies\. 

## Opting out of the AMS Health and Dental Plan[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/tuition\-fees/sponsorship\-billing/information\-sponsored\-students/\#opting\-out\-of\-the\-ams\-health\-and\-dental\-plan](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/sponsorship-billing/information-sponsored-students/#opting-out-of-the-ams-health-and-dental-plan)

If you have extended health and dental coverage elsewhere, you can opt out of the UBC Vancouver [AMS/GSS Health and Dental plan](https://www.ams.ubc.ca/about-us/finances/opt-out-opt-in/) or the UBC Okanagan [SUO Health and Dental plan](https://www.studentcare.ca/rte/en/IHaveAPlan_UBCOkanaganUniversityofBritishColumbiaStudentsUnionOkanaganUBCSUO_ChangeofCoverage_OptOuts)\. If you do not opt out before the deadline, you will be responsible for paying these fees by the deadline\.

## Awards[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/tuition\-fees/sponsorship\-billing/information\-sponsored\-students/\#awards](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/sponsorship-billing/information-sponsored-students/#awards)

Domestic Indigenous students sponsored by their Indigenous community who receive a monetary award through UBC are eligible to keep their full award funding\. The student is responsible for notifying their sponsor or education coordinator of any awards they may receive\.

Sponsored graduate students are not eligible for the following UBC awards:

-   UBC International Tuition Award
-   UBC International Doctoral Fellowship
-   Four\-Year Doctoral Tuition Award
-   Four\-Year Fellowship Tuition Award 
-   Faculty of Science PhD Tuition Award 
-   Chemistry PhD Tuition Award 
-   Graduate Covid Program Delay Tuition Award 
-   Doctoral Recruitment Fellowship Tuition Award

UBC Vancouver graduate students should contact the [Faculty of Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/contact-us) for more information about awards\. UBC Okanagan students can contact the [College of Graduate Studies](https://gradstudies.ok.ubc.ca/about/contact/)\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/tuition\-fees/sponsorship\-billing/information\-sponsored\-students/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/sponsorship-billing/information-sponsored-students/#if-you-have-questions)

Email the Sponsorship Billing office at [ubc\.sponsorship@ubc\.ca](mailto:ubc.sponsorship@ubc.ca) and include your name and UBC student number\. Please be patient, as you may experience delays in email responses\.

To submit a form by fax, use the fax number [604 822 5816](tel:6048225816)\.

If you are an Indigenous student and do not have an assigned [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/), please email [es\.indigenous@ubc\.ca](mailto:es.indigenous@ubc.ca)\.

title: Information for sponsors
content_markdown:
## About sponsorship billing[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/tuition\-fees/sponsorship\-billing/information\-sponsors/\#about\-sponsorship\-billing](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/sponsorship-billing/information-sponsors/#about-sponsorship-billing)

Some UBC students have a portion of their UBC fees paid by a sponsor, such as an Indigenous community, employer, or government agency\. This is called sponsorship billing\. Sponsors must meet the required criteria and apply before the start of the term\. The sponsor should notify the Sponsorship Billing Office of any changes to the sponsoring agency, the coverage amount, or the sponsor’s contact information\.

## Eligibility criteria for sponsors[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/tuition\-fees/sponsorship\-billing/information\-sponsors/\#eligibility\-criteria\-for\-sponsors](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/sponsorship-billing/information-sponsors/#eligibility-criteria-for-sponsors)

You cannot sponsor a student as an individual, parent, or relative\. You must be a government agency, company, Indigenous band, or other organization\. If a sponsor or any third\-party vendor reimburses tuition and fees directly to the student, this is not sponsorship\.

Sponsors are invoiced each term for the costs they agree to and pay UBC directly for these fees\. All sponsors must submit an online [Sponsorship Billing Application](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_dg7icsLodwcOdeu) for each student they wish to sponsor or a group of students who fall under the same sponsorship criteria\. If you are unable to apply online, please fax a completed [Sponsorship Third Party Billing Form](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/sponsorship_third_party_billing_form_2024.pdf) \(pdf\) to the Sponsorship Billing Office\.

UBC has the right to refuse sponsorship or sponsor payments\. Please be aware that contracts or payments from a person, company, or government department can be refused due to rules and regulations enforced by the Canadian government\.

### Accepted currency

UBC can only accept payments in Canadian or US funds\. No other foreign currency is accepted\. All US funds received by UBC will be converted to Canadian funds using the daily exchange rate provided by the UBC Finance Office on the date UBC processes the payment\. UBC cannot use the exchange rate provided by the sponsor\.

Sponsors who want to avoid exchange rate discrepancies should only send funds in Canadian dollars\. UBC cannot control fluctuations in the US and Canadian currency exchange rates, which can change within the same day\.

If setting a sponsorship contract dollar limit, the sponsor can only set dollar limits in Canadian funds\. Any foreign currency limits will be converted to Canadian funds, as UBC can only assess tuition and fees in Canadian funds\. Returns can only be issued to sponsors as a cheque in Canadian funds\.

Please contact the Sponsorship Billing Office if you have any questions about foreign currencies and exchange rates before making payment\.

### Tax receipts

In keeping with Canada Revenue Agency guidelines, the sponsoring organization must issue a T4A tax receipt to their sponsored students\. UBC does not provide this document\.

## How the application process works[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/tuition\-fees/sponsorship\-billing/information\-sponsors/\#how\-the\-application\-process\-works](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/sponsorship-billing/information-sponsors/#how-the-application-process-works)

-   Sponsors must complete the [online application form](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_dg7icsLodwcOdeu) before the start of the term\. Sponsors who are unable to complete the online application can submit a paper [Sponsorship Third Party Billing Form](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/sponsorship_third_party_billing_form_2024.pdf) \(pdf\) and return it by fax to [604 822 5816](tel:6048225816)\. 
-   Sponsors can apply to support a student for as short as one term or over multiple years\. The duration of the sponsorship must be specified on the application form\. Sponsors with a multi\-year contract do not need to submit a new application every term or session\.
-   Sponsors who support a student for only one term only but later determine they can continue the sponsorship are asked to submit a new application\. Contracts do not automatically renew\. 
-   If you wish to sponsor a student for books and supplies in addition to tuition and student fees, UBC can help you to arrange this\. You can indicate this on the sponsorship application form, which will be forwarded to the appropriate department on your behalf\.
-   Once the Sponsorship Billing Office receives your form, they will update your account and let you know your next steps\.

### Application deadlines

Sponsors should submit their sponsorship billing applications by the dates below\. If you’re unable to apply before the deadlines, please contact the Sponsorship Billing Office\.

| Academic Session | Dates | Deadline |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Summer Session | May to August | April 1 |
| Winter Session Term 1 | September to December | August 1 |
| Winter Session Term 2 | January to April | November 1 |

## After you submit your sponsorship billing request[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/tuition\-fees/sponsorship\-billing/information\-sponsors/\#after\-you\-submit\-your\-sponsorship\-billing\-request](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/sponsorship-billing/information-sponsors/#after-you-submit-your-sponsorship-billing-request)

Once the Sponsorship Billing Office receives your application, they will update the student’s account within 2 to 3 business days and send a confirmation email to the student when the sponsorship is added\.

The office will also send you a copy of the invoice by email after the [add/drop deadline](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/course-change-dates/) of each term:

-   **Winter Session Term 1**: late September
-   **Winter Session Term 2**: late January
-   **Summer Session**: mid\-July

UBC will only issue invoice\(s\) for charges you have agreed to cover\. If you wish to make a change to the terms of your sponsor agreement for one or more students, please email [ubc\.sponsorship@ubc\.ca](mailto:ubc.sponsorship@ubc.ca) immediately\.

## Communication with students[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/tuition\-fees/sponsorship\-billing/information\-sponsors/\#communication\-with\-students](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/sponsorship-billing/information-sponsors/#communication-with-students)

As a sponsor, you will only receive an email if your application is refused or if the Sponsorship Billing Office has questions about the sponsorship details\.

If the conditions of your sponsorship include being updated of the student’s progress, or transcripts and other documents, you will need to ask the student to send them directly to you\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/tuition\-fees/sponsorship\-billing/information\-sponsors/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/sponsorship-billing/information-sponsors/#if-you-have-questions)

For more information, email the Sponsorship Billing Office at [ubc\.sponsorship@ubc\.ca](mailto:ubc.sponsorship@ubc.ca)\. Please be patient, as you may experience delays in email responses\.

To submit a form by fax, please use the fax number [604 822 5816](tel:6048225816)\.

title: Student loans
content_markdown:
Student loans are offered by the Canadian and US governments to help students pay for their post\-secondary education\.

If you’re a dual Canadian or American citizen, you may also be eligible to apply for Canada Student Loans through your home province\. 

If you have any residency affiliation through you or your parents to the province of Ontario, there may be an exception\. Please contact your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) for more information\.

## Eligibility to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/\#eligibility\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/#eligibility-to-apply)

Eligibility for student loans is based on many factors, including:

-   Residency requirement
-   Program eligibility
-   Financial need

### Types of loans

-   **[Full\-time students from BC](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/loans-full-time-british-columbia/)**  
    If you are a BC resident in UBC undergraduate or graduate studies, you may be eligible for a government student loan\.
-   **[Part\-time students from BC](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/part-time-funding-british-columbia/)**  
    Part\-time students who live in BC may be eligible for a government student loan\.
-   **[Full\-time students from other provinces](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/loans-full-time-other-provinces/)**  
    If you’re from a province or territory other than BC, you can apply to receive government student loan assistance\.
-   **[Part\-time students from other provinces](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/part-time-funding-out-province/)**  
    UBC students from a province or territory other than BC can apply for funding if they are in part\-time studies\.
-   **[Funding for US Students](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/)**  
    UBC students from the US can access Direct Loans\.
-   **[Loans for summer sessions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/loans-summer-sessions/)**  
    Find information about loan funding for summer courses\.

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/#additional-resources)

-   [Repaying my student loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/repaying-my-student-loans/)

For help with finances, registration, records, and more, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

title: Funding for US students
content_markdown:
UBC is a Title IV institution, which means eligible students can access United States \(US\) federal financial aid programs\.

Various sources of funding are available at UBC to US citizens and eligible non\-citizens, including Direct Loans, 529 Plans, private loans, and more\.

Eligibility varies for each type of funding and is based on many factors\. Please review the individual requirements for each funding source\.

## Direct Loans[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/\#direct\-loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/#direct-loans)

Eligible students and parents can borrow directly from the US Department of Education through the US Federal Direct Loan Program\. 

At UBC, the available types of Direct Loans include 

-   Direct Subsidized Loans
-   Direct Unsubsidized Loans
-   Parent and Grad PLUS Loans

[Get details](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-federal-direct-loan-program/)

## Alternative source of funding[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/\#alternative\-source\-of\-funding](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/#alternative-source-of-funding)

Eligible students may use [alternative funding sources](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/alternative-sources-funding-us/) such as 529 plans, AmeriCorps, and Veterans Affairs education benefits\.

If you’re a dual Canadian citizen, you may also be eligible to apply for [Canadian Student Loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/)\.

## Private loans[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/\#private\-loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/#private-loans)

If you are not eligible for Direct Loans, or need additional funding, [private US student loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-private-student-loans/) are available at UBC through various lenders\.

If you have questions about your funding eligibility or assessment, please contact an Enrolment Services Advisor\.

title: Alternative sources of funding for US students
content_markdown:
## Funding options for US students[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/alternative\-sources\-funding\-us/\#funding\-options\-for\-us\-students](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/alternative-sources-funding-us/#funding-options-for-us-students)

Beyond Direct Loans, UBC offers a range of funding options for US students, including: 

-   Americorps
-   State funding
-   Qualified Tuition Plans \(529 Plans\)
-   Veterans Affairs

## Americorps[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/alternative\-sources\-funding\-us/\#americorps](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/alternative-sources-funding-us/#americorps)

Students who have completed voluntary activities for AmeriCorps may be eligible for an Education Award\. UBC is a qualified institution for certifying Americorps Education Awards\.

To determine your eligibility for educational benefits or request disbursements \(payments\) from your education awards, please log into your [My Americorps account](https://my.americorps.gov/) or call Americorps directly at [1 800 942 2677](tel:18009422677)\.

### Using your benefits at UBC

Once you have applied for your AmeriCorps benefits through your [My AmeriCorps account](https://my.americorps.gov/mp/login.do), UBC will receive an email from AmeriCorps to complete a Cost of Attendance for you and confirm your enrolment\.

AmeriCorps funds are sent directly to UBC and are applied to your tuition account\. If you have a Canadian bank account, consider setting up [direct deposit](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/setting-up-your-direct-deposit/)\. Direct deposit allows any funds remaining after tuition and student fees are paid to be deposited directly into your bank account\.

## State Funding[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/alternative\-sources\-funding\-us/\#state\-funding](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/alternative-sources-funding-us/#state-funding)

UBC can provide you with a Cost of Attendance letter and proof of enrolment for a number of state\-funded plans, including:

-   Alaska Education Loans
-   Rhode Island Higher Education Assistance Authority \(RIHEAA\)
-   Vermont Student Assistance Corporation \(VSAC\)

For RIHEAA and VSAC state funding, email [usloans\.inquiry@ubc\.ca](mailto:usloans.inquiry@ubc.ca) to confirm that your electronic loan or enrolment request has been received\. Be sure to provide your name and UBC student number\.

For Alaska Education Loans, visit [Enrolment Services](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) to get your paperwork signed\. 

If you’re eligible for student loans or funding from a state not listed above, email [usloans\.inquiry@ubc\.ca](mailto:usloans.inquiry@ubc.ca) with your name and UBC student number\.

## Qualified Tuition Plans \(529 Plans\)[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/alternative\-sources\-funding\-us/\#qualified\-tuition\-plans\-529\-plans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/alternative-sources-funding-us/#qualified-tuition-plans-529-plans)

UBC is an eligible institution for the use of 529 Plans\. Contact your 529 Plan provider for information on how to withdraw and use funds\. 

Funds are usually provided via a USD cheque\. Depending on the provider, you may choose to have funds sent to you, or directly to UBC\. If possible, request that your plan provider send your funds to you\.

 If your provider requires a Cost of Attendance letter, please contact [usloans\.inquiry@ubc\.ca](mailto:usloans.inquiry@ubc.ca)\. 

Please ask your plan provider to include your full name and UBC student number on the cheque**\.**

### If you’re studying at UBC Vancouver

You can drop off your cheque in\-person at the [Advising Center in Brock Hall](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) during regular business hours, or mail it to the following address:

Student Support and Advising, Enrolment Services  
1206\-1874 East Mall, Brock Hall  
Vancouver, BC V6T 1Z1

Please write “Attention: External awards processing team” on the front of the mailing envelope\.

### If you’re studying at UBC Okanagan 

Please mail cheques directly to the following address:

Enrolment Services Advising  
214 University Centre, 3272 University Way  
Kelowna BC, V1V 1V7 Canada

Please write “Attention: External Awards Processing Team” on the front of the mailing envelope\.

## Veterans Affairs[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/alternative\-sources\-funding\-us/\#veterans\-affairs](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/alternative-sources-funding-us/#veterans-affairs)

The Veterans Affairs program is under review until further notice\. If you were previously approved under Veterans Affairs and are actively registered at UBC, your benefits will be maintained\.

If you are a new applicant, please email [usloans\.inquiry@ubc\.ca](mailto:usloans.inquiry@ubc.ca) with your Certificate of Eligibility and intended program of study, and we will review your application\.

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/alternative\-sources\-funding\-us/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/alternative-sources-funding-us/#additional-resources)
