title: US Loans FAQ
content_markdown:
## Funding amounts[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/us\-loans\-faq/\#funding\-amounts](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-loans-faq/#funding-amounts)

**

How much US Direct Loan funding am I eligible for?

**

You are eligible to borrow up to the full amount of your Cost of Attendance\. Additional funding from other resources, such as scholarships and loans you may be receiving will be subtracted from the total amount you can borrow\. The Winter Session Cost of Attendance, including living costs, typically ranges from $70,000 to $85,000 for undergraduate international students at UBC\. Your maximum funding also depends on your degree and year level\. UBC can not certify you for funding that exceeds either your Cost of Attendance or the [loan maximums](https://studentaid.gov/understand-aid/types/loans/subsidized-unsubsidized#how-much-can-i-borrow) set by the US Department of Education\.

To learn how your funding is calculated, read about [US Direct Loan funding amounts](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-direct-loan-funding-amounts/)\.

Use the UBC [cost calculator](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/cost/) to plan your first\-year costs\.

**

Do Direct Loan maximums apply to each term or each year?

**

The [loan maximums](https://studentaid.gov/understand-aid/types/loans/subsidized-unsubsidized#how-much-can-i-borrow) set by the US Department of Education apply to the academic year, which is September to August of the following year\.

If you use the maximum amount in Direct Subsidized and Direct Unsubsidized Loan funding for the Winter Session \(September to April period\) and then decide to take summer courses, you are not eligible for any further Direct Subsidized and Direct Unsubsidized loan funding for the Summer Session \(May to August period\)\.

If you do not use the entire annual loan limit during the Winter Session, you can still be considered for the remainder of the amount for the rest of the academic year or Summer Session\.

## Funding eligibility[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/us\-loans\-faq/\#funding\-eligibility](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-loans-faq/#funding-eligibility)

**

What type of funding can I apply for?

**

You can apply for Direct Loans, which may include Direct Subsidized and Direct Unsubsidized Loans, and Grad PLUS or Parent PLUS funding, depending on your personal eligibility\. Undergraduate students may be eligible for Direct Subsidized funding, while graduate students are only eligible for Direct Unsubsidized funding\.

If you are not eligible for Direct Loans, you have the option of applying for private loans through [Sallie Mae](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/sallie-mae-private-loans/)\.

**

Can I get Pell Grants or Perkins Loans?

**

UBC is considered a foreign school and US students attending foreign institutions are not eligible to receive these types of Federal aid\.

**

Can I receive loan funding for Distance Education?

**

Starting in 2023 Summer Session, students participating in any ineligible courses, such as [Online, Hybrid, Multi\-Access](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/course-modes-delivery/), or any type of course or part of a course which is taught online, will lose Direct Loan eligibility for the remainder of their degree\.

Under the temporary COVID\-19 Relief Bill, US students were previously allowed to take online courses or courses with online components until the end of 2022/23 Winter Session Term 2 \(Sep 2022 to Apr 2023\)\. This was applicable to courses completed since Sun, Mar 1, 2020 without it negatively impacting students’ eligibility for Direct Loan funding\.

**

Am I eligible for a US Loan while I’m on exchange?

**

If you’re thinking about going on exchange and are eligible for US Direct Loans, contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) to understand your financial options before you apply for exchange\.

Check the US [Federal School Code Lists](https://fsapartners.ed.gov/knowledge-center/library/resource-type/Federal%20School%20Code%20Lists) \(under “Foreign Country”\) to confirm that your exchange university is also eligible to provide Title IV funds\.

If you choose to do an exchange at a school in the US, you could lose your eligibility for Direct Loans for the rest of your program\. If you require federal loans, it’s not recommended to go on exchange to a US school\.

If your partner university is Title IV and **not located in the US**, UBC can assess you for Direct Loans while you’re on exchange\.

If your partner university is **not Title IV**, you will not be eligible to receive Direct Loans for the period of your exchange\. You may want to consider private loans like [Sallie Mae](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/sallie-mae-private-loans/) in this case\.

**

Can I receive funding for Jump Start?

**

Yes, if you are participating in Jumpstart and would like to include the fee in your US loan assessment, please email your request to [usloans\.inquiry@ubc\.ca](mailto:usloans.inquiry@ubc.ca) with your name and UBC student number\. The registration fee will then be included when your Cost of Attendance is calculated\.

**

Am I eligible for a US Loan while I’m on Co\-op?

**

If you’re thinking about doing your Co\-op in the US, please connect with an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) first to fully understand the financial implications for your future Direct Loan eligibility\. Co\-op placements in the US may make you ineligible for future Direct Loan funding\.

If you’re a graduate student, please check with an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) to confirm if your Co\-op is loan\-eligible\.

## Application and funding timelines[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/us\-loans\-faq/\#application\-and\-funding\-timelines](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-loans-faq/#application-and-funding-timelines)

**

When should I apply for my Direct Loan?

**

You’re recommended to apply for your Direct Loan at least 6 weeks before the start of the term to make sure your funding is available by the first week of classes\.

Follow [step\-by\-step instructions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/#applying-for-a-us-direct-loan) and avoid delays to your application\.

**

When will I receive my Direct Loan \(Subsidized, Unsubsidized or Parent/Grad PLUS\) funds?

**

Your Direct Loan will pay towards your tuition and student fees on the [disbursement date](https://studentaid.gov/help-center/answers/article/what-is-disbursement-date) listed on your assessment letter from UBC\. If there is any money leftover from your loan after your fees are paid, you can receive this money through [direct deposit](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/setting-up-your-direct-deposit/)\.

Please ensure your direct deposit details are up\-to\-date to receive your refund in your bank account\. This funding will be available a few business days after the disbursement date\.

**

When will I receive my US Private Loans?

**

UBC releases your loan funding at the start of the term\. It takes up to 6 weeks to process a US Private Loan, such as the Sallie Mae private loan\. You’re recommended to apply at least 6 weeks before the start of term to ensure you receive your funding for the start of the session\.

**

Can I receive my loan funding before school starts?

**

If you’ve been approved for a Direct Loan, the earliest time your loan funding will be available is the first week of classes\.

You are expected to have some savings to cover housing deposits and other initial costs related to your studies\. If you apply for your Direct Loans at least 6 weeks before the start of the term, you will receive your funding before any late fees are assessed\.

Use the [UBC cost calculator](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/cost/) to plan your first\-year costs\.

## After receiving a Direct Loan[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/us\-loans\-faq/\#after\-receiving\-a\-direct\-loan](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-loans-faq/#after-receiving-a-direct-loan)

**

Can I use audited courses or courses not for credit towards my registration requirement?

**

Any [audited courses](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/auditing-courses/) do not count towards the 6\-credit requirement\.

Direct Subsidized Loans are only available to undergraduate students registered in at least 6 credits per term\. 

Direct Unsubsidized Loans are available for undergraduate and graduate students registered in at least 6 credits per term\.

**

Can I cancel my Direct Loan?

**

You can cancel or reduce your Direct Loan within 30 days from the [disbursement date](https://studentaid.gov/help-center/answers/article/what-is-disbursement-date) by emailing [usloans\.inquiry@ubc\.ca](mailto:usloans.inquiry@ubc.ca)\.

After 30 days, you must contact your lender to make arrangements to return all or a portion of your loan\.

**

How do I file my taxes in the US while I’m studying in Canada?

**

As a Canadian institution, UBC does not issue American tax documents \(e\.g\., Form 1098\-T\)\. However, UBC does issue a form called the T2022 that [can be downloaded](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/downloading-your-tax-forms/) through the UBC Official Documents tool on Workday\. You can use this form or provide it to your accountant for the purposes of filing your taxes in the US\. It is recommended that you file taxes to Canada while you are studying at UBC\.

Learn more about [filing your taxes in Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/filing-taxes-canada/)\.

**

Where do I go to get my In\-School Deferment or Continuation of Interest\-Free Status form filled out?

**

If you have an assigned Enrolment Services Advisor, they can help you complete your In\-School Deferment or Continuation of Interest\-Free Status form\. Find your advisor by [logging into Workday](https://myworkday.ubc.ca/) and selecting the “Support” tab in the Academics app\.

If you don’t have an assigned advisor, you can contact one by calling [604 822 9836](tel:6048229836) or submit your question through the [online form](https://www.askme.ubc.ca/form/s/)\.

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/us\-loans\-faq/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-loans-faq/#additional-resources)

-   [Loans for US students](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/)
-   [Resources for students with US loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/resources-us-loans/)
-   [US Direct Loan funding amounts](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-direct-loan-funding-amounts/)
-   [US Policies and Consumer Information \(pdf\)](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/us_funding_policies_and_consumer_info.pdf)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/us\-loans\-faq/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-loans-faq/#if-you-have-questions)

For help with finances, registration, records, and more, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

title: Loans for full-time students from British Columbia
content_markdown:
## About BC student loans[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/loans\-full\-time\-british\-columbia/\#about\-bc\-student\-loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/loans-full-time-british-columbia/#about-bc-student-loans)

If you are a resident of British Columbia enrolled in full or part\-time undergraduate or graduate studies at UBC, you may be eligible for government student loan assistance\. StudentAid BC funding exists to supplement, not replace, funds available to students through individual and family financial resources, savings, and income\.

A full\-time loan application evaluates a student’s income and other financial resources against the costs of post\-secondary study, including educational costs and typical living costs associated with a moderate standard of living\. 

Since StudentAid BC funding is intended to supplement other available financial resources, federal and provincial student financial assistance programs have weekly and lifetime [in\-study payment\-free](https://studentaidbc.ca/maintain/when-payments-are-not-required) funding maximums\. Not all students receive the [maximum amount](https://studentaidbc.ca/help-centre/applying-loans/maximum-funding-limits)\. Refer to [StudentAid BC](https://studentaidbc.ca/) for more information\. 

The province of British Columbia offers Canada\-BC integrated loans to students studying full\-time\. An integrated student loan has two lenders, the governments of Canada and British Columbia\. However, it is administered as a single loan, which streamlines service delivery as students sign a joint federal\-provincial loan agreement and have a single point of contact for managing their loans\. Residents of BC apply for a student loan through StudentAid BC\.

If you’re a part\-time student living in BC, please review your specific [eligibility requirements and assessments\.](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/part-time-funding-british-columbia/#part-time-funding-coverage)

### Grant funding

Some students who apply for student loans will be eligible for grant funding, which does not have to be repaid\. Your eligibility is based on your application\.  
  
Refer to StudentAid BC to view a [list of available programs](https://studentaidbc.ca/explore/grants-scholarships) to support students with the cost of post\-secondary education\.

### Dependent and Independent Status Residency requirement

Students are classified as dependent or independent to determine residency and financial need\. Please refer to [Student Aid BC’s residency requirements](https://studentaidbc.ca/apply/eligibility#residency) to determine your eligibility\.

## Before you apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/loans\-full\-time\-british\-columbia/\#before\-you\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/loans-full-time-british-columbia/#before-you-apply)

Watch the following YouTube videos created by StudentAid BC to learn about the different types of financial aid available, basic eligibility requirements, application deadlines, processing times, and how to receive your funding\. Additionally, find out about loan repayment and when students qualify for [in\-study payment\-free funding\.](https://studentaidbc.ca/maintain/when-payments-are-not-required)

-   [What is StudentAid BC?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6cEkB7Piu4Q)
-   [Before you apply to StudentAid BC](https://youtu.be/_6Ed3GC98vs)
-   [How to create your StudentAid BC account](https://youtu.be/IEM4gn9iolA)
-   [How much StudentAid BC funding can I get](https://youtu.be/E3D3hyu2dxU)?
-   [How repayment works for StudentAid BC loans](https://youtu.be/GLGPd1ECBcU)

All undergraduate students in a degree program have a dedicated [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) \(ES Advisor\) to help navigate the loan application process\. If you don’t have an assigned advisor, they’re still available to help\.

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/loans\-full\-time\-british\-columbia/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/loans-full-time-british-columbia/#how-to-apply)

Apply for a loan at least 2 months before classes start to receive your funding at the beginning of the term, or up to 6 weeks before the end of your study period\. 

To apply for BC full\-time funding, please follow the steps below:

1.  Set up your [BC Services Card](https://id.gov.bc.ca/account/) account and app if you have not already done so, and log into the [StudentAid BC](https://studentaidbc.ca/sabc-home-page) website for your online application\.
2.  Determine your [course load](https://tools.students.ubc.ca/course-load-guide/) and loan\-eligible study dates\. If you’re unsure, speak to your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.  
      
    If you are a student with a Permanent Disability \(PD\) or Persistent or Prolonged Disability \(PPD\), you must establish PD or PPD status with StudentAid BC to be considered full\-time for government student loans with at least 40% of a full\-time course load\.
3.  Find your program and study dates from the application through [StudentAid BC](https://studentaidbc.ca/sabc-home-page)\.  
      
    If you cannot locate your program or study dates, check the box indicating that your program or study dates are not listed, and proceed until you submit your application\. This will trigger a Program Information Request \(PIR\) to UBC to confirm your program details before your application can be further processed after your submission\.
4.  Submit your application\. You will be asked to provide your consent to the Canada Revenue Agency \(CRA\) and complete the StudentAid BC Declaration\. This allows StudentAid BC to verify the information in your application\.
5.  Monitor your online application for next steps\.   
      
    If applicable, you will need to have your parent\(s\) and/or spouse provide information to StudentAid BC\. This may require them to set up their BC Services Card account and app\.
6.  ​​ Review your Notice of Assessment \(NOA\) on your [StudentAid BC dashboard](https://studentaidbc.ca/dashboard/login) when available\. The NOA will describe:
    -   The type of funding you are eligible to receive
    -   The amount of funding approved
    -   When you will receive the funding
7.  Submit the online [Master Student Financial Assistance Agreement](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/programs/msfaa.html) \(MSFAA\)\.  
      
    You are required to complete an online MSFAA if you are applying for a full\-time student loan for the first time or have taken a leave from your studies for 2 or more years\. 
8.  **Accept your Notice of Assessment** in a timely manner\. This is required before your enrolment can be confirmed\.
9.  UBC will be prompted to confirm your enrolment by StudentAid BC\. UBC will contact you by email if your enrolment cannot be confirmed\.    
      
    Continue to monitor your application status and inbox for notifications from StudentAid BC and UBC\. You are strongly encouraged to log into your [StudentAid BC account](https://studentaidbc.ca/dashboard/login) to view updates, changes to your assessment if applicable, and communications from the provincial lender\. 

If you are receiving a full\-time loan, you are also recommended to apply for the [UBC Bursary](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/)\.

## Maintain your eligibility[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/loans\-full\-time\-british\-columbia/\#maintain\-your\-eligibility](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/loans-full-time-british-columbia/#maintain-your-eligibility)

To continue being eligible for student loans, you must meet all of the following requirements:

-   You are enrolled in an eligible program of study\. 
-   You are making progress in your studies and are in good academic standing in each period of post\-secondary study\.
-   You are maintaining full\-time student status\. This means you are enrolled in and attending a minimum percentage of a full course load\.
    -   Undergraduate students: Consult the [Course Load Guide](https://tools.students.ubc.ca/course-load-guide/) for more details\.
    -   Graduate students: You must be registered and paying full\-time fees in each term that you receive loan funding
    -   Program exceptions: LLMT, LLMCL and MFA in Creative Writing\. Consult the [Course Load Guide](https://tools.students.ubc.ca/course-load-guide/) for more details\.

## Student loan interest[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/loans\-full\-time\-british\-columbia/\#student\-loan\-interest](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/loans-full-time-british-columbia/#student-loan-interest)

There is no interest assessed on the provincial portion of your student loan\. Effective Apr 1, 2023, the Government of Canada has permanently eliminated the accumulation of interest on the federal portion currently being repaid\. You continue to be responsible for paying any interest that may have accrued on your loan before Apr 1, 2023, except during the period of April 2021 to March 2023, when federal interest was waived\.

You are not required to make payments until you’ve been out of school for 6 months\.

If you return to school with a full\-time student loan at a designated post\-secondary institution before this 6\-month grace period ends, the interest \(if any\) that has accumulated since your last study end date will be waived and you will be in [payment\-free status](https://studentaidbc.ca/maintain/when-payments-are-not-required) for your new study term\.

If you return full\-time to school at a designated post\-secondary institution but do not plan on applying for full\-time loans, you will need to apply for in\-study payment\-free status through your loan provider for your previous loans to be in payment\-free status\.

Being in [payment\-free status](https://studentaidbc.ca/maintain/when-payments-are-not-required) means you are in a “funded term” whether you have new loans or not\. If you withdraw or have an unsuccessful term, it may affect your eligibility for further assistance\.

## Automatic tuition deferral[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/loans\-full\-time\-british\-columbia/\#automatic\-tuition\-deferral](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/loans-full-time-british-columbia/#automatic-tuition-deferral)

Eligible graduate and undergraduate students will have fees deferred for one month after the tuition fee deadline in September, January, or May\.

You are eligible for automatic tuition deferral if you meet both requirements: 

-   You are eligible for funding to pay your tuition and fees\.
-   You submit a complete full time loan application by the following dates:
    -   Jul 31 for a loan beginning in September \(Winter session Term 1\)
    -   Nov 15 for a loan beginning in January \(Winter session Term 2\)
    -   Apr 15 for a loan beginning in May \(Summer session\)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/loans\-full\-time\-british\-columbia/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/loans-full-time-british-columbia/#if-you-have-questions)

For help with finances, registration, records, and more, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

title: Loans for summer sessions
content_markdown:
## Full\-time funding[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/loans\-summer\-sessions/\#full\-time\-funding](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/loans-summer-sessions/#full-time-funding)

Students enrolled in Summer Session courses at UBC are eligible for student loan funding if they meet the eligibility criteria for their degree type\. It is your responsibility to register in a loan\-eligible course load\.

If you currently receive loans, please contact your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) to ensure registration changes will not impact your loan eligibility\.

### Undergraduate students

Unlike Winter Session courses, Summer Session courses start and end at a variety of times and can be as short as 3 weeks in length\. To be eligible for [BC full\-time loans](https://studentaidbc.ca/sabc-home-page) during the Summer Session, you must meet all of the following criteria:

-   Be registered in at least 9 credits in most programs \(audited, wait\-listed, and withdrawn courses do not count\)
-   Be registered in a study period that is at least 12 consecutive weeks in length
-   Have no breaks longer than 10 percent of the study period

Eligibility requirements can differ across provinces\. Please consult with an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) if you have questions\.

### Graduate students

Most graduate programs at UBC do not have a minimum course load requirement\.

In order to be eligible for student loans, UBC graduate students must meet both of the following requirements:

-   Pay full\-time fees in each term that they receive loan funding
-   Have an “In Progress” status in their program of study for each term that they receive loan funding

This does not apply to any program that requires credit registration\.

## Part\-time funding[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/loans\-summer\-sessions/\#part\-time\-funding](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/loans-summer-sessions/#part-time-funding)

If you are not taking courses that match the full\-time criteria, you may be eligible for a part\-time student loan\.

Learn more about part\-time funding for [BC students](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/part-time-funding-british-columbia/) or [out of province students](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/part-time-funding-out-province/)\. If you have any questions about the application, contact your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

## Important dates for summer funding[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/loans\-summer\-sessions/\#important\-dates\-for\-summer\-funding](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/loans-summer-sessions/#important-dates-for-summer-funding)

| **Dates** | **Details** |
| --- | --- |
| Wed, Apr 15, 2026 | Apply for a full\-time summer student loan by this date to ensure that you receive your loan funding in time for [Summer Bursaries](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/), the summer tuition deadline, and to receive a deferral on your tuition fees\. |
| Fri, May 1, 2026 | Summer Bursary applications open\. Learn how to [apply to the UBC Bursary Program](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/applying-to-the-ubc-bursary-program/) in Workday\. |
| Mon, Jun 1, 2026 | Summer Bursary applications close\. |
| Course change date | This date varies depending on the start date and the length of your class\. Please refer to the information highlighted on the [Course Schedule](https://courses.students.ubc.ca/) or learn more about [course change dates](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/course-change-dates/)\. |

title: Part-time funding for British Columbia students
content_markdown:
## Part\-time funding coverage[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/part\-time\-funding\-british\-columbia/\#part\-time\-funding\-coverage](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/part-time-funding-british-columbia/#part-time-funding-coverage)

The part\-time student loan program covers:

-   Tuition
-   Books
-   Supplies
-   Transportation
-   Child care \(up to the funding maximums\)

Part\-time funding does not cover living costs\. If you need additional financial support for living costs, please contact your [Enrolment Services Advisors](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) to discuss your financial plan\.

## Eligibility to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/part\-time\-funding\-british\-columbia/\#eligibility\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/part-time-funding-british-columbia/#eligibility-to-apply)

Loans are available for students studying part\-time at UBC\. To be considered a part\-time student, you must be registered in 20% to 59% of the full\-time load listed for your program, which you can check on the [Course Load Guide](https://tools.students.ubc.ca/course-load-guide/)\.

Not all programs are eligible for part\-time funding\. You must be in a program approved for full\-time student loans\. Contact your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) to check if your program is approved\. If you don’t have an assigned advisor, they’re still available to help\.

To apply for part\-time student financial assistance from StudentAid BC, you must be a resident of British Columbia \(BC\)\. 

You are considered a resident of BC if you meet one of the following requirements:

-   You lived in BC for 12 continuous months before starting your studies, excluding any time spent in full\-time post\-secondary education\.  
     
-   You are an independent permanent resident or designated as a protected person living in BC at the time of your application, you will spend your study period in BC, and you have not lived in any province for 12 continuous months before your study start date\.  
      
    For example, if you are an independent student who arrived in Canada as a permanent resident less than 12 months before the start date of classes and intend to study in BC, you would be considered a resident of BC for student financial assistance purposes\.

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/part\-time\-funding\-british\-columbia/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/part-time-funding-british-columbia/#how-to-apply)

You should apply for a loan at least 2 months before classes start to receive your funding at the beginning of the term, or up to 6 weeks before the end of your study period\. 

To apply for BC part\-time funding, follow the steps below:

1.  Set up your [B\.C\. Services Card](https://id.gov.bc.ca/account/) account and app if you have not already done so, and log into [StudentAid BC](https://studentaidbc.ca/sabc-home-page) for your online application\.
2.  Determine your [course load](https://tools.students.ubc.ca/course-load-guide/) and loan\-eligible study dates\. If you’re unsure, speak to your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.  
      
    If you are a student with a Permanent Disability \(PD\) or Persistent or Prolonged Disability \(PPD\) and you are taking a 40% course load or higher, you are encouraged to apply for a [full\-time loan](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/loans-full-time-british-columbia/), as a part\-time loan does not cover living costs\.
3.  Find your program and study dates from the application through [StudentAid BC](https://studentaidbc.ca/sabc-home-page)\.  
      
    If you cannot locate your program or study dates, check the box indicating that your program or study dates are not listed, and proceed until you submit your application\. This will trigger a Program Information Request \(PIR\) to UBC to confirm your program details before your application can be further processed after your submission\.
4.  Submit your application\. You will be asked to provide your consent to the Canada Revenue Agency \(CRA\) and complete the StudentAid BC Declaration\. This allows StudentAid BC to verify the information in your application\.
5.  Monitor your online application for next steps\. Once your application has been assessed, you will be able to review your Notice of Assessment, which describes:
    -   The amount of funding approved
    -   When you will receive the funding
6.  Submit the [Master Student Financial Assistance Agreement](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/programs/msfaa.html) \(MSFAA\) and accept your Notice of Assessment **as soon as possible**\. Both are required before your enrolment can be confirmed\.  
      
    You are required to complete an online MSFAA if you are applying for a part\-time student loan for the first time or have taken a leave from your studies for 2 or more years\.
7.  UBC will be prompted to confirm your enrolment by StudentAid BC\.
8.  Continue to monitor your application status and inbox for notifications from StudentAid BC and UBC\. You are strongly encouraged to log into your [StudentAid BC](https://studentaidbc.ca/dashboard/login) account to view updates, changes to your assessment if applicable, and communications from the provincial lender\.  
      
    UBC will contact you by email if your enrolment cannot be confirmed\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/part\-time\-funding\-british\-columbia/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/part-time-funding-british-columbia/#if-you-have-questions)

For help with finances, registration, records, and more, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

title: Part-time funding for out-of-province students
content_markdown:
## Part\-time funding coverage[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/part\-time\-funding\-out\-province/\#part\-time\-funding\-coverage](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/part-time-funding-out-province/#part-time-funding-coverage)

The part\-time student loan program covers:

-   Tuition
-   Books
-   Supplies
-   Transportation
-   Child care \(up to the funding maximums\)

Part\-time funding does not cover living costs\. If you need additional financial support for living costs, please contact your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) to discuss your financial plan\.

## Eligibility to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/part\-time\-funding\-out\-province/\#eligibility\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/part-time-funding-out-province/#eligibility-to-apply)

Loans are available for students studying part\-time at UBC\. To be considered a part\-time student, you must be registered in 20% to 59% of the full\-time load listed for your program, which you can check on the [Course load guide](https://tools.students.ubc.ca/course-load-guide/)\.

Not all programs are eligible for part\-time funding\. You must be in a program approved for full\-time student loans\. Contact your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) to check if your program is approved\. If you don’t have an assigned advisor, they’re still available to help\.

If you are a student with an established disability status with your loan province and you are taking a 40% course load or higher, you are encouraged to apply for [a full\-time loan](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/loans-full-time-other-provinces/), as a part\-time loan does not cover living costs\.

## Where you should apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/part\-time\-funding\-out\-province/\#where\-you\-should\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/part-time-funding-out-province/#where-you-should-apply)

Your province or territory of residence is typically where you lived for 12 continuous months excluding months of full\-time post\-secondary study before attending UBC, depending on whether you are a dependent or an independent student\.

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/part\-time\-funding\-out\-province/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/part-time-funding-out-province/#how-to-apply)

1.  Download the application form based on your province or territory of residence:  
    -   [Alberta Student Aid](http://studentaid.alberta.ca/resources/applications-and-forms/)
    -   [Manitoba Student Aid](https://www.edu.gov.mb.ca/msa/pt-application-status.html)
    -   [Newfoundland & Labrador Student Aid](https://www.gov.nl.ca/education/studentaid/parttime/)
    -   [Nova Scotia Student Assistance](https://novascotia.ca/studentassistance/Apply/New/PartTimeStudies.asp)   
    -   [Ontario Student Assistance Program](https://www.ontario.ca/page/osap-ontario-student-assistance-program) 
    -   [Prince Edward Island Student Financial Services](https://www.princeedwardisland.ca/en/information/workforce-and-advanced-learning/canada-student-grants-and-loans-for-part-time-students)
    -   [Saskatchewan Student Aid](https://www.saskatchewan.ca/residents/education-and-learning/saskatchewan-student-aid/student-loans-and-grants/apply-for-student-aid)
    -   All other provinces and territories must apply through [National Student Loans](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/education/student-loan/forms.html#h2.7)\.             
         
2.  Fill out your application form and contact [Enrolment Services](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) for instructions on submitting your part\-time student loan application\. You will receive an assessment from the loan provider detailing what kind of funding you’ll receive and when you’ll receive it\.

Your funding will be sent to you through direct deposit by your loan provider after your enrolment has been confirmed by UBC\.

## Students with previous part\-time loans[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/part\-time\-funding\-out\-province/\#students\-with\-previous\-part\-time\-loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/part-time-funding-out-province/#students-with-previous-part-time-loans)

If you have a previous part\-time government student loan and are returning to part\-time or full\-time study, you do not need to begin repayment\. However, you must inform your lender that you are returning to study\. 

Please review the information for [students with previous loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/student-loan-interest/)\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/part\-time\-funding\-out\-province/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/part-time-funding-out-province/#if-you-have-questions)

For help with finances, registration, records, and more, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

title: Repaying my student loans
content_markdown:
## About the non\-repayment period[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/repaying\-my\-student\-loans/\#about\-the\-non\-repayment\-period](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/repaying-my-student-loans/#about-the-non-repayment-period)

The 6 months after you leave full\-time study is called your non\-repayment period\. During this period, the interest on your loan may accumulate, depending on your loan provider, but you are not required to make payments\.

### What to expect

Make sure your lenders have your current contact information\. If your loan involves the National Student Loan Service Centre \(NSLSC\), which is used in all parts of Canada except Nunavut, Quebec, and the Northwest Territories, you will be emailed an invitation to log into your [NSLSC secure account](https://protege-secure.csnpe-nslsc.canada.ca/en/public/sign-in-method) to find details on your repayment\. This includes the amount you owe, when and how to make payments, and your rate of interest\. If you don’t receive an email, contact them to ensure they have your latest email information\. If you’re dealing with multiple lenders, it’s your responsibility to ensure you communicate and stay up to date with each one\.

The non\-repayment period is a good time to review your payment information and modify the terms if you need to\. After repayment begins, you will also be able to contact your lender to discuss or modify your repayment terms\.

You can still make payments during the non\-repayment period, even though it is not required\. This is a way to pay down your loan principal and reduce the amount of interest that you will be charged, if applicable\. Contact your lender\(s\) to have a consolidation agreement sent to you and to arrange early payments\.

## About repayment[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/repaying\-my\-student\-loans/\#about\-repayment](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/repaying-my-student-loans/#about-repayment)

After your 6\-month grace period ends, you will automatically enter repayment, and payments will be withdrawn from your bank account at the end of each month, unless you indicate otherwise\.

The date you leave full\-time study is the date you last attended school, not the date of your graduation ceremony\. If you withdraw part\-way through your study period, you will enter repayment 6 months from the date of your withdrawal\.

If you were previously a full\-time student and are now returning to part\-time study, you will enter repayment 6 months after leaving full\-time study\. You may be eligible for [part\-time student loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/part-time-funding-british-columbia/), if you need further financial assistance\.

### Monthly repayments

To find out the amount of your monthly payments, check your Consolidation Agreement\(s\)\. You’ll receive one in the mail from each of your lenders about 5 months after the date you complete or leave full\-time study\. The Consolidation Agreement outlines your loan repayment details, including: your balance owing, expected monthly payments, the start date of repayment, the length of repayment, and interest rate options\. You can also use the [CanLearn Loan Repayment Estimator](http://tools.canlearn.ca/cslgs-scpse/cln-cln/crp-lrc/af.nlindex-eng.do) to find out how much your payments will be ahead of time\.

### Repayment interest information

Depending on your provincial or territorial loan provider, you may or may not be charged interest during repayment\. Learn more on the [National Student Loans Service Centre webpage](https://www.csnpe-nslsc.canada.ca/en/stages-of-a-loan) or through your loan provider\.

### Repayment period

A Canada Student Loan is normally paid off over a repayment period of 9\.5 years\. If your monthly payments are too high to manage, the repayment period for your Canada Student Loan or BC Student Loan can potentially be increased up to 14\.5 years\. Contact the [National Student Loans Service Centre](https://protege-secure.csnpe-nslsc.canada.ca/en/public/contact/contact-us) \(NSLSC\) for more information\.

If you’re able to afford increased monthly payments, paying off your loans as quickly as possible will decrease the overall amount of interest that you will pay, if applicable\. You are also able to make lump sum payments at any time without penalty\.

### Repayment for graduate and unclassified students

If you’re returning to UBC for graduate studies, you must be paying full\-time fees as a graduate student to qualify for student loans or payment\-free and interest\-free status\.

Unclassified students can receive student loan funding or interest\-free status for a maximum of 52 weeks if they are registered in 60 percent of a full\-time course load and taking courses as prerequisites to enter into a loan\-eligible program\.

You can either apply for [government student loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/) or [interest\-free status](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/student-loan-interest/) federally or through your home province\.

## Help with repayments[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/repaying\-my\-student\-loans/\#help\-with\-repayments](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/repaying-my-student-loans/#help-with-repayments)

If you have trouble with repayment, [browse available options](https://www.csnpe-nslsc.canada.ca/en/repaying-your-loan/loan-repayment-options) on the National Student Loans Service Centre website\.

## Repaying US loans[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/repaying\-my\-student\-loans/\#repaying\-us\-loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/repaying-my-student-loans/#repaying-us-loans)

Read the repayment information on the [US Department of Education website](https://studentaid.gov/manage-loans/repayment) for complete details on the repayment process for students with US loans\.

Repayment for Parent PLUS and Graduate PLUS loans begins on the date the loan is fully paid out\.

If you withdraw part way through your study period, your repayment start date will be based on the date of your withdrawal and not the original term end date\.

When you enter repayment you’ll be required to complete [exit counselling](https://studentaid.gov/exit-counseling/)\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/repaying\-my\-student\-loans/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/repaying-my-student-loans/#if-you-have-questions)

For help with finances, registration, records, and more, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

title: Student loan interest
content_markdown:
## Keep your student loan payment\-free and interest\-free[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/student\-loan\-interest/\#keep\-your\-student\-loan\-payment\-free\-and\-interest\-free](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/student-loan-interest/#keep-your-student-loan-payment-free-and-interest-free)

If you had a previous loan, you must notify your lender that you have returned to your studies to keep your student loan interest\-free and prevent your loan from entering repayment\.

If you do not notify your lenders, your loans may begin to build interest and you will [enter repayment\.](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/repaying-my-student-loans/)

### Notifying your lenders

Notify your lenders as soon as possible for each new eligible study period\.

To find out if you are a part\-time or full\-time student and if you are registered in an eligible course load for your loans, visit the [Course Load Guide](https://tools.students.ubc.ca/course-load-guide/)\.

Your lenders will automatically be notified of your return to study only if one of the following happens: 

-   You submit a payment\-free or interest\-free request to the same province, lender, or loan program as last year\.
-   You apply for a new student loan and receive funding before you enter repayment from the same province, lender, or loan program as last year\.

## Students with full\-time Canadian government funding[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/student\-loan\-interest/\#students\-with\-full\-time\-canadian\-government\-funding](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/student-loan-interest/#students-with-full-time-canadian-government-funding)

Complete the following steps for your province or territory to notify your lenders\.

**

Students from BC

**

Submit a request for interest\-free status through the [National Student Loans Service Centre](https://protege-secure.csnpe-nslsc.canada.ca/en/public/sign-in-method)\.

**

Students from Alberta

**

If you have both Alberta and Canada student loans, or only Canada student loans including previously issued part\-time Canada loans, visit [National Student Loans Service Centre’s \(NSLSC\) online services](https://protege-secure.csnpe-nslsc.canada.ca/en/public/sign-in-method)\.

If you only have Alberta student loans, complete the [Confirmation of Registration \(Form B\)](https://formsmgmt.gov.ab.ca/Public/ASA12750.xdp)\.

**

Students from Ontario

**

Students must apply for interest\-free status through the [Ontario Student Assistance Program \(OSAP\)](https://www.ontario.ca/page/osap-ontario-student-assistance-program)\.

To apply for Continuation of Interest\-Free Status, follow these steps:

1.  Log into your Account on your OSAP portal\.
2.  Select “Apply for Continuation of Interest\-Free Status \(CIFS\)”\.
3.  Complete the online form\.

**

Students from Quebec

**

Email your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) to complete a Form 2006 for an interest\-free request\. You can [find your advisor](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/ubc-advisor-contacts/finding-your-enrolment-services-advisors-contact-information/) in Workday\.

If you do not have an advisor**,** submit your question through the [online form](https://www.askme.ubc.ca/form/s/)\.

**

Students from other provinces

**

Submit a request for interest\-free status through the [National Student Loans Service Centre](https://protege-secure.csnpe-nslsc.canada.ca/en/public/sign-in-method)\.

## Students with part\-time Canadian government funding[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/student\-loan\-interest/\#students\-with\-part\-time\-canadian\-government\-funding](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/student-loan-interest/#students-with-part-time-canadian-government-funding)

### How to notify your lenders

There are specific instructions to notify your lender depending on the type of your part\-time loan\.

-   **If you are not taking out a new part\-time loan**  
    Register in an eligible [course load](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/course-load-guide/) for your part\-time studies and notify your lenders by submitting a request for interest\-free status through the [National Student Loans Service Centre](https://protege-secure.csnpe-nslsc.canada.ca/en/public/sign-in-method)\.
-   **If you are taking out a new part\-time loan**  
    Register in an eligible [course load](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/course-load-guide/) for your part\-time studies, apply for a new loan, and receive funding before you [enter repayment](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/repaying-my-student-loans/)\.

Part\-time studies cannot be used to put previous full\-time loans into interest\-free or payment\-free status\.

## Students with US loans[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/student\-loan\-interest/\#students\-with\-us\-loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/student-loan-interest/#students-with-us-loans)

If you applied for a previous loan, you must notify your lender that you have returned to part\-time or full\-time study\.

If you do not notify your lenders, your loans will begin to accrue interest and you will [enter repayment\.](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/repaying-my-student-loans/)

UBC can inform your lender\(s\) that you’ve returned to school through the [National Student Loan Data System \(NSLDS\)](https://nsldsfap.ed.gov/login)\.

You’ll need to email [usloans\.inquiry@ubc\.ca](mailto:usloans.inquiry@ubc.ca) to request that Enrolment Services submit your current enrolment information to your US lenders\.

Your SSN is needed to add you to the NSLDS roster\. Please provide your SSN to [Enrolment Services](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) by phone\.

Once this update is submitted, you will be on a report that UBC completes once every 60 days for the NSLDS\. You will not need to manually request an enrolment update again, unless you cease to be a full\-time student at UBC for a semester or more\.

### In\-school deferment eligibility

If you are registered in at least 6 credits per term, you will be eligible for [In\-School Deferment](https://studentaid.gov/help-center/answers/topic/glossary/article/deferment) for your current study period\.

Depending on the [types of US loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/) you have, you may still build interest on your loans even if you are eligible for deferment\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/student\-loan\-interest/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/student-loan-interest/#if-you-have-questions)

For help with finances, registration, records, and more, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

title: Taxes
content_markdown:
In Canada, if you earn income tax from working, you must [file your taxes](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/filing-taxes-canada/) for the previous calendar year by April 30\. 

UBC issues the tax forms listed on this site in late February\. At that time, you can [download your tax forms](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/downloading-your-tax-forms/)\.

UBC is only able to provide T2202 and T4A tax forms for the past 7 years\. Requests for tax documents older than 7 years cannot be fulfilled, in accordance with the UBC records retention policy and Canada Revenue Agency \(CRA\) guidelines\.

Before accessing tax form\(s\), make sure you have added your [SIN or ITN](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/personal-information/adding-your-social-insurance-number-sin-or-international-tax-number-itn/) to Workday\. If you’re updating this information on Workday after your tax form\(s\) have been issued, please allow 3 hours to see the change reflected\.

## How to access tax forms[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/\#how\-to\-access\-tax\-forms](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/#how-to-access-tax-forms)

You can access available tax forms from the UBC Official Documents tool in [Workday](https://myworkday.ubc.ca/)\.

Alumni and former students who aren’t able to log into Workday can log into the [UBC Official Documents tool](https://ubc.appiancloud.com/suite/sites/ubc-official-documents) directly\.

Learn how to [download your tax forms](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/downloading-your-tax-forms/)\.

If you are logging into the UBC Official Documents tool for the first time, you may have to wait 3 hours for your information to sync before proceeding with your request\.

You will be emailed when 2025 tax forms are available\. Please ensure your email address and [contact information](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/personal-information/adding-changing-your-contact-information/) on Workday are correct\.

## Tax years and academic years[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/\#tax\-years\-and\-academic\-years](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/#tax-years-and-academic-years)

Tax forms are issued for the previous tax year, which spans from January to December\. As the academic year runs from September to August, your tax form will include amounts from terms spanning two academic years\.

For example, in 2026, you will receive tax forms for the 2025 tax year\.

The 2025 tax year includes:

-   2024 Winter Term 2 \(January to April 2025\)
-   2025 Summer Term 1 \(May to June 2025\)
-   2025 Summer Term 2 \(July to August 2025\)
-   2025 Winter Term 1 \(September to December 2025\)

## T2202 tax form[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/\#t2202\-tax\-form](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/#t2202-tax-form)

The T2202 tax certificate is issued to students registered in eligible courses and programs, and is used for filing income taxes\. The certificate contains the amount of eligible tuition and/or fees paid for the tax year and the number of months a student was registered \(full\-time or part\-time\)\.

Exclusions apply if fees or charges are not yet paid by the student, or if they have been reimbursed\.

### T2202 amendments

If any information on your tax certificate has been changed after it was originally issued, an amendment will be created and sent to the CRA\.

Amendments created on or before April 30 will be issued within 7 to 10 days\. After April 30, these changes will be made by Enrolment Services or your faculty and updated at the end of each month\.

UBC sending an amendment to the CRA does not adjust tax returns that have already been filed\.

### Application fees

Application fees for admission to UBC are not included in your Tuition and Enrolment Certificate \(T2202\)\. Since these fees are paid before a student is admitted and enrolled in Workday, please use the receipt you received at the time of payment when filing your taxes\.

### Co\-op student information

Before the 2024 tax year, students enrolled in a co\-op term were not considered full\-time or part\-time, and were not eligible to report those months on their taxes\.

Starting in the 2024 tax year, if you are enrolled in a co\-op term you are eligible to claim part\-time months for that time\. UBC will report your part\-time months on your T2202 form\.

## T4A tax form[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/\#t4a\-tax\-form](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/#t4a-tax-form)

If you have received a bursary, scholarship, award, Teacher Certificate, or Faculty/Staff Tuition Fee Waiver as a dependant, then you will be issued an online T4A\. The amount on your T4A shows the total funding you received in the tax year, which may not equal the total you received for the academic year\.

Tuition paid by a sponsor is considered taxable income\. However, the sponsoring organizations issue the T4A forms for this income, not UBC\.

### T4A amendments

If there are any changes received to bursary, scholarship, award, Teacher Certificate, or Faculty/Staff Tuition Fee Waiver as a dependant after your T4A was originally issued, an amendment will be created and sent to the CRA\. 

After Feb 28, these changes will be made by Enrolment Services and updated quarterly, in early June, early September, and early December\.  

UBC sending an amendment to the CRA does not adjust tax returns that have already been filed\.

## T4 tax form[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/\#t4\-tax\-form](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/#t4-tax-form)

If you were employed by UBC on a Co\-op work term, as a Teaching Assistant \(TA\) or Residence Advisor \(RA\), or any other position, such as Work Learn, you’ll receive a tax form in the “Benefits and Pay” app in [Workday](https://myworkday.ubc.ca/)\. Follow the [step\-by\-step guide](https://ubc.service-now.com/selfservice?id=kb_article&sysparm_article=KB0017227) to access your T4 form\.

## Social Insurance Number \(SIN\) for T2202 and T4A[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/\#social\-insurance\-number\-sin\-for\-t2202\-and\-t4a](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/#social-insurance-number-sin-for-t2202-and-t4a)

Your tax certificate\(s\) will include the [Social Insurance Number](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/) UBC has on file for you\. Provide your SIN to be included on your T2202 or T4A tax form in Workday as soon as you have it*\.* Learn how to [add your SIN or ITN](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/personal-information/adding-your-social-insurance-number-sin-or-international-tax-number-itn/) in [Workday](https://myworkday.ubc.ca/)\.

Non\-residents of Canada are not required to provide a SIN unless you have earned income while in Canada\. If you are not eligible for a SIN number, you might be eligible for an [Individual Tax Number](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/individual-tax-number-itn/) \(ITN\)\.

## 1098\-T tax form[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/\#1098\-t\-tax\-form](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/#1098-t-tax-form)

If you are filing taxes in the United States, you may be asked to produce the [Form 1098\-T, Tuition Statement](https://www.irs.gov/uac/form-1098-t-tuition-statement) which is used for qualified tuition and related expenses paid during the tax year\. UBC is an eligible educational institution because of participation in the US Direct Loan Program\.

UBC does not issue the Form 1098\-T, Tuition Statement\. As a Canadian institution, UBC only provides Canadian federal \(T2202A\) tax receipts\.

### Claiming tuition and related expenses without a 1098\-T

For the most up\-to\-date information on claiming tuition and related expenses without a 1098\-T, learn more about [Publication 970, Tax Benefits for Education](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-publication-970)\.

title: Filing taxes in Canada
content_markdown:
## Income tax in Canada[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/filing\-taxes\-canada/\#income\-tax\-in\-canada](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/filing-taxes-canada/#income-tax-in-canada)

In Canada, income tax is administered by the Canada Revenue Agency \(CRA\)\. The Canadian income tax year is from January 1 to December 31\. If you owe income tax, you must pay it by April 30 for the previous calendar year\. For example, your income tax payment for the 2024 tax year will be due by April 30, 2025\. Late submissions are accepted, but there may be a penalty\.

If you are employed in Canada, your employer is required to withhold and remit statutory deductions for your wages to the CRA\. These statutory deductions include: income tax, Canada Pension Plan \(CPP\) and Employment Insurance \(EI\)\. In order to deduct the proper amount of income tax from your wages, your employer will ask you to complete both the TD\-1 \(federal\) and the TD1\-BC forms\. Employers will deduct an amount from each pay cheque for Canada Pension Plan \(CPP\) and Employment Insurance \(EI\)\.

You are responsible for determining your tax filing obligations and income tax status in Canada\. You can get help through the [UBC Tax Assistance Clinic](https://ubctacs.com/clinic)\.

## What you need to file a tax return[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/filing\-taxes\-canada/\#what\-you\-need\-to\-file\-a\-tax\-return](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/filing-taxes-canada/#what-you-need-to-file-a-tax-return)

To file a Canadian tax return, you need **one** of the following:

-   A Social Insurance Number \(SIN\)
-   An Individual Tax Number \(ITN\)

As soon as you get a SIN or ITN, enter it in your [Workday](https://myworkday.ubc.ca/) account so that UBC can provide the government with accurate information for your taxes\. Learn how to [add your SIN or ITN](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/personal-information/adding-your-social-insurance-number-sin-or-international-tax-number-itn/) in Workday\.

If you have either of these numbers, but it has expired and you are not currently employed, you can still use the expired number to file taxes\.

### Social Insurance Number \(SIN\)

To apply for a [Social Insurance Number](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/) \(SIN\), you must have a work permit or a study permit which includes a condition to work on and/or off campus\.

### Individual Tax Number \(ITN\)

If you are not eligible for a SIN, you can apply for an [Individual Tax Number](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/individual-tax-number-itn/) \(ITN\)\. This is especially important for students who receive scholarships, as UBC will require you to provide an ITN at the end of Winter Term 1\.

### Additional supporting documents

You may also need the following documents when filing your taxes\.

-   **T2202**  
    The T2202 shows the tuition fees you paid for the tax year\. Learn how to [download your tax forms](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/downloading-your-tax-forms/) in Workday\.
-   **T4A**  
    The [T4A form](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/finances/taxes#t4a-tax-form) is available for students who have received a taxable tuition waiver, teacher certificate, scholarship, or bursary in the tax year\. Learn how to [download your tax forms](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/downloading-your-tax-forms/)\.
-   **T4**  
    The [T4 form](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/#t4-tax-form) highlights your employment income and deductions\. You should receive your T4 from your employer\. If you are employed by UBC, follow instructions online to [access your T4 form](https://ubc.service-now.com/selfservice?id=kb_article&sysparm_article=KB0017227)\.

## Apply for tax deductions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/filing\-taxes\-canada/\#apply\-for\-tax\-deductions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/filing-taxes-canada/#apply-for-tax-deductions)

You may be eligible to deduct certain expenses from your tax payments\. Eligible moving expenses may include transportation, storage of personal belongings, travel, and temporary accommodations\. Save all your receipts for expenses related to your relocation to Canada\. However, you cannot deduct moving expenses if your only income at the new location is scholarship, fellowship, or bursary income that is fully exempt from tax under the current legislation\.

You may also deduct childcare expenses, Registered Retirement Savings Plan \(RRSP\) contributions, and union dues from your taxes\.

## How to file your taxes[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/filing\-taxes\-canada/\#how\-to\-file\-your\-taxes](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/filing-taxes-canada/#how-to-file-your-taxes)

### Online

You might be able to file your income tax directly to the Canada Revenue Agency \(CRA\) online through the electronic tax\-filing software [NETFILE](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/e-services-individuals/netfile-overview.html)\. Tax returns filed via NETFILE must first be prepared using a NETFILE\-certified product you can find on their website\.

### By paper

If you are submitting your tax return by paper, find the forms you need on the [Canada Revenue Agency website](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html)\.

### Mailing your tax return

Check the [Canadian government website](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/individuals/topics/about-your-tax-return/tax-return/sending-a-tax-return.html) to find out where you can submit your taxes by mail\.

## Do international students file taxes?[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/filing\-taxes\-canada/\#do\-international\-students\-file\-taxes](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/filing-taxes-canada/#do-international-students-file-taxes)

The Canadian tax system is based on [your residency status](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/international-non-residents/individuals-leaving-entering-canada-non-residents/international-students-studying-canada.html), not citizenship\. Most international students file a tax return \(submit an income tax form to the government\) to receive [benefits and tax credits](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/international-non-residents/individuals-leaving-entering-canada-non-residents/newcomers-canada-immigrants.html) \(money from governments and/or the chance to lower taxes later\)\. International students may have to pay Canadian income tax on income earned from teaching and/or research assistantships, other employment, and investment and business income\. Generally, students also have to report income they receive from outside of Canada\.

Students from countries that have a [tax treaty](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/international-non-residents/tax-treaties.html) with Canada may not have to pay Canadian income tax\. They may also request that their employer stop withholding tax from their Canadian employment income, as long as they get permission from the CRA\.

### Determine if you must file a return

You must file a return if:

-   You owe income tax to the government \(for example, you earn significant income in Canada\)\.
-   You’re asked by the CRA to file a return\.

Even if you don’t owe any tax, you should file a tax return if:

-   You expect an income tax refund from the government\.
-   You’re applying for the GST/HST credit \(which provides cash payments to low\- and middle\-income taxpayers, to help offset the costs of paying GST/HST on taxable purchases\)\.
-   You’re eligible to receive the child tax credit \(for low\- and middle\-income taxpayers with children\)\.
-   You might earn more income in Canada later, such as through Co\-op, and want to carry forward Tuition Payment and Education Credits \(e\.g\., save for future years\) to reduce the tax you owe in future years\.

Learn more about who has to [file a return](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/individuals/topics/about-your-tax-return/you-have-file-a-return.html)\.

You do not need to pay taxes on your income from scholarships, fellowships, or bursaries, but you must provide UBC with your ITN or SIN when UBC requests it for tax purposes\.

## Get help filing your taxes[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/filing\-taxes\-canada/\#get\-help\-filing\-your\-taxes](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/filing-taxes-canada/#get-help-filing-your-taxes)

-   [Taxes](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/)
-   [UBC Tax Assistance Clinic \(UBC TACS\)](https://ubctacs.com/)
-   [CRA Free tax clinics](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/campaigns/free-tax-help.html)
-   [CRA’s Taxes for international students studying in Canada](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/international-non-residents/individuals-leaving-entering-canada-non-residents/international-students-studying-canada.html)
-   [CRA’s Newcomers to Canada – immigrants and returning residents](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/international-non-residents/individuals-leaving-entering-canada-non-residents/newcomers-canada-immigrants.html)
-   [CRA webinar for international students](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/news/cra-multimedia-library/individuals-video-gallery/webinar-international-students.html)

## International Student Guide[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/filing\-taxes\-canada/\#international\-student\-guide](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/filing-taxes-canada/#international-student-guide)

Find everything you need to know about life as an international student at UBC’s Vancouver campus\.

[View the guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/filing\-taxes\-canada/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/filing-taxes-canada/#if-you-have-questions)

International Student Advisors are not tax experts and cannot provide any tax assistance\. Please use the resources above to guide you through filing your taxes\. If you have questions about how to file a tax return, please contact [Canada Revenue Agency](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/corporate/contact-information/individual-income-tax-enquiries-line.html) directly\.

## What is an ITN?[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/individual\-tax\-number\-itn/\#what\-is\-an\-itn](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/individual-tax-number-itn/#what-is-an-itn)

An Individual Tax Number \(ITN\) is a unique number that Canada Revenue Agency \(CRA\) uses to identify you for tax purposes if you aren’t eligible for a [Social Insurance Number \(SIN\)](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/)\.

If you are an international student who is not eligible for a SIN, you will need an ITN if:

-   **You received a scholarship or award from UBC\.**  
    As an incoming student, you can accept scholarships or awards without a SIN or ITN\. You must enter a SIN or ITN into Workday by January so UBC can issue your [T4A tax forms](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/finances/taxes#t4a-tax-form)\. Learn how to [upload your SIN or ITN](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/personal-information/adding-your-social-insurance-number-sin-or-international-tax-number-itn/) in Workday\.
-   **You want to file a tax return\.**  
    As an international student now living in Canada, you may need to [file a tax return](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/filing-taxes-canada/) depending on your situation\.

> > About the information on this page
> 
> > This is not a legal document and may change without notice\. Always refer to the [Canadian Revenue Agency](https://www.canada.ca/en/services/taxes.html) for the most updated information\.

## Applying for an ITN[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/individual\-tax\-number\-itn/\#applying\-for\-an\-itn](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/individual-tax-number-itn/#applying-for-an-itn)

If you are not eligible for a SIN, follow [step\-by\-step instructions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/individual-tax-number-itn-apply-individual-tax-number-itn/) to apply for your ITN\.

Make sure you **apply early,** as it can take up to 8 weeks to process your application\. If you receive an award, or are planning to file Canadian taxes, you should apply as soon as you arrive in Canada\. If you have not received a reply within 8 weeks, call the CRA for an update on the status of your application\. You can check to [confirm the processing times](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/international-non-residents-tax/in-outside-canada/apply-individual-tax-number.html#how) for your application\.

For questions about the ITN, call the [Sudbury Tax Centre](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/international-non-residents-tax/in-outside-canada/apply-individual-tax-number.html#contact)\.

Contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for questions related to immigration, health insurance, and life as an international student in Canada\.
