title: How to apply for an Individual Tax Number (ITN)
content_markdown:
## About this page[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/individual\-tax\-number\-itn\-apply\-individual\-tax\-number\-itn/\#about\-this\-page](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/individual-tax-number-itn-apply-individual-tax-number-itn/#about-this-page)

This is not a legal document and may change without notice\. Always refer to [Canadian Revenue Agency](https://www.canada.ca/en/services/taxes.html) for the most updated information\.

## What is an ITN?[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/individual\-tax\-number\-itn\-apply\-individual\-tax\-number\-itn/\#what\-is\-an\-itn](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/individual-tax-number-itn-apply-individual-tax-number-itn/#what-is-an-itn)

An Individual Tax Number \(ITN\) is a unique number that Canada Revenue Agency \(CRA\) uses to identify you for tax purposes if you aren’t eligible for a [Social Insurance Number \(SIN\)](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/)\.

If you are an international student who is not eligible for a SIN, you need to get an ITN if:

-   **You received a scholarship or award from UBC\.**  
    You must enter a SIN or ITN into Workday by January so UBC can issue your [T4A tax forms](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/#t4a-tax-form)\. Learn how to [upload your SIN or ITN](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/personal-information/adding-your-social-insurance-number-sin-or-international-tax-number-itn/) in Workday\.
-   **You want to file a tax return\.**  
    As an international student now living in Canada, you may need to [file a tax return](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/filing-taxes-canada/) depending on your situation\.

## Overview of the application process[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/individual\-tax\-number\-itn\-apply\-individual\-tax\-number\-itn/\#overview\-of\-the\-application\-process](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/individual-tax-number-itn-apply-individual-tax-number-itn/#overview-of-the-application-process)

| Topic | Details |
| --- | --- |
| ****When to apply**** | Well in advance, ideally soon after arriving in Canada |
| ****Cost**** | Free |
| ****Processing time**** | Generally 6 to 8 weeks \(sometimes longer\)\. Check [processing times](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/international-non-residents-tax/in-outside-canada/apply-individual-tax-number.html#when) |
| ****How to apply**** | Send your paper application to Ottawa, Ontario\. The address is on the back of the application form |
| ****Application form**** | [“Application for a Canada Revenue Agency Individual Tax Number \(ITN\) for Non\-Residents” \[T1261\]](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/forms-publications/forms/t1261.html) |

## Supporting documents[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/individual\-tax\-number\-itn\-apply\-individual\-tax\-number\-itn/\#supporting\-documents](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/individual-tax-number-itn-apply-individual-tax-number-itn/#supporting-documents)

In addition to the application form, you will need to submit:

-   A copy of your passport bio\-data page \(the page containing your name and photo\)
-   Your UBC Letter of Enrolment\. Learn how to [download your Confirmation of Enrolment Letter](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/student-documents/downloading-your-confirmation-of-enrolment-letter/) in Workday
-   A copy of your study permit, if you have one

Your documents must be certified copies or notarized copies\. You can [find more details](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/international-non-residents-tax/in-outside-canada/apply-individual-tax-number.html#what) on the Government of Canada site\.

### If you do not have a study permit

Please submit all of the following:

-   A copy of passport page\(s\) containing entry stamps to Canada \(if applicable\)
-   A copy of your flight ticket to Canada \(if applicable\)
-   A copy of any UBC scholarship or award offer letters \(if applicable\)
-   Proof of request for an ITN from Enrolment Services \(if applicable\)
-   Cover letter explaining why you need an ITN

## Mailing the application[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/individual\-tax\-number\-itn\-apply\-individual\-tax\-number\-itn/\#mailing\-the\-application](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/individual-tax-number-itn-apply-individual-tax-number-itn/#mailing-the-application)

We suggest using Canada Post Xpresspost to mail your documents securely\.

We highly suggest applying for an ITN from **within** Canada \(before you leave Canada\)\. If you have already left Canada and you need to apply for an ITN, we suggest you include a cover letter explaining your situation to avoid confusion and delay\. You can call the [Sudbury Tax Centre](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/international-non-residents-tax/in-outside-canada/apply-individual-tax-number.html#contact) to check that you are providing the right documents before sending your application\.

## Understanding the form[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/individual\-tax\-number\-itn\-apply\-individual\-tax\-number\-itn/\#understanding\-the\-form](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/individual-tax-number-itn-apply-individual-tax-number-itn/#understanding-the-form)

### Reason for applying

Indicate “Filling a Canadian income tax return” as the reason you are applying for an ITN\.

[Image](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/ISG_ITN_reason_for_applying.png)

### The difference between “Foreign address” and “Mailing address”

The “Foreign Address” refers to your address in the country where you permanently or normally reside\. The “Mailing Address” refers to a Canadian address to which the CRA will send the written notification of your ITN\.

[Image](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/ISG_ITN_foreign_mailing_address.jpeg)

### What do I put for “Foreign Tax Identification Number”?

If you don’t have a Foreign Tax Identification number, you may write “N/A”\.

### Who should sign under the “CERTIFICATION” section at the bottom of the application form?

You should be the one providing your signature\. The person certifying your document, such as your doctor, should sign and certify the photocopy of your passport\.

[Image](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/ISG_ITN_certification.jpeg)

## Frequently Asked Questions \(FAQ\)[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/individual\-tax\-number\-itn\-apply\-individual\-tax\-number\-itn/\#frequently\-asked\-questions\-faq](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/individual-tax-number-itn-apply-individual-tax-number-itn/#frequently-asked-questions-faq)

**

Can I work with an ITN?

**

No\. To start working in Canada and receive benefits from employment, you need to apply for a [Social Insurance Number \(SIN\)](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin) to replace your ITN, and be [eligible to work in Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/career/working-canada)\.

**

Does an ITN expire? Do I have to renew ITN?

**

No\. The ITN does not have an expiry date\. Once you are issued an ITN, you can use it for future tax filing purposes\. But remember that if you get a job in the future, you will need a SIN\.

**

If I lost my ITN or need to make changes to my personal info, should I apply for a new ITN?

**

No\. You must contact the Canada Revenue Agency \(CRA\) to notify them about the lost ITN or changes to your personal information\. You can then either get your previous number re\-issued or keep using the number you have\.

**

I am outside Canada\. Can I get my documents certified by a notary or professional outside Canada in order to submit my ITN application on time?

**

Yes\. Your documents can be certified outside of Canada\. Please refer to the [Government of Canada guidelines](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/international-non-residents-tax/in-outside-canada/apply-individual-tax-number.html#how) for information on who can certify your documents\.  

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/individual\-tax\-number\-itn\-apply\-individual\-tax\-number\-itn/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/individual-tax-number-itn-apply-individual-tax-number-itn/#if-you-have-questions)

For questions about the ITN, call the [Sudbury Tax Centre](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/international-non-residents-tax/in-outside-canada/apply-individual-tax-number.html#contact)\.

title: Social Insurance Number (SIN)
content_markdown:
A Social Insurance Number \(SIN\) is a 9\-digit number issued by Service Canada, a Canadian government department\. You need a SIN to start working in Canada, to file taxes, and to access government programs and benefits, if eligible\. You will also need to provide your SIN to UBC for tax purposes\. 

Certain students who are not eligible for a SIN, such as exchange students without a study permit, can get an [Individual Tax Number](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/individual-tax-number-itn/) \(ITN\) instead\. Learn how to [add your SIN or ITN](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/personal-information/adding-your-social-insurance-number-sin-or-international-tax-number-itn/) in Workday\.

**If you’re an international student**, having a SIN alone is not enough to allow you to work in Canada\. Make sure you are [eligible to work in Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/)\.

## Before you apply for a SIN[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/social\-insurance\-number\-sin/\#before\-you\-apply\-for\-a\-sin](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/#before-you-apply-for-a-sin)

### Domestic students

If you are a Canadian citizen or permanent resident, you’ll need to provide certain documents for your application\. See [how to apply](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/sin/apply.html) for your SIN\.

### International students

You can only get your SIN after you’ve arrived in Canada since you first need to get your study permit at the airport or border crossing before you can apply\.

It‘s very important to follow the steps below to make sure your study permit allows you to work in Canada and to get a SIN\.

[See arrival steps](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/while-you-travel/)

#### Check your study permit conditions

To be eligible for a SIN, you must have a study permit with at least one of the following conditions:

-   “May accept employment on or off campus if meeting eligibility criteria, per paragraph R186\(f\), \(v\) or \(w\) and must cease working if no longer meeting these criteria”
-   “May work 24 hours per week off campus or full time during regular breaks if meeting criteria outlined in paragraph 186\(v\) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations”
-   “May accept employment on the campus of the institution at which registered in full\-time studies”

You can also apply for a SIN if you have a work permit, such as a co\-op work permit, a Post\-Graduation Work Permit, or a spousal work permit\.

#### If your study permit does not state you can work

If you’re [eligible to work in Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/) as a student, but you **do not** have one of the conditions on your study permit listed above, you’ll need to either “amend” or “change the conditions” of your study permit depending on your situation:

-   If there was a mistake when you were issued the study permit, you need to [amend your study permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/amend-study-permit-conditions-work-canada/)\. For example, you applied for your study permit with your UBC letter of acceptance for a degree program and your study permit does not include conditions to work\.
-   If your situation has changed and you’ve now switched to a program which makes you eligible to work off\-campus, you need to [change your study permit conditions](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/extend-study-permit/), which follows the same process as a study permit extension\. For example, you previously studied at a secondary school and are now a degree\-seeking student at UBC\.

You can apply for a SIN after you’ve received your new study permit with the correct conditions allowing you to work\.

## Applying for a SIN as an international student[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/social\-insurance\-number\-sin/\#applying\-for\-a\-sin\-as\-an\-international\-student](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/#applying-for-a-sin-as-an-international-student)

We recommend that you [apply for a SIN online](https://sin-nas.canada.ca/en/Sin/)\. You can also apply by mail or request an in\-person appointment if you face barriers applying online\.

If you are outside of Canada and you have a study or work permit, you can apply online for a new or extended SIN or a confirmation of your SIN, even if you do not have a Canadian mailing address\.

In addition to your study or work permit, you will need a copy of your passport\. If the document is not in English or French, you will need to [translate the document](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/sin/required-documents.html)\.

[Apply for a SIN](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/sin/apply.html)

### Type of work permitted

If you meet the work eligibility requirement and you’ve applied for your SIN, you can work for a job that is considered [insurable employment](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/payroll/payroll-deductions-contributions/employment-insurance-ei.html)\. Insurable employment is work under the authority of an employer in Canada who controls your wages, hours, and tasks\.

### Typical processing times

-   Online applications may take up to 5 business days\.
-   Mail applications may take up to 20 business days\.
-   If you apply in person, you’ll receive the SIN during your visit\.

Check the most up\-to\-date [processing times](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/sin/receiving-updating.html)\.

If your application has exceeded normal processing times by 5 days and you have not received a letter, please [contact the SIN Program](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/corporate/contact/sin.html)\.

### Your SIN digits after applying

International students get a SIN starting with the number “9”, which lets employers know that you are a temporary resident in Canada\. 

Your SIN will remain the same unless you become a permanent resident, in which case you can apply for a new SIN that doesn’t start with the number ‘9’\.

## Keeping your SIN valid[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/social\-insurance\-number\-sin/\#keeping\-your\-sin\-valid](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/#keeping-your-sin-valid)

Your SIN will usually have the same expiry date as your study or work permit\. 

### Extending your SIN

Make sure you keep your SIN valid by **extending** **your SIN** each time you extend your temporary residency in Canada, such as getting your extended study permit or your Post\-Graduation Work Permit\. If you get a co\-op work permit and have already received a SIN from your study permit, you do not need to apply for a SIN again\. 

To extend your SIN, follow the same steps as applying for a [new SIN number](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/sin/apply.html)\.

### Maintained Status

If you applied for a new study or work permit before your current document became invalid and you have not yet received a new one, you can continue to use the same SIN while you are waiting for your permit to be issued, as long as you stay in Canada and are on “[maintained status](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/maintained-status/)“\.

## Keeping your SIN safe[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/social\-insurance\-number\-sin/\#keeping\-your\-sin\-safe](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/#keeping-your-sin-safe)

Your SIN is considered to be sensitive personal information which should not be shared—be sure to [protect your SIN](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/services/sin/reports/shared-responsibility.html)\. Beware of fraudulent phone calls or emails asking for your SIN or any other personal information\. Learn about [scams and fraud](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/campaigns/fraud-scams.html) and how to confirm if it’s really the government contacting you\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/social\-insurance\-number\-sin/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/#if-you-have-questions)

You can contact [Service Canada](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/corporate/contact/sin.html) directly\.

For questions related to immigration, health insurance, and life as an international student in Canada, connect with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/)\.

## International Student Guide[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/taxes/social\-insurance\-number\-sin/\#international\-student\-guide](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/#international-student-guide)

Find everything you need to know about life as an international student at UBC’s Vancouver campus\.

[View the guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/)

title: Third-party authorization
content_markdown:
## Your student information[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/third\-party\-authorization/\#your\-student\-information](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/third-party-authorization/#your-student-information)

Your records and information at UBC are protected under the [Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act](https://universitycounsel.ubc.ca/subject-areas/access-and-privacy-general/) \(FIPPA\)\. This means that information you provide to UBC and information about your academic and financial record is not available to anybody other than you\. Your parents, sponsors, supporters, or companies confirming your enrolment do not have access to this data\.

If you want to give someone access to this information, you can grant third\-party authorization\. Alumni requesting to have third parties verify their credentials are required to submit a request through [AuraData](https://www.auradata.com/)\. Read the [Degree Verifications](https://facultystaff.students.ubc.ca/enrolment-services/scheduling-records-systems-management/degree-verifications) page for more information\. Current students should follow the instructions below for adding third\-party authorization\.

## Adding third\-party authorization[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/third\-party\-authorization/\#adding\-third\-party\-authorization](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/third-party-authorization/#adding-third-party-authorization)

If needed, you can grant another person permission to access specific information on your record or to pick up your documents on your behalf\. The third party will not be able to make changes to your record, take action on your behalf, or receive notification emails from UBC\. Where possible, it is best to manage your own records\.

Learn how to [add your third\-party authorization](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/personal-information/adding-your-third-party-authorization/) in Workday\. You must list a specific name for the person you’re assigning third\-party authorization to, not just a company name\.

You must provide your third party with your student number and the authorization code you assigned to them\. UBC services will require both before releasing any protected information\.

## Types of third\-party authorization[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/third\-party\-authorization/\#types\-of\-third\-party\-authorization](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/third-party-authorization/#types-of-third-party-authorization)

Below are the kinds of information you might choose to share with a third party\.

-   **Student Housing information**  
    Residence fee and room assignment information
-   **Medical information**  
    Information about medical documentation submitted to UBC, such as doctor’s notes\. Medical information does not include information held by [UBC Student Health Services](https://students.ubc.ca/health/student-health-service/) or [UBC Counselling Services](https://students.ubc.ca/health/counselling-services/), which are especially sensitive\. You will need to get a separate authorization for these services
-   **Academic record information**  
    Information about your academic record including biographical details, registration, grades, academic standing, timetable, tuition and fees, degree and enrolment confirmation
-   **Financial assistance and awards**  
    Information about your financial assistance and award status, including student loans, bursaries, scholarships and financial need\. Registration, grades, fees and admission status may also be released, if applicable\.
-   **Document pick up**  
    The release of documents related to your application, admission, registration, academic record, and financial assistance and awards at UBC\. Documents that require payment, such as transcripts or replacement parchments, must be ordered by the student through the UBC Official Documents tool before the third party picks it up\. Documents cannot be ordered in person by the third party\.
-   ****Admission informatio**n**  
    Information related to your application for admission to UBC, including application content and status, documentation, and transcripts\. Third\-party authorization can be added in the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/) by selecting “Third Party Authorizations” under the *Edit Profile* menu at the top right corner\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/third\-party\-authorization/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/third-party-authorization/#if-you-have-questions)

For help with finances, registration, records, and more, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

title: Changing the name on your parchment (diploma)
content_markdown:
Your parchment refers to your diploma\.

The name on your official student record will be the name printed on your parchment, but there are certain acceptable name changes you can request\.

If you’re a UBC Okanagan student, review [information and instructions](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/graduation/changing-the-name-on-your-diploma/) specific to your campus\.

## Updating your legal name[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/changing\-name\-parchment\-diploma/\#updating\-your\-legal\-name](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/changing-name-parchment-diploma/#updating-your-legal-name)

If you have recently changed your legal name, or previously did not include your middle name and want it to be added to your parchment, you must notify UBC by [updating your name](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/changing-name-parchment-diploma/) on your official student record\. The legal name on your student record will be the name printed on your parchment\.

The deadline to update your legal name on your student record and on your [graduation application](https://ubc.appiancloud.com/suite/sites/graduation-management-application) for your parchment for Spring graduation is **Fri, Apr 17, 2026**\. After that date, you will be required to order a [replacement parchment](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-parchment-diploma/)\.

### If you’ve already submitted your graduation application

Please email [graduation@ubc\.ca](mailto:graduation@ubc.ca) after you have [updated your legal name](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/changing-name-student-record/#how-to-update-your-legal-name) with Enrolment Services to ensure your graduation application and parchment are also updated\.

Updating your official student record will not automatically update your graduation application\.

## Using your preferred name for the upcoming graduation ceremony[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/changing\-name\-parchment\-diploma/\#using\-your\-preferred\-name\-for\-the\-upcoming\-graduation\-ceremony](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/changing-name-parchment-diploma/#using-your-preferred-name-for-the-upcoming-graduation-ceremony)

If you would like to have your [preferred or chosen name](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/changing-name-student-record/#preferred-or-chosen-name-changes) read as you cross the stage for the Spring 2026 graduation ceremony and included in the ceremony program, submit a request on your [graduation application](https://ubc.appiancloud.com/suite/sites/graduation-management-application) by **Fri, April 17, 2026**\. This request does not change the name printed on your parchment\.

You do **not** need to submit a request if you want your legal name to be used, since it’s recorded in Workday automatically\.

## Other acceptable changes to your parchment \(diploma\)[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/changing\-name\-parchment\-diploma/\#other\-acceptable\-changes\-to\-your\-parchment\-diploma](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/changing-name-parchment-diploma/#other-acceptable-changes-to-your-parchment-diploma)

-   An unused first name may be abbreviated to initials, such as “J\. Mary Smith”\.
-   Middle names may be abbreviated to initials or omitted from the parchment\.
-   If you are attending UBC under a married name, your birth name can be printed on your parchment upon presentation of appropriate ID\. Your birth name can be added to your records for future reference if necessary\.
-   Changing the order of your legal name \(eg\. first name, last name\) is not permitted\.

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/changing\-name\-parchment\-diploma/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/changing-name-parchment-diploma/#additional-resources)

-   [Ordering a parchment \(diploma\)](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-parchment-diploma/)
-   [Changing your personal information](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/)
-   [Applying to graduate](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/graduation/applying-graduate/)
-   [Graduation FAQ](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/graduation/graduation-faq/)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/changing\-name\-parchment\-diploma/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/changing-name-parchment-diploma/#if-you-have-questions)

For information on changing the name on your parchment, contact: 

-   **UBC Vancouver**: [graduation@ubc\.ca](mailto:graduation@ubc.ca)
-   **UBC Okanagan**: [gradapps\.okanagan@ubc\.ca](mailto:gradapps.okanagan@ubc.ca)

title: Changing your name on your student record
content_markdown:
## Legal name changes[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/changing\-name\-student\-record/\#legal\-name\-changes](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/changing-name-student-record/#legal-name-changes)

If your legal name is incorrect on UBC’s official records, such as your transcript, parchment, or student card, and you wish to be known by your correct legal name, you can request a name change\.

To have your name on your parchment changed after graduation, you will need to [order a replacement parchment](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-parchment-diploma/)\.

## Documents that require your legal name at UBC[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/changing\-name\-student\-record/\#documents\-that\-require\-your\-legal\-name\-at\-ubc](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/changing-name-student-record/#documents-that-require-your-legal-name-at-ubc)

You will need your legal name listed for the documents below:

-   Official letters \(including but not limited to admission, enrolment, award letters, and student loans\)
-   Tax forms
-   Transcripts
-   Parchments
-   Residence contracts

## How to update your legal name[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/changing\-name\-student\-record/\#how\-to\-update\-your\-legal\-name](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/changing-name-student-record/#how-to-update-your-legal-name)

You can request a legal name change on your UBC record in person or online\.

You must follow a separate process to [request a name change](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/changing-name-parchment-diploma/) for your parchment\. There is a deadline to submit name change requests before graduation\.

**

Submit your documents in person

**

Bring your legal documents and UBCcard \(student ID\) to the [Enrolment Services Advising Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) in Brock Hall\.

**

Upload your documents online

**

Contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) to change your legal name on your UBC record\. They will follow up with a secure link for you to upload your legal documents online\.

Please do not email copies of your documents directly to Enrolment Services\.

## Preferred or chosen name changes[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/changing\-name\-student\-record/\#preferred\-or\-chosen\-name\-changes](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/changing-name-student-record/#preferred-or-chosen-name-changes)

### About preferred or chosen names

A preferred or chosen name is a name that you commonly use that is different from your legal name\. It is what you want to be called\.

While we use the term “preferred name”, for many people, this is not just a preference\. It is the only name they use and is an essential part of their identity\. It is especially important for transgender and non\-binary students whose university experience and wellbeing can be negatively impacted when their preferred or chosen name is not used\. Read more about [names and their impact](https://equity.ubc.ca/resources/gender-diversity/names/?login) at UBC\.

### Updating your preferred or chosen name

Inappropriate use of a preferred or chosen name such as attempts to avoid a legal obligation via misrepresentation, or the use of inappropriate language, will result in the denial and/or reversal of the request and can be disciplined through [Academic or Non\-Academic Misconduct](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/campus-wide-policies-and-regulations/student-conduct-and-discipline/discipline-non-academic-misconduct-student-code-conduct#19702)\.

The earlier you update your preferred or chosen name, the more likely you will experience the consistent use of your preferred or chosen first name by UBC faculty, instructors, and staff\.

Learn how to [update your preferred name](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/personal-information/updating-your-preferred-name/) in Workday\.

You should do this even if you have provided your preferred or chosen name when applying to UBC\.

### Use of a preferred or chosen first name

Below are places where UBC uses a student’s preferred name:

-   Class lists
-   UBCcard \(if requested\)
-   Canvas
-   Workday
-   Student Housing Online Service Centre
-   UBC Recreation
-   Counselling Services
-   Student Health Services \(except in places where MSP requires use of your legal name\)
-   Graduation Application
-   Graduation ceremony booklet \(if requested\)
-   Graduation ceremony \(read aloud as you cross the stage, if requested\)

Find [more information](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-parchment-diploma/) on requesting your preferred name to be printed in the graduation ceremony booklet and read aloud as you cross the stage\.

Students may still see their legal name in some online systems and communications due to the complexity of UBC’s information systems and limitations in data sharing\. UBC is working to create a more unified experience that would only display legal given names when legally required\.

#### Possible impact of using a preferred or chosen name

While UBC allows students to indicate their preferred or chosen name without changing their legal name, it’s important to think about the possible impact of this practice:

-   Official documents are often used to verify one’s identity when applying for work or additional education\. Some employers, licensing bodies, or other educational institutions may question the use of a preferred or chosen name in daily or informal correspondence\. This discrepancy happens when institutions rely on the consistent use of legal names\.
-   If someone is using a preferred or chosen name consistently, this may cause some confusion in situations where official documents have to be provided\. For example, employers might be confused about a UBC student portfolio that uses a preferred or chosen name while the transcripts use a legal name\.

#### Update your UBCcard

Your preferred or chosen name can be displayed instead of your legal name on your UBCcard\.

1.  If needed, [update your preferred name](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/personal-information/updating-your-preferred-name/) in Workday\. Please wait 48 hours for the change to appear on the system\.
2.  Contact the [UBC Carding Office](https://ubccard.ubc.ca/contact-us) in the UBC bookstore and request a card renewal with your preferred or chosen name\.

There is no charge to get a new UBCcard with your preferred or chosen name on the card\. Find more information about [UBCcard renewals](https://ubccard.ubc.ca/policies) by selecting “Name and status changes” under *Policies*\.

## Updating your citizenship status[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/changing\-name\-student\-record/\#updating\-your\-citizenship\-status](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/changing-name-student-record/#updating-your-citizenship-status)

If you become a Permanent Resident or Canadian Citizen during your time at UBC, you can update your status in person at the [Enrolment Services Advising Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) in Brock Hall\.

You must bring one of the following pieces of identification:

-   Confirmation of Permanent Residence \(COPR\) and a government\-issued photo ID 
-   Your Permanent Resident card

### Impacts of updating your citizenship status

Read more information in the [UBC Academic Calendar](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/fees/policies-fees#17962) about how your tuition may be impacted when you update your citizenship status\.

Changes to your citizenship status may also impact your [iMED health coverage](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/imed-temporary-health-insurance-international/)\. Please contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) if you have questions related to your health insurance\.

Changes to your citizenship status will also impact awards offered to you as an international student\.

## Indigenous self\-identification[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/records/changing\-name\-student\-record/\#indigenous\-self\-identification](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/changing-name-student-record/#indigenous-self-identification)

UBC has a number of unique programs and services for [Indigenous students](https://indigenous.ubc.ca/students/), including [scholarships and bursaries](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/awards-indigenous/)\. Indigenous self\-identification helps UBC offer and manage these programs and services\. 

As an Indigenous student, you can self\-identify when you apply to UBC, update your Workday student profile, or submit your graduation application\. Learn how to [add your Indigenous Self\-Identification](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/personal-information/updating-your-indigenous-self-identification/) in Workday\.

title: Registration dates
content_markdown:
## When you’ll know your registration date[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/registration\-dates/\#when\-youll\-know\-your\-registration\-date](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/registration-dates/#when-youll-know-your-registration-date)

You’ll receive an email around early June to let you know that your registration appointment is available in your [Workday account](https://myworkday.ubc.ca/)\. You’ll be able to register any time between your registration appointment and the [course change deadline](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/course-change-dates/), also known as the add/drop deadline\.

Registration times are listed in the Pacific Time Zone\. If you’re registering from a [different time zone](https://nrc.canada.ca/en/web-clock/), make sure you know when registration starts in your location\.

If you’re a UBC Okanagan student, please view the [course registration dates](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/registration/registration-dates/) for your campus\.

Learn how to [find your registration appointment](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/viewing-your-registration-appointment/) in Workday when it’s available\.

### If you do not receive a registration email

If you accept your admission offer after early June, you may not receive an email as the registration appointment notification period may have already passed\. If this happens, you can still [follow the steps](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/register-courses/) to register\. If you have questions, please contact your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

title: Letter of Permission
content_markdown:
## About Letter of Permission[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/letter\-permission/\#about\-letter\-of\-permission](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/letter-permission/#about-letter-of-permission)

In certain circumstances, faculties may grant students permission to study outside of UBC with a Letter of Permission \(LOP\)\.

An LOP must be approved by your faculty before you register at another institution\. Without an approved LOP, faculties may not accept transfer credits to be counted towards your UBC degree\.

## After you study outside of UBC[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/letter\-permission/\#after\-you\-study\-outside\-of\-ubc](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/letter-permission/#after-you-study-outside-of-ubc)

Once you have completed your course at another school, you must submit your transcript to UBC\. Official transcripts must be sent directly from the issuing school and received by UBC Undergraduate Admissions either by mail in the original sealed envelope with the name and address of the school, or as an official PDF emailed by the issuing school to [final\.grades@ubc\.ca](mailto:final.grades@ubc.ca)\.

**Mailing address:**

1874 East Mall  
Undergraduate Admissions  
UBC Enrolment Services \(Attention: Transfer Credit\)  
Vancouver, BC V6T 1Z1  
Canada

## Requesting a Letter of Permission[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/letter\-permission/\#requesting\-a\-letter\-of\-permission](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/letter-permission/#requesting-a-letter-of-permission)

Learn how to request a Letter of Permission from your faculty in an undergraduate program:

-   [Applied Science \(Engineering\)](https://academicservices.engineering.ubc.ca/forms-letters/letter-of-permission-lop/)
-   [Arts](https://www.arts.ubc.ca/degree-planning/course-registration/transfer-credits/studying-outside-of-ubc/)
-   [Kinesiology](https://kin.educ.ubc.ca/undergraduate/registration-academic-policies/)
-   [Land & Food Systems](https://www.landfood.ubc.ca/current/undergraduate/student-services/registration-program-info/#outside-courses)
-   [Sauder School of Business \(Commerce\)](https://mybcom.sauder.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/courses-and-registration/taking-courses-outside-ubc)
-   [Science](https://science.ubc.ca/students/advising/lop)
-   [UBC\-O Summer Programs](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/academic-success/degree-planning/study-options/)

If you don’t see your program above, please connect with your [academic advising office](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/)\.

### Professional programs

-   If you are enrolled in the Pharmaceutical Sciences \(Pharmacy\) PharmD program, you must submit the [Pharmacy\-Elective Approval Request Form](http://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3Jb1LFDTBFdO3A1)\.
-   Letter of Permission is not available for the Nursing program\.
-   Most professional programs will not provide a letter of permission to take courses outside of UBC\. Please consult with your specific program to confirm\.

title: Requesting transfer credit
content_markdown:
If you took courses outside of UBC or you are transferring to UBC from another institution, you may be able to request transfer credits for your previous coursework, depending on your scenario\.

You’ll need to submit your transcript to UBC to process any transfer credit\.

## Students applying to UBC[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/transfer\-credits/requesting\-transfer\-credit/\#students\-applying\-to\-ubc](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/transfer-credits/requesting-transfer-credit/#students-applying-to-ubc)

If you’re planning on [applying to UBC](https://you.ubc.ca/), please make sure you’ve updated your post\-secondary attendance record within the Academic History section of your [Education Planner BC](https://www.educationplannerbc.ca/) profile\.

UBC Admissions will review your attendance background and will ask you to submit your transcripts during the review process\. If you are admitted, you will be assigned any eligible [transfer credits in Workday](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/degree-planning/viewing-your-transfer-credit-or-high-school-and-ap-ib-credit/) after you accept your admission offer\. In many cases, transfer credit can be viewed on the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/) before accepting an offer\.

## Current students[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/transfer\-credits/requesting\-transfer\-credit/\#current\-students](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/transfer-credits/requesting-transfer-credit/#current-students)

If you are a student in the Faculty of Arts or Faculty of Science and would like to request a re\-evaluation of any of your General Credits, please complete the [Transfer Credit Evaluation Request](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_bBGurnbl1TTkH54) form\.

For students in faculties other than Arts or Science, please contact an [Academic Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) in your faculty to request a re\-evaluation\.

Not all requests for specific credits are granted\. Course re\-evaluations may take 4 to 8 weeks or longer\. Plan your course registration accordingly\. Contact your faculty’s advising office prior to registering to learn which courses you need to stay on track for your degree\.

### Opportunities to study elsewhere

If you’re a current UBC student and would like to take a course at another institution, you can apply to the [Go Global program](https://global.ubc.ca/go-global) for exchange opportunities or [take courses at UBC Okanagan](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/cross-campus-registration/)\.

You will need a [Letter of Permission](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/letter-permission/) from your faculty to study at another institution\.

## Former UBC Okanagan Students[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/transfer\-credits/requesting\-transfer\-credit/\#former\-ubc\-okanagan\-students](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/transfer-credits/requesting-transfer-credit/#former-ubc-okanagan-students)

If you’re currently a UBC Vancouver student who was admitted from UBC Okanagan, your UBC Okanagan courses will remain as part of your UBC records\.

You can find out how your UBC Okanagan course translates to a UBC Vancouver course with the [https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/courses/equivalency\-search](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/equivalency-search)[BC Transfer Guide](https://www.bctransferguide.ca/)\.

If you were granted UBC Okanagan transfer credits based on your previous studies at other post\-secondary institutions or through university\-level course work in high school \(IB, AP, or A\-levels\), the transfer credits will be re\-evaluated for UBC Vancouver and may result in changes\.

## Non\-Degree students[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/transfer\-credits/requesting\-transfer\-credit/\#non\-degree\-students](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/transfer-credits/requesting-transfer-credit/#non-degree-students)

Non\-Degree students, such as those in [visiting students](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-visiting/), [unclassified students](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-unclassified/), or those in [Access Studies](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-access-studies/) do not receive transfer credit\.

## Second\-degree students[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/transfer\-credits/requesting\-transfer\-credit/\#second\-degree\-students](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/transfer-credits/requesting-transfer-credit/#second-degree-students)

Students pursuing a second degree at UBC do not receive transfer credits from their previous degree\. Please contact an [Academic Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) in your faculty to find out about second degree requirements and how to plan for registration\. 

## Summer courses[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/transfer\-credits/requesting\-transfer\-credit/\#summer\-courses](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/transfer-credits/requesting-transfer-credit/#summer-courses)

You may be eligible for transfer credit if you completed courses at a different university in the summer after you accepted your UBC admission offer\. Those credits will be evaluated in September or October once UBC receives your summer transcript with final grades\.

## Submitting your transcript for transfer credits[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/transfer\-credits/requesting\-transfer\-credit/\#submitting\-your\-transcript\-for\-transfer\-credits](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/transfer-credits/requesting-transfer-credit/#submitting-your-transcript-for-transfer-credits)

If you’ ve applied to UBC, please follow email instructions and timelines from the Undergraduate Admissions office to submit the transcripts required for your application\.

If you’ve been admitted, have accepted your offer of admission, and submitted all your transcript\(s\) required for admission, please follow instructions on the [document submission page](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/submit-documents/) and arrange for your final official transcript to be sent to UBC as soon as possible\.

## Transfer credit search tool[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/transfer\-credits/requesting\-transfer\-credit/\#transfer\-credit\-search\-tool](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/transfer-credits/requesting-transfer-credit/#transfer-credit-search-tool)

Find how courses from your institution transfer to UBC through the [BC Transfer Guide](http://www.bctransferguide.ca/)\.

title: Transfer credit terms
content_markdown:
Review commonly used transfer credit terms and their definitions below\. 

- **Row 1**

  - **Header cell 1:**
  
    Term
  
  - **Header cell 2:**
  
    Definition

- **Row 2**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Articulation
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Articulation is the formal process of determining if coursework completed at another institution is eligible for transfer credit at UBC\. It is a collaborative process that involves Admissions Advisors and Transfer Credit staff who determine the appropriate subject and transfer credit values, as well as faculty articulators who compare the original course content to specific UBC courses\.

- **Row 3**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    BC Transfer Guide
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    The [BC Transfer Guide](https://www.bctransferguide.ca/) is an online tool that allows you to search for courses you took in another institution—within or outside of BC—and how they can be transferred to UBC\.

- **Row 4**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Credit value
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    UBC courses are based on semester credits\. Courses from different credit systems such as quarter credits are converted to equivalent UBC semester credits in the [BC Transfer Guide](https://www.bctransferguide.ca/)\.

- **Row 5**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Effective date
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    The time period within which the course must be completed to receive transfer credit\.

- **Row 6**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Elective
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Elective or “ELEV” transfer credit indicates a general form of transfer credit that has no specific equivalent course at UBC\.

- **Row 7**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    First\-year credit
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    AP, IB or A\-levels exam results that meet the minimum requirements listed on the [Undergraduate Programs and Admissions website](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/applied/first-year-credit/) are eligible for first\-year credit\. Official final exam results need to be sent to the UBC Undergraduate Admissions Office by examination boards for credit to be added on the student’s record in Workday\.

- **Row 8**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    General Credit
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    When an exact UBC equivalent course does not exist within the same department, general transfer credit is granted as close as possible to the course completed elsewhere\. General Credit will indicate the equivalent subject code, year level, and credit value\.  
      
    Example: *HIST\_V 1st*

- **Row 9**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    General Credit with Exemption
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Courses that do not match a specific UBC course but have sufficient overlap in learning outcomes may be assigned General Credit with an Exemption for a specific UBC course\.  
      
    Students with General Credit with Exemption are considered to have completed the Exempted course\.  
      
    Example: MATH\_O 1st \(3\), exempt MATH\_O 100

- **Row 10**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Letter of Permission \(LOP\)
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    A [Letter of Permission \(LOP\)](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/letter-permission/) is an approval from your faculty that the course\(s\) you are planning on taking at another institution will transfer back to your UBC degree\.  
      
    Current UBC students who wish to register in any course at another institution must obtain prior permission from their faculty, in the form of an LOP, before taking courses elsewhere\.  
      
    Requests for an LOP are reviewed on a case\-by\-case basis, and approval is not guaranteed\.

- **Row 11**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    No Credit
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Courses that have been evaluated and deemed not transferable to UBC such as high school equivalency, pre\-university, foundational, professional, applied, technical or other non\-academic courses\.  
      
    English literature and English writing and composition courses taken at institutions located in countries where English is not the principal language are not transferable to UBC, regardless of the language of instruction at the institution\.

- **Row 12**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Not for Credit in Science
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Some transfer credit agreements on the [BC Transfer Guide](https://www.bctransferguide.ca/) indicate that another institution’s course is eligible for transfer credit, but not in the Faculty of Science or in other Science\-based programs, such as Engineering, or Land and Food Systems\.  
      
    The following is an example of how it may be displayed:  
    *CHEM\_V 1NC*  
    Although the course may be considered for credit in a science subject, such as CHEM with corresponding credit value under the “Credits” column indicating the number of transfer credits of general first\-year chemistry, the original course cannot be used to satisfy Faculty of Science degree requirements\. Other faculties may apply such transfer credit differently\.

- **Row 13**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Specific Credit
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Courses that have significant overlap with a specific UBC course are granted Specific Credit\.  
      
    Specific transfer credit will be used as if the course was taken at UBC\. Unless approved by your faculty, you should not register in the same course at UBC for which you have already received specific transfer credit, as you cannot receive the same credit twice\.

## Transfer credit search tool[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/transfer\-credits/transfer\-credit\-terms/\#transfer\-credit\-search\-tool](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/transfer-credits/transfer-credit-terms/#transfer-credit-search-tool)

Find how courses from your institution transfer to UBC through the [BC Transfer Guide](https://www.bctransferguide.ca/)\.

title: Changing your degree program or campus
content_markdown:
## Eligibility requirements[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/changing\-degree\-program\-or\-campus/\#eligibility\-requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/changing-degree-program-or-campus/#eligibility-requirements)

You must meet all of the following requirements to change your degree program at the same campus or switch to another campus:

-   Minimum [admission criteria](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/university-college-transfer/#section-1) for transfer students
-   [Specific requirements](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/university-college-transfer/#section-1) for the program you are planning to transfer to
-   Competitive academic performance described in [Post\-Secondary UBC Admission Requirements](http://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/university-college-transfer/)

## If you’re changing programs[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/changing\-degree\-program\-or\-campus/\#if\-youre\-changing\-programs](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/changing-degree-program-or-campus/#if-youre-changing-programs)

-   Make sure you submit all the documents required for your new program by the application deadline\. Some degree programs may require a portfolio, supplemental application, or Personal Profile\.
-   At least 50% of your required credits must be completed under your new program for you to graduate\.
-   Research the degree requirements for your intended program of study\. Degree program requirements are unique to each program, regardless of campus\.

### Additional resources

-   [UBC Vancouver course planning](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/)
-   [UBC Okanagan faculties, schools, and colleges](https://okanagan.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-schools-and-colleges-0)

## If you’re changing campuses[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/changing\-degree\-program\-or\-campus/\#if\-youre\-changing\-campuses](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/changing-degree-program-or-campus/#if-youre-changing-campuses)

If you’re applying to change to a program at another campus, talk to an Academic Advisor in the program you wish to attend\. You must determine how your previously completed courses can meet registration and degree requirements\.

-   [Academic Advising at UBC Vancouver](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/)
-   [Academic Advising at UBC Okanagan](http://students.ok.ubc.ca/advising/welcome.html)

### Course equivalencies between campuses

UBC courses may be eligible for credit towards a UBC degree program on either campus\. This means credits from a different campus will not be converted to transfer credit, but may be equivalent to credits for a similar course, also known as course equivalency\.

-   Courses that are determined to be equivalent between campuses may be used to satisfy course\-specific degree requirements\.
-   Courses that are not equivalent may be applied to degree requirements as discipline\-specific or general elective credit\.

Use the [https://www\.bctransferguide\.ca/](https://www.bctransferguide.ca/)[BC Transfer Guide](https://www.bctransferguide.ca/) to check if a UBC course is equivalent between campuses\.

If a course does not appear on the BC Transfer Guide, then it does not have an established equivalency and may be applied towards degree requirements as discipline\-specific or general elective credits\. Please speak to an Academic Advisor to find out how your credits may be applied\.

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/changing\-degree\-program\-or\-campus/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/changing-degree-program-or-campus/#how-to-apply)

January 15 is the general deadline to apply for a change of degree or campus for the upcoming Winter Session\. Be sure to check if your program has any additional degree\-specific deadlines\.

Visit the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/) and log in with your CWL\. You can then select the “Re\-admission/Change Program” option and will be asked to follow next steps\.

Applying to change your degree program doesn’t mean giving up your seat in your current program\. You do not give up your current spot until you accept your offer to a new program\.

## If you receive a program or campus change offer[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/changing\-degree\-program\-or\-campus/\#if\-you\-receive\-a\-program\-or\-campus\-change\-offer](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/changing-degree-program-or-campus/#if-you-receive-a-program-or-campus-change-offer)

When you receive your offer on the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/), you will be provided with a specific deadline to accept your offer by\. You’ll be required to pay an acceptance deposit to accept your offer\. This deposit will be applied towards future tuition\.

For any degree planning questions in your new program, you can connect with [academic advising](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/)\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/changing\-degree\-program\-or\-campus/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/changing-degree-program-or-campus/#if-you-have-questions)

For information about degree requirements, program planning, or course registration, contact your Academic Advisor: 

-   [UBC Vancouver Academic Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/)
-   [UBC Okanagan Academic Advising](http://students.ok.ubc.ca/advising/contact.html)

For questions regarding applying to change programs or financial planning and support, please connect with your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

title: Course change dates
content_markdown:
## Making changes to your courses[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/course\-change\-dates/\#making\-changes\-to\-your\-courses](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/course-change-dates/#making-changes-to-your-courses)

### Before the add/drop deadline

Each term, before the add/drop deadline, also known as the course change deadline, you may add, drop, change, or request [Credit/D/Fail](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/creditdfail-grading/) or [auditing status](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/auditing-courses/) for your courses without having the record of registration appear on your academic record\. 

If you drop a course before the course change deadline, you will be eligible for a full [tuition refund](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/tuition-refunds/)\. 

Make sure you are dropping the course from your registered courses and not from your saved schedule\. Removing courses from your saved schedule is not considered dropping those courses\. You can confirm that you have successfully dropped the course by reviewing your timetable\.

You must drop your course in [Workday](http://myworkday.ubc.ca/) by 11:59 pm PT on the course change deadline\.

View step\-by\-step instructions on [adding](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/registering-for-individual-course-sections/), [dropp](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/dropping-a-course/)[i](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/dropping-a-course/)[ng](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/dropping-a-course/), or [swapping](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/swapping-a-course/) a course in Workday\.

### After the add/drop deadline

-   To add a course, you’ll need permission from your faculty\. You’ll also be required to submit the [Change of Registration \(Add/Drop\) Form](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/registration_adddrop_form_2024_fall.pdf) \(pdf\)\.
-   You will not be able to switch between [Credit/D/Fail](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/creditdfail-grading/) and percentage grading\. 
-   You will receive a “W” standing on your academic record if you choose to drop a course after the deadline\. Talk to your [academic advising office](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) if you are facing extenuating circumstances that require you to do so\.
-   Depending on your withdrawal date, you may be eligible for a [partial refund](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/tuition-refunds/)\.
-   View step\-by\-step instructions on [withdrawing from a course](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/withdrawing-from-a-course/) in Workday\.

### What is a W standing? 

A “**W**” standing is recorded on a student’s transcript when they withdraw from a course **after** the add/drop deadline\. While it is not used for computing averages, it may impact applications for future studies\.

### Considerations before dropping or withdrawing from courses

Your credit load directly impacts your eligibility for [awards and student loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/maintaining-awards-loan-eligibility/), [UBC bursary](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/ubc-bursary-program/), [UBC student housing](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/eligibility/#academic), [immigration](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/immigration-impacts-part-time-studies-withdrawing-courses/), and [payment\-free/interest–free status](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/student-loan-interest/) for past government loans\. 

Review the course load requirements for these programs before dropping or withdrawing from your courses\.

## Summer Session[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/course\-change\-dates/\#summer\-session](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/course-change-dates/#summer-session)

Course change dates vary in the Summer Session depending on the start and end date and length of the course\.

For course\-specific add/drop and withdrawal deadlines, [search your course information](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/viewing-the-course-schedule/) in Workday before the start of classes as the course change deadlines come up very quickly for summer courses\.

Get more information through the [Academic Calendar](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/dates-and-deadlines)\.

For course\-specific add/drop and withdrawal deadlines, [search your course information](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/viewing-the-course-schedule/) in Workday\.

Get more information through the [Academic Calendar](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/dates-and-deadlines)\.

title: Cross-campus registration
content_markdown:
If you’re a UBC Vancouver undergraduate, you can take up to 15 credits worth of courses at the Okanagan campus\. Registration and enrolment are reviewed on a case\-by\-case basis\.

UBC Vancouver graduate students can also apply for cross\-campus registration through the [Authorization and Course Registration Form](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/forms/authorization-course-registration-ubc-ubco)\. For more information, graduate students can visit the [UBC Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies’ website](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/), or contact their program staff or Graduate Advisor\.

If you’re transferring to the UBC Okanagan campus and switching to an Okanagan degree program, apply for a [change in campus or faculty](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/changing-degree-program-or-campus/) through the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/) \(ASC\)\.

## Check your eligibility[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/cross\-campus\-registration/\#check\-your\-eligibility](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/cross-campus-registration/#check-your-eligibility)

The information below applies to **undergraduate** programs and courses\. 

To be considered for registration at the Okanagan campus, you must meet the following requirements:

-   You are registered as a UBC Vancouver undergraduate student\.
-   You have completed a minimum of **24 credits** with percentage grades\.
-   You have not failed a course in the most recent 24 credits\.
-   You have a minimum overall average of 68% on your most recent 24 credits\.
-   You have satisfied all the prerequisites for the course you’re requesting to take at UBC Okanagan\.

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/cross\-campus\-registration/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/cross-campus-registration/#how-to-apply)

You will not be able to register for cross\-campus courses by yourself\. An Enrolment Services staff member at the Okanagan campus will help you complete your registration\.

Faculties reserve the right to decline a request if the course is in high demand, or if the equivalent course is available at the UBC Vancouver campus in either the Summer or Winter Session\.

Enrolment may be limited in some or all courses due to high demand from UBC Okanagan students\. If registration has already started, check the course schedule to see how many seats remain in the courses you are requesting\. Courses that are full or very close to full are less likely to be approved for cross campus registration\.

To apply for a cross\-campus course, follow these steps:

1.  Download and complete the [UBC Vancouver cross\-campus request form](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/cross_campus_registration_request_form.pdf) \(pdf\)\. If you are a **graduate** student, please complete the [Authorization and Course Registration Form](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/forms/authorization-course-registration-ubc-ubco) instead\.
2.  Submit the request form to your [academic advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) for approval\.
3.  Your academic advisor will then send the form to Enrolment Services staff at the UBC Okanagan campus, and it will be forwarded to the appropriate faculty at the Okanagan campus for review\.
4.  You will receive an email notifying you if your request has been approved\. Cross\-campus registration is typically scheduled on the Visiting students registration date for **Summer and Winter**, respectively\. You will receive a registration token and an email notifying you that the token has been granted\. You can then register in the approved course on Workday, if there is space\.
5.  You will receive an email with your registration outcome for your requested course\(s\)\.

If you are unable to download and submit the form by email, you can print and complete it by hand and bring it to your [academic advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) in person\.

### Application deadlines

| Academic session | Deadline |
| --- | --- |
| Summer Session | April 15 |
| Winter Session | August 15 |

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/cross\-campus\-registration/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/cross-campus-registration/#if-you-have-questions)

If you’re an undergraduate student, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

If you’re a graduate student, please visit the [UBC Graduate Studies website](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/) and the [Authorization and Course Registration Form](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/forms/authorization-course-registration-ubc-ubco) for more information\. You can also talk to your program advisor\.

title: How to register for courses
content_markdown:
## Find out when you register[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/register\-courses/\#find\-out\-when\-you\-register](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/register-courses/#find-out-when-you-register)

The general [registration dates](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/registration-dates/) for each academic session are posted online and organized by year level, or Class Standing\. You can view your Class Standing under the Summary tab in your Workday student profile\.

[Registration appointments](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/viewing-your-registration-appointment/) are usually set in early June for the Winter session\. You’ll receive an email around early June to let you know that your registration appointment is available in [Workday](https://myworkday.ubc.ca/)\.

Changes to your academic record can impact your registration date and time\. If you are expecting changes to your academic record, check Workday for any updates to your registration appointment\.

### If you do not receive a registration email

If you accept your admission offer after early June, you may not receive an email as the registration appointment notification period may have already passed\. If this happens, you can still register by following the steps on this page\. If you have questions, please contact your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\. 

## Pay your deposit, if applicable[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/register\-courses/\#pay\-your\-deposit\-if\-applicable](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/register-courses/#pay-your-deposit-if-applicable)

If you’re new to UBC, you must pay a non\-refundable acceptance deposit, which will count as your first registration deposit\. Instructions are included in your offer of admission\.

If you are enrolled in a certificate or diploma program, you must pay a [registration deposit](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/fees/policies-fees#17933)\. Once you have registered for that session, your deposit cannot be refunded or transferred to a future session\.

Graduate students should check with their specific program for information regarding acceptance and registration deposits\.

## Plan your courses[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/register\-courses/\#plan\-your\-courses](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/register-courses/#plan-your-courses)

### Check your program requirements

You can find degree requirements and specific requirements for each program in the [Academic Calendar](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/)\.

You can also review your program requirements in the [Academic Progress Report](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/degree-planning/viewing-your-academic-progress-report/) \(APR\) and consider how and when you can fill any major, minor, concentration, or specialization course requirements\.

If you need help with degree requirements or course planning, review the information on your faculty’s website\. Connect with your [academic advising office](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) if you have additional questions\.

### Build your saved schedule

In Workday, saved schedules are draft class timetables that you can create before you register to help you plan out your courses\.

After logging into [Workday](https://myworkday.ubc.ca/), you can create multiple saved schedules, in case one or more of the courses on your first saved schedule are full\. You can add lectures, standard timetables, and other course components to existing saved schedules\.

For the Winter Session, you must create a saved schedule for each term separately\.

Learn how to create a saved schedule and more in Workday through [course registration tutorials](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/)\.  

### Review additional considerations

Some students, including international students and those who are receiving awards or funds from student loans, must register in enough credits to maintain their immigration or funding eligibility\. 

If these scenarios apply to you, review the pages below and make sure you meet your registration requirements:

-   [Awards and student loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/awards-scholarships-bursaries/maintaining-awards-loan-eligibility/)
-   [Immigrations impacts of part\-time studies](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/immigration-impacts-part-time-studies-withdrawing-courses/)

## Get ready for registration[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/register\-courses/\#get\-ready\-for\-registration](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/register-courses/#get-ready-for-registration)

Learn how to [register for courses](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/) in Workday\. You should register for both your Term 1 and Term 2 courses at the time of your registration appointment\.

Below are tips to help you with course registration:

-   Courses fill up quickly, so register for both terms as early as you can\. 
-   Have multiple saved schedules ready in case courses are full\.
-   Troubleshoot and [resolve issues](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/troubleshooting-your-saved-schedule/) in your saved schedule before your registration appointment\.
-   If you are blocked from registering for a course because a pre\-requisite is missing from your account, connect with your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) for feedback\.
-   Check for and resolve any [holds on your account](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/resolving-a-hold-on-your-record/)\.
-   After you register, you can add or drop classes until the [course change deadline](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/course-change-dates/)\.

### Common registration issues

If you’re having trouble registering, make sure you meet the following requirements:

-   You are eligible to register for the session and meet any required prerequisites\.
-   You are registering on or after your registration date and time\.
-   You have paid your [acceptance or registration deposit](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/fees/policies-fees#17933), if applicable\.
-   You have paid any other outstanding fees\.

Learn how to [troubleshoot your course registration](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/troubleshooting-your-course-registration/)\. You can only access this function if your course registration is open\.

### If a course is full

Courses may fill up, particularly those required by the program\. Follow the tips below if your course is full\.

-   Learn how to [get on the waitlist](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/adding-a-course-waitlist-to-your-saved-schedule/) in Workday\.
-   Check the course schedule regularly as additional seats often become available later in the registration period\.
-   When a course is full and does not have available waitlist seats, it will be listed as “closed”\.
-   Contact the department offering the course to check if other sections of the course will be released\.
-   If you’re in your last year of study and need a specific course to graduate, your faculty or department will usually  help to enrol you\. Contact your [academic advising office](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) for more information\.
-   Enrolment Services cannot register students into classes that are still open or that are already full\.

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/register\-courses/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/register-courses/#additional-resources)

-   [Course registration tutorials](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/)
-   [Registration dates](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/registration-dates/)
-   [Course change dates](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/course-change-dates/)
-   [Acceptance and registration deposits](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/fees/policies-fees#17933)
-   [Introduction to UBC classes](https://students.ubc.ca/new-to-ubc/introduction-ubc-classes/)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/registration/register\-courses/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/registration/register-courses/#if-you-have-questions)

For help on planning your degree or choosing your courses, please contact your faculty’s [academic advising office](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/)\. 

If you’re having problems with registration, read the [Workday tutorials](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/course-registration/) first\. If you still have questions, please connect with an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.
