title: What to do after attending career events
content_markdown:
## Reflect on your experience[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/events\-workshops/what\-do\-after\-attending\-career\-events/\#reflect\-on\-your\-experience](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/what-do-after-attending-career-events/#reflect-on-your-experience)

Attending a career fair is one step towards cultivating a strong professional network and a career that matters to you\. Take time to consider what you learned and what your next steps might be\.

1.  Revisit any goals that you set\. What went well? Where were you challenged?
2.  What did you learn about your career options and employers or industries that interest you?
3.  What will you do differently at your next event?

## Stay connected with employers[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/events\-workshops/what\-do\-after\-attending\-career\-events/\#stay\-connected\-with\-employers](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/what-do-after-attending-career-events/#stay-connected-with-employers)

Maintaining contact with your new connections can feel hard and uncomfortable\. As you cultivate your network, practice quality over quantity\. If you had a good conversation with an employer who seemed to be engaged, reach out to them on LinkedIn, other social media or by email to remind them of that conversation and thank them for their time\. Let them know what you appreciated about the conversation and that you’d like to keep in touch\.

As time passes, try to consider how you can add value to their world\. Did you come across an article related to their work? Forward it to them\. Did they announce a major change on LinkedIn? Acknowledge their efforts and accomplishments\. You can learn more about [maintaining your network](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/what-do-after-attending-career-events/#maintain-network) below\.

Consider that cultivating professional relationships doesn’t have to be much different than cultivating friendships\. You don’t have to develop strong friendships with your professional contacts but many of the same principles apply, including the following:

-   Value should be reciprocal\. In other words, it’s not just about you getting a job\. 
-   Engaging with one another should be enjoyable\.

Remember, building professional relationships, or networking, is an essential career building activity\. Think of it as a long\-term investment in your future that can help you with the following:

-   Access opportunities
-   Improve your industry knowledge
-   Consider your interests and identify your career goals
-   Gain referrals and recommendations

### Connect on LinkedIn

LinkedIn notifies you if someone has a work anniversary, job change, or birthday\. This is a great opportunity to stay connected with your new contact and reach out to them in casual and formal ways\. You can also check out their profiles to find pages and people worth following\.

When you request to connect, make sure you include a personalized introduction email so that they don’t think you are spamming them\. Remind them of your previous meeting and let them know you value their time and experience\.

## Join the UBC Hub of Ten Thousand Coffees[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/events\-workshops/what\-do\-after\-attending\-career\-events/\#join\-the\-ubc\-hub\-of\-ten\-thousand\-coffees](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/what-do-after-attending-career-events/#join-the-ubc-hub-of-ten-thousand-coffees)

With the [UBC Hub of Ten Thousand Coffees](https://www.tenthousandcoffees.com/schools/ubc), sponsored by RBC Future Launch, having career\-driven conversations is easy\. You’ll receive one introduction per month to a fellow student or alum based on your career interests and goals\.

Read the platform’s [Terms of Use](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/ten_thousand_coffees_terms_of_usee.pdf) \(pdf\) before signing up\.

1.  Create a free profile on [The UBC Hub](https://www.tenthousandcoffees.com/schools/ubc)\.
2.  Select your area of study or industry, interests, and goals\.
3.  Each month the Hub will introduce you to a new contact that you have something in common with\.
4.  Browse thousands of member profiles and connect directly through the message feature\.

Once you sign up to the platform, matches are made automatically and optimized to your preferences\. You are even given suggested talking points\!

### Set up an informational interview

If you’d like to have a follow\-up conversation with someone you met, request an informational interview\. If you met a recruiter who told you to apply online, you could connect with them, but also research LinkedIn for people in the company’s roles/departments with whom you could speak as well and reach out to them\. Review the [informational interviews guide](https://students.ubc.ca/career/career-resources/informational-interviews/) to learn more\.

### Find more people to connect with

Your new contact may be able to introduce you to others in your field of interest\. If you feel it is appropriate, ask if they know anyone else you should talk to\. When they make a suggestion, ask if they can introduce you directly\. If this isn’t possible, name them as your referral source when you reach out to the potential new contact independently\.

## Tips to maintain your network

It’s important not to overwhelm your new contacts by asking for too much\. Consider what you can offer that they would benefit from or enjoy\. Remember, relationships that are mutually beneficial are the most successful\. Here are some ideas to get you started:

-   **Send them a note if you’re attending an industry event\.**  
    If it’s a popular event for their industry, send them a quick note to let them know you will be attending and hope to see them there\.
-   **Keep them in the loop and acknowledge their support\.**  
    Sharing your successes will fuel their interest in keeping in touch, and if they’ve helped you in any way, let them know\.
-   **Ask for their advice\.**  
    If you have a specific question, ask for their advice via LinkedIn messaging or email\. Be as specific as possible in your question and ensure you remind them of who you are and what you talked about during the event\.
-   **Offer them professional or personal leads\.**  
    If you know of a project or event that would be of interest to them, or have met someone they might value speaking to, make an introduction\. This doesn’t have to remain in the realm of work but can be connected to known hobbies and interests as well\.

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/events\-workshops/what\-do\-after\-attending\-career\-events/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/what-do-after-attending-career-events/#additional-resources)

title: Working in Canada
content_markdown:
> > IRCC Co\-op work permit update
> 
> > Read the [latest announcement](https://students.ubc.ca/news/2026-04-09/ircc-update-for-students-in-a-co-op-internship-or-practicum/) for students participating in a Co\-op, practicum, or internship\.

## About working in Canada[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/\#about\-working\-in\-canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/#about-working-in-canada)

Work experience can help you prepare for your career, gain exposure to the Canadian workplace, earn extra money, and form a closer connection to the local community\.

As an international student, there are several types of work you can do in Canada\. Some of them will require applying for a specific work permit\.

## Permits required to work in Canada[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/\#permits\-required\-to\-work\-in\-canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/#permits-required-to-work-in-canada)

| Type of work | Required permits |
| --- | --- |
| On\-campus work | You don’t need a work permit to work on campus while attending UBC\. If you meet the requirements, you can work unlimited hours on\-campus based on your study permit\. Check your [eligibility to work on\-campus](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/campus-work/)\. |
| Off\-campus work | Students in degree, diploma, certificate programs, or on exchange do not need a work permit to work off campus while attending UBC\. If you meet the requirements, you can work off\-campus for up to 24 hours a week during academic terms, and unlimited hours during your program’s scheduled breaks\. Check your [eligibility to work off\-campus](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/off-campus-work/)\. |
| Co\-op or student work placements | While a co\-op work permit is no longer required for this type of work, make sure you meet the [eligibility requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/co-op-or-student-work-placements/#confirm-eligibility) to participate in a student work placement\. |
| Working after graduation | If you want to stay in Canada and work after graduation, consider applying for the [Post\-Graduation Work Permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/post-graduation-work-permit/)\. |
| Work permit for your spouse or common\-law partner | Depending on your situation, your spouse or common\-law partner might be able to apply for an [open work permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/documentation-family/#status-in-canada) while you study full\-time and/or while you work on the PGWP, if you meet the requirements\. |

## Volunteer or unpaid work that is not required to complete your academic program[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/\#volunteer\-or\-unpaid\-work\-that\-is\-not\-required\-to\-complete\-your\-academic\-program](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/#volunteer-or-unpaid-work-that-is-not-required-to-complete-your-academic-program)

In Canada, the [definition of work for immigration purposes](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-manuals/temporary-residents/foreign-workers/what-is-work.html) is not based on payment, but how competitive your activities are in the labour market\. Volunteer positions, internships, or unpaid work might be considered work, even if you are not paid\. For example, if you volunteer for a position that is normally performed by paid employees , such as photocopying or customer service, it is considered working in Canada\.

If your volunteer position or internship is considered work, you must have the right work authorization before you start\. Unpaid work hours are counted towards the 24 hours per week \(20 hours before Nov 8, 2024\) of off\-campus work you may be eligible for as a full\-time student\. If you work with children, seniors, in healthcare settings, or in agriculture, you might also need a medical exam and the right conditions on your study and/or work permit – check the next section\.

## If you work with children or seniors, in healthcare settings, or in agriculture[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/\#if\-you\-work\-with\-children\-or\-seniors\-in\-healthcare\-settings\-or\-in\-agriculture](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/#if-you-work-with-children-or-seniors-in-healthcare-settings-or-in-agriculture)

You need to complete an immigration [medical exam](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/medical-police/medical-exams/requirements-temporary-residents.html) and have the right conditions on your study and/or work permit if:

-   You work in jobs which bring you into close contact with people, such as:
    -   Workers in health\-care settings or on a hospital campus
    -   Clinical laboratory workers
    -   Patient attendants in nursing and geriatric homes
    -   Medical electives and physicians on short\-term locums
    -   Workers in primary or secondary school settings, or workers in child\-care settings
    -   Domestics
    -   Workers who give in\-home care to children, the elderly and the disabled
    -   Day nursery employees and
    -   Other similar jobs
-   You are a medical student\.
-   You will work in agriculture and have lived in a [designated country](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/medical-police/medical-exams/requirements-temporary-residents/country-requirements.html) for more than 6 months in the past year\.

This is required even if your position is unpaid\. See the [list of example occupations](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/medical-police/medical-exams/requirements-temporary-residents.html#needs)\.

Even if you do not work directly with vulnerable populations, you might require a medical exam based on your place of work, no matter what your position is\. For example in\-person positions in a hospital \(even if you do not directly care for patients, such as research, administrative, or janitorial positions\) or in a daycare \(even if you do not directly care for children, such as administrative positions\)\. 

If you are unsure, contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support before starting your position\.

### When to complete the medical exam

If you will likely work in these kinds of positions, it is best to complete the medical exam before you apply for your study or work permit\. It’s also possible to take the medical exam after you have received your study or work permit, then apply to change the conditions on your permit afterwards\. 

Whether you complete your medical exam with your initial permit application or at a later date, you will need to wait for your application to be processed\.

You cannot start the position until you have received a study or work permit with the appropriate conditions\.

### When you may not need a medical exam

If you previously completed a medical exam with your initial study permit and don’t have a restrictive condition, such as “*Not authorized to work in childcare, primary/secondary school teaching, health service field occupations”,* you would not need to complete another medical exam during the validity of your current study permit unless you lived in one or more of these [countries or territories](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/medical-police/medical-exams/requirements-temporary-residents/country-requirements.html) for at least 6 months in a row within the last year\.

For your next study or work permit application, if you took your medical exam within the past 12 months, it is still valid and you can upload the same e\-medical\. If you completed a medical exam in the past 5 years, you might be eligible for a [temporary medical exam](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/news/notices/2022-foreign-exempt-ime.html) policy which has been extended to October 5, 2029\. Normally you would need to complete another medical exam for your next study or work permit application, however with this temporary policy you can use a medical exam from the past 5 years without taking another exam\. When you prepare your study or work permit application, answer yes to the question in the questionnaire about medical exams, upload your most recent e\-medical from the past 5 years, and include a request in your letter of explanation to have the right conditions on your study/work permit to work in jobs that require medical exams\. The officer who reviews your application will make the final decision and could request a medical exam\. You’ll need to wait to receive your new study/work permit to confirm it has the correct conditions\. 

Contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support if you’ve lived in one or more of these [countries or territories](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/medical-police/medical-exams/requirements-temporary-residents/country-requirements.html) for at least 6 months in a row since your last medical exam\.

### Medical exam requirements

You must book an appointment with an IRCC\-approved [panel physician](http://www.cic.gc.ca/pp-md/pp-list.aspx), who will send your results to IRCC\. Ask the doctor for a copy of your medical exam report, also known as your “e\-medical”, and submit it with your study or work permit application\. Your medical exam results are valid for 12 months from the date of your exam, or you might be eligible for the temporary policy where you can use a medical exam from the past 5 years \(check previous section\)\.

Include a letter of explanation asking specifically for your work permit to indicate that you may work in these occupations\. Upload this in “Client Information” under *Optional Documents\.*

## Starting your own business[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/\#starting\-your\-own\-business](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/#starting-your-own-business)

If you’d like to start your own business in British Columbia, please check the BC government’s [step\-by\-step guide](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/employment-business/business/managing-a-business/starting-a-business)\. You can also check their [resources](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/employment-business/business/small-business/resources) and [help](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/employment-business/business/small-business/help-for-small-businesses-and-entrepreneurs) for small businesses and entrepreneurs\.

International Student Advising is not able to provide advice on taxes or setting up a business\.

If you are self\-employed, be sure to track your hours of work\. Be careful not to work more hours than you are authorized to\.

## Other types of work permits unrelated to studies[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/\#other\-types\-of\-work\-permits\-unrelated\-to\-studies](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/#other-types-of-work-permits-unrelated-to-studies)

Depending on your situation, you may be eligible to apply for other types of work permits\. In general, work permits unrelated to studies can be difficult to qualify for and might take a long time to process\. Please visit the [IRCC website](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/permit.html) to learn about your options\. Students from certain countries which Canada has an agreement with might be eligible for [International Experience Canada](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/iec.html), such as the Working Holiday Work Permit\.

If you’d like more information on other types of work permits, you can [contact IRCC](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/tips-communicating-immigration-refugees-citizenship-canada-ircc/) or find an [authorized immigration representative](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/find-regulated-immigration-consultant-or-lawyer/) for advice\.

 **Mexican and U\.S\. citizens with a bachelor’s or licenciatura**

Individuals in certain fields may be eligible for a CUSMA work permit, formerly known as NAFTA\. International Student Advising does not advise on eligibility for work permits under CUSMA, but you can [find detailed information](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-manuals/temporary-residents/foreign-workers/international-free-trade-agreements/cusma.html) on the IRCC website\.

### Working for an employer outside Canada while you are physically in Canada

Working for an employer located outside Canada while you are in Canada is outside the jurisdiction of IRCC\. As per the Canadian immigration regulations, long\-distance work \(by telephone or Internet\) done by a temporary resident, such as a student whose employer is outside Canada and who gets paid from outside Canada, is not considered to be [“work” in Canada](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-manuals/temporary-residents/foreign-workers/what-is-work.html)\.

## Part\-time studies or taking time away from studies[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/\#part\-time\-studies\-or\-taking\-time\-away\-from\-studies](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/#part-time-studies-or-taking-time-away-from-studies)

If you’re no longer studying full\-time, you are not eligible to work during the term you are part\-time or are not enrolled \(for example, you are on leave\), or during the scheduled breaks before or after the term\. There may also be potential impacts to your status in Canada\. Learn more about how [enrolment impacts immigration](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/immigration-impacts-part-time-studies-withdrawing-courses/), including part\-time studies, and [taking time away from studies](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/taking-time-away-school-international/)\.

## Get help on starting your career[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/\#get\-help\-on\-starting\-your\-career](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/#get-help-on-starting-your-career)

-   [Launch a Career in Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/career/events-workshops/launch-career-canada/)  
    Held every March, hear the stories of former UBC international students now working in Canada across different industries\.
-   [UBC Career Resources](https://students.ubc.ca/career/career-resources/)  
    Improve your resume and cover letter, prepare for interviews, and more\.
-   [CareersOnline](https://ubc-csm.symplicity.com/index.php/pid532770?)  
    Browse and apply for work or volunteer positions on UBC’s online career resources platform\.
-   [Work Learn Program](https://students.ubc.ca/career/work-learn-program/)  
    Develop valuable skills through a part\-time, on\-campus job\.

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/#additional-resources)

-   [Social Insurance Number](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/)
-   [Filing taxes in Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/filing-taxes-canada/)
-   [Permanent Residence](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/prepare-leave-ubc/#permanently)
-   [Job Bank](https://www.jobbank.gc.ca/home)
-   [Definitions for immigration purposes](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/#if-you-have-questions)

You can connect with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for questions related to immigration, health insurance, and life as an international student in Canada\.

## The information on this page may change[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/\#the\-information\-on\-this\-page\-may\-change](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/#the-information-on-this-page-may-change)

The immigration information on this page has been reviewed and endorsed by Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultants \(RCICs\) or Regulated International Student Immigration Advisors \(RISIAs\) in compliance with the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and Regulations\. However, this is not a legal document and information may change without notice\. Always refer to [Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada](http://www.cic.gc.ca/) \(IRCC\) for the most up\-to\-date information\.

## International Student Guide[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/\#international\-student\-guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/#international-student-guide)

title: Off-campus work
content_markdown:
> > IRCC Co\-op work permit update
> 
> > Read the [latest announcement](https://students.ubc.ca/news/2026-04-09/ircc-update-for-students-in-a-co-op-internship-or-practicum/) for students participating in a Co\-op, practicum, or internship\.

## What is considered off\-campus work?[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/off\-campus\-work/\#what\-is\-considered\-off\-campus\-work](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/off-campus-work/#what-is-considered-off-campus-work)

Off\-campus work is work that takes place outside the boundaries of the campus at which a student is registered\. University\-related work at facilities owned, operated, or affiliated with UBC located off\-campus might be considered [on\-campus work](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/campus-work/#what-is-considered-on-campus-work) in some cases\.

## Make sure you’re eligible to work off\-campus[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/off\-campus\-work/\#make\-sure\-youre\-eligible\-to\-work\-off\-campus](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/off-campus-work/#make-sure-youre-eligible-to-work-off-campus)

You may work off campus starting the first day of the term you begin studies at UBC if you meet all of the following requirements:

-   You have a [valid study permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/#maintaining-your-student-status), or you have applied to extend your study permit and have [maintained status](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/maintained-status/)\.
-   You are enrolled [full\-time for immigration purposes](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#full-time) during academic terms in a degree, diploma, certificate program, or exchange program, or you are eligible to work during a [scheduled break](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#scheduled-break)\.
-   Your study permit includes [conditions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/#before-you-apply-for-a-sin) allowing you to work off campus, such as *“May accept employment on or off campus if meeting eligibility criteria, per paragraph R186\(f\), \(v\), or \(w\) and must cease working if no longer meeting these criteria”\.*
-   You have a valid [Social Insurance Number](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/), or you had a SIN and are on [maintained status](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/maintained-status/)\.
-   You are enrolled in a degree, diploma, or certificate program which is at least 6 months in duration\.

You should also consider the following:

-   If you plan to work in [jobs requiring a medical exam](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/#if-you-work-with-children-or-seniors-in-healthcare-settings-or-in-agriculture), such as working with children or in health care settings, you must have taken a medical exam and have the right conditions on your study permit before starting\.
-   If work is required for your program, you must have applied for a [co\-op work permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/co-op-or-student-work-placements/) and received it before starting your position, or be eligible to work while you are waiting\. Review the [co\-op page](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/co-op-or-student-work-placements/) for details\. 
-   If you are doing [volunteer or unpaid work](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/#volunteer-or-unpaid-work-that-is-not-required-to-complete-your-academic-program), this might still be considered work in Canada, and would count towards the 24 hours of work \(20 hours before Nov 8, 2024\) you are permitted to do off\-campus\.
-   You aren’t allowed to work in [jobs at risk of exploitation](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/publications-manuals/operational-bulletins-manuals/temporary-residents/foreign-workers/protecting-workers-abuse-exploitation.html)\.
-   If you are enrolled in a UBC graduate program or the Diploma in Accounting, you must be enrolled full\-time in the summer session to be eligible to work on or off campus\.

Learn how your [enrollment impacts immigration](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/immigration-impacts-part-time-studies-withdrawing-courses/), including work eligibility\.

Non\-degree seeking students, including Visiting International Research Students \(VIRS\), visiting students, and unclassified students, are not eligible to work off campus, but you might be eligible to work [on\-campus](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/campus-work/)\.

## How many hours can I work off campus per week?[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/off\-campus\-work/\#how\-many\-hours\-can\-i\-work\-off\-campus\-per\-week](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/off-campus-work/#how-many-hours-can-i-work-off-campus-per-week)

If you are eligible to work off\-campus, as of Nov 8, 2024, you can work up to a maximum of 24 hours a week for all positions combined \(paid or unpaid\) during [regular academic sessions](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#regular-academic-session)\.

Before Nov 8, 2024, you could have worked up to 20 hours a week, if eligible\. IRCC’s [temporary policies](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-immigration-faq/#international-work-off-campus-hours) allowed some international students to work more than 20 hours a week between **November 15, 2022 and April 30, 2024**\.

You can work full\-time during your program’s [scheduled breaks](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#scheduled-break) if you’re enrolled full\-time in the academic terms immediately before and after your scheduled break\.

For example, if you are enrolled full\-time in Winter Term 1 and will enrol full\-time in the following Winter Term 2, you can work full\-time during the winter break\. There is no specific limit for full\-time hours\. If you are not full\-time in the terms before or after the break, you cannot work during the scheduled break\.

It’s very important that you do not exceed the number of hours you can work each week, and that you only work when you meet the requirements\. If you have worked more hours than you were allowed to or worked when you were not eligible to work, contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support\. 

You cannot work full\-time off campus during a scheduled break for more than 150 consecutive days, and cannot exceed a total of 180 days per calendar year\.

See [definitions for immigration purposes](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/) for details on academic terms and scheduled breaks\.\. A summary is below\.

**

Undergraduate, certificate, and diploma students

**

Your regular academic terms are:

-   Winter Term 1 \(September to December\)
-   Winter Term 2 \(January to April\)

You have scheduled breaks during the summer session \(May to August\), breaks between terms, and during midterm breaks\. Taking courses during the summer scheduled break does not impact your ability to work\.

If you are not enrolled full\-time in the terms before or after the summer scheduled break, you cannot work at all during the summer\. Exceptions are if you enrol full\-time in the summer session or if the summer session is your final academic term, in which case you can work up to 24 hours a week off campus\.

**

Graduate and Diploma in Accounting Program students

**

Your regular academic terms are:

-   Winter Term 1 \(September to December\)
-   Winter Term 2 \(January to April\)
-   Summer session \(May to August\)

You are considered to have an ongoing, full\-time relationship with the university throughout the year\. The summer session is not a scheduled break—you must be enrolled full\-time to work, and you cannot work more than 24 hours per week off campus during the summer \(or more if eligible for the [temporary off\-campus work policies](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-immigration-faq/#international-work-off-campus-hours)\)\.

You have scheduled breaks during breaks between terms and during Midterm breaks\.

**

Exchange students

**

You cannot work during scheduled breaks, and can only work during [academic terms](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#regular-academic-session) if you are enrolled full\-time\.

## When can I start working?[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/off\-campus\-work/\#when\-can\-i\-start\-working](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/off-campus-work/#when-can-i-start-working)

You cannot start working until you’ve begun full\-time studies at UBC—starting from the first day of the term in which you are enrolled according to the [Academic Calendar](https://www.calendar.ubc.ca/vancouver/index.cfm?page=deadlines)—and meet the above requirements\.

## When must I stop working?[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/off\-campus\-work/\#when\-must\-i\-stop\-working](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/off-campus-work/#when-must-i-stop-working)

You must stop working immediately if you no longer meet the above requirements\. For example, do not work if your study permit expires and you did not apply to extend it\.

If you are no longer enrolled full\-time and take time away from studies, you are not allowed to work, and cannot work during the scheduled breaks before or after your break\. Learn about [taking time away from studies](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/taking-time-away-school-international/)\.

If you are an undergraduate or DAP student and withdraw from courses to a part\-time course load, you must stop working right away, and cannot work during the scheduled breaks before or after you are enrolled part\-time\. Learn how your [enrollment impacts immigration](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/immigration-impacts-part-time-studies-withdrawing-courses/)\.

### If you are in your final term

**

Undergraduate and Graduate degree, certificate, diploma, or DAP students

**

If you are an undergraduate, certificate, diploma, or DAP student with fewer than 9 credits in your final term to finish your program requirements, you are considered full\-time and can work\.

If you are in your final term, regardless of when the final term occurs, you may continue to work off\-campus until your [Letter of Completion](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/post-graduation-work-permit/#when-to-apply-for-a-pgwp) becomes available\.

After you have finished your last program requirement, be sure to check every day if your Letter of Completion has become available\. Starting from the day after your Letter of Completion becomes available, you must stop working until you meet additional requirements to resume working, such as one of the following:

-   You apply for the Post\-Graduation Work Permit and meet the requirements to [work after submitting your application](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/post-graduation-work-permit/#can-i-work-while-i-am-applying-for-the-pgwp)\.
-   You have received a letter of acceptance for another program and meet the requirements to work [up to 150 days between programs](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/work-off-campus.html#new)\.

Contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) to discuss your options if you have not received your letter of acceptance for your next program yet, or if you have more than 150 days between programs\.

**

Exchange students

**

Regardless of when your study permit expires, you must stop working on the last day of the posted final exam period when your last enrolled term ends, according to the [Academic Calendar](https://www.calendar.ubc.ca/vancouver/index.cfm?page=deadlines)\.

## If you plan to work on campus[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/off\-campus\-work/\#if\-you\-plan\-to\-work\-on\-campus](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/off-campus-work/#if-you-plan-to-work-on-campus)

If you are also eligible to [work on campus](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/campus-work/), you can work on campus at the same time as working off campus\.

## If you plan to work off campus during your Co\-op or internship[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/off\-campus\-work/\#if\-you\-plan\-to\-work\-off\-campus\-during\-your\-co\-op\-or\-internship](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/off-campus-work/#if-you-plan-to-work-off-campus-during-your-co-op-or-internship)

You must have a [co\-op work permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/co-op-or-student-work-placements/) if work is required for your program, even if you are eligible to work off campus\. You might be eligible to work after you applied for the co\-op work permit while you are waiting\. Review [the co\-op page](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/co-op-or-student-work-placements/) for details\.

If you have a co\-op work permit and you’re enrolled in a co\-op position, internship, or practicum course, you can also work off campus for up to 24 hours per week \(20 hours before Nov 8, 2024\) at the same time, if eligible\. Your co\-op work permit can only be used for program\-required work, and cannot be used to work additional hours off campus\.

## International Student Guide[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/off\-campus\-work/\#international\-student\-guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/off-campus-work/#international-student-guide)

Find everything you need to know about life as an international student at UBC’s Vancouver campus\.

[View the guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/)

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/off\-campus\-work/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/off-campus-work/#additional-resources)

-   [On\-campus work](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/campus-work/)
-   [Working in Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/)
-   [Co\-op or internship work permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/co-op-or-internship-work-permit/)
-   [Post\-graduation work permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/post-graduation-work-permit/) 
-   [Social Insurance Number \(SIN\)](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/)
-   [Job Search](https://students.ubc.ca/career/career-resources/job-search/)
-   [UBC Career Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/ubc-career-centre/)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/off\-campus\-work/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/off-campus-work/#if-you-have-questions)

You can connect with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for questions related to immigration, health insurance, and life as an international student in Canada\.

## The information on this page may change[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/off\-campus\-work/\#the\-information\-on\-this\-page\-may\-change](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/off-campus-work/#the-information-on-this-page-may-change)

The immigration information on this page has been reviewed and endorsed by Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultants \(RCICs\) or Regulated International Student Immigration Advisors \(RISIAs\) in compliance with the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and Regulations\. However, this is not a legal document and information may change without notice\. Always refer to [Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada](http://www.cic.gc.ca/) \(IRCC\) for the most up\-to\-date information\.

title: Complete the PGWP application form
content_markdown:
## About the form[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/apply\-post\-graduation\-work\-permit\-within\-canada/complete\-pgwp\-application\-form/\#about\-the\-form](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/apply-post-graduation-work-permit-within-canada/complete-pgwp-application-form/#about-the-form)

Your application form is a legal document and is an important part of your application\. Missing or incorrect information can lead to a refusal\. Below are five steps to help create a comprehensive application\.

## First, download the newest forms[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/apply\-post\-graduation\-work\-permit\-within\-canada/complete\-pgwp\-application\-form/\#first\-download\-the\-newest\-forms](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/apply-post-graduation-work-permit-within-canada/complete-pgwp-application-form/#first-download-the-newest-forms)

**Required for all applicants:** *Application to Change Conditions, Extend my Stay or Remain in Canada as a Worker \[IMM5710\]*

IRCC makes periodic updates to their application forms\. Always make sure you are using the current version by downloading the form\(s\) directly from the IRCC website\.

[Download the form](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/application-forms-guides.html)

## Get help with commonly asked questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/apply\-post\-graduation\-work\-permit\-within\-canada/complete\-pgwp\-application\-form/\#get\-help\-with\-commonly\-asked\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/apply-post-graduation-work-permit-within-canada/complete-pgwp-application-form/#get-help-with-commonly-asked-questions)

**

What is a UCI?

**

UCI stands for “Unique Client Identifier,” also known as “Client ID\.” It is an eight\- or ten\-digit number on your study permit\. Your UCI has this format: 0000\-0000 or 00\-0000\-0000\.

[Screenshot of the "UCI" section on the PGWP application form](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/pgwp_application_uci_screenshot.png)

**

How do I answer “I am applying for one or more of the following:”?

**

Select “An initial work permit or a work permit with a new employer”\.

[Screenshot of the "I am applying for one or more of the following" section on the PGWP application form](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/pgwp_application_applying_more_screenshot.jpeg)

**

How do I fill out the “Current mailing address” section?

**

[Screenshot of the "Mailing address" section on the PGWP application form](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/pgwp_application_address_screenshot.jpeg)

This section is very important as the officer will use your address to mail you your work permit\. If the address is inaccurate, you might not receive your work permit\.

-   A “P\.O\. Box” is a paid lockable mailbox located in a post office station which you pay to rent\. Your mail box number in your apartment or residence is **not** a P\.O\. Box number\.
-   If you do not have an assigned mailbox number, you can put your apartment number under Apt/Unit\.
-   A street number is the main number on the outside of a building that indicates the location of a building on a street\. 
-   Some “street names” also contain numbers, such as West 10th Ave, but this number is part of the street name\.
-   If you live in a residence on campus and will be moving out, use a friend’s Canadian address\.

If you are unsure of your mailing address or might move during the time your application is being processed, you can provide a mailing address of a trusted friend who does not live in on\-campus housing\. Please ensure that your mail can be received by your friend securely if the mail is under your name and not your friend’s name\. You are welcome to use [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) but you must come in person to check if your mail has arrived\. We cannot guarantee your document will be received, and it will be publicly accessible in our office\.

**

What is a document number?

**

A document number appears on official immigration documents \(e\.g\. study permits, or a “U” for work permits, such as for co\-op work permits\)\. It is usually printed in black ink with a letter \(an “F” for study permits\) followed by a 9\-digit number\.

[Screenshot of the "Document number" section on the PGWP application form](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/pgwp_application_document_number_screenshot.png)

**

How do I complete the “Details of my prospective employer” section?

**

[Screenshot of the "Prospective employer" section on the PGWP application form](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/pgwp_application_employer_screenshot.jpg)

Because the post\-graduation work permit is an open work permit, you are not required to have a job offer\. Even if you have a job offer, it is best to follow the above example and indicate “Not applicable” in these fields\.

**

How do I answer “Intended location of employment in Canada”?

**

In this section you can select “BC”, “Vancouver”, and type “Not applicable” in the field provided for an address\.

**

How do I answer “My occupation in Canada will be”?

**

If you do not have a job, you may indicate your occupation as “Job seeker”\. In the field provided for “brief description of duties” you may type “As assigned”\.

**

How do I answer “Duration of expected employment”?

**

**In the “From” field:** Type in the date when you will submit your application\.

**In the “To” field:** Type in a date that corresponds with the length of work permit that you are eligible\. For example, students who complete a program of two years or more in length are eligible for a three\-year work permit\. For more information on post\-graduation work permit length, refer to the [IRCC website](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/after-graduation/about.html)\.

[Screenshot of the "Duration of expected employment" section on the PGWP application form](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/pgwp_application_duration_screenshot.jpg)

**

How do I complete the “Education” section?

**

The information you provide in this section gives IRCC a fuller picture of your current post\-secondary education\.

-   Indicate ‘yes’ to the first question as you have studied at UBC\. Type in the current year and month in the “to” field\.
-   Type in your completed program \(e\.g\. Bachelor of Arts\) at UBC\.
-   If you need more space, provide additional information in a letter of explanation\.

**

How do I complete the “Employment” section?

**

[Screenshot of the "Employment" section on the PGWP application form](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/pgwp_application_employment_screenshot.jpeg)

The first section under employment is your “current activity”\.

-   **If you are currently employed,** include details of your current employment\.
-   **If you currently do not work,** you can type in “student” and include the time you studied at UBC\.

Provide information about your employment history, including full time or part time work in the past 10 years in any country, if applicable\. If you need more space, provide additional info in a [Letter of Explanation](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/apply-post-graduation-work-permit-within-canada/gather-required-documents-pgwp-application/)\.

**

How do I answer the “Background Information” on page 4?

**

You must answer these questions truthfully\.

-   2 \(a\) Have you remained beyond the validity of your status, attended school without authorization or worked without authorization in Canada?
-   2 \(b\) Have you ever been refused a visa or permit, denied entry or ordered to leave Canada or any other country?

If you are not sure if you worked unauthorized, check work eligibility on our [working in Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/) pages\.

Please speak with an [International Student Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) if you answered “yes” to questions 2\(a\) or \(b\) because it will affect other parts of your application\.

**2 \(c\) Background information: Have you previously applied to enter or remain in Canada?**

[Screenshot of the "Background information" section on the PGWP application form](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/pgwp_application_background_screenshot-768x229.png)

You must report **every** Canadian immigration application you have ever applied for, including a Canadian study permit, a Temporary Resident Visa \(TRV\), a work permit \(such as a co\-op work permit\), or permanent residence, whether it was approved or refused, including extensions\. Make sure to check the box “Yes” to 2\(c\) and add when you applied for each type of document in the box and provide details\.

**

How can I sign the \[IMM5710\] form if I apply online?

**

You will be prompted to electronically sign your application later in the online application process after you have uploaded all documents\.

## Validate your form[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/apply\-post\-graduation\-work\-permit\-within\-canada/complete\-pgwp\-application\-form/\#validate\-your\-form](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/apply-post-graduation-work-permit-within-canada/complete-pgwp-application-form/#validate-your-form)

When you finish filling out your application form, click the blue “Validate” button \(found on the first or last page\)\. This will highlight any missing information required on your application\.

-   You can make changes after the application is successfully validated\. You can edit and validate as many times as you need\. Always validate before uploading\.
-   Remember to validate, save, and upload the final form\.

Once your application has been successfully validated, it should show the following:

[Screenshot of the barcode required to validate your TRV application](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/trv_validate_barcode.jpg)

If you do not see any barcodes when you validate your application, please visit the [RCIC help page](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/helpcentre/answer.asp?qnum=767&top=23)\. 

## Take screenshots as you apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/apply\-post\-graduation\-work\-permit\-within\-canada/complete\-pgwp\-application\-form/\#take\-screenshots\-as\-you\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/apply-post-graduation-work-permit-within-canada/complete-pgwp-application-form/#take-screenshots-as-you-apply)

It is a good practice to take screenshots as you apply in case there are issues after you submit your application\. You are welcome to take screenshots of all screens; however, these are the most important:

1.  The **“Your document checklist”** page after all your documents have been successfully uploaded to your MyCIC account
2.  The “**Acknowledgment of receipt**” page after the application has been submitted
3.  After you submit your application, if an IRCC officer requests you submit any additional documents, take a screenshot to prove you uploaded them

Save your screenshots to a safe place where you can access them easily\. 

Learn how to take screenshots if you’re [using a PC](http://support.microsoft.com/en-us/help/13776/windows-use-snipping-tool-to-capture-screenshots#1TC=windows-7) or [on your Mac](http://support.apple.com/en-ca/HT201361)\.

## The information on this page may change[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/apply\-post\-graduation\-work\-permit\-within\-canada/complete\-pgwp\-application\-form/\#the\-information\-on\-this\-page\-may\-change](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/apply-post-graduation-work-permit-within-canada/complete-pgwp-application-form/#the-information-on-this-page-may-change)

The immigration information on this page has been reviewed and endorsed by Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultants \(RCICs\) or Regulated International Student Immigration Advisors \(RISIAs\) in compliance with the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and Regulations\. However, this is not a legal document and information may change without notice\. Always refer to [Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada](http://www.cic.gc.ca/) \(IRCC\) for the most up\-to\-date information\.

title: How to apply for your post-graduation work permit from within Canada
content_markdown:
## Overview of the process[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/apply\-post\-graduation\-work\-permit\-within\-canada/\#overview\-of\-the\-process](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/apply-post-graduation-work-permit-within-canada/#overview-of-the-process)

- **Row 1**

  - **Header cell 1:**
  
    Topic
  
  - **Header cell 2:**
  
    Details

- **Row 2**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Before appllying
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    First, visit the [Post\-graduation work permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/post-graduation-work-permit/) page for important details on things to prepare before you apply, working before and after you apply, options if you have travel plans, and more\.

- **Row 3**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    When to apply
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    **Apply** **within 90 days** of when your [Letter of Completion](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/post-graduation-work-permit/) first becomes available AND before your study permit expires to apply through the inside Canada process\.   
    To maintain status in Canada, you must submit your application before 11:59 pm [Coordinated Universal Time](https://time.is/UTC) \(UTC\), not local time, on the day your [study permit becomes invalid](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/#maintaining-your-student-status) and within 90 days of when your Letter of Completion becomes available\.  
      
    **Apply within 180** **days** of when your Letter of Completion first becomes available AND within 180 days of your study permit expiring to apply through the outside Canada process\.   
    If you are inside Canada beyond the 90 days and/or your study permit has expired, contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support\.  
      
    You must submit your application within 180 days of when your Letter of Completion first becomes available before 11:59 pm [Coordinated Universal Time](https://time.is/UTC) \(UTC\), not local time \(or within 180 days of your study permit expiring, if that’s sooner\)\.  
    This 180\-day period begins when your [Letter of Completion](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/post-graduation-work-permit/#when-to-apply-for-a-pgwp) first becomes available in Workday or via your program\. NOT the date of your convocation ceremony\.

- **Row 4**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Cost
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    $255\.00 CAD and $85\.00 CAD for biometrics, if applicable

- **Row 5**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Processing time
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    IRCC processing times vary widely\. Check typical processing times for your country on the [IRCC w](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/check-processing-times.html)[e](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/check-processing-times.html)[bsite](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/check-processing-times.html)\.

- **Row 6**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    How to apply
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Apply online through the [IRCC website](http://www.cic.gc.ca/english/e-services/account.asp?)\.  
      
    You can only apply [by paper](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/after-graduation/apply/alternate-format.html) if you have a disability which prevents you from applying online, there is a problem with the online application, you are applying for the remaining time of your PGWP because of your passport expiry date, or you are applying to change conditions of your PGWP \(such as to work in jobs that require a [medical exam](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/#if-you-work-with-children-or-seniors-in-healthcare-settings-or-in-agriculture)\)\.

- **Row 7**

  - **Cell 1:**
  
    Application form
  
  - **Cell 2:**
  
    Application to Change Conditions, Extend my Stay or Remain in Canada as a Worker \[IMM5710\]  
      
    To avoid delays with your application, always download the most current form from the [IRCC website](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/application-forms-guides/imm5710.html)\.

## First, create your document checklist[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/apply\-post\-graduation\-work\-permit\-within\-canada/\#first\-create\-your\-document\-checklist](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/apply-post-graduation-work-permit-within-canada/#first-create-your-document-checklist)

1.  Log into the [IRCC Secure Account](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/account.html), or create a new one if you lost access to your previous account\.
2.  Complete the questionnaire to generate a list of required forms and documents\.
3.  After completing the questionnaire, you will be guided to a screen titled “Your document checklist”\.

Check our [PGWP Canvas application review course](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/LTCJWK) for a video on creating your document checklist\.

## Gather your required documents[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/apply\-post\-graduation\-work\-permit\-within\-canada/\#gather\-your\-required\-documents](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/apply-post-graduation-work-permit-within-canada/#gather-your-required-documents)

You’ll need to prepare your transcript, Letter of Completion, a copy of your passport, and more\.

[Get details](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/apply-post-graduation-work-permit-within-canada/gather-required-documents-pgwp-application/)

## Complete the application form[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/apply\-post\-graduation\-work\-permit\-within\-canada/\#complete\-the\-application\-form](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/apply-post-graduation-work-permit-within-canada/#complete-the-application-form)

Your application form is a legal document and is an important part of your application\. Missing or incorrect information can lead to a refusal\. Learn how to fill out the form\.

[Follow instructions](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/apply-post-graduation-work-permit-within-canada/complete-pgwp-application-form/)

## Before submitting your application[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/apply\-post\-graduation\-work\-permit\-within\-canada/\#before\-submitting\-your\-application](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/apply-post-graduation-work-permit-within-canada/#before-submitting-your-application)

Complete the [Canvas application review course](https://canvas.ubc.ca/enroll/LTCJWK) to go over required documents, learn how to fill out the form, avoid common mistakes, and be ready to submit your application\.

## After you’ve applied[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/apply\-post\-graduation\-work\-permit\-within\-canada/\#after\-youve\-applied](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/apply-post-graduation-work-permit-within-canada/#after-youve-applied)

You may begin working full\-time immediately after submitting your Post\-Graduation Work Permit application while you are waiting for a decision from IRCC if, at the time you submitted your application, you met **all** of the following requirements:

-   You had a [valid study permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/#maintaining-your-student-status) and applied within 90 days of your [Letter of Completion](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/post-graduation-work-permit/) first becoming available
-   You completed your program of study
-   You were eligible to [work off campus](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/off-campus-work/) without a work permit during your studies\. Check that your study permit has a condition allowing off\-campus work, such as “may accept employment on or off campus if meeting eligibility criteria, per paragraph R186\(f\), \(v\) or \(w\) and must cease working if no longer meeting these criteria“\.
-   You did not work off campus for more than 24 hours per week during [academic sessions](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#regular-academic-session) \(or more than 20 hours per week before Nov 8, 2024, unless you were eligible to work more under the [temporary policies](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/)\)\.

If you plan to work in a job which requires a [medical exam](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/#if-you-work-with-children-or-seniors-in-healthcare-settings-or-in-agriculture), you cannot start working in that position until you’ve received your work permit with the correct conditions\. However, if you meet the above criteria, you can work in other jobs which don’t require a medical exam while you are waiting for your PGWP\.

If you have travel plans, review your [options](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/post-graduation-work-permit/)\.

So long as you applied within 90 days of your Letter of Completion first becoming available and before your study permit expired, you will have [maintained status](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/maintained-status/) and can remain in Canada while your application is being processed, and [work](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/post-graduation-work-permit/#can-i-work-while-i-am-applying-for-the-pgwp) if you met the requirements at the time of application\. 

If your MSP will expire before your PGWP is processed, you must take action and request a [temporary extension of your MSP](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/#maintaining-your-msp-coverage)\. 

## After you receive your work permit[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/apply\-post\-graduation\-work\-permit\-within\-canada/\#after\-you\-receive\-your\-work\-permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/apply-post-graduation-work-permit-within-canada/#after-you-receive-your-work-permit)

### Check your work permit

Once you receive your post\-graduation work permit, check the length of the work permit to make sure it was issued correctly:

-   If your program of study was at least eight months and less than two years in length, your work permit should match the length of your program
-   If your program of study was two years or longer, or a master’s degree that was 8 months or longer, you should receive a three\-year work permit

Contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) if you believe the officer made a mistake with the length of your work permit\.

**Exception**: Your work permit cannot be issued for longer than your passport; therefore, a shorter work permit may be issued based on your passport expiry date\. If this is the case, you must first extend your passport, and then apply to extend your work permit [by paper](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/post-graduation-work-permit/) for the remainder of the time for which you are eligible\.

### Keep your documents up to date

Keep your immigration and health insurance documents up to date by completing important steps below:

1.  Keep track of the expiry date of your work permit\. You must either leave Canada or apply for another immigration document such as a [Visitor Record](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/extend-stay.html) to change status to a visitor before your work permit expires\.
2.  Apply for or extend your [Social Insurance Number \(SIN\)](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/)\. You need a valid a SIN to be paid for work in Canada\. 
3.  Be sure to extend your [Medical Services Plan \(MSP\)](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/health-insurance-international/medical-services-plan-msp-international/extend-bc-medical-services-plan-msp/) or make sure you have sufficient health insurance if you are moving to another province/territory
4.  Apply for a new [Temporary Resident Visa \(TRV\)](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/) to enter Canada \(if required\), OR
5.  Check that you have an Electronic Travel Authorization \(eTA\) that is valid until the same date or a future date\.

If your contact information changes after submitting your application, be sure to update it via [IRCC’s webform](https://secure.cic.gc.ca/enquiries-renseignements/canada-case-cas-eng.aspx)\.

### Leaving and entering Canada

Every time you enter Canada, be prepared to prove at the border that you can support yourself financially \(that is, carry an updated bank statement\)\. If you don’t have a job, bring proof that you are actively looking for work \(your resume, list of jobs you are applying for, etc\.\)\. You must have a valid Temporary Resident Visa or Electronic Travel Authorization\. Check our [Travelling to Canada Guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/) for recommended documents to bring\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/apply\-post\-graduation\-work\-permit\-within\-canada/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/apply-post-graduation-work-permit-within-canada/#if-you-have-questions)

You can connect with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for questions related to immigration, health insurance, and life as an international student in Canada\.

## International Student Guide[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/apply\-post\-graduation\-work\-permit\-within\-canada/\#international\-student\-guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/apply-post-graduation-work-permit-within-canada/#international-student-guide)

Find everything you need to know about life as an international student at UBC’s Vancouver campus\.

[Go to guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/)

## The information on this page may change[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/apply\-post\-graduation\-work\-permit\-within\-canada/\#the\-information\-on\-this\-page\-may\-change](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/apply-post-graduation-work-permit-within-canada/#the-information-on-this-page-may-change)

The immigration information on this page has been reviewed and endorsed by Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultants \(RCICs\) or Regulated International Student Immigration Advisors \(RISIAs\) in compliance with the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and Regulations\. However, this is not a legal document and information may change without notice\. Always refer to [Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada](http://www.cic.gc.ca/) \(IRCC\) for the most up\-to\-date information\.
