title: Eligibility requirements for Work Learn International Undergraduate Research Awards
content_markdown:
## About the awards[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/work\-learn\-international\-undergraduate\-research\-awards/eligibility\-requirements\-work\-learn\-international\-undergraduate\-research\-awards/\#about\-the\-awards](https://students.ubc.ca/career/work-learn-international-undergraduate-research-awards/eligibility-requirements-work-learn-international-undergraduate-research-awards/#about-the-awards)

The [Work Learn International Undergraduate Research Awards](https://students.ubc.ca/career/work-learn-international-undergraduate-research-awards/) provide subsidy funding for international undergraduate students to work full\-time on research projects in the Summer Session \(May to August\)\.

## Eligibility requirements[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/work\-learn\-international\-undergraduate\-research\-awards/eligibility\-requirements\-work\-learn\-international\-undergraduate\-research\-awards/\#eligibility\-requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/career/work-learn-international-undergraduate-research-awards/eligibility-requirements-work-learn-international-undergraduate-research-awards/#eligibility-requirements)

To be eligible to apply for an award, you must meet all of the following requirements:

-   You are an international undergraduate student at the UBC Vancouver Campus paying international student fees\.
-   You are not an exchange or visiting student to UBC\.
-   You have a valid [study permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/) and a [Social Insurance Number](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/social-insurance-number-sin/) \(SIN\)\. If you don’t have a valid SIN, it can take several weeks to apply for one\.
-   You are residing in British Columbia, Canada during your work term\.
-   You are considered [full time for immigration purposes](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes#full-time) or are on a [scheduled break](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes#scheduled-break)\.
-   You will be engaged in research activities at the UBC Vancouver campus on a full\-time basis for at least 16 weeks\. This includes 35 paid hours per week, plus a one\-hour unpaid daily lunch break\.
-   You will be working under the supervision of a faculty member\.

### Graduating students

If you’re graduating, you’re eligible for the award only for the academic term directly after you complete your program requirements, regardless of your graduation date\.

Students who finish their courses in Winter Term 2 \(April\) and graduate in the spring \(May\) are eligible to hold a Work Learn International Undergraduate Research Award in the summer term\.

## Program restrictions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/work\-learn\-international\-undergraduate\-research\-awards/eligibility\-requirements\-work\-learn\-international\-undergraduate\-research\-awards/\#program\-restrictions](https://students.ubc.ca/career/work-learn-international-undergraduate-research-awards/eligibility-requirements-work-learn-international-undergraduate-research-awards/#program-restrictions)

Consider the following restrictions before you apply:

-   You may hold **only one** Work Learn International Undergraduate Research Award per fiscal year \(April 1 to March 31\)\.
-   You may only hold a maximum of 3 Work Learn International Undergraduate Research Awards throughout your degree\.
-   You are not allowed to hold a Work Learn International Undergraduate Research Award position in the same term you’re holding an [NSERC Undergraduate Student Research Award](https://students.ubc.ca/career/undergraduate-student-research-awards-nserc-cihr-sshrc/) or a [Work Learn](https://students.ubc.ca/career/work-learn-program/) placement\.
-   During the award period, you’re recommended to take no more than 3 credits in one summer term \(maximum 3\-credits in Term 1 and/or 3 credits in Term 2\), in order to focus on the 35 hour per week requirement of full\-time work in their position\.

## Work authorization documents[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/work\-learn\-international\-undergraduate\-research\-awards/eligibility\-requirements\-work\-learn\-international\-undergraduate\-research\-awards/\#work\-authorization\-documents](https://students.ubc.ca/career/work-learn-international-undergraduate-research-awards/eligibility-requirements-work-learn-international-undergraduate-research-awards/#work-authorization-documents)

UBC students who have completed their program requirements and whose program completion letter is not yet available are considered “[full time for immigration purposes](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes#full-time)” by UBC\.

If your letter of completion is available, you must have applied for a [post\-graduation work permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/post-graduation-work-permit/) or have some other form of authorization to work in Canada\. If you have questions about your work eligibility, please speak with an [International Student Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/)\.

It is your responsibility to ensure you have the necessary work authorization documents to work after completing your studies\.

Undergraduate international students who are planning to work full\-time during the summer must be on a [scheduled break](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes#scheduled-break) to meet the [full\-time definition](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes#full-time) for immigration purposes\. This includes Work Learn International Undergraduate Research Award recipients\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/work\-learn\-international\-undergraduate\-research\-awards/eligibility\-requirements\-work\-learn\-international\-undergraduate\-research\-awards/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/career/work-learn-international-undergraduate-research-awards/eligibility-requirements-work-learn-international-undergraduate-research-awards/#if-you-have-questions)

-   Email [worklearn\.iura@ubc\.ca](mailto:worklearn.iura@ubc.ca) or call [604 827 2937](tel:604%20827%202937) from 9:00 am to 4:00 pm on weekdays\.
-   Read [frequently asked questions](https://facultystaff.students.ubc.ca/sites/facultystaff.students.ubc.ca/files/WLIURA_S26_FAQ_10.23.2025_AVP.pdf) \(pdf\) about the reward\.
-   Contact the [faculty, school, or department coordinator](https://facultystaff.students.ubc.ca/sites/facultystaff.students.ubc.ca/files/WLIURA_2026-27_List_of_Coordinators_11.4.2025_AVP.pdf) \(pdf\) specific to your program for support\.

title: International Tuition Exemption
content_markdown:
UBC determines a student’s tuition and fee assessment based on their citizenship status\. Generally, students who are citizens or permanent residents of Canada are assessed domestic tuition and fees\. Students who do not meet the criteria for domestic tuition are assessed international tuition and fees\.

Certain Indigenous International students may be eligible to pay domestic fees\.

This page outlines the International Tuition Exemption application instructions for students at UBC Vancouver\. If you are a UBC Okanagan student, contact [Enrolment Services Advising](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/courses-money-enrolment/advising/) instead\.

## Eligibility requirements[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/financial\-support\-indigenous/international\-tuition\-exemption/\#eligibility\-requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-support-indigenous/international-tuition-exemption/#eligibility-requirements)

To be eligible for the International Tuition Exemption, you must meet **all** of the following requirements:

-   You belong to one of the exemption categories below:
    -   You’re affiliated with an Indigenous nation of Canada \(First Nations, Métis, or Inuit\)\.
    -   You’re of a transborder Indigenous nation \(American Indian or Alaska Native\)\.
-   You have registered and are being assessed for tuition at UBC for the term in which you are seeking an exemption\.
-   You are in good academic standing at UBC\. Students who are not in good academic standing or those required to leave UBC are not eligible for the exemption\.

## How to Request an International Tuition Exemption[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/financial\-support\-indigenous/international\-tuition\-exemption/\#how\-to\-request\-an\-international\-tuition\-exemption](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-support-indigenous/international-tuition-exemption/#how-to-request-an-international-tuition-exemption)

### First, gather your supporting documentation

Review and gather the supporting documentation required by the category you are eligible for\.

**

If you’re affiliated to an Indigenous nation of Canada \(First Nations, Métis, or Inuit\)

**

Supporting documentation may include a certificate of Indian Status or a Métis citizenship card that meets the Métis National Council Guidelines\. Those without formal documentation may be considered on a case\-by\-case basis\.

**

If you’re of a transborder Indigenous nation \(American Indian or Alaska Native\)

**

Supporting documentation may include enhanced tribal identification cards, which are preferred for the application, or recognition from an American Indian or an Alaska Native tribe\. Those without formal documentation may be considered on a case\-by\-case basis\.

Examples of eligible Nations include American members of the Okanagan Nation Alliance, Kootenai Tribes, and the Haudenosaunee Confederacy\.

### Next, submit your request to Enrolment Services

1.  Submit a request via email to your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) with the following information before the [tuition payment deadline](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/fees/policies-fees#15539-pay-and-due):
    -   Category you’re applying for
    -   Program to which you’ve been admitted
    -   Start and end dates of the study period for which you are requesting domestic tuition
2.  If you meet the eligibility requirements for the category you’re applying for, your ES Advisor will send you an application to complete\. Submit the application and your supporting documentation in person to Enrolment Services on or before the tuition payment deadline\.
    -   Exceptions to deadlines are not permitted, and retroactive fee changes will not be granted\. 
    -   UBC will make copies of the documents and may verify them with the issuer to validate their accuracy and authenticity\.
3.  After your submission, you will receive an email from Enrolment Services with next steps\. You may be asked to provide additional documentation to support your application\.
4.  You’ll receive a decision by email in approximately 3 to 4 weeks once your application has been received\. Processing times may be longer at the start of the term\.

## After you’ve been approved[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/financial\-support\-indigenous/international\-tuition\-exemption/\#after\-youve\-been\-approved](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-support-indigenous/international-tuition-exemption/#after-youve-been-approved)

It is your responsibility to report any changes to your student status immediately during the study period\.

You may be required to provide documents to renew or maintain your international exemption on an annual basis or at other times during your studies at the discretion of Enrolment Services\.

## Extending an International Tuition Exemption[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/financial\-support\-indigenous/international\-tuition\-exemption/\#extending\-an\-international\-tuition\-exemption](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-support-indigenous/international-tuition-exemption/#extending-an-international-tuition-exemption)

Some students may be able to submit a request to extend their tuition exemption\. Requests to extend a tuition exemption are assessed on a case\-by\-case basis\. You can submit a written statement with supporting documentation to Enrolment Services for consideration if you meet both of the following conditions:

-   You unexpectedly left due to medical issues or extenuating personal circumstances\. 
-   You have been away from UBC for a **maximum** of 2 consecutive terms\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/financial\-support\-options/financial\-support\-indigenous/international\-tuition\-exemption/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-support-indigenous/international-tuition-exemption/#if-you-have-questions)

Please contact your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) directly\.

For questions about applying for a study permit, contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/)\.

title: UBC Provincial Attestation Letter
content_markdown:
## About the Provincial Attestation Letter[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/ubc\-provincial\-attestation\-letter/\#about\-the\-provincial\-attestation\-letter](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-provincial-attestation-letter/#about-the-provincial-attestation-letter)

Many new\-to\-UBC students need a Provincial Attestation Letter \(PAL\) before applying for a study permit\.

A [Provincial Attestation Letter](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/get-documents/provincial-attestation-letter.html) \(PAL\) is a document which confirms an international student has a spot in the provincial allocation for study permits and is included in the yearly federal cap to submit a study permit application\. 

UBC expects to receive sufficient PALs for all newly admitted undergraduate degree\-seeking students\.

### Levels of study

Whether your application requires a PAL will depend on the correct [level of study](https://gazette.gc.ca/rp-pr/p1/2025/2025-01-18/html/notice-avis-eng.html) for your program\. There are 2 levels of study in relation to the PAL requirement:

1.  **Graduate level**: Master’s degree and Doctoral degree students are exempt from the PAL requirement\.
2.  **Undergraduate level**: All other programs, including bachelor’s degrees, undergraduate certificates and diplomas, graduate certificates and diplomas, Visiting International Research students, and unclassified studies are considered to be at the Undergraduate level and will require a PAL in most cases\.

### Additional required documents

In addition to the Provincial Attestation Letter, you will need [further documents](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-documents-required-study-permit/) from UBC for your study permit application: a Letter of Admission and/or a Letter of Enrolment\.

## Who needs a PAL?[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/ubc\-provincial\-attestation\-letter/\#who\-needs\-a\-pal](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-provincial-attestation-letter/#who-needs-a-pal)

As of Jan 22, 2025, all international students at the Undergraduate level outside Canada \(except [Go Global exchange](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc/coming-ubc-exchange) students\) and most new\-to\-UBC students submitting a study permit application from inside Canada must include a valid Provincial Attestation Letter \(PAL\) with their study permit application\.

The following groups of students now require a PAL: 

-   Students changing institutions, such as from high school to UBC or from other post\-secondary institutions in Canada to UBC\. Check the [latest updates](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/#latest-updates) on “changing institutions” for additional information\. 
-   Students who have a parent holding a study or work permit 
-   Students who are diplomats or who are a dependent of a diplomat 
-   Visiting students, including [Visiting International Research Students](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc/visiting-international-research-students)
-   Work permit holders
-   Students whose study permit applications were refused
-   Students who are applying to restore their study permit

## Who does not need a PAL?[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/ubc\-provincial\-attestation\-letter/\#who\-does\-not\-need\-a\-pal](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-provincial-attestation-letter/#who-does-not-need-a-pal)

You will not need a PAL for your study permit application if you meet **one** of the following criteria:

-   As of Jan 1, 2026, you do not need a PAL if you are applying for a study permit for a degree\-granting graduate program at the Master’s or Doctoral level\.
    -   This exemption does not apply if you are applying for a study permit as a Visiting International Research Student at the graduate level\.
-   You are applying to extend your study permit to continue in the same [level of study](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-provincial-attestation-letter/#level-of-study) at UBC\. Examples include:
    -   You applied for your study permit with a UBC Letter of Admission for an undergraduate degree, and you are extending your study permit to continue working towards your undergraduate degree at UBC\.
    -   If you took time away from studies at UBC and/or studied at another institution \(other than on a UBC Go Global exchange\), contact [International Student Advising](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0J8VRJgJQkuO2b4) for support\. 
-   Exchange students coming to UBC through [Go Global](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc/coming-ubc-exchange)\.
-   You are eligible for a [temporary public policy](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/corporate/mandate/policies-operational-instructions-agreements/public-policies.html) for citizens of certain countries and submit your study permit application before the policy expires\.

Check IRCC’s page on who is [exempt from the PAL](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/get-documents/provincial-attestation-letter.html) for the complete list\.

## Who may need a PAL in the future[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/ubc\-provincial\-attestation\-letter/\#who\-may\-need\-a\-pal\-in\-the\-future](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-provincial-attestation-letter/#who-may-need-a-pal-in-the-future)

The following groups can begin their program without applying for a study permit and needing a PAL, but may require a PAL in their study permit application in the future\.

### Changing levels of study at UBC

If you applied for your study permit with a UBC Letter of Admission, you could begin your next program at a different [level of study](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-provincial-attestation-letter/#level-of-study) with the same study permit, so long as it’s still [valid](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/#maintaining-your-student-status)\.

For example, you are a UBC undergraduate student who will begin a Master’s degree at UBC [within 150 days](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/taking-time-away-school-international/) of completing your first program\. 

Master’s or Doctoral degree students changing to Undergraduate, Graduate Certificate, Graduate Diploma, or unclassified studies will require a PAL\.

If you took time away from studies at UBC and/or studied at another institution \(other than on a UBC Go Global exchange\), contact [International Student Advising](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0J8VRJgJQkuO2b4) for support\.

### Work permit holders without a study permit

If you are a work permit holder who is eligible to study without a study permit under the [temporary policy for workers](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/permit/temporary/workers-study-without-study-permit.html), you do not need a PAL at this time to continue your studies with your work permit\.

However, if you need more time to finish your program beyond your eligibility for the temporary policy, you must [apply for your study permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/extend-study-permit/) as soon as possible\. Unless you are studying in a degree program at the Master’s or Doctoral level, you will require a PAL for your application\.

Once you are no longer eligible for the temporary policy, you must receive your study permit before you can resume your studies\.

## If you need a PAL[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/ubc\-provincial\-attestation\-letter/\#if\-you\-need\-a\-pal](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-provincial-attestation-letter/#if-you-need-a-pal)

### Confirm your personal details as soon as possible

Please ensure your personal details \(name, date of birth, and address\) in UBC’s systems are correct\. If needed, you must request a change before you accept your offer, since this information will be included on your PAL\. Once issued, the details on your PAL cannot be changed and the PAL cannot be reissued\.

If your personal details on your PAL are not correct, you will need to address this in a letter of explanation as part of your study permit application\. Contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support\.

**

Your address

**

When you are considering whether to use a current address at the time of application or your permanent address, you should be consistent and use the same address which you will have continued access to\. The address on your Letter of Admission, PAL and study permit application should be the same\.  

Not all address details you provide to UBC will appear on the PAL\. The information from address line 2, the postal code, and the province/state will not be included on the PAL\. This will not impact your application\.

**

Your name

**

Make sure the name that you provided in your UBC profile matches your full legal first name and last name as they appear on your passport\. Your name on your UBC Letter of Admission, PAL and study permit application form should be the same\.  

If your passport has a separate field for middle name\(s\) and you enter your middle name separately in your UBC profile, it would show up on your UBC Letter of Admission, but not on your PAL since PALs do not include middle names\. This will not impact your application\.

#### How to check and update your personal details

-   **Undergraduate degree students**: Log into the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/), click *Edit Profile,* then select “Contact Summary” to confirm your personal details\. You can update your address in the system if needed\. To update your name or date of birth, email [ubc\.pal@ubc\.ca](mailto:ubc.pal@ubc.ca)\.
-   **All other students**: find your situation under “[How and when to get your PAL](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-provincial-attestation-letter/#how-and-when-to-get-your-pal)”\.

### PAL Validity

Your PAL only needs to be valid at the time you submit your study permit application and does not need to be valid when you travel to Canada or when you begin your program\.

PALs issued in 2025 expired on **Dec 31, 2025**, at **11:59 pm** Eastern Time \(ET\)\. PALs issued in 2026 will expire on **Dec, 31, 2026** at **11:59 pm** Eastern Time \(ET\)\.

Study permit applications are based on Coordinated Universal Time \(UTC\), not local time zones, so be sure to apply at least one day before your PAL expires\.

### Changing UBC programs or campuses

If you applied to multiple programs at UBC or to both UBC Vancouver and UBC Okanagan campuses, and then you decide to change programs or campuses after you accept your offer, you do **not** need a new PAL, since UBC has one Designated Learning Institution \(DLI\) number\.

## How and when to get your PAL[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/ubc\-provincial\-attestation\-letter/\#how\-and\-when\-to\-get\-your\-pal](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-provincial-attestation-letter/#how-and-when-to-get-your-pal)

UBC will issue 2026 PALs to most newly admitted undergraduate level students automatically via email within about 3 business days after accepting your admission offer\.

Review instructions for your specific situation below\.

### If you are outside Canada

You must apply for your study permit as soon as you receive your Letter of Admission and Provincial Attestation Letter\. You cannot [travel to Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/) until your study permit application is approved and you receive your Letter of Introduction \(study permit approval letter\) and visa, if required\.

**

New undergraduate bachelor’s degree students

**

You will need both your Letter of Admission and your undergraduate level Provincial Attestation Letter \(PAL\) before applying for your study permit\.

1.  **Confirm your personal information in your UBC student record**\.  
    Log into the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/), click *Edit Profile,* then select “Contact Summary” to confirm that your name matches the name on your passport, and that your home address and date of birth are correct\. You can update your address in the system if needed\. To update your name or date of birth, email [ubc\.pal@ubc\.ca](mailto:ubc.pal@ubc.ca)\.
2.  **Accept your offer of admission and pay your deposit**\.  
    Learn how to [accept your UBC offer](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/admitted/your-offer/) and pay the acceptance deposit\.
3.  **Wait for your Provincial Attestation Letter\.  
    **UBC will automatically send you your Provincial Attestation Letter by email within about 3 business days after you accept your offer\. Check the email account that you provided when you applied to UBC\. If you do not get your PAL after 3 business days, contact [ubc\.pal@ubc\.ca](mailto:ubc.pal@ubc.ca)\. 
4.  **Download your Letter of Admission from UBC\.  
    **Log into the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/), click *Admissions*, and select “Letter of Admission”\.
5.  **Apply for your study permit**\.  
    Review our [initial study permit tutorial](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/) to prepare your application\.

**

New Master’s degree and Doctoral degree students

**

You do not require a PAL for your application\. You will need your Letter of Admission before submitting your study permit application\.

**All graduate degree programs, except for FTMBA, MBAN, MM, PMBA and MBA\+MBAN**

1.  **Confirm your personal information in your UBC student record**\.  
    Log into the [graduate application system eVision](https://evision.as.it.ubc.ca/urd/sits.urd/run/siw_ubc_cwl) to confirm that your first and last names match the names on your passport, and that your home address and date of birth are correct before you accept your offer\. Ensure that all personal details are correctly reflected in your Letter of Admission\. If changes are required, please email [graduate\.apply@ubc\.ca](mailto:graduate.apply@ubc.ca)\.
2.  **Download your Letter of Admission and accept your offer of admission\.  
    **Download your Letter of Admission from the [graduate application system eVision](https://evision.as.it.ubc.ca/urd/sits.urd/run/siw_ubc_cwl), then [accept your UBC offer](https://community.grad.ubc.ca/checklists/new-student-checklist/confirm-acceptance-your-offer) and pay the acceptance deposit, if required\.
3.  **Apply for your study permit\.  
    **Review our [initial study permit tutorial](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/) to prepare your application\.

**FTMBA, MBAN, MM, PMBA, MBA\+MBAN students**

This information applies to the following master’s degrees in the Sauder Robert H\. Lee School of Business: Master of Business Administration, Master of Business Analytics, Master of Management, Professional Master of Business Administration, Dual degree Master of Business Administration and Master of Business Analytics\.

You will need your Letter of Admission before submitting your study permit application\.

1.  **Confirm your personal information in your UBC student record\.  
    **Check your Letter of Admission and log into the [Sauder Recruitment and Admissions System \(RAS\)](https://sauder.ubc.ca/login/) to confirm that your name matches the name on your passport, and that your primary/other address and date of birth are correct before you accept your offer\. If changes are required, please contact Sauder Recruitment and Admissions\. 
2.  **Accept your offer of admission and download your Letter of Admission\.  
    **Refer to your offer of admission email to learn how to pay the acceptance deposit, and download your letter of admission\.
3.  **Apply for your study permit\.**  
    Review our [initial study permit tutorial](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/) to prepare your application\.

**

New two\-term exchange students studying more than 6 months

**

This information applies to students coming to UBC through a [Go Global](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc/coming-ubc-exchange) exchange program\. If you are studying at UBC as a [Visiting Student](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc/coming-ubc-exchange) or the UBC\-TEC de Monterrey Joint Academic Program, check the “Non\-degree” sections below\.

If you will go on exchange for one term \(less than 6 months\), you do not require a study permit\. Read the “New non\-degree seeking students studying 6 months or less” section below\.

You will need your Letter of Acceptance before applying for your study permit\. Exchange students coming to UBC through [Go Global](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc/coming-ubc-exchange) are **exempt** from the Provincial Attestation Letter\.

1.  **Confirm your personal information in your UBC student record**\.  
    Check that your name matches the name on your passport and that your home address and date of birth are correct in your profile in the [Go Global Student Application Portal](https://goglobal.students.ubc.ca/ggapplications/s/login/) and on your Letter of Acceptance \(LOA\)\. If you need to correct any information, you **must** notify Go Global within **5 business days** of receiving the email notification about your admission and **before** accepting your offer of admission\.
2.  **Download your UBC Letter of Admission\.  
    **You can find the letter in the [Go Global Student Application Portal\.](https://goglobal.students.ubc.ca/ggapplications)
3.  **Accept your offer of admission\.  
    **Log into the [Applicant Service Centre](https://broker.id.ubc.ca/auth/realms/slid/protocol/openid-connect/auth?scope=openid&state=69cZnqo2wOkddmhRNc-bIHD76djeW_oGa-gKVk2jLPo.CJpXeKwiNh0.8gtT8ngjR0qqHlXcsPYsUg&response_type=code&client_id=client_oidc_idb0_prd&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fbroker.id.ubc.ca%2Fauth%2Frealms%2Fidb0%2Fbroker%2FSLID%2Fendpoint&nonce=PMiQ9HFZ9FSPBcg_nKLeCg) and accept your offer before the deadline\.
4.  **Apply for your study permit**\.  
    Review our [initial study permit tutorial](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/about-initial-study-permits/tutorial-apply-initial-study-permit-overview/) to prepare your application\.

**

New VIRS studying more than 6 months

**

As a Visiting International Research Student \(VIRS\), you will need both your Letter of Acceptance \(LOA\) and your Provincial Attestation Letter \(PAL\) before applying for your study permit if your research period is more than 6 months\. This requirement applies to VIRS students who are studying at the undergraduate level **and** the graduate level\.

If your research period is 6 months or less, you do not require a study permit – read the “New non\-degree seeking students studying 6 months or less” section below\.

1.  **Confirm your personal information in your UBC student record**\.  
    Check that your name matches the name on your passport and that your home address and date of birth are correct in your profile in the [Go Global Student Application Portal](https://goglobal.students.ubc.ca/ggapplications/s/login/) and on your Letter of Acceptance \(LOA\)\. If you need to correct any information, you **must** notify Go Global within **5 business days** of receiving the email notification about your admission and **before** accepting your offer of admission\.
2.  **Download your UBC Letter of Admission\.  
    **You can find the letter in the [Go Global Stu](https://goglobal.students.ubc.ca/ggapplications)[d](https://goglobal.students.ubc.ca/ggapplications)[ent Application Portal\.](https://goglobal.students.ubc.ca/ggapplications)
3.  **Accept your offer of admission\.  
    **Log into the [Applicant Service Centre](https://broker.id.ubc.ca/auth/realms/slid/protocol/openid-connect/auth?scope=openid&state=69cZnqo2wOkddmhRNc-bIHD76djeW_oGa-gKVk2jLPo.CJpXeKwiNh0.8gtT8ngjR0qqHlXcsPYsUg&response_type=code&client_id=client_oidc_idb0_prd&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fbroker.id.ubc.ca%2Fauth%2Frealms%2Fidb0%2Fbroker%2FSLID%2Fendpoint&nonce=PMiQ9HFZ9FSPBcg_nKLeCg) and accept your offer before the deadline\.
4.  **Get your Provincial Attestation Letter**\.  
    If you are a VIRS student studying in Canada for more than 6 months, request your PAL by completing the [online form](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_cXQEHd6vTzIODbg)\.
5.  **Apply for your study permit**\.  
    Review the [VIRS study permit tutorial](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc/visiting-international-research-students/applying-your-initial-study-permit) to prepare your study permit application\.

**

New Certificate and Diploma students

**

You will need both your Letter of Admission and your Provincial Attestation Letter \(PAL\) before applying for your study permit\.

1.  **Confirm your personal information in your UBC student record**\.  
    Log into the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/), click *Edit Profile* and select “Contact Summary” to confirm that your name matches the name on your passport, and that your home address and date of birth are correct\. You can update your address in the system if needed\. To update your name or date of birth, email [ubc\.pal@ubc\.ca](mailto:ubc.pal@ubc.ca)\.
2.  **Accept your offer of admission and pay your deposit**\.  
    Learn how to [accept your UBC offer](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/admitted/your-offer/) and pay the acceptance deposit\.
3.   **Request your Provincial Attestation Letter\.**Contact your program to request this document\.
4.  **Download your Letter of Admission from UBC\.  
    **Log into the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/), click *Admissions*, then select ”*Letter of Admission”*\.
5.  **Apply for your study permit\.**  
    Review our [initial study permit tutorial](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/) to prepare your application\.

**

New Graduate Certificate and Graduate Diploma students

**

You will need both your Letter of Admission and your Provincial Attestation Letter \(PAL\) before applying for your study permit\.

**All graduate certificate and graduate diploma programs except for the Diploma in Accounting \(DAP\)**

1.  **Confirm your personal information in your UBC student record**\.  
    Check with your [program](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/prospective-students/graduate-degree-programs) that your name matches the name on your passport and that your home address and date of birth are correct in their system\. Update any incorrect information with your program, if needed\.
2.  **Get your UBC Letter of Admission\.**Contact your program if you are not sure how to get it\.
3.  **Request your Provincial Attestation Letter\.**Contact your program to request this document\.
4.  **Apply for your study permit\.  
    **Review our [initial study permit tutorial](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/) to prepare your application\.

 **Diploma in Accounting Program \(DAP\) students**

1.  **Upon receiving your offer of admission, confirm your personal information in your UBC record\.  
    **Log into the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/), click *Edit Profile* and select “Contact Summary” to confirm that your name matches the name on your passport, and that your home address and date of birth are correct\. You can update your address in the system, if needed\. To update your name or date of birth, email [ubc\.pal@ubc\.ca](mailto:ubc.pal@ubc.ca)\.
2.  **Accept your offer of admission\.  
    **After you’ve confirmed your personal details are correct, accept your offer in the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/)\.
3.  **Wait for your UBC Letter of Admission \(LOA\)\.**The DAP office will send your LOA to you by email within 3 business days of accepting your offer\. At this time, you will be given instructions for getting your PAL\.
4.  **Request your Provincial Attestation Letter\.**Follow the instructions given to you at the time of receiving your letter of admission\. You can expect your PAL in about 7 business days\.
5.  **Apply for your study permit\.**  
    Review our [initial study permit tutorial](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/) to prepare your application\.

**

New Juris Doctor students

**

You will need both your Letter of Admission and your Provincial Attestation Letter \(PAL\) before applying for your study permit\.

1.  **Accept your offer of admission\.  
    **Learn how to [accept your offer](https://allard.ubc.ca/future-students/congratulations-your-offer) and pay your deposit\. 
2.  **Confirm your personal information in your UBC student record**\.  
    Check that your name matches the name on your passport and that your home address and date of birth are correct in the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/)\. If you need to update any information, please contact [admissions@allard\.ubc\.ca](mailto:admissions@allard.ubc.ca)\.
3.  **Save a copy of the Letter of Admission\.**Download the letter that was emailed to you by JD Admissions\.
4.  **Request your Provincial Attestation Letter\.  
    **Contact [admissions@allard\.ubc\.ca](mailto:admissions@allard.ubc.ca)\. You can expect your PAL within two weeks\.
5.  **Apply for your study permit\.**  
    Review our [initial study permit tutorial](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/) to prepare your application\. If required, you can request a Confirmation of Enrolment Letter from [admissions@allard\.ubc\.ca](mailto:admissions@allard.ubc.ca)\.

**

New non\-degree seeking students studying 6 months or less

**

This section applies to one\-term exchange students through [Go Global](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc/coming-ubc-exchange), one\-term [UBC\-TEC de Monterrey Joint Academic Program](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc/tec-de-monterrey-ubc-joint-academic-program) students, [VIRS](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc/visiting-international-research-students), access studies, [visiting students](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-visiting/), and [unclassified students](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-unclassified/) studying for 6 months or less\.

If you will study in Canada for 6 months or less, you do not need to apply for a study permit and do not need a PAL, but you’ll likely need to apply for a travel document to come to Canada as a visitor\.

Most visitors are allowed to stay in Canada for 6 months from the day they enter Canada\. You can study in Canada without a study permit as a visitor if **both** of the following applies to you:

-   Your entire program of studies will be completed within 6 months or less\.
-   Your program will be completed within your first 6\-month visitor period\.

Therefore, if you will enter and leave Canada within 6 months and complete your studies within your first 6\-month visitor period, a study permit and a PAL are not required\. 

If you would like to stay longer beyond the 6 months, you can apply for a [Visitor Record](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/extend-stay.html) after arriving in Canada to extend your stay as a visitor, however, your studies must be completed within your first 6\-month period\.

You must apply for and receive a travel document before you can travel to Canada\. You should **apply as soon as you receive your Letter of Acceptance** from Go Global or Enrolment Services\. Depending on [your citizenship](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/entry-requirements-country.html), you need one of the following to travel to Canada as a visitor:

-   [Electronic Travel Authorization \(eTA\)](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/eta.html)
-   [Temporary Resident Visa \(TRV\)](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/)

Contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) if you need support with your TRV\.

US citizens and US lawful permanent residents do not need an eTA or TRV\.

Check the [Travelling to Canada guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/travelling-to-canada/) for recommended documents to bring and other considerations\.

**

New non\-degree seeking students studying for more than 6 months

**

This section applies to [unclassified](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-unclassified/), [access studies](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-access-studies/), [visiting students](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-visiting/), and two\-term [UBC TEC de Monterrey Joint Academic Program](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc/tec-de-monterrey-ubc-joint-academic-program) students\.

If your program of studies is 6 months or less, you do not require a study permit—read the section above for “non\-degree seeking students”\.

If your program of studies is more than 6 months, you will need both your Letter of Admission and your undergraduate level Provincial Attestation Letter \(PAL\) before applying for your study permit\.

**Unclassified, access studies, and visiting students**

1.  **Confirm your personal information in your UBC student record**\.  
    Log into the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/), click *Edit Profile* and select “*Contact Summary”* to confirm that your name matches the name on your passport, and that your home address and date of birth are correct\. You can update your address in the system, if needed\. To update your name or date of birth, email [ubc\.pal@ubc\.ca](mailto:ubc.pal@ubc.ca)\.
2.  **Accept your offer of admission\.  
    **Learn how to [accept your offer](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/admitted/your-offer/) and pay your deposit
3.  **Request your Provincial Attestation Letter  
    **Contact [ubc\.pal@ubc\.ca](mailto:ubc.pal@ubc.ca) to discuss next steps\. PALs are limited in supply\. Each applicant’s request will be reviewed on a case\-by\-case basis\.
4.  **Download your Letter of Admission from UBC\.  
    **Log into the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/), click *Admissions*, then select ”*Letter of Admission”*\.
5.  **Apply for your study permit\.  
    **Review our [initial study permit tutorial](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/) to prepare your application\.

**Two\-term UBC\-TEC de Monterrey Joint Academic Program students**

1.  **Confirm your personal information in your UBC student record**\.  
    Check that your name matches the name on your passport and that your home address and date of birth are correct in your profile in the [Go Global Student Application Portal](https://goglobal.students.ubc.ca/ggapplications/s/login/) and on your Letter of Acceptance \(LOA\)\. If you need to correct any information, you **must** notify Go Global within **5 business days** of receiving the email notification about your admission and **before** accepting your offer of admission\.
2.  **Download your UBC Letter of Admission\.**  
    You can find the letter in the [Go Global Student Application Portal\.](https://goglobal.students.ubc.ca/ggapplications)
3.  **Accept your offer of admission**\.  
    Log into the [Applicant Service Centre](https://broker.id.ubc.ca/auth/realms/slid/protocol/openid-connect/auth?scope=openid&state=69cZnqo2wOkddmhRNc-bIHD76djeW_oGa-gKVk2jLPo.CJpXeKwiNh0.8gtT8ngjR0qqHlXcsPYsUg&response_type=code&client_id=client_oidc_idb0_prd&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fbroker.id.ubc.ca%2Fauth%2Frealms%2Fidb0%2Fbroker%2FSLID%2Fendpoint&nonce=PMiQ9HFZ9FSPBcg_nKLeCg) and accept your offer before the deadline\.
4.  **Get your Provincial Attestation Letter**\.  
    If you will study in Canada as a two\-term TEC\-UBC Joint Academic Program student, Go Global will contact you regarding your PAL about 2 weeks after you accept your offer of admission\.
5.  **Apply for your study permit**\.  
    Review our [initial study permit tutorial](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/about-initial-study-permits/tutorial-apply-initial-study-permit-overview/) to prepare your application\.

**

Current and returning UBC students

**

If you cannot return to Canada before your current study permit expires, you will need to apply for a new study permit from outside Canada and wait for your application to be processed before returning to Canada\. In this case, you will need a PAL in addition to a current Letter of Enrolment\. You are exempt from this requirement if you are enrolled in a Master’s or Doctoral degree program\.

1.  **Confirm your personal information in your UBC student record**\.  
    Check that your name matches the name on your passport, and that your home address and date of birth are correct in [Workday](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/personal-information/)\. If you need to update any information, check how to [change your personal information](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/)\.
2.  **Request your UBC Letter of Enrolment\.  
    **Contact an [Academic Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) in your faculty to request a Letter of Enrolment and make sure the letter indicates when you will resume studies, as well as your expected program completion date\. Use a Letter of Enrolment issued within the past 30 days – not your Letter of Admission from when you were first accepted to UBC\.
3.  **Contact International Student Advising\.  
    **Send a [webform](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0J8VRJgJQkuO2b4) to share your document expiry dates, when you will resume studies, if you transferred to UBC from a Canadian high school/post\-secondary institution, and your travel plans\.
4.  **Wait for your Provincial Attestation Letter\.  
    **If a PAL is required, International Student Advising will request it for you and, upon approval by the PAL team, it will be emailed to you directly from the UBC PAL Team\.
5.  **Apply for your study permit**\.  
    Review our [initial study permit tutorial](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/) to prepare your application\. Be sure to include your recently issued Letter of Enrolment and UBC PDF [transcript](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-transcript/) in your application\.

## If you are inside Canada[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/ubc\-provincial\-attestation\-letter/\#if\-you\-are\-inside\-canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-provincial-attestation-letter/#if-you-are-inside-canada)

**

Current UBC students in all programs

**

Plan ahead if your documents expire soon and you have [travel plans](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/travelling-outside-canada/)\. In general, it’s best to extend your study permit and [Temporary Resident Visa](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/temporary-resident-visa-trv/) \(if you need one\) inside Canada before you travel\. It’s also possible to return and [extend your study permit](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/extend-study-permit/) from inside Canada before your study permit expires\. Contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support with planning your document extensions and travel plans\.

You will need a **current UBC Letter of Enrolment** for your study permit extension, not your initial Letter of Admission to UBC\. Learn how to apply for your study permit extension and how to get your Letter of Enrolment by reviewing the [study permit extension tutorial](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/extend-study-permit/)\.Whether you need a Provincial Attestation Letter \(PAL\) in your study permit extension application depends on your situation—check below\.

**Current UBC students in the same level of studies**

If you applied for your study permit with a UBC Letter of Admission, and you are continuing studies at the same level of studies, you do not need a PAL\. For example, if you are extending your study permit to continue your undergraduate degree \(even if you changed programs or majors\), you do not need a PAL\. Apply for your study permit extension from inside Canada before your study permit expires\.

**If you transferred to UBC before Nov 8, 2024**: If you transferred to UBC from a Canadian high school or another post\-secondary institution in Canada before Nov 8, 2024, send International Student Advising an [online form](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0J8VRJgJQkuO2b4) with details about your situation before applying to extend your study permit\. An assessment must be made to determine if a PAL will be required as part of your application\.

If you transferred to UBC after Nov 8, 2024, you need a PAL\. Check the next section\.

**Current UBC students changing levels of studies at UBC**

If you applied for your study permit with a UBC Letter of Admission, and you are changing levels of studies at UBC, you can continue studies with your current valid study permit\. 

For example, if you are an undergraduate student who completed your bachelor’s degree and have been accepted to a master’s degree at UBC, you can continue to study at UBC with the same study permit, so long as it’s still [valid](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/#maintaining-your-student-status)\. If you will have a [gap of more than 150 days](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/taking-time-away-school-international/) between programs, contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/)\. 

If you are changing levels of study from a Doctoral or Master’s degree to certificate, diploma, undergraduate, or unclassified studies, you will need a PAL for your study permit extension application\. Send International Student Advising an [online form](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0J8VRJgJQkuO2b4) about your situation for support\.

**Current UBC students restoring status**

If your study permit extension was refused, or your study permit has expired and you need to apply for [restoration](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/restoration-status/), contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for assistance\.

**

Students coming to UBC from a Canadian high school or Canadian post\-secondary institution with a study permit

**

You will need both your Letter of Admission and your Provincial Attestation Letter \(PAL\) before applying for your study permit\.

As of Nov 8, 2024, you must be enrolled at the Designated Learning Institution \(DLI\) named on your study permit\. If you [change institutions](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/change-schools.html), you must apply for a study permit extension with your UBC Letter of Admission and most students need to receive the new study permit before beginning studies at UBC\. There are special rules for students transferring from a Canadian high school\. Check [important considerations](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/#important-considerations) for details and what to do if you have travel plans\. Be sure to apply for a study permit with your UBC Letter of Admission and PAL as soon as you receive them\.

If you are a new undergraduate bachelor’s degree student:

1.  **Confirm your personal information in your UBC student record**\.  
    Log into the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/), click *Edit Profile,* then select “Contact Summary” to confirm that your name matches the name on your passport, and that your home address and date of birth are correct\. You can update your address in the system if needed\. To update your name or date of birth, email [ubc\.pal@ubc\.ca](mailto:ubc.pal@ubc.ca)\.
2.  **Accept your offer of admission and pay your deposit**\.  
    Learn how to [accept your UBC offer](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/admitted/your-offer/) and pay the acceptance deposit\.
3.  **Wait for your Provincial Attestation Letter\.  
    **UBC will automatically send you your Provincial Attestation Letter by email within about 3 business days after you accept your offer\. Check the email account that you provided when you applied to UBC\. If you do not get your PAL after 3 business days, contact [ubc\.pal@ubc\.ca](mailto:ubc.pal@ubc.ca)\.
4.  **Download your Letter of Admission from UBC\.  
    **Log into the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/), click *Admissions*, and select “Letter of Admission”\.
5.  **Apply for your study permit\.  
    **If you will apply from inside Canada, review our [study permit extension tutorial](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/extend-study-permit/) to prepare your application\. If you will apply from outside Canada, review our [initial study permit tutorial](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/apply-initial-study-permit/)\.

**

New students in Canada as a visitor, worker, or asylum seeker

**

Only some people can apply for a study permit through the [process inside Canada](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/extend-study-permit/) and be [exempt from the PAL](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/get-documents/provincial-attestation-letter.html)\.

Contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for support\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/ubc\-provincial\-attestation\-letter/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-provincial-attestation-letter/#if-you-have-questions)

For support with obtaining your Letter of Admission:

-   **Undergraduate students**: Contact [undergraduate admissions](https://you.ubc.ca/contact-us/)\.
-   **Graduate students**: Contact your [graduate program staff](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/current-students/supervision-advising/program-advising)\.
-   **Current and returning students**: Contact [Academic Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) or your [graduate program staff](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/current-students/supervision-advising/program-advising) for your Letter of Enrolment\.
-   **VIRS, exchange and UBC\-Tec Joint Academic Program students:** Contact [Go Global](https://global.ubc.ca/go-global/contact-go-global)\.
-   **Unclassified, access studies and visiting students:** Contact [Enrolment Services Advisors](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

For support with getting your Provincial Attestation Letter, contact [ubc\.pal@ubc\.ca](mailto:ubc.pal@ubc.ca)\.

For support with your study permit application, travel documents, or other immigration questions, contact [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/)\.

## International Student Guide[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/ubc\-provincial\-attestation\-letter/\#international\-student\-guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-provincial-attestation-letter/#international-student-guide)

Find everything you need to know about life as an international student at UBC’s Vancouver campus\.

[View the guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/)

## Immigration FAQs[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/ubc\-provincial\-attestation\-letter/\#immigration\-faqs](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-provincial-attestation-letter/#immigration-faqs)

Get the [latest updates on immigration](https://students.ubc.ca/news/category-ircc-policy-updates/), and answers to common immigration and health insurance questions in the [Frequently Asked Questions](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-immigration-health-insurance-faq/) \(FAQ\)\.

## The information on this page may change[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/study\-permits/ubc\-provincial\-attestation\-letter/\#the\-information\-on\-this\-page\-may\-change](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/study-permits/ubc-provincial-attestation-letter/#the-information-on-this-page-may-change)

The immigration information on this page has been reviewed and endorsed by Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultants \(RCICs\) or Regulated International Student Immigration Advisors \(RISIAs\) in compliance with the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and Regulations\. However, this is not a legal document and information may change without notice\. Always refer to [Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada](http://www.cic.gc.ca/) \(IRCC\) for the most up\-to\-date information\.

title: Brock Commons South Multifaith Prayer and Quiet Contemplation Room
content_markdown:
> > Prayer room ablution stations
> 
> > The ablution stations are temporarily closed until further notice\. Access to the prayer room remains open\.

The Brock Commons South Multifaith Prayer and Quiet Contemplation Room is located on the fourth floor of the [Brock Commons South building](https://maps.ubc.ca/?code=BRCS) in rooms 4110A and 4001B\.

The two prayer rooms are open by drop\-in to all students for prayer, quiet contemplation, and reflection\. Separate ablution facilities are available in both spaces\. Universal washrooms are across the hall from the prayer space\.

## Before using the room[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/ubc\-multifaith\-prayer\-rooms/brock\-commons\-south\-multifaith\-prayer\-and\-quiet\-contemplation\-room/\#before\-using\-the\-room](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/ubc-multifaith-prayer-rooms/brock-commons-south-multifaith-prayer-and-quiet-contemplation-room/#before-using-the-room)

Please review the [guidelines for use](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/ubc-multifaith-prayer-rooms/#prayer-room-rules-and-responsibilities) and follow all prayer room rules and responsibilities\.

If you’re hosting an event that serves the faith\-based or spiritual student community at UBC, please book the [Brock Commons South Community Space](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/brock-commons-south-community-space/)\.

## Prayer room hours[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/ubc\-multifaith\-prayer\-rooms/brock\-commons\-south\-multifaith\-prayer\-and\-quiet\-contemplation\-room/\#prayer\-room\-hours](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/ubc-multifaith-prayer-rooms/brock-commons-south-multifaith-prayer-and-quiet-contemplation-room/#prayer-room-hours)

The prayer rooms are available from Monday to Friday at the following times:

-   Rooms 4110A and 4110B are open to all genders from 7:00 am to 1:00 pm\. 
-   Room 4110A is open to self\-identifying male students from 1:00 pm to 8:30 pm\.
-   Room 4110B is open to self\-identifying female students from 1:00 pm to 8:30 pm\.

## Room capacity[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/ubc\-multifaith\-prayer\-rooms/brock\-commons\-south\-multifaith\-prayer\-and\-quiet\-contemplation\-room/\#room\-capacity](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/ubc-multifaith-prayer-rooms/brock-commons-south-multifaith-prayer-and-quiet-contemplation-room/#room-capacity)

-   Room 4110A has a capacity of 40 to 45 people\.
-   Room 4110B has a capacity of 20 to 25 people\.

## Location[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/ubc\-multifaith\-prayer\-rooms/brock\-commons\-south\-multifaith\-prayer\-and\-quiet\-contemplation\-room/\#location](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/ubc-multifaith-prayer-rooms/brock-commons-south-multifaith-prayer-and-quiet-contemplation-room/#location)

-   Rooms 4110A, 4110B
-   [Brock Commons South](https://maps.ubc.ca/?code=BRCS) \(6180 Walter Gage Road\)

## How to access the room[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/ubc\-multifaith\-prayer\-rooms/brock\-commons\-south\-multifaith\-prayer\-and\-quiet\-contemplation\-room/\#how\-to\-access\-the\-room](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/ubc-multifaith-prayer-rooms/brock-commons-south-multifaith-prayer-and-quiet-contemplation-room/#how-to-access-the-room)

You can enter and use the prayer rooms without a UBC card during the building hours from 7:00 am to 8:30 pm\.

## Reporting a problem about the facilities[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/ubc\-multifaith\-prayer\-rooms/brock\-commons\-south\-multifaith\-prayer\-and\-quiet\-contemplation\-room/\#reporting\-a\-problem\-about\-the\-facilities](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/ubc-multifaith-prayer-rooms/brock-commons-south-multifaith-prayer-and-quiet-contemplation-room/#reporting-a-problem-about-the-facilities)

If you encounter any issues with the prayer room or its use, please report it as soon as possible to the Office of the Vice\-President, Students at [vpsassist@mail\.ubc\.ca](mailto:vpsassist@mail.ubc.ca)\.

Concerns may include cleanliness, damage, lighting, misuse of these facilities, or complaints about other users\.

### Urgent concerns

In case of fire or emergency evacuation, follow the procedures posted in the rooms\. In the event of an incident or concern that requires attention, contact [UBC Security](https://security.ubc.ca/) by calling [604\.822\.2222](tel:6048222222)\. For emergencies that require an immediate response, call 911\.

title: Wesbrook Building Prayer Room
content_markdown:
The Wesbrook Building Prayer Room is located on the first floor of the [Wesbrook Building](https://maps.ubc.ca/?code=WESB) in rooms 116 and 118\.

The two prayer rooms are open by drop\-in to all students of any faith for prayer, quiet contemplation, and reflection\. Room 116 is open to female\-identifying students, and Room 118 is open to male\-identifying students\.

Single\-occupancy ablution stations are available on the same level and opposite the prayer space in rooms 132A and 132B\.

## Before using the room[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/ubc\-multifaith\-prayer\-rooms/wesbrook\-building\-prayer\-room/\#before\-using\-the\-room](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/ubc-multifaith-prayer-rooms/wesbrook-building-prayer-room/#before-using-the-room)

title: I am Stronger than My Depression: CBT Skills Group
content_markdown:
## About the group[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/i\-am\-stronger\-than\-my\-depression\-cbt\-skills\-group/\#about\-the\-group](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/i-am-stronger-than-my-depression-cbt-skills-group/#about-the-group)

The goal of this group is to explore strategies for managing low mood and reconnecting with the parts of oneself that are lost when depressed\. Each session focuses on learning ways to improve low mood and includes activities to practice between sessions\.

The primary areas of focus are:

-   The triangle of thoughts, feelings, and actions: how each side influences the other
-   Stress, depression, and lifestyle, and how to find balance
-   Thinking styles: the interplay of thoughts and mood
-   Social life: connecting with others and connecting with oneself

## Eligibility[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/i\-am\-stronger\-than\-my\-depression\-cbt\-skills\-group/\#eligibility](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/i-am-stronger-than-my-depression-cbt-skills-group/#eligibility)

All group sessions are held in person on the Vancouver campus\. UBC Student Health and Wellbeing recognizes the unique needs of each student and will provide alternate options if group programming is not an appropriate referral option or fit\.

## How to register[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/i\-am\-stronger\-than\-my\-depression\-cbt\-skills\-group/\#how\-to\-register](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/i-am-stronger-than-my-depression-cbt-skills-group/#how-to-register)

This group is by referral only\.

Student Health and Wellbeing is currently accepting referrals\. Call [604 822 3811](tel:6048223811) to book a a [mental health care appointment](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/)\. 

If you are already connected with a UBC health professional, such as a counsellor, physician, mental health nurse, or a Wellness Advisor, they can make the referral\.

title: Brock Commons South Community Space
content_markdown:
## About the space[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/brock\-commons\-south\-community\-space/\#about\-the\-space](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/brock-commons-south-community-space/#about-the-space)

The Brock Commons South Community Space is a multi\-purpose room available to undergraduate and graduate students currently enrolled at UBC Vancouver\. It’s a space to pray, reflect, worship, meditate, contemplate, and build community\.

The Brock Commons South Community Space is located in Room 4104 of [Brock Commons South](https://www.maps.ubc.ca/?code=BRCS) \(6180 Walter Gage Road\)\. 

### Amenities

To ensure the space can accomodate a variety of events and activities, the following amenities are available:

-   Accessible building entrances, room entrance, and elevators
-   All\-gender washroom located nearby
-   Kitchen facilities, including a microwave, refrigerator, and dishwasher
-   36 chairs for community gathering
-   7 moveable tables and 1 stationary table
-   Screen and audiovisual \(AV\) system for presentations
-   An adjacent [Prayer and Quiet Contemplation Room](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/ubc-multifaith-prayer-rooms/brock-commons-south-multifaith-prayer-and-quiet-contemplation-room/)

## Booking the space[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/brock\-commons\-south\-community\-space/\#booking\-the\-space](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/brock-commons-south-community-space/#booking-the-space)

The Brock Commons South Community Space can be booked for community programming that serves the faith\-based and spiritual student community at UBC\. Bookings are available Monday to Friday from 7:00 am to 10:00 pm, excluding [statutory holidays](https://hr.ubc.ca/working-ubc/statutory-holidays) observed by UBC\. 

To book the space, you must be one of the following:

-   Student from AMS and GSS faith\-based and spiritual clubs at UBC Vancouver
-   The Office of the Vice\-President, Students \(VPSO\) staff member
-   Chaplain at UBC

### How to book the space

If you are interested in booking the space, please follow these steps:

1.  Make sure your programming complies with the [booking guidelines](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/brock_commons_south_community_space_booking_guidelines.pdf) \(pdf\)\.
2.  Check the space availability on [Calendly](https://calendly.com/bcs-communityspace-ubc/event-booking)\. Please do not book on Calendly, as registration happens separately\.
3.  Submit a [booking request form](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eb9Xb1CkQ3OolKe)\.

## Contact us[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/religion\-spirituality/brock\-commons\-south\-community\-space/\#contact\-us](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/religion-spirituality/brock-commons-south-community-space/#contact-us)

Email [bcs\.communityspace@ubc\.ca](mailto:bcs.communityspace@ubc.ca) for more information about booking the Brock Commons South Community Space\.

title: Returning to UBC and applying for readmission
content_markdown:
If you left UBC to deal with a family emergency, to focus on your health and mental well\-being, academic issues, a job opportunity, or to take time away from studies, it can be hard to know where to start to return to your studies\.  
  
It’s important to start planning for your return as early as possible so you can meet various application and program\-specific deadlines and apply for a study permit, housing, or other services you may need to resume your studies\.

## First, review your scenario[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/readmission/\#first\-review\-your\-scenario](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/readmission/#first-review-your-scenario)

Find guidance on common return scenarios to understand what your return might look like, whether you took a leave of absence, had to withdraw, or are enrolling as a mature student or alumnus\.

[Read the scenarios](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/readmission/return-scenarios/)

## Next, follow the returning checklist[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/readmission/\#next\-follow\-the\-returning\-checklist](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/readmission/#next-follow-the-returning-checklist)

Once you’ve reviewed your return scenario, use the [Return to UBC Checklist](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/readmission/return-checklist/) to help you plan your next steps\. 

## If you need help[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/readmission/\#if\-you\-need\-help](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/readmission/#if-you-need-help)

Contact [Enrolment Services](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) during opening hours\.  
  
If you are an international student, connect with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) first\.
