title: Return scenarios for readmission
content_markdown:
If you’re planning to return to UBC after taking a break from your studies, it’s important to understand which scenario applies to you\. This page explains common situations, such as returning from academic leave, readmission after withdrawing from your studies, or returning as a mature student or alumnus\.

Use the list below to jump to the common return scenario that may apply to you\. If you don’t see your specific return scenario below, contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) for help\. If you are an international student, connect with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) first\.

-   [Academic Leave of 1 year or less](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/readmission/return-scenarios/#one-year)
-   [Leave of more than 1 year](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/readmission/return-scenarios/#over-one-year)
-   [If you were required to discontinue or withdraw from your studies](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/readmission/return-scenarios/#if-you-were-required-to-discontinue-or-withdraw-from-your-studies)
-   [Admission or readmission as a mature learner](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/readmission/return-scenarios/#if-youre-a-mature-learner)
-   [Taking courses as a UBC alumnus](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/readmission/return-scenarios/#if-youve-graduated-from-ubc)

## If you’ve taken an Academic Leave[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/readmission/return\-scenarios/\#if\-youve\-taken\-an\-academic\-leave](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/readmission/return-scenarios/#if-youve-taken-an-academic-leave)

For most programs, in accordance with the [Academic Calendar](http://www.calendar.ubc.ca/vancouver/index.cfm?tree=3,289,0,0), students in “Good Standing” may take [Academic Leave](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/taking-break-courses/) \(time away from UBC studies\) of up to one full year or 12 months\. 

Before taking leave, you likely met with an academic advisor at your faculty or school\. Whether you are returning on your originally planned timeline or not, check for any emails you received from your faculty or school and follow the steps outlined\. 

Students who are studying at another institution on exchange or study abroad, dual enrollment, or with a letter of permission from their faculty are not considered to be on academic leave\.

### Academic Leave of 1 year or less

Students who take an academic leave for one year or less **do not** need to follow a formal return process to register for courses\.  
  
For example, a student in “Good Standing” after completing the 2025/26 Winter Session will automatically be eligible to register in the same program for the 2026 Summer, 2026/27 Winter, 2027 Summer and 2027/28 Winter Sessions\.

You are encouraged to discuss course selection and degree planning with an Academic Advisor in your faculty or school upon your return\.

Although you do not need to follow a formal return process, there may be other requirements you must meet to return to UBC\. Use the [Return to UBC and readmission checklist](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/readmission/return-checklist/) to help you plan your next steps\.

### Leave of more than 1 year

If you are in good academic standing but have taken a break for more than one Winter Session, you must submit an application for readmission to re\-enter your program, to transfer into a new program, or to enrol on a different campus\. 

Speak with your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) to learn about program admission requirements for re\-entry and guidance in submitting your readmission application\. If you are an international student, connect with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) first\.

After speaking to an Advisor about readmission, use the [Return to UBC and readmission checklist](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/readmission/return-checklist/) to help you plan your next steps\. 

## If you were required to discontinue or withdraw from your studies[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/readmission/return\-scenarios/\#if\-you\-were\-required\-to\-discontinue\-or\-withdraw\-from\-your\-studies](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/readmission/return-scenarios/#if-you-were-required-to-discontinue-or-withdraw-from-your-studies)

Generally, students required to discontinue or withdraw from their studies must wait for a 12\-month period and may be required to submit a Letter of Appeal with their readmission application\. In some cases, students must complete courses at a recognized post\-secondary institution and attain a minimum GPA to qualify for readmission\. 

If you were required to discontinue your studies or withdraw from UBC after a failed year, refer to the communications you received from your faculty or school\. It will detail your earliest return date and the required steps you must take\. Keep in mind that the maximum time allowed to complete an undergraduate program is typically 6 or 7 years from when you were first admitted to the program, and it will depend on your faculty\. Please confirm this detail with your [faculty or school](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools)\.  
  
Please speak with a [Faculty Academic Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) and an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) for any additional program\-specific readmission requirements\. If you’re an international student, connect with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) first\. 

After speaking to an advisor about readmission, use the [Return to UBC and readmission checklist](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/readmission/return-checklist/) to plan your next steps\. 

## If you’ve graduated from UBC[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/readmission/return\-scenarios/\#if\-youve\-graduated\-from\-ubc](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/readmission/return-scenarios/#if-youve-graduated-from-ubc)

UBC alumni who have completed a 4\-year bachelor’s degree program can apply for unclassified status to take courses at UBC\. Learn how to [apply for unclassified status](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-unclassified/)\. 

## If you’re a mature learner[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/readmission/return\-scenarios/\#if\-youre\-a\-mature\-learner](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/readmission/return-scenarios/#if-youre-a-mature-learner)

Mature applicants are individuals who have not been in full\-time formal education for at least 4 years\. Learn how to [apply as a mature student](https://you.ubc.ca/applying-ubc/requirements/mature-students/)\.  

## If you need help[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/readmission/return\-scenarios/\#if\-you\-need\-help](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/readmission/return-scenarios/#if-you-need-help)

Contact [Enrolment Services](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) during opening hours\.  
  
If you are an international student, connect with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) first\.

title: Return to UBC and readmission checklist
content_markdown:
Your deadlines and responsibilities as a returning student will vary depending on your return scenario and specific situation\. 

If you haven’t yet, follow the [online guide](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/readmission/) on returning to UBC and applying for readmission, and review the [common return scenarios](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/readmission/return-scenarios/) first\.

## First, connect with advising [https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/readmission/return\-checklist/\#first\-connect\-with\-advising](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/readmission/return-checklist/#first-connect-with-advising) 

If you haven’t already, meet with an [Academic Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) to discuss course selection and degree planning, including your remaining requirements for graduation\. If you cannot access Workday to view your academic record, you can access an [unofficial transcript](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/records/ordering-transcript/#unofficial-transcript) through the [UBC Official Documents tool](https://ubc.appiancloud.com/suite/sites/ubc-official-documents)\. You will be able to access [Workday](http://myworkday.ubc.ca/) again once you are readmitted to UBC\.

Then, contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) to learn about admission requirements if you’re submitting a readmission application or returning as a mature student\. You can also receive support with creating a financial plan, course registration issues, or clearing enrolment holds or debts on your account\.

If you’re an international student, connect with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) first to review your visa and study permit with an advisor to ensure that you are eligible to study in Canada\.

## Next, review additional steps for your situation[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/readmission/return\-checklist/\#next\-review\-additional\-steps\-for\-your\-situation](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/readmission/return-checklist/#next-review-additional-steps-for-your-situation)

Read the list below to learn what support is available for your situation and other steps you may need to follow to return to studies\. 

**

Indigenous students

**

Connect with the [Indigenous Student Support Team](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/financial-support-options/financial-support-indigenous/) if you would like help creating a financial plan and require guidance on planning for the costs associated with returning to studies at UBC\. [The First Nations House of Learning \(FNHL\)](https://fnhl.ubc.ca/students/) provides services and activities to support First Nations, Métis, and Inuit students’ academic success and positive social and cultural experiences\.

**

BC Former Youth in Care

**

Connect with [Joe Stevens](mailto:joseph.stevens@ubc.ca), a designated UBC Vancouver campus contact for [BC youth in and from care](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc-life/former-youth-in-care/), before you submit an admission application and prior to re\-enrolling\.

**

Students with enrolment holds or debts

**

All holds and/or debts must be resolved before you can register\. Connect with an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) for help\.

**

Students with government loans

**

If you had previous Canadian or US government student loans, you must notify your loan servicer if you are returning to part\-time or full\-time studies\. Speak to an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) for information about your eligibility for in\-school deferment or interest\-free status\.

**

Students who are sponsored

**

If a portion of your UBC tuition fees is paid by a sponsor, please ensure your sponsor submits a [Sponsorship Billing application](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_dg7icsLodwcOdeu) before the start of the term\. Learn more about your [responsibilities as a sponsored student](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/sponsorship-billing/information-sponsored-students/)\.

**

Students who are parents

**

There are several ways you can receive support as a student parent at UBC\. Learn more about [available resources](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/resources-who-are-parents/)\.

**

Students who plan to live on campus

**

If you are interested in living on campus, review the eligibility requirements and [apply for on\-campus housing](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/how-to-apply/) as early as possible\. UBC Housing has a separate application process and deadlines\.

## Apply for readmission[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/readmission/return\-checklist/\#apply\-for\-readmission](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/readmission/return-checklist/#apply-for-readmission)

If you need to formally apply for readmission based on your return scenario, you can do so through the [Applicant Service Centre](https://myapplication.ubc.ca/) using your Campus Wide Login \(CWL\) and by paying a non\-refundable [application fee](https://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/fees/application-and-administrative-fees)\.

Most programs require you to submit your readmission application by **January 15** for the upcoming Summer or Winter session, but deadlines may vary\. For specific dates, check the UBC Academic Calendar or contact [Enrolment Services](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

## Access other support and resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/readmission/return\-checklist/\#access\-other\-support\-and\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/readmission/return-checklist/#access-other-support-and-resources)

**[Get health support](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-topics/)**

Taking care of your physical and mental health through self\-help resources or support from professional staff and peer communities is an important part of your return to studies at UBC\.

**[Contact an Accessibility Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/)**

The Centre for Accessibility can provide guidance and resources if you require support with medical or disability\-related accommodations\.

**[2SLGBTQIA\+ resources](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/2slgbtqia-resources/)**

Learn more about campus resources, involvement opportunities, and career guidance for Two Spirit, lesbian, gay, bisexual, trans, queer, intersex, and asexual \(2SLGBTQIA\+\) students\.

**[Learn about living off campus](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/other-housing/off-campus-housing/)**

If you don’t plan to stay in residence while attending UBC, access resources to help you find housing, avoid scams, and more\.

## If you need help[https://students\.ubc\.ca/enrolment/readmission/return\-checklist/\#if\-you\-need\-help](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/readmission/return-checklist/#if-you-need-help)

Contact [Enrolment Services](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) during opening hours\.  
  
If you are an international student, connect with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) first\.

title: Understanding your Emotions (AEDP) Group
content_markdown:
## About the group[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/understanding\-your\-emotions\-aedp\-group/\#about\-the\-group](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/understanding-your-emotions-aedp-group/#about-the-group)

In this experiential group, you’ll learn how to work with emotions as pathways to deeper self\-understanding, inner calm, and authenticity\. The goal is to understand that your emotions are messengers, not obstacles\.  
  
This group may be especially meaningful for students who feel disconnected from their emotions, or sense they are “numbing” or avoiding parts of themselves\. It’s also a good fit for those who are curious about how their emotions connect to their sense of identity and relational patterns\.  
  
Grounded in principles from Accelerated Experiential Dynamic Psychotherapy \(AEDP\), this group creates a safe and supportive space for you to explore emotional patterns, build self\-awareness, and connect more fully with your authentic self\.

Topics will include:

-   Understanding emotional responses and patterns
-   Emotional avoidance and defense mechanisms
-   Nervous system regulation and grounding techniques
-   Developing self\-compassion and emotional resilience
-   Exploring the connection between body, emotion, and self
-   Cultivating authentic self\-expression and inner clarity

## Eligibility[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/understanding\-your\-emotions\-aedp\-group/\#eligibility](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/understanding-your-emotions-aedp-group/#eligibility)

The group sessions are held in person on the Vancouver campus\.

Student Health and Wellbeing the unique needs of each student and will provide alternate options if group programming is not an appropriate referral option or fit\.

## Group session details[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/understanding\-your\-emotions\-aedp\-group/\#group\-session\-details](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/understanding-your-emotions-aedp-group/#group-session-details)

-   **Schedule**: Wednesdays, from Oct 7 to Dec 2, 2026
-   **Time:** 4:00 to 5:30 pm
-   **Location**: UBC Vancouver Campus

## How to register[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/understanding\-your\-emotions\-aedp\-group/\#how\-to\-register](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/understanding-your-emotions-aedp-group/#how-to-register)

The group is by referral only\. Call [604 822 3811](tel:6048223811) to book a [mental health care appointment](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/)\.  

If you’re already connected with a UBC Student Health and Wellbeing professional, such as a counsellor, physician, mental health nurse, or a Wellness Advisor, they can make the referral for you to join the group\.

title: Art Therapy for Anxiety Group
content_markdown:
## About the group[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/art\-therapy\-for\-anxiety\-group/\#about\-the\-group](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/art-therapy-for-anxiety-group/#about-the-group)

A 6\-session therapeutic group that blends Cognitive Behavioral Therapy \(CBT\) with Art Therapy to help students explore and manage anxiety through creative expression\.

The primary areas of focus are:

-   Foster insight, emotional regulation, and resilience\.
-   Use visual art to explore and shift anxious thought patterns\.
-   Provide a supportive space for healing\.

## Eligibility[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/art\-therapy\-for\-anxiety\-group/\#eligibility](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/art-therapy-for-anxiety-group/#eligibility)

You do not need artistic experience\. Session facilitators will provide all the supplies you need to create\.

The group sessions are held in person on the UBC Vancouver campus\. UBC Counselling Services recognizes the unique needs of each student and will provide alternate options if group programming is not an appropriate referral option or fit\.

## Group session details[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/art\-therapy\-for\-anxiety\-group/\#group\-session\-details](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/art-therapy-for-anxiety-group/#group-session-details)

-   **Schedule**: Wednesdays from May 20 to Jun 24, 2026
-   **Time**: 3:30 to 5:00 pm
-   **Location**: UBC Vancouver Campus

## How to register[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/art\-therapy\-for\-anxiety\-group/\#how\-to\-register](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/art-therapy-for-anxiety-group/#how-to-register)

Counselling Services is currently accepting referrals\. Call [604 822 3811](tel:6048223811) to request an appointment\. 

If you’re already connected with a UBC health professional, such as a counsellor, physician, mental health nurse, or a Wellness Advisor at [Counselling Services](https://students.ubc.ca/health/counselling-services/), they can make the referral\.

content_markdown:
## Skills you’ll develop[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/your\-degree/arts/health\-and\-society/\#skills\-youll\-develop](https://students.ubc.ca/career/your-degree/arts/health-and-society/#skills-youll-develop)

The [Health and Society \(HESO\) Minor](https://heso.arts.ubc.ca/) offers a multidisciplinary exploration of issues related to health, illness, and society\. As a HESO student, you will tailor your minor to your interests and goals by choosing from approximately 60 courses in social sciences, humanities, arts, population and public health, and more\. Given this flexibility, you will develop a unique course list and set of skills\.

These skills may include:

-   Applying theory to understand sociocultural determinants of health
-   Understanding the ways in which representations of health and disease have changed over time
-   Describing the ways in which cultural representations of health and illness reflect or frame societal understandings of disease and health care
-   Creating interdisciplinary connections and gaining broader perspectives on specific aspects of health, such as historical, social, and psychological perspectives of drug use, and more
-   Understanding how the structure of health care systems impact health in Canada and beyond
-   Describing factors influencing health status and health behaviours in Canada

title: Your degree in the Study of Religion
content_markdown:
## Skills you’ll develop[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/your\-degree/arts/study\-of\-religion/\#skills\-youll\-develop](https://students.ubc.ca/career/your-degree/arts/study-of-religion/#skills-youll-develop)

The [Program in the Study of Religion](https://rgst.arts.ubc.ca/) is an interdisciplinary undergraduate program that includes a [major](https://rgst.arts.ubc.ca/program/major-requirements/) and [minor](https://rgst.arts.ubc.ca/program/minor-requirements/), as well as an [Honours](https://rgst.arts.ubc.ca/program/honours-program) option\. In this program, you’ll study various religions from a number of disciplinary perspectives, incorporating different regions and historical periods\. You will also specialize in a religious tradition of your choice\. By pursuing a degree in the Study of Religion, you’ll gain a number of skills to support your future career\.

These skills may include:

-   Identifying the variety of religious traditions in the contemporary world
-   Analyzing how religious ideals and beliefs are expressed in a variety of textual and expressive traditions, both formal and informal\.
-   Critically assessing and applying a variety of methodologies and approaches to the study of religion\.
-   Applying problem solving to the examination of religious behaviour across a variety of different cultures and historical periods
-   Explaining the persistence of public religious identity and forms of expression as vibrant spiritual, cultural, political and ideological forces\.
-   Expressing and analysing ideas through strategic oral and written communication
-   Researching and collecting data applied to the exploration of ancient and modern\-day religious texts
-   Interpreting primary and secondary sources based on available evidence
-   Analyzing the effects of religion and religious identity across a number of forms of expressive culture such as art, literature, music, popular culture, and more

title: Your degree in Neuroscience
content_markdown:
## Skills you’ll develop[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/your\-degree/science/your\-degree\-in\-neuroscience/\#skills\-youll\-develop](https://students.ubc.ca/career/your-degree/science/your-degree-in-neuroscience/#skills-youll-develop)

While studying [Neuroscience](https://you.ubc.ca/ubc_programs/neuroscience/), you’ll gain a deep understanding of the biological basis of behaviour and explore the structure and function of the brain and nervous system\. You’ll develop important skills and learn advanced research methods to gain a multidisciplinary understanding of behavior and cognition as they relate to nervous system function\.

These skills may include:

-   Critical observation and evaluation of nervous system dysfunction, ranging from psychiatric to neurological conditions
-   Design and execution of neuroscience experiments with human participants or animal models
-   Research and critical evaluation of biomedical literature
-   Application of specialized knowledge related to neurological diseases and disorders
-   Application of ethical considerations in neuroscience research, decision making, and consideration of societal implications
-   Verbal and written communication of technical and scientific data aimed at neuroscientific and non\-neuroscientific audiences
-   Technical usage of computational modeling, neuroimaging, and statistics

title: Your degree in Interdisciplinary Studies
content_markdown:
## Skills you’ll develop[https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/your\-degree/arts/interdisciplinary\-studies/\#skills\-youll\-develop](https://students.ubc.ca/career/your-degree/arts/interdisciplinary-studies/#skills-youll-develop)

During your degree in [Interdisciplinary Studies](https://interdisciplinary.arts.ubc.ca/) \(IDST\), you’ll design your own program by combining at least 3 distinct disciplines into a single undergraduate degree\. Your program will bring together multiple distinct disciplines, like Humanities, Social Sciences, and Creative and Performing Arts, and could even include disciplines from other faculties, like Science\.

Since each IDST program is distinct, you can view the “Your Degree” pages of the programs you are combining to explore all the skills you will develop\. Beyond what you learn from each individual discipline, you’ll develop a set of adaptable and transferable skills\. 

These skills may include:

-   Innovative critical thinking skills that apply creative “outside\-the\-box” methodologies
-   Ability to engage with multiple disciplinary perspectives
-   Clearly communicating complex information to non\-specialist audiences
-   Working effectively on projects with team members from a diverse range of professional and academic backgrounds
-   Understanding the strengths and limitations of different academic disciplines
-   Identifying and solving complex problems that cannot be addressed by a single disciplinary approach
-   Adaptability and flexibility to navigate changing environments, expectations, and challenges, while maintaining focus and effectiveness

Career opportunities vary widely across a range of fields including finance, banking, marketing, communications, sales, operations administration, client services, research, government & policy, and others\.

There are many career paths that can combine your academics, skills, and experience with your different interests\. Read through the job titles below for ideas\.

title: Accessible housing for students with disabilities
content_markdown:
The Centre for Accessibility works with UBC Residence and Housing to assess whether students with disabilities are eligible for accessible housing units or priority placement in on\-campus housing\.

Student housing is a limited resource and successful applications are subject to availability\. Placements are typically offered in year\-round housing in a building in which you are [eligible to live](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/eligibility/)\.

## Eligibility requirements[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/centre\-for\-accessibility/accessible\-housing\-for\-students\-with\-disabilities/\#eligibility\-requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/accessible-housing-for-students-with-disabilities/#eligibility-requirements)

### Course Load Requirements

The credit load requirement for UBC Student Housing is 9 credits per term\. If you are unable to meet this for disability\-related reasons, you can make a request through the Centre for Accessibility to remain eligible for student housing with a minimum of 6 on\-campus credits per term\.

### Determine your eligibility

You may be eligible for accessible student housing if you are eligible for student housing and your disability or chronic health condition presents significant functional limitations, which meets one or both of the following:

-   reduces your housing options
-   requires you to live on campus to equitably access the full academic experience

Please review the information on UBC Student Housing’s [Accessibility in Residence](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/getting-started/accessibility/) page to determine if you should apply\.

## How to apply [https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/centre\-for\-accessibility/accessible\-housing\-for\-students\-with\-disabilities/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/accessible-housing-for-students-with-disabilities/#how-to-apply) 

### Application information

An application for accessible student housing does not remove the requirement to apply for housing and to be eligible for student housing generally\. All applications for on\-campus residence must be made through [UBC Student Housing and Community Services](http://www.housing.ubc.ca/) by the appropriate deadlines\.

### Submit your application

1.  Submit your [general residence application](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/) to UBC Student Housing and Community Services by the [deadline](https://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/applications/important-dates/)\.
2.  Complete and submit the [Accessible Student Housing Request Form](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5Ar0vs3szpOjHnw) along with a [Medical Assessor Form](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/accessible_housing_medical_assessment_form.pdf) \(pdf\) completed by your health care provider\.

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/centre\-for\-accessibility/accessible\-housing\-for\-students\-with\-disabilities/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/accessible-housing-for-students-with-disabilities/#if-you-have-questions)

The [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/) facilitates disability\-related accommodations and supports that are designed to remove barriers for students with disabilities and ongoing medical conditions\.

Contact the Centre by email at [info\.accessibility@ubc\.ca](mailto:info.accessibility@ubc.ca) or call [604 822 5844](tel:6048225844)\.

title: After registering with the Centre for Accessibility
content_markdown:
## First, inform your instructors[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/centre\-for\-accessibility/after\-registering\-with\-the\-centre\-for\-accessibility/\#first\-inform\-your\-instructors](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/after-registering-with-the-centre-for-accessibility/#first-inform-your-instructors)

Once you are registered with the [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility), you will use the [Clockwork online platform](https://clockwork.as.it.ubc.ca/ClockWork/custom/misc/home.aspx) to send your Letter of Accommodation \(LOA\) to your instructor\(s\) automatically\. You will have the option to download a copy of your LOA if needed\. This letter should be sent to the instructor of the class that you’re seeking the accommodation for as soon as possible, preferably within the first 2 weeks of the class\. You will be required to send the LOA in order to access exam booking and note taker request services\. 

You are **not required** to share information or documentation about your disability or ongoing medical condition with your instructor or any other UBC office\. Your transcript will not show your registration with the Centre for Accessibility\.

If your instructor or another UBC unit requires additional information about the nature of your disability or documentation, please direct them to the Centre for Accessibility\.

## Book your exams and tests[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/centre\-for\-accessibility/after\-registering\-with\-the\-centre\-for\-accessibility/\#book\-your\-exams\-and\-tests](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/after-registering-with-the-centre-for-accessibility/#book-your-exams-and-tests)

Please familiarize yourself with the Centre’s [exam booking guidelines and instructions](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-accommodations-disabilities/exam-accommodation-guidelines-expectations/)\. We encourage you to [book your exams](https://clockwork.as.it.ubc.ca/ClockWork/user/test/default.aspx) as early as possible\.

## Requesting a change to your academic accommodations[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/centre\-for\-accessibility/after\-registering\-with\-the\-centre\-for\-accessibility/\#requesting\-a\-change\-to\-your\-academic\-accommodations](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility/after-registering-with-the-centre-for-accessibility/#requesting-a-change-to-your-academic-accommodations)

If you need to request new accommodations or changes to your current ones, meet with your Accessibility Advisor as early as possible\. Depending on the nature of the accommodation and the timing of the request, it may not be possible to implement the changes immediately\.

title: US private student loans
content_markdown:
US private student loans are a useful option for undergraduate and graduate students who meet one of the following: 

-   You’re not eligible for Direct Loans\.
-   You need additional funding beyond Direct Loans\.
-   You wish to apply for funding after an academic session is over\. 

Private loans often have **higher interest rates** than the rates for [Direct Loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/) \(Subsidized, Unsubsidized, or PLUS\)\. If you’re eligible for Direct Loans, you’re encouraged to explore that option first\.

If you’re an independent undergraduate student or a dependent student whose parents did not apply or qualify for a Parent PLUS loan, private student loans may be an option to fully fund your [Cost of Attendance](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-direct-loan-funding-amounts/)\.

Currently, UBC is aware of the following US private student loan providers who have funded UBC students in the past three years: 

-   Earnest
-   Sallie Mae 

If you have questions about another US private student loan provider who has indicated they are able to fund you at UBC, please contact [usloans\.inquiry@ubc\.ca](mailto:usloans.inquiry@ubc.ca)\.

## Eligibility requirements[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/us\-private\-student\-loans/\#eligibility\-requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-private-student-loans/#eligibility-requirements)

### Earnest

To be eligible for an [Earnest private student loan](https://www.earnest.com/student-loans?utm_source=foreign&utm_medium=campus_partnerships), you must meet all of the following requirements:

-   You’re a US citizen or eligible non\-citizen\.
-   You’re registered in an eligible bachelor’s, master’s, or PhD program\.
-   If you’re an undergraduate student, you must be registered in at least 6 credits for each term funded by your loan\.
-   If you’re a graduate student, you must be registered for each term\.

### Sallie Mae

To be eligible for a [Sallie Mae private student loan](https://www.salliemae.com/student-loans/), you must meet all of the following requirements:

-   You’re a US citizen or eligible non\-citizen\.
-   You’re registered in an eligible program at UBC\.
-   You’re registered in at least one course for each term funded by your loan\. If you’re a graduate student, registration in a thesis is sufficient\.
-   If you’re applying for funding for living costs, you must be registered in at least 6 credits for each term funded by your loan\.

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/us\-private\-student\-loans/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-private-student-loans/#how-to-apply)

### Step 1: Submit an application with the lender

Apply for a US private student loan directly with your chosen lender below:

-   [Earnest](https://www.earnest.com/student-loans?utm_source=foreign&utm_medium=campus_partnerships)
-   [Sallie Mae](https://www.salliemae.com/student-loans/)

If you have questions about another private loan provider who has indicated they are able to fund you at UBC, please contact [usloans\.inquiry@ubc\.ca](mailto:usloans.inquiry@ubc.ca)\.

### Step 2: Submit the UBC US Private Loan Request Form

For Earnest and Sallie Mae private student loans, submit the [UBC US Private Loan Request Form](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6LIq7wAFOMjj4Vg) to provide UBC with the information required to certify your loan\.

### Step 3: Check your contact information

Make sure your email address is correct on [Workday](https://myworkday.ubc.ca/), since UBC will email you about the status of your application\. Learn how to add or change your [contact information](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/personal-information/adding-changing-your-contact-information/) in Workday\.

## How your application is processed[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/us\-private\-student\-loans/\#how\-your\-application\-is\-processed](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-private-student-loans/#how-your-application-is-processed)

1.  The lender will automatically notify UBC that your application has been submitted\.
2.  UBC will determine your [Cost of Attendance](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-direct-loan-funding-amounts/) based on the cost of your program and the information provided on your UBC US Private Loan Request Form submission\. 
3.  UBC will email you when your loan is approved\.

## Cancelling your loan application[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/us\-private\-student\-loans/\#cancelling\-your\-loan\-application](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-private-student-loans/#cancelling-your-loan-application)

To cancel your loan application, you can contact the lender directly during the Right of Cancellation period, which is 9 business days from the date of certification\.

## Receiving your loan funding[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/us\-private\-student\-loans/\#receiving\-your\-loan\-funding](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-private-student-loans/#receiving-your-loan-funding)

Once UBC receives your funding from the lender, it will be applied to your UBC tuition account\.

If you have a Canadian bank account, you’re recommended to set up [direct deposit](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/setting-up-your-direct-deposit/)\. Direct deposit allows any remaining loan funding after tuition and student fees are paid to be deposited directly into your bank account\.

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/us\-private\-student\-loans/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-private-student-loans/#additional-resources)

-   [Funding for US Students](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/)
-   [Resources for students with US loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/resources-us-loans/)
-   [US Direct Loan funding amounts](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-direct-loan-funding-amounts/)
-   [US Loans FAQ](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-loans-faq/)
-   [US Policies and Consumer Information \(pdf\)](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/us_funding_policies_and_consumer_info.pdf)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/us\-private\-student\-loans/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-private-student-loans/#if-you-have-questions)

For help with finances, registration, records, and more, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

Associate Career Advisors \(ACAs\) work with the [UBC Career Centre](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/ubc-career-centre/) to help UBC students from all disciplines become career\-ready graduates\. ACAs facilitate career learning for undergraduate and graduate students through one\-to\-one advising, workshops, and more\.

## Who can apply?[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/peer\-programs/associate\-career\-advisors/\#who\-can\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/peer-programs/associate-career-advisors/#who-can-apply)

To apply, students must be:

-   Current upper\-year undergraduate, Master’s, or PhD students
-   Eligible for Work Learn positions
-   Can commit to a one\-year term from May to the following April

There are **4 to 8 positions** available each year\.

### If you require accommodations

The Career Center would like to recognize that being able to participate in student leadership development opportunities such as this is a privilege\. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, perform essential job functions, and receive other benefits and privileges of employment\.

If you have specific accommodations for your ability to participate and contribute to the program, please email the Team Lead, Gelsey, at [gelsey\.guan@ubc\.ca](mailto:gelsey.guan@ubc.ca) to discuss what accommodations can be made for your particular situation\.

## Time commitment[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/peer\-programs/associate\-career\-advisors/\#time\-commitment](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/peer-programs/associate-career-advisors/#time-commitment)

The time commitment is 20 hours per week during the Summer Term \(May to August\), and 10 hours per week during the Winter Term \(September to April\)\. For detailed time requirements, please review the position description\.

## How to Apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/peer\-programs/associate\-career\-advisors/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/peer-programs/associate-career-advisors/#how-to-apply)

This position is listed as a Summer Work Learn position in [CareersOnline](https://ubc-csm.symplicity.com/students/app/home)\.

You can apply in March during the Work Learn application period\. Check the Work Learn website for specific timelines and how to submit your application through CareersOnline\.

## Skills developed[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/peer\-programs/associate\-career\-advisors/\#skills\-developed](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/peer-programs/associate-career-advisors/#skills-developed)

-   Coaching
-   Active listening
-   Communication
-   Career Advising
-   Adaptability
-   Empathy
-   Analysis and problem solving
-   Teamwork
-   Career exploration strategies and Job search skills

## Contact[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/peer\-programs/associate\-career\-advisors/\#contact](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/peer-programs/associate-career-advisors/#contact)

If you have questions, email [gelsey\.guan@ubc\.ca](mailto:gelsey.guan@ubc.ca)\.

title: Food Hub Market Volunteers
content_markdown:
## About Food Hub Market Volunteers[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/peer\-programs/food\-hub\-market\-volunteers/\#about\-food\-hub\-market\-volunteers](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/peer-programs/food-hub-market-volunteers/#about-food-hub-market-volunteers)

The [Food Hub Market](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/food-hub-market/) is a student\-led, not\-for\-profit initiative committed to enhancing food security for the UBC student community\. 

Food Hub Market volunteers support our mission to provide affordable groceries while fostering a welcoming space that promotes food literacy, cultural vibrancy, and social connections at the UBC Vancouver campus\. There are 3 volunteer teams:

-   **Operations**  
    Support daily Food Hub Market operations, connect students with resources, and promote community well\-being\.
-   **Programming**  
    Support food skill\-building workshops and campus info booths\.
-   **Social Media**  
    Create content related to food, nutrition, and food security topics for the [Food Hub Market Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/ubcfoodhubmarket/)\.

## Who can apply?[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/peer\-programs/food\-hub\-market\-volunteers/\#who\-can\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/peer-programs/food-hub-market-volunteers/#who-can-apply)

All UBC students who have interest in food, nutrition, and food security are welcome to apply\.

Each year, there are **over 25 positions** available across the 3 volunteer teams\. 

### If you require accommodations

If you require accommodations to apply and participate in this volunteer opportunity, please reach out via email to [community\.foodhub@ubc\.ca](mailto:community.foodhub@ubc.ca)\.

## Time commitment[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/peer\-programs/food\-hub\-market\-volunteers/\#time\-commitment](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/peer-programs/food-hub-market-volunteers/#time-commitment)

Volunteers must commit to at least 1 full volunteer term\. You should be prepared to dedicate **2 to 3 hours per week** to your shifts during your volunteer term\. There will also be a volunteer appreciation event near the end of each term that will last approximately 1\.5 hours\. 

There are 3 volunteer terms throughout the academic year:

1.  **Winter Term 1:** September to last week of classes in December
2.  **Winter Term 2**: January to last week of classes in April
3.  **Summer Term 1**: May to last week of classes in June

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/peer\-programs/food\-hub\-market\-volunteers/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/peer-programs/food-hub-market-volunteers/#how-to-apply)

Applications are now closed\.

 Each volunteer term has its own recruitment period during the following times:

-   **Winter Term 1**: Late July
-   **Winter Term 2**: Late November
-   **Summer Term 1**: Late March

## Skills developed[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/peer\-programs/food\-hub\-market\-volunteers/\#skills\-developed](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/peer-programs/food-hub-market-volunteers/#skills-developed)

-   Knowledge of food, nutrition, and food security 
-   Communication
-   Public speaking
-   Facilitation
-   Event organization
-   Graphic designing
-   Customer service
-   Empathy
-   Teamwork

## Contact[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/peer\-programs/food\-hub\-market\-volunteers/\#contact](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/peer-programs/food-hub-market-volunteers/#contact)

For questions regarding volunteer opportunities, please email [community\.foodhub@ubc\.ca](mailto:community.foodhub@ubc.ca)\.

title: Innovative Projects Fund
content_markdown:
## About the fund[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/funding\-project/innovative\-projects\-fund/\#about\-the\-fund](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/funding-project/innovative-projects-fund/#about-the-fund)

Established in 1996, the Innovative Project Fund \(IPF\) is an annual fund provided by UBC and administered by the [Office of the Vice\-President, Students](https://vpstudents.ubc.ca/) in partnership with the [Alma Mater Society \(AMS\)](https://www.ams.ubc.ca/)\. 

The fund supports the development of programs, projects, and ideas that enrich and enhance the university experience for students\.

## Eligibility requirements[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/funding\-project/innovative\-projects\-fund/\#eligibility\-requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/funding-project/innovative-projects-fund/#eligibility-requirements)

Applications are accepted from the following:

-   Clubs affiliated with the Alma Mater Society \(AMS\)
-   Graduate Student Society \(GSS\)
-   UBC faculties
-   Other officially recognized UBC organizations
-   Campus community groups led by student organizations

Applications must be submitted by current UBC students as project leads\. Collaboration with faculty and staff is highly encouraged\. All projects should prioritize student involvement and focus on student\-led initiatives\.

## Proposal Review Process[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/funding\-project/innovative\-projects\-fund/\#proposal\-review\-process](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/funding-project/innovative-projects-fund/#proposal-review-process)

Proposals are reviewed by a 6\-member committee, which includes:

-   Three student representatives, appointed by AMS
-   Two staff representatives, appointed by the Office of the Vice\-President, Students
-   One faculty member, appointed by the Office of the Vice\-President, Students

### Selection criteria

Proposals will be evaluated based on the following criteria\.

#### Innovation

Projects must enrich and enhance the University for students and be highly innovative\. This may include projects which solve pressing issues, provide new ways of doing things, or propose new ideas that haven’t been tried at UBC before\. 

Additionally, IPF will support projects which demonstrate a clear connection between the innovative idea and an identified gap, need, or opportunity on campus\.

#### Benefit

Projects must benefit a significant number of students\. Projects need to provide evidence of the reach they will have to students, beyond those directly involved in the project, and demonstrate a compelling need for the project through student survey data or other forms of gap analysis\. 

#### Visibility

Projects must be visible to the campus community\. Projects need to be open, transparent, and accessible to campus and allow for broad engagement from the full community\.

#### Student involvement

Projects must involve students in the design, development, creation, and implementation in significant and meaningful ways\. For all faculty and staff proposed projects, there needs to be a clear and compelling rationale provided for the ways in which students are involved in leading and contributing to the project\.

## Funding limits[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/funding\-project/innovative\-projects\-fund/\#funding\-limits](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/funding-project/innovative-projects-fund/#funding-limits)

-   The maximum funding is $3,500 per project per year\. Applicants can submit proposals for the same project for a maximum of 3 consecutive years and can receive a maximum of $10,500 over those years\. If your project lasts more than 1 year, you will need to reapply for funding each year\.
-   Funds must be used within a 12\-month period and cannot be carried forward without permission from the Committee\. Funds that are unspent each year must be returned to the Office of the Vice\-President, Students\.
-   Applicants who are awarded funding must provide a status report and financial statement twice: halfway through the project implementation and after the project or initiative has been completed\. A detailed reporting schedule will be outlined in the funding letter\.
-   Any equipment purchased with IPF funds becomes property of UBC\. Any funds from the sale of equipment will be returned to the IPF\.

## Additional limits[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/funding\-project/innovative\-projects\-fund/\#additional\-limits](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/funding-project/innovative-projects-fund/#additional-limits)

The following types of projects have additional limits as follows\.

**

International projects and travel

**

Applications for projects where individuals are sent abroad must include an explanation of how the project will substantially enrich and enhance the University for students\.

Funds cannot be used to support learning and personal development for one or a small group of individuals\.

The IPF does not fund travel costs or airfare\. 

**

Conferences

**

The IPF does not fund conference attendance for students\. The IPF may provide funding to create a new annual conference for students and may fund new innovative projects that occur within an already existing annual conference\.

**

Competitions

**

The IPF does not fund sporting or design teams involved in competitions with other universities and/or non\-UBC organizations and which involve relatively few UBC students\. There are other sources of funding available for competitions via the AMS and UBC\.

**

Honoraria and salaries

**

The IPF does not fund honoraria or salaries for project members or students\. 

**

Curriculum Projects

**

The IPF does not fund projects or activities that are in any way a part or extension of the academic curriculum at UBC, such as field trips or student attendance at academic conferences\.

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/funding\-project/innovative\-projects\-fund/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/funding-project/innovative-projects-fund/#how-to-apply)

### Application timeline

Applications open in Winter Term 1 and Winter Term 2 each year\. Check back in September for application instructions\.

Funding decisions will be communicated to applicants within 6 to 8 weeks of each application deadline\.

## Previously funded projects[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/funding\-project/innovative\-projects\-fund/\#previously\-funded\-projects](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/funding-project/innovative-projects-fund/#previously-funded-projects)

The Fund has supported many projects, programs, and initiatives, including:

-   UX Open, a UX/UI design competition where students collaborate to develop digital products and present their work to industry professionals for feedback and prizes
-   [Product Sprint](https://ubcpm.club/productsprint/), an immersive program organized by the UBC Product Management Club that gives students hands\-on experience developing and launching product ideas
-   Engineering design teams such as [UBC Sailbot](https://www.ubcsailbot.org/), where students design and test fully autonomous sailboats used to advance oceanic research
-   [Innovation Onboard](https://www.innovationboard.ca/ubc.html), a cross\-disciplinary program that brings together science, engineering, and business students to develop startup ideas through workshops, mentorship, and a final pitch competition
-   Creative and socially engaged projects like the Embodied Research Project, which explores identity, community, and belonging through experimental theatre and public performances
-   [UBC Astronomy Club](https://www.ubcastronomyclub.com/), which expanded its stargazing events by upgrading telescope equipment, allowing more students to observe celestial objects at campus observation nights

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/funding\-project/innovative\-projects\-fund/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/funding-project/innovative-projects-fund/#if-you-have-questions)

Email [vpsassist@mail\.ubc\.ca](mailto:vpsassist@mail.ubc.ca) if you experience any issues throughout the application or if you have questions about the fund\.

title: Walter Gage Memorial Fund
content_markdown:
## About the fund[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/funding\-project/walter\-gage\-memorial\-fund/\#about\-the\-fund](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/funding-project/walter-gage-memorial-fund/#about-the-fund)

The Walter H\. Gage Memorial Fund provides financial support for non\-curricular student projects and activities that are campus\-oriented, of broad general interest, enhance the reputation of the university, or have academic components involving merit and initiative\.

The Fund is permanently endowed through gifts from alumni, students, faculty, staff and others\. Income from the endowment fund amounts will vary based on the rate of return determined by Financial Services\.

Named in honour of Walter H\. Gage, who served UBC for over 50 years—including as President from 1969 to 1975—the Fund reflects his deep commitment to students and teaching\. Known for his generosity, personal support of students, and dedication to financial assistance programs, Gage left a lasting impact across all faculties\.

## Eligibility requirements[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/funding\-project/walter\-gage\-memorial\-fund/\#eligibility\-requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/funding-project/walter-gage-memorial-fund/#eligibility-requirements)

Applications are accepted from the following:

-   UBC students in good standing at the time of application and during the project period
-   UBC student groups or clubs that are:
    -   Affiliated with the AMS
    -   Affiliated with a Faculty or School
    -   Associated with another officially recognized UBC organization

Applications will not be accepted from faculty members, staff, off\-campus organizations, or from UBC students applying on behalf of off\-campus organizations\.

### Eligible projects

The following projects are eligible for funding:

-   Hosting an undergraduate conference at UBC
-   Attending an undergraduate conference held elsewhere as a UBC delegate
-   Participating in an education\-related activity, such as:
    -   Youth parliaments
    -   Scientific or engineering competitions
    -   Participation in sporting competitions by athletes representing UBC on teams not fully sponsored by UBC Athletics

The Fund does **not** fund projects or activities that are in any way a part or extension of the academic curriculum at UBC, such as field trips or graduate student attendance at academic conferences\.

Students should secure additional sources of funding, including personal contributions\.

## Funding limits[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/funding\-project/walter\-gage\-memorial\-fund/\#funding\-limits](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/funding-project/walter-gage-memorial-fund/#funding-limits)

-   The Committee may allocate up to $2,000 Canadian dollars, but the Fund must **not** be the only or largest single source of funding for any project or activity\.
-   A group may **not** apply for funding support in 2 consecutive years for the same project if its membership remains unchanged\.
-   After the completion of the activity or project, a final report, including a brief summary of the event and the final budget, should be submitted to the Committee\. Future funding for the group or club will be contingent upon the receipt of this information\.
-   Any unspent amount must be returned to the Walter H\. Gage Memorial Fund\.
-   The group can only apply for one project or event per fiscal year \(from April 1 to March 31\)\.

### Conference\-specific guidelines

-   Each delegation may receive funding up to a maximum of $2,000 Canadian dollars\.
-   The grant may not exceed 50% of the total expenses of hosting or attending the conference\.
-   The Fund does not provide support for hosting or attending non\-student conferences, or for graduate student travel or registration at academic conferences\.
-   After the conference, the delegation must provide a cost accounting and a final report\. The student body represented by the delegation must also be given a report on conference activities\.

## Proposal review process[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/funding\-project/walter\-gage\-memorial\-fund/\#proposal\-review\-process](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/funding-project/walter-gage-memorial-fund/#proposal-review-process)

Proposals are reviewed by a 9\-member committee, which includes:

-   3 representatives nominated by the Office of the Vice\-President, Students
-   A representative nominated by the Office of the President
-   2 representatives appointed by the UBC Alumni Association
-   3 representatives nominated by the Alma Mater Society, with normally one being the Vice\-President Administration

The Committee reviews application submissions on separate dates throughout the year\.

| Application deadline | Meeting date |
| --- | --- |
| Tues, Sep 15, 2026 | Tues, Sep 29, 2026 |
| Tues, Oct 13, 2026 | Tues, Oct 23, 2026 |
| Tues, Nov 10, 2026 | Tues, Nov 24, 2026 |

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/funding\-project/walter\-gage\-memorial\-fund/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/funding-project/walter-gage-memorial-fund/#how-to-apply)

### Application timeline

Applications must be received by the Committee a minimum of 4 weeks before an event or project start date\. Applications submitted after an event or project has been completed will **not** be considered\.

There are multiple application deadlines throughout the year\. Below are the most recent application dates:

-   Tues, Sep 15, 2026
-   Tues, Oct 13, 2026
-   Tues, Nov 10, 2026

### Submit your application

1.  Gather the information required for your application, listed in the [Walter Gage Fund Application Checklist](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/walter_gage_application.pdf) \(pdf\)\. The supporting letter from the AMS or department can be submitted later, to meet the application deadline\.
2.  Sign and email your completed application and supporting documentation in a single PDF document to [vpsassist@mail\.ubc\.ca](mailto:vpsassist@mail.ubc.ca)\. The date on which the email is received will be recorded as the submission date\.

## Previously funded projects[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/funding\-project/walter\-gage\-memorial\-fund/\#previously\-funded\-projects](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/funding-project/walter-gage-memorial-fund/#previously-funded-projects)

The Fund has supported a wide range of student\-led initiatives that create impact, such as:

-   A global health initiative that delivered sickle cell disease education and screening in Nepal
-   Cultural events like Langar Day, organized by the [UBC Sikh Students’ Association](https://amsclubs.ca/skih-students-association/), that foster dialogue, inclusion, and community on campus
-   Student research and publications like the [Undergraduate Journal of Art History and Visual Culture](https://ojs.library.ubc.ca/index.php/UJAH)
-   InnovateHer Conference, organized by the [AMS Girls in STEAM](https://amsclubs.ca/girls-in-steam/), which empowers students from underrepresented genders in STEAM
-   International academic competitions such as the [Sauder Summit Global Case Competition](https://www.saudersummit.ca/)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/funding\-project/walter\-gage\-memorial\-fund/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/funding-project/walter-gage-memorial-fund/#if-you-have-questions)

Email [vpsassist@mail\.ubc\.ca](mailto:vpsassist@mail.ubc.ca) if you experience any issues with your application or have questions about the fund\.

content_markdown:

## About the market[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/food\-hub\-market/\#about\-the\-market](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/food-hub-market/#about-the-market)

The Food Hub Market is a student\-led, not\-for\-profit community space offering affordable grocery essentials while fostering social connection on the UBC Vancouver Campus\. The Market is dedicated to improving access to affordable and culturally diverse grocery staples that support student food security and meet everyday student needs in a welcoming and inclusive environment\. 

The space also provides hands\-on food skills workshops, community events and educational outreach on food literacy and nutrition\. These programs promote food literacy and food skills, help students navigate available food security resources, and strengthen student community connections\. 

Visit the Food Hub Market on the main floor of the Centre for Interactive Research in Sustainability \([CIRS Building, 2260 West Mall](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Food+Hub+Market/@49.2619104,-123.2557037,17z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x548673188b325961:0x7300239e3d3655d2!8m2!3d49.2619069!4d-123.2531288!16s%2Fg%2F11ty7w281z?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI2MDIxMS4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D)\)\.

### Available products

The Food Hub Market carries a variety of grocery essentials that support diverse dietary needs and reflect the cultural diversity of the campus community, including:

-   Fresh fruits and vegetables
-   Plant\-based proteins
-   Grains, pasta, and noodles
-   Canned vegetables

-   Dairy and dairy alternatives
-   Sauces, seasonings, and condiments
-   Cleaning supplies
-   Snacks

### History of Food Hub Market

The Food Hub Market began as a UBC pilot initiative that ran from February to April 2022, with the goal of providing at\-cost groceries in a welcoming community space at the UBC Vancouver Campus\. 

Since then, the market has re\-opened under a student\-led governance model with staff support from the [Health Equity, Promotion and Education unit](https://facultystaff.students.ubc.ca/health-wellbeing/health-equity-promotion-education)\.

[Shelves of canned and boxed food with a sign on the left that reads Food Hub Market\. A student wearing a mask peruses the aisles\.](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/food_hub_market.jpg)

## Contact us[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/food\-hub\-market/\#contact\-us](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/food-hub-market/#contact-us)

-   **Address:** CIRS Building, Main Floor \([2260 West Mall](https://www.google.com/maps/place/Food+Hub+Market/@49.2619104,-123.2557037,17z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x548673188b325961:0x7300239e3d3655d2!8m2!3d49.2619069!4d-123.2531288!16s%2Fg%2F11ty7w281z?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI2MDIxMS4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D)\)
-   **Email:** [community\.foodhub@ubc\.ca](mailto:community.foodhub@ubc.ca) 
-   **Instagram:** @ubcfoodhubmarket

### Opening Hours

The Market is closed on all [statutory holidays](https://hr.ubc.ca/working-ubc/statutory-holidays) observed by UBC\. For updates to hours, follow [@ubcfoodhubmarket](http://instagram.com/ubcfoodhubmarket) on Instagram\.

-   **Tuesday**: 10:30 am to 4:30 pm
-   **Wednesday**: 10:30 am to 4:30 pm
-   **Thursday**: 10:30 am to 4:30 pm

## Events and workshops[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/food\-hub\-market/\#events\-and\-workshops](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/food-hub-market/#events-and-workshops)

The Market offers a variety of interactive workshops, presentations, booths, as well as resources related to food, nutrition, and food security to help students build food literacy and skills\. These offerings also foster a sense of belonging and connection among UBC students\. 

For event updates, follow [@ubcfoodhubmarket](http://instagram.com/ubcfoodhubmarket) on Instagram\. 

If you are interested in collaborating with the Food Hub Market for projects or events, email [community\.foodhub@ubc\.ca](mailto:community.foodhub@ubc.ca)\.

## Get involved[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/food\-hub\-market/\#get\-involved](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/food-hub-market/#get-involved)

Apply to be a [Food Hub Market Volunteer](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/peer-programs/food-hub-market-volunteers/) and participate in food security initiatives to support the UBC student community\. 

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/about\-student\-services/food\-hub\-market/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/food-hub-market/#if-you-have-questions)

For additional questions, visit the Food Hub Market during regular hours of operation, or email [community\.foodhub@ubc\.ca](mailto:community.foodhub@ubc.ca)\. 

You can also browse [food and nutrition resources](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-topics/food-nutrition/) to learn about how to maintain a balanced diet, explore your relationship with food, and develop cooking skills\.

title: What can I do with my Kinesiology degree?
content_markdown:
## Who you are matters [https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/your\-degree/what\-can\-i\-do\-with\-my\-kinesiology\-degree/\#who\-you\-are\-matters](https://students.ubc.ca/career/your-degree/what-can-i-do-with-my-kinesiology-degree/#who-you-are-matters) 

Your Kinesiology degree is just one part of what you have to offer\. You also bring skills and knowledge from experiences you’ve had, places you’ve been, and the values you share with family, friends, and community\. 

Reflecting on your skills and interests can help you make life and career decisions\. 

-   [Identify your values](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/identifying_your_values.pdf) \(pdf\)  
    Clarifying your interests and values can help you determine career possibilities that are a good fit for you\. 
-   [Name your skills](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/skills_inventory_worksheet.pdf) \(pdf\)   
    Reflect on your skills and consider how they may be valued by future employers\.
-   [Know your strengths](https://store.gallup.com/product/cliftonstrengths-for-students/01tPa00000Qh7P4IAJ)  
    Purchase the Clifton Strengths assessment tool for $28 CAD using your [student email address](https://it.ubc.ca/services/email-voice-internet/ubc-student-email-service?upn=) to identify and describe your talents\. 
-   [Discover career possibilities with Challenge Cards](https://app.mysparkpath.com/signup)UBC students can use code xwbgaavpor7vfy7 for free access to this online career exploration game\.  
    

## Develop your Skillset [https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/your\-degree/what\-can\-i\-do\-with\-my\-kinesiology\-degree/\#develop\-your\-skillset](https://students.ubc.ca/career/your-degree/what-can-i-do-with-my-kinesiology-degree/#develop-your-skillset) 

Throughout your Kinesiology degree, you’ll develop specific skills that employers are looking for when hiring graduates, including: 

-   Knowledge of safe, effective movement techniques in a wide variety of physical activities 
-   Creative and strategic problem solving 
-   Collaboration with peers, faculty, and community members through group projects and assignments 
-   Critical thinking and analysis 
-   Familiarity with specialized tools, equipment, and modern technologies connected to exercise physiology, motor performance, and more  
-   Data collection, analysis, and interpretation through research within lab and occasional field environments 
-   Effective written and oral communication skills to present ideas to a range of audiences 
-   Ability to understand, examine, and synthesize concepts while considering multiple perspectives 
-   Developing inclusive teaching practices in clinical and educational environments 

## Get experience [https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/your\-degree/what\-can\-i\-do\-with\-my\-kinesiology\-degree/\#get\-experience](https://students.ubc.ca/career/your-degree/what-can-i-do-with-my-kinesiology-degree/#get-experience) 

UBC offers many opportunities for Kinesiology students to build their careers\. 

### Workplace experience 

-   [Work Learn](https://students.ubc.ca/career/work-learn-program/)  
    Build work experience through a part\-time, on\-campus job\. 
-   [UBC Kinesiology Work\-Integrated Learning](https://kin.educ.ubc.ca/undergraduate/bkin-degree-requirements/upper-level-requirements/work-integrated-learning/)  
    Develop work skills through experience\-based learning in for\-credit courses\. 
-   [Kinesiology Outreach Programs](https://kin.educ.ubc.ca/outreach/)  
    Apply your class learnings through experiential paid or volunteer opportunities 
-   [On\-campus jobs](https://students.ubc.ca/career/campus-jobs/)  
    Find student jobs available on campus\. 
-   [Careers Online](https://ubc-csm.symplicity.com/index.php)  
    Browse work or volunteer positions on UBC’s online career resources platform\. 
-   [Canada Summer Jobs Program](https://www.jobbank.gc.ca/youth)  
    Check out summer jobs for full\-time students\. 
-   [Federal Student Work Experience Program](https://www.canada.ca/en/public-service-commission/jobs/services/recruitment/students/federal-student-work-program.html)  
    Apply for government positions across Canada through the student recruitment initiative\. 

### Research 

From volunteering in a lab to getting a research award, there are many possibilities to build your undergrad research experience and prepare you for graduate school or careers in research: 

-   [Faculty research opportunities](https://kin.educ.ubc.ca/research/)
-   [Undergraduate Research Awards](https://students.ubc.ca/career/undergraduate-student-research-awards-nserc-cihr-sshrc/)
-   [Directed Studies \(KIN 490\)](https://kin.educ.ubc.ca/undergraduate/bkin-degree-requirements/upper-level-requirements/directed-studies-kin490/) 
-   [Undergraduate Research Experience \(KIN 492\)](https://kin.educ.ubc.ca/undergraduate/bkin-degree-requirements/upper-level-requirements/undergraduate-research-experience-kin492/) 

### Involvement and leadership 

Connect your academic learning to experiences outside of the classroom\. Take initiative to engage in different communities to strengthen your communication and collaboration skills\. 

-   [Kinesiology Undergraduate Society \(KUS\)](https://www.ubckus.ca/)  
    Join your student council to plan events and advocate on behalf of Kinesiology undergraduates\. 
-   [Centre for Community Engaged Learning](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-community-engaged-learning/)  
    Get involved at a local school or non\-profit organization\. 
-   [Student Directed Seminars](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/student-directed-seminars/)  
    Propose, coordinate, and lead your own seminar class for credit\. 
-   [Student leadership opportunities](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/)  
    Take on a student leadership role with Residence Life, a Peer Program, Orientations, Collegia, and many more campus groups\. 

### International experience 

Living, studying, and working abroad build valuable traits\. Show employers you are adaptable, can work independently, and have global experience\. 

-   [Go Global](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/)  
    Go on exchange, attend a global seminar, or conduct research abroad\. 
-   [Office of Regional and International Community Engagement \(ORICE\)](https://orice.ubc.ca/programs/)  
    Make meaningful connections between the wider community and academia around common interests in complex global issues\. 

## Build your network [https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/your\-degree/what\-can\-i\-do\-with\-my\-kinesiology\-degree/\#build\-your\-network](https://students.ubc.ca/career/your-degree/what-can-i-do-with-my-kinesiology-degree/#build-your-network) 

Friends, family, TAs, instructors, and other people you meet can help you navigate your career questions\. Uncover possibilities and learn from the experiences, stories, and insights of others\. 

-   [Kinesiology Mentorship Program](https://kin.educ.ubc.ca/get-involved/mentorship-program/)  
    Pair up with an alumni mentor to share experiences, build skills, and explore different career paths in Kinesiology\. 
-   [Kinesiology Alumni Stories](https://kin.educ.ubc.ca/alumni/alumni-stories/)  
    Meet alumni, hear their stories, and learn how their Kinesiology degrees contributed to where they are now\.
-   [UBC Hub of Ten Thousand Coffees](https://ubc.tenthousandcoffees.com/signup)  
    Create a free profile and get matched with UBC community members to learn about their career journeys\. 
-   [Find Kinesiology alumni on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/school/universityofbc/people/)  
    Explore paths alumni have taken by viewing their profiles or reach out for a coffee chat\. 

## Career possibilities [https://students\.ubc\.ca/career/your\-degree/what\-can\-i\-do\-with\-my\-kinesiology\-degree/\#career\-possibilities](https://students.ubc.ca/career/your-degree/what-can-i-do-with-my-kinesiology-degree/#career-possibilities)
