title: Family health for students with children
content_markdown:
Find health insurance options and explore healthcare, mental health, and family wellbeing resources available to UBC students and their dependents in British Columbia\.

## Health Insurance for dependents[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/equity\-diversity\-inclusion\-resources/resources\-who\-are\-parents/family\-health\-for\-students\-with\-children/\#health\-insurance\-for\-dependents](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/resources-who-are-parents/family-health-for-students-with-children/#health-insurance-for-dependents)

If you are a UBC student with children, you may be able to add them to your health insurance coverage\. Learn how to enrol family members in UBC student health plans and BC Medical Services Plan \(MSP\) coverage\.

[Overview of health insurance](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-insurance/)

Learn about the main health insurance programs in British Columbia and at UBC\.

[AMS/GSS Health and Dental Plan](https://www.studentcare.ca/rte/en/UniversityofBritishColumbiaAMSGSS_ChangeofCoverage_CoupleFamilyEnrolments)

UBC students can enrol eligible dependents on their plan for an additional fee\.

[BC Medical Services Plan \(MSP\)](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/health/health-drug-coverage/msp/bc-residents/managing-your-msp-account/adding-and-removing-dependents)

Learn about eligibility requirements and how to add dependent family members to your plan\.

[iMED coverage](https://imed.david-cummings.com/enrolment/add-family-members/) 

International students can purchase iMED coverage for eligible dependent family members\.

## Locating healthcare providers[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/equity\-diversity\-inclusion\-resources/resources\-who\-are\-parents/family\-health\-for\-students\-with\-children/\#locating\-healthcare\-providers](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/resources-who-are-parents/family-health-for-students-with-children/#locating-healthcare-providers)

UBC Student Health and Wellbeing provides healthcare for registered students only\. However, you can visit community services in your area to find support for your dependents and family members\.

[Vancouver Coastal Health parenting resources](https://www.vch.ca/en/parenting-resources)

Explore resources related to pregnancy, childbirth and new parenthood\.

[Medimap](https://medimap.ca/)

Search for a clinic off campus and book with a health or wellness practitioner\.

[Foundry](https://foundrybc.ca/)

Access free services for youth aged 15 to 24, including STI testing, birth control, and wellness counselling\.

[Health Link BC](https://www.healthlinkbc.ca/)

Receive free health information and advice\. Call [811](tel:811) for personalized assistance from trained providers\.

[https://www\.healthlinkbc\.ca/](https://www.healthlinkbc.ca/)[MindMapBC](https://www.mindmapbc.ca/)

Search for mental health services, including counselling and support groups, based on your specific needs\.

## Vaccinations or immunizations[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/equity\-diversity\-inclusion\-resources/resources\-who\-are\-parents/family\-health\-for\-students\-with\-children/\#vaccinations\-or\-immunizations](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/resources-who-are-parents/family-health-for-students-with-children/#vaccinations-or-immunizations)

Vaccinations protect people of all ages from harmful bacteria and viruses\. Doctors, pharmacists and nurses provide vaccinations at local public and private health facilities\. 

Be sure to keep complete records of immunizations for you and your family\. An immunization record is usually requested when your child is registered to enter day care, preschool, kindergarten, school and certain programs in post\-secondary institutions\. 

Learn more about [immunizations](https://www.healthlinkbc.ca/health-library/immunizations) in British Columbia and how to access your records\.

## Mental health and counselling[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/equity\-diversity\-inclusion\-resources/resources\-who\-are\-parents/family\-health\-for\-students\-with\-children/\#mental\-health\-and\-counselling](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/resources-who-are-parents/family-health-for-students-with-children/#mental-health-and-counselling)

On\-campus programs, including [Counselling Services](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/) and the [Indigenous Mental Health and Wellbeing program](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/indigenous-mental-health-wellbeing-program/) are available and free for UBC students\.

Beyond UBC services, UBC students and their dependents registered in the AMS/GSS Health and Dental Plan are eligible for coverage for appointments with a private mental health practitioner, including those that specialize in relationships or family therapy\. Learn how to [find a private counsellor](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/finding-private-counsellor/)\.

You can also connect with a healthcare provider for off\-campus resources\.

**

General mental health support

**

-   [Counselling BC directory](https://counsellingbc.com/counsellors)  
    Search for counsellors based on your needs\.
-   [Here2Talk](https://here2talk.ca/)  
    Call or text for 24/7 free, confidential counselling and community referral services\.
-   [BounceBack BC](https://bouncebackbc.ca/)Join a free skill\-building program for youth and adults to manage low mood, depression, anxiety, and stress\.
-   [Kids Help Phone](https://kidshelpphone.ca/)  
    Find peer support, resources for families, and remote counselling for mental health support\.
-   [Parent Support Hub for substances](https://www.talksubstance.org/support/supporthub/)  
    Get 24/7 help for caregivers or parents worried about their child’s use of substances\.
-   [FamilySmart](https://familysmart.ca/)  
    Explore information and support options for parents provided via family peer support, events and workshops\.
-   [Confident Parents: Thriving Kids](https://welcome.cmhacptk.ca/)  
    Access phone\-based coaching and programs for your child’s anxiety or behaviour with a healthcare provider referral\.

**

Resources for Indigenous students

**

-   [First Nations Health Authority Mental Health Benefit](https://www.fnha.ca/benefits/mental-health)Receive counselling services from a qualified mental health provider using your student extended health plan\.
-   [Big Worries, Strong Spirit Coaching Program](https://welcome.cmhacptk.ca/bigworries/)  
    Access a free coaching program for Indigenous families that support kids with anxiety\.

**

Culturally specific resources

**

-   [SouthAsianTherapists\.Org](https://southasiantherapists.org/therapist-region/british-columbia/)Browse the directory for South Asian mental health professionals in British Columbia\.
-   [Vancouver Black Therapy and Advocacy Foundation](https://vancouverblacktherapyfoundation.com/)  
    Apply for free or low\-cost counselling with Black counsellors\.

**

2SLGBTQIA\+ support options

**

-   [Qmunity](https://www.qmunity.ca/)Attend support groups, counselling, and access resources for 2SLGBTQIA\+ youth and their loved ones\.
-   [Trans Lifeline](https://translifeline.org/hotline/)  
    Call [877 330 6366](tel:877%20330%206366) to reach a trans\-run, peer support hotline for trans folks\.

**

Resources for people with disabilities

**

-   [Family Support Institute](https://familysupportbc.com/)  
    Access peer support, training videos and workshops, or interpreter services by volunteers\.
-   [Inclusion BC](https://inclusionbc.org/)  
    Get advocacy support and resource referrals for BC students with intellectual disabilities and their families\.
-   [Child and Family Services directory](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/search?id=3101EE72823047269017D08E55AF6441&tab=1&q=special+needs)  
    Find family services offices in British Columbia for assessments and support\.

## Sexual and reproductive wellbeing[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/equity\-diversity\-inclusion\-resources/resources\-who\-are\-parents/family\-health\-for\-students\-with\-children/\#sexual\-and\-reproductive\-wellbeing](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/equity-diversity-inclusion-resources/resources-who-are-parents/family-health-for-students-with-children/#sexual-and-reproductive-wellbeing)

Find sexual health resources and guidance to help you talk with your children about sexual health and development\.

[Options for Sexual Health](https://www.optionsforsexualhealth.org/what-we-do/about-the-people/contact-us/)

Contact the helpline or visit a clinic to ask questions and receive support

[Action Canada for Sexual Health and Rights](https://www.actioncanadashr.org/)

Locate sexual health services near you\.

[Amaze](https://amaze.org/parents/)

Watch videos to learn how to talk with your children about topics like healthy relationships\.

[https://amaze\.org/parents/](https://amaze.org/parents/)[Sexual health resources on campus](https://students.ubc.ca/health/health-topics/sexual-health/)

Learn about resources and information provided by UBC, including STI testing and birth control\.

title: Cost of Attendance for US students
content_markdown:
The Cost of Attendance \(COA\) for US students is an estimate of your educational expenses for a period of study\. The expenses included in the estimate are determined by US federal law\. Your COA determines the maximum financial aid that you may receive for each study period\.

## What is included[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/cost\-of\-attendance\-for\-us\-students/\#what\-is\-included](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/cost-of-attendance-for-us-students/#what-is-included)

Cost of Attendance is determined by UBC and consists of reasonable amounts calculated yearly for the average student in each program\. 

The COA includes:

-   Tuition and fees based on a full course load\. Per\-credit fees are published in the [Academic Calendar](https://calendar.ubc.ca/)
-   Books, course materials, supplies, and equipment determined by your program
-   Transportation based on average travel costs from US to UBC and local transportation in Vancouver
-   Miscellaneous personal expenses, which are based on the [Moderate Standard of Living](https://studentaidbc.ca/help-centre/applying-loans/your-financial-need) ‘Miscellaneous’ category for a single student away from home, as determined by BC’s student loan provider
-   Living expenses \(food and housing\), based on your situation:
    -   On campus with a UBC Housing meal plan
    -   On campus without a UBC Housing meal plan
    -   On campus with dependent\(s\)
    -   Off campus
    -   Off campus with dependent\(s\)
    -   Dependent student residing at home with parent\(s\)
-   Loan fees, which reflect your exact loan fees for Direct Loans

## Cost of Attendance amounts[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/cost\-of\-attendance\-for\-us\-students/\#cost\-of\-attendance\-amounts](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/cost-of-attendance-for-us-students/#cost-of-attendance-amounts)

The following Cost of Attendance \(COA\) amounts are valid through August 2027\. All values are in Canadian dollars \(CAD\)\.

### Tuition and fees

This amount is based on a full course load for your program\. See per\-credit amounts in the [Academic Calendar](https://calendar.ubc.ca/)**\.**

### Books, course materials, supplies, and equipment

This is based on an amount determined by your program for average reasonable expenses for each year level\. Use the [first year cost estimator](https://you.ubc.ca/financial-planning/cost/) to calculate an estimate for course materials\. 

### Transportation

The estimate includes average travel costs from US to UBC and local transportation in Vancouver\.

These expenses are based on the [Moderate Standard of Living](https://studentaidbc.ca/help-centre/applying-loans/your-financial-need) ‘Miscellaneous’ category for a single student away from home, as determined by BC’s student loan provider\.

## Determining funding amounts[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/cost\-of\-attendance\-for\-us\-students/\#determining\-funding\-amounts](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/cost-of-attendance-for-us-students/#determining-funding-amounts)

Direct Loans and US private loan funding amounts are based on the Cost of Attendance \(COA\)\. 

### Need\-based funding

Direct Subsidized Loans are available to undergraduate students with financial need\. Your financial need is determined by the [Student Aid Index](https://studentaid.gov/complete-aid-process/how-calculated) \(SAI\) generated by the answers provided in your [Free Application for Federal Student Aid](https://studentaid.gov/h/apply-for-aid/fafsa) \(FAFSA\)\.

Direct Subsidized Loan eligibility is calculated through the following equation:

Cost of Attendance \(COA\) – Student Aid Index \(SAI\) – Other Financial Assistance \(OFA\) \= Financial Need

### Non need\-based funding

Direct Unsubsidized Loans, PLUS Loans, and US private loans are not based on financial need\. Eligibility is calculated with the following equation:

Cost of Attendance \(COA\) – Other Financial Assistance \(OFA\) \= Eligible Funding

### Other Financial Assistance \(OFA\)

Other Financial Assistance \(OFA\) refers to eligible funding you can reasonably anticipate to receive during the study period, whether the assistance is awarded by the school or by an individual or organization outside the school\. This includes any awards, scholarships, and other loan funding you are receiving\. It does not include any income you have earned\.

It’s important to report all of your scholarships and awards to avoid having your Direct Loans audited, reduced or returned\. 

## Additional resources[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/cost\-of\-attendance\-for\-us\-students/\#additional\-resources](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/cost-of-attendance-for-us-students/#additional-resources)

title: US Direct Loans
content_markdown:
UBC is a Title IV institution, which means eligible students and parents can borrow directly from the US Department of Education through the US Federal Direct Loan Program\. 

At UBC, the available types of Direct Loans include: 

-   [Direct Subsidized Loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-direct-loans/#direct-subsidized)
-   [Direct Unsubsidized Loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-direct-loans/#direct-unsubsidized)
-   [Parent PLUS Loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-direct-loans/#parent-plus-loans)
-   [Grad PLUS Loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-direct-loans/#grad-plus-loans) \(available only to legacy borrowers as of July 1, 2026\)

Other Title IV funding programs such as Pell Grants, Federal Supplemental Educational Opportunity Grants, and the Federal Work\-Study Program are not available at UBC\.

UBC can provide Direct Loan funding to students who meet the [basic eligibility requirements](https://studentaid.gov/understand-aid/eligibility/requirements?custom2=a9ce5bba-1bfd-4de0-a985-3bce21885f4a&og1=a9ce5bba-1bfd-4de0-a985-3bce21885f4a&tg1=opg_fafsa&tg5=%7Btg5%7D&tg7=%7Btg7%7D&tg8=%7Btg8%7D&tg9=%7Btg9%7D&utm_source=government-assistance.org&utm_medium=crm-guide_crm-1pe&utm_campaign=%7Btg4%7D&utm_content=%7Btg6%7D&utm_term=%7Btg10%7D)\.

Maximum funding amounts depend on whether you’re classified as a dependent or an independent student by the answers you provided on your [Free Application for Federal Student Aid](https://studentaid.gov/h/apply-for-aid/fafsa) \(FAFSA\)\. Please read the [Federal StudentAid guide](https://studentaid.gov/sites/default/files/fafsa-dependency.pdf) \(pdf\) to determine if you are a dependent or independent student\.

If you have questions about your funding eligibility or assessment, please contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/)\.

## Direct Subsidized Loans

Direct Subsidized Loans are offered to eligible undergraduate students with demonstrated financial need\. Financial need is determined by the [Student Aid Index \(SAI\)](https://studentaid.gov/help-center/answers/article/what-is-sai) from your Free Application for Federal Student Aid \(FAFSA\)\. 

The US Department of Education pays the interest on a Direct Subsidized Loan during the following periods:

-   While you’re enrolled in school at least [half\-time](https://studentaid.gov/help-center/answers/article/half-time-enrollment)
-   During the first 6 months after you leave school \(referred to as a grace period\)
-   During a period of deferment \(a temporary postponement of loan payments\)

## Direct Unsubsidized Loans

[Direct Unsubsidized Loans](https://studentaid.gov/understand-aid/types/loans/subsidized-unsubsidized) are another type of federal student loans offered by the U\.S\. Department of Education, available to eligible undergraduate and graduate students\. There is no requirement to demonstrate financial need, and interest accumulates during all periods\.

## Direct Parent PLUS Loans

[Parent Plus Loans](https://studentaid.gov/understand-aid/types/loans/plus/parent) can help parents pay for the educational expenses of dependent children studying at the undergraduate level\. As of July 1, 2026, Parent Plus Loans are capped at $20,000 USD per student per year, with a $65,000 USD lifetime limit per student\. Interest is charged during all periods\. 

Continuing undergraduate students with previous Direct Loans may be eligible for an exception to the new limits for up to 3 years\. Contact [usloans\.inquiry@ubc\.ca](mailto:usloans.inquiry@ubc.ca) for information about your eligibility\.

## Direct Grad PLUS Loans

As of July 1, 2026, the [Grad PLUS Loan program](https://studentaid.gov/understand-aid/types/loans/plus/grad) has ended\. 

Continuing graduate students may be eligible to continue borrowing Grad PLUS Loans for up to 3 years\. Contact [usloans\.inquiry@ubc\.ca](mailto:usloans.inquiry@ubc.ca) for information about your eligibility\.

## Eligibility for the Direct Loan program[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/us\-direct\-loans/\#eligibility\-for\-the\-direct\-loan\-program](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-direct-loans/#eligibility-for-the-direct-loan-program)

To maintain your Direct Loan eligibility, you must not enroll in any online courses during your degree, even during periods in which you are not receiving Direct Loan funding\.

Learn [how courses are delivered](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/course-modes-delivery/) at UBC and check your [course information](http://myworkday.ubc.ca/) on Workday to ensure you are not enrolling in an online course\.

If you have a question about the eligibility of specific hybrid courses, contact [usloans\.inquiry@ubc\.ca](mailto:usloans.inquiry@ubc.ca)\.

| **Course type** | **Eligibility for Direct Loan funding** |
| --- | --- |
| In\-person | Eligible |
| Online | Not eligible |
| Multi\-access | Not eligible |
| Hybrid | Not eligible for most courses |

### Additional eligibility requirements

**

Undergraduate student requirements

**

All undergraduate student applicants must meet all the following requirements:

1.  You must be registered in and maintain at least 6 credits for each term for which you’re applying for funding:
    -   You must be registered only for in\-person and on\-campus courses\.
    -   Registered courses must be for credit\. Audited and waitlisted courses do not meet this requirement\.
    -   For Summer Session eligibility, you must be registered in courses across both terms from May to August\.
2.  You must maintain Satisfactory Academic Progress throughout your studies\. Refer to the [policy guidelines](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/ubc_satisfactory_academic_progress_undergrads.pdf) \(pdf\) for more information\.This includes maintaining a cumulative average of 60% and completing at least 67% of cumulative credits attempted at the end of each term\.

**

Graduate student requirements

**

All graduate student applicants must meet the following requirements:

1.  You must be considered full\- time and be enrolled in at least one course for each term in which you’re applying for funding:
    -   You must be registered only for in\-person and on\-campus courses\.
    -   Registered courses must be for credit\. Audited and waitlisted courses do not meet this requirement\.
    -   For Summer Session eligibility, you must be registered in courses across both terms from May to August\.
2.  You must maintain [Satisfactory Academic Progress](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/ubc_satisfactory_academic_progress_grads.pdf) throughout your studies\. Refer to the [policy guidelines](https://students.ubc.ca/wp-content/uploads/ubc_satisfactory_academic_progress_undergrads.pdf) \(pdf\) for more information\. This includes maintaining a cumulative average of 68% and completing your program of study in a timely manner\.

**

If you are a Canadian citizen or Permanent Resident of Canada

**

You may be eligible for [Canadian Student Loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/) through your home province\. 

If you have any residency affiliation**,** through you or your parents, to the province of Ontario, you may be an exception\. Please contact your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) for more information\.

**

Co\-op terms

**

Co\-op is a great way to gain work experience as you study\. Most co\-op placements arranged through an official [UBC Co\-op](https://coop.ubc.ca/) program are eligible for Direct Loan funding as long as they are not located in the United States\.

If you’re considering doing your Co\-op in the US, please connect with an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) to fully understand the implications to your future Direct Loan eligibility\. Co\-op placements in the US might make you ineligible for future Direct Loan funding\.

If you’re a graduate student, please check with your [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) to confirm if your Co\-op is eligible for loans\.

**

Exchange programs

**

Many opportunities are offered by [Go Global](https://global.ubc.ca/go-global/international-experiences) for students to spend a term or year studying abroad\.

If you’re thinking about going on exchange and you’re eligible for US Direct Loans, contact an [Enrolment Services Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/enrolment-services-advisors/) to understand your financial options before you apply for exchange\.

In addition, check the US [Federal School Code Lists](https://fsapartners.ed.gov/knowledge-center/library/resource-type/Federal%20School%20Code%20Lists) to confirm that your partner university is also eligible for Title IV funds\.

If you choose to do an exchange at a school in the US, you could lose your eligibility for Direct Loans for the rest of your program\. We do not recommend going on exchange to a US school if you require federal loans\.

If your partner university is Title IV and **not located in the US**, UBC can assess you for Direct Loans while you’re on exchange\.

If your partner university is not Title IV, you will not be eligible to receive Direct Loans for the period of your exchange\. You may want to consider [private loans](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-private-student-loans/) instead\. 

## Applying for a US Direct Loan[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/us\-direct\-loans/\#applying\-for\-a\-us\-direct\-loan](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/us-direct-loans/#applying-for-a-us-direct-loan)

The process of applying for a US Direct Loan at UBC is different from the process for students who attend a school in the US\.

When you complete your [Free Application for Federal Student Aid](https://studentaid.gov/h/apply-for-aid/fafsa) \(FAFSA\), the Department of Education will notify UBC of your application\.

### How to apply

1.  Submit your [Free Application for Federal Student Aid](https://studentaid.gov/h/apply-for-aid/fafsa) \(FAFSA\)\. Make sure to select UBC from the school list\. UBC’s school code is G08369\.
2.  Submit a UBC [US Direct Loan Request Form](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_77cbe5dqz3TGKKa)\.
    -   As a foreign school, UBC requires additional information and cannot assess you for Direct Loans until you have submitted this form\.
    -   If you make changes to your FAFSA after submitting your request form, please email [usloans\.inquiry@ubc\.ca](mailto:usloans.inquiry@ubc.ca) so UBC can determine if the updates will affect your assessment\.
    -   Read the Privacy Notice: Your personal information is collected under the authority of section 26\(c\) of the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act \(FIPPA\)\. This information will be used for the purpose of evaluating your US Direct Loan application while attending UBC\. In order to participate in the Title IV Direct Loan program, UBC is required to share your personal information with the US Department of Education, and their agents and contractors\. Questions about the collection of this information may be directed to [usloans\.inquiry@ubc\.ca](mailto:usloans.inquiry@ubc.ca)\.
3.  If you are going to apply for PLUS Loans, [complete your application](https://studentaid.gov/plus-app/) on the Federal Student Aid website\.
4.  Fill out a [Master Promissory Note](https://studentaid.gov/mpn/) \(MPN\) for each type of loan you wish to receive\. There are separate MPNs for Direct Subsidized and Direct Unsubsidized Loans, as well as Parent and Grad PLUS Loans\. New MPNs are required each year at foreign schools\.
5.  If this is your first Direct Loans application at UBC, complete the [Loan Entrance Counselling](https://studentaid.gov/entrance-counseling/) requirement\.
6.  Verify your email\. Log into your [Workday account](http://myworkday.ubc.ca/) and make sure UBC has your current email address\. Learn how to [update your personal information](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/personal-information/adding-changing-your-contact-information/) in Workday\. All US Direct Loan updates and information will be emailed to you at this email address\.

### Application timeline

You’re recommended to apply for Direct Loans at least **4 weeks** before the start of the term\. This will ensure that you receive your funding when the term begins\. 

However, you can apply for a Direct Loan and submit a [US Loan Request Form](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/#applying-for-a-us-direct-loan) up to 2 weeks before the end of your study period\.

Any [late payments](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/tuition-fees/late-payment-fees/) may result in a financial hold applied to your tuition account\.

If you have a Canadian bank account, you’re required to set up [direct deposit](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/finances/setting-up-your-direct-deposit/)\. Direct deposit allows the Direct Loan amount exceeding your fees to be deposited directly into your bank account\.

title: Information for US tax returns
content_markdown:
## 1098\-T tax form[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/information\-for\-us\-tax\-returns/\#1098\-t\-tax\-form](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/information-for-us-tax-returns/#1098-t-tax-form)

If you are filing taxes in the United States, you may be asked to produce [Form 1098\-T, Tuition Statement](https://www.irs.gov/uac/form-1098-t-tuition-statement), which is used for qualified tuition and related expenses paid during the tax year\. 

UBC is an eligible educational institution because of its participation in the US Direct Loan Program\. However, UBC does not issue the Form 1098\-T, Tuition Statement\. As a Canadian institution, UBC only provides Canadian federal tax receipts, such as the [T2202](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/taxes/#t2202-tax-form)\.

Claiming tuition and related expenses without a 1098\-T

For the most up\-to\-date information on claiming tuition and related expenses without a 1098\-T, learn more about [Publication 970, Tax Benefits for Education](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-publication-970)\.

## Codes for your tax return[https://students\.ubc\.ca/finances/student\-loans/funding\-us/information\-for\-us\-tax\-returns/\#codes\-for\-your\-tax\-return](https://students.ubc.ca/finances/student-loans/funding-us/information-for-us-tax-returns/#codes-for-your-tax-return)

American students can use their US IRS Employer Identification Number to claim education tax credits on their income tax\. Parents filling out the [education tax credits form 8863](http://www.irs.gov/uac/Form-8863,-Education-Credits-%28American-Opportunity-and-Lifetime-Learning-Credits%29) may be eligible for a tax credit\. Visit [American Opportunity Credit](http://www.irs.gov/publications/p970/ch02.html) for details\.

Keep the following numbers handy for filing your tax return\.

| **Name of code** | **Code** |
| --- | --- |
| US IRS Employer Identification Number \(for student or parent tax purposes\) | 98\-6001255 |
| Title IV School Code | G08369 |
| OPEID | 00836900 |
| Sallie Mae School Code | 008369\-00 |
| Veterans Affairs Certifying Code | 1\-1\-1016\-75 |
| DUNS Number | 251949962 |

title: Community programs for students with children
content_markdown:
If you’re a student with children, finding activities that work for both school and family life can make a big difference\. 

Browse community centres and family\-friendly activities in the UBC neighbourhood and beyond\.

[University Neighbourhoods Association Community Centres](https://www.myuna.ca/)

Drop into family\-friendly facilities and recreational programs\.

[UBC Inspired Community Programming for Families](https://planning.ubc.ca/community/ubc-inspired)

Connect with the UBC community through programs and fun events for all ages\.

[Culture Club at the Museum of Anthropology](https://moa.ubc.ca/events/)

Participate in monthly art\-based and hands\-on learning events\.

[Kits House](http://www.kitshouse.org/)

Access services like childcare, parent groups, or programs like English language conversation circles\.

[West Point Grey Community Centre](http://www.westpointgrey.org/)

Visit the community centre for recreation, sports, and arts programming for all ages\.

[YWCA Single Moms Group](https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=RAoxFornOUuzJrEeMDkS79nJluSao1xAjPIsyQJTIC1UM0dUU0NJQ0VPQlVPTTlBMU1JNlBSUjJWOS4u)

title: Medical care on campus
content_markdown:
UBC students can receive medical care from a range of healthcare providers, including family physicians, nurse practitioners, specialists, and primary care nurses\. Appointments are offered in person or by phone or video, depending on your needs and preferences\.

If you have a medical provider you already see within your community, we encourage you to connect with them before booking an appointment with Student Health and Wellbeing\. This can support your continuity of care throughout your time at UBC and after you graduate\.

Located on Level 3 of the Gateway Health building at [5955 University Boulevard](https://maps.app.goo.gl/DyvFtS5BbVfefndE9), Student Health and Wellbeing medical providers can support you with:

-   General health concerns
-   Preventive care, including vaccinations and immunization reviews
-   Sexual and reproductive health, such as STI testing, contraception, and pap tests
-   [Mental health care](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/), including diagnosis, treatment, and prescription support
-   Sports Medicine concerns
-   [Allergy shots](https://students.ubc.ca/health/medical-care-on-campus/allergy-shots/)
-   Injuries and wound care
-   Naloxone kit distribution and training
-   Referrals to specialists and other services
-   Completion of third\-party medical forms

## Emergency situations[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/medical\-care\-on\-campus/\#emergency\-situations](https://students.ubc.ca/health/medical-care-on-campus/#emergency-situations)

If you are injured, in danger, or in urgent need of medical care or crisis support, get immediate support using one of the options below:

-   Call [911](tel:911) or visit your [nearest 24/7 emergency department](https://www.vch.ca/your-care/emergency-care) for after\-hours support\.
-   Go to an [Urgent Primary Care Centre](https://www.healthlinkbc.ca/primary-care/service-type/urgent-and-primary-care-centres)\.

If you or someone you know is feeling hopeless or at risk of harm, call or text [988](tel:988) toll\-free at any time to reach the [Suicide Crisis Helpline](https://988.ca/)\.

## Book an appointment[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/medical\-care\-on\-campus/\#book\-an\-appointment](https://students.ubc.ca/health/medical-care-on-campus/#book-an-appointment)

### Book online or by phone

Book an in\-person, video, or phone appointment through the [online portal](https://ubcshw.inputhealth.com/ebooking#new) or by calling [604 822 3811](tel:6048223811) during the opening hours below\.

The fax line is [604 484 2209](tel:6044842209)\.

[Book online](https://ubcshw.inputhealth.com/ebooking#new)

### Visit in person

Drop by the Student Health and Wellbeing Welcome Desk, located on Level 3 of the **Gateway Health Building** \([5955 University Boulevard](https://maps.app.goo.gl/ULJj4mKNdVSRvBcG6)\), or the Koerner Pavilion Clinic \([2211 Wesbrook Mall](https://maps.app.goo.gl/UGxrw2kePCRanibz8), Room S267\) during opening hours, excluding [statutory holidays](https://hr.ubc.ca/working-ubc/statutory-holidays):

-   **Monday**: 8:00 am to 5:00 pm
-   **Tuesday**: 8:00 am to 5:00 pm
-   **Wednesday**: 8:00 am to 6:00 pm
-   **Thursday**: 8:00 am to 5:00 pm
-   **Friday**: 8:00 am to 5:00 pm

## What to expect for appointments[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/medical\-care\-on\-campus/\#what\-to\-expect\-for\-appointments](https://students.ubc.ca/health/medical-care-on-campus/#what-to-expect-for-appointments)

### In\-person appointments

Please arrive at least 15 minutes before your scheduled time\. You may be asked to fill out some forms\. Then, you’ll meet with a doctor or nurse practitioner to discuss your health concerns\.

### Phone appointments

If your appointment is by phone, the call may come from an unlisted number or a number without caller ID\.

### Changing or cancelling your appointment

If you need to cancel your appointment, please provide us with at least 1 to 3 days advance notice\.  
  
You can cancel or change your appointment by logging into the [online booking platform](https://ubcshw.inputhealth.com/portal)\. You can also use the platform to read and respond to clinic messages and update your contact information\.  
  
Appointments cancelled without sufficient notice may have a [cancellation fee](https://students.ubc.ca/health/medical-care-on-campus/student-health-wellbeing-clinic-fees/) applied\.

### Fees

Most appointments are covered by your provincial health plan \(such as MSP\), so there is usually no cost for your visit\. Some forms and non\-insured services have fees\. Review the complete [list of fees](https://students.ubc.ca/health/medical-care-on-campus/student-health-wellbeing-clinic-fees/)\.

### Specialist referrals

In British Columbia, a referral from a doctor or nurse practitioner is needed in order for you to see a specialist physician\. If needed, your doctor or nurse practitioner may refer you to a specialist\. 

Student Health and Wellbeing specialists include allergists, dermatologists, gynecologists, psychiatrists, sports medicine specialists, and respirologists\. Depending on your needs, we may also refer to a specialist physician in the community\.

## Email instructions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/medical\-care\-on\-campus/\#email\-instructions](https://students.ubc.ca/health/medical-care-on-campus/#email-instructions)

If you’re asked to email your documents to [student\.health@ubc\.ca](mailto:student.health@ubc.ca), please ensure you encrypt any medical information, including your symptoms\.

Please call [604 822 3811](tel:6048223811) for encryption instructions if you plan to send medical records or details\.

## Confidentiality notice[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/medical\-care\-on\-campus/\#confidentiality\-notice](https://students.ubc.ca/health/medical-care-on-campus/#confidentiality-notice)

Information you share with Student Health and Wellbeing is confidential\. Your personal health information is protected and is not shared with your faculty or your Workday Student account\.

Aggregate information may be used within Student Health and Wellbeing and shared more broadly at UBC for service planning, quality improvement, and reporting\. This means your information is combined with other students’ information, without names, to improve programs and services\.

Personal information about you and your health can only be shared outside UBC with your permission, or when safety concerns or legal requirements arise\.

If you have any questions about confidentiality, or anything else, please ask during your appointment\. If you wish to release your medical record information to another individual or medical care office, call [604 822 3811](tel:6048223811)\.

## Community primary care services[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/medical\-care\-on\-campus/\#community\-primary\-care\-services](https://students.ubc.ca/health/medical-care-on-campus/#community-primary-care-services)

You can also receive medical care from nearby community clinics and services not affiliated with UBC\.

[Campus of Care \(pdf\)](https://www.ubc.ca/_assets/pdf/ubc_campus_of_care_navigation_flowchart_20260331.pdf)

Review this resource to find the right care at the right time\.

[University Village Medical Clinic](http://www.universityvillageclinic.com/)

Visit one of two appointment\-based clinics in Wesbrook Village or University Village\.

[Walk\-in clinic search tool](https://medimap.ca/)

Find your closest clinic using the online Medimap tool\.

[Call 811 for Healthlink BC](https://www.healthlinkbc.ca/more/about-healthlink-bc/about-8-1-1)

Get free health information and advice from a registered nurse, dietician, pharmacist, or qualified exercise professional\.

title: Co-op or student work placements
content_markdown:
## About student work placements[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/co\-op\-or\-student\-work\-placements/\#about\-student\-work\-placements](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/co-op-or-student-work-placements/#about-student-work-placements)

A [student work placement](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/intern.html), often called a Co\-op, is a work experience, such as a UBC Co\-op, practicum, or work\-integrated learning experience, that is approved by your UBC program or UBC Co\-op office and required for the completion of your degree program\. These can be paid or unpaid positions or volunteer opportunities, and cannot make up more than 50% or your program of study\.

In most cases, you are enrolled in a formal Co\-op, practicum, or work\-integrated learning course or term in order for the student work placement to be considered authorized\. 

If you are not sure whether your work is required for your academic program, please contact an [Academic Advisor](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/academic-learning-resources/academic-advising/) from your faculty or your [graduate program advisor](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/current-students/supervision-advising/program-advising)\. You will need a letter from your faculty or program to prove that the work placement is a program requirement\. Learn more about [UBC Co\-op programs](https://coop.ubc.ca/students/how-co-op-works)\.

### What’s not considered a student work placement

A work placement or internship is not considered a student work placement for immigration purposes if **all** of the following is true:

-   It is arranged independently by the student\. 
-   It isn’t a mandatory requirement of the academic program\.
-   It does not appear on the student’s transcript\.

### Changes to the Co\-op work permit requirement

As of April 1, 2026, you do not need a work permit for required student work placements, such as a UBC Co\-op, internship, or practicum, provided you meet the [eligibility requirements below](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/co-op-or-student-work-placements/#confirm-eligibility)\. 

While a work permit is no longer required, you still need to be admitted into a Co\-op program or registered in a formal required practicum term, work\-integrated learning course, or similar program\-required student work placement course or term\.

If you submitted an application for a Co\-op work permit before April 1, 2026, IRCC will likely withdraw your application and provide you with a letter stating that a Co\-op work permit is not required\.

## Confirm your eligibility for a student work placement[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/co\-op\-or\-student\-work\-placements/\#confirm\-your\-eligibility\-for\-a\-student\-work\-placement](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/co-op-or-student-work-placements/#confirm-your-eligibility-for-a-student-work-placement)

To be eligible for a student work placement, you must meet **all** of the following requirements:

-   You are enrolled as a full\-time student and not currently on leave from your studies\.
-   You have a valid study permit, or you applied to extend your study permit before it expired\.
-   You have conditions printed on your initial study permit that indicate you are allowed to work **on campus\.**
-   You have a UBC letter from your Co\-op office or program indicating that the work is a requirement for your program of study\.
-   Your employer is approved by your Co\-op office or program\.
-   You are registered in a UBC\-approved Co\-op, practicum, work\-integrated learning course, or another similar program\-required student work placement course or term, in which case you are considered [full\-time for immigration purposes](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#full-time)\.
-   Your program of study is at least 6 months in duration, and will lead to a degree, diploma, or certificate from UBC, unless you are a visiting or exchange student who will not receive a credential from UBC\.
-   You are **not** studying as an Access or Unclassified student\.
-   Your primary program of study is **not** English or French as a second language\.

If you’re not eligible for a student work placement, you may be authorized to work on and off campus during your studies for other types of employment, based on your study permit’s work authorization if you meet the [eligibility requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/#permits-required-to-work-in-canada)\.

Usually, [off\-campus work](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/off-campus-work/) is limited to 24 hours per week during academic terms\.

## Complete a medical exam, if applicable[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/co\-op\-or\-student\-work\-placements/\#complete\-a\-medical\-exam\-if\-applicable](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/co-op-or-student-work-placements/#complete-a-medical-exam-if-applicable)

If you will be working in jobs which require a [medical exam](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/#if-you-work-with-children-or-seniors-in-healthcare-settings-or-in-agriculture), such as working with children or seniors, in healthcare settings, clinical laboratories, or in agriculture, you must complete a medical exam and have the right conditions on your study permit before starting your position\. 

Even if you do not work directly with vulnerable populations, you might require a medical exam based on your place of work, no matter what your position is\. Examples include in\-person positions in a hospital \(even if you do not directly care for patients, such as research, administrative, or janitorial positions\) or in a daycare \(even if you do not directly care for children, such as administrative positions\)\. 

If you will likely work in these kinds of positions, or you would like to keep your options open, it is best to complete the medical exam before you apply for your study permit\. Include a brief explanation letter with your study permit application stating that you would like proper conditions on your study permit to work in restricted occupations\.

It’s also possible to take the medical exam after you’ve received your study permit, then apply to change the conditions on your permit afterwards\. However, you will not be able to start the position until you have received a study permit with appropriate conditions\.

## When you can start working[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/co\-op\-or\-student\-work\-placements/\#when\-you\-can\-start\-working](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/co-op-or-student-work-placements/#when-you-can-start-working)

You can only start your UBC student work placement once you meet all of the following requirements: 

-   You fulfill the eligibility requirements [listed above](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/co-op-or-student-work-placements/#confirm-eligibility)\.
-   You have received a UBC letter of acceptance or approval from your Co\-op office or program\. Keep it for your records as you may have to provide it to IRCC later\.
-   You are enrolled in a UBC\-approved Co\-op term, practicum, work\-integrated learning course, or similar\.
-   You have completed a medical exam and have a valid study permit with proper conditions on it, if applicable\.
-   Your student work placement term has begun\.

## When you must stop working[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/co\-op\-or\-student\-work\-placements/\#when\-you\-must\-stop\-working](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/co-op-or-student-work-placements/#when-you-must-stop-working)

You must stop working immediately in any of the following situations: 

-   You no longer meet the eligibility requirements for a student work placement\.
-   Your study permit expires and you did not apply to extend it\.
-   Your [Program Completion Letter](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/post-graduation-work-permit/#when-to-apply-for-a-pgwp) becomes available\.

## On\-campus and off\-campus work eligibility[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/co\-op\-or\-student\-work\-placements/\#on\-campus\-and\-off\-campus\-work\-eligibility](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/co-op-or-student-work-placements/#on-campus-and-off-campus-work-eligibility)

Student work placements or Co\-ops are separate from the eligibility to work on and off campus and refer only to work required to complete your UBC program\. 

If you are eligible for a student work placement, you can work for any employer that is approved by your Co\-op office or program, even if the work takes place off campus\. There is no weekly hour limit while participating in student work placements, but your work placement cannot make up more than 50% of your program of study\. 

If you are enrolled in a UBC Co\-op, practicum, or work\-integrated learning course, you are considered [full\-time for immigration purposes](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes/#full-time)\. You may work on a UBC student work placement and, at the same time, [work on and/or off campus](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/) in another type of employment if you meet the requirements for each\.

## International Student Guide[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/co\-op\-or\-student\-work\-placements/\#international\-student\-guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/co-op-or-student-work-placements/#international-student-guide)

Find everything you need to know about life as an international student at UBC’s Vancouver campus\.

[View the guide](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/)

## If you have questions[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/co\-op\-or\-student\-work\-placements/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/co-op-or-student-work-placements/#if-you-have-questions)

You can connect with [International Student Advising](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/international-student-advising/) for questions related to immigration, health insurance, and life as an international student in Canada\.

## The information on this page may change[https://students\.ubc\.ca/international\-student\-guide/working\-canada/co\-op\-or\-student\-work\-placements/\#the\-information\-on\-this\-page\-may\-change](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/working-canada/co-op-or-student-work-placements/#the-information-on-this-page-may-change)

The immigration information on this page has been reviewed and endorsed by Regulated Canadian Immigration Consultants \(RCICs\) or Regulated International Student Immigration Advisors \(RISIAs\) in compliance with the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and Regulations\. However, this is not a legal document and information may change without notice\. Always refer to [Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada](http://www.cic.gc.ca/) \(IRCC\) for the most up\-to\-date information\.

title: William G. Murrin Fund
content_markdown:
## About the fund [https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/funding\-project/william\-murrin\-fund/\#about\-the\-fund](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/funding-project/william-murrin-fund/#about-the-fund) 

The William G\. Murrin Fund was established through a legacy gift from the late Mr\. William G\. Murrin to support religious work at UBC\. 

The Fund provides up to $1,000 to campus\-based organizations that offer meaningful spiritual leadership and make valuable contributions to the religious lives of UBC students, staff, and faculty\. Funding is awarded in alignment with UBC policies and principles of equity and non\-discrimination\. 

## Eligibility requirements [https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/funding\-project/william\-murrin\-fund/\#eligibility\-requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/funding-project/william-murrin-fund/#eligibility-requirements) 

Any UBC organization or association, including campus religious or spiritual groups, can apply\.

Applications are encouraged for programs that will benefit a wide spectrum of the University community, particularly those led by individual religious clubs and groups\. 

Partnerships and proposals with matching funds are highly encouraged\. The committee will only accept one application per organization per application cycle\. 

## Proposal Review Process [https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/funding\-project/william\-murrin\-fund/\#proposal\-review\-process](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/funding-project/william-murrin-fund/#proposal-review-process) 

Proposals are reviewed by 4 Co\-Chairs of the President’s William G\. Murrin Fund Committee\.

### Selection criteria 

Proposals submitted to the William G\. Murrin Fund will be evaluated by the Committee based on the following criteria: 

-   Demonstrated contribution to the religious and spiritual lives of UBC students, staff, and faculty
-   The anticipated impact of the program or activity on the UBC community
-   Evidence of meaningful spiritual leadership, thoughtful program design, and clear objectives
-   Capacity of the organization to successfully deliver the proposal within the funding period
-   A clear, reasonable, and well‑justified budget that demonstrates responsible use of funds
-   Ability to provide a final report after the initiative has been completed

## Funding limits and requirements [https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/funding\-project/william\-murrin\-fund/\#funding\-limits\-and\-requirements](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/funding-project/william-murrin-fund/#funding-limits-and-requirements) 

-   The maximum funding is $1,000 per project per year\. Funds must be used within a 12\-month period and cannot be carried forward without permission from the Committee\.
-   Funds that are unspent each year must be returned to the Office of the Vice\-President, Students\.
-   Organizations or groups that receive funding must provide a written report explaining their expenditure of funds received from the Murrin Committee and a summary of activities and their impact\. Future funding considerations will be contingent upon the timely receipt of this report\.

## How to apply[https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/funding\-project/william\-murrin\-fund/\#how\-to\-apply](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/funding-project/william-murrin-fund/#how-to-apply)

Applications for the 2026/27 cycle are now closed\. Check back in May 2027 for more details\.

### Application timeline 

Applications open in May for projects planned for September to April\.  

Funding decisions will be communicated to applicants within 4 to 6 weeks of each application deadline\.

## If you have questions [https://students\.ubc\.ca/campus\-life/involved/funding\-project/william\-murrin\-fund/\#if\-you\-have\-questions](https://students.ubc.ca/campus-life/involved/funding-project/william-murrin-fund/#if-you-have-questions) 

Email [sun\.park@ubc\.ca](mailto:sun.park@ubc.ca) if you experience any issues throughout the application or if you have questions about the fund\.

title: Dungeons and Dragons Social Skills Group
content_markdown:
## About the group[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/social\-skills\-group\-counselling/\#about\-the\-group](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/social-skills-group-counselling/#about-the-group)

This is a 7‑session therapeutic group that uses Dungeons and & Dragons to support students with neurodiversity or social anxiety in developing social interaction and personal growth within a structured, supportive setting\.

The primary areas of focus are:

-   Foster insight, emotional awareness, regulation, and resilience in social situations
-   Practice and explore everyday social skills, such as communication, collaboration, and boundary‑setting, in a predictable group environment
-   Provide a supportive and inclusive space for personal growth, confidence‑building, and connection

## Eligibility[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/social\-skills\-group\-counselling/\#eligibility](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/social-skills-group-counselling/#eligibility)

You do not need to have previous experience playing Dungeons and Dragons to join the group\. The facilitators will  provide all game materials needed to enjoy the experience\.

All group sessions are held in person on the UBC Vancouver campus\. 

UBC Student Health and Wellbeing recognizes the unique needs of each student and will provide alternate options if group programming is not an appropriate referral option or fit\.

title: Rooted and Resilient group
content_markdown:
## About the group[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/rooted\-resilient\-group\-counselling/\#about\-the\-group](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/rooted-resilient-group-counselling/#about-the-group)

This 8\-week group is a supportive, practical space designed to help you build mental and emotional resiliency and handle academic stress without burning out\. Instead of pushing tough emotions away, the group will focus on strengthening your ability to navigate common challenges that university students face\. 

Each session will help you understand your emotional experiences, learn to pause and respond rather than react, and navigate discomfort using real, everyday strategies\. This is also a space to connect with other students and build a lasting social support network with one another beyond the group\.

This group is designed for students who are: 

-   Wanting to build resiliency and gain practical tools to cope with school stress, anxiety, and overwhelm
-   Hoping to connect with other students and build a community of mutual support
-   Interested in learning how to navigate their emotions but have little to no previous counselling experience
-   Experiencing mild signs of stress, like mild worry, frequent frustration, or feeling easily overwhelmed
-   Looking for a skills\-based group environment rather than individual therapy

title: Navigating Anxiety Group
content_markdown:
## About the group[https://students\.ubc\.ca/health/mental\-health\-care\-ubc/group\-counselling\-programs/acceptance\-commitment\-therapy\-anxiety\-group/\#about\-the\-group](https://students.ubc.ca/health/mental-health-care-ubc/group-counselling-programs/acceptance-commitment-therapy-anxiety-group/#about-the-group)

Anxiety may show up in many forms, such as perfectionism, exam anxiety, excessive worry about social interactions, or panic\. This in\-person, interactive group is for anyone who feels like they are in a constant struggle with anxiety and worry\.  

Based on Acceptance and Commitment Therapy \(ACT\), the group offers a safe and non\-judgmental space to develop strategies to take a step back from the cognitive struggle, become more accepting of yourself and emotions, and to reconnect with a value\-driven life\.
